00 — Rebrand

Naelao — Not Suna

Everything previously called CF-Suna, suna, or suna-kortix in this codebase is now called Naelao. This is not a cosmetic rename — it affects every file path, every environment variable, every Worker name, every package name, every database table prefix, every R2 bucket name, and every public-facing URL. Do this rename before writing a single line of application code.

What Changes — The Complete Rename Checklist

A junior developer's most common mistake at this step is doing a partial rename — changing names in the frontend but forgetting Worker names, or changing package names but leaving environment variables. The following table is exhaustive. Every row must be renamed before proceeding.

Category Old Name (CF-Suna) New Name (Naelao) Where This Appears
Worker names cf-suna-router naelao-router wrangler.jsonc, Worker fetch() entrypoint, Service Binding names
Worker names cf-suna-auth naelao-auth All 22 workers — same pattern
Package name @cf-suna/agent-sdk @naelao/agent-sdk package.json, all imports
R2 Bucket cf-suna-workspace naelao-workspace wrangler.jsonc r2_buckets, all env.WORKSPACE refs
R2 Bucket cf-suna-assets naelao-assets wrangler.jsonc r2_buckets
KV Namespaces cf-suna-config naelao-config wrangler.jsonc kv_namespaces
CF Queues suna-agent-runs naelao-agent-runs wrangler.jsonc queues producers/consumers
DO class names class SunaAgentDO class NaelaoAgentDO All DO class declarations, wrangler.jsonc durable_objects
DB table prefix suna_* naelao_* (new tables only) SpaceDO SQLite schema — clean implementation, no suna table migration needed. All tables initialized in SpaceDO constructor.
Env vars SUNA_* NAELAO_* .dev.vars, CF Secrets, wrangler.jsonc vars
Container names suna-agent-{id} naelao-agent-{id} SandboxDO container naming logic
Frontend package name: "cf-suna-web" name: "naelao-web" apps/frontend/package.json
Domain prefix *.suna.cfpages.dev *.naelao.dev CF Pages project domain, CORS config
GitHub repo github.com/org/cf-suna github.com/org/naelao package.json repository field
Log prefix [SUNA] [NAELAO] All console.log / structured log calls
⚠ Common Junior Dev Mistake

Do NOT do a global find-and-replace of "suna" → "naelao" across the entire codebase blindly. The upstream kortix-ai/suna attribution must stay in comments and in the LICENSE file. The AgentPress tool names in the system prompt (like computer_call, web_search) do NOT change — these are API contracts between the agent and Anthropic's tool use schema. Only change infrastructure and brand names, never protocol names.

Automated Rename Script

Run this once at project init. Never run it again — it is destructive if run on partially-renamed code.

#!/bin/bash
# scripts/rename-to-naelao.sh
# Run ONCE at project start. Never again.
# Renames all infrastructure references from cf-suna → naelao

set -e

# 1. Worker names in wrangler.jsonc files
find . -name "wrangler.jsonc" -exec sed -i \
  's/cf-suna-/naelao-/g; s/"suna-/"naelao-/g' {} \;

# 2. Package names
find . -name "package.json" -exec sed -i \
  's/@cf-suna\//@naelao\//g; s/"cf-suna"/"naelao"/g' {} \;

# 3. Environment variable names (not values)
find . -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.tsx" -o -name "*.js" | xargs sed -i \
  's/env\.SUNA_/env.NAELAO_/g; s/SUNA_API_KEY/NAELAO_API_KEY/g'

# 4. R2 bucket binding names
grep -r "cf-suna-workspace\|cf-suna-assets" . --include="*.jsonc" -l | \
  xargs sed -i 's/cf-suna-workspace/naelao-workspace/g; s/cf-suna-assets/naelao-assets/g'

# 5. Container name prefixes in SandboxDO
find . -name "sandbox-do.ts" -exec sed -i \
  's/suna-agent-/naelao-agent-/g; s/suna-assistant-/naelao-assistant-/g' {} \;

echo "✓ Rename complete. Run: git diff --stat to verify scope."
echo "⚠ Manually verify: 1) License/attribution comments, 2) AgentPress tool names, 3) SpaceDO table schema matches workers/naelao-spaces/src/dos/SpaceDO.ts"
01 — Foundation

What Naelao Is Built From

Naelao is a fork of kortix-ai/suna (Apache 2.0). Every product concept — threads, projects, agents, the marketplace, billing — is preserved. Every infrastructure component is replaced with Cloudflare-native equivalents. A user migrating from Suna sees the same product. The stack underneath is completely different and dramatically cheaper to operate.

The Core Architecture Philosophy

The original Suna kortix runs on a traditional server stack: a Python FastAPI backend, Redis for queuing and pub/sub, Docker containers managed by Daytona for agent sandboxes, and Supabase for persistence (suna kortix original). This stack costs significant money even when idle — containers running, Redis paying for memory, a FastAPI server billing for uptime regardless of traffic.

Naelao's philosophy inverts this: compute exists only when it is doing compute. The Durable Object is the agent's brain — it costs nothing when the conversation is idle. The container is the agent's hands — it boots when needed and stops when done. R2 is the agent's memory — it never sleeps but never computes either. Cloudflare Workflows are the agent's long-running tasks — they checkpoint between steps and hibernate for free.

Complete Suna → Naelao Technology Map

Suna Component Technology Naelao Replacement Why
API Backend FastAPI (Python) 22 CF Workers (TypeScript) Zero cold-start penalty, global edge, Service Bindings for zero-latency internal calls
Message Queue Dramatiq + Redis CF Queues + runFiber() Durable, checkpointed, zero idle cost. Redis eliminated entirely.
Agent Brain AgentRunner Python class NaelaoAgentDO (Durable Object) Persistent state, zero idle CPU, SQLite built-in, hibernation API
Agent Sandbox Docker via Daytona CF Containers via SandboxDO On-demand only, R2 filesystem mount, no external lifecycle management
Browser Playwright subprocess in Docker CF Browser Rendering (CDP proxy) Managed by CF, no container needed for browser tasks
File Storage Ephemeral Docker FS Cloudflare R2 (permanent) Files survive container restarts, zero egress fees, mounted via FUSE
Real-time Streaming Redis Streams + SSE DO WebSocket Hibernation Zero billing during idle, instant wake on broadcast
LLM Proxy LiteLLM CF AI Gateway + Together AI Semantic caching, fallback routing, BYOK secrets, LoRA fine-tuning
Background Jobs Celery + Redis CF Workflows (durable) Checkpointed steps, free hibernation between steps, no Redis
AgentPress Tools Python tool classes (in FastAPI) TypeScript MCP Workers + R2 skills Language-agnostic, OpenClaw skill format, dynamically loaded
Database Supabase PostgreSQL SpaceDO SQLite — one DB per product (root space) DB boundary = product boundary. No RLS needed. Fixed platform schema. Sub-spaces share parent's SpaceDO, isolated by space_id column. DO SQLite is native CF — no external service.
Auth Supabase Auth Naelao-native JWT + CF Access (admin) Supabase Auth removed. naelao-auth Worker issues and verifies JWTs. CF Access gates admin routes. No external auth service dependency.
Caching Redis CF KV + DO SQLite KV for config/circuit breakers, DO SQLite for session-scoped cache
Analytics Supabase analytics tables (suna kortix) CF Workers Analytics Engine Structured events, SQL queries, no separate DB tables needed

What Is Entirely New in Naelao (Not in Suna Kortix)

  • Space Assistants (OpenClaw-native) — 24/7 per-user persistent AI assistants with full OpenClaw architecture, self-modifying skills, sub-agent spawning, channel integrations
  • Naelao OS + Foundation Platform — the underlying primitive layer that makes all Space Types buildable without hardcoding each one
  • Naelao Apps (MCP-native) — app store where apps are MCP servers consumed by both users and agents, with dynamic UI generation
  • Mini-AGI Space Type — company-level intelligence layer with data access controls, cross-sub-space data restrictions
  • Workers Space Type — virtual employees: definition → instance model, federated learning, wallets, x402 payments
  • Multi-tenant Spaces + Sub-Spaces — 6-layer isolation, Next.js middleware URL rewriting, space_id on every DB query
  • Project Collaboration — file locks in ProjectDO, version history, real-time presence, 3-way text merge
  • Dynamic Workflows as Agent Automation — agent-authored workflows stored in R2, dispatched by Worker Loader, zero pre-registration
  • runFiber() Background Mode — durable agent runs that survive browser close, checkpoint per step
  • Together AI + LoRA Fine-tuning — AutoResearch agent fine-tunes models, fine-tuned model available to Space
  • Bootstrap Mode for Verticals — Schmidt flywheel: expert annotators → paid dataset → automated training → Autopilot mode
  • Artifacts via Dynamic Worker Loader — Claude-style live HTML/React artifacts, V8 isolate, <5ms boot

02 — System Topology

Worker Catalogue — Full Spec

Every Worker listed with its Service Bindings, exact responsibilities, and critical implementation notes for junior developers.

naelao-router
Entry · All Traffic
The single public origin. Every request hits this first. Handles CORS, CF Access JWT validation on admin routes, WebSocket upgrade routing, rate limiting via KV, and Service Binding dispatch to downstream Workers. Contains zero business logic — if you find yourself adding a feature here, it belongs in a downstream Worker instead. Bindings: KV (naelao-config), Service Bindings to all 21 other Workers.
naelao-auth
Service · Auth & RBAC
JWT verification (Naelao-native, no Supabase dependency). Space membership lookup from SpaceDO SQLite (the product's per-space DB — no external round-trips). RBAC role assertion (owner/admin/editor/member/viewer). Called via Service Binding from naelao-router on every protected request. Returns enriched identity: {userId, spaceId, role, rootSpaceId}. Bindings: SpaceDO, KV (session cache).
naelao-agents
Service · Agent Lifecycle
Agent definition CRUD (create, read, update, delete, version, import/export JSON). Marketplace API. AgentDO lifecycle management. Pre-flight checks before dispatch (concurrency limit via ConcurrencyDO, billing check via naelao-billing Service Binding). Routes run requests to AgentDO directly (foreground) or to CF Queue (background). Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), NaelaoAgentDO, ConcurrencyDO, Queue: naelao-agent-runs.
naelao-threads
Service · Threads & Streaming
Thread + message CRUD. Streaming token forwarding from AgentDO WebSocket to client SSE/WS. withSpace() helper injects WHERE space_id = ? on every SpaceDO SQLite query — sub-space isolation within the product DB. GET /threads/:id/messages — returns paginated message history. Deduplication of streaming events. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), NaelaoAgentDO (WebSocket).
naelao-spaces
Service · Spaces & Sub-Spaces
Space CRUD, Sub-Space hierarchy (max 3 levels enforced), member management (invite/remove/role-change), project collaboration member access, resource registry (external containers). Quota enforcement: max sub-spaces, max members per tier. SpaceDO maintains member cache for fast auth. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB — all reads/writes scoped to product's root SpaceDO), ProjectDO, ResourceRegistryDO.
naelao-billing
Service · Credits & Subscriptions
Credit ledger operations. Called by NaelaoAgentDO after every LLM response to record token usage. Stripe webhook handling (subscription created/cancelled/payment_failed). RevenueCat IAP for iOS/Android. Trial management (14-day, hard cutoff at trial_end). deductCredits(spaceId, tokens) must be atomic — use BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction on SpaceDO SQLite, not two separate queries. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), Stripe Secret, RevenueCat Secret.
naelao-knowledge
Service · Knowledge Base
KB folder/entry CRUD. Document upload → R2 storage → Vectorize embedding. KB injection into agent context via SpaceDO.getLlmFormattedMessages() — the stored-function logic is now a typed DO method. Version history per document. Semantic search via Vectorize. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), R2 (naelao-workspace), Vectorize (naelao-kb-index).
naelao-credentials
Service · Encrypted Secrets
AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption via Web Crypto API (available natively in CF Workers — no library needed). Stores user MCP credential profiles. Called by NaelaoAgentDO via Service Binding at run start to inject MCP credentials into agent context without exposing them to agent code or logs. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), Secret: NAELAO_MCP_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
naelao-mcp-hub
Service · MCP Tool Proxy
MCP tool execution proxy. Receives tool call from AgentDO, routes to correct MCP server (user-configured or platform), returns result. Handles OAuth flows for MCP server auth. Caches tool schemas in KV to avoid repeated discovery calls. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), KV (mcp-tool-cache), naelao-credentials (Service Binding).
naelao-browser
Service · CDP Proxy (Moltworker)
CF Browser Rendering CDP proxy shim. Provides Playwright-equivalent browser automation to agents via the CF Browser Rendering API. Screenshot, navigate, form fill, scrape. This is the Moltworker pattern — the same architecture that openclaw uses. Agents call this via MCP tool, not by spawning a container just to run Playwright. Bindings: CF Browser Rendering API, NaelaoAgentDO (for result delivery).
naelao-artifact
Service · Dynamic Worker Loader
spin_artifact() implementation. Receives agent-generated HTML/React/chart code, runs it through 27-pattern security scanner, stores source in R2, loads it into a Dynamic Worker isolate via the Dynamic Worker Loader API, returns preview URL. Artifact gallery API (list, delete, version). Bindings: R2 (naelao-assets), KV (artifact-registry).
naelao-workflows
Worker Loader · Dynamic Workflows
Dynamic Workflows Worker Loader. One DynamicWorkflow binding in wrangler.jsonc covers every agent-authored workflow in every Space. On each step execution, fetches workflow TypeScript from R2, validates spaceId, loads into Dynamic Worker, dispatches step. WorkflowRegistryDO tracks all deployed workflows. Bindings: R2 (naelao-workspace), WorkflowRegistryDO, Queue: naelao-workflow-cron.
naelao-assistant
Entry Worker · Moltworker Pattern
Space Assistant entry Worker. One per deployment (not one per user — the DO handles per-user isolation). CF Access JWT validation. WebSocket origin check (prevents CVE-2026-25253 class). Proxies HTTP/WS to AssistantDO. Governs permission manifest. Bindings: AssistantDO, AssistantSandboxDO.
naelao-apps-registry
Service · Apps Marketplace New
Naelao Apps marketplace. MCP server registration and discovery. App install/uninstall per Space. Dynamic UI generation via Dynamic Worker Loader for app frontends. App capability manifest (what the app can do for users vs what it can do for agents). Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), R2 (naelao-assets), KV (app-registry), SkillRegistryDO.
naelao-mini-agi
Service · Mini-AGI Space Type New
Mini-AGI intelligence layer management. Data access control matrix (which sub-spaces and users can query which data domains). Mini-AGI instance lifecycle (create, configure, deploy to sub-spaces). Cross-space query routing with permission enforcement. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), MiniAGIDO.
naelao-together-ai
Service · Together AI + LoRA
Together AI API proxy. Model selector integration. LoRA fine-tuning job management via FinetuneJobDO. Fine-tuned model registration in Space after completion. AutoResearch agent integration. Admin approval flow for making fine-tuned models available to Space members. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), FinetuneJobDO, R2 (training files), naelao-notifications (Service Binding).
naelao-sweeper
Cron · Heartbeat & Cleanup
Cron trigger every 5 minutes. Scans NaelaoAgentDO instances with heartbeat_age > 10 minutes → marks failed runs. Wakes containers for scheduled cron jobs in assistant_config.json. Cleans stale DO state. Dead letter queue re-processing. Bindings: NaelaoAgentDO, ConcurrencyDO, SpaceDO (product DB), Queue: naelao-dlq.
naelao-notifications
Consumer · Push + Channels
Consumes naelao-notifications Queue. Dispatches: APNs push (iOS), FCM (Android), Slack webhook, Discord webhook, Telegram Bot API, email (Resend API). Run-complete alerts, human-in-the-loop approval requests from AssistantDO. Never call this directly — always enqueue. Bindings: Queue consumer, SpaceDO (product DB), Secrets: APNs cert, FCM key, Resend key.
naelao-analytics
Consumer · Analytics Engine
Consumes naelao-analytics Queue. LLM-powered conversation analysis (sentiment, topic, frustration detection, feature requests, RFM scoring). Writes structured events to CF Workers Analytics Engine. SQL-queryable per Space. Replaces all analytics tables — never write analytics events to SpaceDO. Bindings: Queue consumer, AI Gateway, CF Analytics Engine.
naelao-categorizer
Cron · Project Categorization
Background project categorization. LLM-powered use case assignment. Finds stale projects via SpaceDO.getStaleProjectsForCategorization() — DO method replaces the old Supabase RPC. Updates project metadata. Runs on a 1-hour cron trigger. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), AI Gateway, Cron Trigger.
naelao-feedback
Service · Feedback Analysis
User feedback collection. Thumbs up/down on agent responses. LLM-powered theme extraction, sentiment trending, improvement area identification. CSV export for product team. Feeds quality signals to SkillRegistryDO for skill improvement. Bindings: SpaceDO (product DB), AI Gateway, SkillRegistryDO.
naelao-admin
Service · Admin Operations
CF Access protected (admin role required). Operations: user management, credit adjustments, refunds, DLQ management (CF Queues REST API), stress testing, circuit breaker inspection (KV), system status, DB health checks per product SpaceDO. Every operation audit-logged to Analytics Engine. Bindings: All DOs, KV, CF Access assertion, CF Analytics Engine.
03 — AgentDO

NaelaoAgentDO — The Agent Brain

The NaelaoAgentDO is the most critical Durable Object in the entire system. It is the agent's persistent brain — everything the agent knows, is doing, and has done lives here. Understanding this DO fully before writing anything else is mandatory. Get this wrong and every feature built on top of it will be wrong.

Why a Durable Object Is the Agent Brain

A Durable Object has properties that make it uniquely suited for an agent runtime. It has strong consistency — single-threaded execution, no race conditions when two requests arrive simultaneously. It has zero idle cost — when no requests are coming in, the DO hibernates and you pay nothing. It has built-in SQLite — persistent relational storage in the same process as the request handler, no network hop. It has WebSocket Hibernation — WebSocket connections survive across the DO sleeping and waking, costing nothing while idle. It has Alarm API — built-in scheduling without any external cron infrastructure.

The agent is a state machine. Between turns (user messages), it is idle. A traditional server-based agent (like Suna kortix's Docker approach) pays full server cost during idle. NaelaoAgentDO pays zero. The agent wakes when a message arrives, processes it, dispatches work, and hibernates again. On a platform with thousands of agents most of which are idle at any moment, this is an enormous cost difference.

DO Identity and Naming

// durable-objects/agent-do.ts
// The DO ID determines which agent instance handles which request.
// Critical: this must be stable — the same inputs always produce the same ID.
// If the ID changes, a new DO is created and all state is lost.

// CORRECT — stable, deterministic ID
const agentId = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(
  `${spaceId}:${projectId}:${threadId}`
);
const agentDO = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get(agentId);

// WRONG — random ID creates a new DO every time
const agentId = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.newUniqueId(); // ❌ Never do this for agents

// WRONG — missing spaceId means different spaces share the same agent brain
const agentId = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${projectId}:${threadId}`); // ❌ Security violation

Complete DO SQLite Schema

Every table the NaelaoAgentDO creates in its built-in SQLite storage. Run these in the DO's constructor, wrapped in a transaction, using this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(). If you use this.ctx.storage.put() instead of SQL for structured data, you will regret it — SQL is faster, queryable, and supports migrations.

// durable-objects/agent-do.ts
// Run in constructor — idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS on all tables)

export class NaelaoAgentDO extends DurableObject {
  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    
    // Initialize schema — runs on first request after DO creation
    ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => {
      await this.initSchema();
    });
  }

  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      -- Run WAL: write before execute for crash recovery
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run_wal (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        run_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
        tool_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
        tool_args   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- JSON
        status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending|complete|failed
        result      TEXT,            -- JSON, null while pending
        started_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        finished_at INTEGER,
        CONSTRAINT valid_status CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'complete', 'failed'))
      );

      -- Current active fiber (background run)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fibers (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name        TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',  -- running|complete|failed|cancelled
        snapshot    TEXT,            -- JSON checkpoint state from ctx.stash()
        created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Session: conversation messages as a tree (Project Think)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        thread_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        session_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
        parent_id   TEXT REFERENCES messages(id),   -- tree structure
        role        TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- user|assistant|tool|system
        content     TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- raw text or JSON
        tool_name   TEXT,                            -- if role=tool
        token_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        CONSTRAINT valid_role CHECK (role IN ('user', 'assistant', 'tool', 'system'))
      );
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_session ON messages(session_id, created_at);
      CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts USING fts5(
        content, session_id UNINDEXED,
        content=messages, content_rowid=rowid
      );

      -- Token buffer for reconnect replay (last 1000 tokens)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS token_buffer (
        id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        run_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
        delta       TEXT NOT NULL,  -- streaming token text
        created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Context cache control points
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS context_cache (
        key         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        value       TEXT NOT NULL,
        expires_at  INTEGER
      );

      -- Agent memory (typed JSON, never flat Markdown)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_memory (
        key         TEXT NOT NULL,
        category    TEXT NOT NULL,  -- preference|fact|context|task
        value       TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON
        confidence  REAL DEFAULT 1.0,
        created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        PRIMARY KEY (key, category)
      );

      -- Plan steps (todo.md mirror in SQL for fast queries)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plan_steps (
        id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        run_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
        step_text   TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending|done|skipped
        order_idx   INTEGER NOT NULL,
        updated_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );
    `);
  }
}

The Full Agent Run() Method

This is the most important method in the entire codebase. It orchestrates the entire agent execution loop. Study every line — each decision here has a reason.

// durable-objects/agent-do.ts (continued)

async run(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const body = await request.json() as AgentRunRequest;
  const { threadId, input, backgroundMode, runId, spaceId } = body;

  // 1. Verify space isolation — NEVER skip this
  if (this.spaceId !== spaceId) {
    return new Response('Forbidden: space mismatch', { status: 403 });
  }

  // 2. Create or load session (Project Think SessionManager)
  let sessionId = this.ctx.storage.sql
    .exec('SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?', threadId)
    .one()?.id as string | null;
  
  if (!sessionId) {
    sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO sessions (id, thread_id) VALUES (?, ?)',
      sessionId, threadId
    );
  }

  // 3. Add user message to session tree
  const userMsgId = crypto.randomUUID();
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    'INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, role, content) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)',
    userMsgId, sessionId, 'user', input
  );

  // 4. Background mode → runFiber() for durable execution
  if (backgroundMode) {
    // Register fiber BEFORE starting execution
    // If we crash between registration and execution start, the sweeper finds
    // a 'running' fiber with no recent heartbeat and marks it failed.
    // This is intentional — better to mark failed than to hang forever.
    const fiberId = runId ?? crypto.randomUUID();
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO fibers (id, name, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
      fiberId, 'agent-run', 'running'
    );

    // runFiber() — Project Think primitive for durable execution
    // The fiber is registered in SQLite. If the DO is evicted, onFiberRecovered()
    // is called with the last snapshot. The agent resumes from the last checkpoint.
    void this.runFiber(`agent-run-${fiberId}`, async (ctx) => {
      await this.executeAgentLoop(sessionId!, userMsgId, ctx);
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'UPDATE fibers SET status = ? WHERE id = ?', 'complete', fiberId
      );
    });

    return Response.json({ status: 'background', fiberId });
  }

  // 5. Foreground mode — direct execution, WS-tied
  // If the user closes the browser, the WS closes, the DO hibernates,
  // and the run stops cleanly. No orphaned state.
  await this.executeAgentLoop(sessionId, userMsgId, null);
  return Response.json({ status: 'complete' });
}

private async executeAgentLoop(
  sessionId: string,
  startMsgId: string,
  fiberCtx: FiberContext | null
) {
  const agentPress = new AgentPress(this.env, {
    spaceId: this.spaceId,
    sessionId,
    onToken: (delta: string, runId: string) => {
      // Buffer tokens for reconnect replay
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'INSERT INTO token_buffer (run_id, delta) VALUES (?, ?)', runId, delta
      );
      // Broadcast to all connected WebSocket clients
      this.ctx.getWebSockets().forEach(ws => {
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', delta, runId }));
      });
    }
  });

  let iteration = 0;
  const MAX_ITERATIONS = 50; // prevent infinite loops

  while (iteration < MAX_ITERATIONS) {
    iteration++;

    // Checkpoint fiber state every iteration (Project Think)
    if (fiberCtx) {
      fiberCtx.stash({ iteration, sessionId, lastMsgId: startMsgId });
    }

    // Build context from session messages
    const messages = await agentPress.buildContext(sessionId);
    
    // LLM call via CF AI Gateway
    const response = await agentPress.callLLM(messages);

    // Persist assistant message
    const assistantMsgId = crypto.randomUUID();
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, parent_id, role, content, token_count) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
      assistantMsgId, sessionId, startMsgId, 'assistant', 
      response.content, response.usage.output_tokens
    );

    // Record billing — every LLM response, no exceptions
    await this.env.NAELAO_BILLING.recordTokens({
      spaceId: this.spaceId,
      inputTokens: response.usage.input_tokens,
      outputTokens: response.usage.output_tokens,
      cacheReadTokens: response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0,
      cacheWriteTokens: response.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0,
      model: response.model,
    });

    // If no tool calls, the agent is done
    if (!response.toolCalls || response.toolCalls.length === 0) {
      if (response.stopReason === 'end_turn') break;
      if (response.stopReason === 'max_tokens') {
        // Context full — trigger compaction before next iteration
        await agentPress.compactContext(sessionId);
        continue;
      }
      break;
    }

    // Execute tools — parallel for CF-native, serial for containers
    const toolResults = await agentPress.executeTools(
      response.toolCalls,
      { sessionId, assistantMsgId, fiberCtx }
    );

    // Persist tool results
    for (const result of toolResults) {
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, parent_id, role, content, tool_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
        crypto.randomUUID(), sessionId, assistantMsgId,
        'tool', JSON.stringify(result.output), result.toolName
      );
    }

    // Update todo.md in R2 if plan changed
    await this.syncTodoMd(sessionId);
  }

  // Broadcast completion to connected clients
  this.ctx.getWebSockets().forEach(ws => {
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'run_complete', sessionId }));
  });
}

// Called by CF runtime when DO is recovered after eviction
// The fiber's last stash() snapshot is in ctx.snapshot
async onFiberRecovered(ctx: FiberContext) {
  if (!ctx.snapshot) return; // new fiber, nothing to recover
  
  const { iteration, sessionId, lastMsgId } = ctx.snapshot;
  
  // Resume from last checkpoint
  // We don't replay the completed iterations — only resume from the last stash point
  // The session messages already contain everything up to the checkpoint
  await this.executeAgentLoop(sessionId, lastMsgId, ctx);
}

WebSocket Hibernation — How Streaming Works

WebSocket Hibernation is what makes real-time streaming cost-efficient. Without it, keeping a WebSocket open would keep the DO active and billing. With Hibernation, the DO can hibernate between messages and the WebSocket connection survives — the client sees a continuous stream.

// The DO handles WebSocket upgrades in its fetch() handler
async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  
  if (request.headers.get('Upgrade') === 'websocket') {
    // SECURITY: Always validate origin before upgrading
    // CVE-2026-25253 happened because OpenClaw skipped this check
    const origin = request.headers.get('Origin') ?? '';
    const allowed = ['https://app.naelao.dev', 'https://naelao.dev'];
    if (!allowed.some(a => origin.startsWith(a))) {
      return new Response('Forbidden: invalid origin', { status: 403 });
    }

    // CF WebSocket Hibernation — the correct way to create hibernated WS
    const pair = new WebSocketPair();
    const [client, server] = Object.values(pair);
    
    // acceptWebSocket() registers the WS for hibernation
    // The DO can now sleep between messages — zero cost while idle
    // When client sends a message, DO wakes and webSocketMessage() fires
    this.ctx.acceptWebSocket(server);
    
    return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client });
  }

  // Route non-WS requests to appropriate handler
  if (url.pathname === '/run') return this.run(request);
  if (url.pathname === '/replay') return this.replayBuffer(request);
  return new Response('Not Found', { status: 404 });
}

// Called by CF runtime when a hibernated WS receives a message
async webSocketMessage(ws: WebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer) {
  const data = JSON.parse(message as string);
  
  if (data.type === 'ping') {
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'pong' }));
    return;
  }
  if (data.type === 'cancel') {
    await this.cancelCurrentRun();
    return;
  }
}

// Reconnect: replay buffered tokens so user sees full history
async replayBuffer(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const { runId } = await request.json();
  const tokens = this.ctx.storage.sql
    .exec('SELECT delta FROM token_buffer WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY id', runId)
    .toArray();
  return Response.json({ tokens: tokens.map(r => r.delta) });
}

The WAL (Write-Ahead Log) — Crash Recovery

The WAL is one of the most important patterns in Naelao. Every tool call is written to the WAL before it executes. If the DO crashes mid-execution, the sweeper finds pending WAL entries and replays them. Without the WAL, a crash loses all in-progress work. With it, the agent can always resume.

// agentpress/wal.ts
// Every tool execution MUST go through this. No exceptions.
// If you call a tool without WAL, a crash loses the result and the loop hangs.

export class WAL {
  constructor(private sql: SqlStorage) {}

  async executeWithWAL<T>(
    runId: string,
    toolName: string,
    args: unknown,
    executor: () => Promise<T>
  ): Promise<T> {
    const walId = crypto.randomUUID();
    
    // WRITE BEFORE EXECUTE — this is the entire point of WAL
    // If we crash after this line but before the executor, the sweeper
    // finds this 'pending' entry and knows to either retry or mark failed.
    this.sql.exec(
      `INSERT INTO run_wal (id, run_id, tool_name, tool_args, status) 
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending')`,
      walId, runId, toolName, JSON.stringify(args)
    );

    try {
      const result = await executor();
      
      // Mark complete AFTER successful execution
      this.sql.exec(
        `UPDATE run_wal SET status = 'complete', result = ?, finished_at = ?
         WHERE id = ?`,
        JSON.stringify(result), Date.now(), walId
      );
      
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      // Mark failed — the error is preserved for debugging
      this.sql.exec(
        `UPDATE run_wal SET status = 'failed', result = ?, finished_at = ?
         WHERE id = ?`,
        JSON.stringify({ error: (error as Error).message }), Date.now(), walId
      );
      throw error;
    }
  }

  async getPendingEntries(runId: string): Promise<WALEntry[]> {
    return this.sql
      .exec(`SELECT * FROM run_wal WHERE run_id = ? AND status = 'pending'`, runId)
      .toArray() as WALEntry[];
  }
}

Cost Comparison — Why This Architecture Matters

Scenario Suna Kortix (Docker) Naelao (DO + Container) Savings
Idle (24h, no tasks) ~$3–10/day (container always running) ~$0.0001/day (DO hibernation) 99.9%
30 min active coding/day ~$3–10/day (container always on) $0.01–0.05 (container 30min + DO) 95–99%
Browser scraping (100 pages) Container running during entire scrape CF Browser Rendering (~$0.10) 80–90%
Heartbeat / cron check Container must be alive to receive it CF Cron Trigger wakes DO (free tier) 100%
100 concurrent Spaces idle ~$300–1000/day (all containers running) ~$0.01/day (all DOs hibernating) 99.9%
04 — AgentPress TypeScript Port

AgentPress — Complete TypeScript Port

AgentPress is Suna kortix's execution engine — the Python package under agentpress/ in the original repo. Every module must be ported to TypeScript and live in naelao/agentpress/. This section covers every file, every class, every gotcha, and exactly what a junior developer must implement line-by-line to get a working port.

⚠ Critical Warning Before You Start

The most common mistake when porting AgentPress from Python to TypeScript is assuming Python's streaming behavior maps 1:1 to TypeScript. It does not. Python's async for chunk in stream is synchronous within each chunk — the iterator waits for the next chunk before continuing. In TypeScript with the Anthropic SDK, you use stream.on('text', ...) or for await (const chunk of stream). The XML parser MUST handle partial tags across chunk boundaries — this is where 90% of bugs in AgentPress ports occur. Read the streaming section carefully.

File-by-File Port Guide

1. agentpress/context-manager.ts

The ContextManager builds the message array that gets sent to the LLM. In the Python version, this is agentpress/context_manager.py. Its job: take the raw conversation history from the DO session, truncate to fit context limits, inject system prompt, inject tools, and apply prompt caching markers — in exactly the right order to maximize Anthropic's cache hit rate.

// agentpress/context-manager.ts
// Builds the messages array for every LLM call.
// ORDER MATTERS FOR CACHING — do not rearrange without understanding cache_control.

import type { MessageParam, TextBlockParam } from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/messages';

export interface ContextManagerOptions {
  maxTokens: number;          // Hard limit for context window (e.g., 200000 for Claude)
  systemPrompt: string;       // Base system prompt from agent definition
  spaceContext: string;       // Space-specific context (permissions, Space name, etc.)
  skillsXML: string;          // Skills injected as XML block
  toolDefinitions: ToolDef[]; // Tools the LLM can call
  knowledgeBase?: string;     // Project knowledge documents (optional)
}

export class ContextManager {
  constructor(private opts: ContextManagerOptions) {}

  buildMessages(
    rawMessages: SessionMessage[],
    tokenCounter: TokenCounter
  ): { system: TextBlockParam[]; messages: MessageParam[] } {
    
    // STEP 1: Build the system prompt blocks IN THIS EXACT ORDER.
    // Anthropic caches prefix blocks. Static blocks must come FIRST.
    // Dynamic blocks (knowledge, current task) must come LAST.
    // Swapping these destroys cache efficiency — 90% more input tokens per call.
    
    const system: TextBlockParam[] = [
      // Block 1: Base system prompt — STATIC, cached across all calls for this agent definition
      {
        type: 'text',
        text: this.opts.systemPrompt,
        cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }  // cache this block
      },
      // Block 2: Space context — STATIC for this session (Space name, permissions)
      {
        type: 'text',
        text: this.opts.spaceContext,
        cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }
      },
      // Block 3: Skills XML — SEMI-STATIC (changes only when skills change)
      {
        type: 'text',
        text: this.opts.skillsXML,
        cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }
      },
      // Block 4: Knowledge base — DYNAMIC (may change per query via semantic search)
      // NO cache_control here — different every call
      ...(this.opts.knowledgeBase ? [{
        type: 'text' as const,
        text: `\n${this.opts.knowledgeBase}\n`
      }] : []),
    ];

    // STEP 2: Build the messages array.
    // Truncate from the MIDDLE if context is too long — preserve the latest user message
    // and the oldest context (system prompt is separate, not in messages array).
    
    let messages = rawMessages.map(m => ({
      role: m.role as 'user' | 'assistant',
      content: m.content
    }));

    // Count tokens — use the Anthropic tokenizer, not a character estimate
    // Character estimates are wrong by 30-50% for code-heavy conversations
    const totalTokens = tokenCounter.count(messages);
    
    if (totalTokens > this.opts.maxTokens * 0.85) {
      // Truncate: remove from position 2 (after first user msg) to keep context coherent
      // Never remove the very first user message — it establishes the task
      messages = this.truncateMiddle(messages, this.opts.maxTokens * 0.75, tokenCounter);
    }

    return { system, messages };
  }

  private truncateMiddle(
    messages: MessageParam[],
    targetTokens: number,
    counter: TokenCounter
  ): MessageParam[] {
    // Keep first 2 and last N messages, remove from the middle
    // This preserves task context (first) and recent context (last)
    const keep = [messages[0]]; // Always keep first
    let tokens = counter.count([messages[0]]);
    
    // Add from the end backwards until we hit the target
    for (let i = messages.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
      const msgTokens = counter.count([messages[i]]);
      if (tokens + msgTokens > targetTokens) break;
      keep.splice(1, 0, messages[i]); // insert after first
      tokens += msgTokens;
    }
    
    return keep;
  }
}

2. agentpress/xml-parser.ts

This is the most bug-prone file in the entire port. The LLM emits tool calls as XML inside the streaming response. The problem: a single XML tag can be split across multiple streaming chunks. Your parser must buffer incomplete tags and only emit complete ones. Get this wrong and tool calls will silently fail or produce garbled output.

// agentpress/xml-parser.ts
// Streaming XML parser for tool call extraction.
// CRITICAL: Must handle partial tags across chunk boundaries.
// This is the most common source of bugs in AgentPress ports.

// Example of what the LLM emits (one tool call across 3 streaming chunks):
// Chunk 1: "I'll search for that. CF Worker"
// Chunk 3: "s"
// Your parser must buffer across these three chunks and emit ONE complete tool call.

export interface ParsedToolCall {
  toolName: string;
  parameters: Record<string, string>;
  rawXml: string;
}

export class StreamingXMLParser {
  private buffer = '';
  private insideTag = false;
  private currentTagName = '';
  private onToolCall: (call: ParsedToolCall) => void;

  constructor(onToolCall: (call: ParsedToolCall) => void) {
    this.onToolCall = onToolCall;
  }

  // Call this for EVERY chunk from the LLM stream
  feed(chunk: string): string {
    this.buffer += chunk;
    let textContent = '';

    while (true) {
      if (!this.insideTag) {
        // Look for an opening tool call tag
        // Tool call tags are known tool names in angle brackets
        // We don't know which tag names exist at parse time, so we detect any tag
        const openIdx = this.buffer.indexOf('<');
        if (openIdx === -1) {
          // No tag start — all buffer is text
          textContent += this.buffer;
          this.buffer = '';
          break;
        }
        
        // Text before the tag is regular content
        textContent += this.buffer.slice(0, openIdx);
        this.buffer = this.buffer.slice(openIdx);
        this.insideTag = true;
      }

      if (this.insideTag) {
        // Look for closing > to complete the opening tag
        const closeIdx = this.buffer.indexOf('>');
        if (closeIdx === -1) {
          // Incomplete tag — wait for more chunks
          // This is the NORMAL CASE for partial chunks. DO NOT emit anything.
          break;
        }

        const tag = this.buffer.slice(1, closeIdx); // content between < and >
        
        // Is this a closing tag? (starts with /)
        if (tag.startsWith('/')) {
          this.insideTag = false;
          this.buffer = this.buffer.slice(closeIdx + 1);
          continue;
        }

        // This is an opening tool tag — now find its closing tag
        this.currentTagName = tag.trim().split(' ')[0];
        const closingTag = `</${this.currentTagName}>`;
        const fullCloseIdx = this.buffer.indexOf(closingTag);
        
        if (fullCloseIdx === -1) {
          // The closing tag hasn't arrived yet — wait for more chunks
          break;
        }

        // We have a complete tool call element — parse it
        const rawXml = this.buffer.slice(0, fullCloseIdx + closingTag.length);
        this.buffer = this.buffer.slice(fullCloseIdx + closingTag.length);
        this.insideTag = false;

        const toolCall = this.parseToolXml(rawXml, this.currentTagName);
        if (toolCall) {
          this.onToolCall(toolCall);
        }
      }
    }

    return textContent;
  }

  private parseToolXml(rawXml: string, toolName: string): ParsedToolCall | null {
    // Extract parameter tags from within the tool call XML
    // e.g., <web_search><query>Hello</query><num_results>5</num_results></web_search>
    const parameters: Record<string, string> = {};
    const paramRegex = /<(\w+)>([\s\S]*?)<\/\1>/g;
    let match;
    
    // Strip the outer tool tag to get to parameters
    const inner = rawXml
      .replace(`<${toolName}>`, '')
      .replace(`</${toolName}>`, '');
    
    while ((match = paramRegex.exec(inner)) !== null) {
      parameters[match[1]] = match[2].trim();
    }
    
    return { toolName, parameters, rawXml };
  }

  // Call when stream ends — check for any incomplete buffered content
  flush(): string {
    const remaining = this.buffer;
    this.buffer = '';
    this.insideTag = false;
    return remaining; // Return any trailing text content
  }
}

3. agentpress/orchestrator.ts

The orchestrator takes the parsed tool calls and executes them. It decides: which tools can run in parallel, which must be serial, and which need a container vs which can run at the edge. This is where the execution ladder is implemented.

// agentpress/orchestrator.ts
// Execution ladder: workspace → isolate → npm → browser → sandbox
// Each tier is only used if the tool actually needs it.
// A web_search never needs a container. A python_exec always does.
// Getting this right cuts container costs by 60-80%.

export type ExecutionTier = 'workspace' | 'isolate' | 'npm' | 'browser' | 'sandbox';

export interface ToolManifest {
  name: string;
  tier: ExecutionTier;
  parallel: boolean;  // Can this tool run in parallel with others?
}

// Hard-coded tool tier assignments — these never change per agent
const TOOL_TIERS: Record<string, ToolManifest> = {
  // Tier 1: workspace — pure R2 reads/writes, no compute isolate
  'read_file':       { name: 'read_file',       tier: 'workspace', parallel: true },
  'write_file':      { name: 'write_file',      tier: 'workspace', parallel: false },
  'list_directory':  { name: 'list_directory',  tier: 'workspace', parallel: true },
  'delete_file':     { name: 'delete_file',     tier: 'workspace', parallel: false },
  
  // Tier 2: isolate — V8 Dynamic Worker, <5ms boot, TypeScript/JS only
  'web_search':      { name: 'web_search',      tier: 'isolate',   parallel: true },
  'api_call':        { name: 'api_call',         tier: 'isolate',   parallel: true },
  'render_artifact': { name: 'render_artifact', tier: 'isolate',   parallel: false },
  'data_transform':  { name: 'data_transform',  tier: 'isolate',   parallel: true },
  
  // Tier 4: browser — CF Browser Rendering, ~200ms boot
  'browser_navigate':{ name: 'browser_navigate',tier: 'browser',   parallel: false },
  'browser_scrape':  { name: 'browser_scrape',  tier: 'browser',   parallel: false },
  'browser_click':   { name: 'browser_click',   tier: 'browser',   parallel: false },
  
  // Tier 5: sandbox — CF Container, 2-3s boot, full Linux
  'execute_python':  { name: 'execute_python',  tier: 'sandbox',   parallel: false },
  'execute_bash':    { name: 'execute_bash',    tier: 'sandbox',   parallel: false },
  'execute_node':    { name: 'execute_node',    tier: 'sandbox',   parallel: false },
  'git_clone':       { name: 'git_clone',       tier: 'sandbox',   parallel: false },
  'install_package': { name: 'install_package', tier: 'sandbox',   parallel: false },
};

export class Orchestrator {
  constructor(
    private env: Env,
    private spaceId: string,
    private sandboxDO: DurableObjectStub,
    private wal: WAL
  ) {}

  async executeTools(
    toolCalls: ParsedToolCall[],
    runId: string
  ): Promise<ToolResult[]> {
    
    // Group tools by tier for batching
    const byTier = this.groupByTier(toolCalls);
    const results: ToolResult[] = [];

    // Execute workspace tier in parallel (pure R2 ops, no compute)
    if (byTier.workspace?.length) {
      const parallelResults = await Promise.all(
        byTier.workspace.map(tc => 
          this.wal.executeWithWAL(runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
            this.executeWorkspaceTool(tc)
          )
        )
      );
      results.push(...parallelResults);
    }

    // Execute isolate tier in parallel (V8 Dynamic Workers)
    if (byTier.isolate?.length) {
      const parallelResults = await Promise.all(
        byTier.isolate
          .filter(tc => TOOL_TIERS[tc.toolName]?.parallel)
          .map(tc =>
            this.wal.executeWithWAL(runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
              this.executeIsolateTool(tc)
            )
          )
      );
      results.push(...parallelResults);
    }

    // Execute browser tier SERIALLY (shared browser resource, no parallel)
    if (byTier.browser?.length) {
      for (const tc of byTier.browser) {
        const result = await this.wal.executeWithWAL(runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          this.executeBrowserTool(tc)
        );
        results.push(result);
      }
    }

    // Execute sandbox tier SERIALLY (container commands must be ordered)
    if (byTier.sandbox?.length) {
      // Ensure container is running ONCE before sending multiple commands
      await this.ensureContainerRunning();
      for (const tc of byTier.sandbox) {
        const result = await this.wal.executeWithWAL(runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          this.executeSandboxTool(tc)
        );
        results.push(result);
      }
    }

    return results;
  }

  private async executeWorkspaceTool(tc: ParsedToolCall): Promise<ToolResult> {
    const { toolName, parameters } = tc;
    
    if (toolName === 'read_file') {
      const obj = await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(
        `spaces/${this.spaceId}/workspace/${parameters.path}`
      );
      if (!obj) return { toolName, output: { error: 'File not found' } };
      return { toolName, output: { content: await obj.text() } };
    }
    
    if (toolName === 'write_file') {
      // Write to R2 — this IS the persistent filesystem
      await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
        `spaces/${this.spaceId}/workspace/${parameters.path}`,
        parameters.content,
        { customMetadata: { mimeType: 'text/plain', updatedAt: Date.now().toString() } }
      );
      return { toolName, output: { success: true, path: parameters.path } };
    }
    
    throw new Error(`Unknown workspace tool: ${toolName}`);
  }

  private async ensureContainerRunning(): Promise<void> {
    // Ping SandboxDO to ensure container is running
    // SandboxDO handles the boot idempotently — calling this twice is safe
    await this.sandboxDO.fetch(new Request('http://sandbox/ensure-running', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId: this.spaceId })
    }));
  }

  private async executeSandboxTool(tc: ParsedToolCall): Promise<ToolResult> {
    const response = await this.sandboxDO.fetch(new Request('http://sandbox/exec', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        command: tc.toolName,
        args: tc.parameters,
        spaceId: this.spaceId
      })
    }));
    return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: await response.json() };
  }

  private groupByTier(toolCalls: ParsedToolCall[]): Partial<Record<ExecutionTier, ParsedToolCall[]>> {
    return toolCalls.reduce((acc, tc) => {
      const tier = TOOL_TIERS[tc.toolName]?.tier ?? 'sandbox'; // default to safest tier
      if (!acc[tier]) acc[tier] = [];
      acc[tier]!.push(tc);
      return acc;
    }, {} as Partial<Record<ExecutionTier, ParsedToolCall[]>>);
  }
}

4. agentpress/prompt-cache.ts

Anthropic's prompt caching can save 80-90% of input token costs for long agent runs. The cache works on the prefix of your messages. If the first N tokens of your messages array match a previous call, they're served from cache at 10% of the normal cost. The rules for maximizing cache hits are strict — violate them and you lose all cache benefit.

// agentpress/prompt-cache.ts
// Anthropic prompt caching rules:
// 1. cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'} marks a block as a cache breakpoint
// 2. Blocks BEFORE a cache breakpoint are cached
// 3. cache_control can only be on the LAST content block in a message
// 4. Minimum 1024 tokens must be in the cached portion to activate caching
// 5. Cache TTL is 5 minutes — if your agent is idle >5min between turns, cache misses

export function applyCacheControl(messages: MessageParam[]): MessageParam[] {
  // Find the last 3 'human' role messages that are large enough to cache
  // These are the "cache breakpoints" — everything before them is cached
  const humanMessages = messages
    .map((m, i) => ({ m, i }))
    .filter(({ m }) => m.role === 'user');
  
  // Apply cache_control to the last human message
  // This tells Anthropic: "cache everything up to and including this block"
  if (humanMessages.length > 0) {
    const last = humanMessages[humanMessages.length - 1];
    const content = Array.isArray(last.m.content) ? last.m.content : [{ type: 'text', text: last.m.content }];
    const lastBlock = content[content.length - 1];
    if (lastBlock.type === 'text') {
      (lastBlock as any).cache_control = { type: 'ephemeral' };
    }
    messages[last.i] = { ...last.m, content };
  }
  
  return messages;
}

// Track cache hit rate for billing analytics
export function parseCacheMetrics(usage: APIUsage): CacheMetrics {
  return {
    inputTokens:       usage.input_tokens,
    outputTokens:      usage.output_tokens,
    cacheReadTokens:   usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0,
    cacheWriteTokens:  usage.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0,
    // Effective cost = (input - cacheRead)*100% + cacheRead*10% + cacheWrite*125% + output
    costMultiplier: (
      (usage.input_tokens - (usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0)) +
      ((usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0) * 0.1) +
      ((usage.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0) * 1.25) +
      usage.output_tokens
    ) / (usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens)
  };
}
05 — Space Assistants

Space Assistants — Full OpenClaw Architecture, CF-Native

Space Assistants are the most complex and powerful feature in Naelao. They clone the full OpenClaw architecture — prompts, harness, self-modification, sub-agent spawning — but run on Cloudflare-native infrastructure: Durable Objects for the brain, on-demand containers for execution, R2 for the filesystem, Dynamic Workflows for self-modification. One assistant per user per Space by default. Admin can raise this limit.

"The Space Assistant is OpenClaw, but it lives on Cloudflare instead of your Mac mini. It has the same powers — and more."

What OpenClaw Architecture Naelao Clones

OpenClaw (from the openclaw.ai project) is a self-hosted AI assistant that runs continuously on local hardware. Key architectural properties that Naelao adopts:

  • Continuous existence — OpenClaw doesn't start when you open a chat. It's always running, monitoring channels, taking scheduled actions. Naelao's AssistantDO achieves this via DO hibernation: the DO is always registered but only consumes CPU when active.
  • Self-modifying tools — OpenClaw can inspect and modify its own tool implementations. Naelao limits this to skill folders in R2 (not actual Worker code), plus Dynamic Worker loaders for new tool isolates. The assistant can write a new skill SKILL.md, add a new script, and deploy it as a new tool without a platform redeploy.
  • Sub-agent spawning — OpenClaw can launch sub-agents for complex tasks. Naelao's AssistantDO can dispatch NaelaoAgentDO instances from the Space marketplace or build custom ones using the SDK and Dynamic Worker Loaders.
  • Persistent memory — OpenClaw maintains SOUL.md and MEMORY.md. Naelao uses typed JSON in DO SQLite (never flat Markdown — see §19 Security for why this matters).
  • Channel integrations — OpenClaw monitors Slack, Discord, email, SMS. Naelao's AssistantDO has the same via webhooks registered in R2 channel configs.
  • Heartbeat loop — OpenClaw runs a continuous loop checking for tasks. Naelao uses CF Cron Triggers (free) to wake the AssistantDO every 5 minutes for a heartbeat check.
  • cron-jobs.json — OpenClaw's scheduled tasks. Naelao stores this in R2 at spaces/{spaceId}/assistants/{userId}/cron-jobs.json and the heartbeat reads and dispatches them.

AssistantDO — SQLite Schema

// durable-objects/assistant-do.ts
// The AssistantDO is larger than AgentDO because it has persistent channels,
// memory, scheduled tasks, and self-modification capabilities.

private async initSchema() {
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
    -- Core sessions (same as AgentDO)
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
      id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      channel    TEXT,   -- null = web UI, 'slack'|'discord'|'telegram' for channels
      created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
    );

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
      id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
      session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
      parent_id  TEXT REFERENCES messages(id),
      role       TEXT NOT NULL,
      content    TEXT NOT NULL,
      tool_name  TEXT,
      channel_meta TEXT,   -- JSON: {channelId, authorId, authorName} for channel msgs
      created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_asst_msgs ON messages(session_id, created_at);

    -- Typed memory — never flat Markdown
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memory (
      key        TEXT NOT NULL,
      category   TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'fact'|'preference'|'relationship'|'task'|'context'
      value      TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON only, validated on write
      source     TEXT,          -- which conversation created this memory
      confidence REAL DEFAULT 1.0,
      created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
      updated_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
      PRIMARY KEY (key, category)
    );

    -- Channel configurations (Slack, Discord, Telegram, Email)
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS channels (
      id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      type        TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'slack'|'discord'|'telegram'|'email'
      config      TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON: {webhookUrl, botToken, channelId, ...}
      enabled     INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
      last_active INTEGER,
      created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
    );

    -- Sub-agents spawned by this assistant
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sub_agents (
      id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      thread_id   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- thread in the parent project
      project_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
      status      TEXT DEFAULT 'running', -- running|complete|failed
      task        TEXT NOT NULL,   -- original task description
      result      TEXT,            -- JSON result when complete
      spawned_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
      completed_at INTEGER
    );

    -- Self-modification log (skill additions, tool changes)
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS modification_log (
      id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
      type        TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'skill_added'|'skill_updated'|'workflow_created'|'tool_added'
      target      TEXT NOT NULL, -- skill name or workflow name
      description TEXT NOT NULL,
      r2_path     TEXT,          -- path in R2 where the new code was written
      created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
    );

    -- Permission manifest (what the assistant is allowed to do)
    -- Stored in DO SQLite, NOT R2 — prevents skill code from modifying permissions
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS permissions (
      permission  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      granted     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
      granted_by  TEXT,           -- userId of admin who granted this
      granted_at  INTEGER
    );

    -- Active fibers (background tasks running via runFiber())
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fibers (
      id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      name       TEXT NOT NULL,
      status     TEXT DEFAULT 'running',
      snapshot   TEXT,
      created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
    );
  `);

  // Initialize default permissions (all denied until admin grants)
  const defaultPermissions = [
    'manage_members', 'manage_projects', 'view_billing',
    'create_agents', 'approve_resources', 'manage_workflows'
  ];
  for (const perm of defaultPermissions) {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO permissions (permission, granted) VALUES (?, 0)`, perm
    );
  }
}

The Heartbeat — Replacing OpenClaw's Continuous Loop

OpenClaw runs a continuous while True loop on local hardware. On Cloudflare, we cannot do this — a Worker cannot run forever. Instead, we use a CF Cron Trigger to wake the AssistantDO every 5 minutes. The heartbeat checks: Are there scheduled tasks to run? Are there pending sub-agent results? Are there new channel messages to process? This approach costs essentially zero when idle (cron triggers are free up to 5/worker/day limit, then negligible).

// workers/sweeper/index.ts
// This runs every 5 minutes via CF Cron Trigger
// Wakes ALL active assistants to process their heartbeat

export default {
  async scheduled(event: ScheduledEvent, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    // Get all active product root space IDs from KV (PRODUCT_DB_REGISTRY)
    // 'active' = created in the last 7 days OR has had channel activity in last 30 days
    const activeAssistants = await getActiveAssistants(env);
    
    // Wake each AssistantDO for heartbeat check
    // We use Promise.allSettled so a single DO failure doesn't block others
    await Promise.allSettled(
      activeAssistants.map(async ({ spaceId, userId }) => {
        const doId = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(
          `assistant:${spaceId}:${userId}`
        );
        const assistantDO = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.get(doId);
        
        try {
          await assistantDO.fetch(new Request('http://assistant/heartbeat', {
            method: 'POST',
            body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, userId, timestamp: Date.now() })
          }));
        } catch (e) {
          // Log but don't throw — other assistants must still get their heartbeat
          console.error(`[NAELAO] Heartbeat failed for ${spaceId}:${userId}`, e);
        }
      })
    );
  }
}

// durable-objects/assistant-do.ts — heartbeat handler
async handleHeartbeat(): Promise<void> {
  // 1. Load cron-jobs.json from R2
  const cronObj = await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(
    `spaces/${this.spaceId}/assistants/${this.userId}/cron-jobs.json`
  );
  
  if (cronObj) {
    const cronJobs: CronJob[] = JSON.parse(await cronObj.text());
    const now = Date.now();
    
    for (const job of cronJobs) {
      if (this.shouldRunJob(job, now)) {
        // Run job as a fiber so it doesn't block the heartbeat
        void this.runFiber(`cron-${job.id}-${now}`, async (ctx) => {
          await this.executeJob(job, ctx);
        });
      }
    }
  }

  // 2. Check for completed sub-agents
  const runningSubAgents = this.ctx.storage.sql
    .exec(`SELECT id, thread_id, project_id FROM sub_agents WHERE status = 'running'`)
    .toArray();
  
  for (const sa of runningSubAgents) {
    await this.checkSubAgentStatus(sa.id as string, sa.thread_id as string);
  }

  // 3. Update last heartbeat timestamp
  await this.ctx.storage.put('last_heartbeat', Date.now());
}

cron-jobs.json — The Task Schedule

This file lives in R2 and is the assistant's schedule of recurring tasks. The assistant can read it, modify it, add new jobs, and remove completed ones. Humans can also edit it via the UI. The format must be strict — the heartbeat parser is not forgiving.

// R2 path: spaces/{spaceId}/assistants/{userId}/cron-jobs.json
// The assistant reads this on every heartbeat to decide what to run.
{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "id": "daily-standup",
      "schedule": "0 9 * * 1-5",      // cron expression: 9am Mon-Fri
      "task": "Generate a standup summary of all active projects and post to Slack",
      "channel": "slack",              // where to post the result
      "enabled": true,
      "lastRun": null,                 // ISO timestamp, null if never run
      "nextRun": "2026-05-12T09:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "weekly-report",
      "schedule": "0 18 * * 5",       // 6pm Friday
      "task": "Create a weekly progress report for the team and send via email",
      "channel": "email",
      "enabled": true,
      "lastRun": null,
      "nextRun": "2026-05-10T18:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "version": "1.0",
  "updatedBy": "assistant",           // 'assistant' or 'user'
  "updatedAt": "2026-05-07T10:00:00Z"
}
⚠ Junior Dev Trap: cron-jobs.json Parsing

The heartbeat fires every 5 minutes. Do NOT parse cron expressions in the heartbeat handler using a heavy library — the Worker has a 10ms CPU limit per heartbeat invocation. Use a lightweight cron parser that pre-computes the next run time and stores it in the JSON. When the heartbeat fires, it only needs to check if nextRun <= now. After running, update lastRun and compute the next nextRun. Never re-parse the cron expression on every heartbeat.

Self-Modification — How the Assistant Updates Its Own Skills

OpenClaw can modify its own code. For Naelao, we give the assistant two self-modification pathways: (1) skill folder updates in R2, and (2) Dynamic Worker Loader deployment for new tool isolates. We deliberately do NOT give it access to Worker TypeScript source code — that would require a CF deployment and could break the platform. The assistant modifies its capabilities, not its runtime.

// durable-objects/assistant-do.ts — self-modification via skill update

async addSkill(skillDefinition: {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  instructions: string;
  scripts?: { id: string; type: string; code: string }[];
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; skillPath: string }> {
  
  // Validate skill name — only lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens
  if (!/^[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(skillDefinition.name)) {
    throw new Error('Skill name must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only');
  }

  const skillPath = `spaces/${this.spaceId}/assistants/${this.userId}/skills/${skillDefinition.name}`;

  // Write SKILL.md to R2
  const skillMd = this.generateSkillMd(skillDefinition);
  
  // SECURITY: Run skill through scanner BEFORE writing to R2
  // The scanner checks for dangerous patterns (process.env access, eval, etc.)
  // See §19 Security for the full 27-pattern list
  const scanResult = await this.env.NAELAO_SECURITY.scan(skillMd);
  if (!scanResult.safe) {
    throw new Error(`Skill rejected by security scanner: ${scanResult.reason}`);
  }

  await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(`${skillPath}/SKILL.md`, skillMd);

  // Write scripts to R2 if provided
  if (skillDefinition.scripts) {
    for (const script of skillDefinition.scripts) {
      const scriptScan = await this.env.NAELAO_SECURITY.scan(script.code);
      if (!scriptScan.safe) {
        throw new Error(`Script '${script.id}' rejected: ${scriptScan.reason}`);
      }
      await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
        `${skillPath}/scripts/${script.id}.ts`, script.code
      );
    }
  }

  // Log the self-modification
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `INSERT INTO modification_log (type, target, description, r2_path) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    'skill_added', skillDefinition.name, skillDefinition.description, skillPath
  );

  // Invalidate the skill cache so next agent run picks up the new skill
  await this.ctx.storage.delete('skills_cache');

  return { success: true, skillPath };
}

// Deploy a new tool as a Dynamic Worker Loader isolate
// The assistant writes TypeScript code, which is loaded into a V8 isolate on demand.
// This does NOT require a CF deployment — it loads at runtime.
async addDynamicTool(toolDefinition: {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  code: string;          // TypeScript that runs in a Dynamic Worker isolate
  parameters: JSONSchema;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; toolUrl: string }> {
  
  // Security scan the tool code
  const scan = await this.env.NAELAO_SECURITY.scan(toolDefinition.code);
  if (!scan.safe) throw new Error(`Tool code rejected: ${scan.reason}`);

  // Store in R2
  const toolPath = `spaces/${this.spaceId}/assistants/${this.userId}/dynamic-tools/${toolDefinition.name}.ts`;
  await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(toolPath, toolDefinition.code);

  // Register in SkillRegistryDO so it's available in next agent turn
  const registryDO = this.env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.get(
    this.env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.idFromName(`skills:${this.spaceId}:assistant-${this.userId}`)
  );
  await registryDO.fetch(new Request('http://registry/register-dynamic', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      name: toolDefinition.name,
      description: toolDefinition.description,
      r2Path: toolPath,
      parameters: toolDefinition.parameters
    })
  }));

  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `INSERT INTO modification_log (type, target, description, r2_path) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    'tool_added', toolDefinition.name, toolDefinition.description, toolPath
  );

  return { success: true, toolUrl: toolPath };
}

Sub-Agent Spawning

The Space Assistant can spawn NaelaoAgentDO instances from the Space marketplace or build custom ones. This is how it handles tasks that are too large for its own context window or that require parallel execution.

// durable-objects/assistant-do.ts — sub-agent spawning

async spawnSubAgent(task: {
  agentDefinitionId: string;  // from Space marketplace, or 'custom'
  taskDescription: string;
  projectId: string;
  customDefinition?: AgentDefinition; // if agentDefinitionId === 'custom'
}): Promise<{ subAgentId: string; threadId: string }> {
  
  // Create a new thread in the project for this sub-agent
  const threadId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const subAgentId = crypto.randomUUID();

  // Dispatch the agent run via naelao-agents Worker
  // The sub-agent runs as a background fiber (always background mode)
  await this.env.NAELAO_AGENTS.fetch(new Request('http://agents/spawn', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      spaceId: this.spaceId,
      projectId: task.projectId,
      threadId,
      agentDefinitionId: task.agentDefinitionId,
      customDefinition: task.customDefinition,
      input: task.taskDescription,
      backgroundMode: true,
      parentAssistantId: `${this.spaceId}:${this.userId}` // for result callback
    })
  }));

  // Track the sub-agent in SQLite
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `INSERT INTO sub_agents (id, thread_id, project_id, task) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    subAgentId, threadId, task.projectId, task.taskDescription
  );

  return { subAgentId, threadId };
}

// Called by sweeper when checking sub-agent status
async checkSubAgentStatus(subAgentId: string, threadId: string): Promise<void> {
  // Get the AgentDO for this thread and check its fiber status
  const agentDoId = this.env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(
    `${this.spaceId}:${threadId}`
  );
  const agentDO = this.env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get(agentDoId);
  
  const statusResp = await agentDO.fetch(new Request('http://agent/status'));
  const status = await statusResp.json() as { status: string; result?: unknown };
  
  if (status.status === 'complete') {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `UPDATE sub_agents SET status = 'complete', result = ?, completed_at = ? WHERE id = ?`,
      JSON.stringify(status.result), Date.now(), subAgentId
    );
    
    // Notify the assistant so it can incorporate the result into its context
    void this.runFiber(`sub-agent-result-${subAgentId}`, async (ctx) => {
      await this.processSubAgentResult(subAgentId, status.result);
    });
  }
}

Channel Integrations

Slack, Discord, and Telegram all work through webhooks. The assistant registers webhook endpoints with each platform. When a message arrives, it hits the naelao-router, which routes it to the AssistantDO via the naelao-notifications Worker. The assistant processes it and sends a reply back through the same channel.

// Setting up Slack integration — full flow

// 1. User configures Slack in Space Settings UI
// 2. Frontend calls: POST /api/spaces/{spaceId}/assistants/{userId}/channels
// 3. naelao-assistant Worker stores config in AssistantDO channels table
// 4. naelao-assistant Worker registers a webhook URL with Slack:
//    https://app.naelao.dev/webhooks/slack/{spaceId}/{userId}/{token}

// Incoming Slack message hits naelao-router:
// POST /webhooks/slack/{spaceId}/{userId}/{token}
async handleSlackWebhook(request: Request, params: WebhookParams): Promise<Response> {
  const body = await request.json() as SlackEvent;
  
  // Verify Slack signature (REQUIRED — without this, anyone can send fake messages)
  const signature = request.headers.get('X-Slack-Signature') ?? '';
  const timestamp = request.headers.get('X-Slack-Request-Timestamp') ?? '';
  const isValid = await verifySlackSignature(signature, timestamp, await request.text(), params.token);
  if (!isValid) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
  
  // Handle Slack URL verification challenge (sent on webhook registration)
  if (body.type === 'url_verification') {
    return Response.json({ challenge: body.challenge });
  }
  
  // Route message to AssistantDO
  const doId = this.env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(
    `assistant:${params.spaceId}:${params.userId}`
  );
  const assistantDO = this.env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.get(doId);
  
  // Process asynchronously — Slack requires response within 3 seconds
  this.ctx.waitUntil(
    assistantDO.fetch(new Request('http://assistant/channel-message', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        channel: 'slack',
        messageText: body.event?.text ?? '',
        channelMeta: {
          channelId: body.event?.channel,
          authorId: body.event?.user,
          ts: body.event?.ts
        }
      })
    }))
  );
  
  return new Response('', { status: 200 }); // Acknowledge immediately
}

// AssistantDO processes channel message and sends reply
async handleChannelMessage(channel: string, text: string, meta: ChannelMeta): Promise<void> {
  // Create or find the channel session
  let sessionId = this.ctx.storage.sql
    .exec(`SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE channel = ?`, channel)
    .one()?.id as string | null;
  
  if (!sessionId) {
    sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `INSERT INTO sessions (id, channel) VALUES (?, ?)`, sessionId, channel
    );
  }

  // Add user message to session
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, role, content, channel_meta) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    crypto.randomUUID(), sessionId, 'user', text, JSON.stringify(meta)
  );

  // Run agent loop in a fiber (so heartbeat isn't blocked)
  void this.runFiber(`channel-response-${Date.now()}`, async (ctx) => {
    const response = await this.executeAgentLoop(sessionId!, null, ctx);
    
    // Send response back to the channel
    await this.sendToChannel(channel, response, meta);
  });
}

Assistant Configuration Spec

Default count
1 per user per Space. Space admin can raise this limit in Space Settings → Assistants → Max per user. Maximum 5 per user per Space.
Container model
On-demand CF Container (standard-1: ½ vCPU, 4 GiB RAM). Starts only when a task needs Linux execution. Default idle timeout: 30 minutes. Warm on wakeup from heartbeat: <3s.
R2 filesystem path
spaces/{spaceId}/assistants/{userId}/ mounted at /data/assistant when container starts. Contains: memory.json (deprecated, replaced by DO SQLite), skills/, cron-jobs.json, channel-configs/, dynamic-tools/
Heartbeat frequency
Every 5 minutes via naelao-sweeper cron trigger. Checks: cron-jobs.json, sub-agent status, pending channel messages, DO alarm wakeups.
Memory storage
Typed JSON in AssistantDO SQLite memory table. Key+category primary key. Schema-validated on write. Never flat Markdown. Injected into system prompt as structured XML on each turn.
Permission manifest
Stored in AssistantDO SQLite permissions table. NOT in R2 — prevents skill code from modifying its own permissions. Default: all permissions denied. Admin grants via Space Admin Dashboard.
Self-modification scope
Can write/update: skills in R2, cron-jobs.json, dynamic-tools (via Dynamic Worker Loader). Cannot modify: Worker source code, wrangler.jsonc, SpaceDO schema, other users' data, permission manifest.

Space Assistants — OpenClaw + CF Thinker + Memory OS

Space Assistants represent the complete integration of OpenClaw-style proactive agency, the CF Thinker (Execution Ladder) resource-budget model, product-level multi-tenant Spaces, and a custom Cloudflare-native implementation of Memory OS — the state-of-the-art 6-layer memory stack designed for Hermes Agent.

"By running on top of Cloudflare's serverless edge, a Space Assistant preserves continuous 24/7 existence, self-modifies its capabilities, and utilizes an air-gapped 6-layer Memory OS — with an idle cost of virtually zero."

Architecture Overview: The Four Pillars

Pillar 1
OpenClaw Proactive Core

Clones OpenClaw's continuous loop paradigm. Uses CF Cron triggers to fire a 5-minute heartbeat check. Automatically executes scheduled actions via cron-jobs.json, monitors webhooks, manages Slack/Discord integrations, and spawns sub-agents dynamically.

Pillar 2
CF Thinker Execution Ladder

Ensures that proactive heartbeats and memory lookups do not create high billing overhead. Simple tasks stay in Tier 1 (R2 direct) or Tier 2 (Isolate). The assistant only boots a Tier 5 container sandbox on demand for heavy bash/Python scripts.

Pillar 3
Spaces Tenant Isolation

Strictly isolated across 6 security layers. A user's personal Space Assistant cannot escape the parent space. It writes to the product's centralized SpaceDO SQLite database, with all queries bound by space_id columns to prevent cross-sub-space leakage.

Pillar 4
6-Layer Memory OS

Claudio Drews' Memory OS mapped to CF primitives. Synthesizes Workspace files, Session history, Structured Facts with trust scores, Fabric cross-session summaries, hybrid Vectorize search, and an auto-curated LLM Wiki in a closed loop.

The 6-Layer Memory OS Pipeline

The standard memory storage in agents often relies on unstructured vector database dumps. Memory OS resolves this retrieval gap by establishing six independent local layers of context, coordinated by the AssistantDO's built-in SQLite database and the Space's R2 bucket:

Layer Name Cloudflare Primitive Description & Retrieval Logic
Layer 1 Workspace R2 Workspace Holds active text reference blocks (MEMORY.md, USER.md, CREATIVE.md). Injected as static prefixes inside the system prompt to maximize CF AI Gateway prompt caching.
Layer 2 Sessions DO SQLite state.db Provides high-speed, local session history. Fully indexed via SQLite FTS5 (messages_fts) for instantaneous, zero-latency full-text search across thread histories.
Layer 3 Structured Facts DO SQLite memory_store.db Stores durable semantic triples (Entity-Relation-Attribute) with trust scores and decay rates. Merges identical entities using a Jaro-Winkler comparison script executed at the Isolate tier.
Layer 4 Fabric DO SQLite + R2 Cross-session context consolidator based on the Icarus framework. Runs LLM-driven session extraction post-run and exposes tools such as fabric_recall and fabric_brief to summarize work.
Layer 5 Vector Database CF Vectorize + BM25 Semantic memory search using 768d cosine vectors. Combined with BM25 sparse search implemented as an Isolate-tier tool to yield a low-latency Hybrid Retrieval system.
Layer 6 LLM Wiki R2 + Vectorize Auto-curated concept and entity vault. An async background process (wiki-continuous-ingest) runs on session end to structure new learnings into wiki articles, which are re-indexed into Layer 5.
