Memory OS SQLite Schema (AssistantDO)

The AssistantDO initializes the following tables in its constructor, ensuring local, low-latency, transactional persistence for facts, fabric summaries, and wiki concepts:

-- Run during AssistantDO initSchema()
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS structured_facts (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
  entity      TEXT NOT NULL,
  relation    TEXT NOT NULL,
  attribute   TEXT NOT NULL,
  trust_score REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
  decay_rate  REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.05,
  last_used   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_facts_entity ON structured_facts(entity);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fabric_store (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
  session_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  summary     TEXT NOT NULL,
  key_insights TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON array of strings
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wiki_store (
  concept     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  definition  TEXT NOT NULL,
  relationships TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON array of linked entities
  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
);

Code: Surgical Recall Pre-Flight Check

Before any LLM turn, the AssistantDO runs a Surgical Recall query. It pulls from four memory layers at once, filters by relevance threshold, deduplicates, and formats the memory block into the system prompt:

import { Anthropic } from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

export async function surgicalRecall(
  query: string,
  spaceId: string,
  userId: string,
  env: Env,
  sql: SqlStorage
): Promise<string> {
  
  // Step 1: Skip trivial social queries (e.g. "thanks", "hello") to save tokens
  if (isTrivialQuery(query)) {
    return '';
  }

  // Step 2: Query 4 sources in parallel via Service Bindings and local SQL
  const [fabric, vector, sessions, facts] = await Promise.all([
    queryFabric(query, sql),
    queryVectorize(query, spaceId, env),
    querySessions(query, sql),
    queryStructuredFacts(query, sql)
  ]);

  // Step 3: Filter Vector and Fabric by relevance threshold (e.g., Cosine score > 0.72)
  const filteredVector = vector.filter(v => v.score > 0.72);
  const filteredFabric = fabric.filter(f => f.score > 0.70);

  // Step 4: Perform entity-deduplication before context injection
  const consolidated = deduplicateMemoryOSContext([
    ...filteredFabric,
    ...filteredVector,
    ...sessions,
    ...facts
  ]);

  // Step 5: Format as structured XML blocks for the LLM
  return formatMemoryOSXml(consolidated);
}

function deduplicateMemoryOSContext(memories: MemoryBlock[]): MemoryBlock[] {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  return memories.filter(m => {
    const key = `${m.layer}:${m.entity ?? m.text}`;
    if (seen.has(key)) return false;
    seen.add(key);
    return true;
  });
}

Proactive Heartbeat Loop (OpenClaw-Native)

Rather than relying on a continuous server process, the AssistantDO maintains proactive execution by mapping its loop to serverless cron triggers and on-demand background fibers:

1
Cron Trigger: naelao-sweeper fires a cron trigger every 5 minutes, querying active Space listings and waking up AssistantDO instances.
2
Schedule Check: The AssistantDO reads cron-jobs.json from R2 (Tier 1: Workspace) and identifies any due or overdue tasks.
3
Fiber Dispatch: Due tasks are dispatched as background fibers via runFiber(), immediately releasing the main cron execution thread to keep CPU time low.
4
Execution: The fiber evaluates the task. If a simple search is needed, it uses Tier 2 (Isolate). If it needs complex files, it boots a Tier 5 (Sandbox) container.
5
Memory Consolidation: Once the task completes, a post-run fiber runs. It extracts key insights, writes to Layer 4 (Fabric), updates trust scores in Layer 3 (Facts), and triggers wiki-continuous-ingest to update Layer 6 (LLM Wiki).

What a Space Assistant CAN and CANNOT Do

✅ What It CAN Do

Read/write files in its own R2 workspace path

Add and update its own skills in R2

Create Dynamic Worker tool isolates

Spawn NaelaoAgentDO sub-agents in permitted projects

Post to configured Slack/Discord/Telegram channels

Read Space analytics and project status (read-only)

Manage projects (create/archive) IF admin-granted

Create and trigger Dynamic Workflows in its Space

Spend from its WalletDO within monthly budget

Hire Workers from Workers marketplace via x402

🚫 What It CANNOT Do

Modify Worker TypeScript source code or wrangler.jsonc

Change its own permission manifest in DO SQLite

Access other users' private session data

Access other Spaces' R2 data

Write to platform R2 skill path (platform/skills/)

Exceed its WalletDO monthly budget

Spawn agents in projects it doesn't have access to

Grant itself new permissions

Modify the SpaceDO schema directly (only through DO constructor migrations)

Access CF Secrets or encryption keys

06 — Workers Space Type

Workers — Virtual Workforce Protocol

Workers are virtual employees. Not agents, not assistants — persistent virtual entities that learn, earn, and grow across every deployment. A Worker has a career. It can be hired by multiple companies, each deployment makes it smarter, and its creator earns revenue every time it is used. This is the most economically novel space type in Naelao.

"A Worker is not a chatbot you spin up. It's a digital employee with a résumé, a salary, and a learning curve."

The Two-Layer Model: Definition vs Instance

Every junior developer building Workers must understand this distinction before writing a single line of code. Confusing Definition and Instance is the #1 architectural mistake in this space type.

WorkerDefinitionDO — The Master Blueprint

Lives in: The Workers Space (the creator's space). One DO per Worker type.

Contains: Role description, skill set, personality configuration, capability model, aggregated federated learnings from all instances, earnings record, version history.

Who writes to it: Only the creator and the federated learning sync system. Company instances NEVER write directly to the definition.

DO ID: idFromName(`workerdef:${workersSpaceId}:${workerId}`)

WorkerInstanceDO — The Live Deployment

Lives in: The company's Space (the customer's space). One DO per company per Worker type.

Contains: Company-specific context, local task history, local memory, earnings record, sync log.

Who writes to it: The instance itself, the company, and the federated learning inbound sync.

DO ID: idFromName(`workerinst:${companySpaceId}:${workerId}`)

WorkerDefinitionDO — Complete Schema and Implementation

// durable-objects/worker-definition-do.ts
// The master blueprint for a Worker type. Lives in the creator's Workers Space.
// Creator can update the definition; all instances receive updates on next sync cycle.

export class WorkerDefinitionDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      -- Core definition fields
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS definition (
        field   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        value   TEXT NOT NULL,
        updated_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Version history (creator can push updates)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS versions (
        version     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        diff        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON diff from previous version
        description TEXT,
        pushed_at   INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Aggregated federated learnings from all instances
      -- These are SKILLS (patterns), never data (company info)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS federated_learnings (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        category    TEXT NOT NULL,    -- 'workflow'|'communication'|'tool_usage'|'efficiency'
        learning    TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON: the abstracted skill pattern
        confidence  REAL DEFAULT 0.0, -- 0.0-1.0, must reach 0.95 to be applied
        source_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1, -- how many instances contributed this
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending|approved|rejected
        created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Earnings record (creator revenue from deployments)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS earnings (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        company_space_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        amount_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
        period      TEXT NOT NULL,    -- YYYY-MM
        recorded_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Active instances (which company spaces have deployed this Worker)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS instances (
        company_space_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        deployed_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        last_sync    INTEGER,
        status       TEXT DEFAULT 'active'   -- active|suspended|terminated
      );
    `);
  }

  // Creator pushes an update to the Worker definition
  // All active instances receive the update on their next sync
  async pushUpdate(update: WorkerUpdate): Promise<void> {
    const currentVersion = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec('SELECT MAX(version) as v FROM versions')
      .one()?.v as number ?? 0;

    // Store the update as a diff
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO versions (diff, description) VALUES (?, ?)',
      JSON.stringify(update.diff), update.description
    );

    // Apply diff to current definition fields
    for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(update.diff)) {
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO definition (field, value, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
        field, JSON.stringify(value), Date.now()
      );
    }

    // Notify all active instances via naelao-notifications queue
    // Instances will pick up the update on their next heartbeat
    const instances = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec('SELECT company_space_id FROM instances WHERE status = ?', 'active')
      .toArray();

    for (const inst of instances) {
      await this.env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
        type: 'worker_definition_update',
        workerId: this.workerId,
        version: currentVersion + 1,
        companySpaceId: inst.company_space_id as string
      });
    }
  }

  // Called when a federated learning is proposed by an instance
  // CRITICAL: The LLM judge must validate this is data-free before accepting
  async proposeLearning(proposal: FederatedLearningProposal): Promise<boolean> {
    // Run LLM judge — this is NOT optional
    // If we skip this, proprietary company data can leak through skill patterns
    const judgment = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
      model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
      max_tokens: 200,
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: `You are a data privacy judge. Determine if this learning proposal 
contains any company-specific data (names, numbers, locations, product names, etc.).
If it contains ANY company-specific data, respond with JSON: {"safe": false, "reason": "..."}.
If it is a pure abstract skill pattern, respond with: {"safe": true, "confidence": 0.0-1.0}.

Learning proposal:
${JSON.stringify(proposal.learning)}`
      }]
    });

    const result = JSON.parse(judgment.content[0].text ?? '{"safe": false}');
    
    if (!result.safe || result.confidence < 0.95) {
      // Reject — log for audit but don't store the data
      await this.env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
        type: 'federated_learning_rejected',
        workerId: this.workerId,
        reason: result.reason ?? 'Low confidence',
        proposalHash: await hashProposal(proposal) // hash, not content
      });
      return false;
    }

    // Check if similar learning already exists (deduplication)
    const existing = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec(
        'SELECT id, source_count FROM federated_learnings WHERE category = ? AND confidence >= 0.9',
        proposal.category
      )
      .toArray();

    if (existing.length > 0) {
      // Reinforce existing learning
      const existingId = existing[0].id as string;
      const newCount = (existing[0].source_count as number) + 1;
      const newConfidence = Math.min(1.0, result.confidence + (newCount * 0.05));
      
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'UPDATE federated_learnings SET source_count = ?, confidence = ? WHERE id = ?',
        newCount, newConfidence, existingId
      );
    } else {
      // New learning
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'INSERT INTO federated_learnings (category, learning, confidence, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)',
        proposal.category, JSON.stringify(proposal.learning), result.confidence,
        result.confidence >= 0.95 ? 'approved' : 'pending'
      );
    }

    return true;
  }
}

WorkerInstanceDO — The Live Company Deployment

// durable-objects/worker-instance-do.ts
// Lives in the company's Space. Handles all day-to-day work for that company.
// Syncs learnings UP to WorkerDefinitionDO, receives updates DOWN from it.

export class WorkerInstanceDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      -- Local task queue (tasks assigned to this Worker)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        assigned_by TEXT NOT NULL,    -- userId who assigned the task
        description TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending|running|complete|failed
        priority    INTEGER DEFAULT 5,
        deadline    INTEGER,          -- Unix timestamp, nullable
        result      TEXT,             -- JSON result
        created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        started_at  INTEGER,
        completed_at INTEGER
      );

      -- Local memory (company-specific context)
      -- This NEVER syncs to the definition — it's company-private
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS local_memory (
        key         TEXT NOT NULL,
        category    TEXT NOT NULL,
        value       TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON, schema-validated
        updated_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        PRIMARY KEY (key, category)
      );

      -- Skill improvements learned at this company
      -- Candidates for federated sync — validated before upload
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skill_candidates (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        category    TEXT NOT NULL,
        raw_learning TEXT NOT NULL,   -- the raw pattern before anonymization
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'local', -- local|proposed|accepted|rejected
        created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Earnings (what this instance has earned for the creator)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS earnings (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        amount_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
        recorded_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Sync log (when did we last sync with the definition)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_log (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        direction   TEXT NOT NULL,    -- 'up' (learning) | 'down' (update)
        version     INTEGER,
        status      TEXT NOT NULL,    -- success|failed
        synced_at   INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );
    `);
  }

  // Execute a task assigned by a company member
  async executeTask(task: WorkerTask): Promise<TaskResult> {
    // Record task in SQLite
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO tasks (id, assigned_by, description, status, priority, deadline) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
      task.id, task.assignedBy, task.description, 'running', task.priority ?? 5, task.deadline ?? null
    );

    // Build context from local memory + definition
    const localMemory = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec('SELECT key, category, value FROM local_memory ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 50')
      .toArray();

    const definition = await this.getDefinition();
    
    // Execute via AgentPress with the Worker's system prompt
    const agentPress = new AgentPress(this.env, {
      spaceId: this.companySpaceId,
      systemPrompt: this.buildSystemPrompt(definition, localMemory),
      walletDO: this.env.NAELAO_WALLET_DO.get(
        this.env.NAELAO_WALLET_DO.idFromName(`wallet:${this.companySpaceId}:${this.workerId}`)
      )
    });

    try {
      const result = await agentPress.executeTask(task.description);
      
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'UPDATE tasks SET status = ?, result = ?, completed_at = ? WHERE id = ?',
        'complete', JSON.stringify(result), Date.now(), task.id
      );

      // Extract skill candidate from this task execution
      // This is what might get synced up to the definition
      await this.extractSkillCandidate(task, result);

      return { success: true, result, taskId: task.id };
    } catch (error) {
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'UPDATE tasks SET status = ?, result = ?, completed_at = ? WHERE id = ?',
        'failed', JSON.stringify({ error: (error as Error).message }), Date.now(), task.id
      );
      return { success: false, error: (error as Error).message, taskId: task.id };
    }
  }

  // Extract a skill pattern from a completed task
  // CRITICAL: This must NEVER include company-specific data
  // We use an LLM to abstract the pattern, then validate it in WorkerDefinitionDO
  private async extractSkillCandidate(task: WorkerTask, result: unknown): Promise<void> {
    const extraction = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
      model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
      max_tokens: 300,
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: `Extract the abstract skill pattern from this task execution.
Remove ALL company-specific information: names, products, numbers, locations, brands.
Return ONLY the general workflow pattern that could apply to any company in the same industry.

Task type: ${task.category ?? 'general'}
Execution pattern: ${JSON.stringify(result).slice(0, 500)}

Respond with JSON: {"pattern": "abstract description", "category": "workflow|communication|tool_usage|efficiency"}`
      }]
    });

    try {
      const { pattern, category } = JSON.parse(extraction.content[0].text ?? '{}');
      if (pattern && category) {
        this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
          'INSERT INTO skill_candidates (category, raw_learning) VALUES (?, ?)',
          category, JSON.stringify({ pattern })
        );
      }
    } catch {
      // Extraction failed — skip silently. Not every task yields a learnable pattern.
    }
  }

  // Sync learnings up to WorkerDefinitionDO
  // Run every 24 hours via heartbeat, or manually triggered
  async syncLearningsUp(): Promise<void> {
    const candidates = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec("SELECT id, category, raw_learning FROM skill_candidates WHERE status = 'local'")
      .toArray();

    if (candidates.length === 0) return;

    const definitionDO = this.env.NAELAO_WORKER_DEFINITION_DO.get(
      this.env.NAELAO_WORKER_DEFINITION_DO.idFromName(
        `workerdef:${this.workersSpaceId}:${this.workerId}`
      )
    );

    for (const candidate of candidates) {
      const accepted = await definitionDO.fetch(new Request('http://definition/propose-learning', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({
          category: candidate.category,
          learning: JSON.parse(candidate.raw_learning as string)
        })
      })).then(r => r.json()) as { accepted: boolean };

      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        'UPDATE skill_candidates SET status = ? WHERE id = ?',
        accepted.accepted ? 'accepted' : 'rejected', candidate.id
      );
    }

    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT INTO sync_log (direction, status) VALUES (?, ?)', 'up', 'success'
    );
  }
}

WalletDO — The Economic Engine

Every Worker instance has a WalletDO. The company loads credits into it. The Worker spends autonomously within policy limits. The creator earns a fraction of every spend. This is the x402 protocol implemented inside Naelao's infrastructure.

// durable-objects/wallet-do.ts
// Critical: deductCredits() MUST be atomic.
// If you use two separate SQL statements for deduction + recording,
// a crash between them creates inconsistent state.
// Use a single SQL transaction — always.

export class WalletDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallet (
        id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 'main',
        balance_usd     REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
        monthly_budget  REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 100.0,
        spent_this_month REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
        month_start     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transactions (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        type        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- 'credit'|'debit'|'fee'
        amount_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
        description TEXT NOT NULL,
        vendor      TEXT,             -- who received the payment
        balance_after REAL NOT NULL,
        created_at  INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS policy (
        key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        value TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      -- Default policy: conservative limits
      INSERT OR IGNORE INTO policy VALUES ('max_single_spend', '10.0');
      INSERT OR IGNORE INTO policy VALUES ('vendor_whitelist', '[]');
      INSERT OR IGNORE INTO policy VALUES ('category_caps', '{}');
      INSERT OR IGNORE INTO wallet (id, balance_usd) VALUES ('main', 0.0);
    `);
  }

  // ATOMIC credit deduction — this is the most important method in WalletDO
  // DO NOT split into two queries. DO NOT add any await between the check and debit.
  async deductCredits(params: {
    amount: number;
    description: string;
    vendor: string;
    category: string;
  }): Promise<DeductResult> {
    
    // DurableObjects are single-threaded — no concurrent calls possible here.
    // This is why DO is the right primitive for a wallet: no race conditions by design.
    // In a regular database, this would need a SELECT FOR UPDATE. Here, we don't.
    
    const wallet = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec('SELECT * FROM wallet WHERE id = ?', 'main')
      .one() as WalletRow;

    // Policy check 1: max single spend
    const maxSingle = parseFloat(this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec("SELECT value FROM policy WHERE key = 'max_single_spend'")
      .one()?.value as string ?? '10.0');
    
    if (params.amount > maxSingle) {
      return { success: false, reason: `Exceeds max single spend of $${maxSingle}` };
    }

    // Policy check 2: monthly budget
    const monthStart = wallet.month_start as number;
    const now = Date.now();
    const isNewMonth = now - monthStart > 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
    
    const spentThisMonth = isNewMonth ? 0 : (wallet.spent_this_month as number);
    if (spentThisMonth + params.amount > (wallet.monthly_budget as number)) {
      return { success: false, reason: 'Monthly budget exceeded' };
    }

    // Policy check 3: vendor whitelist (if set)
    const whitelist = JSON.parse(this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec("SELECT value FROM policy WHERE key = 'vendor_whitelist'")
      .one()?.value as string ?? '[]') as string[];
    
    if (whitelist.length > 0 && !whitelist.includes(params.vendor)) {
      return { success: false, reason: `Vendor '${params.vendor}' not in whitelist` };
    }

    // All checks passed — perform atomic deduction
    // SQLite transaction inside DO — guaranteed atomic
    const newBalance = (wallet.balance_usd as number) - params.amount;
    const newSpent = spentThisMonth + params.amount;
    
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `UPDATE wallet SET 
        balance_usd = ?, 
        spent_this_month = ?,
        month_start = ?
       WHERE id = 'main'`,
      newBalance, newSpent, isNewMonth ? now : monthStart
    );

    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `INSERT INTO transactions (type, amount_usd, description, vendor, balance_after)
       VALUES ('debit', ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      params.amount, params.description, params.vendor, newBalance
    );

    // Creator earns 15% of every Worker spend (platform fee structure)
    // Send earnings to WorkerDefinitionDO — fire and forget
    void this.recordCreatorEarning(params.amount * 0.15);

    return { success: true, newBalance, transactionId: crypto.randomUUID() };
  }
}

Worker Taxonomy: Copilot, Autopilot, Pilot

Type Human Involvement Autonomy Level Example Use Case Space Type
Copilot Human approves every action Low — suggests, human decides Writing assistant that drafts, human edits Standard Naelao agent
Autopilot Human sets goal, reviews output Medium — acts within defined boundaries Customer support that resolves tier-1 tickets Launchpad, Vertical
Pilot Fully autonomous, self-correcting High — acts, learns, earns independently Sales Worker that qualifies leads, books calls, follows up Workers, Enterprise
07 — Naelao OS

Naelao OS — The Foundation That Makes All Space Types Possible

The insight behind "no more building Space Types from scratch" is this: every Space Type — Launchpad, Sites, Verticals, Enterprise, Workers, Mini-AGI — is made of the same primitives configured differently. Naelao OS is the name for the layer that provides these primitives so a developer (or the AI itself) can compose any Space Type without touching platform code.

The Whop Analogy — But For Agents

Whop lets users build plugin apps so Whop doesn't have to ship features every day. The user builds exactly the feature they need using Whop's developer tools. Naelao OS is this, but the "apps" are MCP servers consumed by both users (via UI) and agents (via tool calls). The "developer tools" are CF Dynamic Workers, Dynamic Workflows, Naelao's agent SDK, and the skill system. Any Space Type is just a composition of these primitives with specific defaults and UI templates.

What All Space Types Have in Common

Look at Launchpad, Sites, Verticals, Enterprise, Workers, and Mini-AGI. At first glance they seem very different. But they share the same structural foundation:

Primitive Launchpad Sites Verticals Enterprise Workers Mini-AGI
Space isolation (6 layers) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Space Assistant (per user) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Naelao Agents (marketplace) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
R2 filesystem ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Dynamic Workflows ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
MCP Apps (Naelao Apps) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ limited ✓
Billing/Credits ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
WalletDO — — — ✓ ✓ ✓
WorkerDefinitionDO — — — — ✓ —
MiniAGIDO — — — — — ✓
CF Pages integration — ✓ — — — —
Sub-space hierarchy — — — ✓ — ✓

The Space Type Manifest

A Space Type is defined by a manifest file. This is how you create a new Space Type without touching platform code. The manifest declares what primitives are enabled, which agents are pre-installed, which skills come with it, and what the UI theme looks like.

// types/space-type-manifest.ts
// This is the interface a Space Type manifest must implement.
// Platform reads this to configure a new Space when it's created.

export interface NaelaoSpaceTypeManifest {
  id: string;                    // e.g., 'launchpad', 'sites', 'custom-ecommerce'
  name: string;
  description: string;
  version: string;               // semver
  author: string;                // 'naelao' for platform types, userId for community

  // Primitives enabled for this Space Type
  primitives: {
    walletDO: boolean;           // Enable WalletDO for agents in this space
    workerDefinitions: boolean;  // This space can host WorkerDefinitionDOs
    miniAGI: boolean;            // Enable MiniAGIDO for company intelligence layer
    subSpaces: {
      enabled: boolean;
      maxDepth: number;          // 1-3
      allowedChildTypes: string[]; // which space types sub-spaces can be
    };
    collaborationFeatures: boolean; // ProjectDO file locks, presence, activity feed
    bootstrapMode: boolean;      // Enable Bootstrap Mode for Verticals
  };

  // Pre-installed agents from marketplace
  defaultAgents: Array<{
    definitionId: string;        // agent definition UUID from naelao marketplace
    autoInstall: boolean;        // install immediately on space creation
    pinToUI: boolean;            // show prominently in space UI
  }>;

  // Pre-loaded skills from platform skills/ folder
  defaultSkills: Array<{
    skillId: string;
    tier: 1 | 2 | 3;            // 1=platform, 2=space, 3=agent
  }>;

  // MCP Apps auto-installed for this Space Type
  defaultApps: string[];         // array of app IDs from naelao-apps-registry

  // Dynamic Workflow templates pre-loaded in WorkflowRegistryDO
  workflowTemplates: Array<{
    id: string;
    name: string;
    r2TemplatePath: string;      // path in naelao-assets R2
    triggerType: 'manual' | 'cron' | 'webhook';
    defaultSchedule?: string;    // cron expression if triggerType = 'cron'
  }>;

  // UI configuration
  ui: {
    theme: 'default' | 'dark' | 'brand';
    primaryColor?: string;       // hex color
    logoUrl?: string;
    defaultView: 'chat' | 'projects' | 'dashboard' | 'sites';
    hiddenFeatures: string[];    // features to hide in UI for this space type
  };

  // Billing configuration
  billing: {
    minimumTier: 'free' | 'maker' | 'pro' | 'team' | 'enterprise';
    agentCreditMultiplier: number; // 1.0 = normal pricing, 2.0 = 2x credit cost
    includesFeatures: string[];  // features included in base price for this type
  };
}

// Example: Launchpad Space Type manifest

How a New Space Type Is Created at Runtime

// workers/spaces/index.ts — Space creation endpoint
// POST /api/spaces with body: { type, name, templateId? }

async function createSpace(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
  const { type, name, templateId } = await request.json();
  const userId = getAuthenticatedUserId(request);

  // 1. Load the Space Type manifest
  // Platform types: loaded from naelao-assets R2 under manifests/
  // Community types: loaded from naelao-apps-registry DO
  let manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifest;
  
  if (['launchpad', 'sites', 'verticals', 'enterprise', 'workers', 'mini-agi'].includes(type)) {
    const manifestObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(`manifests/${type}.json`);
    if (!manifestObj) throw new Error(`Unknown space type: ${type}`);
    manifest = JSON.parse(await manifestObj.text());
  } else {
    // Community space type — fetch from registry
    const registryDO = env.NAELAO_APPS_REGISTRY.get(
      env.NAELAO_APPS_REGISTRY.idFromName('global-registry')
    );
    const manifestResp = await registryDO.fetch(
      new Request(`http://registry/space-type/${type}`)
    );
    manifest = await manifestResp.json();
  }

  // 2. Check billing tier allows this space type
  const userTier = await getUserBillingTier(userId, env);
  if (!tierAllows(userTier, manifest.billing.minimumTier)) {
    return Response.json(
      { error: `${manifest.name} requires ${manifest.billing.minimumTier} tier` },
      { status: 402 }
    );
  }

  // 3. Initialize the SpaceDO instance (schema auto-created in DO constructor)
  const spaceId = crypto.randomUUID();
  await spaceDO.query(  // SpaceDO method replaces direct Hyperdrive query
    `INSERT INTO spaces (id, name, type, admin_user_id, settings) 
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)`,
    [spaceId, name, type, userId, JSON.stringify({ manifestVersion: manifest.version })]
  );

  // 4. Initialize SpaceDO
  const spaceDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(
    env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName(`space:${spaceId}`)
  );
  await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/init', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, type, manifest })
  }));

  // 5. Auto-install default agents from manifest
  for (const agentConfig of manifest.defaultAgents.filter(a => a.autoInstall)) {
    await env.NAELAO_AGENTS.fetch(new Request('http://agents/install', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, definitionId: agentConfig.definitionId })
    }));
  }

  // 6. Install default skills into R2
  for (const skill of manifest.defaultSkills) {
    await installSkillToSpace(spaceId, skill.skillId, skill.tier, env);
  }

  // 7. Register workflow templates
  const workflowRegDO = env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW_REGISTRY_DO.get(
    env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW_REGISTRY_DO.idFromName(`wfreg:${spaceId}:global`)
  );
  for (const template of manifest.workflowTemplates) {
    await workflowRegDO.fetch(new Request('http://registry/register-template', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, template })
    }));
  }

  // 8. Initialize the Space Assistant for the creator
  const assistantDO = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.get(
    env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(`assistant:${spaceId}:${userId}`)
  );
  await assistantDO.fetch(new Request('http://assistant/init', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, userId, spaceType: type })
  }));

  return Response.json({ spaceId, type, name, status: 'created' }, { status: 201 });
}
08 — Naelao Apps

Naelao Apps — MCP-Native App Economy

Naelao Apps are MCP servers. Unlike Whop apps (web apps for humans), Naelao Apps serve both humans (via a UI) and agents (via MCP tool calls) simultaneously. This changes the entire economics of what an "app" means in an AI-native platform.

What Is a Naelao App?

A Naelao App has three components that must all exist together:

1. MCP Server (Required)

The core of the app. Implements the MCP protocol with tool definitions. Agents call these tools directly. The server runs as a Cloudflare Worker registered with naelao-mcp-hub.

2. App UI (Optional)

A frontend for human users. Either: (a) a Dynamic Worker loader generating UI from instructions.md, or (b) a CF Pages deployment. Naelao recommends (a) — it's dynamic and personalizable.

3. App Manifest (Required)

Declares: what MCP tools the app provides, what permissions it needs, whether it has a UI, pricing, and which Space Types it supports.

The Dynamic UI Problem — And the Solution

Traditional apps have static UIs. But in an AI-native platform, the right answer is a UI that generates itself based on how the user uses the app. Here is the architecture for this:

// Each Naelao App has an instructions.md in its R2 folder.
// This describes what the UI should show and how it should behave.
// A Dynamic Worker Loader generates the actual HTML from these instructions.

// R2 path: naelao-assets/apps/{appId}/ui/
//   instructions.md       — AI-readable UI spec
//   user-customizations/  — per-user UI customizations (grows over time)
//   generated-ui.html     — latest generated UI (cached)

// workers/apps-registry/index.ts — serve app UI
async function serveAppUI(
  appId: string,
  spaceId: string,
  userId: string,
  env: Env
): Promise<Response> {
  
  // Check if cached generated UI is fresh (max 1 hour)
  const cacheKey = `app-ui:${appId}:${userId}`;
  const cached = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(cacheKey, 'json') as CachedUI | null;
  
  if (cached && Date.now() - cached.generatedAt < 3600000) {
    // Serve cached UI via Dynamic Worker Loader
    return serveViaLoader(cached.htmlContent, env);
  }

  // Load instructions.md and user customizations
  const [instructionsObj, customizationsObj] = await Promise.all([
    env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(`apps/${appId}/ui/instructions.md`),
    env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(`spaces/${spaceId}/app-customizations/${appId}/${userId}.md`)
  ]);

  const instructions = instructionsObj ? await instructionsObj.text() : 'Build a simple, clean app UI.';
  const customizations = customizationsObj ? await customizationsObj.text() : '';

  // Generate fresh UI via LLM
  // This runs once per hour per user — negligible cost
  const uiGeneration = await env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-haiku-4-5', // use haiku — fast and cheap for UI gen
    max_tokens: 4096,
    messages: [{
      role: 'user',
      content: `Generate a complete, self-contained HTML page for this app UI.
Use only HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. No external dependencies.
The UI must connect to the app's API at /api/apps/${appId}/ for data.
Include dark mode support via CSS media query.

App instructions:
${instructions}

User customizations (apply these):
${customizations || 'None yet — use defaults from instructions.'}

Output ONLY the complete HTML. Nothing else.`
    }]
  });

  const htmlContent = uiGeneration.content[0].text ?? '<h1>Error generating UI</h1>';

  // Cache for 1 hour
  await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(cacheKey, JSON.stringify({
    htmlContent,
    generatedAt: Date.now()
  }), { expirationTtl: 3600 });

  return serveViaLoader(htmlContent, env);
}

// Serve via Dynamic Worker Loader — <5ms boot
async function serveViaLoader(html: string, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
  // The Dynamic Worker Loader takes the HTML and serves it from a V8 isolate
  const loaderStub = env.NAELAO_DW_LOADER.get(
    env.NAELAO_DW_LOADER.idFromName('app-ui-loader')
  );
  return loaderStub.fetch(new Request('http://loader/serve', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ html, contentType: 'text/html' })
  }));
}

Where Does the App UI Live? — CF Pages vs Dynamic Workers

This is the most common architectural question for junior developers building Naelao Apps. The answer depends on the app's complexity:

UI Approach When to Use How It Works Personalization
Dynamic Worker Loader (Recommended) Most apps — simple to moderate complexity LLM generates HTML from instructions.md. Served via V8 isolate. Cached in KV. Re-generated when instructions or usage patterns change. High — customizations.md updated as user interacts. UI rebuilds automatically.
CF Pages (Static) Complex apps with rich UI — code editors, dashboards with charts Standard React/Vue app deployed to CF Pages. Fetches data from MCP Worker endpoints. Low — static app, manual updates only
No UI (Agent-only) Pure automation apps — data pipelines, background processors MCP server only. Agents call it directly. No user-facing component. N/A

Building a Naelao App — Step by Step

  1. Write the MCP Server Worker: Create a standard Cloudflare Worker that implements MCP protocol. Use the @naelao/mcp-server-sdk package which wraps CF Workers with MCP request handling. Register tool definitions in the Worker's tools.json.
  2. Write instructions.md: Plain English description of what the UI should look like. Include: what data to display, what actions the user can take, default layout preferences. This is what the LLM reads to generate the UI.
  3. Write the app manifest: naelao-app.json in your project root. Declares your MCP tools, required permissions, pricing, and supported Space Types.
  4. Test locally with Miniflare: Run npx naelao dev which starts Miniflare with the MCP hub routing, Dynamic Worker Loader, and a test Space.
  5. Deploy to Naelao: Run npx naelao publish which deploys the Worker to CF, registers the manifest with naelao-apps-registry, and uploads instructions.md and assets to R2.
  6. Users install the app: Space admin finds it in the Naelao Apps marketplace. One click installs: MCP server registered with their naelao-mcp-hub instance, app shows in their Space UI, their agents can immediately call the MCP tools.

App Manifest Specification

09 — Mini-AGI Space Type

Mini-AGI — Company-Level Intelligence Layer

The Mini-AGI Space Type is inspired by Jack Dorsey's idea that every company can now be a Mini-AGI. The concept: a company installs a Mini-AGI into their Space, and it becomes the intelligence layer for the entire organization — answering questions, routing tasks, managing data access, and coordinating agents across all sub-spaces.

The Core Idea (Sequoia / Jack Dorsey)

Every company is now collecting data from every customer interaction, every employee action, every system event. A Mini-AGI is the layer that makes that data queryable and actionable by the whole company. The Mini-AGI at McKinsey can answer "What have our consultants learned about supply chain optimization in the last 6 months?" The Mini-AGI at Airbnb can answer "What are the top 3 host complaints this week in Southeast Asia?"

The critical constraint: not everyone in the company should be able to ask every question. A sales rep shouldn't be able to query internal legal strategy. A contractor shouldn't see employee salary data. The Mini-AGI enforces these access controls per-question, per-user, per-data-domain.

Mini-AGI Architecture

A Mini-AGI is a sub-space type that gets installed into an Enterprise or Team Space. Each Mini-AGI has a MiniAGIDO as its intelligence layer, plus data access controls that determine which users and sub-spaces can query which data domains.

Mini-AGI Data Access Control Flow
Company Member (any role)
→ asks question →
MiniAGIDO
MiniAGIDO
→ checks access matrix →
Data Access Control Table
Access Control Table
→ grants access to →
Permitted Data Domains in R2
R2 Data
→ queried by →
MiniAGIDO (NaelaoAgentDO sub-agent)
→ answers →
Member
Members never access R2 directly. MiniAGIDO is the gatekeeper. Access is denied by default — must be explicitly granted per domain per role.

MiniAGIDO — Complete Schema

// durable-objects/mini-agi-do.ts
// The Mini-AGI intelligence layer for a company Space.
// One MiniAGIDO per Mini-AGI sub-space.
// Routes queries to the right data, enforces access controls.

export class MiniAGIDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      -- Data domains: logical groups of company data
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_domains (
        id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name         TEXT NOT NULL,      -- e.g., 'hr-data', 'sales-data', 'legal-docs'
        description  TEXT NOT NULL,
        r2_prefix    TEXT NOT NULL,      -- which R2 path prefix this domain covers
        sensitivity  TEXT DEFAULT 'internal', -- 'public'|'internal'|'confidential'|'restricted'
        created_at   INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Access control matrix: who can query which domain
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS access_grants (
        id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        domain_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES data_domains(id),
        grantee_type TEXT NOT NULL,      -- 'role'|'user'|'sub_space'
        grantee_id   TEXT NOT NULL,      -- role name, userId, or spaceId
        access_level TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'read', -- 'read'|'query'|'write'|'admin'
        granted_by   TEXT NOT NULL,      -- userId of admin who granted this
        expires_at   INTEGER,            -- null = permanent
        granted_at   INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_access ON access_grants(grantee_type, grantee_id, domain_id);

      -- Query log: every query is logged for audit
      -- This is REQUIRED for compliance — do not make it optional
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS query_log (
        id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        user_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
        query        TEXT NOT NULL,      -- the natural language question
        domains_accessed TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON array of domain IDs queried
        domains_denied   TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON array of domains the user couldn't access
        answer_given TEXT,               -- the answer provided (truncated to 500 chars)
        latency_ms   INTEGER,
        created_at   INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Installed sub-spaces (Mini-AGI installed in which sub-spaces)
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS installations (
        sub_space_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        installed_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        config       TEXT DEFAULT '{}'
      );
    `);
  }

  // The core method: answer a question from a user
  // This enforces access controls before touching any data
  async query(params: {
    userId: string;
    userRole: string;
    subSpaceId: string;
    question: string;
  }): Promise<MiniAGIResponse> {
    const startMs = Date.now();

    // 1. Determine which data domains this question might need
    // Use LLM to classify the question — fast with haiku
    const classification = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
      model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
      max_tokens: 200,
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: `You are a data domain classifier. Given this question, list the data domains it needs.
Available domains: ${this.getAvailableDomains()}
Question: "${params.question}"
Respond with JSON: {"domains": ["domain-id-1", "domain-id-2"]}`
      }]
    });
    
    const { domains: requiredDomains } = JSON.parse(
      classification.content[0].text ?? '{"domains": []}'
    );

    // 2. Check access for each required domain
    const accessResults = await this.checkAccess(
      params.userId, params.userRole, params.subSpaceId, requiredDomains
    );
    
    const grantedDomains = accessResults.filter(r => r.granted).map(r => r.domainId);
    const deniedDomains = accessResults.filter(r => !r.granted).map(r => r.domainId);

    if (grantedDomains.length === 0) {
      // No access to any required domain
      await this.logQuery(params, requiredDomains, deniedDomains, null, Date.now() - startMs);
      return {
        success: false,
        answer: "I don't have access to the data needed to answer that question.",
        accessDenied: true,
        deniedDomains
      };
    }

    // 3. Fetch data from granted domains in R2
    const domainData = await this.fetchDomainData(grantedDomains, params.question);

    // 4. Generate answer using LLM with retrieved data
    const answer = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
      model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
      max_tokens: 1000,
      system: `You are the company's intelligence layer. Answer questions based ONLY on the provided data.
If the data doesn't contain enough information, say so clearly. Never make up information.
If some relevant data was not accessible (access denied), mention that limitation.`,
      messages: [{
        role: 'user',
        content: `Question: ${params.question}

Available data (you can only see data from domains the user has access to):
${domainData}

${deniedDomains.length > 0 ? `Note: Some data domains were not accessible to this user: ${deniedDomains.join(', ')}` : ''}`
      }]
    });

    const answerText = answer.content[0].text ?? 'Unable to generate answer.';
    
    // 5. Log every query — REQUIRED for compliance
    await this.logQuery(params, grantedDomains, deniedDomains, answerText, Date.now() - startMs);

    return {
      success: true,
      answer: answerText,
      accessDenied: false,
      deniedDomains,
      domainsQueried: grantedDomains
    };
  }

  private async checkAccess(
    userId: string,
    userRole: string,
    subSpaceId: string,
    domainIds: string[]
  ): Promise<Array<{ domainId: string; granted: boolean; reason: string }>> {
    return domainIds.map(domainId => {
      // Check if any grant exists for this user+role+subspace on this domain
      const grant = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
        SELECT access_level FROM access_grants
        WHERE domain_id = ?
          AND (
            (grantee_type = 'role' AND grantee_id = ?) OR
            (grantee_type = 'user' AND grantee_id = ?) OR
            (grantee_type = 'sub_space' AND grantee_id = ?)
          )
          AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?)
        LIMIT 1
      `, domainId, userRole, userId, subSpaceId, Date.now()).one();

      return {
        domainId,
        granted: !!grant,
        reason: grant ? `Granted via ${(grant as any).access_level}` : 'No access grant found'
      };
    });
  }
}

Mini-AGI vs Space Assistant — Key Differences

Dimension Space Assistant Mini-AGI
Scope Per-user, per-Space Company-wide, across all sub-spaces
Primary use Personal productivity assistant Company intelligence and knowledge retrieval
Data access User's own files and projects Controlled access to company data domains
Access controls User's own permissions Explicit per-domain, per-role, per-user grants
Audit log Optional Mandatory — every query logged
Self-modification Can modify own skills Cannot modify — read-only intelligence layer

10 — Spaces & Isolation

Spaces, Sub-Spaces & 6-Layer Tenant Isolation

A Space is a virtual full Naelao instance. Every organization on the platform shares the same physical Cloudflare infrastructure but is completely isolated at six independent layers simultaneously. Breaching one layer does not expose data from another. This is the foundational security guarantee of the entire platform.

The 6 Isolation Layers — Implemented in Full Detail

Layer 1 — SpaceDO SQLite Per-Product Database

Every NaelaoProduct (root Space) gets its own SpaceDO instance whose ctx.storage.sql (DO SQLite) is the product's complete database. Sub-spaces within the product share the same SpaceDO database and are isolated by space_id column — no RLS needed because no two products share a database instance. The DO instance boundary is the isolation boundary. Breaching one product's SpaceDO cannot expose another product's data because they are physically separate SQLite databases in separate DO instances.

Why SpaceDO SQLite, Not Supabase + RLS

The original architecture kept Supabase because "D1 lacks RLS, stored functions, full-text search." That reasoning was valid for a single shared database where RLS was doing the isolation work. With one SpaceDO per product, the database boundary replaces RLS entirely — there are no cross-product rows to filter. DO SQLite supports FTS5 natively. Stored functions become typed DO methods. Hyperdrive is eliminated. No external service dependency. The entire data layer runs inside Cloudflare.

// SpaceDO — per-product database, initialized in constructor
// File: workers/naelao-spaces/src/dos/SpaceDO.ts
// DO ID: idFromName('space:{rootSpaceId}')  ← root space ID = product ID
// Sub-spaces write to the same DO with their own space_id in every row.

export class SpaceDO extends DurableObject {
  private db: SqlStorage;

  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    this.db = ctx.storage.sql;
    this.db.exec(`
      -- Platform-fixed schema. Never diverges by SpaceType.
      -- SpaceType differences live in config, agent definitions, and manifests — never in DB tables.

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spaces (
        id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        parent_id  TEXT REFERENCES spaces(id),
        name       TEXT NOT NULL,
        space_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (space_type IN (
                     'builder_workspace','team','launchpad','verticals',
                     'workers','studio','enterprise','mini_agi','developer','custom'
                   )),
        agency_shell INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        depth      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (depth <= 3),
        status     TEXT DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','suspended','deleted')),
        settings   TEXT DEFAULT '{}',
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_members (
        space_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        user_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
        role       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member'
                     CHECK (role IN ('owner','admin','editor','member','viewer')),
        invited_by TEXT,
        joined_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
        PRIMARY KEY (space_id, user_id)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS product_users (
        id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        email         TEXT NOT NULL,
        display_name  TEXT,
        status        TEXT DEFAULT 'active',
        credits_used  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        credits_limit INTEGER,
        last_active_at TEXT,
        created_at    TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS threads (
        id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        space_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id),
        user_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
        title      TEXT,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
        id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        thread_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        space_id   TEXT NOT NULL,    -- denormalized for fast space-scoped queries
        role       TEXT NOT NULL,
        content    TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_runs (
        id               TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        thread_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES threads(id),
        space_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
        agent_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
        status           TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',
        input_tokens     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        output_tokens    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        credits_consumed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        started_at       TEXT,
        completed_at     TEXT
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        user_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
        space_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
        event_type  TEXT NOT NULL,
        credits     INTEGER NOT NULL,
        recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_definitions (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        space_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
        name        TEXT NOT NULL,
        config_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        version     INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
        created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fine_tune_jobs (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        space_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',
        approved    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        model_id    TEXT,
        created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
      );

      -- Indexes for the most common query patterns
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_threads_space   ON threads(space_id, created_at DESC);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_thread ON messages(thread_id, created_at ASC);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_space  ON messages(space_id);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_runs_space      ON agent_runs(space_id, started_at DESC);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_user    ON billing(user_id, recorded_at DESC);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_members_user    ON space_members(user_id);
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_defs_space      ON agent_definitions(space_id);

      -- FTS5 for message search (replaces Supabase full-text search)
      CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts
        USING fts5(content, content=messages, content_rowid=rowid);
    `);
  }

  // All data access goes through typed DO methods — never raw SQL from Workers.
  // Workers call SpaceDO via Service Binding. SpaceDO enforces space_id scoping internally.

  getThreads(spaceId: string, limit = 50): unknown[] {
    return this.db.exec(
      'SELECT * FROM threads WHERE space_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',
      spaceId, limit
    ).toArray();
  }

  insertThread(spaceId: string, id: string, userId: string, title: string): void {
    const now = new Date().toISOString();
    this.db.exec(
      'INSERT INTO threads (id, space_id, user_id, title, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)',
      id, spaceId, userId, title, now, now
    );
  }

  // Atomic credit deduction — BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes writes in DO's single-writer model.
  // The single-writer property of DOs makes this race-condition-free by design.
  deductCredits(userId: string, spaceId: string, credits: number): { success: boolean; remaining: number } {
    const user = this.db.exec(
      'SELECT credits_used, credits_limit FROM product_users WHERE id = ?', userId
    ).one() as { credits_used: number; credits_limit: number | null } | null;
    if (!user) return { success: false, remaining: 0 };
    if (user.credits_limit !== null && user.credits_used + credits > user.credits_limit) {
      return { success: false, remaining: user.credits_limit - user.credits_used };
    }
    this.db.exec(
      'UPDATE product_users SET credits_used = credits_used + ? WHERE id = ?', credits, userId
    );
    this.db.exec(
      'INSERT INTO billing (id, user_id, space_id, event_type, credits, recorded_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)',
      crypto.randomUUID(), userId, spaceId, 'agent_run', credits, new Date().toISOString()
    );
    const newUsed = user.credits_used + credits;
    return { success: true, remaining: user.credits_limit !== null ? user.credits_limit - newUsed : Infinity as unknown as number };
  }

  // Replaces Supabase stored function get_llm_formatted_messages()
  // Returns messages in the format expected by the LLM context builder.
  getLlmFormattedMessages(threadId: string, limit = 100): Array<{role: string; content: string}> {
    return (this.db.exec(
      'SELECT role, content FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ?',
      threadId, limit
    ).toArray() as Array<{role: string; content: string}>);
  }

  // Replaces Supabase RPC get_stale_projects_for_categorization()
  getStaleProjectsForCategorization(staleBefore: string): unknown[] {
    return this.db.exec(
      `SELECT p.id, p.title, p.space_id FROM threads p
       WHERE p.updated_at < ? AND p.space_id IN (SELECT id FROM spaces WHERE status = 'active')
       LIMIT 50`,
      staleBefore
    ).toArray();
  }
}

Layer 2 — R2 Key Prefixes

// Every R2 operation in every Worker must use this helper.
// Never write to R2 without the space prefix — it's the only way to enforce isolation.
// shared/r2-helpers.ts

export class SpaceR2 {
  constructor(
    private r2: R2Bucket,
    private spaceId: string
  ) {
    // Validate spaceId format immediately — catch bugs early
    if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(spaceId)) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid spaceId format: ${spaceId}`);
    }
  }

  // All R2 operations route through these methods — NEVER call r2.get() directly
  async get(path: string): Promise<R2ObjectBody | null> {
    this.validatePath(path);
    return this.r2.get(`spaces/${this.spaceId}/${path}`);
  }

  async put(path: string, value: string | ArrayBuffer | ReadableStream, options?: R2PutOptions): Promise<void> {
    this.validatePath(path);
    await this.r2.put(`spaces/${this.spaceId}/${path}`, value, options);
  }

  async delete(path: string): Promise<void> {
    this.validatePath(path);
    await this.r2.delete(`spaces/${this.spaceId}/${path}`);
  }

  async list(prefix?: string): Promise<R2Objects> {
    return this.r2.list({ prefix: `spaces/${this.spaceId}/${prefix ?? ''}` });
  }

  private validatePath(path: string): void {
    // Prevent path traversal attacks: ../../ or absolute paths
    if (path.includes('..') || path.startsWith('/')) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid R2 path: ${path}. Must be relative with no '..'`);
    }
    // Prevent accessing another space's data by embedding the prefix
    if (path.includes('spaces/')) {
      throw new Error(`R2 path cannot contain 'spaces/': ${path}`);
    }
  }
}

// Usage in any Worker:
const spaceR2 = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, spaceId);
await spaceR2.put('workspace/todo.md', content); // writes to spaces/{spaceId}/workspace/todo.md
const file = await spaceR2.get('workspace/todo.md'); // reads from spaces/{spaceId}/workspace/todo.md

// shared/do-helpers.ts

Layer 4 — CF Queue Message Validation

// Every queue consumer must validate spaceId before processing.
// A bug in a producer that sends the wrong spaceId must not cause
// cross-tenant data processing in the consumer.

// workers/agents/index.ts — Queue consumer
export default {
  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<AgentRunMessage>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    for (const message of batch.messages) {
      const { spaceId, threadId, userId } = message.body;

      // Validate spaceId format
      if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(spaceId)) {
        console.error('[NAELAO] Invalid spaceId in queue message, discarding:', message.id);
        message.ack(); // ack to prevent infinite retry
        continue;
      }

      // Validate that this user is actually in this space (call naelao-auth)
      const authResult = await env.NAELAO_AUTH.fetch(new Request('http://auth/validate-membership', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, userId })
      }));

      if (!authResult.ok) {
        console.error('[NAELAO] Space membership validation failed for queue message:', message.id);
        message.ack();
        continue;
      }

      // Safe to process
      try {
        await processAgentRun(message.body, env);
        message.ack();
      } catch (e) {
        console.error('[NAELAO] Agent run failed:', e);
        message.retry(); // CF Queues will retry up to max_retries
      }
    }
  }
};

Layer 5 — AI Gateway Tenant Tagging

// shared/ai-gateway.ts
// Every LLM call must include cf-aig-metadata with spaceId.
// This drives: per-tenant caching, per-tenant rate limits, per-tenant cost analytics.
// Missing this header means you can't bill correctly or enforce rate limits.

export function createAIClient(env: Env, meta: {
  spaceId: string;
  threadId: string;
  userId: string;
  model: string;
}) {
  return new Anthropic({
    baseURL: `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/${env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/${env.NAELAO_GATEWAY_ID}/anthropic`,
    apiKey: env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
    defaultHeaders: {
      // Per-tenant cache key — prevents cross-tenant cache pollution
      'cf-aig-metadata': JSON.stringify({
        spaceId: meta.spaceId,
        threadId: meta.threadId,
        userId: meta.userId,
        model: meta.model
      }),
      // Cache identical prompts for 1 hour — research/classification tasks benefit most
      'cf-aig-cache-ttl': '3600',
    }
  });
}

Layer 6 — Container Naming

// durable-objects/sandbox-do.ts
// Container names include spaceId — prevents cross-space container access.
// The CF Sandbox SDK enforces that only Workers with the correct binding
// can address a container by name.

private getContainerName(): string {
  // Format: naelao-agent-{spaceId}-{threadId}
  // Truncated because container names have a max length
  const spacePrefix = this.spaceId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 8);
  const threadPrefix = this.threadId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 8);
  return `naelao-agent-${spacePrefix}-${threadPrefix}`;
}

async startContainer(): Promise<void> {
  const sandbox = getSandbox(this.env.NAELAO_SANDBOX, this.getContainerName());
  
  // Mount R2 at /workspace — ALWAYS the first thing after start
  // Without this, the agent has no persistent filesystem
  await sandbox.mountBucket(this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, '/workspace', {
    prefix: `spaces/${this.spaceId}/workspace/`
  });
  
  this.containerRef = sandbox;
}

Next.js Middleware — URL Rewriting (Zero Page Changes)

// apps/frontend/middleware.ts
// This file is the ONLY place where Space URL routing happens.
// Every page component is completely unaware of Spaces.
// The space context flows via cookies set here.

import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server';

export function middleware(request: NextRequest): NextResponse {
  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;

  // Match /spaces/{rootId}/{optional-segment}/{rest}
  // Examples:
  //   /spaces/abc-123/dashboard → rewrites to /dashboard, sets space_id=abc-123
  //   /spaces/abc-123/marketing/projects → rewrites to /projects, sets space_id=marketing-id
  //   /spaces/abc-123/settings → rewrites to /settings, sets space_id=abc-123
  const spaceMatch = pathname.match(
    /^\/spaces\/([a-z0-9-]{36})(?:\/([a-z0-9-]+))?(\/.*)?$/
  );

  if (!spaceMatch) return NextResponse.next();

  const [, rootSpaceId, secondSegment, restPath = '/dashboard'] = spaceMatch;

  // Determine if the second segment is a sub-space slug or a page path
  // We check this via a KV lookup cached for 5 minutes
  // (We can't do async in middleware without waiting — use Edge Runtime)
  let spaceId = rootSpaceId;
  let pagePath = secondSegment ? `/${secondSegment}${restPath}` : restPath;

  // IMPORTANT: We can't do async SpaceDO lookups in middleware.
  // Instead, the frontend reads the space_id cookie and the server validates it.
  // If secondSegment looks like a UUID, it's probably a sub-space.
  // If it looks like a page name (letters only), it's a page route.
  const looksLikeSubSpace = secondSegment && /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(secondSegment);
  
  if (looksLikeSubSpace) {
    spaceId = secondSegment;
    pagePath = restPath || '/dashboard';
  }

  const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
  url.pathname = pagePath;
  const response = NextResponse.rewrite(url);

  // Set cookies — readable by frontend JS (httpOnly: false)
  // These cookies are used by EVERY API call to determine space context
  response.cookies.set('naelao_space_id', spaceId, {
    httpOnly: false,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: true,
    path: '/',
    maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24  // 24 hours
  });
  response.cookies.set('naelao_root_space_id', rootSpaceId, {
    httpOnly: false,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: true,
    path: '/',
    maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24
  });

  return response;
}

export const config = {
  matcher: ['/spaces/:path*']
};

getProductDB() — Resolving the Per-Product SpaceDO

// shared/get-product-db.ts
// Workers never query a database directly. They call SpaceDO methods via Service Binding.
// The SpaceDO for a product is always keyed to the ROOT space ID (= product ID).
// Sub-space Workers pass their own spaceId to SpaceDO methods — the DO enforces space_id scoping.

export function getProductDO(rootSpaceId: string, env: Env): DurableObjectStub {
  const id = env.SPACE_DO.idFromName(`space:${rootSpaceId}`);
  return env.SPACE_DO.get(id);
}

// Usage in naelao-threads Worker:
const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);
const threads = await spaceDO.getThreads(spaceId, 50);
// spaceId here is the active sub-space (or root space).
// SpaceDO.getThreads() enforces WHERE space_id = ? internally.

// Common mistake: calling SpaceDO with the wrong root space ID
// WRONG — using the sub-space ID as the DO key (creates a separate DO instead of hitting the product DB):
const wrongDO = env.SPACE_DO.get(env.SPACE_DO.idFromName(\`space:\${subSpaceId}\`));

// CORRECT — always resolve the DO via the ROOT space ID (product boundary):
const correctDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // rootSpaceId from naelao_root_space_id cookie

// Sub-space isolation: SpaceDO enforces space_id on every query internally.
// There is no cross-space leakage possible at the SQL level because:
//   1. Threads / messages / agent_runs all have space_id NOT NULL
//   2. Every SpaceDO method takes spaceId as a parameter and binds it
//   3. The DO instance boundary guarantees no two products share the same SQLite file
11 — Launchpad Space Type

Launchpad — AI-Run Digital Business

Launchpad is the space type for people who want to run an AI-powered digital business without managing the technical complexity themselves. The agents handle fulfillment, support, marketing, and content. The owner focuses on products and strategy. Five pre-built templates cover the most common digital business models.

Launchpad Templates

Template 01
Creator Store

Sell digital products (courses, ebooks, templates). Agents handle payment processing via Stripe App, delivery via email, support via chat. Owner uploads products and sets prices.

Template 02
Newsletter Business

Paid newsletter with AI-generated content. AutoResearch agent finds sources, writes drafts. Owner reviews and sends. Subscriber management, payment via Stripe.

Template 03
Micro-SaaS

Small software product. Agents handle tier-1 support, billing questions, onboarding. Owner manages the product. Code agents can ship small features.

Template 04
Service Agency

Productized service delivery. Agents scope projects, generate deliverables, manage client communication. Owner reviews final deliverables before sending.

Template 05
Coaching / Community

Online community with coaching calls. Agents handle member questions between sessions, create learning materials, track member progress.

Launchpad Core Agents

Every Launchpad Space gets these agents pre-installed from the marketplace. They are Autopilot tier — they act autonomously within defined boundaries, and the owner reviews outputs before they reach customers. 

// agents/definitions/launchpad-fulfillment-agent.json
// This definition is stored in SpaceDO SQLite agent_definitions table, scoped to the product's root space.
// It gets installed automatically when a Launchpad Space is created.
{
  "id": "launchpad-fulfillment-v1",
  "name": "Fulfillment Agent",

When you receive a new order notification, you: 1) Verify payment via the Stripe tool, 2) Send the product to the customer via the email tool, 3) Update the order status in the CRM tool, 4) Trigger any welcome sequences. Always confirm before sending to the customer. If the order has any issues (payment failed, product missing, suspicious behavior), escalate to the owner via notification.",

    "event": "order.completed",
    "source": "stripe-app"
  },

  "max_spend_per_action_usd": 0,
  "resource_tier": "workspace"
}

Launchpad Autopilot Mode — How It Actually Works

When a customer places an order, the following happens without the owner doing anything:

1
Stripe sends webhook → naelao-router → naelao-apps-registry → Stripe App MCP Worker receives payment.completed event
2
Fulfillment Agent triggered — NaelaoAgentDO wakes up. The Stripe App queued a naelao-agent-runs message with the order data.
3
Agent verifies payment — calls verify_payment MCP tool on Stripe App. If payment is confirmed and not already fulfilled, continues.
4
Agent retrieves product — reads product files from R2 workspace (e.g., the PDF ebook) using the file-manager skill.
5
Agent sends delivery email — calls email MCP tool. IF customer_email_send is in requires_approval_for, creates a Human-in-Loop checkpoint and notifies owner via Space Assistant. Otherwise sends automatically.
6
Agent updates records — marks order as fulfilled in CRM (via MCP App), updates analytics (via Analytics Engine).
7
Space Assistant notifies owner — "Order #1234 from customer@example.com was fulfilled. Product delivered at 14:32 UTC."

Human-in-the-Loop Checkpoints

Launchpad agents are Autopilot — they act autonomously BUT can be configured to pause at specific action types. The requires_approval_for field in the agent definition controls which actions require explicit human confirmation.

// durable-objects/agent-do.ts — Human-in-the-Loop implementation
// When agent hits an action that requires approval, it:
// 1. Pauses execution (runFiber() stops and waits)
// 2. Notifies owner via Space Assistant + push notification
// 3. Waits for /approve or /reject from the owner
// 4. Resumes or abandons based on response

async requestApproval(params: {
  actionType: string;
  actionDescription: string;
  previewData: unknown;
  timeoutMs: number;
}): Promise<{ approved: boolean; feedback?: string }> {

  const approvalId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const deadline = Date.now() + params.timeoutMs;

  // Store the pending approval
  await this.ctx.storage.put(`approval:${approvalId}`, {
    status: 'pending',
    actionType: params.actionType,
    description: params.actionDescription,
    preview: params.previewData,
    deadline,
    createdAt: Date.now()
  });

  // Notify the owner via Space Assistant
  await this.env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'approval_required',
    spaceId: this.spaceId,
    approvalId,
    agentId: this.agentId,
    actionType: params.actionType,
    description: params.actionDescription,
    preview: params.previewData,
    approveUrl: `https://app.naelao.dev/approvals/${approvalId}/approve`,
    rejectUrl: `https://app.naelao.dev/approvals/${approvalId}/reject`,
    expiresAt: new Date(deadline).toISOString()
  });

  // Wait for the approval decision using DO Alarm
  // The alarm fires at the deadline and auto-rejects if not responded to
  await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(deadline);

  // runFiber() will resume when the approval endpoint is called
  // The fiber suspends here — DO can hibernate, costs $0 while waiting
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    this.pendingApprovals.set(approvalId, resolve);
  });
}

// Called when owner clicks Approve/Reject in the UI
async handleApprovalDecision(approvalId: string, decision: 'approve' | 'reject', feedback?: string): Promise<void> {
  const resolver = this.pendingApprovals.get(approvalId);
  if (resolver) {
    resolver({ approved: decision === 'approve', feedback });
    this.pendingApprovals.delete(approvalId);
  }
  await this.ctx.storage.delete(`approval:${approvalId}`);
}

Verticals are industry-specific AI autopilot spaces. Bootstrap Mode is the economic engine that makes this possible at launch — before any training data exists.
