Test Helper Utilities

// tests/helpers/index.ts — shared test utilities
import { env, SELF, fetchMock } from 'cloudflare:test';
import { sign } from 'jsonwebtoken';

// Create a valid test JWT for a given user and space
export function createTestJWT(params: {
  userId: string;
  spaceId?: string;
  role?: string;
  expiresIn?: number;
}): string {
  return sign(
    {
      sub: params.userId,
      aud: 'authenticated',
      role: 'authenticated',
      space_id: params.spaceId,
      space_role: params.role ?? 'member',
      exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + (params.expiresIn ?? 3600)
    },
    env.NAELAO_JWT_SECRET
  );
}

// Create a test request with auth headers
export function authRequest(
  path: string,
  options: {
    method?: string;
    body?: unknown;
    userId?: string;
    spaceId?: string;
    role?: string;
  } = {}
): Request {
  const jwt = createTestJWT({
    userId: options.userId ?? 'test-user-id',
    spaceId: options.spaceId ?? 'test-space-id',
    role: options.role ?? 'member'
  });

  return new Request(`http://localhost${path}`, {
    method: options.method ?? 'GET',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${jwt}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Space-Id': options.spaceId ?? 'test-space-id',
      'Cookie': `naelao_space_id=${options.spaceId ?? 'test-space-id'}`
    },
    body: options.body ? JSON.stringify(options.body) : undefined
  });
}

// Get a test Durable Object instance
export function getTestDO<T extends DurableObject>(
  binding: DurableObjectNamespace,
  name: string
): DurableObjectStub {
  return binding.get(binding.idFromName(name));
}

// Write a file to the test R2 workspace
export async function writeTestFile(
  path: string,
  content: string,
  spaceId = 'test-space-id'
): Promise<void> {
  await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(`spaces/${spaceId}/${path}`, content);
}

// Read a file from the test R2 workspace
export async function readTestFile(
  path: string,
  spaceId = 'test-space-id'
): Promise<string | null> {
  const obj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(`spaces/${spaceId}/${path}`);
  return obj ? obj.text() : null;
}

// Mock the AI Gateway (Anthropic) responses in tests
export function mockAnthropicResponse(response: {
  content: string;
  toolCalls?: Array<{ name: string; params: Record<string, string> }>;
  usage?: { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number };
}): void {
  fetchMock.activate();
  fetchMock.disableNetConnect();
  fetchMock
    .get('https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com')
    .intercept({ path: /\/anthropic/ })
    .reply(200, {
      id: 'test-msg-id',
      type: 'message',
      role: 'assistant',
      content: [
        { type: 'text', text: response.content },
        ...(response.toolCalls ?? []).map(tc => ({
          type: 'text',
          text: `<${tc.name}>${Object.entries(tc.params).map(([k,v]) => `<${k}>${v}</${k}>`).join('')}</${tc.name}>`
        }))
      ],
      stop_reason: 'end_turn',
      usage: response.usage ?? { input_tokens: 100, output_tokens: 50 }
    });
}

// Restore fetch mocks after test
export function restoreMocks(): void {
  fetchMock.deactivate();
  fetchMock.enableNetConnect();
}

Example Complete Test File

// tests/suites/03-wallet-do.test.ts — complete test file example
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { env } from 'cloudflare:test';
import { getTestDO } from '../helpers';

describe('WalletDO', () => {
  let walletDO: DurableObjectStub;

  beforeEach(() => {
    // Fresh DO instance for each test (different name = different isolated instance)
    const testId = crypto.randomUUID();
    walletDO = getTestDO(
      env.NAELAO_WALLET_DO,
      `wallet:test-space-${testId}:test-agent`
    );
  });

  it('credits and then deducts correctly', async () => {
    // Credit the wallet first
    const creditResp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/credit', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 50.00, description: 'Initial credit', source: 'test' })
    }));
    expect(creditResp.ok).toBe(true);

    // Deduct and verify balance
    const deductResp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        amount: 12.50, description: 'API call', vendor: 'openai', category: 'llm'
      })
    }));
    const deductResult = await deductResp.json() as { success: boolean; newBalance: number };
    expect(deductResult.success).toBe(true);
    expect(deductResult.newBalance).toBeCloseTo(37.50, 2);
  });

  it('rejects deduction exceeding max_single_spend policy', async () => {
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/credit', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 1000, description: 'credit', source: 'test' })
    }));

    // Default max_single_spend is $10. Trying to spend $50 should fail.
    const resp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 50.00, description: 'Big spend', vendor: 'test', category: 'test' })
    }));
    const result = await resp.json() as { success: boolean; reason: string };
    expect(result.success).toBe(false);
    expect(result.reason).toContain('max single spend');
  });

  it('rejects deduction when monthly budget exceeded', async () => {
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/credit', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 1000, description: 'credit', source: 'test' })
    }));

    // Set a low monthly budget
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/set-policy', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ key: 'monthly_budget', value: '5.00' })
    }));

    // Spend $4 (ok)
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 4.00, description: 'first spend', vendor: 'test', category: 'test' })
    }));

    // Try to spend $4 more (exceeds $5 budget)
    const resp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 4.00, description: 'second spend', vendor: 'test', category: 'test' })
    }));
    const result = await resp.json() as { success: boolean; reason: string };
    expect(result.success).toBe(false);
    expect(result.reason).toContain('Monthly budget exceeded');
  });

  it('records all transactions with correct data', async () => {
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/credit', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 100, description: 'credit', source: 'stripe' })
    }));
    await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 5, description: 'API call', vendor: 'openai', category: 'llm' })
    }));

    const historyResp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/history'));
    const { transactions } = await historyResp.json() as { transactions: unknown[] };

    expect(transactions).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(transactions[0]).toMatchObject({ type: 'credit', amount_usd: 100 });
    expect(transactions[1]).toMatchObject({ type: 'debit', amount_usd: 5, vendor: 'openai' });
  });

  it('never allows balance to go negative', async () => {
    // Wallet starts at $0. Try to deduct $5.
    const resp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/deduct', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 5, description: 'test', vendor: 'test', category: 'test' })
    }));
    const result = await resp.json() as { success: boolean };
    expect(result.success).toBe(false);

    // Balance should still be 0
    const statusResp = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/status'));
    const { balance_usd } = await statusResp.json() as { balance_usd: number };
    expect(balance_usd).toBe(0);
  });
});

GitHub Actions CI Pipeline

# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run type check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Run linting
        run: npx eslint . --ext .ts --max-warnings 0

      - name: Run all tests in workerd
        run: npx vitest run --reporter=verbose
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.TEST_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          NAELAO_MCP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${{ secrets.TEST_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}
          NAELAO_JWT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.TEST_JWT_SECRET }}

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: ./coverage/lcov.info

  deploy-staging:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Deploy to staging
        run: npx wrangler deploy --env staging
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}

  deploy-production:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: 'npm' }
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Deploy to production
        run: npx wrangler deploy --env production
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}

web-search Skill — Complete Implementation

--- # skills/platform/web-search/SKILL.md
name: web-search
description: >
  Search the web for current information, news, facts, and research.
  Use this skill when the user asks about: current events, recent
  developments, fact-checking, researching a topic, finding statistics,
  looking up companies, people, or products.

  DO NOT use for: searching the user's own files (use file-manager),
  searching the knowledge base (that happens automatically),
  or for tasks you already know the answer to.

  This skill uses the Tavily API for high-quality search results with
  citations. Results include source URLs for verification.

metadata:
  naelao:
    tier: 1
    resource: isolate
    version: "1.0.0"
    scripts:
      - id: search
        type: cf-worker
        file: scripts/search.ts
        description: "Search the web for information"
        args:
          query: { type: string, required: true, description: "Search query" }
          max_results: { type: number, default: 5, description: "Number of results (1-10)" }
          search_depth: { type: string, enum: [basic, advanced], default: basic }
          include_answer: { type: boolean, default: true }
      - id: crawl_page
        type: cf-worker
        file: scripts/crawl.ts
        description: "Read the full content of a specific URL"
        args:
          url: { type: string, required: true }
          extract_links: { type: boolean, default: false }
    security:
      sha256: "PLATFORM_SIGNED"
      verified_by: platform
      sandbox_only: false
      codemode_allowed: true
---

# Web Search

Use the `search` script for general web searches. Use `crawl_page`
when you need to read a full article or page after a search reveals
a relevant URL.

## Search Strategy
1. Start with a specific query — vague queries return poor results
2. For research tasks: search multiple times with different query angles
3. For current events: include the year (2026) in your query
4. Always cite your sources when using search results

## When to Use crawl_page
After a search returns a promising URL, use crawl_page to get the
full article text. The search result snippet is often truncated.

## Using codemode for Multi-Search
For research tasks requiring multiple searches, use codemode to
write a program that searches in parallel:
```
const results = await Promise.all([
  tools.search({ query: 'Cloudflare Workers limits 2026' }),
  tools.search({ query: 'Cloudflare Durable Objects pricing' }),
  tools.search({ query: 'Cloudflare R2 vs S3 comparison' })
]);
```

code-exec Skill — Complete Implementation

--- # skills/platform/code-exec/SKILL.md
name: code-exec
description: >
  Execute code in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or Bash.
  Use this skill for: data analysis, calculations, transformations,
  file processing, running scripts, testing code snippets, and
  any computational task.

  EXECUTION TIER RULES (follow these exactly):
  - JavaScript/TypeScript with no file I/O → use codemode (fastest, no container)
  - Python with standard library only → use execute_python in container
  - Python with packages (pandas, numpy, etc.) → use execute_python with install_deps
  - Bash commands → use execute_bash in container
  - Any code that reads/writes files → use container tier (files live in /workspace)

  DO NOT use execute_python for simple JS calculations.
  DO NOT use the browser skill for code execution.

metadata:
  naelao:
    tier: 1
    resource: sandbox
    version: "1.0.0"
    requires:
      bins: ["python3", "node", "bash"]
    install:
      - kind: python_package
        package: "pip"
        version: "--upgrade"
    scripts:
      - id: execute_python
        type: bash
        file: scripts/execute_python.sh
        description: "Execute Python code in the container"
        args:
          code: { type: string, required: true, description: "Python code to execute" }
          install_deps: { type: array, items: { type: string }, description: "pip packages to install first" }
          timeout: { type: number, default: 30, description: "Timeout in seconds" }
      - id: execute_bash
        type: bash
        file: scripts/execute_bash.sh
        description: "Execute bash commands in the container"
        args:
          commands: { type: string, required: true, description: "Bash commands to execute" }
          working_dir: { type: string, default: "/workspace", description: "Working directory" }
    security:
      sha256: "PLATFORM_SIGNED"
      verified_by: platform
      sandbox_only: true
      codemode_allowed: true
---

# Code Execution

## Python Execution (execute_python)
The container has Python 3.12 with pip available.
Always write clean, readable code with print() for output.
For data analysis, always save results to /workspace/output/ so the user can access them.

## Installing Packages
Use install_deps array: `["pandas", "numpy", "matplotlib"]`
Packages are installed before your code runs.
Installed packages persist for the duration of the container session.

## Bash Execution (execute_bash)
Use for: file operations, git commands, system tasks, running other tools.
All commands run in /workspace by default unless you specify working_dir.

## codemode for TypeScript/JavaScript
For JS/TS without file I/O, prefer codemode — it runs in a V8 isolate
in under 5ms without starting a container. Much faster for calculations.

How to SHA-256 Sign a Platform Skill

// scripts/sign-skills.ts — run this in CI after updating any platform skill
// This is the ONLY way platform skills are signed. Never sign manually.
import { createHash } from 'crypto';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'fs';
import { glob } from 'glob';

async function signPlatformSkills() {
  const skillFiles = await glob('skills/platform/*/SKILL.md');
  const signatures: Record<string, { hash: string; signedAt: string }> = {};

  for (const skillFile of skillFiles) {
    const content = readFileSync(skillFile, 'utf-8');
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex');
    const skillName = skillFile.split('/')[2];
    signatures[skillName] = {
      hash,
      signedAt: new Date().toISOString()
    };
    console.log(`✓ Signed ${skillName}: ${hash.slice(0, 16)}...`);
  }

  // Write signatures to a manifest file
  // This manifest is uploaded to naelao-assets R2 at platform/skill-signatures.json
  writeFileSync(
    'skills/platform/skill-signatures.json',
    JSON.stringify(signatures, null, 2)
  );

  console.log(`
✓ Signed ${skillFiles.length} platform skills`);
  console.log('Upload skills/platform/ to naelao-assets R2 to deploy');
}

signPlatformSkills().catch(console.error);

# Add to package.json scripts:
# "sign-skills": "npx tsx scripts/sign-skills.ts"
# "upload-skills": "npx wrangler r2 object put naelao-assets/platform/ --file skills/platform/ --recursive"
40 — Execution Ladder Deep Dive

The 5-Tier Execution Ladder — Complete Specification

The execution ladder is a Project Think concept that defines five tiers of compute, from cheapest/fastest (direct R2 reads) to most expensive/capable (full Linux container). The agent automatically selects the right tier for each tool call. This section documents every tier with exact cost, boot time, capability limits, and the code that routes between them.

The 5 Tiers — Complete Specification

Tier 1 — Workspace (Direct R2)

Tier 1: Workspace — Direct R2 Operations

Boot time: ~0ms (no isolate created). Cost: R2 read/write pricing only (~$0.00004 per 1k operations). No CPU billing for the operation itself.

Capabilities: Read files, write files, list directories, delete files, copy files within R2. Nothing else. Cannot execute code. Cannot make HTTP requests. Cannot access system resources.

When to use: read_file, write_file, list_directory, delete_file, todo-workflow updates. Any operation that is purely a file read or write.

When NOT to use: Any computation on file contents (use Tier 2). Any file format conversion (use Tier 5). Any HTTP request (use Tier 2).

// agentpress/orchestrator.ts — Tier 1 execution
// No isolate created. Direct R2 API call via SpaceR2 helper.
// This is why workspace-tier tools are parallelized — they're pure I/O.

private async executeWorkspaceTool(tc: ParsedToolCall, spaceId: string, projectId: string): Promise<ToolResult> {
  const r2 = new SpaceR2(this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, spaceId);
  const prefix = `projects/${projectId}/workspace/`;

  switch (tc.toolName) {
    case 'read_file': {
      const obj = await r2.get(`${prefix}${tc.parameters.path}`);
      if (!obj) return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: { error: 'File not found', path: tc.parameters.path } };
      return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: { content: await obj.text(), size: obj.size } };
    }
    case 'write_file': {
      await r2.put(`${prefix}${tc.parameters.path}`, tc.parameters.content ?? '');
      return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: { success: true, path: tc.parameters.path } };
    }
    case 'list_directory': {
      const listing = await r2.list(`${prefix}${tc.parameters.path ?? ''}`);
      return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: {
        files: listing.objects.map(o => ({
          name: o.key.replace(`spaces/${spaceId}/${prefix}`, ''),
          size: o.size
        })),
        count: listing.objects.length
      }};
    }
    default:
      throw new Error(`Unknown workspace tool: ${tc.toolName}`);
  }
}

Tier 2 — Isolate (Dynamic Worker)

Tier 2: Isolate — V8 Dynamic Worker

Boot time: <5ms (V8 isolate, no OS overhead). Cost: CF Workers billing (~$0.50 per 1M requests + $0.02 per GB-second CPU). Typical tool call: <$0.000001.

Capabilities: Full TypeScript/JavaScript execution. Fetch to external HTTP endpoints (sandboxed). Web Crypto. No filesystem access. No native binaries. No npm at runtime (packages must be bundled at deploy time).

When to use: web_search (Tavily API call), api_caller (REST/GraphQL), data_transform (JS-based), render_artifact (HTML generation), any TypeScript computation that doesn't need filesystem access.

Implementation: The agent's tool call code is a TypeScript function. The orchestrator sends it to a pre-deployed Dynamic Worker via Service Binding. The Worker executes the function and returns the result. 

// agentpress/orchestrator.ts — Tier 2 execution via Dynamic Worker
private async executeIsolateTool(tc: ParsedToolCall): Promise<ToolResult> {
  // Route to the appropriate platform skill Worker via naelao-mcp-hub
  const response = await this.env.NAELAO_MCP_HUB.fetch(
    new Request('http://mcp-hub/execute', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        toolName: tc.toolName,
        parameters: tc.parameters,
        spaceId: this.spaceId,
        tier: 'isolate'
      })
    })
  );
  const result = await response.json();
  return { toolName: tc.toolName, output: result };
}

Tier 3 — npm (Isolate + Package Resolution)

Tier 3: npm — Dynamic Worker with Package Resolution

Boot time: <10ms (npm resolution cached by Cloudflare). Cost: Same as Tier 2 plus npm package fetching (minimal).

Capabilities: Everything in Tier 2 plus ability to import npm packages not bundled at deploy time. Used for: markdown parsing, PDF text extraction (pure JS), JSON schema validation, date parsing libraries.

When to use: Tasks that need a specific npm package but no filesystem access or native binaries. Example: parsing a YAML string with js-yaml, validating JSON with ajv, generating CSV with papaparse.

Note: Most platform skills are at Tier 2 (bundled) not Tier 3. Tier 3 is primarily for agent-authored codemode programs that need to import packages at runtime.

Tier 4 — Browser (CF Browser Rendering)

Tier 4: Browser — Cloudflare Browser Rendering

Boot time: ~200ms (Chrome instance cold start). Cost: CF Browser Rendering billing (currently included in Workers plans up to certain limits). ~$0.002 per page load at scale.

Capabilities: Full Chrome browser. JavaScript execution on pages. DOM manipulation. Screenshot capture. Form filling. Cookie management. Network request interception. Everything Playwright can do.

When to use: browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_fill_form, browser_screenshot, browser_scrape for JS-rendered pages. Any page that requires JavaScript execution to render its content.

Critical implementation detail: The CDP proxy (naelao-browser Worker) runs as a Moltworker — a single persistent Worker that proxies CDP protocol messages to the CF Browser Rendering API. Agents never get direct CDP access. All browser automation goes through the proxy, which enforces security limits.

// workers/browser/index.ts — CDP proxy for agents
// Agents call this via MCP tool, get HTML/screenshot back.
// They never touch CDP directly.

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const { action, url, selector, value, spaceId } = await request.json();

    // Security: validate the URL is not a private/internal address
    const parsedUrl = new URL(url);
    if (BLOCKED_IP_RANGES.some(p => p.test(parsedUrl.hostname))) {
      return Response.json({ error: 'Blocked: private IP address' }, { status: 403 });
    }
    if (parsedUrl.protocol !== 'https:' && parsedUrl.protocol !== 'http:') {
      return Response.json({ error: 'Only http/https URLs allowed' }, { status: 403 });
    }

    const browser = await puppeteer.launch(env.NAELAO_BROWSER);
    const page = await browser.newPage();

    try {
      await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle0', timeout: 30000 });

      let result: unknown;
      switch (action) {
        case 'get_content':
          result = {
            html: await page.content(),
            title: await page.title(),
            url: page.url()
          };
          break;
        case 'screenshot':
          const screenshot = await page.screenshot({ type: 'png', fullPage: false });
          result = { image: Buffer.from(screenshot).toString('base64'), mimeType: 'image/png' };
          break;
        case 'click':
          await page.click(selector);
          result = { success: true, clicked: selector };
          break;
        case 'fill':
          await page.type(selector, value);
          result = { success: true, filled: selector };
          break;
        case 'extract_text':
          const text = await page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText);
          result = { text };
          break;
        default:
          return Response.json({ error: `Unknown action: ${action}` }, { status: 400 });
      }

      return Response.json({ success: true, result });
    } finally {
      await browser.close();
    }
  }
};

Tier 5 — Sandbox (Full CF Container)

Tier 5: Sandbox — Full Linux Container

Boot time: 2-3 seconds cold, <100ms warm (after first start, stays warm for 10 minutes). Cost: CF Containers pricing (~$0.015/hr for standard-1, billed per-second). Most agent runs use <5 minutes of container time.

Capabilities: Full Ubuntu Linux. Python 3.12 with pip. Node.js 22. Git. Any bash command. Any installed package. File access at /workspace (R2 mounted). Port exposure for dev servers.

When to use: execute_python, execute_bash, git_clone, install_package, run_jupyter, compile_code, generate_pdf. Any task that requires native binaries, system calls, or Python packages.

Cost optimization tips: (1) Check if Tier 1-4 can do the same thing first. (2) Batch multiple Tier 5 commands into one container session — container stays warm for 10 minutes. (3) Do file reads/writes in Tier 1 even if a container is running — R2 reads from Tier 1 don't require an exec() call.

Execution Ladder Router — Complete Implementation

// agentpress/orchestrator.ts — complete routing logic
// This is called for every tool call the LLM emits.
// The router determines which tier handles each tool.

export async function routeAndExecuteTools(
  toolCalls: ParsedToolCall[],
  context: ExecutionContext,
  env: Env
): Promise<ToolResult[]> {
  const orchestrator = new Orchestrator(env, context);

  // Group tool calls by their required execution tier
  const grouped = groupByTier(toolCalls);
  const results: ToolResult[] = [];

  // Tier 1: Workspace — always parallel (pure I/O, no resource contention)
  if (grouped.workspace?.length) {
    const t1Results = await Promise.all(
      grouped.workspace.map(tc =>
        orchestrator.wal.executeWithWAL(context.runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          orchestrator.executeWorkspaceTool(tc)
        )
      )
    );
    results.push(...t1Results);
  }

  // Tier 2 + 3: Isolate/npm — parallel for independent tools
  const isolateTools = [...(grouped.isolate ?? []), ...(grouped.npm ?? [])];
  if (isolateTools.length) {
    // Tools marked parallel=true can run concurrently
    const parallelTools = isolateTools.filter(tc => TOOL_TIERS[tc.toolName]?.parallel !== false);
    const serialTools = isolateTools.filter(tc => TOOL_TIERS[tc.toolName]?.parallel === false);

    const t2Results = await Promise.all(
      parallelTools.map(tc =>
        orchestrator.wal.executeWithWAL(context.runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          orchestrator.executeIsolateTool(tc)
        )
      )
    );
    results.push(...t2Results);

    for (const tc of serialTools) {
      const result = await orchestrator.wal.executeWithWAL(
        context.runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          orchestrator.executeIsolateTool(tc)
      );
      results.push(result);
    }
  }

  // Tier 4: Browser — serial (shared browser resource)
  if (grouped.browser?.length) {
    for (const tc of grouped.browser) {
      const result = await orchestrator.wal.executeWithWAL(
        context.runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          orchestrator.executeBrowserTool(tc)
      );
      results.push(result);
    }
  }

  // Tier 5: Sandbox — ensure container running ONCE, then serial commands
  // DO NOT call ensureRunning() inside the loop — it would restart the container each time
  if (grouped.sandbox?.length) {
    await orchestrator.ensureContainerRunning();
    for (const tc of grouped.sandbox) {
      const result = await orchestrator.wal.executeWithWAL(
        context.runId, tc.toolName, tc.parameters, () =>
          orchestrator.executeSandboxTool(tc)
      );
      results.push(result);
    }
  }

  return results;
}

// Tool tier assignment — every platform tool mapped to its tier
// Junior dev: add your new tools here when you add them to the skill system
export const TOOL_TIERS: Record<string, { tier: ExecutionTier; parallel: boolean }> = {
  // Tier 1 — Workspace (R2 direct)
  read_file:         { tier: 'workspace', parallel: true },
  write_file:        { tier: 'workspace', parallel: false }, // writes are serial (lock needed)
  list_directory:    { tier: 'workspace', parallel: true },
  delete_file:       { tier: 'workspace', parallel: false },
  update_todo:       { tier: 'workspace', parallel: false },

  // Tier 2 — Isolate (Dynamic Worker)
  web_search:        { tier: 'isolate', parallel: true },
  api_call:          { tier: 'isolate', parallel: true },
  render_artifact:   { tier: 'isolate', parallel: false },
  data_transform:    { tier: 'isolate', parallel: true },
  validate_json:     { tier: 'isolate', parallel: true },
  create_workflow:   { tier: 'isolate', parallel: false },
  get_weather:       { tier: 'isolate', parallel: true },

  // Tier 4 — Browser (CF Browser Rendering)
  browser_navigate:  { tier: 'browser', parallel: false },
  browser_click:     { tier: 'browser', parallel: false },
  browser_fill:      { tier: 'browser', parallel: false },
  browser_screenshot:{ tier: 'browser', parallel: false },
  browser_scrape:    { tier: 'browser', parallel: false },
  browser_extract:   { tier: 'browser', parallel: false },

  // Tier 5 — Sandbox (CF Container)
  execute_python:    { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  execute_bash:      { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  execute_node:      { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  git_clone:         { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  git_commit:        { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  install_package:   { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  generate_pdf:      { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  generate_pptx:     { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  run_tests:         { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
  wrangler_deploy:   { tier: 'sandbox', parallel: false },
};
41 — Prompt Engineering

System Prompt Architecture for Naelao Agents

The quality of agent behavior is determined by the system prompt more than any other single factor. This section covers the exact structure, ordering, and content of every system prompt component in Naelao — from the base prompt to the skills XML to the tool definitions.

The Base System Prompt (Suna Kortix Port)

// agentpress/prompts/base-agent.ts
// This is the core system prompt for all Naelao agents.
// Ported from suna kortix's base prompt with CF-native additions.
// Do NOT shorten this — every section exists for a specific behavioral reason.

export const BASE_AGENT_PROMPT = `You are Naelao, an AI agent with the ability to take real actions in the world.

## Your Core Capabilities
You can read and write files, search the web, execute code, interact with browsers, call APIs, create workflows, and build artifacts. You have persistent memory across conversations and access to your project's full file history.

## How You Work
You operate in a loop:
1. **Observe**: Read the user's request and your available context (files, memory, skills)
2. **Plan**: Break complex tasks into concrete steps. Write your plan to todo.md.
3. **Act**: Execute one or more tool calls to make progress
4. **Observe**: Review the results of your actions
5. **Repeat**: Continue until the task is complete or you need user input

## Using Tools
Tools are called using XML syntax. Each tool is a self-contained action:
- Always prefer the simplest tool that accomplishes the task
- Prefer workspace-tier tools (file reads/writes) over container-tier (code execution) when possible
- Multiple tools can be used in the same response - they run in parallel where safe
- Use the codemode pattern for complex multi-step operations in a single LLM call

## File Operations
Your project workspace is at /workspace — this maps to persistent R2 storage.
Files you create persist across ALL conversations. You can build on your previous work.
Always check what files already exist before creating new ones.

## Planning with todo.md
For complex tasks, create /workspace/todo.md at the start:
- Break the task into numbered steps
- Check off each step as you complete it ([ ] → [x])
- Update the plan if you discover new requirements
- The todo.md persists — pick up where you left off in subsequent sessions

## Error Handling
If a tool fails, try to understand why before retrying:
- File not found: check the path with list_directory first
- API error: check the response body for specific error messages
- Code execution error: read stderr carefully, fix the issue, retry
- Container timeout: break the task into smaller operations

## Communication
Be concise in your responses. Show your work when it's complex. Ask for clarification only when genuinely ambiguous — try to proceed with reasonable assumptions when possible.

## Current Context
Space ID: {SPACE_ID}
Project ID: {PROJECT_ID}
Model: {MODEL}
Background mode: {BACKGROUND_MODE}`;

// Space context injected after base prompt (cached — changes only when space settings change)
export function buildSpaceContext(space: Space, userRole: string): string {
  return `
## Space Context
You are operating in Space: "${space.name}" (${space.type})
Your role in this space: ${userRole}
Space description: ${space.settings?.description ?? 'No description set'}
${space.settings?.customInstructions ?? ''}`;
}

// Tool definitions injected as system prompt XML (cached per skill set)
export function buildToolDefinitions(tools: ToolDefinition[]): string {
  const toolsXml = tools.map(t => `
  <tool name="${t.name}">
    <description>${t.description}</description>
    <parameters>
${Object.entries(t.parameters).map(([key, param]) => `      <param name="${key}" type="${param.type}" required="${param.required ?? false}">${param.description}</param>`).join('
')}
    </parameters>
  </tool>`).join('
');

  return `<available_tools>${toolsXml}
</available_tools>`;
}

// Memory injection — typed, not flat markdown
export function buildMemoryContext(memory: AgentMemory[]): string {
  if (!memory.length) return '';

  const grouped = memory.reduce((acc, m) => {
    if (!acc[m.category]) acc[m.category] = [];
    acc[m.category].push(m);
    return acc;
  }, {} as Record<string, AgentMemory[]>);

  const memoryXml = Object.entries(grouped).map(([category, items]) => `
  <${category}>
${items.map(m => `    <item key="${m.key}">${JSON.stringify(m.value)}</item>`).join('
')}
  </${category}>`).join('
');

  return `<agent_memory>${memoryXml}
</agent_memory>`;
}

Prompt Construction Order (Critical for Cache Efficiency)

Order Component Cached? Changes When? Max Tokens
1st Base system prompt YES — ephemeral Never (platform update only) ~800 tokens
2nd Space context YES — ephemeral Space settings change (rare) ~200 tokens
3rd Skills XML YES — ephemeral Skills added/removed for this agent ~1500 tokens
4th Tool definitions YES — ephemeral MCP tools change (rare) ~1000 tokens
5th Agent memory NO Every conversation (grows over time) ~500 tokens
6th Knowledge base chunks NO Every turn (semantic search results) ~2000 tokens
7th Conversation history NO Every turn (grows during conversation) up to 180k tokens
Why This Order Matters (Cache Savings)

Anthropic's prompt caching works on the prefix of your token sequence. If the first 4 components (1-4) are identical between two calls, they're served from cache at 10% of the normal input token cost. For a typical agent with 3000 tokens of static context and 20k tokens of conversation, caching components 1-4 saves ~$0.009 per turn on Claude Sonnet.

For an agent with 100 turns per run, this saves ~$0.90 per run in prompt caching alone. At scale (10k runs/month), that's $9,000/month in savings just from correct prompt ordering.

The rule: Static content first. Dynamic content last. Never put dynamic content before static content or you lose all cache hits.

Assistant System Prompt (Space Assistant — OpenClaw-style)

// agentpress/prompts/assistant-prompt.ts
// Space Assistants have a different system prompt from regular agents.
// They are proactive, space-aware, and have memory/channel context.

export function buildAssistantSystemPrompt(params: {
  spaceName: string;
  spaceType: string;
  userName: string;
  userRole: string;
  permissions: string[];
  memory: AgentMemory[];
  channels: ChannelConfig[];
  cronJobs: CronJob[];
}): string {
  const permissionList = params.permissions.filter(p =>
    params.permissions.includes(p)
  ).join(', ') || 'none';

  return `You are the Space Assistant for "${params.spaceName}" — a ${params.spaceType} Space on the Naelao platform.

## Your Identity
You are ${params.userName}'s dedicated AI assistant in this Space. You know this Space deeply — its projects, its members, its history, its recurring tasks. You are proactive, organized, and always on top of what's happening.

## Your Capabilities
You can help with everything in this Space:
- **Monitoring**: Watch agent runs, check project status, read analytics
- **Management**: Create and archive projects, update settings, manage workflows
- **Communication**: Respond across Slack, Discord, Telegram, and email
- **Sub-agents**: Spawn Naelao Agents from the marketplace for complex tasks
- **Scheduled tasks**: Your cron jobs run automatically — I'll handle them
- **Self-improvement**: I can add new skills and tools to myself as needed

## Your Admin Permissions (granted by ${params.userName})
${permissionList}

## What I Know About This Space
From my memory:
${formatMemoryForPrompt(params.memory)}

## Active Channels
${params.channels.map(ch => `- ${ch.type}: ${ch.config.channelName ?? ch.config.channelId}`).join('
') || 'No channels configured yet'}

## Today's Scheduled Tasks
${params.cronJobs.filter(j => j.enabled).map(j => `- ${j.id}: ${j.task} (${j.schedule})`).join('
') || 'No scheduled tasks today'}

## How to Respond
Be concise and action-oriented. When you can take action without asking, do it.
When you're not sure what the user wants, ask one clear question.
Always confirm before taking destructive actions (deleting, archiving).
For complex tasks, tell the user what you're doing before you start.`;
}

function formatMemoryForPrompt(memory: AgentMemory[]): string {
  if (!memory.length) return 'No stored memories yet.';
  return memory.slice(0, 20).map(m =>
    `- [${m.category}] ${m.key}: ${JSON.stringify(m.value)}`
  ).join('
');
}
42 — SDK API Reference

@naelao/agent-sdk — Complete API Reference

The Naelao Agent SDK is the npm package that developers use to build custom agents. It exposes all Naelao platform capabilities as typed TypeScript APIs. This section is the complete reference: every class, every method, every parameter, every return type.

NaelaoAgent Base Class

// @naelao/agent-sdk — src/NaelaoAgent.ts
// Developers extend this class to build custom agents.
// All platform capabilities are accessible via this.* methods.

export abstract class NaelaoAgent extends Agent<Env, NaelaoAgentState> {

  // ── IDENTITY ─────────────────────────────────────────
  readonly spaceId: string;
  readonly projectId: string | undefined;
  readonly agentId: string;

  // ── SESSION MANAGEMENT (Project Think) ───────────────

  // Create a new conversation session
  protected createSession(threadId: string): Session;

  // Get an existing session by thread ID
  protected getSession(threadId: string): Session | null;

  // Add a message to a session
  protected addMessage(sessionId: string, message: {
    role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool' | 'system';
    content: string;
    parentId?: string;
    toolName?: string;
  }): string; // returns messageId

  // Search messages via FTS5 full-text search
  protected searchMessages(sessionId: string, query: string): Message[];

  // Fork a session at a given message (creates parallel branch)
  protected forkSession(sessionId: string, fromMessageId: string): Session;

  // Compact session (summarize old messages to reduce token count)
  protected compactSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>;

  // ── BACKGROUND EXECUTION (Project Think) ─────────────

  // Run a durable fiber — survives DO eviction, browser close
  protected runFiber(name: string, fn: (ctx: FiberContext) => Promise<void>): Promise<void>;

  // Called when a fiber is recovered after eviction
  protected abstract onFiberRecovered(ctx: FiberContext): Promise<void>;

  // Spawn a sub-agent (Facets — colocated, typed RPC)
  protected spawnSubAgent<T extends NaelaoAgent>(
    AgentClass: new (...args: unknown[]) => T,
    name: string
  ): T;

  // ── FILE OPERATIONS (R2) ─────────────────────────────

  // Read a file from R2 workspace
  protected async readWorkspace(path: string): Promise<string | null>;

  // Write a file to R2 workspace (with versioning)
  protected async writeWorkspace(path: string, content: string, commitMsg?: string): Promise<void>;

  // List files in R2 workspace directory
  protected async listWorkspace(prefix?: string): Promise<FileInfo[]>;

  // Delete a file from R2 workspace
  protected async deleteWorkspace(path: string): Promise<void>;

  // ── LLM CALLS (CF AI Gateway) ────────────────────────

  // Make a streaming LLM call with automatic billing and caching
  protected async callLLM(params: {
    messages: MessageParam[];
    system?: TextBlockParam[];
    model?: string;
    maxTokens?: number;
    tools?: ToolDefinition[];
    onToken?: (delta: string) => void;
  }): Promise<LLMResponse>;

  // ── ARTIFACTS ────────────────────────────────────────

  // Create a live HTML/React artifact (Dynamic Worker Loader)
  protected async spinArtifact(name: string, code: string, type: 'html' | 'react' | 'chart'): Promise<{ previewUrl: string; artifactId: string }>;

  // ── DYNAMIC WORKFLOWS ────────────────────────────────

  // Create and deploy an agent-authored Dynamic Workflow
  protected async createWorkflow(params: {
    name: string;
    code: string;          // TypeScript WorkflowEntrypoint class
    schedule?: string;     // cron expression for scheduled workflows
    triggerType?: 'manual' | 'cron' | 'webhook';
  }): Promise<{ workflowId: string; path: string }>;

  // Trigger a deployed workflow manually
  protected async triggerWorkflow(workflowId: string, input?: unknown): Promise<string>; // returns instanceId

  // ── MEMORY ───────────────────────────────────────────

  // Write a typed memory entry (schema-validated)
  protected async rememberFact(key: string, subject: string, predicate: string, object: string): Promise<void>;
  protected async rememberPreference(key: string, domain: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
  protected async rememberTask(key: string, description: string, status: 'pending' | 'in_progress' | 'complete'): Promise<void>;

  // Query memory entries
  protected getMemory(category?: string, limit?: number): AgentMemory[];

  // ── SKILLS ───────────────────────────────────────────

  // Execute a platform skill tool call
  protected async callSkill(skillName: string, toolId: string, params: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<ToolResult>;

  // Register a self-authored tool (callable in next LLM turn)
  protected async registerTool(definition: {
    name: string;
    description: string;
    parameters: JSONSchema;
    implementation: string; // TypeScript code
  }): Promise<void>;

  // ── ABSTRACT: Developer implements this ──────────────

  // Main entry point — called for every user message
  abstract run(input: AgentInput): AsyncGenerator<AgentEvent>;
}

Building a Custom Agent — Minimal Example

// Example: A simple research agent that answers questions with citations
// Deployed to Cloudflare as a Worker, registered with Naelao marketplace

import { NaelaoAgent, AgentInput, AgentEvent } from '@naelao/agent-sdk';

export class ResearchAgent extends NaelaoAgent {

  async *run(input: AgentInput): AsyncGenerator<AgentEvent> {
    const session = this.createSession(input.threadId);
    this.addMessage(session.id, { role: 'user', content: input.message });

    yield { type: 'thinking', content: 'Searching for information...' };

    // Search the web for relevant information
    const searchResult = await this.callSkill('web-search', 'search', {
      query: input.message,
      max_results: 5,
      include_answer: true
    });

    // Build context with search results
    const searchContext = JSON.stringify(searchResult.output);

    // Call LLM with search results for grounded response
    const llmResponse = await this.callLLM({
      messages: [
        { role: 'user', content: input.message }
      ],
      system: [{
        type: 'text',
        text: `You are a research assistant. Answer questions using the provided search results. Always cite your sources.

Search results:
${searchContext}`
      }],
      onToken: (delta) => {
        this.ctx.getWebSockets().forEach(ws =>
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', delta }))
        );
      }
    });

    // Save the response to the session
    this.addMessage(session.id, {
      role: 'assistant',
      content: llmResponse.content,
      parentId: this.lastMessageId
    });

    // Save any facts learned for future sessions
    if (llmResponse.content.length > 100) {
      await this.rememberFact(
        `research-${Date.now()}`,
        'user inquiry',
        'asked about',
        input.message.slice(0, 200)
      );
    }

    yield { type: 'complete', content: llmResponse.content };
  }

  async onFiberRecovered(ctx: FiberContext): Promise<void> {
    // This agent uses foreground mode only — no fiber recovery needed
    // For background mode, implement resumption logic here
  }
}

export default ResearchAgent;

This section provides exact cost calculations for operating Naelao at different scales. Every component is itemized. These are real CF pricing figures as of May 2026 (Supabase removed from stack).

Cost Per Component at Scale

Component Suna Kortix Cost Naelao Cost Scale Point
FastAPI/Workers $25-100/mo VPS (always on) $0.50 / 1M requests (usage only) Break-even at ~50k req/mo
Redis (queue + pub/sub) $15-100/mo (always on) $0 (CF Queues free tier: 1M messages/mo) Always cheaper
Docker/Daytona sandbox $0.18-0.48/hr per container (always on) $0.015/hr (on-demand only) 90%+ savings at any scale
Browser (Playwright) $0.60/hr + container running CF Browser Rendering (included in Workers plans) Always cheaper
Object storage DO SQLite: ~$0.20/GB-month (included in DO pricing) + R2 egress for large files $0.015/GB R2 + $0 egress 28% cheaper + no egress fees
LLM proxy (LiteLLM) $49-299/mo (LiteLLM cloud) or self-hosted $0 (CF AI Gateway free tier) Always cheaper
Real-time (Redis SSE) Redis pub/sub + server connection DO WebSocket hibernation ($0 when idle) Always cheaper
Space Assistants Not available ~$0.015/hr active, $0 idle New capability
Dynamic Workflows Not available $0 idle, Workers CPU billing when active New capability

44 — Mini-AGI: Vision to Implementation

Mini-AGI — From Jack Dorsey's Vision to Running Code

Jack Dorsey's insight: every company now has access to AI that can process, understand, and act on every piece of data it generates. The company that wires its internal data to an intelligence layer becomes a Mini-AGI — able to answer complex questions about itself, route decisions intelligently, and coordinate action across departments. This section implements that vision completely on Cloudflare.

The Mini-AGI Mental Model

Think of a company with three layers: (1) data scattered across CRM, ERP, Slack, email, documents; (2) employees who understand pieces of that data in isolation; (3) a CEO who needs to make decisions requiring cross-functional synthesis. A Mini-AGI is the intelligence layer that sits between the data and the decision-makers — it can answer "what's happening across the whole company right now?" in seconds, not weeks.

Without Mini-AGI
Data Silos

Sales VP asks IT for a report. IT runs a SQL query. Returns data next Tuesday. VP makes decision based on 2-week-old data and incomplete picture.

With Mini-AGI (Basic)
Query Layer

Sales VP asks Mini-AGI. Mini-AGI checks access permissions, queries the sales data domain in real time, returns synthesized answer in seconds. HR data still invisible to VP.

With Mini-AGI (Advanced)
Action Layer

Sales VP asks Mini-AGI about a deal at risk. Mini-AGI identifies the technical issue from engineering tickets, checks customer health from support data, drafts a rescue plan — all in one response, all data-permission-gated.

Cross-Domain Query Handling — The Full Implementation

// durable-objects/mini-agi-do.ts — handleCrossdomainQuery()
// The most complex query type: one question needs data from multiple domains.
// Answer must combine accessible data while being transparent about gaps.

async handleCrossDomainQuery(params: {
  userId: string;
  userRole: string;
  subSpaceId: string;
  question: string;
}): Promise<MiniAGIResponse> {
  const startMs = Date.now();

  // Step 1: Classify question and identify ALL possibly relevant domains
  const classification = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
    max_tokens: 300,
    system: 'You are a data domain classifier for a company intelligence system. Respond only with JSON.',
    messages: [{
      role: 'user',
      content: `Which data domains are needed to answer this question?

Available domains:
${this.getAvailableDomains()}

Question: "${params.question}"

Respond with JSON: {
  "primaryDomains": ["domain-id"],      // essential domains
  "secondaryDomains": ["domain-id"],    // helpful but not required
  "queryType": "lookup|analysis|synthesis|action",
  "estimatedComplexity": "low|medium|high"
}`
    }]
  });

  const { primaryDomains, secondaryDomains, queryType } =
    JSON.parse(classification.content[0].text ?? '{"primaryDomains":[],"secondaryDomains":[]}');

  const allRequiredDomains = [...new Set([...primaryDomains, ...secondaryDomains])];

  // Step 2: Check access for all domains simultaneously
  const accessChecks = await Promise.all(
    allRequiredDomains.map(domainId =>
      this.checkDomainAccess(params.userId, params.userRole, params.subSpaceId, domainId)
    )
  );

  const accessMap = Object.fromEntries(
    allRequiredDomains.map((domainId, i) => [domainId, accessChecks[i]])
  );

  const grantedPrimary = primaryDomains.filter((d: string) => accessMap[d]?.granted);
  const deniedPrimary = primaryDomains.filter((d: string) => !accessMap[d]?.granted);
  const grantedSecondary = secondaryDomains.filter((d: string) => accessMap[d]?.granted);

  // If no primary domains are accessible, the question cannot be answered
  if (grantedPrimary.length === 0) {
    await this.logQuery({
      userId: params.userId,
      question: params.question,
      domainsAccessed: [],
      domainsDenied: primaryDomains,
      answerGiven: null,
      latencyMs: Date.now() - startMs
    });

    return {
      success: false,
      answer: `I cannot answer this question because it requires access to: ${
        deniedPrimary.map((d: string) => this.getDomainName(d)).join(', ')
      }. You don't have permission to access these data domains. Contact your admin to request access.`,
      accessDenied: true,
      deniedDomains: deniedPrimary
    };
  }

  // Step 3: Fetch data from all accessible domains in parallel
  const domainDataPromises = [...grantedPrimary, ...grantedSecondary].map(
    async (domainId: string) => {
      const domain = this.getDomain(domainId);
      if (!domain) return { domainId, data: null, error: 'Domain not found' };

      try {
        // Perform semantic search within this domain's R2 prefix
        const searchResults = await this.env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query(
          await this.getQueryEmbedding(params.question),
          {
            topK: 5,
            filter: { domainId },
            returnMetadata: 'all'
          }
        );

        const data = searchResults.matches
          .filter(m => m.score > 0.65)
          .map(m => m.metadata?.text as string)
          .filter(Boolean)
          .join('

');

        return { domainId, data: data || 'No relevant data found in this domain', error: null };
      } catch (e) {
        return { domainId, data: null, error: String(e) };
      }
    }
  );

  const domainData = await Promise.all(domainDataPromises);

  // Step 4: Synthesize answer from retrieved data
  const dataContext = domainData
    .filter(d => d.data)
    .map(d => `
## ${this.getDomainName(d.domainId)}
${d.data}`)
    .join('
');

  const deniedContext = deniedPrimary.length > 0
    ? `

Note: The following data domains were NOT accessible to this user and are NOT included in the answer: ${deniedPrimary.map((d: string) => this.getDomainName(d)).join(', ')}`
    : '';

  const answer = await this.env.NAELAO_AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
    max_tokens: 1500,
    system: `You are the company's intelligence layer. Your job is to synthesize information from multiple data sources to answer executive questions.

Rules:
1. Only use data from the provided sources — never make up numbers or facts
2. Be specific: cite numbers, dates, and sources when available
3. If data is incomplete or missing for part of the question, say so explicitly
4. If some data domains were inaccessible, mention what additional context they might provide
5. Format your response clearly with headers if covering multiple topics
6. Be concise — executives need actionable insights, not data dumps`,
    messages: [{
      role: 'user',
      content: `Question: ${params.question}

Available Data:
${dataContext}
${deniedContext}`
    }]
  });

  const answerText = answer.content[0].text ?? 'Unable to generate answer.';

  // Step 5: MANDATORY audit log — every query, no exceptions
  await this.logQuery({
    userId: params.userId,
    question: params.question,
    domainsAccessed: [...grantedPrimary, ...grantedSecondary],
    domainsDenied: deniedPrimary,
    answerGiven: answerText.slice(0, 500),
    latencyMs: Date.now() - startMs
  });

  return {
    success: true,
    answer: answerText,
    accessDenied: false,
    domainsQueried: [...grantedPrimary, ...grantedSecondary],
    deniedDomains: deniedPrimary,
    queryType,
    latencyMs: Date.now() - startMs
  };
}

// Helper: get query embedding for semantic search
// Cached for identical queries within the same minute
private async getQueryEmbedding(query: string): Promise<number[]> {
  const cacheKey = `embed:${btoa(query).slice(0, 32)}`;
  const cached = this.ctx.storage.sql
    .exec('SELECT value FROM context_cache WHERE key = ? AND expires_at > ?', cacheKey, Date.now())
    .one();

  if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached.value as string);

  const result = await this.env.NAELAO_AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', {
    text: [query]
  });

  const embedding = result.data[0];
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO context_cache (key, value, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
    cacheKey, JSON.stringify(embedding), Date.now() + 60000
  );

  return embedding;
}

Mini-AGI Data Ingestion Pipeline

The Mini-AGI only knows what you feed it. Data ingestion is how company data gets into the R2/Vectorize system that Mini-AGI queries. There are four ingestion paths:

// Path 1: Manual upload (admin uploads files via UI)
// Files uploaded to R2 at mini-agi/{domainId}/docs/{filename}
// naelao-knowledge Worker chunks + embeds them via Vectorize
// Same pipeline as project knowledge base

// Path 2: AutoResearch agent (Enterprise tier)
// AutoResearch continuously monitors company data sources,
// generates summaries, and ingests them into Mini-AGI domains
// Configured via the Mini-AGI admin panel

// Path 3: Webhook integration (real-time data)
// External systems push data updates via webhooks

async function ingestMiniAGIData(params: {
  domainId: string;
  spaceId: string;
  content: string;
  source: string;
  timestamp: Date;
}, env: Env): Promise<void> {

  const miniAGISpaceId = await getMiniAGISpaceId(params.spaceId, env);

  // Chunk the content
  const chunks = chunkText(params.content, 512, 50);

  // Generate embeddings
  const embeddings = await env.NAELAO_AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', {
    text: chunks.map(c => c.text)
  });

  // Upsert into Vectorize with domain metadata
  const docId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const vectors = chunks.map((chunk, i) => ({
    id: `${params.domainId}:${docId}:${i}`,
    values: embeddings.data[i],
    metadata: {
      domainId: params.domainId,
      spaceId: miniAGISpaceId,
      source: params.source,
      timestamp: params.timestamp.toISOString(),
      text: chunk.text.slice(0, 1000)
    }
  }));

  await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.upsert(vectors);

  // Store raw data in R2 for audit trail
  await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
    `spaces/${miniAGISpaceId}/mini-agi/${params.domainId}/${docId}.txt`,
    params.content
  );
}

// Path 4: Agent-generated reports
// Agents can write summarized data into Mini-AGI domains
// after completing analysis tasks
// e.g., "After analyzing Q1 sales calls, write summary to sales-pipeline domain"
45 — Isolation Tests: Expanded

Space Isolation — Complete Test Implementation

The space isolation tests are the most critical tests in the entire platform. A failure here means a data breach. Every test in this suite must pass with 100% reliability before any production deployment. This section provides the complete, runnable test implementation — not just descriptions.

Complete Test File — tests/suites/04-isolation.test.ts

// tests/suites/04-isolation.test.ts
// Space isolation tests — 100% pass rate required before production deploy
// These tests simulate real attack vectors, not just happy paths

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { env } from 'cloudflare:test';
import { writeTestFile, readTestFile, getTestDO, authRequest } from '../helpers';
import { SELF } from 'cloudflare:test';

const SPACE_A = 'aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa';
const SPACE_B = 'bbbbbbbb-bbbb-bbbb-bbbb-bbbbbbbbbbbb';
const USER_A  = 'user-a-id';
const USER_B  = 'user-b-id';

describe('Suite 04 — Space Isolation (6 Layers)', () => {

  describe('Layer 1: SpaceR2 Path Validation', () => {
    it('blocks path traversal with ..', () => {
      const r2 = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_A);
      expect(() => r2.get('../../etc/passwd')).toThrow('path traversal');
    });

    it('blocks absolute paths', () => {
      const r2 = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_A);
      expect(() => r2.get('/workspace/secret.txt')).toThrow('no leading /');
    });

    it('blocks re-embedding the spaces/ prefix', () => {
      const r2 = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_A);
      expect(() => r2.get(`spaces/${SPACE_B}/secret.txt`)).toThrow("cannot contain 'spaces/'");
    });

    it('correctly prefixes all operations with spaces/{spaceId}/', async () => {
      const r2 = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_A);
      await r2.put('workspace/test.txt', 'hello from space A');

      // Verify the actual R2 key has the space prefix
      const rawObj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(`spaces/${SPACE_A}/workspace/test.txt`);
      expect(rawObj).not.toBeNull();
      expect(await rawObj!.text()).toBe('hello from space A');

      // Verify Space B cannot read the file via SpaceR2
      const r2B = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_B);
      const result = await r2B.get('workspace/test.txt');
      expect(result).toBeNull(); // SpaceR2 for B reads spaces/B/workspace/test.txt — doesn't exist
    });

    it('rejects invalid spaceId format in SpaceR2 constructor', () => {
      expect(() => new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, 'not-a-uuid')).toThrow('Invalid spaceId');
      expect(() => new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, '')).toThrow('Invalid spaceId');
      expect(() => new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, 'spaces/../../etc')).toThrow('Invalid spaceId');
    });
  });

  describe('Layer 2: Durable Object Naming', () => {
    it('different spaceIds produce different DO instances', async () => {
      const idA = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${SPACE_A}:project-1:thread-1`);
      const idB = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${SPACE_B}:project-1:thread-1`);
      expect(idA.toString()).not.toBe(idB.toString());
    });

    it('AgentDO rejects run() request with wrong spaceId', async () => {
      const doId = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${SPACE_A}:project-1:thread-1`);
      const agentDO = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get(doId);

      // Send a run request claiming to be from SPACE_B but targeting SPACE_A's DO
      const resp = await agentDO.fetch(new Request('http://agent/run', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({
          spaceId: SPACE_B, // wrong space
          threadId: 'thread-1',
          input: 'hello',
          backgroundMode: false
        })
      }));

      expect(resp.status).toBe(403);
      const { error } = await resp.json() as { error: string };
      expect(error).toContain('space mismatch');
    });

    it('AssistantDO has unique instance per (spaceId, userId) pair', async () => {
      const idA1 = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(`assistant:${SPACE_A}:${USER_A}`);
      const idA2 = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(`assistant:${SPACE_A}:${USER_B}`);
      const idB1 = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(`assistant:${SPACE_B}:${USER_A}`);

      expect(idA1.toString()).not.toBe(idA2.toString()); // different users, same space
      expect(idA1.toString()).not.toBe(idB1.toString()); // same user, different space
      expect(idA2.toString()).not.toBe(idB1.toString()); // different user, different space
    });
  });

  describe('Layer 1: SpaceDO per-product isolation', () => {
    it('withSpace() adds .eq(space_id) to query', () => {
      const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);
      const filtered = withSpace(SPACE_A)(query);
      // The query string should include space_id filter
      expect(filtered.toString()).toContain(`space_id.eq.${SPACE_A}`);
    });

    it('thread created without space_id is invisible to space queries', async () => {
      // Insert directly without space_id (bypassing withSpace)
      await spaceDO.insertThread(spaceId, 'thread-id', 'user-id', 'Test Thread'); // was: supabase.from('threads').insert({
        id: 'orphan-thread', title: 'Orphan', user_id: USER_A
        // no space_id — this simulates a bug where space_id is missing
      });

      // Query with withSpace — orphan thread should not appear
      const { data } = await withSpace(SPACE_A)(
        spaceDO.getThreads(spaceId)
      );
      expect(data?.find(t => t.id === 'orphan-thread')).toBeUndefined();
    });
  });

  describe('Layer 4: CF Queue Message Validation', () => {
    it('queue consumer rejects message with invalid spaceId format', async () => {
      // Simulate a queue message with a tampered spaceId
      const result = await validateQueueMessage({
        spaceId: 'not-a-uuid; DROP TABLE threads',
        threadId: 'thread-1',
        userId: USER_A,
        input: 'test'
      }, env);

      expect(result.valid).toBe(false);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('invalid spaceId format');
    });

    it('queue consumer validates that userId is a member of spaceId', async () => {
      // USER_A is a member of SPACE_A, not SPACE_B
      const result = await validateQueueMessage({
        spaceId: SPACE_B,
        threadId: 'thread-1',
        userId: USER_A, // not a member of SPACE_B
        input: 'test'
      }, env);

      expect(result.valid).toBe(false);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('not a member');
    });
  });

  describe('Layer 5: AI Gateway Metadata', () => {
    it('createAnthropicClient includes spaceId in cf-aig-metadata', () => {
      const client = createAnthropicClient(env, {
        spaceId: SPACE_A, threadId: 'thread-1', userId: USER_A, model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5'
      });

      const metadata = JSON.parse(
        client.defaultHeaders['cf-aig-metadata'] as string
      );
      expect(metadata.spaceId).toBe(SPACE_A);
    });

    it('two clients with different spaceIds have different metadata', () => {
      const clientA = createAnthropicClient(env, { spaceId: SPACE_A, threadId: 't1', userId: USER_A, model: 'claude-haiku-4-5' });
      const clientB = createAnthropicClient(env, { spaceId: SPACE_B, threadId: 't1', userId: USER_B, model: 'claude-haiku-4-5' });

      const metaA = JSON.parse(clientA.defaultHeaders['cf-aig-metadata'] as string);
      const metaB = JSON.parse(clientB.defaultHeaders['cf-aig-metadata'] as string);

      expect(metaA.spaceId).toBe(SPACE_A);
      expect(metaB.spaceId).toBe(SPACE_B);
      expect(metaA.spaceId).not.toBe(metaB.spaceId);
    });
  });

  describe('Layer 6: Container Naming', () => {
    it('containers for different spaces get different names', () => {
      // Access the private getContainerName via a test shim
      const nameA = getContainerName(SPACE_A, 'project-1');
      const nameB = getContainerName(SPACE_B, 'project-1');
      expect(nameA).not.toBe(nameB);
      expect(nameA).toContain('naelao-');
      expect(nameB).toContain('naelao-');
    });

    it('container name includes spaceId prefix fragment', () => {
      const name = getContainerName(SPACE_A, 'project-1');
      const spaceHex = SPACE_A.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 8);
      expect(name).toContain(spaceHex);
    });
  });

  describe('Cross-Layer Attack Scenarios', () => {
    it('combined attack: SpaceR2 traversal + DO access still blocked', async () => {
      // Attacker in SPACE_B tries to read SPACE_A data by:
      // 1. Using SpaceR2 with SPACE_B credentials
      // 2. Trying to traverse to SPACE_A path
      // Both should be blocked independently

      const r2B = new SpaceR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, SPACE_B);

      // Write data to space A directly (simulating existing Space A data)
      await writeTestFile('secret.txt', 'space-a-secret', SPACE_A);

      // Attempt 1: Path traversal
      expect(() => r2B.get(`../../${SPACE_A}/workspace/secret.txt`))
        .toThrow('path traversal');

      // Attempt 2: Normal read (will read from SPACE_B's prefix — file doesn't exist there)
      const result = await r2B.get('workspace/secret.txt');
      expect(result).toBeNull();

      // Attempt 3: AgentDO with SPACE_B token trying to read SPACE_A DO
      const spaceADO = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get(
        env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${SPACE_A}:project-1:thread-1`)
      );
      const attackResp = await spaceADO.fetch(new Request('http://agent/run', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId: SPACE_B, threadId: 'thread-1', input: 'steal secrets', backgroundMode: false })
      }));
      expect(attackResp.status).toBe(403);
    });

    it('sub-space member cannot access sibling sub-space', async () => {
      // SPACE_A is root. Marketing and Engineering are sub-spaces.
      // Engineering member should not access Marketing data.
      const engineeringSpaceId = 'eng-sub-space-id';
      const marketingSpaceId = 'mkt-sub-space-id';
      const engineerUserId = 'engineer-user';

      // Engineer is member of engineering sub-space only
      const authResult = await validateSpaceMembership(engineerUserId, marketingSpaceId, env);
      expect(authResult.isMember).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});
46 — Agent Definition Spec

Agent Definition JSON — Complete Specification

Every agent in Naelao (platform agents, marketplace agents, SDK agents) is defined by a JSON document stored in SpaceDO SQLite. This section documents every field, its type, its validation rules, and the correct values for each agent tier.

Complete Agent Definition Schema

// types/agent-definition.ts
export interface AgentDefinition {
  // Identity
  id:           string;     // UUID, generated on create
  name:         string;     // max 100 chars, human-readable
  description:  string;     // max 500 chars, shown in marketplace
  version:      string;     // semver: "1.0.0"
  author:       string;     // userId or "naelao" for platform agents
  icon_url?:    string;     // optional, shown in marketplace

  // LLM Configuration
  model:        string;     // model ID from getAvailableModels()
  max_tokens?:  number;     // max output tokens per turn, default 4096
  temperature?: number;     // 0.0-1.0, default 0.7

  // System Prompt
  system_prompt: string;   // the agent's base instructions, up to 100k chars

  // Skills and Capabilities
  allowed_skills: string[]; // skill names from platform/space/agent skill registry
  mcp_configs?:  MCPConfig[]; // external MCP server configurations

  // Execution Configuration
  resource_tier: 'workspace' | 'isolate' | 'browser' | 'sandbox';
                            // minimum tier this agent needs. workspace=cheapest, sandbox=most capable

  // Human-in-the-Loop
  requires_approval_for?: string[]; // action types requiring user approval before execution
  max_iterations?:    number;   // max agent loop iterations, default 50
  timeout_ms?:        number;   // max run duration, default 300000 (5 min)

  // Marketplace Configuration
  marketplace_visible: boolean; // false = private to author's space
  price_usd_per_run?:  number; // null = free, number = creator earns per run
  supported_space_types: string[]; // which space types can install this agent

  // For SDK Agents (deployed externally)
  worker_url?:    string;   // CF Worker URL for SDK agents
  sdk_version?:   string;   // minimum @naelao/agent-sdk version required

  // Metadata
  created_at:   Date;
  updated_at:   Date;
  space_id?:    string;     // null = global marketplace, set = space-private
  status:       'active' | 'deprecated' | 'suspended';
}

// Example: Complete Launchpad Fulfillment Agent definition
export const LAUNCHPAD_FULFILLMENT_AGENT: AgentDefinition = {
  id:          'launchpad-fulfillment-v1',
  name:        'Fulfillment Agent',
  description: 'Automatically processes orders, delivers digital products, and handles receipts for Launchpad businesses.',
  version:     '1.2.0',
  author:      'naelao',
  icon_url:    'https://assets.naelao.dev/icons/fulfillment-agent.png',

  model:       'claude-haiku-4-5',  // haiku for speed and cost on high-volume order processing
  max_tokens:  1024,
  temperature: 0.3,                 // low temperature — fulfillment should be deterministic

  system_prompt: `You are an automated order fulfillment specialist for a digital business...`, // see §11

  allowed_skills: [
    'file-manager',   // to read product files from R2
    'api-caller',     // to call Stripe API for payment verification
    'web-search',     // to look up customer information if needed
  ],
  mcp_configs: [
    { appId: 'stripe-payments', toolsAllowed: ['verify_payment', 'create_refund'] },
    { appId: 'email-sender',    toolsAllowed: ['send_email'] }
  ],

  resource_tier: 'isolate',  // fulfillment doesn't need a container — API calls only

  requires_approval_for: [
    'send_customer_email',  // notify owner before emailing customers
    'issue_refund'          // always require approval for refunds
  ],
  max_iterations: 10,        // fulfillment is a short workflow — 10 iterations is plenty
  timeout_ms:     60000,     // 1 minute max per order

  marketplace_visible:     true,
  price_usd_per_run:       null,   // free platform agent
  supported_space_types:   ['launchpad'],

  status:      'active',
  created_at:  new Date(),
  updated_at:  new Date()
};

SpaceDO Table: agent_definitions

-- Add to SpaceDO constructor schema (already included in the base SpaceDO init)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_definitions (
  id                    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  space_id              UUID REFERENCES spaces(id),   -- null = global marketplace
  name                  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  description           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(description) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  version               TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0.0',
  author                TEXT NOT NULL,                -- userId or 'naelao'
  icon_url              TEXT,

  model                 TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
  max_tokens            INTEGER DEFAULT 4096 CHECK (max_tokens BETWEEN 256 AND 200000),
  temperature           REAL DEFAULT 0.7 CHECK (temperature BETWEEN 0.0 AND 1.0),
  system_prompt         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(system_prompt) BETWEEN 10 AND 100000),

  allowed_skills        TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',          -- array of skill names
  mcp_configs           JSONB DEFAULT '[]',

  resource_tier         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'isolate'
    CHECK (resource_tier IN ('workspace', 'isolate', 'browser', 'sandbox')),

  requires_approval_for TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',
  max_iterations        INTEGER DEFAULT 50 CHECK (max_iterations BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  timeout_ms            INTEGER DEFAULT 300000,

  marketplace_visible   BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  price_usd_per_run     REAL,                         -- null = free
  supported_space_types TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}'::TEXT[],

  worker_url            TEXT,                         -- for SDK agents
  sdk_version           TEXT,

  status                TEXT DEFAULT 'active'
    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'deprecated', 'suspended')),
  created_at            TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at            TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_agent_def_space ON agent_definitions(space_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_agent_def_marketplace ON agent_definitions(marketplace_visible, status)
  WHERE marketplace_visible = true;

-- RLS: platform agents visible to all, space agents only to space members
ALTER TABLE agent_definitions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY agent_def_visibility ON agent_definitions FOR SELECT
  USING (
    space_id IS NULL                                             -- global marketplace
    OR space_id IN (
      SELECT space_id FROM space_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()  -- space member
    )
  );
47 — Launch Checklist

Pre-Launch Checklist — Everything That Must Be True Before Production

This is the definitive checklist before deploying Naelao to production. Every item must be checked off. Items marked BLOCKING must be 100% complete — launching without them is a security vulnerability or data loss risk.

Security Checklist

Item How to Verify Priority
WebSocket origin validation enabled on all WS endpoints Suite 07 test "WebSocket upgrade with non-allowlisted Origin returns 403" passes BLOCKING
SpaceDO schema initialized for all products Run: SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND rowsecurity=false — returns 0 rows BLOCKING
getProductDO() used to resolve SpaceDO in every Worker — never raw SQL from Workers ESLint rule enforcement. Manual audit of all db.query() calls. BLOCKING
All secrets in CF Secrets (not in wrangler.jsonc vars) Check wrangler.jsonc — no API keys, no passwords in vars section BLOCKING
27-pattern skill scanner active for all unverified skills Suite 07 test "SKILL.md with process.env. pattern blocked" passes BLOCKING
NAELAO_MCP_ENCRYPTION_KEY is exactly 32 bytes (decoded) Run: echo $KEY | base64 -d | wc -c — must output 32 BLOCKING
Path traversal prevention active in SpaceR2 and SandboxDO Suite 07 "path traversal: validateContainerPath" tests pass BLOCKING
Memory poisoning prevention: memory schema validates all writes Suite 05 "Memory write rejects prompt injection patterns" passes BLOCKING
Dynamic Workflow spaceId validation on every step dispatch Suite 08 "tampered spaceId in metadata rejected before code load" passes BLOCKING
Federated learning LLM judge threshold enforced (0.95) Suite 13 "entity names in proposal rejected by LLM judge" passes BLOCKING

SSRF prevention in api-caller skill (RFC 1918 blocked) Suite 07 "SSRF: api-caller blocks 10.0.0.1" passes HIGH
