55 — Workflow Examples

Dynamic Workflow Examples — 5 Complete Templates

These five Dynamic Workflow templates cover the most common agent automation patterns. They are stored in R2 under naelao-assets/platform/workflows/templates/ and can be deployed by agents using the workflow-creator skill. Each is a complete, runnable TypeScript file.

Template 1 — Daily Report Workflow

// platform/workflows/templates/daily-report.ts
// Generates a daily summary report and sends to configured channels
// Cron: "0 8 * * 1-5" (8am Mon-Fri)

import { WorkflowEntrypoint, WorkflowEvent, WorkflowStep } from 'cloudflare:workers';

export class DailyReportWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint {
  async run(event: WorkflowEvent<{
    spaceId: string;
    reportConfig: {
      sources: string[];         // data sources to include
      recipients: string[];      // user IDs to notify
      format: 'brief' | 'detailed';
    };
  }>, step: WorkflowStep): Promise<void> {

    const { spaceId, reportConfig } = event.payload;

    // Step 1: Gather data from all configured sources
    const sourceData = await step.do('gather-data', async () => {
      const results: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      for (const source of reportConfig.sources) {
        try {
          const resp = await fetch(
            `https://app.naelao.dev/api/spaces/${spaceId}/data/${source}`,
            { headers: { 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN } }
          );
          results[source] = await resp.json();
        } catch {
          results[source] = { error: `Failed to fetch ${source}` };
        }
      }
      return results;
    });

    // Step 2: Generate report via LLM
    const reportText = await step.do('generate-report', async () => {
      const resp = await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/ai/complete', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'X-Space-Id': spaceId,
          'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
          prompt: `Generate a ${reportConfig.format} daily report from this data:
${JSON.stringify(sourceData, null, 2)}`
        })
      });
      const { text } = await resp.json() as { text: string };
      return text;
    });

    // Step 3: Save report to R2 workspace
    await step.do('save-report', async () => {
      const date = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0];
      await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/write', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'X-Space-Id': spaceId,
          'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          path: `reports/${date}-daily-report.md`,
          content: reportText
        })
      });
    });

    // Step 4: Notify recipients via Space Assistants
    await step.do('notify-recipients', async () => {
      for (const userId of reportConfig.recipients) {
        await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/notifications/send', {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: {
            'X-Space-Id': spaceId,
            'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN
          },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            userId,
            type: 'daily_report',
            message: reportText.slice(0, 500) + (reportText.length > 500 ? '...' : ''),
            channels: ['assistant', 'push']
          })
        });
      }
    });
  }
}

Template 2 — Data Pipeline Workflow

// platform/workflows/templates/data-pipeline.ts
// Runs a data processing pipeline: extract → transform → load
// Triggered by webhook when source data is ready

import { WorkflowEntrypoint, WorkflowEvent, WorkflowStep } from 'cloudflare:workers';

export class DataPipelineWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint {
  async run(event: WorkflowEvent<{
    spaceId: string;
    pipelineConfig: {
      sourceUrl: string;         // where to fetch the raw data
      transformScript: string;   // R2 path to transform TypeScript
      outputPath: string;        // R2 path for processed data
      notifyOnComplete: string[];
    };
  }>, step: WorkflowStep): Promise<void> {

    const { spaceId, pipelineConfig } = event.payload;

    // Step 1: Extract — fetch raw data from source
    const rawData = await step.do('extract', async () => {
      const resp = await fetch(pipelineConfig.sourceUrl);
      if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`Extract failed: ${resp.status} from ${pipelineConfig.sourceUrl}`);
      return resp.text();
    });

    // Step 2: Transform — run transform script via Agent container
    const transformedData = await step.do('transform', async () => {
      // Write raw data to workspace for the container to process
      await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/write', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId, 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN },
        body: JSON.stringify({ path: 'pipeline/raw-input.json', content: rawData })
      });

      // Execute transform script in container
      const execResp = await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/container/exec', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId, 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          command: 'python3',
          args: [pipelineConfig.transformScript],
          env: { INPUT_PATH: '/workspace/pipeline/raw-input.json', OUTPUT_PATH: '/workspace/pipeline/output.json' }
        })
      });

      const { success, stderr } = await execResp.json() as { success: boolean; stderr: string };
      if (!success) throw new Error(`Transform failed: ${stderr}`);

      // Read transformed output
      const outputResp = await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/read', {
        headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId, 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN },
        body: JSON.stringify({ path: 'pipeline/output.json' })
      });
      return (await outputResp.json() as { content: string }).content;
    });

    // Step 3: Load — write processed data to destination
    await step.do('load', async () => {
      await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/write', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId, 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          path: pipelineConfig.outputPath,
          content: transformedData,
          commitMsg: `Data pipeline output: ${new Date().toISOString()}`
        })
      });
    });

    // Step 4: Notify on completion
    await step.do('notify', async () => {
      for (const userId of pipelineConfig.notifyOnComplete) {
        await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/notifications/send', {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId, 'X-Internal-Token': this.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            userId,
            type: 'pipeline_complete',
            message: `Data pipeline complete. Output at: ${pipelineConfig.outputPath}`
          })
        });
      }
    });
  }
}
56 — naelao-analytics Deep Dive

Analytics Engine — All Analytics Events (Never Written to SpaceDO)

Naelao replaces all analytics tables from Suna kortix with Cloudflare Workers Analytics Engine. This gives structured event ingestion with SQL-queryable output at essentially zero cost. Every agent run, every tool call, every billing event, every error — structured, queryable, per-Space. This section documents the complete event schema and query patterns.

Why Workers Analytics Engine Instead of SpaceDO Tables

Inline Analytics Tables — Old Pattern (Do Not Use)

Suna kortix stores analytics in PostgreSQL tables: agent_run_analytics, token_usage, conversation_metrics. This creates write amplification on every agent action (every token usage = a DB write), fills storage quickly (1M agent runs = millions of rows), and requires expensive analytic queries on OLTP storage.

CF Workers Analytics Engine (Naelao)

Workers Analytics Engine is a time-series columnar store optimized for event ingestion and analytics queries. Writes are fire-and-forget (non-blocking). Queries use SQL against a columnar store (100x faster for aggregations). No storage cost beyond $0.25/million events above free tier. Perfect fit for event analytics.

Complete Event Schema

// types/analytics-events.ts
// Every event type that flows through naelao-analytics-queue and into Analytics Engine.
// All events MUST include: spaceId, timestamp, type.
// All events SHOULD include: userId, agentId, threadId where relevant.

export type NaelaoAnalyticsEvent =
  | AgentRunEvent
  | ToolExecutionEvent
  | TokenUsageEvent
  | ErrorEvent
  | BillingEvent
  | UserActionEvent
  | SecurityEvent
  | SystemEvent;

export interface AgentRunEvent {
  type: 'agent_run_start' | 'agent_run_complete' | 'agent_run_failed' | 'agent_run_cancelled';
  spaceId: string;
  userId: string;
  agentId: string;
  threadId: string;
  runId: string;
  agentDefinitionId: string;
  backgroundMode: boolean;
  durationMs?: number;      // set on complete/failed/cancelled
  iterationCount?: number;  // set on complete
  errorCode?: string;       // set on failed
  timestamp: number;        // Unix ms
}

export interface ToolExecutionEvent {
  type: 'tool_execution';
  spaceId: string;
  agentId: string;
  runId: string;
  toolName: string;
  tier: 'workspace' | 'isolate' | 'npm' | 'browser' | 'sandbox';
  success: boolean;
  durationMs: number;
  errorCode?: string;
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface TokenUsageEvent {
  type: 'token_usage';
  spaceId: string;
  userId: string;
  agentId: string;
  runId: string;
  model: string;
  inputTokens: number;
  outputTokens: number;
  cacheReadTokens: number;
  cacheWriteTokens: number;
  costUsd: number;
  cacheHitRate: number;     // 0.0-1.0
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface ErrorEvent {
  type: 'error';
  spaceId: string;
  component: string;        // which Worker/DO threw
  errorCode: string;
  errorMessage: string;
  severity: 'info' | 'warn' | 'error' | 'critical';
  userId?: string;
  agentId?: string;
  runId?: string;
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface BillingEvent {
  type: 'billing_credit' | 'billing_debit' | 'subscription_created' | 'subscription_cancelled';
  spaceId: string;
  userId: string;
  amountUsd: number;
  billingTier?: string;
  reason: string;
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface UserActionEvent {
  type: 'space_created' | 'agent_installed' | 'app_installed' | 'member_invited' | 'skill_added';
  spaceId: string;
  userId: string;
  targetId?: string;        // agentId, appId, memberId, etc.
  metadata?: Record<string, string>;
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface SecurityEvent {
  type: 'security_origin_rejected' | 'security_path_traversal' | 'security_skill_blocked'
      | 'security_injection_detected' | 'security_access_denied' | 'security_rate_limit';
  spaceId?: string;
  ip?: string;
  component: string;
  reason: string;
  blocked: boolean;
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface SystemEvent {
  type: 'sweeper_run' | 'sweeper_task_failed' | 'container_started' | 'container_stopped'
      | 'fiber_recovered' | 'dl_queue_reprocessed';
  component: string;
  metadata?: Record<string, string>;
  timestamp: number;
}

naelao-analytics Worker — Complete Implementation

// workers/analytics/index.ts
// Queue consumer — reads from naelao-analytics-queue and writes to Analytics Engine

export default {
  async queue(
    batch: MessageBatch<NaelaoAnalyticsEvent>,
    env: Env
  ): Promise<void> {
    const dataPoints: AnalyticsEngineDataPoint[] = [];

    for (const msg of batch.messages) {
      const event = msg.body;

      // Map each event type to Analytics Engine data point format
      const dp = mapEventToDataPoint(event);
      if (dp) dataPoints.push(dp);

      msg.ack();
    }

    // Batch write to Analytics Engine (one API call for entire batch)
    // Analytics Engine is the ONLY place we write analytics data.
    // Never write analytics to SpaceDO SQLite — SpaceDO is for structured product data, not event streams.
    if (dataPoints.length > 0) {
      await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS.writeDataPoints(dataPoints);
    }
  }
};

function mapEventToDataPoint(event: NaelaoAnalyticsEvent): AnalyticsEngineDataPoint | null {
  const base = {
    indexes: [event.spaceId ?? 'global', event.type],
    timestamp: new Date(event.timestamp)
  };

  switch (event.type) {
    case 'agent_run_complete':
    case 'agent_run_failed':
    case 'agent_run_cancelled':
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [event.durationMs ?? 0, event.iterationCount ?? 0],
        blobs: [
          event.type, event.userId, event.agentId,
          event.runId, event.agentDefinitionId,
          event.backgroundMode ? 'background' : 'foreground',
          event.errorCode ?? ''
        ]
      };

    case 'tool_execution':
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [event.durationMs, event.success ? 1 : 0],
        blobs: [event.type, event.agentId, event.toolName, event.tier, event.errorCode ?? '']
      };

    case 'token_usage':
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [
          event.inputTokens, event.outputTokens,
          event.cacheReadTokens, event.cacheWriteTokens,
          event.costUsd, event.cacheHitRate
        ],
        blobs: [event.type, event.userId, event.agentId, event.model, event.runId]
      };

    case 'security_origin_rejected':
    case 'security_path_traversal':
    case 'security_skill_blocked':
    case 'security_injection_detected':
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [event.blocked ? 1 : 0],
        blobs: [event.type, event.component, event.reason, event.ip ?? '']
      };

    case 'error':
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [event.severity === 'critical' ? 4 : event.severity === 'error' ? 3 : event.severity === 'warn' ? 2 : 1],
        blobs: [event.type, event.component, event.errorCode, event.errorMessage.slice(0, 200)]
      };

    default:
      return {
        ...base,
        doubles: [],
        blobs: [event.type, JSON.stringify(event).slice(0, 500)]
      };
  }
}

Admin Dashboard Queries

// workers/admin/analytics-queries.ts
// SQL queries against Workers Analytics Engine for the admin dashboard.
// These power the Space Analytics dashboard, billing overview, and error monitoring.

// Query 1: Total token usage by model for a Space in the last 30 days
const TOKEN_USAGE_BY_MODEL = `
  SELECT
    blob4 as model,
    SUM(double1) as total_input_tokens,
    SUM(double2) as total_output_tokens,
    SUM(double3) as total_cache_read_tokens,
    SUM(double5) as total_cost_usd,
    AVG(double6) as avg_cache_hit_rate
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE index1 = '{SPACE_ID}'
    AND blob1 = 'token_usage'
    AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
  GROUP BY model
  ORDER BY total_cost_usd DESC
`;

// Query 2: Agent run success rate by agent definition
const RUN_SUCCESS_RATE = `
  SELECT
    blob3 as agent_definition_id,
    COUNT(*) as total_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_complete' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as successful_runs,
    AVG(double1) as avg_duration_ms,
    SUM(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_complete' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) as success_rate
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE index1 = '{SPACE_ID}'
    AND blob1 IN ('agent_run_complete', 'agent_run_failed', 'agent_run_cancelled')
    AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  GROUP BY agent_definition_id
  ORDER BY total_runs DESC
`;

// Query 3: Tool usage heatmap (which tools are used most)
const TOOL_USAGE_HEATMAP = `
  SELECT
    blob3 as tool_name,
    blob4 as execution_tier,
    COUNT(*) as total_calls,
    AVG(double1) as avg_duration_ms,
    SUM(CASE WHEN double2 = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed_calls
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE index1 = '{SPACE_ID}'
    AND blob1 = 'tool_execution'
    AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  GROUP BY tool_name, execution_tier
  ORDER BY total_calls DESC
  LIMIT 20
`;

// Query 4: Security events in the last 24 hours
const SECURITY_EVENTS_24H = `
  SELECT
    blob1 as event_type,
    blob2 as component,
    blob3 as reason,
    COUNT(*) as occurrences,
    MAX(timestamp) as last_seen
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE index2 LIKE 'security_%'
    AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
  GROUP BY event_type, component, reason
  ORDER BY occurrences DESC
`;
57 — SpaceDO Methods

SpaceDO Methods — Replacing All Stored Functions

Several critical operations in Naelao require stored functions in Supabase PostgreSQL. These functions run inside the database, avoiding round-trips and ensuring atomicity. This section documents every stored function, its purpose, and its complete SQL implementation.

Function 1 — get_llm_formatted_messages

Fetches and formats conversation messages for LLM context injection. This is the most important stored function — called on every agent turn. It returns messages in the exact format needed by the Anthropic SDK.

// workers/naelao-spaces/src/dos/SpaceDO.ts — method implementations
// All former Supabase RPCs are now typed DO methods called via Service Binding.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_llm_formatted_messages(
  p_thread_id UUID,
  p_space_id  UUID,
  p_limit     INTEGER DEFAULT 100,
  p_before    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  role    TEXT,
  content TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER  -- runs as function owner, not caller (allows cross-table reads)
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- RLS check: verify caller has access to this space
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM space_members
    WHERE space_id = p_space_id AND user_id = auth.uid()
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Access denied to space %', p_space_id;
  END IF;

  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT
    m.role,
    m.content,
    m.created_at
  FROM messages m
  WHERE m.thread_id = p_thread_id
    AND m.space_id = p_space_id
    AND m.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (p_before IS NULL OR m.created_at < p_before)
    AND m.role != 'system'  -- system messages are in system_prompt, not messages array
  ORDER BY m.created_at ASC
  LIMIT p_limit;
END;
$$;

Function 2 — get_stale_projects_for_categorization

-- Called by naelao-categorizer cron Worker every hour
-- Returns projects with uncategorized conversations

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_stale_projects_for_categorization(
  p_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 20
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  project_id UUID,
  space_id   UUID,
  thread_count INTEGER,
  last_message_at TIMESTAMPTZ
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT
    p.id AS project_id,
    p.space_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.id)::INTEGER AS thread_count,
    MAX(m.created_at) AS last_message_at
  FROM projects p
  JOIN threads t ON t.project_id = p.id
  JOIN messages m ON m.thread_id = t.id
  WHERE p.status = 'active'
    AND (p.last_categorized_at IS NULL
         OR p.last_categorized_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours')
    AND m.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  GROUP BY p.id, p.space_id
  HAVING COUNT(m.id) > 10  -- only categorize projects with meaningful activity
  ORDER BY last_message_at DESC
  LIMIT p_limit;
END;
$$;

Function 3 — create_space_with_defaults

-- Atomic space creation: creates space + member record + default settings in one transaction
-- Called by naelao-spaces Worker on POST /api/spaces

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_space_with_defaults(
  p_name         TEXT,
  p_type         TEXT,
  p_admin_user_id UUID,
  p_parent_id    UUID DEFAULT NULL,
  p_settings     JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  space_id    UUID,
  slug        TEXT,
  depth       INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_space_id UUID;
  v_slug     TEXT;
  v_depth    INTEGER;
BEGIN
  -- Generate URL-friendly slug from name
  v_slug := LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(p_name, '[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', '-', 'g'));
  v_slug := TRIM(BOTH '-' FROM v_slug);

  -- Ensure slug uniqueness by appending random suffix if needed
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM spaces WHERE slug = v_slug) THEN
    v_slug := v_slug || '-' || SUBSTRING(gen_random_uuid()::TEXT FROM 1 FOR 6);
  END IF;

  -- Calculate depth from parent
  IF p_parent_id IS NULL THEN
    v_depth := 0;
  ELSE
    SELECT depth + 1 INTO v_depth FROM spaces WHERE id = p_parent_id;
    IF v_depth IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Parent space not found: %', p_parent_id;
    END IF;
    IF v_depth > 3 THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Maximum sub-space depth (3) exceeded';
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- Create the space (atomic with member creation below)
  INSERT INTO spaces (name, slug, type, admin_user_id, parent_id, depth, settings)
  VALUES (p_name, v_slug, p_type, p_admin_user_id, p_parent_id, v_depth, p_settings)
  RETURNING id INTO v_space_id;

  -- Add creator as owner
  INSERT INTO space_members (space_id, user_id, role)
  VALUES (v_space_id, p_admin_user_id, 'owner');

  -- Create initial credit balance
  INSERT INTO space_credits (space_id, balance_usd, billing_tier)
  VALUES (v_space_id, 5.00, 'free');  -- $5 free credit on signup

  RETURN QUERY SELECT v_space_id, v_slug, v_depth;
END;
$$;

Function 4 — get_active_assistants

-- Called by naelao-sweeper every 5 minutes to get assistants that need heartbeat
-- Returns only truly active assistants to avoid wasting DO wakeups

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_active_assistants(
  p_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 1000
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  user_id  UUID,
  space_id UUID
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  WITH recent_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      t.user_id,
      t.space_id
    FROM threads t
    WHERE t.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
      AND t.deleted_at IS NULL
    UNION
    -- Also include new members (may not have threads yet)
    SELECT
      sm.user_id,
      sm.space_id
    FROM space_members sm
    WHERE sm.joined_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  )
  SELECT ru.user_id, ru.space_id
  FROM recent_users ru
  JOIN spaces s ON s.id = ru.space_id
  WHERE s.status = 'active'
  LIMIT p_limit;
END;
$$;

Function 5 — deduct_space_credits (Atomic)

-- Called by naelao-billing to atomically deduct credits from a Space
-- Returns success=true + new balance, or success=false if insufficient funds
-- Using a stored function guarantees atomicity without application-level transactions

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION deduct_space_credits(
  p_space_id UUID,
  p_amount   NUMERIC,
  p_reason   TEXT,
  p_run_id   TEXT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  success       BOOLEAN,
  new_balance   NUMERIC,
  error_message TEXT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_current_balance NUMERIC;
  v_new_balance     NUMERIC;
BEGIN
  -- Lock the row to prevent concurrent deductions
  -- PostgreSQL row-level lock via FOR UPDATE
  SELECT balance_usd INTO v_current_balance
  FROM space_credits
  WHERE space_id = p_space_id
  FOR UPDATE;

  IF v_current_balance IS NULL THEN
    RETURN QUERY SELECT FALSE, 0::NUMERIC, 'Space credit record not found';
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  IF v_current_balance < p_amount THEN
    RETURN QUERY SELECT FALSE, v_current_balance,
      format('Insufficient credits: balance $%s, required $%s', v_current_balance, p_amount);
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  v_new_balance := v_current_balance - p_amount;

  -- Update balance
  UPDATE space_credits
  SET balance_usd = v_new_balance, updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE space_id = p_space_id;

  -- Record the transaction
  INSERT INTO credit_transactions (space_id, type, amount_usd, reason, run_id, balance_after)
  VALUES (p_space_id, 'debit', p_amount, p_reason, p_run_id, v_new_balance);

  RETURN QUERY SELECT TRUE, v_new_balance, NULL::TEXT;
END;
$$;
58 — Global Deployment

Multi-Region & Global Deployment — Cloudflare's Edge

Naelao runs natively on Cloudflare's global edge network — 310+ cities worldwide. This section documents what "global" means in practice for each component, where data actually lives, and how to reason about latency for users in different regions.

Where Each Component Lives

Component Where It Runs Data Location Latency Impact
CF Workers (all 22) Nearest CF PoP to the user (310+ locations) Stateless — no data ~5-20ms from user to Worker globally
Durable Objects One location per DO instance. CF pins the DO to the location where it was first accessed. DO SQLite in CF's infrastructure at pinned location ~10-50ms from Worker to DO (cross-region possible)
R2 (naelao-workspace) CF's global storage layer (not region-specific) Globally replicated with CF's storage infrastructure ~10-50ms for R2 reads from any PoP
SpaceDO SQLite SpaceDO: co-located with the CF PoP handling the request (DO placement is automatic) SQLite data in the DO instance, physically near the request origin <3ms for local DO reads — no network hop, no connection pool
CF AI Gateway CF's global edge — nearest PoP handles the request Cached responses at PoP level (if cache hit) ~10ms overhead over direct Anthropic call
CF Containers User's nearest container-capable PoP Container FS is ephemeral. R2 is the persistent store. 2-3s cold start. Warm: same as Worker latency.
CF Browser Rendering CF's browser fleet (specific regions) No persistent data ~200ms cold start for new browser session
CF Queues CF global queue infrastructure Messages replicated globally ~50-100ms for enqueue + worker pick-up

DO Pinning — Critical for Agent Continuity

Durable Objects are pinned to a location when first accessed. If a user in London first accesses their AgentDO, it's pinned in a European CF location. Subsequent requests from the same user route to that location. This is excellent — the DO is near the user's primary access pattern.

The problem: if the user's IP changes (VPN, travel), subsequent requests still go to the same DO location — but now the Worker executing the request is in a different region than the DO. This adds ~50-150ms cross-region latency for DO calls. This is unavoidable and acceptable — DO consistency requires a single location.

// Do NOT try to "optimize" DO location — let CF handle it.
// The worst thing you can do is try to manually pin DOs to specific regions
// by creating them with region-specific names. CF's automatic pinning
// based on first-access is the correct behavior.

// What you SHOULD do: minimize DO round-trips by batching operations.
// Instead of 3 separate DO calls, batch them into one:

// BAD: 3 round-trips to DO
const session = await agentDO.getSession(threadId);
const memory = await agentDO.getMemory();
const fibers = await agentDO.getFibers();

// GOOD: 1 round-trip to DO
const { session, memory, fibers } = await agentDO.getAgentState(threadId);
// The DO handles all reads internally in one request.

Latency Budget — What a Typical Agent Turn Costs

Operation Latency Optimization
User request → naelao-router ~10ms (CF edge) Cannot optimize — this is physics
Auth validation via naelao-auth ~5ms (Service Binding) SpaceDO cache eliminates most DB calls
Message persist to SpaceDO SQLite ~1–3ms (DO local write, no network hop) Fire-and-forget, don't block LLM call
Skill loading from R2 ~30ms (first load) Cached in SkillRegistryDO SQLite after first load
Knowledge search (Vectorize) ~40ms Run in parallel with message persist
LLM first token (Claude Sonnet) ~800-1200ms Prompt caching reduces this to ~300ms on cache hits
Tool execution (Tier 1, R2 read) ~20ms Tier 1 is the fastest — use it when possible
Tool execution (Tier 2, Dynamic Worker) ~50ms Parallel execution for independent tools
Tool execution (Tier 5, Container) ~3000ms cold, ~100ms warm Keep container warm by running tasks batched
Total foreground turn (simple question) ~1200ms (time to first token) With cache hit: ~500ms
Total foreground turn (code execution) ~5000ms (container cold start) Keep container warm: ~500ms warm
59 — Migration Guide

Migrating From Suna Kortix to Naelao — Complete Guide

If you are running a self-hosted Suna kortix instance and want to migrate your existing data and users to Naelao, this section documents the complete migration process. Data migration from PostgreSQL (Suna) to SpaceDO SQLite (Naelao) requires careful handling of space_id assignment — always pass spaceId to every DO method.

Phase 1 — Schema Migration

-- migration/001_add_space_to_existing_data.sql
-- Run this BEFORE any application migration code
-- Creates a default space for all existing Suna kortix data

BEGIN;

-- Create a migration space for existing data
INSERT INTO spaces (id, name, slug, type, admin_user_id, settings)
SELECT
  gen_random_uuid(),
  'Migrated Workspace',
  'migrated-workspace',
  'team',
  (SELECT id FROM auth.users ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1),  -- first user becomes admin
  '{"migrated": true, "migrationDate": "2026-05-01"}'::JSONB
RETURNING id AS migration_space_id;

-- Store the migration space ID for use in subsequent queries
DO $$
DECLARE
  v_migration_space_id UUID;
BEGIN
  SELECT id INTO v_migration_space_id FROM spaces WHERE slug = 'migrated-workspace';

  -- Add all existing users as members of migration space
  INSERT INTO space_members (space_id, user_id, role)
  SELECT v_migration_space_id, id, 'editor'
  FROM auth.users
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

  -- Assign all existing threads to migration space
  UPDATE threads SET space_id = v_migration_space_id WHERE space_id IS NULL;

  -- Assign all existing projects to migration space
  UPDATE projects SET space_id = v_migration_space_id WHERE space_id IS NULL;

  -- Assign all existing agent_runs to migration space
  UPDATE agent_runs SET space_id = v_migration_space_id WHERE space_id IS NULL;

  -- Create credit record for migration space
  INSERT INTO space_credits (space_id, balance_usd, billing_tier)
  VALUES (v_migration_space_id, 50.00, 'pro');  -- generous starting credits for migrated users
END $$;

COMMIT;

-- Verify: no records without space_id
SELECT
  'threads' as table_name, COUNT(*) as null_space_count
  FROM threads WHERE space_id IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT
  'projects', COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE space_id IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT
  'agent_runs', COUNT(*) FROM agent_runs WHERE space_id IS NULL;
-- All should return 0

Phase 2 — File Migration (Docker FS → R2)

#!/bin/bash
# migration/migrate-files.sh
# Migrates agent workspace files from Daytona/Docker to R2
# Requires: AWS CLI configured to talk to R2 (use S3-compatible endpoint)

MIGRATION_SPACE_ID="your-migration-space-id-here"
R2_BUCKET="naelao-workspace"
R2_ENDPOINT="https://{ACCOUNT_ID}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com"

# For each project, copy workspace files to R2 under the correct prefix
while IFS=, read -r project_id local_path; do
  echo "Migrating project: $project_id"

  # Convert local Docker path to R2 prefix
  R2_PREFIX="spaces/${MIGRATION_SPACE_ID}/projects/${project_id}/workspace"

  # Upload all files maintaining directory structure
  aws s3 sync     "$local_path"     "s3://${R2_BUCKET}/${R2_PREFIX}"     --endpoint-url "${R2_ENDPOINT}"     --exclude "*.pyc"     --exclude "__pycache__/*"     --exclude ".git/*"     --delete

  echo "✓ Migrated $project_id: $(aws s3 ls s3://${R2_BUCKET}/${R2_PREFIX}/ --endpoint-url ${R2_ENDPOINT} --recursive | wc -l) files"

done < migration/project-mappings.csv
# project-mappings.csv format:
# project-uuid-1,/var/suna/projects/project-uuid-1/workspace
# project-uuid-2,/var/suna/projects/project-uuid-2/workspace

Phase 3 — Worker/Service Cutover

// migration/cutover-checklist.ts
// Run this script to verify everything is ready before switching DNS to Naelao

async function runCutoverChecks(): Promise<void> {
  const checks = [
    {
      name: 'Schema migration complete',
      check: async () => {
        const result = await db.query(
          "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM threads WHERE space_id IS NULL"
        );
        return parseInt(result.rows[0].count) === 0;
      }
    },
    {
      name: 'R2 file migration complete',
      check: async () => {
        const listing = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.list({ prefix: 'spaces/' });
        return listing.objects.length > 0;
      }
    },
    {
      name: 'All 22 Workers deployed',
      check: async () => {
        const REQUIRED_WORKERS = [
          'naelao-router', 'naelao-auth', 'naelao-agents',
          // ... all 22
        ];
        // Check via CF API that each Worker is deployed
        return true; // implement via wrangler list command
      }
    },
    {
      name: 'Platform skills signed and in R2',
      check: async () => {
        const signaturesObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get('platform/skill-signatures.json');
        if (!signaturesObj) return false;
        const sigs = JSON.parse(await signaturesObj.text());
        return Object.keys(sigs).length === 13;
      }
    },
    {
      name: 'SpaceDO per-product isolation verified',
      check: async () => {
        const result = await db.query(
          "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND rowsecurity=false"
        );
        return parseInt(result.rows[0].count) === 0;
      }
    },
  ];

  for (const { name, check } of checks) {
    const passed = await check().catch(() => false);
    console.log(`${passed ? '✓' : '✗'} ${name}`);
    if (!passed) process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log('
✓ All cutover checks passed. Safe to redirect DNS to Naelao.');
}
60 — Production Observability

Production Observability — Logs, Alerts & Dashboards

Running Naelao in production requires knowing when something is wrong before users complain. This section documents the complete observability setup: what to log, what to alert on, and how to build dashboards from CF Analytics Engine data.

Structured Logging Pattern

// shared/logger.ts
// Structured logging for all Workers. Every log entry is a JSON object.
// CF Workers logs are captured in Workers Logs (Cloudflare Dashboard)
// and optionally forwarded to Logpush (Splunk, Datadog, S3, etc.)

export interface LogEntry {
  level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error' | 'critical';
  message: string;
  component: string;      // which Worker
  spaceId?: string;
  userId?: string;
  agentId?: string;
  runId?: string;
  errorCode?: string;
  durationMs?: number;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
  timestamp: string;      // ISO 8601
}

export class Logger {
  constructor(private component: string, private spaceId?: string) {}

  private log(level: LogEntry['level'], message: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>): void {
    const entry: LogEntry = {
      level,
      message,
      component: this.component,
      spaceId: this.spaceId,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      ...meta
    };

    // In CF Workers, console.log is captured by Workers Logs
    // Always use structured JSON — never use template literals for log messages
    console.log(JSON.stringify(entry));
  }

  debug = (msg: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>) => this.log('debug', msg, meta);
  info  = (msg: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>) => this.log('info',  msg, meta);
  warn  = (msg: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>) => this.log('warn',  msg, meta);
  error = (msg: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>) => this.log('error', msg, meta);

  critical(msg: string, meta?: Partial<LogEntry>): void {
    this.log('critical', msg, meta);
    // Critical logs also go to Analytics Engine for alerting
    // Do NOT await this — fire and forget
    void this.sendToAnalytics({ ...meta, level: 'critical', message: msg });
  }

  private async sendToAnalytics(entry: Partial<LogEntry>): Promise<void> {
    // Implementation: send to naelao-analytics-queue
    // This is separate from console.log to enable alerting on critical events
  }
}

// Usage in any Worker:
const logger = new Logger('naelao-agents', spaceId);
logger.info('Agent run started', { runId, agentDefinitionId, backgroundMode });
logger.error('Agent run failed', { runId, errorCode: 'CONTAINER_TIMEOUT', durationMs: 30001 });

Alert Rules

Alert Name Trigger Condition Severity Response
High Agent Run Failure Rate agent_run_failed > 10% of agent_run_start over 5 minutes Critical Page on-call engineer. Check CF Container availability.
Sweeper Not Running No 'sweeper_run' event in Analytics Engine for > 10 minutes Critical Check naelao-sweeper cron trigger in CF dashboard.
High LLM Latency Average LLM first token > 3000ms over 5 minutes Warning Check CF AI Gateway logs. Verify fallback routing is active.
R2 Write Failures Any SpaceR2.put() error logged in last 5 minutes Critical R2 availability incident. Check Cloudflare status page.
SpaceDO SQLite Latency Average SpaceDO method call > 100ms over 5 minutes Warning Check DO SQLite query plans. Verify indexes exist. Check DO storage usage in CF dashboard.
Security Events Spike > 100 security_* events in 1 minute (any type) Critical Possible attack. Check CF WAF and Bot Management. Enable rate limiting if needed.
Credit Balance Critical Any Space billing_debit event that results in credits_exhausted Warning Automated email to Space admin. No engineer action needed.
DLQ Depth Growing naelao-dlq depth > 100 messages for > 30 minutes Warning Check naelao-sweeper DLQ reprocessing. Manual intervention may be needed.

The Admin Health Dashboard

// Workers Analytics Engine queries that power the admin health dashboard
// Accessible at: /_admin/health (CF Access protected)

// Last 1 hour: key platform metrics
const PLATFORM_HEALTH_QUERY = `
  SELECT
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_start' THEN 1 END) as runs_started,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_complete' THEN 1 END) as runs_completed,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_failed' THEN 1 END) as runs_failed,
    AVG(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_complete' THEN double1 END) as avg_run_duration_ms,
    SUM(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'token_usage' THEN double5 END) as total_cost_usd,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN index2 LIKE 'security_%' THEN 1 END) as security_events,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'error' AND double1 >= 3 THEN 1 END) as error_events
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
`;

// Error rate by component — which Worker is failing?
const ERROR_RATE_BY_COMPONENT = `
  SELECT
    index3 as component,
    COUNT(*) as total_events,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'error' THEN 1 END) as errors,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'error' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*), 2) as error_rate_pct
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  GROUP BY index3
  ORDER BY error_rate_pct DESC
  LIMIT 10
`;

// LLM latency percentiles — model performance tracking
const LLM_LATENCY_PERCENTILES = `
  SELECT
    blob2 as model,
    COUNT(*) as call_count,
    AVG(double1) as avg_ttft_ms,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY double1) as p95_ttft_ms,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY double1) as p99_ttft_ms
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE blob1 = 'llm_response' AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  GROUP BY model
`;

// Top spending spaces — 24h cost breakdown
const TOP_SPACES_BY_COST = `
  SELECT
    index1 as space_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'token_usage' THEN double5 ELSE 0 END) as total_cost_usd,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'agent_run_start' THEN 1 END) as run_count
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
  GROUP BY index1
  ORDER BY total_cost_usd DESC
  LIMIT 20
`;

// Security event timeline — detect attack patterns
const SECURITY_EVENT_TIMELINE = `
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('minute', timestamp) as minute,
    blob2 as event_type,
    COUNT(*) as count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT index1) as unique_spaces
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
    AND index2 LIKE 'security_%'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  ORDER BY 1 DESC, 3 DESC
`;

// Queue health — DLQ depth and processing rate
const QUEUE_HEALTH = `
  SELECT
    blob2 as queue_name,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'queue_message_sent'  THEN 1 END) as sent,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'queue_message_ack'   THEN 1 END) as processed,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'queue_message_retry' THEN 1 END) as retried,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN blob1 = 'queue_message_dlq'   THEN 1 END) as dead_lettered
  FROM naelao_analytics
  WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  GROUP BY queue_name
`;

Logpush Configuration — Exporting to External SIEM

For Enterprise Spaces with compliance requirements (HIPAA, SOC 2), CF Logpush streams all Worker logs to an external SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, S3). Configure once at the CF account level:

# CF Logpush to Datadog — run during initial account setup
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CF_ACCOUNT_ID/logpush/jobs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "naelao-workers-logpush",
    "dataset": "workers_trace_events",
    "destination_conf": "datadog://https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/api/v2/logs?header_DD-API-KEY='$DD_API_KEY'&ddsource=cloudflare&ddtags=env:prod,service:naelao",
    "logpull_options": "fields=Event,EventTimestampMs,Outcome,Logs,ScriptName×tamps=rfc3339",
    "filter": "{\"where\":{\"and\":[{\"key\":\"ScriptName\",\"operator\":\"StartsWith\",\"value\":\"naelao-\"}]}}",
    "enabled": true
  }'

On-Call Runbook — Top 5 Alert Responses

Alert Immediate Action Recovery
High Agent Run Failure Rate Check status.cloudflare.com for Container incidents. If containers are down: set NAELAO_CONTAINER_DISABLED=1 in CF env vars — agents will reject container-tier tasks gracefully instead of hanging. When containers recover, remove the env var. Sweeper auto-retries queued runs.
Sweeper Not Running CF Dashboard → Workers → naelao-sweeper → Triggers tab. If cron is missing, redeploy: npx wrangler deploy. Check Workers Logs for crash in the sweeper's main handler. Once running, abandoned runs clean up within 5 minutes (next sweeper cycle).
SpaceDO SQLite Performance Degradation Check DO metrics in Cloudflare dashboard. For large products hitting DO SQLite limits (>10GB), consider promoting sub-spaces to separate products. Run TOP_SPACES_BY_COST to check if one space is in a DB-hammering loop. If a workflow is causing the spike: POST /_admin/workflows/{id}/pause.
Security Events Spike Run SECURITY_EVENT_TIMELINE to identify attack type. If from authenticated users (valid JWTs), query GET /_admin/audit/{spaceId} and suspend the space if needed. Enable CF Bot Management's "Definitely Automated" challenge mode for high volume — does not affect authenticated API calls.
DLQ Depth Growing GET /_admin/dlq/messages to inspect payloads. Identify the common error. Check git log for recent code changes to the queue's consumer Worker. Fix bug → deploy. Reprocess with POST /_admin/dlq/retry/{messageId}. Bulk retry via the ops playbook drain script.
61 — Space Type Architecture

Space Types — Platform Instances, Not Configuration

The original Naelao design treated Space Types as configuration bundles — a manifest that installs default agents and skills. This is wrong. A Space Type is a platform definition. When a user creates a space and selects a type, they are spinning up an instance of a specific platform with its own agent architecture, execution environment, UI, backend systems, and permissions model. This section is the authoritative rewrite.

"Naelao is the operating system. Space Types are the applications that run on it. A Standard space and a Launchpad space are as different from each other as a terminal and a spreadsheet app."

The Three Layers of Every Space Type

Layer 1 — Most Important
Agent Environment

Defines how agents work inside this space type. Which execution tier is default. Container idle timeout. Always-loaded skills. Disabled skills. Agent loop model (chat loop, file-edit loop, knowledge-graph loop, task-completion loop). What the agent can access and what it cannot.

A Cursor-like type: warm container always, file-edit loop. A CoWork-like type: no container, task-completion loop. An Excel-like type: spreadsheet engine, no bash. A Verticals type: knowledge-graph loop, long context, restricted network.

Layer 2
Backend Infrastructure

Which platform DOs are instantiated (WalletDO, MiniAGIDO, etc.), which custom DOs the space type brings, which Dynamic Workflows are registered, which cron jobs run, what SpaceDO schema version each product is on.

Verticals: AutoResearchDO running nightly, KnowledgeGraphDO, benchmark system, fine-tuning pipeline. Standard: none of that. Idle cost for both is near zero — backend systems cost only when active.

Layer 3
UI — Two Surfaces

Operator console at naelao.app/spaces/{id} — always Naelao-branded back-office. Apps inject panels into shell slots. Space type manifest defines sidebar, dashboard, hidden nav items.

External portal at {slug}.naelao.com — public-facing, zero Naelao chrome, custom domain support. Only for types with a public face (Launchpad storefront, Sites website, Workers marketplace, Verticals client portal).

Space Type Manifest v2 — Complete Interface

The old manifest was thin. This is the complete manifest that captures all three layers.

// types/space-type-manifest-v2.ts
// Every space type — platform or community — must implement this interface.
// The platform reads this manifest to provision, operate, and deprovision a space instance.

export interface NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2 {
  // ── Identity ─────────────────────────────────────────
  id:          string;          // e.g. 'launchpad', 'verticals', 'com.creator.my-type'
  name:        string;
  description: string;
  version:     string;          // semver. Minor = auto-upgrade. Major = opt-in migration.
  author:      'naelao' | string; // userId for community types
  icon:        string;          // URL to 128x128 icon
  tags:        string[];        // for marketplace search

  // ── Layer 1: Agent Environment ────────────────────────
  agentEnvironment: {
    defaultExecutionTier: 'workspace' | 'isolate' | 'browser' | 'sandbox';
    containerIdleTimeoutMs: number;   // 0 = no container. -1 = never idle (always warm).
    loopModel: AgentLoopModel;
    alwaysLoadedSkills: string[];     // skill IDs always in context, regardless of user config
    disabledSkills:     string[];     // skills agents in this type CANNOT use
    networkPolicy: 'open' | 'restricted' | 'none';
    networkAllowlist?: string[];      // if restricted: only these domains allowed
    memorySchemaOverride?: JSONSchema; // override agent_memory schema for this type
    maxContextTokens:  number;        // context window limit for this type
    agentPermissions:  string[];      // e.g. ['wallet_spend', 'external_deploy', 'read_cross_space']
    // Note: customLoopWorker (RemoteLoop) is reserved for Naelao platform types only.
    // Community developers requiring custom agent reasoning should use the Apps SDK
    // and publish an App with a custom MCP server instead.
  };

  // ── Layer 2: Backend Infrastructure ──────────────────
  backend: {
    platformDOs: PlatformDOConfig[];      // which platform DOs to instantiate on provision
    spaceDoInitHook?: string;             // optional SpaceDO.initSpaceType() hook name for this space type
    workflowTemplates: WorkflowTemplate[];
    cronJobs: CronJobDeclaration[];       // declared cron work that runs for this type
    r2Prefixes: string[];                 // which R2 sub-prefixes to initialize on provision
    resourceBudget: ResourceBudget;       // REQUIRED — defines per-instance compute limits
  };

  // ── Layer 3: UI ───────────────────────────────────────
  ui: {
    operatorShell: {
      sidebarItems:    SidebarItem[];     // what shows in the left nav
      dashboardWidgets:string[];          // app IDs that inject dashboard widgets
      hiddenCoreItems: string[];          // hide default Naelao nav: 'threads'|'projects'|'marketplace'
      defaultView:     string;            // which sidebar item opens by default
      theme?:          ThemeConfig;
    };
    externalPortal?: {
      enabled:      boolean;
      deploymentType: 'cf-pages' | 'dynamic-worker';
      templateId:   string;              // which portal template to use
      defaultSlug:  string;              // {defaultSlug}.naelao.com
      customDomain: boolean;             // allow custom domain configuration
      authModel:    'public' | 'customer-auth' | 'gated';
    };
  };

  // ── Provisioning Lifecycle ────────────────────────────
  lifecycle: {
    provisionerWorker?:   string;        // URL called after platform provisioning, for custom setup
    deprovisionerWorker?: string;        // URL called before platform deprovisioning
    migratorWorker?:      string;        // required if version is a major bump
    healthCheckUrl?:      string;        // platform polls this to verify instance health
  };

  // ── Marketplace & Economics ───────────────────────────
  marketplace: {
    visible:          boolean;
    minimumNaelaoPlan:'free'|'maker'|'pro'|'team'|'enterprise';
    priceUsdPerMonth: number;            // 0 = free. Creator gets 80% of this.
    trialDays:        number;
    capabilities:     string[];          // declared capabilities for user review before install
  };
}

// Agent loop models — defines how the agent processes each turn
export type AgentLoopModel =
  | 'chat'           // default: user message → LLM → tool calls → response
  | 'file-edit'      // cursor-like: user intent → read files → edit files → verify → respond
  | 'knowledge-graph'// verticals: query → graph traversal → verify → respond
  | 'task-completion'// cowork-like: task assigned → decompose → execute → deliver
  | 'content'        // sites: research → draft → review → publish
  | 'remote'         // custom: delegate to customLoopWorker
  ;

export interface ResourceBudget {
  maxDOsPerInstance:       number;   // how many custom DOs this type creates per space
  maxR2WritesPerDay:       number;
  maxContainerHoursPerDay: number;
  maxLLMTokensPerDay:      number;
  maxCronJobsPerInstance:  number;
  maxWorkflowsPerInstance: number;
}

Network policy open open restricted open open

Always-loaded skills file-manager, web-search stripe, email, web-search knowledge-graph, literature-search cms, seo, deploy git-ops, code-exec, artifact-builder

62 — SpaceTypeRegistryDO & Provisioner

SpaceTypeRegistryDO — The Space Type Marketplace Engine

SpaceTypeRegistryDO is a Durable Object that serves as the single source of truth for all registered Space Types. Space Types are exclusively authored and published by Naelao. Community developers do not create Space Types — they create Apps (MCP Servers + UI) and Space Templates (curated starting configurations). One instance: idFromName('global-space-type-registry').

SpaceTypeRegistryDO Schema

// durable-objects/space-type-registry-do.ts
// ONE global instance. ID: idFromName('global-space-type-registry')
// This is the only global singleton DO in Naelao.
// It is read-heavy (every space creation reads it) and write-rare (new versions infrequent).
// Cache responses aggressively in KV.

export class SpaceTypeRegistryDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_types (
        id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name            TEXT NOT NULL,
        description     TEXT NOT NULL,
        author          TEXT NOT NULL,
        current_version TEXT NOT NULL,
        manifest        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2
        status          TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'
          CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','suspended','deprecated')),
        visible         INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        price_usd       REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
        install_count   INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        rating_avg      REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
        rating_count    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        security_scan   TEXT,             -- JSON: last scan result
        reviewed_at     INTEGER,
        created_at      INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        updated_at      INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS versions (
        type_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES space_types(id),
        version     TEXT NOT NULL,
        manifest    TEXT NOT NULL,        -- snapshot of manifest at this version
        change_type TEXT NOT NULL         -- 'minor' | 'major'
          CHECK (change_type IN ('minor','major')),
        canary_pct  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,    -- 0-100: percentage of instances on this version
        stable      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,    -- 1 = fully rolled out
        published_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        PRIMARY KEY (type_id, version)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS earnings (
        id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
        type_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
        author_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
        space_id    TEXT NOT NULL,        -- the instance that generated this earning
        amount_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
        period      TEXT NOT NULL,        -- YYYY-MM
        paid        INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        recorded_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS instances (
        type_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES space_types(id),
        space_id    TEXT NOT NULL,        -- which user space is running this type
        version     TEXT NOT NULL,
        status      TEXT DEFAULT 'running'
          CHECK (status IN ('provisioning','running','migrating','deprovisioning','error')),
        installed_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        PRIMARY KEY (type_id, space_id)
      );
    `);
  }

  // Register a new space type (internal Naelao platform use only — NOT a public API)
  // Community developers do not call this. Space Types are exclusively Naelao-authored.
  async registerSpaceType(params: {
    manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2;
    authorId: string; // must be 'naelao' — validated, any other value is rejected
  }): Promise<{ accepted: boolean; reason?: string; scanId?: string }> {

    // 1. Validate manifest schema
    const schemaErrors = validateManifestSchema(params.manifest);
    if (schemaErrors.length) {
      return { accepted: false, reason: `Manifest validation failed: ${schemaErrors.join(', ')}` };
    }

    // 2. Enforce Naelao-only authorship. Space Types are platform-internal only.
    if (params.authorId !== 'naelao') {
      return { accepted: false, reason: 'Space Types are exclusively authored by Naelao. Community developers publish Apps or Space Templates instead.' };
    }

    // 3. Validate resource budget is declared
    if (!params.manifest.backend.resourceBudget) {
      return { accepted: false, reason: 'Resource budget declaration required for all space types' };
    }

    // 4. Platform types auto-approved — no community review pipeline needed
    const status = 'approved';

    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO space_types
         (id, name, description, author, current_version, manifest, status, visible, price_usd)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      params.manifest.id,
      params.manifest.name,
      params.manifest.description,
      params.authorId,
      params.manifest.version,
      JSON.stringify(params.manifest),
      status,
      status === 'approved' ? 1 : 0,
      params.manifest.marketplace.priceUsdPerMonth
    );

    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      `INSERT INTO versions (type_id, version, manifest, change_type, canary_pct, stable)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'minor', 100, 1)`,
      params.manifest.id, params.manifest.version, JSON.stringify(params.manifest)
    );

    return { accepted: true };
  }

  async getSpaceType(typeId: string): Promise<NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2 | null> {
    const row = this.ctx.storage.sql
      .exec('SELECT manifest FROM space_types WHERE id = ? AND status = ?', typeId, 'approved')
      .one();
    if (!row) return null;
    return JSON.parse(row.manifest as string);
  }

  async listMarketplace(filter?: { tags?: string[]; maxPrice?: number }): Promise<SpaceTypeListing[]> {
    let query = `
      SELECT id, name, description, author, current_version,
             price_usd, install_count, rating_avg, rating_count
      FROM space_types
      WHERE status = 'approved' AND visible = 1
    `;
    if (filter?.maxPrice !== undefined) {
      query += ` AND price_usd <= ${filter.maxPrice}`;
    }
    query += ' ORDER BY install_count DESC LIMIT 100';
    return this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(query).toArray() as SpaceTypeListing[];
  }

  // Record a new instance of a space type being created
  async recordInstall(typeId: string, spaceId: string, version: string): Promise<void> {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO instances (type_id, space_id, version) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
      typeId, spaceId, version
    );
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
      'UPDATE space_types SET install_count = install_count + 1 WHERE id = ?', typeId
    );
  }
}

The Space Provisioner — Complete Implementation

When a user creates a space, the provisioner runs. It is the most critical lifecycle function in the entire Space Type system. If provisioning fails partway through, it must roll back cleanly — leaving no orphaned DOs, R2 prefixes, or SpaceDO SQLite records.

// workers/spaces/provisioner.ts
// Called by naelao-spaces Worker on POST /api/spaces when a type is selected.
// Transactional: on any failure, deprovisionSpace() is called to clean up.

export async function provisionSpace(params: {
  spaceId: string;
  typeId:  string;
  userId:  string;
  name:    string;
  env:     Env;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; error?: string }> {

  const { spaceId, typeId, userId, name, env } = params;

  // Load manifest from SpaceTypeRegistryDO (cached in KV)
  let manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2;
  const cached = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(`space-type-manifest:${typeId}`, 'json');
  if (cached) {
    manifest = cached as NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2;
  } else {
    const registryDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_TYPE_REGISTRY.get(
      env.NAELAO_SPACE_TYPE_REGISTRY.idFromName('global-space-type-registry')
    );
    const manifestResp = await registryDO.fetch(
      new Request(`http://registry/type/${typeId}`)
    );
    if (!manifestResp.ok) {
      return { success: false, error: `Space type not found: ${typeId}` };
    }
    manifest = await manifestResp.json();
    await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(
      `space-type-manifest:${typeId}`,
      JSON.stringify(manifest),
      { expirationTtl: 3600 }
    );
  }

  const provisioned: string[] = []; // track what's been done for rollback

  try {
    // Step 1: Create SpaceDO instance and initialize schema
    const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
    await db.query(
      'SELECT create_space_with_defaults($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
      [name, typeId, userId, null, JSON.stringify({ manifestVersion: manifest.version })]
    );
    provisioned.push('space_do');

    // Step 2: Initialize SpaceDO
    const spaceDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(
      env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName(`space:${spaceId}`)
    );
    await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/init', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, typeId, manifest })
    }));
    provisioned.push('space-do');

    // Step 3: Instantiate declared platform DOs
    for (const doConfig of manifest.backend.platformDOs) {
      await instantiatePlatformDO(doConfig, spaceId, env);
      provisioned.push(`platform-do:${doConfig.type}`);
    }

    // Step 4: Initialize R2 prefixes
    for (const prefix of manifest.backend.r2Prefixes) {
      await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
        `spaces/${spaceId}/${prefix}/.keep`,
        '',
        { customMetadata: { initializedAt: Date.now().toString() } }
      );
      provisioned.push(`r2:${prefix}`);
    }

    // Step 5: SpaceDO.initSpaceType() handles any space-type-specific initialization
    // Space type initialization is handled by spaceDO.initSpaceType(spaceType) — no SQL migration files needed.
      const migObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(migrationPath);
      if (migObj) {
        const sql = await migObj.text();
        // Replace placeholder with actual spaceId
        const scopedSql = sql.replace(/\{SPACE_ID\}/g, spaceId);
        await db.query(scopedSql);
        provisioned.push(`migration:${migrationPath}`);
      }
    }

    // Step 6: Register workflow templates
    if (manifest.backend.workflowTemplates.length > 0) {
      const workflowRegDO = env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW_REG.get(
        env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW_REG.idFromName(`wfreg:${spaceId}:global`)
      );
      for (const template of manifest.backend.workflowTemplates) {
        await workflowRegDO.fetch(new Request('http://registry/register-template', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, template })
        }));
      }
      provisioned.push('workflow-templates');
    }

    // Step 7: Deploy external portal (if declared)
    if (manifest.ui.externalPortal?.enabled) {
      await provisionExternalPortal(spaceId, manifest, env);
      provisioned.push('external-portal');
    }

    // Step 8: Call custom provisioner Worker (community types)
    if (manifest.lifecycle.provisionerWorker) {
      const customResp = await callCustomWorker(
        manifest.lifecycle.provisionerWorker,
        spaceId,
        { action: 'provision', spaceId, typeId, userId },
        env
      );
      if (!customResp.ok) {
        throw new Error(`Custom provisioner failed: ${await customResp.text()}`);
      }
      provisioned.push('custom-provisioner');
    }

    // Step 9: Create Space Assistant for the user
    const assistantDO = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.get(
      env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(`assistant:${spaceId}:${userId}`)
    );
    await assistantDO.fetch(new Request('http://assistant/init', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, userId, spaceType: typeId })
    }));
    provisioned.push('assistant');

    // Step 10: Record install in SpaceTypeRegistryDO
    await env.NAELAO_SPACE_TYPE_REGISTRY.get(
      env.NAELAO_SPACE_TYPE_REGISTRY.idFromName('global-space-type-registry')
    ).fetch(new Request('http://registry/record-install', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ typeId, spaceId, version: manifest.version })
    }));

    return { success: true };

  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[PROVISIONER] Failed at step: ${provisioned[provisioned.length - 1]}`, error);

    // Rollback everything that was provisioned
    await deprovisionSpace({ spaceId, typeId, provisioned, env });
    return { success: false, error: (error as Error).message };
  }
}

// Deprovisioner — called on space deletion OR on provisioning rollback
export async function deprovisionSpace(params: {
  spaceId:    string;
  typeId:     string;
  provisioned?: string[];  // if rollback: only deprovision what was provisioned
  env:        Env;
}): Promise<void> {
  const { spaceId, typeId, provisioned, env } = params;

  const manifest = await getManifest(typeId, env);
  if (!manifest) return;

  // Call custom deprovisioner first (before platform cleanup)
  if (manifest.lifecycle.deprovisionerWorker &&
      (!provisioned || provisioned.includes('custom-provisioner'))) {
    await callCustomWorker(
      manifest.lifecycle.deprovisionerWorker,
      spaceId,
      { action: 'deprovision', spaceId, typeId },
      env
    ).catch(e => console.error('[DEPROVISIONER] Custom deprovisioner failed:', e));
  }

  // Delete external portal
  if (manifest.ui.externalPortal?.enabled) {
    await deleteExternalPortal(spaceId, env).catch(console.error);
  }

  // Delete all R2 objects under this space prefix
  await deleteR2Prefix(`spaces/${spaceId}/`, env);

  // Delete SpaceDO data: call spaceDO.purge() which handles cascade internally
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  await db.query('UPDATE spaces SET status = $1 WHERE id = $2', ['deleted', spaceId]);

  // Note: DOs are not explicitly deleted — they expire naturally after 30 days of no access.
  // All DO data is spaceId-scoped so it cannot be accessed after the space is deleted (RLS blocks it).

  console.log(`[DEPROVISIONER] Space ${spaceId} (${typeId}) deprovisioned successfully`);
}
63 — External Portal System

External Portals — {slug}.naelao.com & Custom Domains

Some space types have a public-facing component separate from the operator console. A Launchpad space has a customer storefront. A Sites space IS a website. A Verticals space has a client portal. A Workers space has a talent marketplace. These external portals are provisioned automatically when the space is created, have zero Naelao chrome, and support custom domains.

Portal Deployment Architecture

Two Portal Deployment Models
Model A: Dynamic Worker Portal
→ content in R2 →
Dynamic Worker Loader serves HTML
→
{slug}.naelao.com
Model B: CF Pages Portal
→ static build in R2 →
CF Pages project
→
{slug}.naelao.com
Both models support custom domains via CF Custom Domains API. Dynamic Worker = instant updates. CF Pages = better for complex SPAs.
// workers/spaces/portal-provisioner.ts

export async function provisionExternalPortal(
  spaceId: string,
  manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2,
  env: Env
): Promise<{ portalUrl: string; customDomainEnabled: boolean }> {

  const portalConfig = manifest.ui.externalPortal!;
  const slug = await generateUniqueSlug(portalConfig.defaultSlug, spaceId, env);

  if (portalConfig.deploymentType === 'dynamic-worker') {
    // Copy the portal template to this space's R2 prefix
    const templateObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(
      `portal-templates/${portalConfig.templateId}/index.ts`
    );
    if (!templateObj) throw new Error(`Portal template not found: ${portalConfig.templateId}`);

    const templateCode = await templateObj.text();

    // Inject space context into the template
    const portalCode = templateCode
      .replace('{{SPACE_ID}}', spaceId)
      .replace('{{PORTAL_SLUG}}', slug)
      .replace('{{AUTH_MODEL}}', portalConfig.authModel)
      .replace('{{NAELAO_API_BASE}}', env.NAELAO_API_BASE);

    // Store the portal code in R2 under the space prefix
    await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
      `spaces/${spaceId}/portal/index.ts`,
      portalCode
    );

    // Register the slug → spaceId mapping in KV
    // The naelao-portal Worker reads this to route requests
    await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(`portal-slug:${slug}`, spaceId);
    await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(`portal-space:${spaceId}`, slug);

    const portalUrl = `https://${slug}.naelao.com`;

    // Store portal config in SpaceDO
    const spaceDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(
      env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName(`space:${spaceId}`)
    );
    await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/set-portal', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ portalUrl, slug, deploymentType: 'dynamic-worker', authModel: portalConfig.authModel })
    }));

    return { portalUrl, customDomainEnabled: portalConfig.customDomain };

  } else {
    // CF Pages deployment — for complex SPA portals
    // Create a new CF Pages project via API
    const pagesProject = await fetch(
      `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/pages/projects`,
      {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.CF_API_TOKEN}`,
          'Content-Type': 'application/json'
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          name: `naelao-portal-${slug}`,
          production_branch: 'main',
          source: {
            type: 'github', // or upload-based
          }
        })
      }
    ).then(r => r.json());

    const portalUrl = `https://${slug}.naelao.com`;
    return { portalUrl, customDomainEnabled: portalConfig.customDomain };
  }
}

// naelao-portal Worker — handles all {*.naelao.com} requests
// Routes to the correct space's portal code
export const PORTAL_WORKER = {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const host = request.headers.get('Host') ?? '';

    // Extract slug from host: {slug}.naelao.com
    const slugMatch = host.match(/^([a-z0-9-]+)\.naelao\.com$/);
    if (!slugMatch) return new Response('Not Found', { status: 404 });

    const slug = slugMatch[1];

    // Look up spaceId from slug
    const spaceId = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(`portal-slug:${slug}`);
    if (!spaceId) return new Response('Portal not found', { status: 404 });

    // Load portal code from R2
    const portalObj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(`spaces/${spaceId}/portal/index.ts`);
    if (!portalObj) return new Response('Portal not configured', { status: 503 });

    const portalCode = await portalObj.text();

    // Execute via Dynamic Worker Loader
    // The portal code is a CF Worker that handles the request
    const loaderDO = env.NAELAO_DW_LOADER.get(
      env.NAELAO_DW_LOADER.idFromName(`portal:${spaceId}`)
    );

    return loaderDO.fetch(new Request('http://loader/execute', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        code: portalCode,
        request: {
          url: request.url,
          method: request.method,
          headers: Object.fromEntries(request.headers.entries()),
          body: await request.text()
        }
      })
    }));
  }
};

Custom Domain Configuration

// Operator flow: Space Settings → Portal → Custom Domain → enter domain
// POST /api/spaces/{spaceId}/portal/custom-domain

export async function configureCustomDomain(params: {
  spaceId: string;
  domain:  string;  // e.g., 'mystore.com'
  env:     Env;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; verificationRecord?: string }> {

  const { spaceId, domain, env } = params;

  // 1. Add the domain to CF Custom Domains via API
  const customDomainResp = await fetch(
    `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/workers/domains`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.CF_API_TOKEN}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        environment: 'production',
        hostname: domain,
        service: 'naelao-portal',  // the portal Worker
        zone_id: env.CF_ZONE_ID
      })
    }
  ).then(r => r.json());

  if (!customDomainResp.success) {
    return { success: false };
  }

  // 2. Store the custom domain → spaceId mapping in KV
  await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(`portal-custom-domain:${domain}`, spaceId);

  // 3. Update naelao-portal Worker to also check custom domains
  // The portal Worker checks both slug.naelao.com AND custom domain mappings

  return {
    success: true,
    verificationRecord: `_naelao-verify.${domain} TXT naelao-${spaceId.slice(0, 8)}`
  };
}
64 — Community Contribution

Community Contribution — Apps & Space Templates

Architecture Decision: Naelao Owns Space Types

Space Types are exclusively authored by Naelao. Community developers do not create Space Types. This decision eliminates the entire class of risks associated with community-authored infrastructure: arbitrary provisioner code, third-party RemoteLoop Workers receiving all user conversation data, community SpaceDO schema changes against the per-product database, and complex multi-tenant security review pipelines.

The community contributes through two clean, safe primitives: Apps (MCP Servers + UI, running on the developer's own Cloudflare account) and Space Templates (curated configuration bundles with no executable code). Together these create a rich ecosystem without exposing platform infrastructure to third-party code.

For the complete community model, see Community Contribution Model and Space Templates. For the App publishing system, see Naelao Apps Economy.

Scoped Token — Retained for Internal Use

The Scoped Token mechanism (short-lived HMAC-signed tokens granting per-space R2 and DB access) is still used internally — by RemoteLoop Workers within Naelao-authored Space Types, and by the external portal SDK (@naelao/portal-sdk). It is not exposed to community developers as a general integration mechanism.

// shared/scoped-token.ts — INTERNAL USE ONLY
// Used by: RemoteLoop (Naelao platform types), @naelao/portal-sdk (external portals)
// NOT used by: community Apps (use MCP OAuth instead), Space Templates (no code)

export interface ScopedToken {
  spaceId:     string;
  typeId:      string;
  permissions: string[];    // subset of declared capabilities from manifest
  expiresAt:   number;      // short-lived: 5 minutes
  signature:   string;      // HMAC-SHA256 signed by platform key
}

export async function generateScopedToken(params: {
  spaceId:     string;
  typeId:      string;
  permissions: string[];
  env:         Env;
}): Promise<string> {
  const token: Omit<ScopedToken, 'signature'> = {
    spaceId:     params.spaceId,
    typeId:      params.typeId,
    permissions: params.permissions,
    expiresAt:   Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000
  };
  const payload = JSON.stringify(token);
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    'raw',
    new TextEncoder().encode(params.env.NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN),
    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    false, ['sign']
  );
  const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, new TextEncoder().encode(payload));
  const signature = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(sig)));
  return btoa(JSON.stringify({ ...token, signature }));
}

The Task-Completion Loop

Unlike the Standard chat loop where the agent waits for user input, the task-completion loop is designed for headless background execution. When a webhook arrives, the Naelao Router bypasses the UI entirely and wakes the AgentDO directly.

// agentpress/loops/task-completion.ts
// The isolated execution loop for Launchpad agents.
// Optimizes for speed, low token usage, and strict success/fail states.

export async function executeTaskCompletionLoop(
  triggerEvent: WebhookEvent,
  agentDO: NaelaoAgentDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  
  // 1. Generate system prompt based strictly on the webhook payload
  const messages = [
    { 
      role: 'user', 
      content: `Execute fulfillment for the following event: \n${JSON.stringify(triggerEvent)}` 
    }
  ];

  let iterations = 0;
  const MAX_ITERATIONS = 5; // Strict limit. Fulfillment should be fast.

  while (iterations < MAX_ITERATIONS) {
    iterations++;

    // 2. Call LLM (Haiku is preferred here for speed/cost)
    const response = await agentDO.callLLM({
      messages,
      model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
      temperature: 0.1 // Highly deterministic
    });

    messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: response.content });

    // 3. If no tool calls, the task is considered complete.
    if (!response.toolCalls || response.toolCalls.length === 0) {
      await agentDO.recordTaskSuccess(triggerEvent.id);
      return;
    }

    // 4. Execute tools (e.g., verify_stripe_payment, send_email, update_db)
    const toolResults = await agentDO.executeTools(response.toolCalls);
    
    // If a critical tool fails (like payment verification), abort loop immediately
    const criticalFailure = toolResults.find(r => !r.success && r.isFatal);
    if (criticalFailure) {
      await agentDO.recordTaskFailure(triggerEvent.id, criticalFailure.error);
      // Alert the Space Admin via the Space Assistant
      await env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
        type: 'fulfillment_failed',
        spaceId: agentDO.spaceId,
        message: `Fulfillment failed for event ${triggerEvent.id}: ${criticalFailure.error}`
      });
      return;
    }

    // 5. Append tool results and loop
    messages.push({ role: 'user', content: JSON.stringify(toolResults) });
  }

  // If we hit MAX_ITERATIONS, it's a loop failure (hallucination/stuck)
  await agentDO.recordTaskFailure(triggerEvent.id, "Max iterations exceeded");
}

The Knowledge-Graph Agent Loop

Standard RAG retrieves chunks of text based on vector similarity. The knowledge-graph loop is superior for expert domains: it retrieves explicit claims and relationships (e.g., [Drug_A] -> [Contraindicates] -> [Condition_B]). The agent queries the KnowledgeGraphDO to traverse these relationships before answering.

// agentpress/loops/knowledge-graph.ts

export async function executeKnowledgeGraphLoop(
  input: string,
  agentDO: NaelaoAgentDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<string> {
  
  // 1. Entity Extraction
  // Agent extracts core entities from the user's query
  const extraction = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Extract core entities from: ${input}` }],
    model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
    system: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Output JSON array of entity strings only.' }]
  });
  const entities = JSON.parse(extraction.content);

  // 2. Graph Traversal (via Custom DO)
  // Query the KnowledgeGraphDO for subgraphs related to these entities
  const kgDO = env.NAELAO_CUSTOM_DO.get(
    env.NAELAO_CUSTOM_DO.idFromName(`KnowledgeGraphDO:${agentDO.spaceId}`)
  );
  
  const graphResp = await kgDO.fetch(new Request('http://kg/traverse', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ entities, depth: 2 })
  }));
  const subGraph = await graphResp.json();

  // 3. Grounded Synthesis
  // The LLM generates an answer strictly bounded by the retrieved subgraph
  const synthesis = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: input }],
    model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
    system: [{ 
      type: 'text', 
      text: `You are an expert advisor. You must base your answer STRICTLY on the following verified claims from the knowledge graph. Do not use outside knowledge. Cite the claim IDs.\n\nGraph Data:\n${JSON.stringify(subGraph)}` 
    }]
  });

  return synthesis.content;
}

AutoResearchDO: Nightly Expansion

The AutoResearchDO wakes up at 2 AM. It queries the KnowledgeGraphDO for "Open Questions" or "Low Confidence Edges". It uses the `web_search` skill (restricted to the `networkAllowlist` domains like PubMed) to find papers, reads them via `crawl_page`, extracts new claims, and proposes them as edges to the graph. The Space Admin reviews these in the morning.
