The Content Agent Loop

The content loop differs from chat because the ultimate output is a file (Markdown) rather than a message sent to the user. It enforces a structured pipeline: Outline → Draft → SEO Review → Publish.

// agentpress/loops/content.ts

export async function executeContentLoop(
  topic: string,
  agentDO: NaelaoAgentDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  
  // Stage 1: Research & Outline
  const outlineResp = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Research and outline a comprehensive article about: ${topic}` }],
    tools: [getToolDef('web_search')]
  });
  
  // Stage 2: Drafting
  // Write the draft directly to the R2 workspace via Tier 1 operation
  const draftResp = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [
      { role: 'user', content: `Based on this outline, draft the article in Markdown: \n${outlineResp.content}` }
    ]
  });
  
  const filePath = `content/posts/drafts/${topic.replace(/\s+/g, '-')}.md`;
  await executeWorkspaceTool({
    toolName: 'write_file',
    parameters: { path: filePath, content: draftResp.content }
  }, agentDO.spaceId, agentDO.projectId);

  // Stage 3: SEO Review (Self-Correction)
  const seoReview = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Review this draft for SEO best practices. Focus on headers, keyword density, and meta description. Suggest edits. \n\n${draftResp.content}` }]
  });

  // Apply edits to the file
  const finalContent = applyEdits(draftResp.content, seoReview.content);
  await executeWorkspaceTool({
    toolName: 'write_file',
    parameters: { path: filePath, content: finalContent }
  }, agentDO.spaceId, agentDO.projectId);

  // Stage 4: Trigger CF Pages Deployment
  // The agent uses the `deploy-expose` skill to tell Cloudflare Pages to rebuild the site
  await agentDO.executeTools([{
    toolName: 'trigger_pages_build',
    parameters: { commitMessage: `Auto-draft: ${topic}` }
  }]);
}
CF Pages Direct Integration

Because the Sites manifest declares externalPortal.deploymentType: 'cf-pages', the Naelao provisioner creates a real Cloudflare Pages project bound to this Space's R2 bucket. When the Agent writes Markdown to spaces/{spaceId}/workspace/content/posts/ and calls trigger_pages_build, Cloudflare Pages pulls the R2 content, runs Astro/Next.js to build static HTML, and pushes it to the global edge network. This guarantees sub-millisecond TTFB for the public website, completely decoupled from Naelao's internal API latency.

Wallet-Gated Agent Loop Interception

In Enterprise spaces, agents can hire other agents, buy data, or spin up expensive resources. The platform injects a middleware check into the standard execution loop: before any tool executes, the WalletDO verifies the agent has sufficient budget for the operation.

// agentpress/orchestrator.ts — Enterprise Wallet Interceptor
async function executeWalletGatedTool(
  tc: ParsedToolCall,
  agentDO: NaelaoAgentDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<ToolResult> {
  
  // 1. Determine cost of the tool call (e.g., buying dataset vs free R2 read)
  const estimatedCost = await estimateToolCost(tc);

  // 2. If it costs money, check the Agent's WalletDO
  if (estimatedCost > 0) {
    const walletDO = env.NAELAO_WALLET_DO.get(
      env.NAELAO_WALLET_DO.idFromName(`wallet:${agentDO.spaceId}:${agentDO.agentId}`)
    );

    const auth = await walletDO.fetch(new Request('http://wallet/pre-authorize', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: estimatedCost, tool: tc.toolName })
    })).then(r => r.json());

    if (!auth.authorized) {
      // Agent's loop is interrupted. It must inform the user it needs more budget.
      return { 
        toolName: tc.toolName, 
        output: { error: `Wallet denied: ${auth.reason}. Ask admin to increase budget.` } 
      };
    }
  }

  // 3. Execute tool and log to CF Analytics Engine (Logpush for Enterprise)
  const result = await standardExecuteTool(tc, agentDO, env);
  
  await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'audit_action',
    spaceId: agentDO.spaceId,
    agentId: agentDO.agentId,
    toolName: tc.toolName,
    cost: estimatedCost,
    timestamp: Date.now()
  });

  return result;
}

The x402 Task-Completion Loop

When an external space (e.g., an Enterprise Space) hires a Worker, they assign a task and attach an x402 payment proof. The Worker's execution loop verifies the payment, executes the task (optionally spawning sub-agents), and delivers the result.

// agentpress/loops/worker-task.ts

export async function executeWorkerTaskLoop(
  taskEvent: { taskId: string; payload: string; x402Proof: string },
  workerInstDO: WorkerInstanceDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  
  // 1. Verify Payment
  const paymentValid = await verifyX402Payment(taskEvent.x402Proof, env);
  if (!paymentValid) {
    await workerInstDO.rejectTask(taskEvent.taskId, "x402 payment verification failed");
    return;
  }

  // 2. Execute Task
  const response = await workerInstDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: taskEvent.payload }],
    model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
    system: [{ 
      type: 'text', 
      text: `You are an autonomous worker. Execute the requested task. 
             If the task is too large, use the 'subagent-spawn' tool to hire sub-workers.`
    }]
  });

  // 3. Handle Sub-Agent Spawning (Gig Economy inside AI)
  if (response.toolCalls?.some(tc => tc.toolName === 'spawn_subagent')) {
    // The Worker uses its own WalletDO to pay the sub-agent out of the funds it just received
    await handleSubAgentDelegation(response.toolCalls, workerInstDO, env);
  }

  // 4. Deliver Result and Settle
  await workerInstDO.deliverResult(taskEvent.taskId, response.content);
  
  // 5. Extract Federated Learning (Privacy-Safe)
  await extractSkillCandidate({
    task: taskEvent.payload,
    result: response.content
  }, workerInstDO, env);
}

Mini-AGI — The Federated Query Loop

Mini-AGI is fundamentally different from other space types: it is a Sub-Space only type designed to act as an intelligence overlay for an entire Enterprise. Its agent loop is strictly federated-query. It is heavily constrained: it cannot write to R2 workspaces and its network is entirely closed. Its only job is to synthesize data across silos safely.

The Federated Query Loop (In-Memory Processing)

When a user asks a question, the agent does not download files to a workspace. It uses the MiniAGIDO to stream data into memory, synthesizes an answer, and dumps the memory. This ensures sensitive HR or Financial data is never written to disk in a secondary location.

// agentpress/loops/federated-query.ts

export async function executeFederatedQueryLoop(
  question: string,
  userContext: { userId: string; role: string; subSpaceId: string },
  miniAgiDO: MiniAGIDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<string> {
  
  // 1. Route query through MiniAGIDO to enforce permissions
  const queryPlan = await miniAgiDO.buildSecureQueryPlan(question, userContext);
  
  if (queryPlan.grantedDomains.length === 0) {
    return "Access Denied: You do not have permission to query the required data domains.";
  }

  // 2. Fetch data entirely in-memory (No R2 writes)
  const memoryContexts = await Promise.all(
    queryPlan.grantedDomains.map(async (domain) => {
      // Directly queries Vectorize indices of the granted sub-spaces
      return await performVectorSearchInMemory(domain, question, env);
    })
  );

  // 3. Synthesize response with strict system prompt
  const synthesis = await env.AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-opus-4-5',                  // Opus used for highest reasoning capability
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: question }],
    system: `You are the company's Mini-AGI. Answer based ONLY on the provided context.
    
Context from permitted domains:
${JSON.stringify(memoryContexts)}

Notice: The user was DENIED access to these domains: ${queryPlan.deniedDomains.join(', ')}. 
Do not hallucinate data for these domains.`
  });

  // 4. Audit Log (Mandatory)
  await miniAgiDO.logQuery({
    userId: userContext.userId,
    question,
    domainsAccessed: queryPlan.grantedDomains,
    answerGiven: synthesis.content[0].text
  });

  return synthesis.content[0].text;
}

The File-Edit Loop & Live Preview

In the file-edit loop, the agent acts like a developer in an IDE. It reads files, proposes diffs, runs tests via `npm run test` inside the container, and if successful, spins up a live preview via the Dynamic Worker Loader.

// agentpress/loops/file-edit.ts

export async function executeFileEditLoop(
  intent: string,
  agentDO: NaelaoAgentDO,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  
  // 1. Search Codebase
  const search = await agentDO.executeTools([{
    toolName: 'execute_bash',
    parameters: { commands: `grep -rnw '/workspace/src' -e '${intent}'` }
  }]);

  // 2. Edit Files (Agent uses AST-aware codemode to apply diffs)
  const editResult = await agentDO.callLLM({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Implement this feature: ${intent}. Current files: ${search[0].output.stdout}` }],
    tools: [getToolDef('write_file')]
  });
  await agentDO.executeTools(editResult.toolCalls);

  // 3. Run Tests inside Warm Container
  const testRun = await agentDO.executeTools([{
    toolName: 'execute_bash',
    parameters: { commands: 'npm run test' }
  }]);

  if (testRun[0].output.exitCode !== 0) {
    // Self-correction loop triggers if tests fail
    await handleTestFailure(testRun[0].output.stderr, agentDO);
    return;
  }

  // 4. Live Preview (Dynamic Worker Loader)
  // The agent bundles the React component and spins up an Artifact
  const bundle = await agentDO.executeTools([{
    toolName: 'execute_bash',
    parameters: { commands: 'npx esbuild src/App.tsx --bundle --format=esm' }
  }]);

  const preview = await agentDO.executeTools([{
    toolName: 'render_artifact',
    parameters: { name: 'dev-preview', code: bundle[0].output.stdout, type: 'react' }
  }]);

  // 5. Return Preview URL to Developer
  agentDO.broadcast({ type: 'preview_ready', url: preview[0].output.previewUrl });
}
74 — Core Space Types

Standard Space — The Baseline Chat Environment

The Standard Space Type is the baseline. It represents the original "Suna Kortix" experience — threads, projects, file management, and a capable general-purpose agent. It uses the chat loop model and provisions no special Durable Objects beyond the core set every Space gets. Every other Space Type is a superset of Standard. If a Naelao Space Type manifest omits a field, it inherits its default from here.

What Standard Provides

Capability Detail Limit (Free / Pro)
Threads Persistent conversation threads with full message history Unlimited / Unlimited
Projects Named workspaces with shared file context and KB 3 / Unlimited
Agent execution Chat loop with tool calling. Default tier: Isolate. 100 runs/day / Unlimited
R2 storage Per-project file storage under workspace/projects/{projectId}/ 1 GB / 10 GB
Skills file-manager, web-search always loaded. Any platform skill can be enabled. All platform skills available
Apps Any published Naelao App can be installed 5 apps / Unlimited
Knowledge base Vectorised document search via naelao-knowledge 50 MB / 1 GB

What Standard Does Not Provide

Standard intentionally omits capabilities that require elevated infrastructure. This keeps the provisioning fast, the security surface small, and the billing predictable:

  • No WalletDO — no autonomous spending, no credit balance, no x402 payment flows. Agents cannot purchase on behalf of users.
  • No WorkflowRegistryDO — no persistent background workflows. Tasks run within a single agent turn; nothing runs while the user is offline.
  • No external portal — the Space cannot serve a public-facing URL with an embedded agent. Standard Spaces are private by default.
  • No custom RemoteLoop — Standard uses the built-in chat loop. There is no way to inject a custom reasoning Worker.
  • No cron jobs — Agents do not run on a schedule. For scheduled execution, upgrade to Launchpad or Workers.

The Provisioner Path

When a user creates a Standard Space, SpaceTypeRegistryDO runs the Standard provisioner. It is the fastest provisioner on the platform because there are no special DOs to spin up:

// workers/naelao-provisioner/src/types/standard.ts
export async function provisionStandard(
  ctx: ProvisionContext
): Promise<ProvisionResult> {
  const { spaceId, userId, env } = ctx;

  // 1. Create the core SpaceDO stub (every space gets this)
  const spaceDO = env.SPACE_DO.get(env.SPACE_DO.idFromName(spaceId));
  await spaceDO.fetch('http://internal/init', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, typeId: 'standard', userId }),
  });

  // 2. Insert record into SpaceDO SQLite
  await spaceDO.createSpace({
    id: spaceId,
    user_id: userId,
    type_id: 'standard',
    name: ctx.name ?? 'Builder Workspace',
    created_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  });

  // 3. Create the default project
  const projectId = crypto.randomUUID();
  await spaceDO.createProject({
    id: projectId,
    space_id: spaceId,
    name: 'Default Project',
    created_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  });

  // 4. Seed R2 with the project root
  await env.R2.put(
    `workspace/projects/${projectId}/.naelao`,
    JSON.stringify({ projectId, spaceId, createdAt: Date.now() })
  );

  // Standard needs nothing else — no WalletDO, no WorkflowRegistryDO
  return { spaceId, projectId, typeId: 'standard' };
}

Upgrade Path

Standard is the entry point. Users grow into more capable Space Types as their needs evolve:

Need Upgrade To Key Addition
"I need the agent to run while I'm offline" Launchpad WorkflowRegistryDO, cron jobs, background execution
"I need the agent to spend money autonomously" Launchpad WalletDO, x402 payment rail, credit balance
"I need a public-facing agent portal" Launchpad External portal on {slug}.naelao.app
"I need to build and deploy code" Developer CF deploy access, git integration, preview URLs
"I need a team to share this space" Enterprise Multi-user RBAC, audit log, SSO
Standard as the Default Fallback

If any part of the Space Type system fails — the manifest is missing, the registry is unreachable, the provisioner returns an error — the platform falls back to Standard. This means a degraded Naelao is still a functional Naelao: threads work, file manager works, the agent responds. No other Space Type can make this guarantee because they all depend on additional DOs or migrations that may themselves be unavailable.

75 — Space Types Architecture

RemoteLoop — Platform-Internal Agent Execution

RemoteLoop is a Naelao-internal interface that allows certain Naelao-authored Space Types to delegate agent reasoning to a dedicated internal Worker while keeping tool execution and security enforcement inside the platform. It is the mechanism that makes Space Types like Mini-AGI and Legal Verticals possible — they need reasoning patterns the standard chat loop cannot express. It is not exposed to community developers. For the complete API specification, see Appendix A8 — RemoteLoop.

Why RemoteLoop Is Not a Community Primitive

A RemoteLoop Worker receives the full conversation history, user intent, and a live Scoped Token on every agent turn. Exposing this surface to arbitrary third-party code creates an unacceptable data exfiltration vector. Community developers who need custom reasoning should instead publish a Naelao App with a custom MCP server — the tool call boundary provides the necessary isolation. See Community Contribution Model.

When Standard Loops Are Not Enough

The three built-in loop models cover the majority of Space Types:

  • chat — Single-turn or multi-turn conversational. The agent responds, waits. Standard Space, Developer Space.
  • content — Long-form generation with structured output. Sites, Documentation Verticals.
  • task — Autonomous tool-calling until a goal condition is met. Launchpad, Workers.

Some Space Types require patterns none of these can express. Mini-AGI runs a recursive planner that spawns sub-agents and waits on futures. Legal Verticals runs a Tree-of-Thought search across case law before committing to any response. These are not loop variants — they are different computational models. RemoteLoop provides a clean delegation boundary so these Workers can be developed, tested, and deployed independently of the core platform.

The Three Invariants

Every RemoteLoop implementation, regardless of complexity, must honour three invariants enforced by AgentDO before and after delegation:

Invariant Enforced By Detail
Token Scope AgentDO pre-flight The Scoped Token issued to the RemoteLoop Worker is bound to the exact spaceId and agentId of the current turn. It cannot be used to read another space's files, even if the Worker attempts it.
Tool Gating naelao-gateway Every tool call the Worker makes back to the Scoped API passes through the 27-pattern security scanner and the network allowlist for that Space Type. The Worker cannot call tools the Space Type manifest does not declare.
Stream Integrity AgentDO post-flight The token stream returned by the Worker is validated for encoding and size before being forwarded to the WebSocket. A Worker that returns malformed or oversized chunks is disconnected and the turn fails gracefully.

How AgentDO Chooses a Loop

On every agent turn, AgentDO reads the Space Type manifest from the SpaceTypeRegistryDO and checks for a customLoopWorker binding:

// workers/naelao-agent/src/AgentDO.ts (turn dispatch)
async function dispatchTurn(ctx: TurnContext): Promise<ReadableStream> {
  const manifest = await ctx.spaceTypeRegistry.getManifest(ctx.spaceTypeId);

  if (manifest.customLoopWorker) {
    // Delegate to the internal RemoteLoop Worker
    return dispatchRemoteLoop(ctx, manifest.customLoopWorker);
  }

  // Fall through to the built-in loop models
  switch (manifest.agentEnvironment.loopModel) {
    case 'chat':    return runChatLoop(ctx);
    case 'content': return runContentLoop(ctx);
    case 'task':    return runTaskLoop(ctx);
    default:        return runChatLoop(ctx);
  }
}

async function dispatchRemoteLoop(
  ctx: TurnContext,
  workerBinding: string
): Promise<ReadableStream> {
  const scopedToken = await ctx.tokenIssuer.issue({
    spaceId: ctx.spaceId,
    agentId: ctx.agentId,
    ttlMs: 120_000,         // 2-minute turn TTL
    allowedTools: ctx.manifest.agentEnvironment.agentPermissions,
  });

  const loopWorker = ctx.env[workerBinding] as Fetcher;
  const response = await loopWorker.fetch('http://internal/turn', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      spaceId: ctx.spaceId,
      agentId: ctx.agentId,
      messages: ctx.messages,
      availableTools: ctx.toolManifest,
      scopedToken,
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok || !response.body) {
    throw new AgentError('RemoteLoop worker failed', { status: response.status });
  }

  return response.body;
}

Manifest Declaration

A Space Type that uses RemoteLoop declares it with a single field in its manifest. The value is the CF Worker binding name as declared in wrangler.jsonc:

// platform/manifests/mini-agi.json (excerpt)
{
  "id": "mini-agi",
  "agentEnvironment": {
    "loopModel": "task",                      // Fallback if customLoopWorker is absent
    "customLoopWorker": "MINI_AGI_LOOP"       // Worker binding name in wrangler.jsonc
  }
}

// wrangler.jsonc (naelao-agent Worker)
{
  "services": [
    { "binding": "MINI_AGI_LOOP", "service": "naelao-mini-agi-loop" },
    { "binding": "LEGAL_LOOP",    "service": "naelao-legal-loop" }
  ]
}

Failure Handling

RemoteLoop Workers run in the same Cloudflare infrastructure as the rest of Naelao, so network failures between them are rare but possible. AgentDO applies a fixed retry policy:

  • Timeout: 30 seconds for the initial response header. If the Worker does not begin streaming within 30s, the turn is cancelled and the user receives a graceful error message.
  • Stream drop: If the stream closes unexpectedly mid-turn, AgentDO records the partial output and surfaces it with a truncation notice. It does not retry a partial turn — the conversation state would be undefined.
  • Worker unavailable: If the binding itself is missing or the target Worker returns 503, AgentDO falls back to the manifest's loopModel and logs a remoteloop_fallback event to the analytics pipeline.
Current Internal RemoteLoop Workers

naelao-mini-agi-loop — Implements the recursive planner for Mini-AGI Spaces. Spawns sub-agent futures, aggregates results, maintains a working memory store in a KV namespace scoped to the turn.

naelao-legal-loop — Tree-of-Thought reasoning for Legal Verticals. Runs 3–5 parallel LLM branches, scores them against a legal-reasoning rubric, selects the highest-scoring branch, and streams only the winner.

naelao-research-loop — Iterative web research loop for the Research Verticals type. Decomposes a query into sub-questions, retrieves and ranks sources, synthesises a citation-backed answer.

For the Full RemoteLoop API Contract

See Appendix A8 — Custom Intelligence for the complete RemoteLoopRequest / RemoteLoopResponse interfaces, the Scoped API endpoint reference, the streaming protocol, and worked examples of each internal loop Worker.

76 — Upgrades & Migrations

Space Type Versioning & Canary Rollouts

When Naelao engineers update a Space Type manifest (e.g., adding a new sidebar widget, changing a SpaceDO schema changes, or updating a required DO), existing spaces do not instantly break. Naelao enforces a strict SemVer upgrade protocol managed by the SpaceTypeRegistryDO. Because Naelao exclusively authors Space Types, the versioning and migration pipeline is fully internal — there is no third-party submission or review step.

Version Bump Protocol

Version Change Definition Upgrade Process
Patch (1.0.0 → 1.0.1) Bug fixes in Worker code or manifest. No schema or UI changes. Automatic and instant. Worker routing transparently uses the new code.
Minor (1.0.0 → 1.1.0) Added non-breaking UI slots, new non-destructive cron jobs, or new skills. Canary Rollout: 5% of active spaces receive the update for 24 hours. If no spike in error events is detected by the Analytics Engine, rolled out to 100%.
Major (1.0.0 → 2.0.0) SpaceDO schema changes (column additions/removals), required DO class renames, or breaking UI changes. Opt-in only. Space Admins see an "Upgrade Available" banner. Clicking it triggers the internal migrationEndpoint.

SpaceTypeRegistryDO — Canary Rollout Engine

// durable-objects/space-type-registry-do.ts
// Handles the canary rollout state machine for Minor version bumps.

async function processCanaryRollouts(env: Env) {
  // 1. Find minor versions currently in canary state
  const canaries = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
    SELECT type_id, version, canary_pct, published_at 
    FROM versions 
    WHERE stable = 0 AND change_type = 'minor'
  `).toArray();

  for (const canary of canaries) {
    const hoursSincePublish = (Date.now() - canary.published_at) / (1000 * 60 * 60);

    // 2. Check CF Analytics Engine for errors on instances running this version
    const errorRate = await checkErrorRateForVersion(canary.type_id, canary.version, env);

    if (errorRate > 0.05) {
      // ERROR SPIKE DETECTED: Automatically rollback canary
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
        UPDATE versions SET stable = -1 WHERE type_id = ? AND version = ?
      `, canary.type_id, canary.version);
      
      // Downgrade the canary instances back to the last stable version
      await rollbackInstances(canary.type_id, canary.version);
      
      // Alert the developer
      await env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
        type: 'canary_failed',
        target: canary.type_id,
        reason: 'Error rate exceeded 5% threshold.'
      });
      continue;
    }

    // 3. Progress the Canary if healthy
    if (hoursSincePublish > 24 && canary.canary_pct === 5) {
      // Bump to 20%
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`UPDATE versions SET canary_pct = 20 WHERE type_id = ? AND version = ?`, canary.type_id, canary.version);
    } else if (hoursSincePublish > 48) {
      // 100% rollout - mark as stable
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`UPDATE versions SET stable = 1, canary_pct = 100 WHERE type_id = ? AND version = ?`, canary.type_id, canary.version);
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`UPDATE space_types SET current_version = ? WHERE id = ?`, canary.version, canary.type_id);
    }
  }
}

Major Version Migrations

For breaking changes (Major bumps), the manifest must declare a migrationEndpoint pointing to an internal Naelao Worker. When the Space Admin opts in, Naelao generates a Scoped Token and calls this endpoint. The internal migration Worker handles the data transformation atomically.

// Inside the Naelao internal migration Worker
// e.g., workers/space-type-migrations/legal-verticals.ts
app.post('/migrate', async (req) => {
  const spaceId = req.headers.get('X-Space-Id');
  const token = req.headers.get('Authorization');
  const { fromVersion, toVersion } = await req.json();

  if (fromVersion === '1.0.0' && toVersion === '2.0.0') {
    // Example: legal-verticals type adds a tax_rate column in v2.
    // Migration runs via the Naelao scoped query API.
    await fetch('https://api.naelao.dev/v1/scoped/query', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Authorization': token, 'X-Space-Id': spaceId },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        sql: `ALTER TABLE custom_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tax_rate REAL DEFAULT 0.0;`
      })
    });
    
    // Migrate R2 files to new prefix structure
    await fetch('https://api.naelao.dev/v1/scoped/r2/move', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Authorization': token, 'X-Space-Id': spaceId },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        source: 'workspace/old-data/',
        destination: 'workspace/v2-data/'
      })
    });
  }

  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ success: true }));
});
77 — Naelao Apps Economy

Naelao Apps — Packaging, CLI & AppRegistryDO

A Naelao App consists of an MCP Server (the intelligence) and UI Instructions (the interface). To make publishing frictionless, Naelao provides a CLI tool (npx naelao app publish). This section covers how apps are bundled, validated, and registered in the AppRegistryDO.

The App File Structure

A developer creating an app maintains a simple repository:

my-weather-app/
├── naelao-app.json       # The App Manifest (Tools, Pricing, Permissions)
├── src/
│   └── index.ts          # The MCP Server Worker
├── ui/
│   └── instructions.md   # LLM instructions for Dynamic UI generation
└── wrangler.toml         # Standard CF Worker config

What `npx naelao app publish` Actually Does

When the developer runs the CLI command, it performs a 4-step orchestration to ensure the app is secure, valid, and available globally.

// cli/src/commands/publish.ts (Inside the Naelao npm package)

export async function publishApp(directory: string) {
  console.log("📦 Packaging Naelao App...");

  // 1. Read and Validate Manifest locally
  const manifestRaw = readFileSync(path.join(directory, 'naelao-app.json'), 'utf8');
  const manifest = AppManifestSchema.parse(JSON.parse(manifestRaw));

  // 2. Deploy the Worker to Cloudflare
  // The MCP server runs on the developer's CF account, NOT Naelao's account.
  // This decentralizes compute costs for the MCP endpoints.
  console.log("🚀 Deploying MCP Worker to Cloudflare...");
  execSync('npx wrangler deploy', { cwd: directory, stdio: 'inherit' });

  // 3. Verify the MCP server is alive
  console.log("🔍 Verifying MCP endpoints...");
  const mcpCheck = await fetch(`${manifest.mcpServer.workerUrl}/mcp/tools`);
  if (!mcpCheck.ok) throw new Error("MCP Server failed to respond with tools.");

  // 4. Submit to Naelao App Registry
  // This calls the platform's naelao-apps-registry Worker
  console.log("📝 Registering with Naelao Marketplace...");
  const uiInstructions = readFileSync(path.join(directory, manifest.ui.instructionsPath), 'utf8');
  
  const response = await fetch('https://api.naelao.dev/v1/registry/apps/publish', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.NAELAO_CLI_TOKEN}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      manifest,
      uiInstructions
    })
  });

  if (response.ok) {
    console.log("✅ App successfully published to the marketplace!");
  } else {
    console.error("❌ Publish failed:", await response.text());
  }
}

AppRegistryDO — The Marketplace Database

The naelao-apps-registry Worker routes requests to the AppRegistryDO, which tracks app metadata, install counts, ratings, and triggers the UI instructions updates in R2.

// durable-objects/app-registry-do.ts
export class AppRegistryDO extends DurableObject {
  private async initSchema() {
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS apps (
        id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name            TEXT NOT NULL,
        version         TEXT NOT NULL,
        manifest        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON: Contains pricing and required permissions
        worker_url      TEXT NOT NULL,    -- The MCP server endpoint
        status          TEXT DEFAULT 'active',
        install_count   INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        published_at    INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
      );

      -- Tracks which Spaces have installed which Apps
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS installs (
        app_id          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES apps(id),
        space_id        TEXT NOT NULL,
        installed_at    INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
        PRIMARY KEY (app_id, space_id)
      );
    `);
  }

  async handlePublish(payload: { manifest: AppManifest, uiInstructions: string }): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Write metadata to SQLite
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
      INSERT OR REPLACE INTO apps (id, name, version, manifest, worker_url)
      VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    `, payload.manifest.id, payload.manifest.name, payload.manifest.version, 
       JSON.stringify(payload.manifest), payload.manifest.mcpServer.workerUrl);

    // 2. Write UI Instructions to the Global Assets R2 Bucket
    // The Dynamic Worker Loader reads from here when generating the UI iframe
    await this.env.NAELAO_ASSETS.put(
      `apps/${payload.manifest.id}/ui/instructions.md`,
      payload.uiInstructions
    );
  }

  // Called when a Space Admin clicks "Install App"
  async handleInstall(appId: string, spaceId: string): Promise<void> {
    const app = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT manifest FROM apps WHERE id = ?', appId).one();
    if (!app) throw new Error('App not found');
    
    const manifest = JSON.parse(app.manifest as string);

    // Record the installation in the registry DO
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`INSERT INTO installs (app_id, space_id) VALUES (?, ?)`, appId, spaceId);
    this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`UPDATE apps SET install_count = install_count + 1 WHERE id = ?`, appId);

    // Register the app in the Space's SpaceDO SQLite so the space knows it's active
    const spaceDO = getProductDO(this.rootSpaceId, this.env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
    await db.query(
      `INSERT INTO space_app_installs (space_id, app_id, worker_url, tool_permissions)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)`,
      [spaceId, appId, manifest.mcpServer.workerUrl, JSON.stringify(manifest.permissions)]
    );

    // Invalidate the MCP Hub cache for this space so agents immediately see the new tools
    await this.env.NAELAO_MCP_HUB.fetch(new Request('http://mcp-hub/tools/invalidate', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'X-Space-Id': spaceId }
    }));
  }
}
Community Model

Community Contribution Model — The Two Primitives

Naelao has a clear and deliberate split: Naelao exclusively authors Space Types (the operating environments). The community contributes through two well-defined primitives: Apps and Space Templates. This is not a limitation — it is a security and quality decision that keeps the platform's infrastructure stable while still enabling a rich ecosystem.

Why Naelao Owns Space Types

A Space Type defines the fundamental operating environment of a space: which DOs are provisioned, which SpaceDO schema version per product, what the agent loop model is, what the network policy is, what the external portal looks like. This is infrastructure — not content. Allowing community-authored Space Types would require trusting arbitrary code to run at provisioning time, arbitrary SpaceDO schema extensions against the database, and arbitrary RemoteLoop Workers receiving all user conversation data. The security surface is too large. The community instead extends Naelao through safer, well-isolated primitives.

The Three-Layer Ecosystem

Layer Who Creates What It Is Complexity Revenue Model
Space Types Naelao only Operating environment: DOs, agent loop, network policy, UI shell, external portal Full platform infrastructure User subscriptions
Apps Community + Naelao MCP Server + UI Instructions. Installs into any Space. Runs on developer's CF account. Low — MCP Worker + JSON manifest Per-use micropayments or subscription add-on
Space Templates Community + Naelao Curated starting configuration within an existing Space Type: agents, apps, KB, cron jobs, assistant config Lowest — JSON + R2 content, no code One-time install fee or free

Decision Guide: App or Template?

  • Build an App if you're adding new capabilities — new tools the agent can use, new UI panels, new data integrations, new automations triggered by external events.
  • Build a Template if you're adding new starting configurations — a pre-configured legal assistant for a Verticals space, a pre-built e-commerce setup for Launchpad, a starter blog setup for Sites.
  • You cannot build a Space Type — if what you want to do genuinely requires a new operating environment (custom DO, custom SpaceDO schema extension, custom agent loop), submit a feature request to Naelao. The team will evaluate whether a new platform Space Type is warranted.

App Architecture — What a Developer Controls

A Naelao App is a self-contained package that the developer deploys to their own Cloudflare account. Naelao never touches the developer's Worker code or data. The platform interacts with the App only through the MCP protocol boundary:

// A complete minimal Naelao App
// Developer deploys this to their OWN CF account

// 1. The manifest (submitted to the Naelao App Registry)
{
  "id": "my-crm-connector",
  "name": "CRM Connector",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Connects the agent to your CRM system",
  "author": { "name": "Acme Corp", "url": "https://acme.com" },

  "mcp": {
    "endpoint": "https://my-crm-mcp.acme-workers.workers.dev/mcp",
    "authScheme": "naelao-scoped-token"     // Naelao passes its Scoped Token
  },

  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "crm_get_contact",
      "description": "Look up a CRM contact by email",
      "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "email": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["email"] }
    },
    {
      "name": "crm_create_deal",
      "description": "Create a new deal in the CRM pipeline",
      "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "contactId": { "type": "string" }, "value": { "type": "number" } }, "required": ["contactId", "value"] }
    }
  ],

  "ui": {
    "sidebarSlot": {
      "icon": "ti-address-book",
      "label": "CRM",
      "panelUrl": "https://my-crm-ui.acme-workers.workers.dev/panel"
    }
  },

  "pricing": {
    "model": "per-use",
    "pricePerCall": 0.001                    // $0.001 per tool call via x402
  }
}

// 2. The MCP Worker (developer's CF Worker)
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const { tool, input, scopedToken } = await request.json();

    // Validate the Naelao Scoped Token (optional but recommended)
    await validateScopedToken(scopedToken, env.NAELAO_PUBLIC_KEY);

    // Call the real CRM API using developer's own credentials
    const result = await callCRMAPI(tool, input, env.CRM_API_KEY);

    return Response.json({ result });
  }
}

Space Template Architecture — What a Developer Controls

A Space Template is pure configuration — JSON and R2 assets, no executable code. It describes a starting state for a Space of a particular type:

// A Space Template for a "Legal Research Assistant" built on Verticals
{
  "id": "legal-research-starter",
  "name": "Legal Research Assistant",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "targetSpaceType": "verticals",            // Must match an existing platform Space Type
  "description": "Pre-configured legal research assistant with case law KB",

  "agents": [
    {
      "name": "Legal Researcher",
      "systemPrompt": "You are a legal research assistant specialised in case law analysis...",
      "skills": ["web-search", "pdf-reader", "file-manager"],
      "executionTier": "container"
    }
  ],

  "apps": [
    { "appId": "westlaw-connector", "autoInstall": true },
    { "appId": "citation-formatter", "autoInstall": true }
  ],

  "knowledgeBase": {
    "documents": [
      { "name": "Citation Style Guide", "r2Key": "templates/legal-research-starter/citation-guide.pdf" },
      { "name": "Research Methodology", "r2Key": "templates/legal-research-starter/methodology.md" }
    ]
  },

  "assistantConfig": {
    "greeting": "I'm your legal research assistant. What case or statute should we examine?",
    "suggestedPrompts": [
      "Summarise recent Supreme Court decisions on...",
      "Find cases where courts have held that...",
      "Draft a research memo on..."
    ]
  }
}

Revenue Flows

Community developers earn revenue through two mechanisms, both handled by Naelao's billing infrastructure so the developer never sees raw payment data:

Mechanism How It Works Naelao Cut
Per-use micropayments Each tool call the agent makes to the App costs a developer-set amount in Naelao credits. Billed from the user's credit balance via the x402 rail. Developer receives 80% monthly. 20%
Subscription add-on User pays a monthly flat fee to install the App. Processed through Naelao's billing provider. Developer receives 80% monthly. 20%
Template install fee One-time credit charge when a user installs the template into their Space. Optional — developer can set price to 0. 20%
Free Developer chooses no monetisation. Common for open-source apps and promotional templates. 0%

Publishing Workflow

The path from code to listed App is intentional and short. Naelao reviews for security and quality, not for business model:

  1. Submit manifest to registry.naelao.dev/apps/submit via the developer portal or CLI (npx naelao publish).
  2. Automated scan: Naelao's CI fetches the declared MCP endpoint, calls each tool with fuzz inputs, and checks that the Worker does not exfiltrate the Scoped Token or make calls to undeclared domains.
  3. Human review for Apps that declare agentPermissions beyond read-only, or that charge >$0.01 per call.
  4. Listed in the App Registry within 48 hours of submission if automated checks pass.
What Gets Rejected

Apps that proxy Scoped Tokens to third parties, that claim more tools in the manifest than the Worker exposes, that charge for tools that demonstrably do nothing, or that inject arbitrary HTML into the operator shell outside of a declared panelUrl slot. Templates that reference non-existent R2 assets or that target a Space Type that is not yet published.

Space Templates

Space Templates — Community-Authored Starting Configurations

A Space Template is a curated starting configuration that a community developer publishes for a specific Space Type. It contains no executable code — only JSON configuration, R2 content seeds, and references to existing Apps. When a user creates a new Space and selects a Template, the provisioner runs the Space Type first (Naelao infrastructure, fully trusted), then the template installer populates the space with the template's content (community content, safely sandboxed to R2 writes and SpaceDO method calls within the space's own prefix).

Security Model

Template installation is safe because templates contain no code that executes at the platform level. The worst a malicious template can do is seed bad content into a user's space — which the user can see and delete. There is no path from template installation to platform infrastructure access, cross-tenant data access, or conversation data exfiltration. This is why templates have a lightweight review process compared to Apps.

Space Template Format

// naelao-template.json — The Template Manifest
// Stored in R2: naelao-assets/templates/{templateId}/manifest.json

interface NaelaoSpaceTemplate {
  // Identity
  id:          string;           // e.g. "legal-firm-starter"
  name:        string;           // e.g. "Legal Firm Starter Pack"
  description: string;           // max 500 chars
  author:      string;           // developer userId or 'naelao'
  version:     string;           // semver: "1.0.0"
  icon_url?:   string;

  // Which Space Type this template targets (REQUIRED — templates are type-specific)
  targetSpaceType: string;       // e.g. "verticals-legal", "launchpad", "developer"

  // Apps to install when this template is applied
  apps: Array<{
    appId:    string;            // must exist in AppRegistryDO
    required: boolean;           // if true, space creation fails if app install fails
  }>;

  // Agent definitions to create in the space
  agents: AgentDefinition[];

  // Knowledge base seed content (R2 paths relative to template bundle in naelao-assets)
  knowledgeBase: Array<{
    fileName:    string;         // e.g. "legal-intake-guide.pdf"
    r2SourceKey: string;         // path in naelao-assets/templates/{id}/kb/
    description: string;
  }>;

  // Assistant configuration
  assistantConfig: {
    systemPromptOverride?: string;  // override the default assistant prompt
    initialMemory?: Array<{         // pre-seed typed memory (validated against MEMORY_SCHEMA)
      key: string;
      category: 'fact' | 'preference' | 'task';
      value: Record<string, unknown>;
    }>;
    cronJobs?: CronJob[];           // pre-configured scheduled tasks
  };

  // Marketplace listing
  marketplace: {
    visible:         boolean;
    priceUsdOneTime: number;     // 0 = free. Developer earns 80% of this.
    tags:            string[];   // for discovery: ["legal", "starter", "professional"]
  };
}

Template Installation Flow

1
User selects template at Space creation. naelao-spaces Worker loads template manifest from naelao-assets/templates/{id}/manifest.json.
2
Space Type provisioned first — standard Naelao provisioner runs for the target type. DOs, SpaceDO records, R2 prefixes all created by platform code. Template has no involvement at this step.
3
Apps installed — AppRegistryDO's handleInstall() is called for each App in the template. If a required App fails to install, the template installation fails and the space is provisioned without template content (not rolled back — the space exists, just unconfigured).
4
Agent definitions created — each AgentDefinition in the template is inserted into agent_definitions table with space_id set to the new space. Agents are private to this space.
5
Knowledge base seeded — template KB files are copied from naelao-assets (read-only source) to naelao-workspace/spaces/{spaceId}/knowledge/ and indexed via naelao-knowledge.
6
Assistant configured — if assistantConfig is present, AssistantDO is called to write initial memory (validated through the standard writeMemory() schema) and register cron jobs.

Template Installer Implementation

// workers/spaces/template-installer.ts
// Called after provisionSpace() completes successfully.
// Template installation is best-effort: failures seed warning logs but don't roll back the space.

export async function installTemplate(params: {
  spaceId:    string;
  templateId: string;
  userId:     string;
  env:        Env;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; warnings: string[] }> {

  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const { spaceId, templateId, userId, env } = params;

  // Load template manifest
  const manifestObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(
    `templates/${templateId}/manifest.json`
  );
  if (!manifestObj) return { success: false, warnings: ['Template manifest not found'] };

  const template: NaelaoSpaceTemplate = JSON.parse(await manifestObj.text());

  // Verify target type matches the space's provisioned type
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  const space = await db.query(
    'SELECT space_type FROM spaces WHERE id = $1', [spaceId]
  );
  if (space.rows[0]?.space_type !== template.targetSpaceType) {
    return { success: false, warnings: [`Template targets ${template.targetSpaceType} but space is ${space.rows[0]?.space_type}`] };
  }

  // Install Apps
  const appRegistry = env.NAELAO_APP_REGISTRY_DO.get(
    env.NAELAO_APP_REGISTRY_DO.idFromName('global-app-registry')
  );
  for (const appRef of template.apps) {
    try {
      await appRegistry.fetch(new Request('http://registry/install', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ appId: appRef.appId, spaceId })
      }));
    } catch (e) {
      if (appRef.required) {
        return { success: false, warnings: [`Required app ${appRef.appId} failed to install: ${e}`] };
      }
      warnings.push(`Optional app ${appRef.appId} failed: ${e}`);
    }
  }

  // Create agent definitions
  for (const agent of template.agents) {
    try {
      await db.query(
        `INSERT INTO agent_definitions (id, space_id, name, description, model, system_prompt,
           allowed_skills, resource_tier, marketplace_visible, status)
         VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, false, 'active')`,
        [spaceId, agent.name, agent.description, agent.model,
         agent.system_prompt, agent.allowed_skills, agent.resource_tier]
      );
    } catch (e) {
      warnings.push(`Agent ${agent.name} failed to create: ${e}`);
    }
  }

  // Seed knowledge base
  for (const kbEntry of template.knowledgeBase) {
    try {
      // Copy from naelao-assets (template source) to naelao-workspace (space instance)
      const sourceObj = await env.NAELAO_ASSETS.get(kbEntry.r2SourceKey);
      if (!sourceObj) throw new Error('Source file not found in template bundle');

      await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
        `spaces/${spaceId}/knowledge/${kbEntry.fileName}`,
        await sourceObj.arrayBuffer()
      );

      // Trigger indexing via naelao-knowledge
      await env.NAELAO_KNOWLEDGE.fetch(new Request('http://knowledge/index', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, fileName: kbEntry.fileName, description: kbEntry.description })
      }));
    } catch (e) {
      warnings.push(`KB file ${kbEntry.fileName} failed: ${e}`);
    }
  }

  // Configure the Space Assistant
  if (template.assistantConfig) {
    const assistantDoId = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.idFromName(
      `assistant:${spaceId}:${userId}`
    );
    const assistantDO = env.NAELAO_ASSISTANT_DO.get(assistantDoId);

    // Seed initial memory (goes through standard writeMemory() schema validation)
    for (const mem of (template.assistantConfig.initialMemory ?? [])) {
      try {
        await assistantDO.fetch(new Request('http://assistant/memory/write', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ key: mem.key, category: mem.category, value: mem.value })
        }));
      } catch (e) {
        warnings.push(`Memory seed ${mem.key} failed: ${e}`);
      }
    }

    // Write cron jobs to R2
    if (template.assistantConfig.cronJobs?.length) {
      await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(
        `spaces/${spaceId}/assistants/${userId}/cron-jobs.json`,
        JSON.stringify({
          jobs: template.assistantConfig.cronJobs,
          version: '1.0',
          updatedBy: 'template-installer',
          updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()
        })
      );
    }
  }

  // Record the template install for marketplace analytics
  await db.query(
    `INSERT INTO space_template_installs (space_id, template_id, installed_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, NOW())`,
    [spaceId, templateId]
  );

  return { success: true, warnings };
}

Template Registry — SpaceDO Table

-- Added to SpaceDO constructor schema (no migration files — self-initializing)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_templates (
  id                TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  author_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  target_space_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  name              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  description       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(description) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  version           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0.0',
  manifest_path     TEXT NOT NULL,    -- R2 path in naelao-assets
  status            TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'deprecated')),
  install_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  price_usd         REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
  created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_template_installs (
  space_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  template_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES space_templates(id),
  installed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (space_id, template_id)
);

-- RLS: anyone can read approved templates; only authors can update their own
ALTER TABLE space_templates ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "approved templates are public"
  ON space_templates FOR SELECT USING (status = 'approved');
CREATE POLICY "authors manage own templates"
  ON space_templates FOR ALL USING (author_id = auth.uid());
78 — Worker Deep Dive: naelao-admin

naelao-admin — Audit Logs, DLQ & Platform Ops

The naelao-admin Worker provides the internal APIs for Naelao's platform operations team. It handles compliance audit querying, Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) inspection, and emergency state recovery. Because this Worker exposes highly privileged operations, it is strictly protected by Cloudflare Zero Trust (CF Access).

Security Boundary: CF Access

Admin endpoints cannot rely solely on product JWTs, as a compromised user database could lead to platform-wide compromise. Every request to naelao-admin must carry a valid Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header signed by the Cloudflare Access team domain. If the token is missing or the cryptographic signature is invalid, the request drops at the edge.

Complete Implementation

// workers/admin/index.ts
// Handles platform operations, DLQ management, and Analytics Engine queries.

import { Hono } from 'hono';

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>();

// 1. CF Access Zero Trust Middleware (Mandatory)
app.use('*', async (c, next) => {
  const jwt = c.req.header('Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion');
  if (!jwt) return c.text('Forbidden: Missing CF Access JWT', 403);

  // Validate the JWT signature using the public keys from CF Access
  // Developers MUST use the @cloudflare/kv-asset-handler or manual JWKS verification
  const isValid = await verifyCloudflareAccessJWT(jwt, c.env.CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN, c.env.CF_ACCESS_AUD);
  if (!isValid) return c.text('Forbidden: Invalid CF Access JWT', 403);

  await next();
});

// 2. Audit Log Querying (Reads from CF Analytics Engine via SQL API)
// Allows support engineers to query immutable logs for a specific Space
app.get('/audit/:spaceId', async (c) => {
  const spaceId = c.req.param('spaceId');
  const { eventType, limit = '100' } = c.req.query();

  // We query the Analytics Engine GraphQL/SQL API
  // Naelao logs all actions (wallet spends, security events, etc.) here
  const query = `
    SELECT timestamp, blob1 as event_type, blob2 as actor_id, blob3 as details, double1 as amount
    FROM naelao_analytics
    WHERE index1 = '${spaceId}'
    ${eventType ? `AND blob1 = '${eventType}'` : ''}
    ORDER BY timestamp DESC
    LIMIT ${parseInt(limit)}
  `;

  const response = await fetch(`https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${c.env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/analytics_engine/sql`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${c.env.CF_API_TOKEN}` },
    body: query
  });

  return c.json(await response.json());
});

// 3. DLQ (Dead Letter Queue) Management
// Inspect messages that failed 3+ times in the agent-runs queue
app.get('/dlq/messages', async (c) => {
  const response = await fetch(
    `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${c.env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/queues/naelao-dlq/messages`,
    { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${c.env.CF_API_TOKEN}` } }
  );
  return c.json(await response.json());
});

// Retry a specific DLQ message (Support engineer intervention)
app.post('/dlq/retry/:messageId', async (c) => {
  const messageId = c.req.param('messageId');
  const payload = await c.req.json(); // The modified payload if the engineer fixed the bug

  // Send it back to the primary agent runs queue
  await c.env.NAELAO_AGENT_QUEUE.send(payload);

  // Acknowledge/delete it from the DLQ
  await fetch(
    `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${c.env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/queues/naelao-dlq/messages/${messageId}/ack`,
    { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${c.env.CF_API_TOKEN}` } }
  );

  return c.json({ success: true, message: "Re-queued to primary queue" });
});

// 4. Circuit Breaker Management
// If a 3rd party API (e.g., Stripe) goes down, Naelao trips a circuit breaker in KV.
// Admins can manually reset it once the provider resolves the incident.
app.post('/system/circuit-breakers/reset', async (c) => {
  const { service } = await c.req.json();
  await c.env.NAELAO_CIRCUIT_KV.delete(`circuit:${service}`);
  return c.json({ success: true, service, state: 'CLOSED' });
});

export default app;
79 — Worker Deep Dive: naelao-notifications

naelao-notifications — Omnichannel Alerting & VAPI

The naelao-notifications Worker is a pure Queue Consumer. It handles asynchronous delivery of alerts, digests, and approval requests across all supported channels. By offloading this to a queue, the AgentDO never blocks waiting for an SMTP server or APNs gateway to respond.

Supported Channels & Integrations

Channel Provider Primary Use Case
Email Resend API Daily analytics digests, billing invoices, offline alerts.
Push (Mobile) FCM / APNs Real-time waitForApproval() human-in-the-loop requests.
Chat Slack / Discord Webhooks Space Assistant updates, CI/CD deployment alerts.
Voice (New) VAPI (Voice AI) Critical escalations (e.g., Server down, massive Stripe refund request). Agent physically calls the Space Admin.

Complete Implementation

// workers/notifications/index.ts
// Queue consumer for `naelao-notifications`

export default {
  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<NotificationPayload>, env: Env) {
    // Process messages concurrently, but catch errors to prevent the whole batch from failing
    await Promise.allSettled(
      batch.messages.map(async (msg) => {
        try {
          await processNotification(msg.body, env);
          msg.ack();
        } catch (error) {
          console.error(`Notification failed: ${msg.id}`, error);
          msg.retry(); // Will retry up to max_retries before going to DLQ
        }
      })
    );
  }
};

async function processNotification(payload: NotificationPayload, env: Env) {
  // 1. Idempotency Check
  // Prevent double-sending emails if CF Queues delivers the message twice (at-least-once delivery)
  const idempotencyKey = `notif_lock:${payload.id}`;
  const alreadySent = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(idempotencyKey);
  if (alreadySent) return;

  const deliveries: Promise<any>[] = [];

  // 2. Route to requested channels
  if (payload.channels.includes('email')) {
    deliveries.push(sendEmail(payload, env));
  }
  
  if (payload.channels.includes('push')) {
    deliveries.push(sendPushNotification(payload, env));
  }

  if (payload.channels.includes('voice') && payload.priority === 'critical') {
    deliveries.push(triggerVapiCall(payload, env));
  }

  // Wait for all requested deliveries
  await Promise.all(deliveries);

  // Lock for 24 hours to ensure idempotency
  await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(idempotencyKey, 'sent', { expirationTtl: 86400 });

  // Log success to Analytics Engine
  await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'notification_sent',
    spaceId: payload.spaceId,
    channels: payload.channels,
    timestamp: Date.now()
  });
}

// ── VAPI Integration (Voice AI Escalation) ──
// If a Launchpad storefront agent gets a $10,000 refund request, it can trigger a voice call
// to the store owner's cell phone to wake them up and ask for verbal approval.

async function triggerVapiCall(payload: NotificationPayload, env: Env) {
  // Fetch the user's phone number from SpaceDO SQLite
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  const user = await db.query('SELECT phone FROM user_profiles WHERE id = $1', [payload.userId]);
  if (!user.rows[0]?.phone) return;

  const response = await fetch('https://api.vapi.ai/call/phone', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.VAPI_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      phoneNumberId: env.VAPI_PHONE_NUMBER_ID,
      customer: { number: user.rows[0].phone },
      assistant: {
        firstMessage: `Hello. I am your Naelao Space Assistant. I am calling because there is a critical alert in your workspace: ${payload.message}. Do you want me to approve or reject this action?`,
        model: {
          provider: "anthropic",
          model: "claude-3-haiku-20240307",
          systemPrompt: "You are the user's AI assistant. Keep responses very brief. If they say approve, thank them and end the call. If reject, confirm and end the call."
        }
      }
    })
  });

  if (!response.ok) throw new Error("VAPI call failed");
}
80 — Worker Deep Dive: naelao-eval

naelao-eval — Benchmarking & QA (GAIA + Braintrust)

How do you know an agent is getting better? Or that a fine-tuned LoRA model for a Vertical Space didn't regress on core logic? The naelao-eval Worker is an automated testing harness for agents. It runs benchmark datasets (like GAIA) through isolated AgentDO threads, scores the outputs, and syncs metrics to Braintrust.

The Evaluation Loop

1. User or CI triggers an eval run.
2. naelao-eval reads a dataset (JSONL) from R2.
3. For each row, it creates a temporary eval_thread and runs the agent.
4. It passes the output to a Scorer (Exact Match, Regex, or LLM-as-a-Judge).
5. Results are written to SpaceDO SQLite (eval_runs table) and synced to Braintrust for visual analysis.

Complete Implementation

// workers/eval/index.ts

import { Hono } from 'hono';

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>();

app.post('/eval/run', async (c) => {
  const { spaceId, agentDefinitionId, datasetPath, scorerType } = await c.req.json();
  
  // Fire and forget the evaluation runner
  c.executionCtx.waitUntil(
    runEvaluationSuite({ spaceId, agentDefinitionId, datasetPath, scorerType, env: c.env })
  );

  return c.json({ status: 'started', datasetPath });
});

async function runEvaluationSuite(params: EvalParams) {
  const { spaceId, agentDefinitionId, datasetPath, scorerType, env } = params;

  // 1. Load dataset from R2 Workspace (e.g., spaces/{spaceId}/evals/dataset.jsonl)
  const datasetFile = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(datasetPath);
  if (!datasetFile) throw new Error("Dataset not found");
  
  const rawData = await datasetFile.text();
  const dataset = rawData.split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(line => JSON.parse(line));

  let passed = 0;
  const results = [];

  // 2. Run test cases
  for (const testCase of dataset) {
    // Create a strictly isolated thread for this test
    const testThreadId = `eval-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    const agentDoId = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(`${spaceId}:eval-project:${testThreadId}`);
    const agentDO = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get(agentDoId);

    // Execute the agent synchronously for the eval
    const agentResp = await agentDO.fetch(new Request('http://agent/run-sync', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ 
        input: testCase.input, 
        agentDefinitionId 
      })
    })).then(r => r.json());

    const actualOutput = agentResp.finalMessage;

    // 3. Score the output
    const score = await evaluateOutput(actualOutput, testCase.expected, scorerType, env);
    if (score.passed) passed++;

    results.push({
      input: testCase.input,
      expected: testCase.expected,
      actual: actualOutput,
      score
    });
  }

  const finalScore = (passed / dataset.length) * 100;

  // 4. Sync results to SpaceDO SQLite (eval_runs table)
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  await db.query(
    `INSERT INTO eval_runs (space_id, agent_definition_id, dataset, score, details, created_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW())`,
    [spaceId, agentDefinitionId, datasetPath, finalScore, JSON.stringify(results)]
  );

  // 5. Sync to Braintrust (Enterprise ML observability)
  if (env.BRAINTRUST_API_KEY) {
    await fetch('https://api.braintrust.dev/v1/experiment', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.BRAINTRUST_API_KEY}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        project_name: `naelao-${spaceId}`,
        experiment_name: `eval-${agentDefinitionId}-${Date.now()}`,
        metrics: { accuracy: finalScore },
        records: results
      })
    });
  }
}

// ── Scorers ──
async function evaluateOutput(
  actual: string, 
  expected: string, 
  type: 'exact' | 'includes' | 'llm-judge',
  env: Env
): Promise<{ passed: boolean; reason?: string }> {
  
  if (type === 'exact') {
    return { passed: actual.trim() === expected.trim() };
  }
  
  if (type === 'includes') {
    return { passed: actual.includes(expected) };
  }
  
  if (type === 'llm-judge') {
    // Use LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate semantic correctness (e.g. for long-form text)
    const judgement = await env.AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
      model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
      system: 'You are an objective evaluator. Compare the ACTUAL output to the EXPECTED output. Does the actual output correctly and accurately satisfy the expected criteria? Respond with JSON: {"passed": boolean, "reason": "string"}',
      messages: [{ 
        role: 'user', 
        content: `EXPECTED:\n${expected}\n\nACTUAL:\n${actual}` 
      }]
    });
    return JSON.parse(judgement.content[0].text);
  }

  return { passed: false, reason: "Unknown scorer type" };
}

export default app;

GAIA Benchmark Dataset Format

Naelao uses the GAIA benchmark (General AI Assistants) as its primary quality gate. The GAIA JSONL format must be prepared and uploaded to the Space's eval workspace before running benchmarks. Each row contains a real-world task, the expected answer, and metadata about how hard it is.

// Format: spaces/{spaceId}/evals/gaia-validation.jsonl
// Each line is a JSON object (NOT an array — one JSON object per line):

{"id":"gaia-001","level":1,"input":"What is the total number of words in the Gettysburg Address?","expected":"272","scorer":"exact","metadata":{"source":"gaia","category":"counting","toolsNeeded":[]}}
{"id":"gaia-002","level":2,"input":"Search for the current CEO of Anthropic and tell me their first name.","expected":"Dario","scorer":"includes","metadata":{"source":"gaia","category":"web-search","toolsNeeded":["web_search"]}}
{"id":"gaia-003","level":3,"input":"Download the S&P 500 closing prices for the last 5 trading days, compute the average, and write it to a file called 'sp500-avg.txt'.","expected":"sp500-avg.txt","scorer":"file-exists","metadata":{"source":"gaia","category":"data-processing","toolsNeeded":["browser_navigate","execute_python","write_file"]}}

// Level 1: Reasoning only (no tools needed)
// Level 2: 1-2 tool calls needed (web search, file read)
// Level 3: Multi-step tasks requiring planning across 3+ tools

// Custom scorers beyond exact/includes/llm-judge:
// "file-exists": checks if the agent wrote a file with the expected name to the workspace
// "json-field": parses agent output as JSON and checks a specific field value
// "numeric-within": checks if numeric output is within a tolerance band

Extended Scorer Types

// Extended scorers for eval/index.ts

async function evaluateOutput(
  actual: string,
  testCase: EvalRow,
  env: Env,
  spaceId: string
): Promise<{ passed: boolean; reason?: string }> {

  const { expected, scorer } = testCase;

  if (scorer === 'file-exists') {
    // Check if the agent wrote a file with this name to the eval workspace
    const key = `spaces/${spaceId}/evals/temp/${expected}`;
    const obj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(key);
    return { 
      passed: obj !== null,
      reason: obj ? 'File found' : `File '${expected}' not found in eval workspace` 
    };
  }

  if (scorer === 'json-field') {
    // testCase.expected format: "fieldName:expectedValue"
    const [fieldName, expectedValue] = expected.split(':');
    try {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(actual);
      const actual_value = String(parsed[fieldName]);
      return { passed: actual_value === expectedValue };
    } catch {
      return { passed: false, reason: 'Agent output is not valid JSON' };
    }
  }

  if (scorer === 'numeric-within') {
    // testCase.expected format: "value±tolerance" e.g. "42.5±0.5"
    const [valueStr, toleranceStr] = expected.split('±');
    const target = parseFloat(valueStr);
    const tolerance = parseFloat(toleranceStr ?? '0.01');
    const actual_num = parseFloat(actual.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, ''));
    return { passed: Math.abs(actual_num - target) <= tolerance };
  }

  // fallback to standard scorers
  if (scorer === 'exact') return { passed: actual.trim() === expected.trim() };
  if (scorer === 'includes') return { passed: actual.includes(expected) };
  
  return { passed: false, reason: 'Unknown scorer' };
}

CI Integration — GitHub Actions Trigger

The eval Worker exposes a /eval/run endpoint that CI calls after every deployment. If the score drops below the threshold, the deployment is blocked.

# .github/workflows/eval-gate.yml
name: Eval Gate

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run GAIA Benchmark
        id: eval
        run: |
          RESULT=$(curl -s -X POST \
            https://api.naelao.dev/v1/eval/run \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.NAELAO_CI_TOKEN }}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{
              "spaceId": "${{ vars.EVAL_SPACE_ID }}",
              "agentDefinitionId": "platform-default-agent",
              "datasetPath": "spaces/${{ vars.EVAL_SPACE_ID }}/evals/gaia-validation.jsonl",
              "scorerType": "auto",
              "waitForCompletion": true,
              "timeoutSeconds": 300
            }')
          
          SCORE=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.score')
          echo "eval_score=$SCORE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Eval Score: $SCORE%"

      - name: Check Eval Threshold
        run: |
          SCORE="${{ steps.eval.outputs.eval_score }}"
          THRESHOLD=70  # 70% pass rate required on GAIA validation
          
          if (( $(echo "$SCORE < $THRESHOLD" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "❌ Eval score $SCORE% is below threshold $THRESHOLD%"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ Eval score $SCORE% passes threshold"

      - name: Comment Score on PR
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🤖 **Eval Score:** ${{ steps.eval.outputs.eval_score }}% on GAIA validation set'
            })

Regression Tracking — Score History

The eval Worker stores every run result in the SpaceDO SQLite eval_runs table. The naelao-admin dashboard plots this over time, making it immediately visible when a new deployment causes a quality regression.

// SpaceDO SQLite: eval_runs table (add to SpaceDO constructor schema)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_runs (
  id                    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  space_id              TEXT NOT NULL,
  agent_definition_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  dataset               TEXT NOT NULL,        -- R2 key of the dataset JSONL
  scorer_type           TEXT NOT NULL,
  score                 REAL NOT NULL,         -- 0-100
  cases_total           INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cases_passed          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  details               JSONB,                -- Full result array for drill-down
  braintrust_experiment TEXT,                -- Link to Braintrust for visual analysis
  git_sha               TEXT,                -- Git SHA at time of run (from CI env var)
  created_at            TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Query for score history (used in admin dashboard chart)
SELECT 
  DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at) as day,
  AVG(score) as avg_score,
  MIN(score) as min_score,
  MAX(score) as max_score
FROM eval_runs
WHERE space_id = $1 AND agent_definition_id = $2
  AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
Eval Isolation — Why Agent Threads Are Temporary

Each eval test case creates a fresh eval_thread AgentDO instance via idFromName with a unique UUID. This ensures test cases don't bleed into each other — memory from test case 1 cannot influence test case 2. After the eval run completes, naelao-sweeper deletes these temporary DO instances on its next pass. The isolation also ensures that eval runs cannot access real user workspace data — the eval AgentDO has no access to the Space's primary R2 paths.

81 — Worker Deep Dive

Categorizer & Feedback — Background Intelligence

Conversations generate massive amounts of unstructured data. The naelao-categorizer and naelao-feedback Workers process this data in the background. They auto-tag projects for the UI, analyze user satisfaction, and calculate quality scores for self-authored agent skills without blocking the critical path of the chat loop.

naelao-categorizer

A cron-driven worker that scans recently active projects, reads the last few messages, and uses a fast, cheap LLM (Haiku) to generate tags, summaries, and intent categories. It updates the SpaceDO SQLite projects table so the user's dashboard is always neatly organized.

naelao-feedback

An API endpoint that receives explicit user feedback (thumbs up/down, retry requests, or text feedback). It maps this feedback directly back to the specific skill or tool the agent used, updating the SkillRegistryDO reputation scores.

Categorizer Implementation

// workers/categorizer/index.ts
export default {
  // Triggered by a CF Cron (e.g., hourly)
  async scheduled(event: ScheduledEvent, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive

    // 1. Fetch stale projects using the stored function from §57
    const staleProjects = await db.query(
      'SELECT * FROM get_stale_projects_for_categorization(50)'
    );

    if (staleProjects.rows.length === 0) return;

    // 2. Process in parallel, capped at 10 concurrent LLM calls to avoid rate limits
    const limit = pLimit(10);
    await Promise.all(
      staleProjects.rows.map(project => limit(() => categorizeProject(project, env, db)))
    );
  }
};

async function categorizeProject(project: any, env: Env, db: any) {
  // Fetch recent messages for context
  const messages = await db.query(
    `SELECT role, content FROM messages 
     WHERE project_id = $1 AND space_id = $2 
     ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10`,
    [project.project_id, project.space_id]
  );

  const conversationText = messages.rows.reverse()
    .map((m: any) => `${m.role}: ${m.content.slice(0, 500)}`)
    .join('\n');

  // LLM Call to generate tags and summary
  const completion = await env.AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
    max_tokens: 150,
    system: 'You are an auto-categorizer. Return JSON: {"tags": string[], "summary": "short title"}',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: conversationText }]
  });

  try {
    const { tags, summary } = JSON.parse(completion.content[0].text);

    // Update the project record
    await db.query(
      `UPDATE projects SET tags = $1, summary = $2, last_categorized_at = NOW() 
       WHERE id = $3 AND space_id = $4`,
      [tags, summary, project.project_id, project.space_id]
    );
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`Categorization failed for project ${project.project_id}`, e);
  }
}

Feedback Implementation (Skill Scoring)

// workers/feedback/index.ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>();

app.post('/feedback', async (c) => {
  const { spaceId, agentId, messageId, score, text, toolUsed } = await c.req.json();
  // score: 1 for thumbs up, -1 for thumbs down

  // 1. Write immutable log to Analytics Engine
  await c.env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'user_feedback',
    spaceId, agentId,
    metadata: { messageId, toolUsed, score: score.toString(), text }
  });

  // 2. If a specific tool was used, update its reputation in SkillRegistryDO
  if (toolUsed) {
    const registryId = c.env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.idFromName(`skills:${spaceId}:${agentId}`);
    const registryDO = c.env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.get(registryId);
    
    // The DO updates a moving average rating for the skill. 
    // If an agent-authored skill drops below a 2.0 rating, the DO quarantines it.
    await registryDO.fetch(new Request('http://registry/score', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ toolName: toolUsed, score })
    }));
  }

  // 3. If negative text feedback provided, trigger self-correction analysis
  if (score < 0 && text) {
    c.executionCtx.waitUntil(analyzeFailure(spaceId, agentId, text, toolUsed, c.env));
  }

  return c.json({ success: true });
});

// ── Self-Correction Analysis ──
// When a user provides negative text feedback, this function uses an LLM to
// classify the failure mode and write an improvement suggestion back to the
// agent's SKILL.md in the workspace.
async function analyzeFailure(
  spaceId: string,
  agentId: string,
  feedbackText: string,
  toolUsed: string | undefined,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {

  // 1. Classify the failure mode
  const classification = await env.AI_GATEWAY.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
    max_tokens: 300,
    system: `You are a QA analyzer for AI agent failures. Classify the user's negative feedback into one of these categories:
- WRONG_TOOL: Agent used the wrong tool for the task
- WRONG_PARAMS: Agent used the right tool with incorrect parameters
- MISUNDERSTOOD_INTENT: Agent misunderstood what the user wanted
- INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT: Agent's answer was correct but missing key details
- HALLUCINATION: Agent stated something factually incorrect
- SKILL_BUG: The tool itself has a bug or missing feature
Return JSON: {"category": string, "suggestion": "one-sentence improvement for the agent"}`,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `User feedback: "${feedbackText}"\nTool used: ${toolUsed ?? 'unknown'}` }]
  });

  let analysis: { category: string; suggestion: string };
  try {
    analysis = JSON.parse(classification.content[0].text);
  } catch {
    return; // LLM returned non-JSON, skip
  }

  // 2. Write improvement suggestion to a feedback log in the agent's workspace
  // The Space Assistant reads these logs during its daily standup to self-improve
  const feedbackKey = `spaces/${spaceId}/agents/${agentId}/feedback-log.jsonl`;
  const existingObj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(feedbackKey);
  const existing = existingObj ? await existingObj.text() : '';

  const entry = JSON.stringify({
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    feedbackText,
    toolUsed: toolUsed ?? null,
    category: analysis.category,
    suggestion: analysis.suggestion
  });

  await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(feedbackKey, existing + entry + '\n');

  // 3. Log to Analytics Engine for platform-level quality tracking
  await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'failure_analysis',
    spaceId, agentId,
    failureCategory: analysis.category,
    toolUsed: toolUsed ?? 'none'
  });

  // 4. If this is a SKILL_BUG, escalate to platform team via naelao-admin
  if (analysis.category === 'SKILL_BUG' && toolUsed) {
    await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
      type: 'skill_bug_report',
      spaceId, agentId, toolUsed,
      feedbackText, suggestion: analysis.suggestion
    });
  }
}

export default app;

Skill Quarantine System

When the SkillRegistryDO accumulates enough negative feedback for a self-authored skill, it enters quarantine — temporarily disabled until the agent rewrites it. This prevents a buggy agent-written skill from continuing to frustrate the user across multiple sessions.

// durable-objects/skill-registry-do.ts — updateSkillScore()

async function updateSkillScore(toolName: string, score: number): Promise<void> {
  // Get or initialize skill score record
  const existing = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `SELECT total_score, rating_count, status FROM skill_scores WHERE tool_name = ?`,
    toolName
  ).one();

  const totalScore = ((existing?.total_score as number) ?? 0) + score;
  const ratingCount = ((existing?.rating_count as number) ?? 0) + 1;
  const movingAverage = totalScore / ratingCount;

  // Quarantine threshold: average below 2.0 after at least 5 ratings
  let newStatus = existing?.status ?? 'active';
  if (ratingCount >= 5 && movingAverage < 2.0) {
    newStatus = 'quarantined';

    // Notify the Space Assistant that the skill needs rewriting
    await this.env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
      type: 'skill_quarantined',
      spaceId: this.spaceId,
      toolName,
      movingAverage,
      ratingCount,
      message: `Skill '${toolName}' has been quarantined due to repeated poor performance (avg score: ${movingAverage.toFixed(2)}). The agent will rewrite this skill during the next session.`
    });
  }

  // Promote from quarantine if agent fixes the skill and feedback improves
  if (newStatus === 'quarantined' && movingAverage >= 3.0 && ratingCount > 10) {
    newStatus = 'active';
  }

  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO skill_scores (tool_name, total_score, rating_count, moving_average, status, updated_at)
     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    toolName, totalScore, ratingCount, movingAverage, newStatus, Date.now()
  );
}

// getSkill() blocks quarantined tools from loading
async function getSkill(toolName: string): Promise<Skill | null> {
  const score = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `SELECT status FROM skill_scores WHERE tool_name = ?`, toolName
  ).one();

  if (score?.status === 'quarantined') {
    throw new Error(`Skill '${toolName}' is quarantined due to poor performance. The agent must rewrite it.`);
  }

  // ... normal skill loading ...
}

Daily Quality Standup — Space Assistant Integration

Every morning, the Space Assistant's cron job reads the feedback-log.jsonl for each agent and generates a self-improvement plan. This closes the loop between user feedback and agent behavior.

// The Space Assistant's daily standup cron handler

async function runDailyQualityReview(spaceId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> {
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive

  // Get all agents in this space
  const agents = await db.query(`SELECT id FROM agent_definitions WHERE space_id = $1`, [spaceId]);

  for (const agent of agents.rows) {
    const logKey = `spaces/${spaceId}/agents/${agent.id}/feedback-log.jsonl`;
    const logObj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(logKey);
    if (!logObj) continue;

    const log = await logObj.text();
