Retry Backoff Strategy

For errors where shouldRetry: true, the orchestrator uses exponential backoff with jitter: attempt 1 → 1s, attempt 2 → 2s, attempt 3 → 4s, max 3 retries. After the third failure, the error is downgraded to a non-retryable correction prompt. Rate limit errors (ERR_RATE_LIMIT) start at 5s to respect provider windows. LLM overload (ERR_LLM_OVERLOADED) uses the AI Gateway's built-in fallback routing first before invoking the retry logic.

How the Orchestrator Uses This

Inside the Agent Loop (AgentDO.run()), errors caught during executeTools() are mapped through the processor before being appended to the conversation history.

// Inside agentpress/orchestrator.ts

let retryCount = 0;

async function executeWithErrorHandling(toolCall: ParsedToolCall): Promise<ToolResult> {
  while (true) {
    try {
      const result = await dispatchTool(toolCall);
      session.add({ role: 'tool', content: result.output, toolName: toolCall.name });
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      const processed = processAgentException(error as Error, {
        toolName: toolCall.name,
        stderr: (error as any).stderr,
        allowlist: spaceManifest.agentConfig?.networkPolicy?.allowlist
      });

      // Log structured error to CF Analytics Engine
      await env.ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
        type: 'agent_tool_error',
        errorCode: processed.code,
        category: processed.category,
        toolName: toolCall.name,
        spaceId, runId
      });

      if (processed.isFatal) {
        throw new Error(`FATAL:${processed.code}:${processed.agentMessage}`);
      }

      if (processed.shouldRetry && retryCount < 3) {
        retryCount++;
        const backoffMs = [1000, 2000, 4000][retryCount - 1];
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoffMs));
        continue; // retry the tool call
      }

      // Feed the correction prompt back to the LLM as a tool result
      session.add({
        role: 'tool',
        content: processed.agentMessage,
        toolName: toolCall.name,
        isError: true
      });
      return { toolName: toolCall.name, output: { error: processed.agentMessage }, success: false };
    }
  }
}
A4 — Space Type Registry

SpaceTypeRegistryDO — The Marketplace & Versioning Engine

The SpaceTypeRegistryDO is the only global singleton Durable Object in Naelao. It serves as the authoritative source for all available Space Types, managing the full lifecycle from submission through canary rollout to deprecation. See §62 for the provisioner and §76 for canary rollout mechanics — this appendix covers what those sections omit: the KV cache invalidation flow, the earnings micropayment ledger, and the deprecation pipeline.

KV Cache Invalidation — The Read-Through Pattern

The RegistryDO is a global singleton, which means every manifest read that goes to the DO adds cross-region latency. To avoid this, naelao-spaces reads manifests from CF KV first. The DO is only consulted on cache miss. This gives ~1ms reads at the global edge instead of ~50ms to the DO's pinned location.

// workers/spaces/index.ts — How naelao-spaces resolves a manifest

async function resolveSpaceTypeManifest(
  typeId: string,
  version: string,
  env: Env
): Promise<NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2> {
  
  const cacheKey = `manifest:${typeId}:${version}`;

  // 1. Try KV first (sub-1ms from any PoP)
  const cached = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(cacheKey, 'json');
  if (cached) return cached as NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2;

  // 2. KV miss — go to the registry DO (one round-trip to DO's location)
  const registryId = env.NAELAO_REGISTRY_DO.idFromName('global-registry');
  const registry = env.NAELAO_REGISTRY_DO.get(registryId);

  const resp = await registry.fetch(new Request('http://registry/manifest', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ typeId, version })
  }));

  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`Space Type '${typeId}@${version}' not found`);
  const manifest = await resp.json() as NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2;

  // 3. Populate KV so subsequent reads are fast
  // TTL: 1 hour. The DO calls broadcastUpdate() to invalidate when a type changes.
  await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(cacheKey, JSON.stringify(manifest), {
    expirationTtl: 3600
  });

  return manifest;
}

// Inside SpaceTypeRegistryDO — called on any version publish or status change
async function broadcastUpdate(typeId: string, version: string): Promise<void> {
  // Delete the KV cache entry. Next read from any Worker will repopulate it.
  await this.env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.delete(`manifest:${typeId}:${version}`);

  // Also invalidate the 'latest' pointer if this is the current version
  const spaceType = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `SELECT current_version FROM space_types WHERE id = ?`, typeId
  ).one();

  if (spaceType?.current_version === version) {
    await this.env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.delete(`manifest:${typeId}:latest`);
  }

  // Notify naelao-admin of the update for audit logging
  await this.env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({
    type: 'registry_update',
    typeId, version,
    timestamp: Date.now()
  });
}

Earnings Micropayment Ledger

When a Space uses a community-authored Space Type (currently Naelao-authored only, but community contribution is planned), the platform deducts a usage fee and credits the type's author. This is tracked in the RegistryDO's registry_earnings table and settled to the author's Stripe Connect account weekly. 

// Called by naelao-billing whenever a Space is billed for a community Space Type
async function recordTypeUsage(params: {
  typeId: string;
  sourceSpaceId: string;
  monthlyBilledUsd: number;
}): Promise<void> {

  // Community authors earn 20% of the Space Type's monthly fee
  const AUTHOR_REVENUE_SHARE = 0.20;

  const authorEarnings = params.monthlyBilledUsd * AUTHOR_REVENUE_SHARE;

  // Look up the author of this Space Type
  const spaceType = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `SELECT author_id FROM space_types WHERE id = ?`, params.typeId
  ).one();

  if (!spaceType || spaceType.author_id === 'naelao') {
    return; // Platform-native types don't pay out to an author
  }

  // Write to the earnings ledger
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
    INSERT INTO registry_earnings (author_id, amount_usd, source_space_id)
    VALUES (?, ?, ?)
  `, spaceType.author_id, authorEarnings, params.sourceSpaceId);

  // Update the Space Type's total revenue counter
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `UPDATE space_types SET total_revenue_usd = total_revenue_usd + ? WHERE id = ?`,
    authorEarnings, params.typeId
  );
}

// Weekly settlement job (called by naelao-sweeper cron)
async function settleEarnings(env: Env): Promise<void> {
  // Find all authors with unsettled earnings
  const pendingEarnings = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
    SELECT author_id, SUM(amount_usd) as total_due
    FROM registry_earnings
    WHERE settled = 0
    GROUP BY author_id
    HAVING total_due >= 10.00
  `).toArray();

  for (const row of pendingEarnings) {
    // Look up the author's Stripe Connect account ID from SpaceDO SQLite
    const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
    const author = await db.query(
      `SELECT stripe_connect_account_id FROM user_profiles WHERE id = $1`,
      [row.author_id]
    );

    if (!author.rows[0]?.stripe_connect_account_id) continue;

    // Transfer via Stripe Connect
    const transfer = await fetch('https://api.stripe.com/v1/transfers', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
      },
      body: new URLSearchParams({
        amount: String(Math.floor((row.total_due as number) * 100)), // cents
        currency: 'usd',
        destination: author.rows[0].stripe_connect_account_id,
        description: 'Naelao Space Type Author Revenue Share'
      })
    }).then(r => r.json());

    if (transfer.id) {
      // Mark as settled
      this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
        `UPDATE registry_earnings SET settled = 1, stripe_transfer_id = ? WHERE author_id = ? AND settled = 0`,
        transfer.id, row.author_id
      );
    }
  }
}

Deprecation Pipeline

When a Space Type is deprecated, existing Spaces using it are not broken immediately. The deprecation pipeline notifies admins, gives them a migration window, and finally marks the type as archived — at which point no new Spaces can use it but existing ones remain functional until they migrate.

// Deprecation state machine: approved → deprecated → archived
// Transition from deprecated → archived requires a 90-day notice period.

async function deprecateSpaceType(typeId: string, migrationGuideUrl: string): Promise<void> {
  const archiveDate = new Date();
  archiveDate.setDate(archiveDate.getDate() + 90); // 90-day window

  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    `UPDATE space_types SET status = 'deprecated', archive_date = ?, migration_guide_url = ? WHERE id = ?`,
    archiveDate.getTime(), migrationGuideUrl, typeId
  );

  // Notify all Space admins using this type
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(this.rootSpaceId, this.env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  const affected = await db.query(
    `SELECT DISTINCT s.admin_user_id FROM spaces s WHERE s.space_type_id = $1`,
    [typeId]
  );

  for (const row of affected.rows) {
    await this.env.NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send({
      type: 'space_type_deprecated',
      userId: row.admin_user_id,
      typeId,
      archiveDate: archiveDate.toISOString(),
      migrationGuideUrl,
      message: `Space Type '${typeId}' will be archived on ${archiveDate.toLocaleDateString()}. Please migrate to a supported type before then.`
    });
  }

  await this.broadcastUpdate(typeId, 'status-change');
}
The Canary Rollout Protocol

Naelao supports Canary Provisioning for Space Types. When a Minor version (v1.1.0) is published, the Registry DO sets canary_percent to 5%. For the next 24 hours, only 5% of new Spaces created with that Type will use the new manifest. The naelao-analytics Worker monitors these canary instances for error rate spikes. If the error rate stays below 5%, the registry auto-promotes through 5% → 20% → 100% over 48 hours. See §76 for the full canary rollout implementation.

Complete DO SQLite Schema

// durable-objects/space-type-registry-do.ts
// Singleton ID: idFromName('global-registry')
private async initSchema() {
this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`
-- Authority: Platform vs Community
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_types (
id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
name TEXT NOT NULL,
author_id TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'naelao' or userId
author_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'platform' | 'community'
current_version TEXT NOT NULL,
status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending|approved|rejected|deprecated
rating REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
install_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
);
code
Code
-- Versioning: Every manifest revision is immutable
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS manifest_versions (
  type_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES space_types(id),
  version         TEXT NOT NULL,    -- SemVer string
  manifest_json   TEXT NOT NULL,    -- The full NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2
  change_log      TEXT,
  canary_percent  INTEGER DEFAULT 0, -- 0-100 for rollout control
  published_at    INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000),
  PRIMARY KEY (type_id, version)
);

-- Developer Earnings (Micropayment ledger for type creators)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS registry_earnings (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))),
  author_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_usd      REAL NOT NULL,
  source_space_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  processed_at    INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000)
);
`);
}
The Canary Rollout Protocol

Naelao supports Canary Provisioning for Space Types. When a community developer pushes a "Minor" version (v1.1.0), the Registry DO updates the canary_percent to 5%. For the next 24 hours, only 5% of new Spaces created with that Type will use the new manifest. The naelao-analytics Worker monitors these canary instances for 4xx/5xx spikes. If healthy, the registry auto-promotes to 100%.

Registering a Type — The Security Handshake

// Called by naelao-admin after passing the 31-pattern scanner
async registerType(params: { manifest: ManifestV2, authorId: string }) {
// Validate author authority
if (params.manifest.id.startsWith('naelao.') && params.authorId !== 'naelao') {
throw new Error('Forbidden: Reserved namespace');
}
// Store manifest in SQLite
this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(INSERT INTO manifest_versions (type_id, version, manifest_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?),
params.manifest.id, params.manifest.version, JSON.stringify(params.manifest)
);
// Update KV cache for high-speed read access in naelao-spaces
await this.env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(
manifest:${params.manifest.id}:${params.manifest.version},
JSON.stringify(params.manifest)
);
}
A5 — Lifecycle Hooks

Provisioning & Deprovisioning — Transactional Assembly

Naelao treats a Space as an atomic unit of infrastructure. The Provisioner is a durable state machine that assembles all platform hardware — Durable Objects, SpaceDO SQLite records, R2 prefixes, KV entries — required by a specific Space Type in the correct order, with full rollback if any step fails. Deprovisioning is not just a deletion: it is a sanitised scrub that guarantees no data leakage, no orphaned billing, and no zombie DOs.

The Provisioning Chain

Every Space creation runs through six ordered phases. Each phase appends a compensating action to a Compensation Log before proceeding. If any phase throws, the log is replayed in reverse order to undo all completed work:

1
Manifest fetch & validation: naelao-spaces calls SpaceTypeRegistryDO to retrieve the signed manifest for the requested Space Type. The manifest's Ed25519 signature is verified against the platform public key. An invalid or missing manifest is a hard failure — no compensation needed at this point.
2
Slug reservation: A unique slug is chosen (user-provided or auto-generated). The slug is written to a KV lock key (slug-lock:{slug}) with a 30s TTL. If the KV write fails, the slug is already taken. Compensation: delete the KV lock.
3
SpaceDO record: The spaces row is inserted into SpaceDO SQLite. The provisioner then runs any Space-Type-specific SQL migrations from manifest.backend.sqlMigrations, with {SPACE_ID} tokens replaced in every statement so that Row Level Security predicates are baked in from the first microsecond. Compensation: DELETE FROM spaces WHERE id = ?.
4
DO assembly (Platform Hardware): For each binding listed in manifest.backend.platformDOs, the provisioner calls env[binding].get(idFromName(spaceId)) and POSTs an /init message to the DO. DOs are addressed by name so they are deterministically retrievable later. Compensation: POST /destroy to each initialised DO.
5
R2 seeding: Creates the R2 prefix roots declared in manifest.backend.r2Prefixes. For types that include starter content (Launchpad, Sites, Verticals), this step copies template assets from a shared platform R2 bucket. Compensation: r2.list + r2.delete for all seeded objects.
6
Portal provisioning (if enabled): Calls provisionExternalPortal() (see A6) to register the slug in the KV route table and issue the initial portal Scoped Token. Compensation: delete all three KV portal entries.

Compensation Log Implementation

// workers/naelao-provisioner/src/provision.ts

export async function provisionSpace(
  spaceId:  string,
  slug:     string,
  manifest: ManifestV2,
  env:      Env
): Promise<ProvisionResult> {

  const compLog: Array<() => Promise<void>> = [];

  try {
    // ── Phase 2: slug reservation ────────────────────────────
    await env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(`slug-lock:${slug}`, spaceId, { expirationTtl: 30 });
    compLog.push(() => env.PORTAL_ROUTES.delete(`slug-lock:${slug}`));

    // ── Phase 3: DB row + migrations ─────────────────────────
    await spaceDO.createSpaceRecord({
      id: spaceId, slug, type_id: manifest.id,
      created_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    });
    compLog.push(() => spaceDO.deleteSpaceRecord(spaceId));

    for (const migration of manifest.backend.sqlMigrations ?? []) {
      const sql = migration.sql.replaceAll('{SPACE_ID}', spaceId);
      await spaceDO.runMigration(sql);  // SpaceDO migration method
      // Migrations are irreversible — log their inverse if provided
      if (migration.rollbackSql) {
        const rollback = migration.rollbackSql.replaceAll('{SPACE_ID}', spaceId);
        compLog.push(() => spaceDO.runMigration(rollback));
      }
    }

    // ── Phase 4: DO assembly ─────────────────────────────────
    const initialisedDOs: string[] = [];
    for (const doConf of manifest.backend.platformDOs) {
      const binding = env[doConf.binding] as DurableObjectNamespace;
      const stub = binding.get(binding.idFromName(spaceId));
      await stub.fetch(new Request('http://internal/init', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, typeId: manifest.id, config: doConf.config }),
      }));
      initialisedDOs.push(doConf.binding);
      // Capture binding name for closure — JS let scoping
      const capturedBinding = doConf.binding;
      compLog.push(async () => {
        const b = env[capturedBinding] as DurableObjectNamespace;
        const s = b.get(b.idFromName(spaceId));
        await s.fetch(new Request('http://internal/destroy', { method: 'POST' }));
      });
    }

    // ── Phase 5: R2 seeding ──────────────────────────────────
    const seededKeys: string[] = [];
    for (const prefix of manifest.backend.r2Prefixes) {
      const rootKey = `${prefix}/${spaceId}/.naelao`;
      await env.R2.put(rootKey, JSON.stringify({ spaceId, typeId: manifest.id, createdAt: Date.now() }));
      seededKeys.push(rootKey);
    }
    if (manifest.backend.starterContent) {
      const copied = await copyStarterContent(spaceId, manifest.backend.starterContent, env);
      seededKeys.push(...copied);
    }
    compLog.push(async () => {
      await Promise.all(seededKeys.map(k => env.R2.delete(k)));
    });

    // ── Phase 6: portal ──────────────────────────────────────
    let portalUrl: string | undefined;
    if (manifest.ui.externalPortal?.enabled) {
      portalUrl = await provisionExternalPortal(spaceId, slug, env);
      compLog.push(() => deprovisionPortal(spaceId, slug, env));
    }

    return { spaceId, slug, portalUrl, initialisedDOs };

  } catch (err) {
    // FAILURE: replay compensation log in reverse
    for (const rollback of [...compLog].reverse()) {
      await rollback().catch(e =>
        console.error('Compensation step failed:', e)
      );
    }
    throw err;  // Re-throw so the caller surfaces the error to the user
  }
}

Deprovisioning — The Full Scrub

Deleting a database row is not deprovisioning. A Space owns R2 objects, KV entries, active DOs, SpaceDO SQLite records across multiple tables, and potentially an external portal registration. Every byte must be accounted for or it becomes storage bloat that Naelao pays for indefinitely. Deprovisioning uses a CF Workflow so it survives timeouts on large Spaces:

// workers/naelao-provisioner/src/deprovision.ts
// Runs as a CF Workflow step-function — each step is durable and retried on failure

export class DeprovisionWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint<Env, { spaceId: string }> {
  async run(event: WorkflowEvent<{ spaceId: string }>, step: WorkflowStep) {
    const { spaceId } = event.payload;

    // Step A: Disable portal immediately (stop serving traffic)
    await step.do('disable-portal', async () => {
      const host = await this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.get(`portal:space:${spaceId}`);
      if (host) await this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(
        `portal:host:${host}`,
        JSON.stringify({ spaceId, enabled: false, disabledMessage: 'This Space has been deleted.' })
      );
    });

    // Step B: Destroy all DOs for this Space
    await step.do('destroy-dos', async () => {
      const doBindings = ['AGENT_DO', 'WALLET_DO', 'SPACE_DO', 'PROJECT_DO', 'CONCURRENCY_DO'];
      await Promise.all(doBindings.map(async binding => {
        try {
          const ns = this.env[binding] as DurableObjectNamespace;
          const stub = ns.get(ns.idFromName(spaceId));
          await stub.fetch(new Request('http://internal/destroy', { method: 'POST' }));
        } catch { /* DO may not exist for this Space Type — ignore */ }
      }));
    });

    // Step C: Delete all R2 objects (paginated — may be thousands of files)
    await step.do('delete-r2', async () => {
      let cursor: string | undefined;
      do {
        const list = await this.env.R2.list({ prefix: `workspace/${spaceId}/`, cursor, limit: 1000 });
        if (list.objects.length) {
          await this.env.R2.delete(list.objects.map(o => o.key));
        }
        cursor = list.truncated ? list.cursor : undefined;
      } while (cursor);

      // Also scrub portal artifacts
      const portalList = await this.env.R2.list({ prefix: `portals/${spaceId}/` });
      if (portalList.objects.length) {
        await this.env.R2.delete(portalList.objects.map(o => o.key));
      }
    });

    // Step D: Call spaceDO.purge() — cascades through all tables in SpaceDO SQLite
    await step.do('delete-db', async () => {
      await spaceDO.purge();  // SpaceDO.purge() deletes all records for this space + sub-spaces
      // CASCADE handles: projects, threads, messages, agents, knowledge_docs
    });

    // Step E: Clean up KV entries
    await step.do('delete-kv', async () => {
      const host = await this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.get(`portal:space:${spaceId}`);
      const slug = host?.split('.')[0];
      await Promise.all([
        host   ? this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.delete(`portal:host:${host}`) : Promise.resolve(),
        slug   ? this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.delete(`portal:slug:${slug}`) : Promise.resolve(),
        this.env.PORTAL_ROUTES.delete(`portal:space:${spaceId}`),
      ]);
    });
  }
}

Lifecycle Hook Registry

Space Type manifests can declare hooks that fire at specific lifecycle events. Hooks are called synchronously within the provisioner step — if a hook fails, the step fails and compensation runs:

Hook When It Fires Typical Use
onProvision After all platform hardware is assembled, before returning to the user Send welcome email, seed default agent config, create first project
onFirstAgentRun Before the first agent turn in a newly provisioned Space Run an onboarding workflow, inject Space-Type-specific context into the first system prompt
onDeprovision After portal is disabled, before DOs and R2 are destroyed Export user data to a download link, notify integrations of Space deletion
onUpgrade When a Space changes Space Type (e.g. Standard → Launchpad) Provision additional DOs required by the new type, run incremental SQL migrations
The Most Common Junior Dev Mistake

Forgetting to paginate R2 deletion. r2.list() returns at most 1,000 objects per call. A Space with 10,000 files requires 10 list calls. The Workflow step pattern handles this correctly — each list+delete iteration is checkpointed. If the Worker times out mid-deletion, the Workflow resumes from the last successful checkpoint rather than starting over or leaving orphan objects.

A6 — Public Surface

External Portals — {slug}.naelao.com & Custom Domains

For Space Types like Sites, Launchpad, and Workers, the public-facing UI is the product. Naelao provisions a dedicated, zero-chrome public endpoint for every Space instance that declares "externalPortal": { "enabled": true } in its manifest. The agent can build and publish a live website, storefront, or API in a single turn — without the user ever seeing the Naelao management interface.

URL Structure

Every portal-enabled Space gets a subdomain on naelao.app derived from a user-chosen slug chosen at Space creation. Custom domains are supported via Cloudflare for SaaS:

URL Type Example How It Works
Platform subdomain my-shop.naelao.app Automatic. Provisioned when the Space is created. Immutable slug.
Custom domain shop.mybrand.com User adds a CNAME pointing to portal.naelao.app. TXT verification required. SSL managed by CF for SaaS.
Preview URL preview-{hash}.naelao.app Auto-generated for each agent deployment before it goes live. Expires in 24h.

Routing Architecture

*.naelao.app points to the naelao-portal-router Worker via a Cloudflare wildcard DNS record. On every request, the router performs a KV lookup to resolve the hostname to a Space ID, then dispatches to the portal's Isolate:

// workers/naelao-portal-router/src/index.ts
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const host = request.headers.get('Host') ?? '';

    // Step 1: Resolve hostname → spaceId
    const routeKey = `portal:host:${host}`;
    const route = await env.PORTAL_ROUTES.get(routeKey, 'json') as PortalRoute | null;

    if (!route) {
      return new Response('Portal not found', { status: 404 });
    }

    // Step 2: Check if Space is active and portal is enabled
    if (!route.enabled) {
      return new Response(route.disabledMessage ?? 'This portal is offline', { status: 503 });
    }

    // Step 3: Check cache (static-first strategy)
    const cacheKey = new Request(`https://cache.internal/${route.spaceId}${new URL(request.url).pathname}`);
    const cached = await caches.default.match(cacheKey);
    if (cached) return cached;

    // Step 4: Dispatch to the portal Isolate via Dynamic Worker Loader
    const portalWorker = env.DYNAMIC_LOADER.get(
      env.DYNAMIC_LOADER.idFromName(`portal:${route.spaceId}`)
    );

    const portalRequest = new Request(request.url, {
      method:  request.method,
      headers: new Headers({
        ...Object.fromEntries(request.headers),
        'X-Naelao-Space-Id':   route.spaceId,
        'X-Naelao-Portal-Token': route.scopedToken,  // Read-only, space-scoped
      }),
      body: request.body,
    });

    const response = await portalWorker.fetch(portalRequest);

    // Step 5: Cache cacheable responses at the edge
    if (response.headers.get('Cache-Control')?.includes('max-age')) {
      await caches.default.put(cacheKey, response.clone());
    }

    return response;
  }
};

interface PortalRoute {
  spaceId:        string;
  enabled:        boolean;
  disabledMessage?: string;
  scopedToken:    string;   // Pre-issued read-only token, refreshed every 5 min by naelao-sweeper
  deploymentR2Key: string;  // Path to the portal artifact in R2
}

KV Route Table — How Hostnames Are Registered

When the provisioner creates a portal-enabled Space, it writes three KV entries: one for the platform subdomain, a placeholder for the custom domain (filled when the user connects one), and a reverse lookup for the slug uniqueness check:

// workers/naelao-provisioner/src/portal.ts
export async function provisionExternalPortal(
  spaceId: string,
  slug: string,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  // Validate slug uniqueness
  const existing = await env.PORTAL_ROUTES.get(`portal:slug:${slug}`);
  if (existing) throw new Error(`Slug "${slug}" is already taken`);

  const platformHost = `${slug}.naelao.app`;

  // Issue a long-lived read-only portal token (rotated every 5 min by sweeper)
  const scopedToken = await issueScopedToken({
    spaceId,
    permissions: ['workspace_read', 'knowledge_read'],
    ttlMs: 5 * 60 * 1000,
    env,
  });

  const route: PortalRoute = {
    spaceId,
    enabled: true,
    scopedToken,
    deploymentR2Key: `portals/${spaceId}/current/index.js`,
  };

  await Promise.all([
    env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(`portal:host:${platformHost}`, JSON.stringify(route)),
    env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(`portal:slug:${slug}`, spaceId),
    env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(`portal:space:${spaceId}`, platformHost),
  ]);
}

The @naelao/portal-sdk

Portal code — generated by the agent or written by the user — accesses Space data through the @naelao/portal-sdk. The SDK reads the Scoped Token injected by the router and uses it to make authenticated reads against the Scoped API. It never exposes the token to the browser:

// A portal generated by the agent for a Launchpad e-commerce Space
// Deployed to: portals/{spaceId}/current/index.ts
import { createPortal } from '@naelao/portal-sdk';

const portal = createPortal({
  auth: 'platform-injected',  // Token injected by naelao-portal-router header
});

export default {
  async fetch(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const url = new URL(req.url);

    // Read product data from the Space's SpaceDO SQLite DB
    const products = await portal.db.query<Product[]>(
      'SELECT id, name, price, stock, image_r2_key FROM products WHERE stock > 0 ORDER BY name'
    );

    // Serve product images directly from R2 (zero egress fee)
    if (url.pathname.startsWith('/images/')) {
      const key = url.pathname.slice(1);
      const image = await portal.r2.get(key);
      if (!image) return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
      return new Response(image.body, {
        headers: { 'Content-Type': image.httpMetadata?.contentType ?? 'image/jpeg' }
      });
    }

    // Render storefront HTML
    return new Response(renderStorefront(products), {
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8',
        'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300',
      }
    });
  }
}

interface Product { id: string; name: string; price: number; stock: number; image_r2_key: string; }

function renderStorefront(products: Product[]): string {
  return `... ${products.map(p => `
...
`).join('')} ...`;
}

Custom Domain Flow

When a user connects a custom domain, the Naelao agent walks them through the DNS step, then calls the Cloudflare for SaaS API to provision the custom hostname. SSL is issued automatically by Cloudflare's certificate authority within minutes:

// workers/naelao-spaces/src/custom-domain.ts
export async function attachCustomDomain(
  spaceId: string,
  customHostname: string,
  env: Env
): Promise<{ verificationRecord: string }> {
  // Register with CF for SaaS
  const cfResponse = await fetch(
    `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${env.CF_ZONE_ID}/custom_hostnames`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.CF_API_TOKEN}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        hostname: customHostname,
        ssl: { method: 'txt', type: 'dv', settings: { min_tls_version: '1.2' } },
      }),
    }
  );
  const { result } = await cfResponse.json() as any;

  // Add the custom hostname to the KV route table
  const existingRoute = await env.PORTAL_ROUTES.get(`portal:space:${spaceId}`, 'json') as PortalRoute;
  await env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put(
    `portal:host:${customHostname}`,
    JSON.stringify({ ...existingRoute })
  );

  // Return the TXT record the user needs to add
  return {
    verificationRecord: result.ssl.txt_record.value,
  };
}

Static-First Caching Strategy

Portal performance is critical — a slow storefront loses customers. The router implements a static-first strategy that makes most portal requests cost zero compute:

  • Cache-Control propagation: If the portal's fetch() handler sets Cache-Control: max-age=60, the router caches that response at the CF edge for 60 seconds. Subsequent requests for that URL are served from cache — no Isolate invocation, no Scoped API call, no cost.
  • Cache invalidation on deploy: When the agent deploys a new version of the portal artifact to R2, naelao-sweeper purges the cache for that Space's portal hostname via the CF Cache Purge API.
  • Stale-while-revalidate: Portals should set stale-while-revalidate=300. Users always get a fast cached response; the cache refreshes in the background. Only first-hit after a cache miss hits the Isolate.
Security: What the Portal Isolate Cannot Do

Portal Workers run in Tier 2 Isolates with no direct CF bindings. They cannot call env.AGENT_DO, env.R2, or any other platform binding. The only way a portal reads data is through the @naelao/portal-sdk, which uses the read-only Scoped Token injected by the router. The token is bound to a single spaceId and grants only workspace_read and knowledge_read — never write permissions. A compromised portal artifact cannot exfiltrate other users' data, modify Space state, or trigger agent runs.

A7 — UI Orchestration

Operator Shell Slot System — The App Injection Pattern

The Naelao Operator Console is a "Shell" that provides core services (Auth, WebSocket, Navigation, Agent Chat) while leaving named "Slots" for Space Apps and Space Types to inject their own UIs. To ensure security and prevent CSS/JS leakage between apps and the host shell, every injected panel runs in a sandboxed <iframe> on a dedicated origin: ui.naelao.app.

"The shell is the stage; the apps are the performers. Neither can break the other's environment."

The Slot Architecture

The Space Type manifest and installed App manifests declare which app IDs mount into which slots. The Shell reads all active slot declarations on startup and renders the appropriate iframes. Slot declarations are merged and de-conflicted by UIOrchestrationDO:

Slot Name Location Dimensions Typical Use Case
sidebar Left navigation rail, below core nav items 48px × 48px icon; expands to 240px panel on click Custom navigation links, resource counts, notifications
main-content Primary content area, replaces thread/project view Full width × full height (minus shell chrome) Custom dashboards, code editors, data grids, video
dashboard-widget Home screen card grid 1–3 column grid cells, 200px min-height Revenue charts, agent status, pending task counts
drawer Slide-out panel from the right edge 380px wide × full height Contextual settings, file history, agent logs, detail views
header-action Action buttons in the top header bar 36px × 36px icon button Quick actions, global search, sync triggers
context-menu Right-click context menu additions Variable — menu items only Custom actions on files, threads, agents

Manifest Declaration

An App declares its slot requirements in its manifest. A Space Type manifest can also declare slot pre-fills — slots that are populated from the Space Type itself, not from an installed App:

// App manifest: declares the sidebar slot and a dashboard widget
{
  "id": "crm-connector",
  "ui": {
    "slots": [
      {
        "slot": "sidebar",
        "icon": "ti-address-book",
        "label": "CRM",
        "panelUrl": "https://crm-ui.acme.workers.dev/panel",
        "badge": {
          "type": "count",
          "dataSource": "tool:crm_get_pending_count"  // Agent calls this tool to get the badge number
        }
      },
      {
        "slot": "dashboard-widget",
        "title": "CRM Pipeline",
        "widgetUrl": "https://crm-ui.acme.workers.dev/widget",
        "gridColumns": 2
      }
    ]
  }
}

// Space Type manifest: pre-fills main-content with a custom dashboard
{
  "id": "mini-agi",
  "ui": {
    "operatorShell": {
      "defaultView": "custom-dashboard",
      "sidebarSlots": [
        { "slot": "sidebar", "appId": "naelao-mini-agi-console", "position": "top" }
      ],
      "dashboardWidgets": [
        { "slot": "dashboard-widget", "appId": "naelao-mini-agi-status", "gridColumns": 3 }
      ],
      "hiddenCoreItems": ["new-thread-button"]  // Mini-AGI hides the standard thread UI
    }
  }
}

Cross-Origin Communication (postMessage)

Because panels run on ui.naelao.app, they cannot access the Shell's localStorage, DOM, or WebSocket. All communication is through a strictly typed JSON protocol validated on both sides:

// shared/ui-protocol.ts — the full message contract

export type ShellToAppMessage =
  | { type: 'CONTEXT';        spaceId: string; agentId: string; theme: 'light'|'dark'; locale: string }
  | { type: 'PERSONALIZATION'; data: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { type: 'AGENT_STATUS';   status: 'idle'|'running'|'error' }
  | { type: 'THEME_CHANGE';   theme: 'light'|'dark' };

export type AppToShellMessage =
  | { type: 'NAVIGATE';       path: string }
  | { type: 'NOTIFY';         level: 'info'|'success'|'warning'|'error'; message: string }
  | { type: 'GET_CONTEXT' }
  | { type: 'RESIZE_WIDGET';  height: number }
  | { type: 'OPEN_DRAWER';    appId: string }
  | { type: 'RUN_AGENT';      prompt: string; agentId?: string }
  | { type: 'UPDATE_BADGE';   slot: string; count: number }
  | { type: 'WRITE_LEARNING'; key: string; value: unknown };  // Writes to UIInstructionsDO

// ── App panel implementation (inside the iframe) ─────────────────────
class NaelaoAppPanel {
  private shellOrigin = 'https://app.naelao.dev';

  constructor() {
    window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
      if (e.origin !== this.shellOrigin) return;
      this.handleShellMessage(e.data as ShellToAppMessage);
    });
    // Request initial context on load
    this.postToShell({ type: 'GET_CONTEXT' });
  }

  private handleShellMessage(msg: ShellToAppMessage) {
    switch (msg.type) {
      case 'CONTEXT':
        this.init(msg.spaceId, msg.agentId, msg.theme);
        break;
      case 'THEME_CHANGE':
        document.documentElement.dataset.theme = msg.theme;
        break;
    }
  }

  notify(message: string, level: 'info'|'success'|'warning'|'error' = 'info') {
    this.postToShell({ type: 'NOTIFY', level, message });
  }

  runAgent(prompt: string) {
    this.postToShell({ type: 'RUN_AGENT', prompt });
  }

  private postToShell(msg: AppToShellMessage) {
    window.parent.postMessage(msg, this.shellOrigin);
  }
}

// ── Shell listener (inside the main window) ──────────────────────────
window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
  if (event.origin !== 'https://ui.naelao.app') return;
  const msg = event.data as AppToShellMessage;

  switch (msg.type) {
    case 'NOTIFY':        showToast(msg.message, msg.level);       break;
    case 'NAVIGATE':      router.push(msg.path);                   break;
    case 'RESIZE_WIDGET': resizeIframe(event.source, msg.height);  break;
    case 'RUN_AGENT':     agentDispatch(msg.prompt, msg.agentId);  break;
    case 'WRITE_LEARNING': uiInstructionsDO.writeLearning(msg.key, msg.value); break;
  }
});

UIInstructionsDO Personalisation

Every App panel is backed by a UIInstructionsDO instance, scoped to {spaceId}:{appId}. As the user interacts with the panel, the App writes structured "UI learnings" back to the Shell via WRITE_LEARNING messages. The DO persists these learnings. When the iframe reloads, the Shell injects the current learnings as a personalization JSON object in the URL hash:

// The Shell constructs the iframe src with personalization injected
function buildPanelUrl(app: SlotDeclaration, learnings: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const url = new URL(app.panelUrl);
  // Hash is not sent to the server — safe for sensitive preferences
  url.hash = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({
    personalization: learnings,
    theme: getCurrentTheme(),
    locale: navigator.language,
  }));
  return url.toString();
}

// The App reads it on load
const hash = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1));
const { personalization, theme, locale } = JSON.parse(hash);
// e.g. personalization = { "preferDarkCards": true, "hideAdvancedFilter": false }

Slot Conflict Resolution

Multiple Apps or a Space Type and an App can both declare the same slot. UIOrchestrationDO resolves conflicts by priority:

  1. Space Type declarations have the highest priority. A Space Type that claims main-content for its own dashboard will always win over an App's request for the same slot.
  2. Explicitly pinned Apps (pinned by the user in Settings) take the next priority level.
  3. Recently installed Apps take the next level.
  4. Sidebar and drawer slots are additive — multiple Apps can each have a sidebar icon; they stack vertically in install order. Only main-content and dashboard-widget are exclusive per-position.
Security Boundary Summary

The Shell and App panels are on different origins by design. The Shell is on app.naelao.dev; panels are on ui.naelao.app. The browser's same-origin policy prevents panel code from accessing Shell cookies, localStorage, the WebSocket connection, or any DOM outside the iframe. The postMessage protocol is the only bridge, and both sides validate the origin header on every message. An App that sends a malformed or unknown message type is silently ignored — never executed.

A8 — Custom Intelligence

RemoteLoop — Platform-Internal Custom Agent Brains

While Naelao provides three standard loops (Chat, Content, Task), some Naelao-built Space Types require unique reasoning patterns that cannot be expressed as variants of these models. RemoteLoop is the internal protocol that allows Naelao's own Workers to implement custom agent reasoning while delegating tool execution, security enforcement, and streaming to the core platform. This interface is not exposed to community developers. Community developers who need custom reasoning should publish a Naelao App with a custom MCP server instead — the MCP tool boundary provides the necessary isolation without exposing conversation history or Scoped Tokens.

The Inverse Proxy Pattern

The name "RemoteLoop" reflects the inversion: normally a Worker calls out to an LLM. In RemoteLoop, the agent's core (AgentDO) calls out to the Loop Worker, which runs an LLM chain internally and calls back to Naelao for any tool execution. The platform remains in control of all side-effects.

1
Trigger: User message arrives at AgentDO. The DO reads the Space Type manifest and finds a customLoopWorker binding.
2
Token issuance: AgentDO mints a short-lived Scoped Token (TTL: 120s) bound to spaceId + agentId + the tool permissions declared in the manifest.
3
Delegation: AgentDO POSTs the full RemoteLoopRequest to the Loop Worker via a CF Service Binding (no public network hop).
4
Reasoning: The Loop Worker runs its custom LLM chain (Tree-of-Thought, recursive planner, etc.). It has no platform bindings of its own — it cannot read R2, call SpaceDO, or write to KV directly.
5
Tool callbacks: When the Loop Worker needs to execute a tool (read_file, run_code, call_api), it calls the Naelao Scoped API at https://api.naelao.dev/scoped/v1/tools with the Scoped Token. Naelao validates the token, checks the tool against the allowlist, runs the security scanner, and returns the result.
6
Streaming: The Loop Worker returns a ReadableStream of tokens to AgentDO, which validates the stream and forwards it over WebSocket to the user's browser.

RemoteLoop Request/Response Interfaces

// shared/types/remoteloop.ts

export interface RemoteLoopRequest {
  // Identity
  spaceId:  string;
  agentId:  string;
  turnId:   string;              // UUID for this specific turn — used for idempotency
  typeId:   string;              // Space Type ID, e.g. 'mini-agi'

  // Conversation state
  messages: Array<{
    role:    'user' | 'assistant' | 'system' | 'tool';
    content: string;
    toolCallId?: string;         // Present when role === 'tool'
  }>;

  // Tool surface available to this Loop
  availableTools: Array<{
    name:        string;
    description: string;
    inputSchema: Record<string, unknown>;  // JSON Schema
  }>;

  // Credential for calling back to Naelao
  scopedToken:   string;         // JWT, signed by Naelao, TTL 120s
  scopedApiBase: string;         // Always 'https://api.naelao.dev/scoped/v1'

  // Optional context injected by the Space Type
  spaceContext?: Record<string, unknown>;  // e.g. { "caseNumber": "2024-CV-1234" }
}

// The Loop Worker must return a streaming Response
// Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
// The stream is a sequence of UTF-8 text chunks (token fragments)
// Tool call results are interspersed as JSON lines prefixed with 'TOOL_RESULT:'

// Scoped API — tool execution endpoint
export interface ScopedToolRequest {
  tool:    string;               // Must be in the availableTools list
  input:   Record<string, unknown>;
  turnId:  string;               // Must match the turnId from the RemoteLoopRequest
}

export interface ScopedToolResponse {
  result:  unknown;
  error?:  { code: string; message: string };
  latency: number;               // ms
}

Calling the Scoped API from a Loop Worker

// Inside a RemoteLoop Worker
async function callTool(
  toolName: string,
  input: Record<string, unknown>,
  ctx: RemoteLoopRequest
): Promise<unknown> {
  const response = await fetch(`${ctx.scopedApiBase}/tools`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${ctx.scopedToken}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      tool:   toolName,
      input,
      turnId: ctx.turnId,
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const err = await response.json() as { error: { code: string; message: string } };
    throw new Error(`Tool ${toolName} failed: ${err.error.message}`);
  }

  const { result } = await response.json() as ScopedToolResponse;
  return result;
}

Worked Example — Legal Verticals Tree-of-Thought Loop

// workers/naelao-legal-loop/src/index.ts
// Runs a 3-branch Tree-of-Thought: generates 3 legal analyses in parallel,
// scores them against a legal-reasoning rubric, streams the best one.

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const req = await request.json() as RemoteLoopRequest;

    // Step 1: Generate 3 parallel analysis branches
    const branches = await Promise.all([
      runAnalysisBranch(req, 'conservative'),
      runAnalysisBranch(req, 'balanced'),
      runAnalysisBranch(req, 'expansive'),
    ]);

    // Step 2: Score each branch
    const scored = await scoreBranches(branches, req);

    // Step 3: Pick the highest-scoring branch
    const winner = scored.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)[0];

    // Step 4: Fetch supporting case law via the Scoped API
    const cases = await callTool('knowledge_search', {
      query: winner.legalQuestion,
      topK: 5,
    }, req);

    // Step 5: Stream the final answer with citations
    const finalAnswer = await streamFinalAnswer(winner, cases, req);

    return new Response(finalAnswer, {
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' },
    });
  }
}

async function runAnalysisBranch(
  req: RemoteLoopRequest,
  stance: 'conservative'|'balanced'|'expansive'
): Promise<Branch> {
  // Call the LLM with a stance-specific system prompt
  const prompt = buildBranchPrompt(req.messages, stance);
  return callLLM(prompt, env.AI);  // CF Workers AI binding
}

Security Constraints the Loop Worker Cannot Bypass

Attempted Bypass Why It Fails
Call a tool not in availableTools Scoped API validates the tool name against the manifest allowlist. Returns 403.
Reuse the Scoped Token after the turn Token TTL is 120s. After expiry, all Scoped API calls return 401.
Use a different turnId to replay a tool call Naelao tracks turnId usage. A token cannot be used with a different turnId than the one it was issued for.
Access another space's files The token is bound to spaceId. File paths that don't match workspace/{spaceId}/ return 403.
Make outbound HTTP calls directly Loop Workers have no egress. All side-effects must go through the Scoped API. Workers AI bindings are the only permitted direct call.
Return a response body larger than 4 MB per turn AgentDO enforces a 4 MB stream size limit. Excess bytes are dropped and a truncation notice is appended.
Why Community Developers Get MCP, Not RemoteLoop

RemoteLoop gives the Worker full visibility of the conversation history, the Scoped Token, and the user's tool surface — all in a single request body. A community developer operating a RemoteLoop Worker could log conversation history, exfiltrate Scoped Tokens, or abuse the tool surface in ways the user has not consented to. The MCP tool-call model gives community developers a much narrower surface: they receive only the specific tool name and its typed input, nothing else. The security tradeoff is intentional and permanent.

A9 — Runtime Constraints

Agent Environment Declaration — Layer 1 Deep Dive

The Agent Environment section of the manifest (Layer 1) is the "Hardware Spec" for the AI. It tells the provisioner exactly how to configure the AgentDO and its associated SandboxDO. This is where you define the difference between a "Light Chatbot" and a "Heavy Coding Agent." Every field in agentConfig has a direct runtime effect — this is not documentation, it is code.

Complete agentConfig Field Reference

Field Type Default Runtime Effect
defaultExecutionTier "workspace" | "isolate" | "npm" | "browser" | "sandbox" "isolate" If the LLM calls a tool without specifying a tier, the orchestrator uses this tier. Set to "workspace" for writing-only agents (Sites). Set to "sandbox" for Developer and Enterprise.
containerIdleTimeoutMs number 600000 0 = containers disabled. -1 = always warm (never idle). Any positive value = SandboxDO sets a DO Alarm to terminate the container after this many ms of inactivity. Directly controls cost.
loopModel "chat" | "task-completion" | "content" | "knowledge-graph" | "federated-query" | "file-edit" | "worker-task" "chat" Selects which loop function in agentpress/loops/ handles agent execution. Each loop has different iteration limits, output targets, and self-correction behaviors.
alwaysLoadedSkills string[] [] Skill IDs to inject into every agent's system prompt at initialization. Skills listed here are always available, even if the agent doesn't request them. Loaded from SkillRegistryDO.
disabledSkills string[] [] Skill IDs that are blocked for this Space Type, even if the agent or user requests them. Enforced at SkillRegistryDO.getSkill() — throws ERR_SKILL_DISABLED if the agent attempts to load a blocked skill.
networkPolicy.mode "open" | "restricted" | "none" "restricted" open: all outbound fetch() allowed. restricted: only allowlist domains. none: air-gapped, all outbound blocked. Enforced in the api-caller skill's pre-flight check AND in SandboxDO's container network policy.
networkPolicy.allowlist string[] [] When mode is "restricted", only these domains may be contacted. Wildcards only permitted for developer-labeled Space Types. The Security Scanner blocks wildcard allowlists in non-developer types.
maxContextTokens number 50000 Maximum conversation context the AgentDO will build before compacting. When the rolling token count exceeds this threshold, the orchestrator triggers context compaction: summarize oldest N messages into a single summary block.
agentPermissions AgentPermission[] ["workspace_read"] Fine-grained capability gates checked by the orchestrator before tool dispatch. Each tool declares which permissions it requires. If the agent lacks the permission, the tool call returns ERR_PERMISSION_DENIED without executing.
remoteLoopWorkers string[] [] List of internal Loop Worker IDs (e.g., "legal-loop") this Space Type's agents are permitted to dispatch to via dispatchRemoteLoop(). If empty, only the standard loop is available. Enforced by AgentDO's token scope check.
maxConcurrentRuns number 3 Maximum simultaneous background agent runs per Space. Enforced by ConcurrencyDO. Exceeding this causes ERR_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT. Enterprise defaults to 50.
promptCachingEnabled boolean true Whether to use Anthropic's prompt caching (ephemeral cache on system prompt + skills). Reduces time-to-first-token by ~60% on cache hits. Only disable for Space Types with highly dynamic system prompts where caching would waste budget.

agentPermissions — Complete Permission Matrix

Permission Grants Access To Checked By
workspace_read read_file, list_directory, search_workspace file-manager skill
workspace_write write_file, delete_file, create_directory file-manager skill
external_api_read api_caller (GET requests only) api-caller skill
external_api_write api_caller (POST/PUT/DELETE requests) api-caller skill
wallet_spend WalletDO.debit(), x402 payment sends WalletDO pre-authorize
x402_receive Accepting x402 payment proofs from external callers naelao-router x402 middleware
subspace_manage Creating/deleting sub-spaces, managing sub-space members naelao-spaces
graph_read KnowledgeGraphDO.traverse(), KnowledgeGraphDO.search() KnowledgeGraphDO
graph_propose KnowledgeGraphDO.proposeEdge() — requires admin approval KnowledgeGraphDO
cross_space_read MiniAGIDO cross-space data fetch (read-only, in-memory) MiniAGIDO permission graph
audit_write Writing immutable entries to the audit log naelao-analytics
cf_pages_deploy trigger_pages_build skill, deploy-expose skill deploy-expose skill CF API call
cf_api_access wrangler CLI inside container, CF API Token in env SandboxDO container env injection
marketplace_publish Publishing Worker Definitions to the talent marketplace WorkerDefinitionDO

How the Provisioner Reads agentConfig

When naelao-spaces provisions a new Space, it reads the manifest's agentConfig and writes the resolved configuration into two places: the SpaceDO SQLite spaces row (for fast runtime reads) and a KV key (for the SkillRegistryDO to bootstrap from).

// workers/spaces/provisioner.ts

async function applyAgentEnvironment(
  spaceId: string,
  manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifestV2,
  env: Env
): Promise<void> {
  const cfg = manifest.agentConfig;

  // 1. Write resolved config to SpaceDO SQLite (spaces.settings column) + KV cache for <1ms reads
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, env);  // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive
  await db.query(
    `UPDATE spaces SET agent_config = $1 WHERE id = $2`,
    [JSON.stringify({
      defaultExecutionTier: cfg.defaultExecutionTier ?? 'isolate',
      containerIdleTimeoutMs: cfg.containerIdleTimeoutMs ?? 600000,
      loopModel: cfg.loopModel ?? 'chat',
      networkPolicy: cfg.networkPolicy ?? { mode: 'restricted', allowlist: [] },
      maxContextTokens: cfg.maxContextTokens ?? 50000,
      agentPermissions: cfg.agentPermissions ?? ['workspace_read'],
      maxConcurrentRuns: cfg.maxConcurrentRuns ?? 3,
      promptCachingEnabled: cfg.promptCachingEnabled ?? true,
      remoteLoopWorkers: cfg.remoteLoopWorkers ?? []
    }), spaceId]
  );

  // 2. Pre-populate SkillRegistryDO with always-loaded skills
  const skillRegistryId = env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.idFromName(`skills:${spaceId}:default`);
  const skillRegistry = env.NAELAO_SKILL_REGISTRY.get(skillRegistryId);

  for (const skillId of (cfg.alwaysLoadedSkills ?? [])) {
    await skillRegistry.fetch(new Request('http://registry/install', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ skillId, autoLoad: true })
    }));
  }

  // 3. Register disabled skills so SkillRegistryDO can reject them at runtime
  if (cfg.disabledSkills?.length) {
    await skillRegistry.fetch(new Request('http://registry/disable', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ skillIds: cfg.disabledSkills })
    }));
  }

  // 4. Set container policy in SandboxDO for this space
  // (only if containerIdleTimeoutMs > 0)
  if ((cfg.containerIdleTimeoutMs ?? 600000) !== 0) {
    const sandboxId = env.NAELAO_SANDBOX_DO.idFromName(`sandbox:${spaceId}:default`);
    const sandbox = env.NAELAO_SANDBOX_DO.get(sandboxId);
    await sandbox.fetch(new Request('http://sandbox/configure', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        idleTimeoutMs: cfg.containerIdleTimeoutMs,
        networkAllowlist: cfg.networkPolicy?.allowlist ?? [],
        networkMode: cfg.networkPolicy?.mode ?? 'restricted'
      })
    }));
  }

  // 5. Initialize ConcurrencyDO with the correct limit
  const concurrencyId = env.NAELAO_CONCURRENCY_DO.idFromName(`concurrency:${spaceId}`);
  const concurrency = env.NAELAO_CONCURRENCY_DO.get(concurrencyId);
  await concurrency.fetch(new Request('http://concurrency/configure', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ maxConcurrentRuns: cfg.maxConcurrentRuns ?? 3 })
  }));
}
