⚠ Legal Callout — conversationLogAccess Is a Legally Significant Decision

This is not a simple boolean toggle. Whether a builder can read their end users' conversations has direct legal implications under GDPR Article 13, CCPA Section 1798.100, and potentially HIPAA and sector-specific regulations. The following requirements are mandatory.

1. Explicit Terms of Service disclosure. The product's Terms of Service must explicitly state that the builder or their designated admins may access conversation content. Vague language about "service improvement" is not sufficient.

2. Consent checkbox at signup. The user signup flow must include a dedicated checkbox — not bundled with the general Terms acceptance — that specifically mentions conversation access. This checkbox state is recorded in product_users.conversation_access_consented with a timestamp. If this column is false or null, builder-admin conversation access is blocked at the API level regardless of the product config flag.

3. Immutable audit trail. Every conversation access event by a builder-admin — every single one — must write an append-only record to CF Analytics Engine with: adminUserId, targetUserId, targetThreadId, accessTimestamp, IP address, justification (free text that admin must fill before access is granted). This cannot be disabled or batch-deleted.

4. Naelao-level policy gatekeeping. The conversationLogAccess flag can only be set to true if: (a) the builder's plan tier is Enterprise or higher, (b) the builder has acknowledged legal obligations in a separate checkbox during product setup, (c) a Naelao platform admin has manually reviewed and approved. Any attempt to enable this flag via the API without this approval chain returns HTTP 403: "conversationLogAccess requires platform-level approval. Submit a request at platform.naelao.app/access-review."

5. GDPR Article 13 compliance. At the time of data collection (signup), the builder must have informed users of: the identity of the data controller, the purposes of processing, the legal basis, the recipients, and the retention period. Naelao provides a template disclosure but the builder is legally responsible for its accuracy.

Complete Postgres Schema — Product Tables

-- ─── products ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE products (
  id                              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  builder_id                      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  space_id                        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  name                            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 2 AND 80),
  slug                            TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (slug ~ '^[a-z0-9-]{2,40}$'),
  domain                          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  custom_domain_verified          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  brand_color                     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '#3B82F6' CHECK (brand_color ~ '^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$'),
  logo_url                        TEXT,
  favicon_url                     TEXT,
  product_description             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  auth_provider                   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'naelao-native'
                                    CHECK (auth_provider IN ('naelao-native','clerk','custom-oidc','saml-sso')),
  allow_public_signup             BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  require_admin_approval          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  allowed_email_domains           TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  sso_config                      JSONB,
  pricing_type                    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free'
                                    CHECK (pricing_type IN ('free','subscription','credits','seats')),
  pricing_config                  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  builder_billing_model           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'usage-based'
                                    CHECK (builder_billing_model IN ('usage-based','flat-monthly')),
  builder_wholesale_rate_per_1k   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  user_permissions                JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  admin_features                  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  feature_flags                   JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  allow_user_sub_spaces           BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  sub_space_terminology           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'workspaces',
  max_sub_space_depth             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (max_sub_space_depth IN (1,2)),
  suppress_naelao_branding        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  naelao_attribution_text         TEXT,
  conversation_access_approved_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  conversation_access_approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  status                          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
                                    CHECK (status IN ('draft','active','suspended','deleted')),
  created_at                      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at                      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  launched_at                     TIMESTAMPTZ,
  suspended_at                    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  suspended_reason                TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_products_builder_id ON products(builder_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_products_space_id ON products(space_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_products_status ON products(status) WHERE status != 'deleted';
CREATE INDEX idx_products_domain ON products(domain);

CREATE TRIGGER products_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON products
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- ─── product_users ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A product user is NOT the same entity as a Naelao platform user even if they
-- share the same email. The same person using two different builder products is
-- two separate product_user records with isolated credit balances and permissions.
CREATE TABLE product_users (
  id                              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id                      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  external_user_id                TEXT NOT NULL,  -- ID from the builder's auth provider
  naelao_user_id                  UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  email                           TEXT NOT NULL,
  display_name                    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  avatar_url                      TEXT,
  role                            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'end-user'
                                    CHECK (role IN ('end-user','product-admin')),
  credits_used                    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  credits_limit                   BIGINT,         -- null = unlimited
  credits_reset_at                TIMESTAMPTZ,
  conversation_access_consented   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  conversation_access_consented_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  status                          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                                    CHECK (status IN ('active','pending-approval','suspended','deleted')),
  created_at                      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_active_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  UNIQUE (product_id, external_user_id),
  UNIQUE (product_id, email)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_product_users_product_id ON product_users(product_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_product_users_email ON product_users(product_id, email);
CREATE INDEX idx_product_users_status ON product_users(product_id, status);

-- ─── product_sessions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Active end-user sessions scoped to a product. Completely separate from Naelao
-- platform sessions. A user can have simultaneous sessions in multiple products.
CREATE TABLE product_sessions (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  product_user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES product_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  session_token_hash  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- SHA-256 hex, never store raw token
  ip_address          INET,
  user_agent          TEXT,
  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_active_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  revoked_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoke_reason       TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_product_sessions_product_user ON product_sessions(product_user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_product_sessions_expires ON product_sessions(expires_at) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

-- ─── product_audit_log ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- APPEND-ONLY. NEVER update or delete rows.
-- Every admin action that affects a user or their data MUST write here.
CREATE TABLE product_audit_log (
  id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  actor_user_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  target_user_id  UUID REFERENCES product_users(id),
  action          TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'conversation.access', 'user.suspend', 'feature-flag.update'
  target_resource TEXT,
  metadata        JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  justification   TEXT,            -- required for conversation.access actions
  ip_address      INET,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON product_audit_log FROM naelao_app;
GRANT INSERT, SELECT ON product_audit_log TO naelao_app;

CREATE INDEX idx_audit_product ON product_audit_log(product_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_action ON product_audit_log(product_id, action, created_at DESC);

BuilderAccountDO — Durable Object

One DO instance per Tier 1 builder. DO ID: idFromName('builder:{builderId}'). Manages the builder's product portfolio, aggregated usage, wholesale billing, builder-level analytics, API key management, and rate limiting state.

// File: workers/naelao-builder/src/BuilderAccountDO.ts
export class BuilderAccountDO extends DurableObject {
  private db: SqlStorage;

  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    this.db = ctx.storage.sql;
    this.initSchema();
  }

  private initSchema(): void {
    this.db.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS products (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        slug TEXT NOT NULL,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
        wholesale_rate_per_1k INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        added_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usage_snapshots (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        product_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
        billing_period TEXT NOT NULL,   -- YYYY-MM
        credits_consumed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        active_users INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        agent_runs INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        storage_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        UNIQUE(product_id, billing_period)
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS invoices (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        billing_period TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        line_items_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        total_credits_consumed INTEGER NOT NULL,
        total_usd_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
        generated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        stripe_invoice_id TEXT,
        paid_at TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_keys (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        hashed_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- SHA-256 hex, never store raw
        label TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        last_used_at TEXT,
        revoked_at TEXT
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rate_limit_state (
        window_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        request_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        last_request_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
    `);
  }

  async addProduct(productId: string, name: string, slug: string, wholesaleRate: number): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO products (id, name, slug, wholesale_rate_per_1k, added_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name, slug=excluded.slug,
         wholesale_rate_per_1k=excluded.wholesale_rate_per_1k`,
      productId, name, slug, wholesaleRate, new Date().toISOString()
    );
  }

  async removeProduct(productId: string): Promise<void> {
    // Never hard-delete — preserves billing history
    this.db.exec(`UPDATE products SET status = 'removed' WHERE id = ?`, productId);
  }

  async aggregateUsage(snapshot: {
    productId: string; billingPeriod: string; creditsConsumed: number;
    activeUsers: number; agentRuns: number; storageBytes: number;
  }): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO usage_snapshots
         (product_id, billing_period, credits_consumed, active_users, agent_runs, storage_bytes, recorded_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(product_id, billing_period) DO UPDATE SET
         credits_consumed = usage_snapshots.credits_consumed + excluded.credits_consumed,
         active_users = MAX(usage_snapshots.active_users, excluded.active_users),
         agent_runs = usage_snapshots.agent_runs + excluded.agent_runs,
         storage_bytes = MAX(usage_snapshots.storage_bytes, excluded.storage_bytes),
         recorded_at = excluded.recorded_at`,
      snapshot.productId, snapshot.billingPeriod, snapshot.creditsConsumed,
      snapshot.activeUsers, snapshot.agentRuns, snapshot.storageBytes, new Date().toISOString()
    );
  }

  async calculateMonthlyInvoice(billingPeriod: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    const rows = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT u.product_id, p.name, u.credits_consumed, p.wholesale_rate_per_1k
       FROM usage_snapshots u JOIN products p ON p.id = u.product_id
       WHERE u.billing_period = ?`, billingPeriod
    ).toArray();

    const lineItems = (rows as any[]).map(r => ({
      productId: r.product_id,
      productName: r.name,
      creditsConsumed: r.credits_consumed,
      wholesaleRatePerThousand: r.wholesale_rate_per_1k,
      subtotalUsdCents: Math.ceil((r.credits_consumed / 1000) * r.wholesale_rate_per_1k),
    }));

    const totalCredits = lineItems.reduce((s, l) => s + l.creditsConsumed, 0);
    const totalCents = lineItems.reduce((s, l) => s + l.subtotalUsdCents, 0);

    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO invoices (id, billing_period, line_items_json, total_credits_consumed, total_usd_cents, generated_at, status)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'draft')
       ON CONFLICT(billing_period) DO UPDATE SET
         line_items_json = excluded.line_items_json,
         total_credits_consumed = excluded.total_credits_consumed,
         total_usd_cents = excluded.total_usd_cents,
         generated_at = excluded.generated_at`,
      crypto.randomUUID(), billingPeriod, JSON.stringify(lineItems),
      totalCredits, totalCents, new Date().toISOString()
    );

    return { billingPeriod, lineItems, totalCreditsConsumed: totalCredits, totalUsdCents: totalCents };
  }

  async getAnalyticsSummary(billingPeriod: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    const rows = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT p.id, p.name, p.slug, p.status,
              COALESCE(u.credits_consumed, 0) as credits_consumed,
              COALESCE(u.active_users, 0) as active_users,
              COALESCE(u.agent_runs, 0) as agent_runs
       FROM products p
       LEFT JOIN usage_snapshots u ON u.product_id = p.id AND u.billing_period = ?
       WHERE p.status != 'removed' ORDER BY credits_consumed DESC`, billingPeriod
    ).toArray();
    return {
      period: billingPeriod,
      products: rows,
      totalCredits: (rows as any[]).reduce((s, r) => s + r.credits_consumed, 0),
      totalActiveUsers: (rows as any[]).reduce((s, r) => s + r.active_users, 0),
    };
  }

  async rotateApiKey(label: string): Promise<{ rawKey: string; keyId: string }> {
    const rawKey = `nbk_${crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '')}`;
    const keyId = crypto.randomUUID();
    const hashBuffer = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(rawKey));
    const hashedKey = Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuffer)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')).join('');
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO api_keys (id, hashed_key, label, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      keyId, hashedKey, label, new Date().toISOString()
    );
    return { rawKey, keyId }; // rawKey returned ONCE — cannot be recovered
  }

  async checkRateLimit(windowKey: string, limitPerWindow: number): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining: number }> {
    const row = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT request_count FROM rate_limit_state WHERE window_key = ?`, windowKey
    ).one() as { request_count: number } | null;
    const current = row?.request_count ?? 0;
    if (current >= limitPerWindow) return { allowed: false, remaining: 0 };
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO rate_limit_state (window_key, request_count, last_request_at) VALUES (?, 1, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(window_key) DO UPDATE SET request_count = rate_limit_state.request_count + 1,
         last_request_at = excluded.last_request_at`,
      windowKey, new Date().toISOString()
    );
    return { allowed: true, remaining: limitPerWindow - current - 1 };
  }
}

ProductUserDO — Durable Object

One DO per (product, end user) pair. DO ID always: idFromName('product-user:{productId}:{externalUserId}'). The same person using two different builder products has two completely isolated DOs — no shared credit balance, no shared session history, no shared state of any kind.

// File: workers/naelao-builder/src/ProductUserDO.ts
export class ProductUserDO extends DurableObject {
  private db: SqlStorage;

  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    this.db = ctx.storage.sql;
    this.initSchema();
  }

  private initSchema(): void {
    this.db.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session_state (
        key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS credit_ledger (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        delta INTEGER NOT NULL,         -- negative = deduction, positive = top-up
        balance_after INTEGER NOT NULL,
        reason TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'agent-run', 'monthly-reset', 'purchase', 'admin-grant'
        thread_id TEXT,
        recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversation_refs (
        thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        product_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        title TEXT,
        message_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        credits_consumed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        last_message_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS preferences (
        key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notification_queue (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        type TEXT NOT NULL, payload TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL, delivered_at TEXT,
        failed_at TEXT, retry_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
      );
    `);
  }

  async createSession(sessionData: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(sessionData)) {
      this.db.exec(
        `INSERT INTO session_state (key, value, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
         ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,
        key, JSON.stringify(value), new Date().toISOString()
      );
    }
  }

  async deductCredits(amount: number, reason: string, threadId?: string):
    Promise<{ success: boolean; balanceAfter: number; error?: string }> {
    const row = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT balance_after FROM credit_ledger ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`
    ).one() as { balance_after: number } | null;
    const currentBalance = row?.balance_after ?? 0;
    if (currentBalance < amount) return { success: false, balanceAfter: currentBalance, error: 'insufficient_credits' };
    const balanceAfter = currentBalance - amount;
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO credit_ledger (delta, balance_after, reason, thread_id, recorded_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      -amount, balanceAfter, reason, threadId ?? null, new Date().toISOString()
    );
    return { success: true, balanceAfter };
  }

  async checkCreditBalance(): Promise<{ balance: number; limit: number | null }> {
    const row = this.db.exec(`SELECT balance_after FROM credit_ledger ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`).one() as any;
    const limitRow = this.db.exec(`SELECT value FROM preferences WHERE key = 'credits_limit'`).one() as any;
    return { balance: row?.balance_after ?? 0, limit: limitRow ? JSON.parse(limitRow.value) : null };
  }

  async recordConversationRef(threadId: string, productId: string, title?: string): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO conversation_refs (thread_id, product_id, title, created_at, last_message_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(thread_id) DO UPDATE SET
         title = COALESCE(excluded.title, conversation_refs.title),
         message_count = conversation_refs.message_count + 1,
         last_message_at = excluded.last_message_at`,
      threadId, productId, title ?? null, new Date().toISOString(), new Date().toISOString()
    );
  }

  async getUsageSummary(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    const balance = await this.checkCreditBalance();
    const threadCount = (this.db.exec(`SELECT COUNT(*) as c FROM conversation_refs`).one() as any)?.c ?? 0;
    const creditsUsed = (this.db.exec(`SELECT SUM(credits_consumed) as s FROM conversation_refs`).one() as any)?.s ?? 0;
    return { balance, threadCount, creditsUsed };
  }

  async suspendUser(reason: string): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO session_state (key, value, updated_at) VALUES ('suspended', ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value, updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,
      JSON.stringify({ reason, at: new Date().toISOString() }), new Date().toISOString()
    );
  }

  async exportUserData(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    // GDPR Article 20 — right to data portability. No redaction.
    return {
      exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
      sessionState: this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM session_state`).toArray(),
      creditHistory: this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM credit_ledger ORDER BY id`).toArray(),
      conversationRefs: this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM conversation_refs ORDER BY created_at`).toArray(),
      preferences: this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM preferences`).toArray(),
    };
  }
}

Builder Dashboard API — Complete Endpoint Reference

All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer nbk_... header. The first operation of every handler is validateProductScope(productId, builderId, env). This is never optional. Any handler that skips it is a security vulnerability.

// ─── validateProductScope — first line of every builder-facing handler ─────────
// File: workers/naelao-builder/src/middleware/validateProductScope.ts
export async function validateProductScope(productId: string, builderId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> {
  const row = await env.DB.prepare(
    `SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? AND builder_id = ? AND status != 'deleted'`
  ).bind(productId, builderId).first();
  if (!row) {
    throw new Response(JSON.stringify({
      error: 'PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND_OR_UNAUTHORIZED',
      message: `Product ${productId} does not exist or does not belong to builder ${builderId}.`,
    }), { status: 403, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
  }
}

// ─── ENDPOINT DEFINITIONS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// POST /builder/products
// Auth: builder API key. Creates a new product for the authenticated builder.
// Request body: { name, slug, domain, spaceId, authProvider, pricingType, brandColor }
// Response 201: { product: NaelaoProduct }
// Errors: 400 (slug taken), 400 (space not owned by builder), 409 (domain conflict)

// GET /builder/products
// Lists all products. Query params: status, page, limit (max 100).
// Response 200: { products: NaelaoProduct[], total: number, page: number }

// GET /builder/products/{productId}
// validateProductScope first. Response 200: { product: NaelaoProduct }

// PATCH /builder/products/{productId}
// Partial update. If adminFeatures.conversationLogAccess → true, check
// conversation_access_approved_at is non-null or return 403.
// Response 200: { product: NaelaoProduct }

// DELETE /builder/products/{productId}
// Soft delete. status = 'suspended'. Data retained 90 days.
// Response 200: { deletedAt, dataRetainedUntil }

// POST /builder/products/{productId}/domain
// Body: { domain: "lexspace.com" }
// Steps: validate format → check uniqueness → call CF SSL for SaaS API →
//   write to DOMAIN_REGISTRY_KV key='domain:{hostname}' value=productId →
//   return DNS TXT record for verification
// Response 202: { verificationRecord: { type: 'TXT', name, value }, status: 'pending' }

// GET /builder/products/{productId}/users
// Query: status, role, email, page, limit.
// Response 200: { users: ProductUser[], total: number }

// GET /builder/products/{productId}/users/{userId}
// Response 200: { user: ProductUser, usage: UsageSummary }

// DELETE /builder/products/{productId}/users/{userId}
// GDPR deletion cascade. User record anonymized, audit log retained.
// Response 200: { deletedAt }

// POST /builder/products/{productId}/users/{userId}/suspend
// Body: { reason: string }. Writes to ProductUserDO + product_audit_log.
// Response 200: { suspendedAt }

// GET /builder/products/{productId}/users/{userId}/conversations
// REQUIRES: conversationLogAccess=true AND conversation_access_approved_at!=null
//           AND target user's conversation_access_consented=true
// WRITES to product_audit_log AND CF Analytics Engine BEFORE returning data.
// Returns conversation METADATA ONLY — not content.
// Response 200: { conversations: ConversationRef[], auditEventId: string }
// Errors: 403 (not approved), 403 (user not consented), 403 (feature disabled)

// GET /builder/products/{productId}/analytics
// Query: period (YYYY-MM), granularity ('day'|'week'|'month')
// Response 200: { period, dau: number[], mau, creditsConsumed, agentRuns,
//                topThreadsByActivity, newUsers, churnedUsers }

// GET /builder/products/{productId}/analytics/revenue
// Only available if pricingConfig.type != 'free'
// Response 200: { period, grossRevenue, naelaoWholesaleCost, netMargin, arpu, mrr }

// PUT /builder/products/{productId}/feature-flags
// Body: { flags: Record<string, boolean> } — replaces entire flag map atomically.
// Side effect: invalidates KV cache for product config (TTL reset).
// Response 200: { flags, updatedAt }

// POST /builder/products/{productId}/webhooks
// Body: { url, events: string[], secret }
// Response 201: { webhookId }

// GET /builder/billing
// Current in-progress Naelao invoice for the builder.
// Response 200: { invoice: MonthlyInvoice }

// GET /builder/billing/history
// Response 200: { invoices: MonthlyInvoice[], page, total }

White-Label Portal Architecture

// ─── naelao-router Worker ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// File: workers/naelao-router/src/index.ts
// Sits in front of ALL product deployments. Every request to any Naelao-hosted
// product passes through this Worker before reaching the product frontend.

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const hostname = request.headers.get('Host') ?? new URL(request.url).hostname;

    // 1. Resolve productId from hostname via KV
    // Key format: 'domain:{hostname}' → value: productId
    const productId = await env.DOMAIN_REGISTRY_KV.get(`domain:${hostname}`);
    if (!productId) return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });

    // 2. Fetch product config from KV cache (TTL: 60 seconds)
    let productConfig = await env.PRODUCT_CONFIG_KV.get(`product-config:${productId}`, 'json');
    if (!productConfig) {
      const resp = await env.NAELAO_INTERNAL.fetch(`http://internal/products/${productId}/config`);
      productConfig = await resp.json();
      await env.PRODUCT_CONFIG_KV.put(`product-config:${productId}`, JSON.stringify(productConfig), { expirationTtl: 60 });
    }

    // 3. Inject product context into request headers (consumed by product frontend Worker)
    // NEVER pass the full product config — only the fields the frontend needs.
    // Other products' configs must never leak through shared headers.
    const augmentedRequest = new Request(request, {
      headers: {
        ...Object.fromEntries(request.headers.entries()),
        'X-Naelao-Product-Id': productId,
        'X-Naelao-Brand-Color': (productConfig as any).brandColor,
        'X-Naelao-Branding-Suppressed': (productConfig as any).suppressNaelaoBranding ? '1' : '0',
        'X-Naelao-Auth-Provider': (productConfig as any).authProvider,
        'X-Naelao-Feature-Flags': JSON.stringify((productConfig as any).featureFlags),
      }
    });

    // 4. Proxy to the product's CF Pages deployment (one Pages project per product)
    return env.PRODUCT_FRONTEND.fetch(augmentedRequest);
  }
}

// ─── getProductConfig() — server-side only ────────────────────────────────────
// File: apps/product-shell/src/lib/getProductConfig.ts
// Called in server components / getServerSideProps. Reads from request headers.
// NEVER called client-side. NEVER exposes other products' configs.
export function getProductConfig(request: Request): ProductConfig {
  const headers = request.headers;
  const productId = headers.get('X-Naelao-Product-Id');
  if (!productId) throw new Error('Missing product context — not routed through naelao-router');
  return {
    productId,
    brandColor: headers.get('X-Naelao-Brand-Color') ?? '#3B82F6',
    brandingSuppressed: headers.get('X-Naelao-Branding-Suppressed') === '1',
    authProvider: headers.get('X-Naelao-Auth-Provider') as ProductAuthProvider,
    featureFlags: JSON.parse(headers.get('X-Naelao-Feature-Flags') ?? '{}'),
  };
}
CF Pages Deployment Strategy — One Project Per Product

Each NaelaoProduct gets its own CF Pages project. The alternative — a single multi-tenant Pages project with runtime config injection — is rejected because: (1) a deployment bug in one product would affect all products, (2) CF Pages rollback is per-project, (3) builders may want different framework versions for their products, (4) CF Pages project isolation maps cleanly to the product isolation model. When a builder creates a new product, the Builder Dashboard API triggers a CF Pages project creation via the CF API, deploys the base product shell template, and links the custom domain. This is automated — the builder never touches CF dashboards directly.

NAELAO_BRANDING_SUPPRESSED — What It Gates and What It Cannot Gate

When suppressNaelaoBranding = true, the following are removed: "Powered by Naelao" footer text, any Naelao logo marks, the Naelao help center link, and Naelao's product name in auth emails. The following are NEVER removed: legal terms of service attribution if required by the builder's plan tier, the Naelao data processing agreement reference in privacy policy boilerplate, and security contact information required by law. A builder cannot suppress legal disclosures. If they attempt to do so via CSS or custom code injection, the CF Worker layer enforces the disclosure text at the response level before it reaches the browser.

SSL Certificate Provisioning for Custom Domains

Custom domain SSL is handled via Cloudflare SSL for SaaS. When a builder POSTs to /builder/products/{productId}/domain, the Worker calls the CF API to add a custom hostname to the Naelao zone. CF issues the certificate automatically via Let's Encrypt. The builder verifies domain ownership by adding a DNS TXT record. Verification is polled every 60 seconds by the naelao-domain-verifier Cron Worker, which updates products.custom_domain_verified = true and writes the productId to DOMAIN_REGISTRY_KV once verified. The entire flow takes under 5 minutes for domains with standard TTLs.

Three-Tier Billing Architecture

// ─── Credit Metering — CF Analytics Engine (not Postgres) ─────────────────────
// Every AI message, every tool call completion, every agent run writes a credit event.
// At 500,000 events/day for a mid-scale product, writing to Postgres would saturate
// connection pools. CF Analytics Engine is a write-optimized time-series store:
// fire-and-forget, no transactions, native aggregation.

// In AgentDO — called on every tool call completion:
async function recordCreditUsage(env: Env, event: {
  productId: string; spaceId: string; threadId: string; userId: string;
  creditsConsumed: number; agentRuns: number; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number;
}): Promise<void> {
  env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS.writeDataPoint({
    blobs: [event.productId, event.spaceId, event.threadId, event.userId],
    doubles: [event.creditsConsumed, event.agentRuns, event.inputTokens, event.outputTokens],
    indexes: [event.productId],  // partition key for fast product-level aggregation
  });
}

// ─── Revenue Flow ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// End user ──pays──> Builder's Stripe account    (builder sets price, keeps revenue)
// Builder  ──pays──> Naelao's Stripe account     (metered monthly, wholesale rate)
// Naelao   ──pays──> Cloudflare                  (Workers, DO, R2, KV, Analytics)
//
// Naelao NEVER intermediates end-user payments. Stripe Connect is NOT used.
// Builder manages their own Stripe account entirely.

// ─── Credit Balance Exhaustion — Graceful Degradation ────────────────────────
// When ProductUserDO.deductCredits() returns { success: false, error: 'insufficient_credits' }:
//   1. AgentDO halts the current tool chain gracefully — no uncaught exception
//   2. AgentDO sends a final message: a system "credits exhausted" UI card with
//      a top-up link (if builder has credits bundles configured)
//   3. Thread is NOT deleted. User's work is preserved.
//   4. Error is NEVER surfaced as a raw error message in the product UI.

// ─── Builder Account Delinquency Flow ─────────────────────────────────────────
// Day 0:  Invoice generated. Stripe charge attempted automatically.
// Day 3:  Charge failed. Builder receives email warning. Grace period begins.
// Day 6:  Grace period ends. Products set to 'suspended' in DB and KV.
//         End users see "temporarily unavailable" with no Naelao branding.
// Day 36: 30-day data retention window begins. No data deleted yet.
// Day 66: Data deletion begins. User data anonymized per retention policy.
// Resolution: Builder pays → products reactivated within 60s (KV cache TTL).

// ─── WholesaleBillingDO ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// DO ID: idFromName('wholesale-billing:{builderId}:{YYYY-MM}')
export class WholesaleBillingDO extends DurableObject {
  private db: SqlStorage;
  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    this.db = ctx.storage.sql;
    this.db.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS credit_events (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        product_id TEXT NOT NULL, space_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        thread_id TEXT NOT NULL, credits INTEGER NOT NULL, recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ce_product ON credit_events(product_id);
    `);
  }
  async recordEvent(productId: string, spaceId: string, threadId: string, credits: number): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO credit_events (product_id, space_id, thread_id, credits, recorded_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      productId, spaceId, threadId, credits, new Date().toISOString()
    );
  }
  async getInvoiceData(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    const byProduct = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT product_id, SUM(credits) as total_credits, COUNT(*) as event_count
       FROM credit_events GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY total_credits DESC`
    ).toArray();
    return {
      lineItems: byProduct,
      totalCredits: (byProduct as any[]).reduce((s, r) => s + r.total_credits, 0),
    };
  }
}

Security and Isolation Guarantees

⚠ Junior Developer Warning — The Most Common Multi-Tenant Bug

You will write SELECT * FROM product_users WHERE email = ? instead of SELECT * FROM product_users WHERE product_id = ? AND email = ?. You will instantiate a DO with idFromName(userId) instead of idFromName('product-user:{productId}:{userId}'). These mistakes leak one builder's data to another. The rule: validateProductScope(productId, builderId, env) is the first line of every builder-facing handler. Never optional. Never skipped. Every call. Every time.

Builders CAN see
Usage metadata per user (credits, agent runs, last active) · Conversation metadata if explicitly approved + audit trail · Agent run logs scoped to their product · Aggregate analytics (DAU, MAU, credit burn) · User profile data provided at signup
Builders CANNOT see
Other builders' products or users · Naelao infrastructure details (DO IDs, Worker names, KV namespaces) · Raw credit costs (abstracted to usage units) · Conversation content from users who have not consented · Any data outside their builderId scope
Tenant Isolation Test Suite — Must Pass Before Any Product Goes Live15 tests
Builder A cannot read Builder B's product list via /builder/products
Builder A's API key returns 403 for any productId owned by Builder B
validateProductScope throws on valid productId + wrong builderId (not just missing)
End user of Product A cannot access Product B's threads via thread ID guessing
ProductUserDO for user X in Product A is a different DO than user X in Product B
Credit deduction in Product A does not affect credit balance in Product B for same email
Session token for Product A cannot authenticate in Product B
Conversation access blocked when user consent is false, regardless of product config flag
Audit log write cannot be bypassed via race condition in conversation access endpoint
Custom domain resolution returns 404 for unregistered domains — no product config leakage
DOMAIN_REGISTRY_KV returns no data for domains not explicitly registered
Feature flags for Product A are not accessible by authenticated user of Product B
KV cache invalidation correctly scopes to productId, not global invalidation
Rate limit state in BuilderAccountDO is per-builder, not global
Builder A cannot read Builder B's user list via product ID guessing attacks
49 — Sub-Space Architecture

Sub-Spaces in the Platform Model

Sub-spaces are organizational units within a product deployment. They share the parent product's identity, domain, and UI shell. They differ in data scope, member list, agent configuration, and permissions. Sub-spaces are not separate products. They do not get separate domains. They do not have independent billing relationships. Every one of these statements is enforced at the API level — not just documented.

Core Definition — Read This Before Touching Any Sub-Space Code

A sub-space is always a child of a root space within a product. It shares the product's domain. It shares the product's UI shell. It may have its own agent configuration, knowledge base prefix, and member list — but it is part of the same product. The product admin has full visibility across all sub-spaces. Billing rolls up to the product. The one exception — where mixed space types are permitted — is the agency shell scenario (Scenario B). This exception is narrow, explicit, and enforced by the agency_shell database column. Do not generalize it.

Scenario A — Internal Organizational Structure (same space type throughout)

A single product where end users are organized into departments, teams, or practice groups. All sub-spaces share the parent's space type. A law firm deploys Naelao as an internal tool. The parent space is the firm root. Sub-spaces are practice groups: Litigation, M&A, IP, Employment. Each has its own knowledge base, its own agents tuned for that workflow, and its own member list. A Litigation member cannot query M&A's deal documents unless an explicit cross-sub-space access grant exists. The parent admin has full visibility across all groups. The UI is the same product shell throughout — navigation context changes based on active sub-space, but domain and branding never change.

The API enforcement: POST /api/spaces/{parentId}/sub-spaces with a different spaceType than the parent when parent.agency_shell = false returns HTTP 400: "Mixed space types are only permitted when the parent space is configured as an agency shell. The parent space {parentId} is type {parentType}. Set agencyShell: true on the parent or create a same-type sub-space."

React Component Architecture — Scenario A

// ─── ProductShell ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// File: apps/product-shell/src/components/ProductShell.tsx
// The outermost component. Never changes regardless of which sub-space is active.
// Provides product branding, top-level nav, and auth context.
// Has zero awareness of sub-space content — it only renders the chrome.

interface ProductShellProps {
  config: ProductConfig;    // injected server-side via getProductConfig()
  user: ProductUser;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

export function ProductShell({ config, user, children }: ProductShellProps) {
  return (
    <ProductConfigContext.Provider value={config}>
      <ProductUserContext.Provider value={user}>
        <div className="product-shell" style={{ '--brand-color': config.brandColor } as React.CSSProperties}>
          <ProductTopBar config={config} user={user} />
          <div className="product-shell__body">
            <SubSpaceSwitcher />         {/* sidebar — lists all accessible sub-spaces */}
            <main className="product-shell__content">
              {children}                  {/* SubSpaceLayout renders here */}
            </main>
          </div>
        </div>
      </ProductUserContext.Provider>
    </ProductConfigContext.Provider>
  );
}

// ─── SubSpaceContext ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
interface SubSpaceContextValue {
  activeSubSpaceId: string;
  activeSubSpace: SubSpaceRecord;
  userRole: 'member' | 'admin' | 'read-only';
  userPermissions: SubSpacePermissions;
  spaceType: SpaceType;                    // always same as parent in Scenario A
  availableNavItems: NavItem[];
  crossSubSpaceGrants: CrossSubSpaceGrant[]; // spaces this user can access cross-boundary
}
// Re-fetches from server when active sub-space ID changes.
// Does NOT trigger full page reload on sub-space switch.

// ─── SubSpaceLayout ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Renders the appropriate layout for the space type.
// In Scenario A: always same layout as parent. Reads from SubSpaceContext.
// Handles: sidebar nav, breadcrumb, sub-space header.

// ─── SubSpaceSwitcher ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// In left sidebar of ProductShell. Lists all sub-spaces the user is a member of.
// Switching sub-spaces:
//   1. Updates URL: /{productSlug}/spaces/{subSpaceId}/...
//   2. Calls SubSpaceContext.setActiveSubSpace(subSpaceId)
//   3. Re-fetches sub-space data from server
//   4. Re-renders SubSpaceLayout and ActiveView
//   5. Does NOT trigger full page reload

// ─── URL Structure — Scenario A ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// Platform:    https://firmtool.naelao.app/spaces/parent-id/litigation/projects
// White-label: https://firmtool.com/departments/litigation/projects
// Navigation within the product never exposes a Naelao URL.

Scenario B — Agency / Holding Company Model (mixed space types ONLY here)

A builder owns an agency managing multiple client deployments. The parent space is an internal admin shell — never exposed to clients, no public-facing portal, serves only agency staff. Each client gets their own child sub-space with its own space type appropriate for that client's use case and, optionally, its own domain.

Because the parent is an internal admin shell and each child is effectively a separate product, mixed space types are permitted in Scenario B only. Client A might be Verticals/Legal. Client B might be Launchpad. Client C might be Developer.

// ─── Agency shell enforcement in Worker handler ───────────────────────────────
// File: workers/naelao-spaces/src/handlers/createSubSpace.ts
export async function handleCreateSubSpace(request: Request, env: Env, parentId: string): Promise<Response> {
  const body = await request.json() as { spaceType?: string; [key: string]: unknown };
  const parent = await spaceDO.getSpaceMeta(parentId)  // SpaceDO typed method — no raw SQL from Workers as { space_type: string; agency_shell: boolean; depth: number } | null;

  if (!parent) return new Response('Parent space not found', { status: 404 });

  // Depth check — platform hierarchy reserves depth 3
  if (parent.depth >= 2) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({
      error: 'MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED',
      message: 'Sub-spaces cannot be nested more than 2 levels deep.',
    }), { status: 400, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
  }

  // Mixed type check — only permitted for agency shells
  if (body.spaceType && body.spaceType !== parent.space_type && !parent.agency_shell) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({
      error: 'MIXED_SPACE_TYPE_NOT_PERMITTED',
      message: `Mixed space types are only permitted when the parent space is configured as an ` +
               `agency shell. The parent space ${parentId} is type '${parent.space_type}'. ` +
               `Set agencyShell: true on the parent or create a same-type sub-space.`,
    }), { status: 400, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
  }

  // For non-agency-shell parents, ALWAYS inherit the parent's space type
  const effectiveType = parent.agency_shell ? (body.spaceType ?? parent.space_type) : parent.space_type;
  // ... proceed to create sub-space with effectiveType
}

// ─── Agency billing rollup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
// All client sub-spaces bill to the agency's Naelao invoice.
// SubSpaceDO.rollupBillingUsage() called by billing cron Worker daily.
// Writes to sub_space_billing_rollup which WholesaleBillingDO reads at invoice time.

// ─── Staff access control ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Agency admins grant individual staff members access to specific client sub-spaces
// via sub_space_members with inherited_from_parent = false.
// Revoking access removes the record — client sub-space data remains intact.

// ─── Client transfer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// POST /api/spaces/{spaceId}/promote-to-product
// Converts a client sub-space to a standalone NaelaoProduct.
// See "When a Sub-Space Becomes a Separate Product" section below.

Agency Scenario UI Architecture

The parent admin shell has its own management dashboard — showing all client sub-spaces, their health, usage, billing, and quick links. This is the builder-admin view. Each child sub-space has its own completely independent UI deployed as its own CF Pages project. There is no shared React component tree between the parent admin shell and any client sub-space. A client user going to lexspace.com has zero awareness that an agency admin shell exists. The parent and child never render together in the same browser context.

Scenario C — Product-Defined User Workspaces (same space type, builder-controlled)

A builder's product supports workspace sub-division for its end users. From the infrastructure perspective these are sub-spaces. From the end user's perspective they are "workspaces" or "teams" or "projects" — whatever the builder configured in subSpaceTerminology. The builder configures: whether end users can create sub-spaces, the maximum depth permitted (1 or 2 — never 3), and the terminology. Sub-spaces created by end users always inherit the parent's space type. A Cursor-equivalent product is Developer type. Every workspace an end user creates within it is also Developer type. The builder does not expose space type selection to end users.

// API enforcement for end-user-created sub-spaces:
// When the request originates from a product_user session (not a builder API key),
// the Worker forces effectiveType = parent.space_type regardless of request body.
// The end user cannot select a space type — the builder fixed it at product config.
// This check runs BEFORE the agency_shell check — end users cannot create agency shells.

Sub-Space Postgres Schema — Complete Extension

-- ─── Extension to spaces table ────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE spaces
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS parent_space_id UUID REFERENCES spaces(id),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS depth INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS agency_shell BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scenario_type TEXT
    CHECK (scenario_type IN ('organizational', 'agency-child', 'user-workspace')),
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_depth CHECK (depth BETWEEN 0 AND 2),
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_no_self_parent CHECK (parent_space_id IS DISTINCT FROM id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_spaces_parent ON spaces(parent_space_id) WHERE parent_space_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_spaces_depth ON spaces(depth);

-- ─── sub_space_members ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE sub_space_members (
  id                    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  space_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id               UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role                  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member'
                          CHECK (role IN ('member', 'admin', 'read-only', 'observer')),
  inherited_from_parent BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  granted_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  granted_by            UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  expires_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
  UNIQUE (space_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_ssm_space ON sub_space_members(space_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_ssm_user ON sub_space_members(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_ssm_active ON sub_space_members(space_id, user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

-- ─── cross_sub_space_grants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE cross_sub_space_grants (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  granting_space_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  receiving_space_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  grant_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (grant_type IN ('read-knowledge', 'read-threads', 'full-access')),
  granted_by          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  granted_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
  audit_log_id        BIGINT REFERENCES product_audit_log(id),
  CHECK (granting_space_id != receiving_space_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_csg_granting ON cross_sub_space_grants(granting_space_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_csg_receiving ON cross_sub_space_grants(receiving_space_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

-- ─── sub_space_billing_rollup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Written by billing cron Worker on daily cadence. Consumed by WholesaleBillingDO.
CREATE TABLE sub_space_billing_rollup (
  id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  space_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id),
  parent_space_id UUID REFERENCES spaces(id),
  billing_period  TEXT NOT NULL,    -- YYYY-MM
  day             DATE NOT NULL,
  credits_consumed BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  agent_runs      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  storage_bytes   BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  written_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, day)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_ssbr_period ON sub_space_billing_rollup(parent_space_id, billing_period);

SubSpaceDO — Complete Durable Object Implementation

The authoritative source for sub-space hierarchy state, member relationships, permission grants, and cross-sub-space access decisions. Every cross-sub-space data operation across the entire platform calls SubSpaceDO.checkPermission() before executing. No exceptions. The checkPermission() method must never throw silently or default to permitted on error. On any error condition it defaults to denied and logs the error.

// File: workers/naelao-spaces/src/SubSpaceDO.ts

interface PermissionResult {
  permitted: boolean;
  reason: string;           // human-readable — used for error messages
  grantType: string | null; // null if direct membership
}

export class SubSpaceDO extends DurableObject {
  private db: SqlStorage;

  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    this.db = ctx.storage.sql;
    this.initSchema();
  }

  initSchema(): void {
    this.db.exec(`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS space_meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS members (
        user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
        inherited_from_parent INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        granted_at TEXT NOT NULL, granted_by TEXT,
        expires_at TEXT, revoked_at TEXT
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cross_space_grants (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, granting_space_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        receiving_space_id TEXT NOT NULL, grant_type TEXT NOT NULL,
        granted_by TEXT NOT NULL, granted_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        expires_at TEXT, revoked_at TEXT
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_usage (
        day TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
        credits_consumed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        agent_runs INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        storage_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
      );
    `);
  }

  async addMember(userId: string, role: string, grantedBy: string, inheritedFromParent: boolean, expiresAt?: string): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO members (user_id, role, inherited_from_parent, granted_at, granted_by, expires_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(user_id) DO UPDATE SET role=excluded.role, granted_at=excluded.granted_at,
         granted_by=excluded.granted_by, expires_at=excluded.expires_at, revoked_at=NULL`,
      userId, role, inheritedFromParent ? 1 : 0, new Date().toISOString(), grantedBy, expiresAt ?? null
    );
  }

  async removeMember(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(`UPDATE members SET revoked_at = ? WHERE user_id = ?`, new Date().toISOString(), userId);
  }

  async getMemberRole(userId: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const now = new Date().toISOString();
    const row = this.db.exec(
      `SELECT role FROM members WHERE user_id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?)`,
      userId, now
    ).one() as { role: string } | null;
    return row?.role ?? null;
  }

  // ─── checkPermission — THE CRITICAL PATH ──────────────────────────────────
  // Called before EVERY cross-sub-space data operation in the platform.
  // Default behavior on any error: DENIED. Never silently permitted.
  async checkPermission(
    requestingUserId: string,
    requestingSpaceId: string,
    targetSpaceId: string,
    requiredGrantType: string,
    env: Env
  ): Promise<PermissionResult> {
    try {
      // Check 1: Is requesting user a direct member of the target space?
      const memberRole = await this.getMemberRole(requestingUserId);
      if (memberRole) {
        return { permitted: true, reason: `Direct member with role '${memberRole}'.`, grantType: null };
      }

      // Check 2: Does a valid cross-sub-space grant exist?
      const now = new Date().toISOString();
      const grant = this.db.exec(
        `SELECT id, grant_type FROM cross_space_grants
         WHERE granting_space_id = ? AND receiving_space_id = ? AND grant_type = ?
           AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?)
         LIMIT 1`,
        targetSpaceId, requestingSpaceId, requiredGrantType, now
      ).one() as { id: string; grant_type: string } | null;

      if (!grant) {
        return {
          permitted: false,
          reason: `User ${requestingUserId} is not a member of space ${targetSpaceId} and no ` +
                  `cross-sub-space grant exists from space ${requestingSpaceId} to ${targetSpaceId} ` +
                  `for grant type '${requiredGrantType}'.`,
          grantType: null,
        };
      }

      // Cross-boundary access confirmed — MUST write audit trail before returning
      // Failure to write audit trail is logged as a platform error — it does NOT block access.
      try {
        await env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS.writeDataPoint({
          blobs: ['cross-sub-space-access', requestingUserId, requestingSpaceId, targetSpaceId, grant.id],
          doubles: [Date.now()],
          indexes: [targetSpaceId],
        });
      } catch (auditErr) {
        console.error('[SubSpaceDO] AUDIT TRAIL WRITE FAILED', { requestingUserId, targetSpaceId, error: auditErr });
        // Access still permitted. Platform monitoring must alert on this. Never silently ignored.
      }

      return {
        permitted: true,
        reason: `Cross-sub-space grant '${grant.grant_type}' exists.`,
        grantType: grant.grant_type,
      };

    } catch (err) {
      // ANY unexpected error → DENIED. Never permit on error.
      console.error('[SubSpaceDO] checkPermission UNEXPECTED ERROR — defaulting to DENIED', err);
      return {
        permitted: false,
        reason: 'Permission check failed due to an internal error. Access denied as a safety default.',
        grantType: null,
      };
    }
  }

  async grantCrossSubSpaceAccess(grantingSpaceId: string, receivingSpaceId: string, grantType: string, grantedBy: string, expiresAt?: string): Promise<string> {
    const id = crypto.randomUUID();
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO cross_space_grants (id, granting_space_id, receiving_space_id, grant_type, granted_by, granted_at, expires_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      id, grantingSpaceId, receivingSpaceId, grantType, grantedBy, new Date().toISOString(), expiresAt ?? null
    );
    return id;
  }

  async revokeCrossSubSpaceAccess(grantId: string): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(`UPDATE cross_space_grants SET revoked_at = ? WHERE id = ?`, new Date().toISOString(), grantId);
  }

  async getHierarchy(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    const meta = Object.fromEntries(
      (this.db.exec(`SELECT key, value FROM space_meta`).toArray() as any[]).map(r => [r.key, JSON.parse(r.value)])
    );
    return {
      meta,
      members: this.db.exec(`SELECT user_id, role, inherited_from_parent FROM members WHERE revoked_at IS NULL`).toArray(),
      grants: this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM cross_space_grants WHERE revoked_at IS NULL`).toArray(),
    };
  }

  async rollupBillingUsage(day: string, credits: number, agentRuns: number, storageBytes: number): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO billing_usage (day, credits_consumed, agent_runs, storage_bytes) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(day) DO UPDATE SET
         credits_consumed = billing_usage.credits_consumed + excluded.credits_consumed,
         agent_runs = billing_usage.agent_runs + excluded.agent_runs,
         storage_bytes = MAX(billing_usage.storage_bytes, excluded.storage_bytes)`,
      day, credits, agentRuns, storageBytes
    );
  }

  async transferToStandaloneProduct(newOwnerId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO space_meta (key, value) VALUES ('parent_space_id', 'null')
       ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = 'null'`
    );
    this.db.exec(
      `INSERT INTO space_meta (key, value) VALUES ('owner_id', ?)
       ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value`,
      JSON.stringify(newOwnerId)
    );
  }
}

When a Sub-Space Becomes a Separate Product

Promotion Threshold — Any One of These Triggers It

1. Its own custom domain independent of the parent product

2. Its own brand identity distinct from the parent (different logo, name, colors)

3. Its own billing relationship where its users pay separately from the parent's users

4. Its own independent user signup flow not through the parent's auth

5. Its own builder-admin who is not an admin of the parent product

If you are unsure, promote to a Product. Sub-spaces are for organizational convenience. Products are for independent business entities. The cost of promoting too late is a data migration. The cost of promoting too early is minimal.

// POST /api/spaces/{spaceId}/promote-to-product
// One-way operation. Cannot be undone without a manual data migration.
// Request body:
{
  "acknowledgeIrreversible": true,          // required field — no default
  "newOwnerOrganizationId": "org_...",
  "newProductName": "ClientCo AI",
  "newProductSlug": "clientco-ai",
  "newProductDomain": "ai.clientco.com",
  "billingTransferDate": "2026-06-01"
}

// Steps executed:
// 1. Validate spaceId is a sub-space (parent_space_id IS NOT NULL)
// 2. Validate calling builder owns the parent space
// 3. Validate acknowledgeIrreversible = true (reject immediately if false or missing)
// 4. Create NaelaoProduct record in products table pointing to this spaceId
// 5. Initialize BuilderAccountDO for newOwnerOrganizationId
// 6. Call BuilderAccountDO.addProduct()
// 7. Call SubSpaceDO.transferToStandaloneProduct()
// 8. UPDATE spaces SET parent_space_id = NULL, depth = 0 WHERE id = spaceId
// 9. Create DOMAIN_REGISTRY_KV entry for new domain
// 10. Send confirmation emails to both original builder and new owner
// 11. Write immutable product_audit_log record

// What CANNOT be undone:
// - spaces.parent_space_id is now NULL — the space is a root space
// - Billing responsibility has transferred
// - SubSpaceDO internal state reflects new ownership

// Response 200:
{
  "product": NaelaoProduct,
  "promotedAt": "ISO8601",
  "note": "This operation is irreversible. Data migration would be required to reverse it."
}
50 — Platform UX & Builder Experience

How Builders Use Naelao — The Platform Experience

Naelao itself has a UI. Two distinct surfaces: the Naelao Platform (for Naelao's own team and builder onboarding) and the Builder Dashboard (for Tier 1 builders creating and managing their products). Neither surface is ever seen by end users of builder products.

"Naelao is not a product. Naelao is the factory that builds products. The factory is never shown to the factory's customers."

Surface 1 — The Naelao Platform (platform.naelao.app)

Used by the Naelao team. Contains: the builder registration and approval flow, the global infrastructure dashboard (active DOs, KV usage, R2 storage, credit metering health), the conversation log access approval queue (where Naelao staff manually reviews builder requests to enable conversationLogAccess), the wholesale billing console, and the global product directory. From the platform, Naelao staff can suspend builder products, approve or reject conversation log access requests, view aggregated usage across all builders (without reading individual conversations), and trigger infrastructure maintenance events.

Surface 2 — The Builder Dashboard (dashboard.naelao.app)

The Builder Dashboard is the primary interface for Tier 1 builders. It is designed to feel like Vercel, Stripe, or Cloudflare's developer dashboard — infrastructure-first, precise, no consumer-product aesthetics. It serves a technical audience comfortable with API keys, webhooks, auth providers, and credit metering.

Products
Primary Nav
List of all NaelaoProduct records. Card view: product name, domain, status badge, active users, credits this month. Click → product detail page.
Create Product Wizard
Primary Action
Multi-step: name + slug → space type selection → auth config → pricing setup → branding → domain → launch. Each step validates before proceeding.
Product Detail — Overview
Tab
DAU/MAU sparklines, credits consumed this month vs limit, agent runs, top threads, new users today, churn this week. No raw infrastructure data visible.
Product Detail — Users
Tab
Searchable list: email, display name, role, credits used/limit, last active, status. Actions: suspend, delete, adjust credits, view usage. Conversation access gated behind separate audit flow.
Product Detail — Analytics

DAU/MAU charts, credit burn rate by sub-space, agent run counts, average session length, top users by usage, revenue metrics. All date-range filterable.
Product Detail — Configuration

Auth provider config, allowed domains, approval settings, pricing, user permissions, admin features. Collapsible panels with inline editing and save confirmation.
Product Detail — Feature Flags

Toggle switches for all registered flags. Changes live within 60 seconds (KV TTL). Audit log shows who changed what flag and when. No code deploy required.

Current period wholesale invoice: credits consumed per product, estimated Naelao cost, invoice due date. Historical invoices as PDF. Stripe Customer Portal embedded for payment management.
Product Detail — Danger Zone

Suspend product, delete product (90-day retention warning), transfer to another builder org. All actions require typing the product name to confirm. All write to product_audit_log.
Builder Billing

Current month's Naelao wholesale invoice across all products. Historical invoices. Payment method management. Delinquency warnings with countdown to suspension.

Surface 3 — What Builders Build: The Product Frontend

Builders construct their product's UI on top of the Naelao product shell using the @naelao/product-sdk. The platform provides a base shell with routing, auth, sub-space switching, and the core agent thread UI. Builders extend this shell with their product-specific views. The product shell is deployed as a CF Pages project per product.

// ─── Builder UI Development Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────

// 1. Install the SDK:
//    npm install @naelao/product-sdk

// 2. Initialize a product project:
//    npx naelao-product init --product-id prod_legal_001
//    → Creates a Next.js project with the Naelao product shell pre-configured
//    → Copies product config from dashboard (auth provider, space type, feature flags)
//    → Sets up local dev pointing to Naelao staging API

// 3. The base shell provides:
//    - Auth flow (login, signup, SSO redirect) — customized with product branding
//    - Thread list and thread detail — core AI conversation UI
//    - Sub-space switcher (if sub-spaces enabled)
//    - User settings
//    - Credit balance indicator (if credits pricing)
//    Builders add everything else their product needs on top.

// 4. Feature-flag-gate new features:
import { useFeatureFlag } from '@naelao/product-sdk';
const matterManagementEnabled = useFeatureFlag('matter-management');
// Flag value is injected at runtime by naelao-router — no code deploy to change it.

// 5. Deploy:
//    npx naelao-product deploy
//    → Builds the project
//    → Deploys to the product's CF Pages project via CF API credentials in SDK config
//    → Traffic switches to new deployment atomically

// ─── @naelao/product-sdk — Key Exports ─────────────────────────────────────────

// Auth:
useProductUser()                      // → ProductUser | null
useProductSession()                   // → ProductSession
signOut()                             // → void

// Threads:
useThreadList(filters)                // → Thread[]
useThread(threadId)                   // → Thread with messages
sendMessage(threadId, content)        // → void (streaming response via SSE)
createThread(options)                 // → Thread

// Credits:
useCreditBalance()                    // → { balance: number, limit: number | null }

// Feature flags:
useFeatureFlag(flagKey)               // → boolean (server-injected, available client-side)

// Sub-spaces:
useSubSpaces()                        // → SubSpace[]
useActiveSubSpace()                   // → SubSpace
switchSubSpace(id)                    // → void (URL navigation + context update)

// Knowledge:
uploadDocument(file, subSpaceId)      // → DocumentRef
searchKnowledge(query, subSpaceId)    // → KnowledgeSearchResult[]

Naelao Platform Aesthetic — Design System

The Naelao Platform and Builder Dashboard follow a deliberate design language: dark, precise, infrastructure-grade. Not consumer. Not playful. Not generic SaaS. The aesthetic communicates: this is serious infrastructure, and the numbers on this screen are real things in a real system.

Platform Aesthetic Principles — Non-Negotiable

Builder Dashboard: Dark theme (#060D1A base), monospace system values (DM Mono), orange accent (#E8682A), status badges using traffic-light colors, infrastructure-first information hierarchy. Identical to the aesthetic of this specification document. No purple gradients. No illustration libraries. No hero sections. Data tables, cards, code blocks, and precise metric displays only.

Product Shell templates: Neutral base, responsive to the builder's brandColor. Two template families: Chat-first (for builder products targeting consumer AI or chat use cases — Team space type) and Workspace-first (Developer, Verticals). Both professionally designed but intentionally unopinionated — the builder's branding is the dominant visual identity, not Naelao's.

The contrast is intentional. The Builder Dashboard looks like a well-designed technical document made interactive — because that is what it is. Builder products look like their own products — because that is what they are. Naelao's aesthetic never bleeds through into builder products. That is the promise of the platform.

What Builders Never See — The Infrastructure That Runs Their Products

The Builder Dashboard deliberately hides: raw credit costs (builders see credits consumed, not CF compute costs in dollars), infrastructure topology (no DO instance IDs, no Worker names, no KV namespace IDs exposed), other builders' products and users (the entire API is scoped to the authenticated builderId), and Naelao's internal tooling and platform configuration. A builder building a legal AI product never needs to think about Cloudflare at all. They think about their product, their users, and their pricing. Naelao thinks about everything else.

This is the same relationship a merchant has with Shopify: they configure their store, manage their products, and run their marketing. They never interact with Stripe's infrastructure even though Stripe processes every payment. The infrastructure is invisible by design. Its invisibility is not an accident — it is the product.

51 — New Space Type

Studio — The Creative Production Space

Studio is the space type for people and teams that produce creative output professionally: writers, designers, video producers, musicians, marketers, and creative agencies. Where Launchpad automates a business, Studio automates a production pipeline. The agents are not customer-facing — they are collaborators in a craft. Studio is the answer to the question: what does an AI-native creative tool look like when the infrastructure is serious?

"Launchpad runs a business with zero employees. Studio runs a production line with zero junior staff."
Why Studio Is a Separate Space Type — Not a Launchpad Template

Launchpad's execution model is fulfillment: a customer order arrives, agents deliver a product, owner reviews. Studio's execution model is iterative production: a brief arrives, agents produce a draft, the creative director revises, agents incorporate feedback, the cycle repeats. The approval model is different. The knowledge base is different (brand guidelines, style references, past work, tone documents). The output artifacts are different (files, not messages). The billing model is different (project-scoped credit consumption, not per-order). A Studio Space cannot be reduced to a Launchpad template without losing its core execution model. It requires its own space type manifest, its own agent definitions, and its own UI layout — the Production Board.

Studio Templates

Template 01
Content Studio

Long-form articles, social posts, email campaigns. Agents research, draft, and format. Creative director reviews and publishes. Brand voice document anchors all output to the client's tone.

Template 02
Design Brief Machine

Brief intake → moodboard generation → copy variants → final asset packaging. Agents handle every stage that doesn't require a human aesthetic decision. Designer approves each gate.

Template 03
Video Production Office

Script → shot list → production schedule → post notes → social cuts. Agents produce all text deliverables. Producer reviews before anything enters physical production.

Template 04
Brand Agency

Multi-client brand management. Each client sub-space holds their brand guidelines, asset library, and campaign history. Agents generate on-brand content across channels simultaneously.

Template 05
Music & Podcast Production

Show notes, episode summaries, transcript editing, social clips, guest briefs. Agents handle all text-layer production. Creator focuses on the recording.

The Production Board — Studio's Core UI

Studio replaces the thread-first layout of Team and Developer spaces with the Production Board: a Kanban-style project view where each card is a creative brief. Cards move through stages: Brief → In Production → Review → Approved → Published. The agent thread for each card is accessible from a slide-over panel — it's not the primary view, it's the audit trail. What the creative director sees first is the artifact: the draft, the asset, the script. Not the conversation that produced it.

// ─── Studio Production Board — React Component Architecture ──────────────────
// File: apps/product-shell/src/layouts/StudioLayout.tsx

// ProductionBoard — top-level Studio view
// Columns: Brief | In Production | Review | Approved | Published
// Each card: BriefCard — title, assigned agent, last updated, artifact preview thumbnail

// BriefCard → click → BriefDetail slide-over
//   Tabs: Artifact (primary) | Agent Thread | Revision History | Comments
//   Actions: Request Revision | Approve | Reject | Assign Agent | Publish

// The Artifact tab renders the output file inline:
//   - Markdown/long-form → rendered prose view with inline commenting
//   - Structured copy (social, email) → card layout per variant
//   - Brief documents → split view: brief on left, output on right

// ─── URL Structure ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Platform:    https://studio.naelao.app/spaces/{spaceId}/board
// White-label: https://studio.acmecreative.com/board
// Brief:       https://studio.acmecreative.com/board/{briefId}
// No threadId ever appears in the URL — Studio is artifact-first, not thread-first.

Studio Core Agents

Every Studio Space gets these agents pre-installed. All are Supervised tier — they produce drafts autonomously, but every artifact requires explicit creative director approval before it can be marked Published. Approval is never skippable in Studio. Creative accountability cannot be delegated to the agent.

// agents/definitions/studio-researcher.json
{
  "id": "studio-researcher-v1",
  "name": "Research Agent",
  "description": "Produces research briefs, source summaries, and competitive analyses for creative briefs",
  "system_prompt": "You are a senior research analyst embedded in a creative studio. When given a creative brief, you: 1) Identify the 5-8 most relevant sources for the topic, 2) Summarize each source in 3-5 sentences, 3) Extract key facts, statistics, and quotes relevant to the brief, 4) Identify the strongest angles or narratives the creative team could pursue, 5) Note any brand or tone constraints from the Space knowledge base. Output is a structured research brief in Markdown. You do not write the final creative content — that is the Copywriter Agent's role.",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  "allowed_skills": ["web-search", "knowledge-base-read", "file-manager"],
  "trigger": { "type": "brief_stage_change", "from": "Brief", "to": "In Production" },
  "requires_approval_for": [],
  "output_format": "markdown",
  "resource_tier": "workspace"
}

// agents/definitions/studio-copywriter.json
{
  "id": "studio-copywriter-v1",
  "name": "Copywriter Agent",
  "description": "Produces long-form and short-form copy variants from research briefs and brand guidelines",
  "system_prompt": "You are an expert copywriter. You always read the brand voice document in the Space knowledge base before writing. You produce multiple variants — never a single draft — so the creative director has genuine choice. For long-form: produce a full draft plus a 3-bullet TL;DR. For social: produce 3 variants per platform (tone: direct, playful, authoritative). For email: produce subject line (3 variants), preview text, and body. All output goes to the Artifact tab of the current brief — never to a plain chat message.",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  "allowed_skills": ["knowledge-base-read", "file-manager", "web-search"],
  "trigger": { "type": "agent_handoff", "from": "studio-researcher-v1" },
  "requires_approval_for": ["artifact_publish"],
  "output_format": "structured_artifact",
