Required: Tiered Context Strategy // context-builder.ts — replaces the raw last-50 slice async function buildContext(threadId: string, db: SpaceDB): Promise<Message[]> { const totalCount = db.exec('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE thread_id=?',[threadId]).rows[0][0]; if (totalCount <= 50) { // Under 50: use everything — no compaction needed return db.exec('SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? ORDER BY created_at', [threadId]).rows; } // Over 50: three-zone context assembly // Zone 1 — ANCHOR (first 3 messages): always included // Contains the user's original goal and initial context const anchor = db.exec( 'SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 3', [threadId] ).rows; // Zone 2 — SUMMARY (messages 4 to N-30): replaced by a generated summary // The…

// context-builder.ts — replaces the raw last-50 slice
async function buildContext(threadId: string, db: SpaceDB): Promise<Message[]> {

  const totalCount = db.exec('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE thread_id=?',[threadId]).rows[0][0];

  if (totalCount <= 50) {
    // Under 50: use everything — no compaction needed
    return db.exec('SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? ORDER BY created_at', [threadId]).rows;
  }

  // Over 50: three-zone context assembly

  // Zone 1 — ANCHOR (first 3 messages): always included
  // Contains the user's original goal and initial context
  const anchor = db.exec(
    'SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 3', [threadId]
  ).rows;

  // Zone 2 — SUMMARY (messages 4 to N-30): replaced by a generated summary
  // The summary is generated once and cached in SpaceDO: summaries table
  // Regenerated only when new messages push more content into this zone
  const summary = await getOrGenerateSummary(threadId, db);
  const summaryMessage = {
    role: 'system',
    content: `[Conversation summary — ${summary.messageCount} earlier messages]: ${summary.text}`,
    created_at: summary.generatedAt
  };

  // Zone 3 — RECENT (last 30 messages): always included verbatim
  const recent = db.exec(
    'SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 30', [threadId]
  ).rows.reverse();

  // Zone 4 — PINNED: messages the user or agent explicitly pinned
  const pinned = db.exec(
    'SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id=? AND pinned=1 ORDER BY created_at', [threadId]
  ).rows;

  return deduplicateByMessageId([...anchor, summaryMessage, ...pinned, ...recent]);
}
// Total in-context: 3 anchor + 1 summary block + N pinned + 30 recent
// The user always experiences continuity. The agent always knows the goal.

function validateEnv(env: Env, required: (keyof Env)[]): void { const missing = required.filter(key => env[key] == null); if (missing.length > 0) { // Fail loudly — a missing binding is a deployment error, not a request error throw new Error( `[ENV] Missing required bindings: ${missing.join(', ')}. ` + `Check wrangler.jsonc matches the Env interface.` ); } } // Each Worker calls this at startup: // validateEnv(env, ['NAELAO_CONFIG_KV','NAELAO_WORKSPACE','NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE','...']) // This surfaces deployment drift on the first request, not on the first affected code path Gap T-77 — Medium

// workers/shared/validate-env.ts
// Called at the top of every Worker's fetch handler — before any routing
export function validateEnv(env: Env, required: (keyof Env)[]): void {
  const missing = required.filter(key => env[key] == null);
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    // Fail loudly — a missing binding is a deployment error, not a request error
    throw new Error(
      `[ENV] Missing required bindings: ${missing.join(', ')}. ` +
      `Check wrangler.jsonc matches the Env interface.`
    );
  }
}
// Each Worker calls this at startup:
// validateEnv(env, ['NAELAO_CONFIG_KV','NAELAO_WORKSPACE','NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE','...'])
// This surfaces deployment drift on the first request, not on the first affected code path

Knowledge Chunks Have No Overlap — Sentences Split Across Boundaries Are Lost

The Gap

Knowledge Chunks Have No Overlap — Sentences Split Across Boundaries Are Lost The knowledge pipeline chunks documents into 512-token segments with no specified overlap. Hard 512-token boundaries mean a sentence that begins at token 510 and ends at token 520 is split across two chunks. Chunk N contains the start of the sentence; chunk N+1 contains the end. A semantic search that is relevant to that sentence may rank neither chunk highly because the meaning is fragmented across the boundary. This is a well-known information retrieval problem — every production RAG pipeline uses overlapping chunks to avoid it. Naelao's knowledge pipeline doesn't. Why This Matters at Scale For short documents…

Required Fix

pWords = Math.floor(overlapTokens * 0.75); const stride = chunkWords - overlapWords; const chunks: string[] = []; for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i += stride) { chunks.push(words.slice(i, i + chunkWords).join(' ')); if (i + chunkWords >= words.length) break; } return chunks; } // Additional improvement: semantic chunking (split on paragraph/section boundaries // rather than fixed token counts) produces better retrieval for structured documents. // This requires a document-structure parser (detect headings, paragraphs, list items) // before chunking — not currently specified. Gap T-91N — High

// Current (broken for long documents):
// Split at every 512 tokens, no overlap
// Chunk 1: tokens 1–512
// Chunk 2: tokens 513–1024
// A concept spanning tokens 500–530 appears in neither chunk with full context

// Required: sliding window with overlap
// Standard values: chunk size 512 tokens, overlap 64 tokens (12.5%)
// Chunk 1: tokens 1–512
// Chunk 2: tokens 449–960   (starts 64 tokens before previous boundary)
// Chunk 3: tokens 897–1408

function chunkDocument(text: string, chunkTokens = 512, overlapTokens = 64): string[] {
  const words = text.split(/\s+/);
  // Approximate: 1 token ≈ 0.75 words for English prose
  const chunkWords = Math.floor(chunkTokens * 0.75);
  const overlapWords = Math.floor(overlapTokens * 0.75);
  const stride = chunkWords - overlapWords;
  const chunks: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i += stride) {
    chunks.push(words.slice(i, i + chunkWords).join(' '));
    if (i + chunkWords >= words.length) break;
  }
  return chunks;
}

// Additional improvement: semantic chunking (split on paragraph/section boundaries
// rather than fixed token counts) produces better retrieval for structured documents.
// This requires a document-structure parser (detect headings, paragraphs, list items)
// before chunking — not currently specified.

Update vector-ID mapping in SpaceDO await spaceDO.fetch(new Request(`http://space/knowledge/${docId}/vector-ids`, { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(newVectorIds) })); } // Without this: every document update doubles the stale vector count in the index. // After 10 edits to the same document, 11 versions are all in Vectorize. // This requires the vector-ID mapping from T-42 (GDPR erasure) — same mechanism:
// Every document upload stores: docId → [vectorId1, vectorId2, ...] in SpaceDO

// Knowledge Worker — on document UPDATE (not initial upload):
async function updateDocument(spaceId: string, docId: string, newFile: File, env: Env) {
  // 1. Delete old vectors for this document
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(spaceId, env);
  const oldVectorIds: string[] = await spaceDO.fetch(
    new Request(`http://space/knowledge/${docId}/vector-ids`)
  ).then(r => r.json());

  if (oldVectorIds.length > 0) {
    const indexName = getVectorizeIndexForSpace(spaceId);
    await env[indexName].deleteByIds(oldVectorIds);  // remove stale vectors
  }

  // 2. Chunk and embed the new version (existing flow)
  const newChunks = chunkDocument(await newFile.text());
  const newVectorIds: string[] = [];
  for (const chunk of newChunks) {
    const embedding = await generateEmbedding(chunk, env);
    const vectorId = `${docId}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    await env[indexName].insert([{ id: vectorId, values: embedding,
                                   metadata: { spaceId, docId, version: Date.now() } }]);
    newVectorIds.push(vectorId);
  }

  // 3. Update vector-ID mapping in SpaceDO
  await spaceDO.fetch(new Request(`http://space/knowledge/${docId}/vector-ids`, {
    method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(newVectorIds)
  }));
}
// Without this: every document update doubles the stale vector count in the index.
// After 10 edits to the same document, 11 versions are all in Vectorize.

Syntax check — MISSING FROM SPEC // A Worker with a syntax error will fail to deploy but return a cryptic CF API error. // Parse the code before submitting to give a useful error message. try { new Function(code); // basic syntax check — not perfect but catches most errors } catch (e) { return { valid: false, error: `Artifact contains a syntax error: ${(e as Error).message}` }; } return { valid: true }; } Gap T-11 — Medium

// Required: size validation in naelao-artifact before Dynamic Worker creation

async function validateArtifact(code: string): Promise<{ valid: boolean; error?: string }> {
  // 1. Security scan (27 patterns — already in spec)
  const securityResult = await runSecurityScanner(code);
  if (!securityResult.clean) return { valid: false, error: securityResult.violation };

  // 2. Size check — MISSING FROM SPEC
  const compressed = await compress(code); // gzip
  if (compressed.length > 900_000) { // 1MB limit with 100KB safety margin
    return { valid: false, error: 'Artifact exceeds maximum size (900 KB compressed). Reduce inline data.' };
  }

  // 3. Syntax check — MISSING FROM SPEC
  // A Worker with a syntax error will fail to deploy but return a cryptic CF API error.
  // Parse the code before submitting to give a useful error message.
  try {
    new Function(code); // basic syntax check — not perfect but catches most errors
  } catch (e) {
    return { valid: false, error: `Artifact contains a syntax error: ${(e as Error).message}` };
  }

  return { valid: true };
}

Required Fix — DO Alarm API Replaces Sweeper Fan-out // The correct architecture: each AssistantDO schedules its OWN next heartbeat // using the DO Alarm API. The sweeper is NOT responsible for waking assistants. // The sweeper is ONLY responsible for cleanup of crashed runs — a much smaller job. // In AssistantDO — after every heartbeat, schedule the next one: async alarm(): Promise<void> { await this.handleHeartbeat(); // Schedule next heartbeat in 5 minutes // This runs inside the DO — zero sweeper involvement await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000); } // On DO creation (first time an assistant is activated): async activate(): Promise<void> { await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'UPDATE permissions SET granted = 1…

// The correct architecture: each AssistantDO schedules its OWN next heartbeat
// using the DO Alarm API. The sweeper is NOT responsible for waking assistants.
// The sweeper is ONLY responsible for cleanup of crashed runs — a much smaller job.

// In AssistantDO — after every heartbeat, schedule the next one:
async alarm(): Promise<void> {
  await this.handleHeartbeat();
  // Schedule next heartbeat in 5 minutes
  // This runs inside the DO — zero sweeper involvement
  await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000);
}

// On DO creation (first time an assistant is activated):
async activate(): Promise<void> {
  await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000);
  this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(
    'UPDATE permissions SET granted = 1 WHERE permission = ?', 'active'
  );
}

// On deactivation (user disables the assistant):
async deactivate(): Promise<void> {
  await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();
}

// DO Alarms are persisted — they survive DO eviction and CF infrastructure restarts.
// They cost nothing while sleeping. Each DO wakes itself — no central coordinator needed.
// The sweeper's cron trigger still fires every 5 minutes but only for cleanup:
// - Find runs in NaelaoAgentDO with heartbeat_age > 10min → mark failed
// - Release leaked ConcurrencyDO slots (Gap T-13)
// NOT for waking assistants. Completely decoupled.

// Required: a model fallback chain per requested model
const MODEL_FALLBACK_CHAIN: Record<string, string[]> = {
  'claude-opus-4-6':   ['claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-5'],
  'claude-sonnet-4-6': ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-5'],
  'claude-haiku-4-5':  ['claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6'],
};

async function callWithModelFallback(
  requestedModel: string, params: LLMParams, env: Env
): Promise<LLMResponse> {
  const chain = MODEL_FALLBACK_CHAIN[requestedModel] ?? [requestedModel];
  let lastError: Error | null = null;

  for (const model of chain) {
    try {
      const response = await callAIGateway({ ...params, model }, env);
      if (model !== requestedModel) {
        // Log the fallback for billing accuracy and builder transparency
        console.warn(`[model-fallback] ${requestedModel} → ${model}`);
      }
      return response;
    } catch (err) {
      if (isModelUnavailableError(err)) { lastError = err; continue; }
      throw err; // non-model errors (auth, context length) propagate immediately
    }
  }
  throw lastError ?? new Error(`All models in fallback chain for ${requestedModel} failed`);
}

// Required: execution lock on cron jobs
// Before starting a cron-triggered agent run, check if the same cron job
// is already running. Skip (not queue) if it is.

async function triggerCronJob(cronJobId: string, spaceId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> {
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(spaceId, env);

  // Atomic check-and-set in SpaceDO (blockConcurrencyWhile — T-60)
  const alreadyRunning = await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/cron/check-lock', {
    method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ cronJobId })
  })).then(r => r.json()) as { running: boolean; runId?: string };

  if (alreadyRunning.running) {
    // Skip this execution — log the skip for observability
    console.warn(`[cron] ${cronJobId} skipped — previous run ${alreadyRunning.runId} still active`);
    return;
  }

  // Acquired lock — start the run (lock released when run completes or fails)
  await dispatchAgentRun({ cronJobId, spaceId, lockId: cronJobId }, env);
}
// The "skip not queue" behavior is important: if a cron job consistently runs longer
// than its interval, queuing creates an ever-growing backlog. Skip = self-limiting.
// A monitoring alert should fire if skips exceed N consecutive executions.

After the promises resolve, it merges by explicit precedence: agent > space > platform. However, the loadSkillsFromR2 function for each tier fetches from R2 with `bucket.list({ prefix })`. The list order is not guaranteed to be deterministic in R2 — if two skills have similar names and R2 returns them in different order on different calls, the merge could happen in different order even if precedence is correctly applied in code. More critically: if a skill has the same name…

Required Fix

Required Fix Explicitly sort merged skills by tier before merging: extract just the skill name, then for each unique skill name, select the highest-tier version. Don't rely on iteration order. Add explicit precedence checks in the merge function: `for (const skillName of uniqueSkillNames) { const winner = skills[skillName] with tier = max(tier) }`. Add a test that verifies skill precedence is consistent regardless of R2 list order or Promise resolution order. Severity: Medium — Skill tier precedence is not guaranteed to be deterministic if Promise resolution order or R2 list order varies. A space-tier skill could be overridden by platform-tier if promises resolve in a certain order. T-149 — Schema & RLS

G-AGE-20

System Prompt Ordering — Cache Prefix Not Recalculated When Components Change

The Gap

System Prompt Ordering — Cache Prefix Not Recalculated When Components Change The spec says static components (1-4) should be cached together for prompt caching efficiency. The prompt is constructed in order: base prompt → space context → skills → tools → memory → knowledge → history. Anthropic's prompt caching works on exact token prefixes. However, there is no mechanism to recalculate or invalidate the cache prefix when space context changes (e.g., custom instructions updated) or when skills are added/removed. The buildSpaceContext() and buildToolDefinitions() functions are called fresh on every request, but if they return the same content, the cache key remains unchanged. If a space…

Required Fix

Required Fix Add a content hash of components 1-4 to the cache key. When any component changes, the hash changes and the cache key is invalidated automatically. Alternatively, store the component versions in a DO and increment them when space settings change. Check versions before cache lookup. Add explicit logging of which cache (hit/miss) was used for each request so debugging is easier. Severity: Medium — Cache prefix not invalidated when space context or skills change. Old cached instructions may be served, breaking prompt customization. T-160 — Prompt Engineering

G-AGE-21

Tool Discovery Cache — Stale Schemas After App Installation; No Immediate Invalidation

The Gap

Tool Discovery Cache — Stale Schemas After App Installation; No Immediate Invalidation The naelao-mcp-hub caches tool schemas for 1 hour. When a Space installs a new app (adding new tools), the cache is supposed to be invalidated via the `/tools/invalidate` endpoint. However, there is no guarantee that this endpoint is called when an app is installed — the spec doesn't show where the installation triggers the invalidation. If invalidation is missed or delayed, the new tools won't appear in the agent's system prompt for up to 1 hour. An agent could try to use a newly installed tool and get "tool not found" because the cache wasn't cleared.

Required Fix

Required Fix Make cache invalidation automatic: in the space-app-installs table, add a trigger that calls DELETE on the cache key whenever a new row is inserted (app installed) or status changes (installed → suspended). Or, shorten the cache TTL from 1 hour to 5 minutes, and implement periodic refresh (background cron that re-fetches schemas). Add explicit logging when cache is invalidated so debugging is easier. Severity: Medium — New app tools not available for up to 1 hour after installation. Cache invalidation is manual and error-prone. T-162 — naelao-mcp-hub

G-AGE-22

MCP Tool Execution Timeout — 30s Hard Limit; No Streaming Or Progressive Results

The Gap

MCP Tool Execution Timeout — 30s Hard Limit; No Streaming Or Progressive Results The MCP hub has a hard 30-second timeout for tool execution: `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30000)`. If a tool takes 31 seconds to complete (long API call, batch processing), it times out and fails with no partial results returned. For tools like "fetch large dataset" or "run analysis", 30 seconds is too short. Additionally, there's no streaming or progressive result capability — the hub waits for the complete result before returning. For long-running tools, this is inefficient and user experience is poor (agent waits 30s, then fails).

Required Fix

Required Fix Make the timeout configurable per tool: store `timeout_ms` in the tool schema. Allow tools to declare their expected duration. Implement streaming results: if a tool returns partial results or a "progress" field, stream those back to the agent immediately instead of waiting for completion. For truly long-running tools, implement async execution: return a job ID immediately, let the agent continue, and poll for results later. Severity: Medium — 30s timeout too strict for long-running tools. No streaming or progressive results. Tools fail silently if they take too long. T-163 — naelao-mcp-hub

G-AGE-23

Tool Schema Aggregation — No Conflict Detection; Two Apps Can Provide Identical Tool Names

The Gap

Tool Schema Aggregation — No Conflict Detection; Two Apps Can Provide Identical Tool Names The naelao-mcp-hub aggregates tool schemas from all installed apps without checking for name collisions. If App A provides a tool called "send_email" and App B also provides "send_email", both are added to the aggregated schema. When the agent calls "send_email", the hub has to choose which one to route to. The current implementation uses the first match, which is non-deterministic (depends on Promise.allSettled() order). This could cause agents to call the wrong tool — e.g., calling Sendgrid's send_email when they meant Gmail's.

Required Fix

Required Fix Add conflict detection: when aggregating schemas, check for duplicate tool names. If found, either: (a) reject the installation of the conflicting app, or (b) require apps to namespace their tools (e.g., "sendgrid.send_email" vs "gmail.send_email"). Alternatively, give Space admins the ability to choose which app provides a tool: store a `tool_overrides` table where admins can specify which app handles which tool name. Add logging when tool name conflicts are detected so admins are aware of the issue. Severity: Medium — Tool name collisions from multiple apps cause unpredictable routing. Agents may call the wrong tool. No conflict detection or resolution. T-164 — Launch Checklist

G-AGE-24

Cron Double Dispatch — Race Between sweepSchedules() And Concurrent Agent Calls

The Gap

Cron Double Dispatch — Race Between sweepSchedules() And Concurrent Agent Calls The naelao-sweeper calls WorkflowRegistryDO.sweepSchedules() every 5 minutes. The sweeper checks for due workflows (next_run

Required Fix

Required Fix Make next_run update atomic with the dispatch: don't calculate next_run separately, include it in the same transaction that marks the workflow as run. Add a "last_dispatch_time" column: if a workflow was dispatched in the last 60 seconds, skip it in the current sweep. Prevents accidental rapid re-dispatch. Log every workflow dispatch with the source (cron vs manual) so double-dispatches are detectable in analytics. Severity: Medium — Cron and agent dispatch can race. Workflows execute multiple times. next_run update can be lost if concurrent with dispatch. T-175 — Error Processor

// Required: explicit sync manifest
// SandboxDO stores a sync manifest in SpaceDO:
// sync_config(id TEXT PK, container_path TEXT, r2_key TEXT, direction TEXT, last_synced_at TEXT)
// direction: 'r2_to_container' | 'container_to_r2' | 'bidirectional'

// On container START — pull from R2:
async syncFromR2(): Promise<void> {
  const configs = this.db.exec("SELECT * FROM sync_config WHERE direction IN ('r2_to_container','bidirectional')").rows;
  for (const [,containerPath, r2Key] of configs) {
    const obj = await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(String(r2Key));
    if (obj) {
      const content = await obj.text();
      await this.writeFile(String(containerPath), content);
    }
  }
}

// On container STOP (graceful) — push to R2 with etag conflict check:
async syncToR2(): Promise<void> {
  const configs = this.db.exec("SELECT * FROM sync_config WHERE direction IN ('container_to_r2','bidirectional')").rows;
  for (const [,containerPath, r2Key] of configs) {
    try {
      const content = await this.readFile(String(containerPath));
      // Etag check — if R2 was updated since last sync, this is a conflict
      const existing = await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.head(String(r2Key));
      const lastSynced = this.db.exec("SELECT last_synced_at FROM sync_config WHERE r2_key=?", [r2Key]).rows[0]?.[0];
      if (existing && existing.uploaded > new Date(String(lastSynced ?? 0))) {
        // CONFLICT — store both versions, alert agent on next run
        await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(String(r2Key) + '.conflict.' + Date.now(), content);
      } else {
        await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(String(r2Key), content);
      }
    } catch { /* file may not exist in container — skip */ }
  }
}

// On container CRASH — sweeper detects status='running' with lastUsedAt > 20min
// Marks status='error'. Files not synced. Agent warned on next session start.

Container Network Isolation — Agents Can Reach Internal CF Infrastructure

The Gap

Container Network Isolation — Agents Can Reach Internal CF Infrastructure The spec states the Developer space type has an "open" network policy. The container is a Linux environment with full outbound network access. There is no specification for whether the container can reach Cloudflare's internal metadata APIs, link-local addresses ( 169.254.0.0/16 ), or the host's internal network. In cloud container environments, the metadata service (AWS: 169.254.169.254 , GCP: metadata.google.internal ) is a well-known SSRF target. CF Containers may have analogous internal endpoints. An agent instructed via prompt injection to make requests to link-local addresses could exfiltrate container…

Required Fix

uld scan the user's home network The Local Tunnel Amplifies This The Local Tunnel runs commands on the user's actual machine — which is on their home or office network. An agent instructed (via prompt injection) to run curl http://192.168.1.1/admin would reach the user's router admin panel. The local CLI agent must block commands that make network requests to RFC 1918 addresses. This is harder than it sounds — the command could be python -c "import urllib; urllib.request.urlopen('http://192.168.1.1')" . Blocking requires intent analysis, not just string matching on the command. Gap T-86 — High

// Required: network egress policy for containers
// Must be specified in naelao-base and enforced at the container/network level

const BLOCKED_NETWORK_RANGES = [
  '169.254.0.0/16',   // link-local (metadata services)
  '100.64.0.0/10',    // shared address space (carrier-grade NAT internals)
  '10.0.0.0/8',       // RFC 1918 private (CF internal)
  '172.16.0.0/12',    // RFC 1918 private
  '192.168.0.0/16',   // RFC 1918 private
  '::1/128',          // IPv6 loopback
  'fc00::/7',         // IPv6 unique local
];

Local ↔ Cloud File Conflict Resolution — No Protocol When Both Sides Change

The Gap

Local ↔ Cloud File Conflict Resolution — No Protocol When Both Sides Change The Developer space type is designed for a workflow where a developer works locally (via the LocalTunnelDO CLI) while cloud agents work on the same codebase (via SandboxDO containers). Both sides write to the same files. The spec defines both the local tunnel and the cloud container but specifies no protocol for when they modify the same file simultaneously or sequentially without synchronization. This is the standard version control problem — and it is completely unaddressed. Scenario What Happens Without a Protocol Dev edits app.ts locally, agent edits same file in container Last sync wins. The other's changes are…

filesystem writes: all agent file writes go through a git commit , and the local developer pulls via normal git operations. The R2 workspace stores the git repo (bare or working tree). The container clones from it on start. The local tunnel clones or pulls from the same R2-backed repo. Conflicts surface as merge conflicts — handled by the standard git workflow both humans and agents know. This is a design decision that needs to be explicit in the spec: is the Developer space a filesystem-sync model or a git-sync model? The current spec uses both, creating an undefined hybrid. // Required: explicit sync tools exposed to the agent
// These become LOCAL_MACHINE_TOOLS when the local agent is connected

// sync_to_local: copy a file from R2 workspace to the user's local machine
{
  name: 'sync_to_local',
  description: 'Copy a file from the cloud workspace to the user local machine',
  inputSchema: {
    r2Path: { type: 'string' },      // e.g. 'reports/q3-analysis.pdf'
    localPath: { type: 'string' },   // e.g. '/Users/alice/Downloads/q3-analysis.pdf'
  },
  handler: async ({ r2Path, localPath }, env) => {
    // 1. Download from R2 workspace
    const obj = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(`spaces/${spaceId}/workspace/${r2Path}`);
    if (!obj) return { error: 'File not found in workspace' };
    const bytes = await obj.arrayBuffer();

    // 2. Send to LocalTunnelDO which forwards to the local agent for writing
    return localTunnelDO.execOnLocal({
      tool: 'write_file_local',
      params: { path: localPath, contentBase64: btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(bytes))) }
    });
  }
}

// sync_from_local: copy a file from the local machine to the R2 workspace
{
  name: 'sync_from_local',
  description: 'Copy a file from the user local machine to the cloud workspace',
  inputSchema: {
    localPath: { type: 'string' },
    r2Path: { type: 'string' },
  },
  handler: async ({ localPath, r2Path }, env) => {
    // 1. Read from local machine via tunnel
    const result = await localTunnelDO.execOnLocal({
      tool: 'read_file_local',
      params: { path: localPath, encoding: 'base64' }
    });
    if (result.error) return result;

    // 2. Write to R2 workspace
    const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(result.contentBase64), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
    await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(`spaces/${spaceId}/workspace/${r2Path}`, bytes);
    return { success: true, r2Path };
  }
}
// Neither tool is in the spec. The local agent and cloud workspace are currently isolated.

Operational & Versioning

G-OPE-01

Disaster Recovery — No Plan, No RTO, No RPO

The Gap

Disaster Recovery — No Plan, No RTO, No RPO The entire spec assumes Cloudflare's infrastructure is always available. There is no specified disaster recovery plan, no defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO), no defined Recovery Point Objective (RPO), and no backup strategy for the three stateful systems: SpaceDO SQLite , R2 workspaces , and Vectorize indexes . For any enterprise customer, this is a hard procurement blocker before a contract is signed. Cloudflare's Durable Objects are globally distributed and survive most single-region failures. But DO SQLite storage is not replicated to customer-accessible backups. If a DO's SQLite database is corrupted — by a bad migration, a bug in schema…

Required Fix

Required Mitigations — Must Specify Before Enterprise Sales // 1. Add to naelao-sweeper: daily SpaceDO → R2 backup // Cron: "0 3 * * *" (3am UTC daily — low traffic window) async function backupSpaceDO(spaceId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> { const spaceDO = getProductDO(spaceId, env); // Call a new SpaceDO method: exportSnapshot() // Returns: { tables: Record<string, Row[]>, exportedAt: string, schemaVersion: number } const snapshot = await spaceDO.fetch( new Request('http://space/export-snapshot') ).then(r => r.json()); const date = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]; const backupKey = `backups/${spaceId}/${date}/space-snapshot.json.gz`; // Compress and write to R2 — not naelao-workspace (product data) // but a separate naelao-backups bucket (write-once, lifecycle: 90 days) const…

// 1. Add to naelao-sweeper: daily SpaceDO → R2 backup
// Cron: "0 3 * * *" (3am UTC daily — low traffic window)
async function backupSpaceDO(spaceId: string, env: Env): Promise<void> {
  const spaceDO = getProductDO(spaceId, env);
  
  // Call a new SpaceDO method: exportSnapshot()
  // Returns: { tables: Record<string, Row[]>, exportedAt: string, schemaVersion: number }
  const snapshot = await spaceDO.fetch(
    new Request('http://space/export-snapshot')
  ).then(r => r.json());
  
  const date = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0];
  const backupKey = `backups/${spaceId}/${date}/space-snapshot.json.gz`;
  
  // Compress and write to R2 — not naelao-workspace (product data)
  // but a separate naelao-backups bucket (write-once, lifecycle: 90 days)
  const compressed = await compressGzip(JSON.stringify(snapshot));
  await env.NAELAO_BACKUPS.put(backupKey, compressed, {
    customMetadata: { spaceId, exportedAt: snapshot.exportedAt, schemaVersion: String(snapshot.schemaVersion) }
  });
}

// 2. Enable R2 bucket versioning (add to infrastructure setup)
// wrangler.jsonc — naelao-workspace bucket config
// { "bucket_name": "naelao-workspace", "versioning": true }
// This enables: env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.list({ include: ['versions'] })
// Previous versions retained for 30 days before deletion

// 3. SpaceDO.exportSnapshot() — new method needed
exportSnapshot(): object {
  const tables = ['spaces','space_members','product_users','threads',
                  'messages','agent_runs','billing','agent_definitions'];
  const result: Record<string, unknown[]> = {};
  for (const table of tables) {
    result[table] = [...this.db.exec(`SELECT * FROM ${table}`).rows];
  }
  return { tables: result, exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
           schemaVersion: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION };
}
G-OPE-02

Global Rate Limiting — No Ingress Protection, Noisy Neighbour Possible

The Gap

Global Rate Limiting — No Ingress Protection, Noisy Neighbour Possible The spec specifies per-space AI Gateway rate limits but has no global ingress rate limiting at the naelao-router layer. A single product receiving a sudden traffic spike — a launch-day surge, a DDoS, or a misconfigured client sending in a loop — can exhaust Cloudflare Workers request budget and increase latency for every other product on the platform simultaneously. This is the noisy neighbour problem. It is not hypothetical: it is the first production incident category for every multi-tenant platform. The Three Missing Rate Limit Layers Layer What It Limits Current State Required Global ingress (per product) HTTP…

Required Fix

-RateLimit-Limit: {limit} // + X-RateLimit-Reset: {nextWindowTimestamp} Infinite Tool Loop — The Missing Hard Stop The AgentDO orchestrator loop has no maximum iteration count. An agent that enters a tool-call loop (calls tool A, gets result, decides to call tool A again, indefinitely) will run until it exhausts the builder's credit balance. The spec has no hard stop. Required: a per-turn tool call counter (max 50) and a per-run wall-clock timeout (max 10 minutes for isolate tier, 30 minutes for container tier) after which the run is marked 'cancelled' and the user is notified. Gap T-45 — High

// naelao-router: KV token bucket rate limiting per productId
// Simple sliding window — 1000 req/min per product (configurable per tier)

async function checkRateLimit(productId: string, env: Env): Promise<boolean> {
  const key = `rl:${productId}:${Math.floor(Date.now() / 60000)}`; // 1-min window
  const current = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(key);
  const count = current ? parseInt(current) : 0;

  const limits: Record<string, number> = {
    starter: 200, growth: 1000, scale: 5000, enterprise: 20000
  };
  const tier = await getProductTier(productId, env); // cached in KV
  const limit = limits[tier] ?? 200;

  if (count >= limit) return false; // rate limited

  // Increment atomically — KV doesn't support atomic increment
  // Use DO for true atomicity in high-traffic scenarios
  await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(key, String(count + 1), { expirationTtl: 120 });
  return true;
}

// Response when rate limited:
// HTTP 429 + Retry-After: 60 + X-RateLimit-Limit: {limit}
// + X-RateLimit-Reset: {nextWindowTimestamp}
G-OPE-03

Provisioner Rollback — Migrations Are Declared Irreversible, Rollback SQL Is Optional

The Gap

Provisioner Rollback — Migrations Are Declared Irreversible, Rollback SQL Is Optional The Provisioner's compensation log pattern is sound for phases 2–4 (KV slug lock, SpaceDO row, DO assembly). But phase 3 SQL migrations have a critical gap: `rollbackSql` is optional . If a migration does not include a rollback SQL, and a later phase fails, the compensating run skips that migration entirely. The SpaceDO has had DDL applied (e.g. `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) that is now orphaned — the space record is deleted but the schema change persists in the DO's SQLite storage. On the next provision attempt with the same DO name, the schema is already partially applied, and the idempotent `IF NOT…

Hardest to debug because the error appears at runtime, not at provision time. T-129 — Space Type Versioning

This threshold is hard-coded. There is no specification for: (a) what counts as an "error" in the Analytics Engine query — a 4xx HTTP response? An uncaught exception? A billing deduction failure? (b) whether the 5% is measured over all event types or only `agent_run_failed` events; (c) what the minimum sample size is before the threshold is meaningful (a Space with 2 users and 1 error triggers a rollback at 50%); (d) what happens if the Analytics Engine query itself fails — the `checkErrorRateForVersion()`…

Required Fix

The Gap

File Lock TTL — Agent Crash Orphans the Lock for 60 Seconds, Blocking All Writers The `ProjectDO.acquireLock()` method releases stale locks via a 60-second `expires_at` TTL. This is the only recovery mechanism. If an agent run is cancelled mid-write (user presses Stop, or the DO crashes), the lock is orphaned for up to 60 seconds. During that window every other agent or user trying to write the same file gets `{ acquired: false }` — the spec does not define whether the caller should retry, show an error, or queue behind the lock. The frontend has no mechanism to show "locked by Agent X — wait 45s" because the lock holder info is only returned from the DO, not surfaced to the UI layer.…

The sweeper's cleanup path should call force-release (not releaseLock) to avoid the ownership check throwing. Severity: Medium — Every agent crash produces a 60-second write blockout on affected files. In multi-agent projects this silently stalls parallel agents. T-132 — ProjectDO

G-OPE-07

The Gap

3-Way Merge Is Line-Based Only — Binary Files and JSON Silently Corrupt on Concurrent Write The `mergeTextFile()` implementation is a line-based split on `\n`. It handles the three trivial cases (both same, only A changed, only B changed) correctly, but when both agents modify the same file concurrently it produces a `<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>` conflict marker block. This is only meaningful for plain text. The spec applies this merge to all file types listed in the comment: "Markdown, code, JSON". JSON files with conflict markers are syntactically invalid and will crash any consumer that parses them. Binary files (images, PDFs, WASM) should never go through a text merge at all — the…

Required Fix

Required Fix Before merging, inspect file extension. Binary types (`.png .jpg .pdf .wasm .zip`) must not be merged — keep the latest write and log a conflict event to the activity feed. JSON files: parse both versions, use a structural JSON merge (last-write-wins per key, with conflict logging) rather than line-based. Enforce that `mergeTextFile()` is only reachable when a lock was not acquired (i.e., document the exact call site) or remove it and rely purely on the lock system. Severity: High — JSON files written by two concurrent agents will silently become invalid JSON with no error. Any downstream parse will throw, and the user sees no indication of data corruption. The orchestrator is expected to retry the tool call automatically. However the spec defines no retry budget. There is no `maxRetries` counter, no back-off delay, and no escalation path when retries are exhausted. An LLM that consistently produces malformed XML (due to a model bug or a very long context that pushes the XML template out of context) will retry indefinitely, consuming tokens and credits until the run is force-cancelled by the sweeper's heartbeat timeout (which is 10…

Required Fix

Required Fix Add `maxRetries: number` and `backoffMs: number` to the `ProcessedError` interface. Default: `maxRetries: 3, backoffMs: 1000`. The orchestrator must track a per-error-code retry counter per run turn. When `maxRetries` is exceeded, escalate to a fatal run error even if `isFatal` was originally false. For `isFatal: true` errors, the orchestrator must write a `status: 'awaiting_user'` row in the run WAL and suspend the agent loop (not terminate). The WebSocket connection stays alive. A user response reactivates the loop. Severity: High — A model stuck on malformed XML will spin for 10 minutes consuming tokens. Fatal errors that require user input have no mechanism to actually pause and await that input. T-134 — Operator Shell Slot System

G-OPE-09

Analytics Blob Field Mapping — Not Versioned; Schema Changes Break Queries

The Gap

Analytics Blob Field Mapping — Not Versioned; Schema Changes Break Queries The mapEventToDataPoint() function maps event fields to Analytics Engine blob and doubles arrays. For example, AgentRunEvent maps to: `blobs: [type, userId, agentId, runId, agentDefinitionId, mode, errorCode]`. If a new event field is added later (e.g., model name), the mapping must change: the new field goes into blob[7], and all previous events had 7 blobs. Old queries looking for blob[6] (errorCode) now get the wrong data. The mapping is not versioned, so there's no way to know which blob index corresponds to which field across time.

Required Fix

Required Fix Version the mapping: include a `schema_version` in the Analytics Engine data point. When queries run, they check the schema version and use the correct blob/doubles mapping. Alternatively, use named fields instead of positional indexing: Analytics Engine supports JSON payloads, so use `blobs: { type: "...", userId: "...", agentId: "..." }` instead of positional arrays. Document the blob field order explicitly and never change it retroactively. If a new field is needed, add it to the END of the blobs array. The Gap

At the end, there is an implicit fallthrough: if an error doesn't match any pattern, a generic message is returned: `agentMessage: "Unknown error occurred. Check the logs."`. This is unhelpful to the agent. A tool fails with a custom error message from a third-party API that the error processor doesn't recognize. The agent has no context about what failed and no way to self-correct. The logs are only visible to platform engineers, not to the agent or user.

Required Fix

Required Fix Always include the original error message in the agent message, even for unknown errors: agentMessage: \`Unknown error: ${error.message.slice(0, 200)}\`. For critical errors, have the agent automatically escalate with the raw error included, so an admin can investigate. Severity: Medium — Unhandled errors are hidden from agents. G-OPE-13

Compensation Race — Async Cleanup Can Fail; Partial Rollbacks Leave Orphans

The Gap

Compensation Race — Async Cleanup Can Fail; Partial Rollbacks Leave Orphans The compensation log stores async cleanup functions. When provisioning fails, they are replayed in reverse: `for (const rollback of [...compLog].reverse()) { await rollback().catch(...) }`. Each rollback is awaited, but errors are caught and logged. If a rollback fails (e.g., R2 deletion times out, DO destroy request fails), the loop continues. The Space ends up partially provisioned: some DOs were destroyed, some R2 objects remain, the SpaceDO row was deleted but the KV slug lock expired. The user sees "provisioning failed", but behind the scenes, there are orphaned resources that Naelao pays for.

Required Fix

Required Fix Use a CF Workflow for provisioning, not a single Worker request. Each compensation step is checkpointed. If a rollback fails, the Workflow retries it until it succeeds, rather than continuing and leaving orphans. Or, implement a "garbage collection" cron job that periodically scans for orphaned DOs and R2 prefixes and cleans them up. Log every failed rollback to an alerting system so ops can manually intervene. Severity: Medium — Async rollbacks can fail. Failed compensation steps are logged but not retried. Orphaned resources left behind increase storage costs. T-178 — Provisioner

G-OPE-14

The Gap

Lifecycle Hooks — No Timeout Or Failure Recovery; Hook Hang Blocks Entire Provisioning Lifecycle hooks (onProvision, onDeprovision) are called synchronously within provisioning steps: `await provisionExternalPortal(...)`. If a hook hangs (makes an HTTP request that never completes, gets stuck in an infinite loop), the entire provisioning is blocked. There is no timeout. The user's browser times out waiting for the Space to be created, but behind the scenes, the provisioner is still waiting for the hook. The Space may be partially provisioned (DOs created, R2 seeded) but the UI never confirms success. A subsequent deprovision attempt would be triggered manually, adding to the orphan problem.

Required Fix

Required Fix Add a timeout to hook execution: `await Promise.race([hookPromise, timeoutPromise])`. If a hook times out, treat it as a recoverable failure and continue provisioning (don't block). Or, invoke hooks asynchronously via a queue (naelao-lifecycle-queue) so provisioning returns immediately. Hooks run in the background. Log hook execution time and failures. Alert on timeouts so the ops team can investigate. Severity: Medium — Lifecycle hooks have no timeout. A hanging hook blocks entire provisioning indefinitely. No recovery mechanism. User sees no response. T-180 — naelao-spaces Worker

G-OPE-15

Space Hierarchy Depth Check — Race Between Recursive Query And Parent Deletion

The Gap

Space Hierarchy Depth Check — Race Between Recursive Query And Parent Deletion When creating a sub-space, naelao-spaces runs a recursive CTE query to check the depth of the parent space. If the depth is >= 3, creation is rejected. Between the depth check and the INSERT, another request could delete the parent space or change its parent. The depth check becomes stale. A Space could be created with a parent that no longer exists, violating the hierarchy constraint. Alternatively, two concurrent creates could pass the depth check and both succeed, resulting in a space tree deeper than 3 levels.

Required Fix

Required Fix Use a transaction with SELECT...FOR UPDATE on the parent space row to lock it during the depth check and insert: `SELECT * FROM spaces WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE`. Or, add a CHECK constraint at the database level that enforces the depth limit: CHECK (depth . Let the database reject violations atomically. Verify parent existence in the same transaction before allowing the insert. Severity: Medium — Depth check is not atomic. Parent space can be deleted between check and insert. Concurrent creates can bypass depth limit. T-181 — naelao-spaces Worker

The Gap

Member Cache Invalidation — Async Request Not Awaited; Members Stay Cached After Removal When a member is removed from a space, the worker calls `spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/invalidate-member-cache', ...))` but does not await it. The function returns immediately with `{ success: true }`. Meanwhile, the async invalidation request is sent to the DO in the background. If the DO is slow to respond or times out, the cache entry remains valid. A removed member can still authenticate and access the space until the cache TTL expires (could be hours).

Required Fix

Required Fix Await the invalidation request before returning: `await spaceDO.fetch(...)`. If it fails, return an error. Or, use a queue instead: send the invalidation message to a queue and have the worker acknowledge success only after the queue message is accepted. The DO processes it asynchronously. // Required: manifest review pipeline specification

// naelao-apps-registry must implement a review queue for third-party space type submissions.

interface SpaceTypeManifestSubmission {
  manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifest;
  submittedBy: string;        // builderAccountId
  submittedAt: number;
  reviewStatus: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'needs_changes';
  reviewNotes?: string;
  reviewedBy?: string;        // 'automated' | naelaoAdminId
}

// Automated checks (run synchronously on submission, before human review):
async function validateManifestSafety(manifest: NaelaoSpaceTypeManifest): Promise<ValidationResult> {
  const issues: string[] = [];

  // 1. System prompt injection check — run the security scanner on all system prompts
  for (const agentDef of manifest.agents ?? []) {
    const scan = scanSkillContent(agentDef.systemPrompt ?? '');
    if (!scan.safe) issues.push(`Agent '${agentDef.id}' system prompt: ${scan.violatedPatterns[0]?.reason}`);
  }

  // 2. Billing primitives validation — only known primitives allowed
  const ALLOWED_PRIMITIVES = ['walletDO', 'workerDefinitions', 'miniAgi', 'r2Workspace', 'knowledgeBase'];
  for (const prim of Object.keys(manifest.primitives ?? {})) {
    if (!ALLOWED_PRIMITIVES.includes(prim)) {
      issues.push(`Unknown primitive '${prim}' — only platform primitives are allowed`);
    }
  }

  // 3. RBAC defaults sanity check
  if (manifest.defaultMemberRole === 'admin' || manifest.defaultMemberRole === 'owner') {
    issues.push('defaultMemberRole cannot be admin or owner — security risk');
  }

  // 4. External URL references in skills
  const urlPattern = /https?:\/\/(?!cdn\.naelao\.app)/;
  for (const skill of manifest.platformSkills ?? []) {
    if (urlPattern.test(JSON.stringify(skill))) {
      issues.push(`Skill '${skill.name}' references an external URL — not allowed in manifests`);
    }
  }

  return { valid: issues.length === 0, issues };
}

// Required: timestamp validation + idempotency key on all webhook handlers

// Stripe webhook handler — add timestamp check:
async handleStripeWebhook(request: Request, params: WebhookParams): Promise<Response> {
  const body = await request.text();
  const signature = request.headers.get('Stripe-Signature') ?? '';

  // Stripe signature includes t={timestamp} — validate staleness
  const timestampMatch = signature.match(/t=(\d+)/);
  const webhookTimestamp = timestampMatch ? parseInt(timestampMatch[1]) * 1000 : 0;
  const REPLAY_WINDOW_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes

  if (Date.now() - webhookTimestamp > REPLAY_WINDOW_MS) {
    return new Response('Webhook timestamp too old — possible replay attack', { status: 400 });
  }

  // Idempotency: use Stripe's event ID as the dedup key
  const event = JSON.parse(body) as Stripe.Event;
  const dedupKey = `stripe-webhook:${event.id}`;
  const alreadyProcessed = await env.NAELAO_DEDUP_KV.get(dedupKey);

G-PLA-04

Webhook Dispatch Race — Concurrent Triggers Can Dispatch Duplicate Workflows

The Gap

Webhook Dispatch Race — Concurrent Triggers Can Dispatch Duplicate Workflows The webhook ingress queries space_triggers to find all handlers, then dispatches to each one. Between the query and the dispatch, the same trigger could be added again (if a user double-clicks the "Connect App" button). Two simultaneous webhooks arriving in quick succession would both pass the query and both dispatch, resulting in duplicate workflow executions. The dispatch is not idempotent — running the same workflow twice from the same webhook results in duplicate operations (double charges, duplicate orders, etc.).

Required Fix

Required Fix Add an idempotency key to webhooks: store a hash of (spaceId, provider, event_type, event_id) and reject duplicate webhooks within a 24-hour window. Use a unique constraint on space_triggers to prevent duplicate registrations: no two triggers with the same (space_id, provider, event_type, target_type, target_id). Make workflow execution idempotent: if the same workflow is triggered twice with the same input, the second one is a no-op. Severity: Medium — Concurrent triggers cause duplicate workflow dispatches. No idempotency key or deduplication. Workflows execute multiple times for single webhooks. T-173 — naelao-notifications

G-PLA-05

Notification Batch Failure — Promise.all() Blocks All Deliveries If Any Channel Fails

The Gap

Notification Batch Failure — Promise.all() Blocks All Deliveries If Any Channel Fails The processNotification() function uses `Promise.all(deliveries)` to send across all requested channels (email, push, voice). If one channel fails (e.g., Resend email API is down), the entire Promise.all() rejects and the whole function throws. The message is retried. However, if the email API is temporarily down but push is working, the user still gets the push notification but the retry waits for email to recover. Meanwhile, subsequent notifications queue up. The idempotency lock prevents double-delivery only AFTER a successful send, so partial failures leave the system in an inconsistent state.

Required Fix

Required Fix Use Promise.allSettled() instead of Promise.all(): send to all channels regardless of individual failures. Return partial success: { success: true, email: failed, push: succeeded, voice: skipped }. Log which channels failed. Retry failed channels separately via a DLQ, not the entire notification. Severity: Medium — Promise.all() on notification channels blocks all deliveries on any failure. Partial channel outages prevent all notifications from sending. T-174 — WorkflowRegistryDO

MiniAGI Domain Classifier — LLM Called on Every Query, No Cache

The Gap

MiniAGI Domain Classifier — LLM Called on Every Query, No Cache The MiniAGIDO's query() method makes an LLM call to classify which data domains are needed for the user's question, before it makes the second LLM call to actually answer the question. This means every MiniAGI query costs two LLM calls. For a company with 50 employees each making 10 queries per day, that is 1,000 classification LLM calls per day — each one adding 200–500ms of latency and a non-trivial credit cost — just for question classification. The spec uses claude-haiku-4-5 for classification, which is the cheapest option. But the deeper problem is that the classification is doing something simple — mapping a natural…

Required Fix

vector matches, fall back to Haiku LLM classification // (only in ambiguous cases — not for every query) const result = domains.length > 0 ? domains : await this.classifyWithLLM(question); // Cache the result await this.env.NAELAO_KV.put(cacheKey, JSON.stringify(result), { expirationTtl: 3600 }); return result; } // Also unspecified: domain descriptions must be pre-embedded when a domain is created. // POST /api/mini-agi/{id}/domains must trigger an embedding of the domain description // into a naelao-domain-vectorize index (separate from knowledge base and memory indexes). // Required: domain classification cache + keyword fallback

// Option A: Cache classification results by question semantic hash
// Questions that mean the same thing should hit the same domains.
// Use a fast embedding + ANN search over domain descriptions to classify without LLM.

async classifyDomains(question: string): Promise<string[]> {
  // 1. Check classification cache (KV, TTL 1 hour)
  //    Key: sha256 of the question (normalized, lowercased)
  const cacheKey = `domain-classify:${await sha256(question.toLowerCase().trim())}`;
  const cached = await this.env.NAELAO_KV.get(cacheKey, 'json');
  if (cached) return cached as string[];

  // 2. Fast path: embed the question, compare to pre-embedded domain descriptions
  //    This replaces the Haiku LLM call with a vector similarity search ( m.score > 0.65)
    .map(m => m.metadata!.domainId as string);

  // 3. If no strong vector matches, fall back to Haiku LLM classification
  //    (only in ambiguous cases — not for every query)
  const result = domains.length > 0 ? domains : await this.classifyWithLLM(question);

  // Cache the result
  await this.env.NAELAO_KV.put(cacheKey, JSON.stringify(result), { expirationTtl: 3600 });
  return result;
}

// Also unspecified: domain descriptions must be pre-embedded when a domain is created.
// POST /api/mini-agi/{id}/domains must trigger an embedding of the domain description
// into a naelao-domain-vectorize index (separate from knowledge base and memory indexes).

// Required: HybridQueryDO — a thin query router for paginated reads
// Sits between naelao-agents Worker and SpaceDO/R2
// One instance per product — low memory usage (just routing + page merging)

export class HybridQueryDO extends DurableObject {
  // Paginated thread messages — merges live + archive
  async getThreadMessages(params: {
    spaceId: string; threadId: string; page: number; pageSize: number;
  }): Promise<{ messages: Message[]; hasMore: boolean; source: 'live'|'archive'|'hybrid' }> {
    const { spaceId, threadId, page, pageSize } = params;
    const offset = page * pageSize;

    // 1. Try SpaceDO first (newest messages are here)
    const spaceDO = getProductDO(spaceId, this.env);
    const liveResult = await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/messages', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ threadId, limit: pageSize, offset })
    })).then(r => r.json());

    if (liveResult.messages.length === pageSize) {
      return { ...liveResult, source: 'live' };
    }

    // 2. If SpaceDO returned fewer than pageSize, gap-fill from R2 archive
    const archiveKey = `archives/${spaceId}/threads/${threadId}/messages.jsonl`;
    const archived = await this.env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(archiveKey);
    if (!archived) return { ...liveResult, hasMore: false, source: 'live' };

    const archiveLines = (await archived.text()).split('\n').filter(Boolean);
    const archiveMessages = archiveLines.map(l => JSON.parse(l));

    // Merge and deduplicate by message.id, sort by created_at
    const merged = [...liveResult.messages, ...archiveMessages]
      .sort((a, b) => new Date(b.created_at).getTime() - new Date(a.created_at).getTime())
      .filter((m, i, arr) => arr.findIndex(x => x.id === m.id) === i)
      .slice(offset, offset + pageSize);

    return { messages: merged, hasMore: merged.length === pageSize, source: 'hybrid' };
  }
}

// Required: namespace-partitioned index strategy
// Instead of one index per space, use a fixed pool of indexes (e.g. 10)
// and partition by metadata filter within each index

// Assign each space to one of N shard indexes:
function getVectorizeIndexForSpace(spaceId: string, shardCount = 10): string {
  // Stable hash of spaceId to a shard number
  const hash = spaceId.split('').reduce((a, c) => a + c.charCodeAt(0), 0);
  const shard = hash % shardCount;
  return `naelao-kb-shard-${shard}`;  // 10 fixed indexes, not one per space
}

}]);

  topK: 5,
  filter: { spaceId: { $eq: currentSpaceId } }
});

// Each shard serves ~1,000 spaces with ~50K vectors per space

G-MIS-10

Federated Learning LLM Judge — Confidence Threshold at 0.95 With No Fallback; Rejection Silent

The Gap

Federated Learning LLM Judge — Confidence Threshold at 0.95 With No Fallback; Rejection Silent The `proposeLearning()` method calls an LLM judge to determine if a proposed learning is data-free before accepting it. The LLM must return `{"safe": true, "confidence": 0.95+}` to be accepted. However: (a) the LLM can hallucinate and return a false positive, approving a learning that actually contains company data; (b) if the judge returns `confidence: 0.93` (below threshold), the learning is rejected silently — there is no fallback or escalation to a human reviewer; (c) the judge is called on every proposal, but there is no caching of the judgment, so similar proposals are re-evaluated…

Required Fix

Required Fix Add a `judgmentCache` table keyed by proposal fingerprint. Reuse judgments for identical proposals across instances. For borderline confidences (0.85–0.95), escalate to the Worker creator via a notification instead of silently rejecting. Let them decide whether to accept the learning. Add a max-tokens budget to the judge LLM call (200 is already specified) and add retry logic if the LLM times out or returns invalid JSON. Require human approval for federated learnings that will change agent behavior in production (confidence threshold for auto-approval should be configurable). Severity: Medium — LLM judge can hallucinate and approve unsafe learnings. Borderline proposals are silently rejected with no human review path. Judgment results are never cached. T-139 — Naelao Apps

Domain Classifier LLM — Called Every Query, No Cache; Hallucinates Domain IDs Outside Access

The Gap

Domain Classifier LLM — Called Every Query, No Cache; Hallucinates Domain IDs Outside Access The `query()` method calls an LLM on every question to classify which data domains the question needs. The LLM is given the list of available domains. However: (a) there is no caching — identical questions are reclassified every time, wasting tokens; (b) the LLM can hallucinate and return domain IDs that don't exist in the available list; (c) the spec does not validate that the returned domain IDs are real — it just uses them directly in the `checkAccess()` call. An attacker or confused user could craft a question that tricks the LLM into returning a domain ID it shouldn't access, and if that domain…

Required Fix

Required Fix Cache domain classifications per question. Store: `{ question_hash → [domain_ids, timestamp] }`. Reuse for identical or similar questions (use semantic similarity, not exact match). After the LLM returns domain IDs, validate each ID against the actual domains table . Filter out hallucinated IDs. If the user's question requires a domain that doesn't exist in this Mini-AGI, mention that in the response. Add a debug flag to the response: which domains were classified vs which were available vs which were denied. This helps identify LLM hallucination in logs. Severity: Medium — LLM can hallucinate domain IDs. Every query pays the cost of a fresh LLM call. Hallucinations are hidden behind generic access denial. T-142 — Space Assistants
