WalletDO.getTransactions() uses LIMIT/OFFSET pagination — offset pagination is O(n), scanning 10,000 transactions to reach offset 9,900 is a full SQLite table scan.

Required Fix

Add cursor (a message_id) parameter to getLlmFormattedMessages(): SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ? AND id < ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?. Return nextCursor in the response when more messages exist. Replace offset pagination in WalletDO.getTransactions() with keyset pagination: WHERE id < ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?. Update ContextManager to use cursor pagination when building long-context windows, fetching earlier pages only when the token budget allows.

G-F23 MEDIUM naelao-admin / KV

KV-Based Emergency Kill Switch Has 60-Second Propagation Delay — Agents Continue Running During Incidents

The Gap

AgentDO checks env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get('emergency:kill-all-agents') at the top of every LLM loop iteration. CF KV is eventually consistent with up to 60-second propagation SLA to all edge nodes. During a security incident requiring immediate agent halt, agents at edge nodes that haven't received the KV update continue executing for up to 60 seconds. For an agent actively exfiltrating data via tool calls, 60 seconds is significant damage.

Required Fix

Supplement the KV kill switch with a DO-based kill signal for immediate propagation: maintain a KillSwitchDO singleton (idFromName('global-kill-switch')) that AgentDO checks via Service Binding before each LLM call. Service Binding calls propagate in under 1ms. Keep the KV check as secondary for steady-state (lower cost). Document the dual-check pattern in the security architecture section and add a test: 'Kill switch activation halts agent within 1 LLM iteration'.

G-F24 MEDIUM FinetuneJobDO / AssistantDO

Alarm Handlers Not Idempotent — CF At-Least-Once Delivery Causes Duplicate Notifications and Status Updates

The Gap

CF's alarm system guarantees at-least-once delivery. FinetuneJobDO.alarm() calls Together AI API → UPDATE fine_tune_jobs → send notification. If the alarm fires twice (CF retry on timeout), two notifications are sent and NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE.send() produces duplicate messages downstream. The UPDATE itself is idempotent, but notification sends are not — they produce duplicate emails/push messages to the builder.

Required Fix

Add idempotency guard to all alarm handlers. Store last_alarm_executed_at in DO storage. At the start of every alarm: const lastExec = await this.ctx.storage.get('last_alarm_executed_at'); if (lastExec && Date.now() - lastExec < 60_000) return;. Update after execution: await this.ctx.storage.put('last_alarm_executed_at', Date.now()). For notification sends, pass a deterministic id: id: `finetune-complete:${jobId}` rather than a random UUID, using the existing KV idempotency check with 24-hour TTL.

G-F25 MEDIUM naelao-credentials

Single Global Encryption Key for All Tenant MCP Credentials — No Per-Tenant Key Isolation

The Gap

naelao-credentials encrypts all MCP credentials (Stripe keys, GitHub tokens, CRM credentials) using a single platform-wide NAELAO_MCP_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Key rotation requires re-encrypting all credentials for all spaces simultaneously. A side-channel attack extracting the key from any Worker instance exposes all tenant credentials. The spec's BYOK section shows HKDF per-space key derivation but this pattern is not applied to the main credential store.

Required Fix

Adopt the BYOK HKDF pattern: derive a per-space encryption key using HKDF(masterKey, salt=spaceId, info='mcp-credentials'). Store only the master key as NAELAO_MCP_MASTER_KEY. Per-space derived keys are never stored — recomputed on each decrypt. This means compromise of any single worker instance does not expose all credentials. Version the HKDF info string (mcp-credentials-v2) to allow rotation without full re-encryption.

G-F26 MEDIUM All systems / Observability

No Distributed Trace ID Propagation Across 22-Worker Call Chain — Cross-Worker Debugging Is Impossible

The Gap

An agent run involves: naelao-router → naelao-agents → NaelaoAgentDO → naelao-mcp-hub → [App Worker] → naelao-billing → naelao-analytics. Each Worker logs independently with its own request IDs. There is no X-Trace-ID header propagated through Service Binding calls. Analytics Engine records runId for agent events but not for billing or MCP events, breaking the correlation chain. Debugging a failed agent run requires manually correlating logs from 6+ Workers by matching timestamps — slow and error-prone.

Required Fix

Generate traceId = crypto.randomUUID() at naelao-router entry point for every request. Propagate as X-Trace-ID header in all Service Binding calls (Service Binding fetch() accepts custom headers). Add traceId to the AnalyticsEvent base interface so all Analytics Engine events include the trace. Add CF-Ray correlation to link CF's own request traces. Add to pre-launch checklist: 'Query Analytics Engine for a single traceId — confirm events from all 22 Workers appear in the result'.

Appendix F complete. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) = 249 documented technical gaps with required fixes. Recurring themes in this pass: DO eviction not accounted for (G-F05, G-F07, G-F12), missing KV binding declarations (G-F10, G-F17), alarm handler at-least-once semantics ignored (G-F24), and per-tenant isolation gaps (G-F03, G-F25).

Appendix G · Sixth-Pass Audit

Architecture Contradictions, Missing Infrastructure & Runtime Correctness Gaps

26 additional gaps from the deepest audit pass yet. A critical architectural contradiction runs through this entire pass: the spec simultaneously declares "no PostgreSQL, data layer is SpaceDO SQLite" while containing PostgreSQL-syntax queries, plpgsql stored functions, and undefined db.query() calls across 56 call sites in Worker code. The PostgreSQL-to-SpaceDO migration was never completed in the spec itself. This pass also surfaces missing wiring (canary rollout never called, Vectorize binding absent, extractEventType undefined), Stripe billing race conditions, and GDPR erasure gaps.

6 CRITICAL 13 HIGH 7 MEDIUM
CRITICAL SEVERITY — 6 GAPS
G-G01 CRITICAL All Workers (naelao-billing, naelao-spaces, naelao-mcp-hub, naelao-sweeper, naelao-admin, naelao-knowledge, naelao-triggers)

rootSpaceId Used in 56 Call Sites Across Workers But Never Declared — Universal ReferenceError on First Request

The Gap

The spec declares the data layer as 'SpaceDO SQLite, no Hyperdrive, no external PostgreSQL.' However, 56 occurrences of getProductDO(rootSpaceId, c.env) appear in Worker handler bodies where rootSpaceId is never assigned before use. The db variable used in subsequent db.query() calls is also never declared. In naelao-billing's /token-usage handler, const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, c.env) appears before any rootSpaceId assignment — this is a ReferenceError at the first request. naelao-spaces calls db.query() using INTERVAL '7 days' and gen_random_uuid() — PostgreSQL-only syntax that cannot execute against DO SQLite. Every Worker that touches data will throw at runtime.

Required Fix

For each Worker, rootSpaceId must be extracted from the validated JWT context (c.get('rootSpaceId') from the auth middleware) before any data call. The db variable must be replaced with a typed SpaceDO stub obtained via env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName(`space:${rootSpaceId}`)). All PostgreSQL-syntax queries (DATE_TRUNC, INTERVAL, auth.users, FOR UPDATE, RETURNING) must be rewritten as DO SQLite statements using this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() with SQLite equivalents (strftime, integer comparisons, separate SELECT then UPDATE patterns). create_space_with_defaults must use crypto.randomUUID() and a SpaceDO typed method. Add an ESLint rule banning db.query in Worker code outside DO files.

G-G02 CRITICAL SpaceDO Methods / naelao-billing / naelao-spaces

Five plpgsql Stored Functions with SECURITY DEFINER and auth.uid() Cannot Execute in DO SQLite

The Gap

The 'SpaceDO Methods — Replacing All Stored Functions' section contains five CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION blocks written in plpgsql with SECURITY DEFINER, LANGUAGE plpgsql, auth.uid(), auth.users, FOR UPDATE, and RETURNING clauses. SQLite in Durable Objects does not support stored functions, plpgsql, LANGUAGE clause, or auth.uid(). The deduct_space_credits function uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (PostgreSQL row-level locking), which has no SQLite equivalent and would silently fail. naelao-sweeper queries auth.users to fan out heartbeats — a table that only exists in Supabase/PostgreSQL. These five functions will fail at ctx.storage.sql.exec() with syntax errors, making credit deductions, space creation, and heartbeats non-functional.

Required Fix

All five stored function bodies must be converted to TypeScript methods on the SpaceDO class using this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() with SQLite syntax. deduct_space_credits must use the WalletDO.deductCredits() pattern (single-threaded DO = no FOR UPDATE needed). create_space_with_defaults becomes a SpaceDO.createSpace() method using SQLite transactions via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('BEGIN'). auth.users and auth.uid() references must be replaced with the naelao-auth JWT validation path and SpaceDO space_members table. naelao-sweeper must query active assistants from a dedicated SpaceDO.getActiveSpaceMembers() method, not via raw SQL against auth.users.

G-G03 CRITICAL naelao-billing / Stripe webhook

Stripe Webhook Handler Has No Idempotency Protection — Duplicate checkout.session.completed Events Double-Credit Users

The Gap

CF Queues and Stripe both guarantee at-least-once delivery. The Stripe webhook handler handles checkout.session.completed by executing INSERT INTO space_credits ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET balance_usd = balance_usd + EXCLUDED.balance_usd. If Stripe retries the same event (it retries for up to 72 hours on 2xx responses), the credit is added again — a direct financial loss. invoice.payment_failed also triggers a notification queue message on each delivery, so the builder receives duplicate emails. The naelao-notifications consumer has a KV idempotency key but the billing handler never sets it or checks it before queuing notifications.

Required Fix

Before processing any Stripe event, write a KV idempotency record: const key = `stripe-event:${event.id}`; if (await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(key)) return c.json({ received: true }); await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(key, '1', { expirationTtl: 86400 * 7 }). Place this check at the top of the webhook handler before the switch(event.type) block. For additional safety, the credit upsert must include the Stripe event ID as a unique constraint: INSERT INTO stripe_events (event_id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id — if this returns 0 rows, skip processing.

G-G04 CRITICAL naelao-billing / Stripe subscription events

invoice.payment_failed Reads spaceId from subscription_details.metadata — null for Most Stripe Invoice Shapes, Payment Failures Silently Ignored

The Gap

The invoice.payment_failed handler reads: const spaceId = invoice.subscription_details?.metadata?.spaceId. Stripe only populates subscription_details when the invoice is directly linked to a subscription. For checkout-session invoices, metadata is on invoice.metadata directly. For subscription invoices, subscription_details.metadata may be null if metadata was set on the subscription object rather than the invoice. spaceId is undefined in several real billing scenarios, the if (spaceId) guard silently passes through, the UPDATE spaces SET status='payment_failed' never runs, and the space continues serving traffic despite a failed payment. This also affects subscription lifecycle events which read sub.metadata?.spaceId — if spaceId was placed on the Checkout Session metadata but not copied to the Subscription metadata, all subscription lifecycle events silently no-op.

Required Fix

When creating Stripe Checkout Sessions, set metadata: { spaceId } on both the Checkout Session AND the Subscription via subscription_data: { metadata: { spaceId } }. In the webhook handler, implement a multi-path resolver: const spaceId = invoice.metadata?.spaceId ?? invoice.subscription_details?.metadata?.spaceId ?? (await stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(invoice.subscription)).metadata?.spaceId. Log a structured error to Analytics Engine whenever spaceId cannot be resolved from a billing event — this catches metadata configuration bugs in staging before they reach production.

G-G05 CRITICAL naelao-spaces / space provisioning

Concurrent POST /api/spaces Requests Have No Serialization Lock — Race Creates Duplicate DOs and Half-Provisioned Spaces

The Gap

The space creation flow does three non-atomic operations with no lock: INSERT INTO spaces, then spaceDO.fetch('http://space/init'), then c.executionCtx.waitUntil(registryDO.fetch('provision')). If two simultaneous requests arrive, both pass quota checks (reading the same counts before either commits), both attempt the DB insert (one fails on unique violation), but if one fails the DB insert the other proceeds to call spaceDO.fetch(init). Worse, provisioning is fired via waitUntil — if the HTTP response returns before provisioning completes and the user immediately navigates to the space, they hit a SpaceDO that hasn't called initSpaceType() yet.

Required Fix

Route POST /api/spaces through a per-user SpaceCreationDO via idFromName(`space-create-lock:${userId}`) — the DO's single-threaded guarantee serializes concurrent creation attempts. Inside the DO, check for an in-progress creation before starting a new one. Alternatively, use a KV NX lock: await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(`creating-space:${spaceId}`, '1', { expirationTtl: 30 }) using a conditional write that fails if the key exists. The provisioning step must complete synchronously before returning 201, not via waitUntil — the client must not receive success until provisioning is confirmed complete.

G-G06 CRITICAL naelao-billing / naelao-admin

db.query('BEGIN') / db.query('ROLLBACK') Pattern Used in Workers — Cannot Execute Against SpaceDO, Atomic Billing Invariant Broken

The Gap

The spec's most emphasized invariant is 'atomic-or-nothing credit deduction.' The billing Worker shows await db.query('BEGIN'); try { ... await db.query('COMMIT'); } catch { await db.query('ROLLBACK'); }. In the CF DO model there is no db object — data access goes through this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() inside the DO. If db is undefined, this throws ReferenceError on the first request. If someone implements db as a wrapper around SpaceDO calls, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK have no meaning outside a direct SQLite connection. The actual atomic pattern in DO SQLite is a single this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() call with all statements in one string — which is not what the spec shows.

Required Fix

Move all credit deduction logic into a SpaceDO.deductCredits() typed method that uses this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() with a single multi-statement transaction block: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`BEGIN; INSERT INTO token_usage ...; UPDATE space_credits ...; COMMIT`). The AgentDO and billing Worker call this single DO method via Service Binding — the DO's single-threaded guarantee provides the atomicity that PostgreSQL's FOR UPDATE provided before. The three-step transaction (INSERT token_usage, UPDATE space_usage_monthly, UPDATE space_credits) must be combined into a single exec() call. Remove all db.query('BEGIN') / db.query('ROLLBACK') patterns from Worker-level code.

HIGH SEVERITY — 13 GAPS
G-G07 HIGH NaelaoAgentDO / webSocketMessage

JSON.parse(message) Without try/catch in webSocketMessage — Malformed Frame Crashes DO and Terminates All Active Runs

The Gap

The webSocketMessage handler calls const data = JSON.parse(message as string) with no try/catch. If the client sends a binary frame, message is an ArrayBuffer and JSON.parse throws SyntaxError. If the client sends a partial JSON frame (network truncation), JSON.parse also throws. An unhandled exception in webSocketMessage inside a Durable Object will cause CF to close the WebSocket connection and may trigger DO eviction. Since the agent loop runs inside the DO, an eviction mid-run triggers fiber recovery — but if the DO evicts during an active await (e.g., during an LLM call), the fiber state may not have been stashed yet (stash happens at the top of each iteration), losing the current LLM response.

Required Fix

Wrap the entire webSocketMessage body in try/catch: try { if (typeof message !== 'string') { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'error', message: 'Binary frames not supported' })); return; } const data = JSON.parse(message); ... } catch (e) { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'error', message: 'Invalid message format' })); return; }. Also define the webSocketClose handler to handle client disconnections cleanly rather than leaving the agent loop running headlessly with no recipient for token stream broadcasts.

G-G08 HIGH GitHub Actions CI / wrangler deploy

All Workers Deployed in a Single wrangler deploy Command With No Dependency Ordering — Service Binding Resolution Fails on First Deploy

The Gap

The CI pipeline runs npx wrangler deploy --env production as a single step. Cloudflare Service Bindings require the referenced Worker to already exist at deployment time. If naelao-router is deployed before naelao-auth, the Service Binding { 'binding': 'NAELAO_AUTH', 'service': 'naelao-auth' } in naelao-router's wrangler config will fail validation. On a first deploy to a fresh account (staging setup, new developer onboarding), the correct dependency order is: (1) DO-hosting Workers, (2) leaf Workers (naelao-auth, naelao-billing, naelao-knowledge), (3) aggregator Workers (naelao-mcp-hub, naelao-agents), (4) naelao-router last. A single wrangler deploy deploys in alphabetical order — not the dependency graph order.

Required Fix

The CI pipeline must deploy Workers in dependency order. Add a deploy-production GitHub Actions job that runs wrangler deploy for each Worker in sequence: first all DO-hosting Workers, then leaf service Workers, then aggregator Workers, then the router. Use wrangler deploy --config workers/auth/wrangler.jsonc, wrangler deploy --config workers/billing/wrangler.jsonc, etc., in order with && chaining. Add a validation step that runs wrangler publish --dry-run for each Worker to catch binding resolution errors before they reach production.

G-G09 HIGH naelao-triggers / webhook security

Stripe Webhook Signature Verification in naelao-triggers Returns true Unconditionally — Anyone Can Trigger Agent Runs

The Gap

The verifySignature function has a full GitHub HMAC-SHA256 implementation followed by // Stripe uses a custom timestamped signature, implemented similarly... return true. This means any POST request to /webhooks/stripe/{spaceId} with any payload and any signature will pass verification and trigger workflows or agent runs in the target space. An attacker who discovers the URL pattern can forge Stripe events targeting any space, triggering agent runs, waking sleeping agents, and consuming billing credits. The spaceId is in the URL and can be correlated from public portal URLs.

Required Fix

Implement Stripe's timestamp-based webhook signature immediately. Stripe's format is t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature> where v1 is HMAC-SHA256(secret, '{timestamp}.{payload}'). Enforce a timestamp tolerance: reject requests where |now - t| > 300 seconds to prevent replay attacks. The verifySignature function must throw or return false for unrecognized providers — never default to return true. Add a PROVIDER_VERIFIED allowlist: only providers with implemented verification (github, stripe) are accepted; all others return 401 until implemented.

G-G10 HIGH naelao-knowledge / Vectorize

Vectorize Binding Missing from wrangler.jsonc — env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE Is undefined, All Knowledge Upserts and Queries Throw TypeError

The Gap

The knowledge Worker upserts to c.env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE and queries the same binding. The wrangler.jsonc does not define any vectorize binding. The spec's architecture text says 'Vectors stored in Vectorize index naelao-kb-{spaceId}' suggesting per-tenant indexes, but CF Vectorize indexes are static infrastructure defined in wrangler.jsonc at deploy time — they cannot be created programmatically at runtime. With no vectorize binding in wrangler.jsonc, c.env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE is undefined and every call to .upsert() or .query() throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined. The entire RAG/knowledge feature is broken before a single line of application logic runs.

Required Fix

Define a single shared Vectorize index in wrangler.jsonc: "vectorize": [{ "binding": "NAELAO_VECTORIZE", "index_name": "naelao-knowledge-base" }]. Create this index before first deploy: wrangler vectorize create naelao-knowledge-base --dimensions=768 --metric=cosine. Use spaceId metadata filter on every query (filter: { spaceId }) for tenant isolation. Add index creation to the workspace setup checklist as a required one-time step. For document deletion, call NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds() for all chunk IDs — this must be part of the deprovisioning workflow which currently does not call Vectorize at all.

G-G11 HIGH SpaceTypeRegistryDO / canary rollout

processCanaryRollouts() Is Never Called by Any Scheduler — Canary Versions Stuck at 5% Forever

The Gap

The processCanaryRollouts function exists as an async function inside SpaceTypeRegistryDO but is never registered as a DO alarm handler, never called from naelao-sweeper, and the global singleton DO has no alarm() method defined in the spec. The sweeper tasks are sweepAssistantHeartbeats, sweepAbandonedAgentRuns, sweepExpiredFileLocks, sweepDeadLetterQueue, and sweepStaleFineTuneJobs — no sweepCanaryRollouts. The rollbackInstances function referenced inside processCanaryRollouts is also never defined. The canary_pct field starts at 0 per the schema default and is only set to 5 at publish time via a code path that is also absent. The entire canary mechanism is specified but not wired up.

Required Fix

Add sweepCanaryRollouts to the naelao-sweeper's Promise.allSettled task list. Inside that task, fetch the global SpaceTypeRegistryDO and call processCanaryRollouts() on it. Define the missing rollbackInstances(typeId, version) function which must query the instances table for spaces on the failing version and update them to the last stable version. Set canary_pct = 5 explicitly in registerSpaceType() when change_type = 'minor'. Add a checkErrorRateForVersion() implementation that queries Analytics Engine for the error_rate of the specific version over the past hour. Add a minimum sample size guard (min 50 provisioning events) before allowing promotion.

G-G12 HIGH RevenueCat / naelao-billing

RevenueCat Webhook Endpoint Has No Public Route — RevenueCat Cannot POST to an Internal Service Binding Worker

The Gap

The RevenueCat handler authenticates via Authorization header comparison. naelao-billing is an internal Worker called via Service Binding — it has no public HTTP route (all endpoints are internal, naelao-router does NOT expose these routes). But the RevenueCat webhook must be publicly accessible for RevenueCat to POST to it. If there's an undocumented public route in naelao-router passing the Authorization header through, the JWT middleware that validates Bearer tokens would reject the RevenueCat request (which uses a shared secret, not a user JWT) with 401 before it reaches billing. RevenueCat's webhook Authorization header conflicts with standard Bearer JWT auth patterns.

Required Fix

The RevenueCat webhook must have a dedicated public route: POST /api/billing/revenuecat/webhook exposed through naelao-router with auth middleware explicitly bypassed for this path (whitelisted alongside /api/auth/*). Validate the RevenueCat shared secret using a constant-time comparison (timingSafeEqual via Web Crypto) to prevent timing attacks. Alternatively, use RevenueCat's X-RevenueCat-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) rather than the Authorization header to avoid conflicts with JWT middleware.

G-G13 HIGH All Durable Objects / schema evolution

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Silently Ignores New Columns on Existing DOs — Schema Evolution Is Broken for Live DOs

The Gap

The constructor calls ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(() => this.initSchema()) on every DO instantiation. initSchema() uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for all tables. If a new deployment adds a column (e.g., tool_args_hash TEXT to run_wal), the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run_wal statement is a no-op because the table already exists — the new column is never added. Code that writes to tool_args_hash receives 'table run_wal has no column named tool_args_hash' SQLite error, crashing the agent loop. There is no migration versioning, no schema version table, and no ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pattern specified. DOs can live for months between evictions, meaning old-schema DOs coexist with new code indefinitely.

Required Fix

Add a schema_version table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 0). In initSchema(), after creating tables, check the current version and apply migrations sequentially: const v = sql.exec('SELECT version FROM schema_version').one()?.version ?? 0; if (v < 1) { sql.exec('ALTER TABLE run_wal ADD COLUMN tool_args_hash TEXT'); sql.exec('UPDATE schema_version SET version = 1'); }. Each new column addition becomes a numbered migration. SQLite supports ADD COLUMN without table recreation for non-destructive schema changes. Add a 'DO Schema Migration Pattern' section to the spec documenting this as required for all DO schema changes.

G-G14 HIGH naelao-analytics / Queue consumer

naelao-analytics Queue Consumer Has No DLQ — Analytics Batch Failures Permanently Drop Events Including Security Audit Logs

The Gap

The wrangler.jsonc queue consumers section shows { 'queue': 'naelao-analytics', 'max_batch_size': 100 } with no max_retries and no dead_letter_queue. CF Queues with no DLQ permanently delete messages after max retries (default 3). The analytics Worker writes 100-event batches to Analytics Engine. If Analytics Engine has a transient outage, the entire batch fails, retries 3 times, then disappears. Because Analytics Engine is the only place analytics data is written, lost analytics means lost billing audit trail, missing security event logs, and incomplete admin dashboard data — all of which have compliance implications under GDPR Article 30 (records of processing activities).

Required Fix

Add max_retries: 5, dead_letter_queue: 'naelao-analytics-dlq' to the naelao-analytics queue consumer in wrangler.jsonc. Create the naelao-analytics-dlq queue. Add a naelao-admin endpoint to replay analytics DLQ messages after Analytics Engine outages. For security events specifically, add a secondary KV write as a backup: await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(`sec-event:${event.timestamp}:${event.type}`, JSON.stringify(event), { expirationTtl: 86400 * 30 }) so security events are never lost even if Analytics Engine is down.

G-G15 HIGH naelao-mcp-hub / tool route resolution

resolveToolRoute() Always Looks Up 'unknown' AgentId Cache Key — Installed App Tools Return 404 for All Real Agents

The Gap

resolveToolRoute() fetches tool-schemas:${spaceId}:unknown — with the agentId hardcoded as the literal string 'unknown'. The GET /tools endpoint caches with cacheKey = `tool-schemas:${spaceId}:${agentId}` where agentId comes from the request query parameter. If two agents in the same space have different tool permissions, their schemas are cached at tool-schemas:{spaceId}:agentA and tool-schemas:{spaceId}:agentB respectively. resolveToolRoute always looks up tool-schemas:{spaceId}:unknown, which only exists if a tools discovery request was made with agentId=unknown. For all normal agents, route resolution finds no cache entry and returns null, causing every installed MCP app tool call to return 'Tool not found: {toolName}' with 404. Platform tools are unaffected; all installed App tools become unreachable.

Required Fix

resolveToolRoute() must accept the agentId parameter and look up tool-schemas:${spaceId}:${agentId}. The POST /execute endpoint already receives agentId in the request body — pass it through to resolveToolRoute. Add a fallback: if no cache entry exists for agentId, call the /tools endpoint internally to refresh before returning null. The /tools/invalidate cache-clearing endpoint must delete all agent-specific cache keys, not just the 'unknown' key — use list({ prefix: `tool-schemas:${spaceId}:` }) and delete all.

G-G16 HIGH file-manager skill / append_to_file

append_to_file Is O(n) in File Size — Reads and Rewrites the Entire File to Append a Few Bytes, Hits 30s CPU Limit on Large Files

The Gap

The append_to_file handler reads the full existing file with r2.get(), calls existing.text() (fully buffering in memory), concatenates new content as a string, then writes the entire result back. For a log file that accumulates 10,000 append operations during a long agent run, each append must read and rewrite the entire file. At 50KB per append (common for agent output logs), the 10,000th append reads and writes ~500MB — well beyond what a Worker can do in 30 seconds. The agent's todo.md maintenance pattern involves constant appends, making this a hot code path that degrades until it breaks.

Required Fix

For files intended for append operations, store content as versioned chunks in R2: workspace/logs/{filename}/{chunkIndex}.txt, with a manifest object listing all chunks. read_file assembles chunks on read. Alternatively, enforce MAX_APPEND_FILE_SIZE_MB (e.g., 10MB) and rotate the file when exceeded: rename file.txt to file.1.txt and start a fresh file.txt. Update the SKILL.md instruction: 'Use write_file with full updated content for small files (<1MB); use append_to_file only for write-only logging where you will never read back the full history.'

G-G17 HIGH SpaceTypeRegistryDO / global singleton

Global SpaceTypeRegistryDO Singleton Serializes All Space Creation at Scale — 1000 Concurrent Creates = 5 Seconds of Head-of-Line Blocking

The Gap

The SpaceTypeRegistryDO getSpaceType() method is called for every space creation. CF Durable Objects are single-threaded and process one request at a time. On KV cache miss (after 1-hour TTL expiry), all concurrent space creations hit the DO simultaneously and queue behind each other. For a SaaS platform with viral growth (1000 spaces created in an hour after a Product Hunt launch), all 1000 requests queue serially through a single DO. Each DO request takes ~5ms, so 1000 queued requests = 5 seconds of head-of-line blocking for the last request, violating the latency budget for space creation.

Required Fix

Implement a stale-while-revalidate pattern: set KV TTL to 24 hours but include a staleAt timestamp set to 1 hour in the cached value. Workers that read a stale-but-not-expired entry return it immediately and trigger background revalidation via ctx.waitUntil(). This means the DO is only hit by the first request per hour, not all requests on cache expiry. The per-typeId KV shard (space-type-manifest:{typeId}) should be the primary read path — the singleton DO becomes a cache-miss path only.

G-G18 HIGH naelao-triggers / webhook event routing

extractEventType() Referenced But Never Defined — All Webhook-Triggered Workflows Silently Dispatch Zero Agents

The Gap

The extractEventType(provider, payload) function is called in the triggers handler to determine which registered trigger to fire. This function is never defined in the spec. If stub-implemented as return 'unknown', then the query WHERE event_type = 'unknown' matches no registered triggers and zero workflows are dispatched for any webhook. Additionally, rawBody is correctly passed to verifySignature, but JSON.parse(rawBody) is called with no try/catch. For non-JSON webhooks (form-urlencoded Shopify, plain-text GitHub ping), JSON.parse throws, crashing the handler and returning 500 — causing the external service to retry indefinitely.

Required Fix

Implement extractEventType(provider, payload) with provider-specific mappings: for Stripe, return payload.type (e.g., 'invoice.paid'); for GitHub, return ${req.header('X-GitHub-Event')}.${payload.action} (e.g., 'push.created'). Add try/catch around JSON.parse with fallback to URLSearchParams: let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(rawBody); } catch { payload = Object.fromEntries(new URLSearchParams(rawBody)); }. Return 200 immediately when the payload cannot be parsed but was signature-verified to prevent infinite retries from the provider.

G-G19 HIGH ConcurrencyDO / alarm management

Concurrent checkAndReserve() Calls Each Invoke setAlarm() — Each Overwrites the Previous, Leaving Only One Alarm for N Concurrent Runs

The Gap

CF DO alarms support only one alarm at a time per DO. Calling setAlarm when an alarm is already scheduled overwrites it. In checkAndReserve, every new run reservation calls ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000). If a user starts 10 concurrent runs in rapid succession, the 10th setAlarm call overwrites all previous ones. If no new reservations arrive after the alarm fires, the remaining active runs never get their alarm-based cleanup triggered — stale run slots remain occupied, eventually blocking all new agent runs for that space until the slots naturally expire.

Required Fix

In checkAndReserve, only call setAlarm if no alarm is currently scheduled: const existingAlarm = await ctx.storage.getAlarm(); if (!existingAlarm) { await ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000); }. This prevents N concurrent reservations from overwriting each other's alarms. The alarm() handler must always reschedule if any active runs remain: check remaining count AFTER deleting stale runs (not before), then call setAlarm unconditionally if remaining > 0.

MEDIUM SEVERITY — 7 GAPS
G-G20 MEDIUM naelao-knowledge / Vectorize filter

Vectorize filter: { spaceId } Shorthand May Not Enforce Tenant Isolation — Silent Cross-Tenant Leak Depending on Binding Version

The Gap

The knowledge search calls env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query(embedding, { topK, filter: { spaceId }, returnMetadata: 'all' }). Cloudflare Vectorize's metadata filtering API requires filter expressions in the form { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } } rather than { spaceId: value } shorthand. If the plain object form is not supported by the Vectorize binding version in use, the filter is silently ignored — all vector neighbors are returned regardless of tenant. With thousands of spaces and millions of knowledge chunks, the first 5 results may include documents from a completely different space — a cross-tenant knowledge leak.

Required Fix

Use the explicit filter operator syntax: filter: { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } }. Add a post-query assertion: results.matches = results.matches.filter(m => m.metadata?.spaceId === spaceId). Add a test in Suite 04 (Space Isolation): upload a document to space A, query from space B, assert zero results are returned. This test must run against a real Vectorize index (not miniflare) in the integration test suite.

G-G21 MEDIUM naelao-notifications / idempotency

Notification Idempotency Keys Written With No TTL — Permanent KV Keys Block Legitimate Admin Resends Forever

The Gap

The notif_lock:{payload.id} KV write has no expirationTtl. CF KV with no TTL retains the key forever. For subscription lifecycle events (sub-cancelled-{spaceId}), if Stripe fires the same webhook twice, the second notification is correctly dropped. However, if an admin wants to manually re-trigger a notification (e.g., resend the 'credits exhausted' email after a bug fix), the permanent idempotency key blocks it. There is no admin endpoint to clear idempotency keys, making manual notification resends impossible without direct KV deletion.

Required Fix

Set a 7-day TTL on idempotency keys: await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.put(idempotencyKey, '1', { expirationTtl: 86400 * 7 }). This covers Stripe's maximum webhook retry window (72 hours) while allowing manual resends after a week. Add a naelao-admin endpoint DELETE /notifications/idempotency/{notificationId} that deletes the KV key, allowing admin-triggered resends. For subscription lifecycle events, use composite IDs including the Stripe event ID: sub-cancelled-{spaceId}-{event.id} so natural key expiry handles re-delivery without ever blocking legitimate resends.

G-G22 MEDIUM naelao-knowledge / GDPR compliance

Vectorize Vectors Not Deleted on Space Deprovisioning — GDPR Article 17 Right to Erasure Violated for Embedded Knowledge

The Gap

The DeprovisionWorkflow deletes R2 objects (Step C), calls spaceDO.purge() to cascade SpaceDO SQLite records (Step D), and cleans KV entries (Step E). It does not call Vectorize to delete embedded vectors. Knowledge document chunks are stored in Vectorize with IDs in the format {docId}:chunk:{index} and metadata containing spaceId. After deprovisioning, all vector data for the space remains in the shared Vectorize index indefinitely. Under GDPR Article 17, right to erasure requires deletion of all copies of personal data, including derived data — embeddings are derived from user-uploaded documents.

Required Fix

Add deprovisioning Step C2: query SpaceDO SQLite for all knowledge_docs records for the space to get all docId values, construct Vectorize IDs ({docId}:chunk:0, {docId}:chunk:1, ...) up to the stored chunk_count for each doc, and call NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(ids) in batches of 1000 (Vectorize API limit per call). For individual document deletion, DELETE /knowledge/{docId} must also call Vectorize deletion. Add a GDPR compliance note documenting that Analytics Engine data cannot be deleted by design — provide a DSAR API that returns all Analytics Engine data for a spaceId without deleting it.

G-G23 MEDIUM naelao-billing / deduct_space_credits concurrency

deduct_space_credits Uses PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE Pattern That Is Unsafe Outside a Durable Object — Spec Shows Both Safe and Unsafe Implementations Simultaneously

The Gap

The spec shows deduct_space_credits as a PostgreSQL stored function with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, which would be a race condition if implemented as a Worker-level function against any database other than a single-threaded DO: two concurrent calls both read balance=100 before either commits, both deduct 80, resulting in balance=-60. The spec simultaneously shows the correct safe SpaceDO pattern (DO single-threading provides atomicity) and the unsafe PostgreSQL pattern, creating ambiguity for the implementer. If a developer follows the PostgreSQL version without understanding the DO guarantee, they implement a double-spend vulnerability.

Required Fix

Explicitly document that deductCredits must only ever be a SpaceDO method and that the safety guarantee comes from DO single-threading. Add a comment: 'This method is safe from race conditions ONLY because it runs inside a Durable Object. If you move this logic into a Worker or serverless function, you MUST use a distributed lock or CAS operation.' Remove the PostgreSQL stored function version entirely to eliminate implementer ambiguity. Add an ESLint rule flagging any deductCredits-pattern outside of DO class files.

G-G24 MEDIUM wrangler.jsonc / broken JSONC

wrangler.jsonc Contains Malformed JSONC With Multi-Line // Comment and Invalid localConnectionString on DO Binding — wrangler deploy Fails to Parse

The Gap

The wrangler.jsonc queues section has no max_retries or dead_letter_queue for naelao-notifications. The hyperdrive section shows // No Hyperdrive binding on line 1 of a multi-line block, but // only comments out the remainder of that single line — subsequent lines containing { 'binding': 'SPACE_DO', 'localConnectionString': 'postgresql://...' } are NOT commented out. localConnectionString is not a valid wrangler property for DO bindings (it only exists for Hyperdrive). Some wrangler versions reject the file with a parse error; others include a duplicate SPACE_DO binding that conflicts with the existing DO binding of the same name.

Required Fix

Remove the entire malformed comment block and the localConnectionString entry — DO bindings only need name and class_name. Replace with a single-line comment: // Hyperdrive binding removed — see SpaceDO per-product DB architecture (§22). Add max_retries: 3 and dead_letter_queue: 'naelao-dlq' to the naelao-notifications consumer. Add max_retries: 3 to naelao-analytics consumer so failed analytics batches don't silently drop. Validate the complete wrangler.jsonc by running npx wrangler deploy --dry-run in CI before any test step.

G-G25 MEDIUM naelao-analytics / Analytics Engine schema

Analytics Engine Positional Fields Have No Schema Registry — Adding a Field Silently Shifts All Subsequent Fields and Corrupts Existing Queries

The Gap

Analytics Engine data points use positional indexing: TOKEN_USAGE_BY_MODEL queries blob4 as model and double5 as total_cost_usd. The mapping from position to field name is only defined in mapEventToDataPoint(). If a developer adds a new field at position 3 in the doubles array, double5 (total_cost_usd) shifts to double6 — all existing Analytics queries silently return wrong values for cost (likely zero). No schema versioning, no compile-time check, and query strings are raw SQL with no type safety.

Required Fix

Create a typed schema registry file analytics-schema.ts exporting named constants: export const TOKEN_USAGE = { doubles: { inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 1, cacheReadTokens: 2, cacheWriteTokens: 3, costUsd: 4, cacheHitRate: 5 }, blobs: { eventType: 0, userId: 1, agentId: 2, model: 3, runId: 4 } }. Use these constants in both mapEventToDataPoint() and all query strings. Add a CI test that generates a data point and verifies positional values match the schema registry. Version the schema (e.g. v1_ prefix on index names) so breaking changes require explicit migration.

G-G26 MEDIUM naelao-knowledge / search correctness

Knowledge Full-Text Search Uses LIKE '%term%' With No Index — O(n) Scan Over All Documents, Breaks at Scale

The Gap

The knowledge Worker's text search fallback (used when Vectorize is unavailable or for exact-match queries) executes SELECT * FROM knowledge_docs WHERE content LIKE '%{term}%' against SpaceDO SQLite. LIKE with a leading wildcard cannot use a B-tree index and performs a full table scan. At 10,000 knowledge documents per space (common for a large knowledge base), this is a 10,000-row full scan per search query inside a DO with strict CPU budget. Additionally, the term is interpolated directly into the LIKE pattern with no escaping — a search for '50%' would be interpreted as LIKE '%50%%' (SQL wildcard) not as literal '50%', returning incorrect results.

Required Fix

Enable SQLite FTS5 (full-text search) for the knowledge_docs table: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE knowledge_fts USING fts5(title, content, content='knowledge_docs', content_rowid='rowid'). Use FTS5 queries: SELECT * FROM knowledge_fts WHERE knowledge_fts MATCH ? — this is O(log n) with a full-text index. For the LIKE fallback, escape the search term before interpolation: const escaped = term.replace(/[%_\\]/g, c => `\\${c}`); then use LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' with the escaped term as a parameter. CF DO SQLite supports FTS5 as of the 2025-01-01 compatibility date.

Appendix G complete. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) + G (26) = 275 documented technical gaps with required fixes. The most systemic finding in this pass: the spec contains an incomplete PostgreSQL→SpaceDO migration with undefined variables at 56 call sites, 5 plpgsql stored functions that cannot execute in SQLite, and db.query('BEGIN') transaction syntax that has no valid CF DO equivalent. These are not isolated bugs — they represent an architectural schism that must be resolved before implementation begins, or every Worker that touches data will throw on first request.

Appendix H · Billing Provider Strategy

Lemon Squeezy Primary / Stripe Future — Provider-Agnostic Billing Architecture

The current spec hardcodes Stripe throughout the billing layer. Stripe is unavailable in many regions, requiring Lemon Squeezy as the primary provider with Stripe as a future addition. This appendix documents: (1) a provider-agnostic BillingProvider interface that makes both work without code duplication, (2) every place the spec must change to support Lemon Squeezy, and (3) a clean migration path for when Stripe becomes available.

Provider Abstraction Interface
// workers/naelao-billing/src/providers/types.ts
interface NormalizedBillingEvent {
  type:           'payment.success' | 'payment.failed' | 'subscription.created'
                | 'subscription.updated' | 'subscription.cancelled'
                | 'subscription.paused' | 'subscription.resumed' | 'refund.issued';
  provider:       'lemon_squeezy' | 'stripe';
  spaceId:        string;
  customerId:     string;
  subscriptionId: string | null;
  variantOrPriceId: string;
  amountCents:    number;   // always integer, always cents
  currency:       string;
  metadata:       Record<string, string>;
}

interface BillingProvider {
  verifyWebhook(rawBody: string, headers: Headers): Promise<boolean>;
  parseWebhookEvent(rawBody: string): NormalizedBillingEvent;
  createCheckout(params: CheckoutParams): Promise<{ url: string }>;
  getCustomerPortalUrl(subscriptionId: string): Promise<string>;
  cancelSubscription(subscriptionId: string): Promise<void>;
}

// Runtime provider selection — change BILLING_PROVIDER env var to switch
const provider: BillingProvider =
  env.BILLING_PROVIDER === 'stripe'
    ? new StripeProvider(env)
    : new LemonSqueezyProvider(env);
Lemon Squeezy Event Mapping
// Lemon Squeezy → Normalized
order_created                → payment.success
order_refunded               → refund.issued
subscription_created         → subscription.created
subscription_updated         → subscription.updated
subscription_cancelled       → subscription.cancelled
subscription_paused          → subscription.paused    ← no Stripe equiv
subscription_unpaused        → subscription.resumed
subscription_payment_success → payment.success
subscription_payment_failed  → payment.failed
subscription_payment_recovered → payment.success

// spaceId path in LS webhooks
event.meta.custom_data.spaceId           // order events
event.data.attributes.custom_data.spaceId // subscription events

// Amount parsing — always parse as integer
const amountCents = parseInt(event.data.attributes.total, 10); // NOT parseFloat
4 CRITICAL 8 HIGH 3 MEDIUM
CRITICAL SEVERITY — 4 GAPS
G-H01 CRITICAL naelao-billing / billing architecture

Entire Billing Layer Hardcoded to Stripe — No Provider Abstraction, Cannot Use Lemon Squeezy Without Full Rewrite

The Gap

Every billing touchpoint in the spec assumes Stripe: checkout sessions, webhooks, subscription lifecycle events, customer portal, RevenueCat for mobile, and the naelao-billing Worker's handler switch cases. There is no provider interface, no routing layer, and no abstraction between billing events and credit logic. Stripe is unavailable in many regions (including the builder's current country), making this architecture unbuildable today. Even once Stripe becomes available, migrating from Lemon Squeezy without a provider abstraction would require touching every billing-related call site across the codebase simultaneously — a high-risk big-bang migration.

Required Fix

Define a BillingProvider interface in a shared types package: interface BillingProvider { createCheckout(params: CheckoutParams): Promise<{ url: string }>; verifyWebhook(rawBody: string, headers: Headers): boolean; parseWebhookEvent(rawBody: string): NormalizedBillingEvent; getCustomerPortalUrl(customerId: string): Promise<string>; cancelSubscription(subscriptionId: string): Promise<void>; }. Implement LemonSqueezyProvider and StripeProvider separately, both implementing this interface. The naelao-billing Worker selects the provider at runtime from an environment variable: BILLING_PROVIDER = 'lemon_squeezy' | 'stripe'. All credit logic and SpaceDO writes use NormalizedBillingEvent only — never provider-specific types. This allows switching providers by changing one env var with zero code changes.

G-H02 CRITICAL naelao-billing / Lemon Squeezy webhooks

No Lemon Squeezy Webhook Signature Verification Implemented — All LS Webhooks Accepted Unauthenticated

The Gap

Lemon Squeezy uses a different webhook authentication scheme than Stripe. Rather than Stripe's timestamped t=...,v1=... format, Lemon Squeezy signs webhooks with a single X-Signature header containing a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using the webhook secret. The current verifySignature() function only implements GitHub (HMAC-SHA256 with X-Hub-Signature-256) and Stripe formats. Adding Lemon Squeezy without implementing its verification means all LS webhooks are either rejected (if the unknown-provider guard is fixed per G-F09) or accepted unauthenticated (if the current return true bug is still present), allowing anyone to forge payment confirmations and grant themselves unlimited credits.

Required Fix

Implement Lemon Squeezy webhook verification in verifySignature(): case 'lemon_squeezy': { const signature = headers.get('X-Signature'); if (!signature) return false; const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', new TextEncoder().encode(secret), { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['sign']); const expected = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, new TextEncoder().encode(rawBody)); const expectedHex = [...new Uint8Array(expected)].map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')).join(''); return timingSafeEqual(expectedHex, signature); } Store the LS webhook secret in naelao-credentials as LEMON_SQUEEZY_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Implement timingSafeEqual using crypto.subtle to avoid timing attacks.

G-H03 CRITICAL naelao-billing / Lemon Squeezy checkout

Lemon Squeezy Passes spaceId via custom_data Not Metadata — Current spaceId Resolution Path Breaks for LS Events

The Gap

The spec resolves spaceId from Stripe's invoice.metadata.spaceId or invoice.subscription_details.metadata.spaceId. Lemon Squeezy has no concept of subscription metadata or invoice metadata. Instead, custom data is passed on the checkout URL as custom_data[spaceId]=... and is returned in webhook payloads under data.meta.custom_data.spaceId (for order events) or data.attributes.custom_data.spaceId (for subscription events). If the existing spaceId resolver is used against a Lemon Squeezy webhook payload, it returns undefined for every event, subscription status updates silently no-op, and credit grants never happen.

Required Fix

In the NormalizedBillingEvent layer, the LemonSqueezyProvider.parseWebhookEvent() must extract spaceId from the correct LS path: const spaceId = payload.meta?.custom_data?.spaceId ?? payload.data?.attributes?.custom_data?.spaceId. When generating the Lemon Squeezy checkout URL, embed spaceId in the custom_data query parameter: checkoutUrl + '?checkout[custom][spaceId]=' + encodeURIComponent(spaceId). For subscriptions, also embed spaceId in the variant's custom_data via the LS API at checkout creation time so it survives all subscription lifecycle events. Add a unit test: parse a real LS order_created webhook fixture and assert spaceId is correctly extracted.

G-H04 CRITICAL naelao-billing / event taxonomy

Lemon Squeezy Event Names Are Entirely Different From Stripe — Billing Handler switch() Cases All Miss

The Gap

The naelao-billing webhook handler switch(event.type) has cases for Stripe event names: 'checkout.session.completed', 'invoice.payment_failed', 'customer.subscription.updated', 'customer.subscription.deleted'. Lemon Squeezy event names are completely different: 'order_created', 'order_refunded', 'subscription_created', 'subscription_updated', 'subscription_cancelled', 'subscription_resumed', 'subscription_expired', 'subscription_payment_success', 'subscription_payment_failed', 'subscription_payment_recovered'. None of the Stripe switch cases will match any Lemon Squeezy event, meaning every LS webhook falls through to the default case with no action — no credits are granted, no subscription states are updated, and no cancellations are processed.

Required Fix

The NormalizedBillingEvent interface must map all provider-specific events to a unified taxonomy: type NormalizedEventType = 'payment.success' | 'payment.failed' | 'subscription.created' | 'subscription.updated' | 'subscription.cancelled' | 'subscription.resumed' | 'refund.issued'. LemonSqueezyProvider maps: order_created → payment.success, subscription_created → subscription.created, subscription_cancelled → subscription.cancelled, subscription_payment_failed → payment.failed, subscription_payment_recovered → payment.success, order_refunded → refund.issued. StripeProvider maps its own events to the same taxonomy. The billing handler switch() operates only on NormalizedEventType — provider-specific event names never reach the handler logic.

HIGH SEVERITY — 8 GAPS
G-H05 HIGH naelao-billing / Lemon Squeezy checkout creation

Lemon Squeezy Uses Variant IDs Not Price IDs — All Product/Pricing Config Must Change

The Gap

The spec creates Stripe Checkout Sessions with price IDs from environment variables (STRIPE_PRICE_ID_PRO, STRIPE_PRICE_ID_ENTERPRISE). Lemon Squeezy uses a fundamentally different product model: a Store contains Products, each Product has Variants (equivalent to Stripe Prices). The checkout URL is generated per Variant, not per Session. Unlike Stripe, Lemon Squeezy does not support programmatic product or variant creation via API — all products, variants, and pricing must be created manually in the LS dashboard. There is no STRIPE_PRICE_ID equivalent to put in the env — the LS variant ID is a numeric integer found in the dashboard, not a generated ID.

Required Fix

Add Lemon Squeezy environment variables: LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID, LEMON_SQUEEZY_VARIANT_ID_STARTER, LEMON_SQUEEZY_VARIANT_ID_PRO, LEMON_SQUEEZY_VARIANT_ID_ENTERPRISE, LEMON_SQUEEZY_API_KEY. The LemonSqueezyProvider.createCheckout() generates a checkout URL via the LS API: POST https://api.lemonsqueezy.com/v1/checkouts with body { data: { type: 'checkouts', attributes: { checkout_options: { embed: false }, checkout_data: { custom: { spaceId } } }, relationships: { store: { data: { type: 'stores', id: STORE_ID } }, variant: { data: { type: 'variants', id: variantId } } } } }. Document in the pre-launch checklist that LS products must be manually created in the dashboard and variant IDs entered in the environment config before billing can be tested.

G-H06 HIGH naelao-billing / subscription lifecycle

Lemon Squeezy Subscription Pause and Resume Events Have No Handler — Paused Spaces Continue Serving Requests

The Gap

Lemon Squeezy supports subscription_paused and subscription_unpaused events (when a builder pauses their plan or when Lemon Squeezy pauses it due to failed payment). Stripe has no direct equivalent — a paused LS subscription is neither active nor cancelled. The current billing handler (designed for Stripe) has no case for these states. If a builder's LS subscription is paused due to payment failure, Naelao receives the subscription_paused webhook but takes no action — the space continues serving traffic, agents continue running, and credits continue being consumed with no payment. Similarly, subscription_resumed has no handler, so a builder who resumes their subscription after payment recovery is not reactivated.

Required Fix

Add 'subscription.paused' and 'subscription.resumed' to the NormalizedEventType union. In LemonSqueezyProvider, map: subscription_paused → subscription.paused, subscription_unpaused → subscription.resumed. In the billing handler, add cases: case 'subscription.paused': await spaceDO.setStatus('paused'); await notifyBuilder('subscription_paused', spaceId); break; case 'subscription.resumed': await spaceDO.setStatus('active'); await creditSubscriptionPeriod(event); break; Add 'paused' as a valid value in the space_status CHECK constraint in SpaceDO SQLite. Paused spaces should return HTTP 402 Payment Required on API calls with a { error: 'SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED', resumeUrl: customerPortalUrl } response body.

G-H07 HIGH naelao-billing / customer portal

Lemon Squeezy Customer Portal Is Hosted by LS With No Customization — naelao-billing Must Generate a Portal URL Per Customer, Not a Static Link

The Gap

Stripe's customer portal is configured once per account and builders access it via a session URL generated server-side. Lemon Squeezy's customer portal works differently: each subscription has a unique customer portal URL stored at data.attributes.urls.customer_portal in subscription webhook payloads. This URL must be stored at subscription creation time and retrieved when the builder requests access to their billing portal. The current spec has a single POST /api/billing/portal endpoint that creates a Stripe portal session — this does not work for Lemon Squeezy. Additionally, LS customer portal URLs can expire and must be refreshed via the subscriptions API.

Required Fix

At subscription_created time, store the customer portal URL in SpaceDO: spaceDO.exec('UPDATE spaces SET billing_portal_url = ? WHERE id = ?', payload.data.attributes.urls.customer_portal, spaceId). The POST /api/billing/portal endpoint for LS retrieves this stored URL: const { billing_portal_url } = spaceDO.exec('SELECT billing_portal_url FROM spaces WHERE id = ?', spaceId)[0]; return c.redirect(billing_portal_url). If the stored URL is older than 24 hours, refresh it via the LS API: GET https://api.lemonsqueezy.com/v1/subscriptions/{id} and re-store the updated URL. Add billing_portal_url TEXT to the spaces table schema.

G-H08 HIGH naelao-billing / credit amounts

Credit-Per-Payment Mapping Not Defined for Lemon Squeezy — No Equivalent of Stripe Price ID to Credit Amount Config

The Gap

The Stripe billing handler maps checkout.session.completed to a credit grant by reading the price ID from the event and looking up a PRICE_TO_CREDITS map (e.g., STRIPE_PRICE_ID_PRO → 10000 credits). Lemon Squeezy events contain a variant ID and the order total (in cents) but no server-side price ID mapping. The current credit mapping logic will find no match for any LS variant ID and grant zero credits. Additionally, Lemon Squeezy's order_created event contains the total_formatted field ($29.00) but the billing handler expects a numeric credit count — there is no specified conversion from dollar amount to credits.

Required Fix

Define a VARIANT_TO_CREDITS map in environment config: LEMON_SQUEEZY_VARIANT_CREDITS = '{"VARIANT_ID_STARTER":5000,"VARIANT_ID_PRO":10000,"VARIANT_ID_ENTERPRISE":50000}'. Parse this JSON string at Worker startup and store in module scope. In LemonSqueezyProvider.parseWebhookEvent(), extract the variant ID from event.data.attributes.first_order_item.variant_id (order events) or event.data.attributes.variant_id (subscription events). Map variant ID to credit amount: const credits = variantCreditsMap[variantId] ?? 0. If credits === 0 for a known payment, log a structured error to Analytics Engine and emit an ops alert — this prevents silent zero-credit grants on misconfiguration.

G-H09 HIGH naelao-billing / refund handling

Lemon Squeezy order_refunded Event Has No Handler — Refunded Users Retain Credits Indefinitely

The Gap

Lemon Squeezy fires an order_refunded event when a payment is refunded (either partial or full). The current billing handler has no case for refunds — neither for Stripe chargebacks (handled via dispute.created) nor for LS refunds. When a builder receives a refund on their credit purchase, Naelao takes no action and the builder retains all purchased credits. At scale this is exploitable: purchase credits, use them, request refund, receive refund, repeat. Additionally, Lemon Squeezy refunds can be partial (refund_amount < total_amount), meaning the credit deduction should be proportional, not full.

Required Fix

Map order_refunded → refund.issued in LemonSqueezyProvider. In the billing handler, handle refund.issued: const { refundAmountCents, totalAmountCents, variantId, spaceId } = event; const totalCredits = variantCreditsMap[variantId] ?? 0; const refundFraction = refundAmountCents / totalAmountCents; const creditsToDeduct = Math.ceil(totalCredits * refundFraction); await walletDO.deductCredits(spaceId, creditsToDeduct, 'refund'); If the wallet balance goes negative after deduction, set space status to 'suspended'. Notify the builder via the notifications queue. For Stripe, map charge.refunded with the same proportional logic.

G-H10 HIGH naelao-billing / provider switching

No Migration Path When Switching From Lemon Squeezy to Stripe — Existing Subscribers Cannot Be Transitioned Without Data Loss

The Gap

When Stripe becomes available and builders are migrated from Lemon Squeezy to Stripe, there is no mechanism to map existing LS subscription IDs to new Stripe subscription IDs or to transfer the billing portal link. Builders mid-subscription period would need to re-subscribe on Stripe, potentially being double-billed for the overlapping period. The SpaceDO schema has no field to store the payment provider identifier or customer ID per provider — only a single stripe_customer_id field implied by the spec's Stripe-only design. A builder with an active LS subscription has no path to Stripe without manual intervention.

Required Fix

Store provider-agnostic billing fields in SpaceDO: billing_provider TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'lemon_squeezy' CHECK(billing_provider IN ('lemon_squeezy','stripe')), billing_customer_id TEXT, billing_subscription_id TEXT, billing_variant_or_price_id TEXT, billing_portal_url TEXT, billing_status TEXT DEFAULT 'none'. At migration time, run a naelao-admin migration job that: (1) cancels each LS subscription at period end (not immediately), (2) emails the builder a Stripe checkout link for re-subscription at the same plan price, (3) grants prorated credits for the remaining LS subscription period, (4) updates billing_provider = 'stripe' once Stripe subscription is confirmed. The BILLING_PROVIDER env var controls which provider handles new checkouts during the migration window.

G-H11 HIGH naelao-billing / RevenueCat

RevenueCat Integration Is Mobile-Specific and Has No Lemon Squeezy Equivalent — Mobile Billing Is Undefined for LS Phase

The Gap

The spec integrates RevenueCat for mobile in-app purchases, which feeds into naelao-billing via a separate webhook endpoint. RevenueCat is a mobile purchase abstraction layer that normalizes Apple App Store and Google Play purchases. Lemon Squeezy is a web-based payment platform with no mobile SDK or App Store integration. During the Lemon Squeezy phase, any mobile billing (iOS/Android app purchases) has no defined path — the RevenueCat webhook handler that requires Stripe customer IDs will fail against LS-only accounts. The spec does not specify whether a mobile app exists or if mobile billing is deferred.

Required Fix

Defer RevenueCat integration entirely until the Stripe phase. Remove the RevenueCat webhook endpoint from the naelao-billing Worker's public routes during the Lemon Squeezy phase — return 503 Service Unavailable with body { error: 'MOBILE_BILLING_NOT_YET_AVAILABLE' }. In the pre-launch checklist, add a phase gate: 'RevenueCat integration — Stripe phase only.' When Stripe is activated, re-enable the RevenueCat endpoint and configure RevenueCat to use Stripe as the backend payment processor. Document that mobile billing requires Stripe and cannot be fulfilled via Lemon Squeezy.

G-H12 HIGH naelao-billing / test mode

Lemon Squeezy Test Mode Works Differently From Stripe — No Per-Request Test Mode Toggle, Separate API Keys Required

The Gap

Stripe test mode is toggled per API key: test keys (sk_test_...) hit the test API and are completely separate from live keys (sk_live_...). The spec uses STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in dev/staging and STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY in production. Lemon Squeezy test mode works at the store level: a store can be in test mode (toggle in the LS dashboard), not per API key. Both test and live stores use the same API key format. This means the spec's pattern of using different env var names for test vs live keys doesn't apply to LS — in staging vs production, the same LEMON_SQUEEZY_API_KEY env var is used but pointing to different store IDs. A misconfigured LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID in staging that points to the live store would process real payments in staging tests.

Required Fix

Use separate LS stores for test and production: LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID_TEST and LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID_PROD. The Worker selects the store ID based on the ENVIRONMENT env var: const storeId = env.ENVIRONMENT === 'production' ? env.LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID_PROD : env.LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID_TEST. Maintain separate variant IDs for test and production: test variants can be priced at $0.01 for easy testing. Maintain separate webhook secrets for each store in naelao-credentials. Add a canary assertion at Worker startup: if ENVIRONMENT === 'production' && LEMON_SQUEEZY_STORE_ID contains 'test', throw a configuration error to prevent accidental staging config in production.

MEDIUM SEVERITY — 3 GAPS
G-H13 MEDIUM naelao-billing / Lemon Squeezy webhook public route

Lemon Squeezy Webhook Endpoint Must Be Publicly Accessible and Auth-Middleware-Exempt — naelao-router Must Whitelist the Route

The Gap

Like the RevenueCat issue (G-G12), the Lemon Squeezy webhook must be publicly accessible for LS to POST to it. The naelao-router's auth middleware validates Bearer JWTs on all routes except /api/auth/*. A POST from Lemon Squeezy's servers carries an X-Signature header but no Authorization header — the JWT middleware will reject it with 401 before it reaches naelao-billing. The current spec only whitelists /api/auth/* from JWT validation, not /api/billing/webhook/*.

Required Fix

Add /api/billing/webhook to the auth middleware whitelist in naelao-router: const PUBLIC_PATHS = ['/api/auth/', '/api/billing/webhook/', '/api/portal/']. The billing webhook endpoint authenticates itself via the LS webhook signature verification (G-H02), not via JWT. Add a separate public route group in the router that skips JWT validation: router.use('/api/billing/webhook/*', (c, next) => next()). Log every unauthenticated request to /api/billing/webhook with the source IP for security monitoring — reject any request that fails signature verification with 401 and emit a security event to Analytics Engine.

G-H14 MEDIUM naelao-billing / Lemon Squeezy order total

Lemon Squeezy Reports Amounts in Cents as Strings Not Integers — Billing Arithmetic Uses Wrong Type, Credit Grants Are Off By 100x

The Gap

Lemon Squeezy order amounts are returned as strings in the format '2900' representing $29.00 (cents as string). The spec's credit grant logic uses event.amount_total / 100 (Stripe's pattern where amount_total is already an integer in cents). If a developer applies this same division to the LS amount string '2900', JavaScript coerces it to the number 2900 and divides by 100, giving 29 — which happens to be correct for the dollar amount but is meaningless when the expected value is a credit count from the variant map. The real risk is when amount-based credit formulas are used: a $29 order mistakenly treated as $0.29 (parsing '2900' as 29.00 and dividing by 100 again) would grant 1/100th of the expected credits.

Required Fix

In LemonSqueezyProvider, always parse LS amounts via parseInt(): const totalCents = parseInt(payload.data.attributes.total, 10); const refundCents = parseInt(payload.data.attributes.refund_amount, 10); Never use parseFloat() on LS amounts — floating point rounding on monetary values causes incorrect credit grants. The NormalizedBillingEvent must carry amounts as integer cents with explicit documentation: amountCents: number (integer, in cents). Add a unit test: LemonSqueezyProvider.parseWebhookEvent() for a $29.00 order returns amountCents === 2900 (not 29, not 0.29).

G-H15 MEDIUM naelao-billing / dual provider

No Billing Dashboard Aggregation Across Providers — Admin Revenue Reporting Breaks When Both LS and Stripe Are Active

The Gap

When both Lemon Squeezy and Stripe are active (e.g., during migration period or if some users are on LS and others on Stripe), the naelao-admin revenue dashboard queries Analytics Engine for billing events. If LS events and Stripe events are written to Analytics Engine with different blob1 (event_type) values (e.g., 'ls_payment_success' vs 'stripe_payment_success'), the dashboard's SUM(double1) WHERE blob1 = 'payment_success' query misses half the revenue. If both use the same event type string ('payment_success'), the provider is indistinguishable in Analytics Engine and provider-level reporting is impossible (e.g., 'how much revenue from LS vs Stripe this month').

Required Fix

Use the NormalizedEventType for blob1 ('payment.success', not provider-prefixed). Store the provider in a separate blob field: blob6 = billing_provider ('lemon_squeezy' | 'stripe'). The admin revenue query aggregates across both: SELECT SUM(double1) as total_cents FROM naelao_events WHERE blob1 = 'payment.success'. For provider breakdown: SELECT blob6 as provider, SUM(double1) as total_cents FROM naelao_events WHERE blob1 = 'payment.success' GROUP BY blob6. Update the Analytics Engine schema registry (G-F20) to include billing_provider at the reserved blob6 position.

Billing Rollout Phases
PhaseProviderAction
NowLemon SqueezyImplement BillingProvider interface + LemonSqueezyProvider. Set BILLING_PROVIDER=lemon_squeezy. Create products manually in LS dashboard. Configure webhooks at api.naelao.com/api/billing/webhook.
LaterStripe (added)Implement StripeProvider. Set BILLING_PROVIDER=stripe for new accounts. Keep LemonSqueezyProvider active for existing LS subscribers until period end. Run migration job to transition active LS subscriptions to Stripe with prorated credits.
OptionalBothRoute by account region: LS for regions where Stripe is unavailable, Stripe everywhere else. billing_provider field in SpaceDO tracks which provider owns each subscription.

Appendix H complete. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) + G (26) + H (15) = 290 documented technical gaps with required fixes.

Appendix I · Cross-Reference, Integration & Platform Gap Analysis

GAP-291 – GAP-324: Wrangler Config Mismatches, Broken Seams, CF Platform Violations

This appendix documents 34 new gaps discovered by cross-referencing every _BUILD_PLAN/prompts/ file against 28_wrangler_configs.md and against each other. The focus is on runtime failures that only manifest after deployment: missing wrangler bindings, broken inter-worker seams, Cloudflare platform constraints violated by the current prompt designs, and security holes in the auth/credit/artifact layers. None of these gaps were covered in Appendices A–H.

9 CRITICAL 17 HIGH 7 MEDIUM 1 LOW
CRITICAL SEVERITY — 9 GAPS
GAP-291 CRITICAL 25b_naelao_eval.md / 28_wrangler_configs.md

naelao-eval Wrangler Config Declares Wrong Binding (NAELAO_AGENTS) — All Five Real Bindings Are Missing

The Gap

The naelao-eval wrangler config in 28_wrangler_configs.md declares a single service binding: NAELAO_AGENTS -> naelao-agents. The actual eval worker (25b_naelao_eval.md) uses five completely different bindings: TOGETHER_AI_SERVICE (service binding to naelao-together-ai), ANALYTICS_SERVICE (service binding to naelao-analytics), R2_EVAL_RESULTS (R2Bucket), KV_EVAL_LOCK (KVNamespace), and the secrets ADMIN_SECRET, EVAL_SPACE_ID, MAX_EVAL_CONCURRENCY. None of these appear in the wrangler config. NAELAO_AGENTS, which does appear, is never referenced by the eval worker at all. At runtime every binding access throws: "Cannot read properties of undefined".

Required Fix

Replace the naelao-eval section in 28_wrangler_configs.md with the correct binding set: // wrangler.jsonc – naelao-eval { "services": [ { "binding": "TOGETHER_AI_SERVICE", "service": "naelao-together-ai" }, { "binding": "ANALYTICS_SERVICE", "service": "naelao-analytics" } ], "r2_buckets": [{ "binding": "R2_EVAL_RESULTS", "bucket_name": "naelao-eval-results" }], "kv_namespaces": [{ "binding": "KV_EVAL_LOCK", "id": "<KV_ID>" }], "vars": { "EVAL_SPACE_ID": "<space-id>", "MAX_EVAL_CONCURRENCY": "4" } } // Secrets (via wrangler secret put): ADMIN_SECRET // Remove the NAELAO_AGENTS service binding entirely.

GAP-292 CRITICAL 20_naelao_triggers.md / 28_wrangler_configs.md

naelao-triggers Wrangler Config Missing NAELAO_SPACE_DO Service Binding — SpaceDO Trigger Queries Always Fail

The Gap

The naelao-triggers wrangler config lists only a Queue producer binding (NAELAO_WORKFLOW_DISPATCH) and secrets. The triggers index.ts, at step 5 of its request handling flow, must "Query SpaceDO for registered triggers matching (provider, eventType, spaceId)". This requires a NAELAO_SPACE_DO DurableObjectNamespace binding pointing to the naelao-spaces worker. Without it, env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO is undefined and every inbound webhook that requires trigger lookup throws at runtime, making the entire trigger dispatch system non-functional.

Required Fix

Add the following to the naelao-triggers wrangler config in 28_wrangler_configs.md: // wrangler.jsonc – naelao-triggers (add to existing config) { "durable_objects": { "bindings": [ { "name": "NAELAO_SPACE_DO", "class_name": "SpaceDO", "script_name": "naelao-spaces" } ] } } In 20_naelao_triggers.md, add NAELAO_SPACE_DO: DurableObjectNamespace to the Env interface. The trigger lookup call becomes: const id = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName('space:' + spaceId); const stub = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(id); const res = await stub.fetch('/internal/triggers/match', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ provider, eventType }) });

GAP-293 CRITICAL 13f_local_tunnel.md

LocalTunnelDO /exec Uses Non-Existent Blocking Storage Poll — Synchronous Request/Response Pattern Is Broken

The Gap

The /exec route in LocalTunnelDO describes a "Wait for response via DO storage poll (use storage.get/waitForResponse pattern)". There is no blocking poll in Cloudflare Durable Objects storage. storage.get() is async but returns immediately with the current stored value — it does not block until a value appears. The DO cannot long-poll its own storage. The /exec handler will return immediately with undefined instead of waiting for the local agent to POST a response back. The entire synchronous tool-call bridge is non-functional.

Required Fix

Replace the storage-poll pattern with WebSocket hibernation inside the DO. The /exec handler upgrades the inbound request to a WebSocket, stores the pending call in SQLite, and suspends via hibernation. When the local agent POSTs the response to /exec/:callId/respond, the DO wakes, fetches the stored WebSocket tag, and sends the result down the socket. The caller receives it via the WebSocket client. // LocalTunnelDO – /exec handler const { 0: client, 1: server } = new WebSocketPair(); this.ctx.acceptWebSocket(server, ['exec:' + callId]); // store pending call in SQLite this.sql.exec('INSERT INTO pending_calls VALUES (?,?,?)', callId, JSON.stringify(payload), Date.now()); return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client }); // LocalTunnelDO – /exec/:callId/respond handler const sockets = this.ctx.getWebSockets('exec:' + callId); if (sockets[0]) { sockets[0].send(JSON.stringify(result)); sockets[0].close(); } this.sql.exec('DELETE FROM pending_calls WHERE id=?', callId);

GAP-294 CRITICAL 12_naelao_knowledge.md / 19_naelao_analytics.md / 28_wrangler_configs.md

Knowledge Indexing Jobs Sent to NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE — Consumed by Analytics Worker, Never Indexed

The Gap

The naelao-knowledge ingest handler enqueues messages of shape { type: 'knowledge_index', docId, spaceId, content, title, mimeType } to NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE. The wrangler config declares naelao-analytics as the sole consumer of that queue. The analytics worker expects MessageBatch<AnalyticsEvent> with fields event_type, space_id, agent_id, credits_used — it writes records to Analytics Engine and has no knowledge of chunking, embedding, or Vectorize. The analytics consumer will attempt to write the knowledge_index messages as analytics data points using wrong field names and silently produce garbage rows. Actual knowledge indexing (chunking → embedding → vectorize upsert) never happens. The knowledge base is permanently empty.

Required Fix

Create a dedicated queue for knowledge indexing. In 28_wrangler_configs.md add: // New queue in account queues config { "queue_name": "naelao-knowledge-queue", "dead_letter_queue": "naelao-knowledge-dlq", "max_retries": 3 } // wrangler.jsonc – naelao-knowledge: add consumer binding { "queues": { "consumers": [{ "queue": "naelao-knowledge-queue", "max_batch_size": 10, "max_retries": 3 }], "producers": [{ "binding": "NAELAO_KNOWLEDGE_QUEUE", "queue": "naelao-knowledge-queue" }] } } In 12_naelao_knowledge.md: change all env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE.send({ type: 'knowledge_index', ... }) to env.NAELAO_KNOWLEDGE_QUEUE.send(...). Implement the queue() consumer in the knowledge worker's default export to handle knowledge_index messages with chunking, embedding, and vectorize upsert. Remove knowledge_index message handling from any analytics consumer path.

GAP-295 CRITICAL 13a_agent_worker.md

naelao-agents Calls SPACES_SERVICE /internal/members/check — Route Does Not Exist in naelao-spaces

The Gap

The agent worker's /agents/run/start handler calls SPACES_SERVICE.fetch('/internal/members/check') with { userId, spaceId } expecting { isMember: boolean }. The naelao-spaces worker (07a_spaces_worker.md) defines only public REST routes under /v1/spaces/. There are no /internal/* routes defined anywhere in that worker. Every membership check returns 404. The agent worker treats a non-200 response as "not a member" and returns 403, making every single agent run fail at authorization before the agent DO is ever contacted.

Required Fix

Add an internal route to 07a_spaces_worker.md: // workers/naelao-spaces/src/index.ts app.post('/internal/members/check', async (c) => { const { userId, spaceId } = await c.req.json<{ userId: string; spaceId: string }>(); const id = c.env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName('space:' + spaceId); const stub = c.env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(id); const res = await stub.fetch('/members/check?userId=' + encodeURIComponent(userId)); const { isMember } = await res.json<{ isMember: boolean }>(); return c.json({ isMember }); }); Add the corresponding /members/check handler in SpaceDO (07b_SpaceDO.md) that queries: SELECT 1 FROM members WHERE space_id=? AND user_id=? AND status='active'

GAP-296 CRITICAL 27_naelao_artifact.md

wrapHtmlArtifact Uses document.write(atob(base64)) — Base64 Does Not Sanitize; Stored XSS via User HTML

The Gap

The sandbox.ts wrapHtmlArtifact function embeds user HTML as: '<script>document.write(atob("' + btoa(code) + '"))</script>'. Base64 encodes bytes but does not sanitize content. When the browser decodes and writes it, all user-supplied scripts, inline event handlers, and iframe srcdoc attributes execute in full. The CSP on the GET route declares script-src 'self', but document.write() injects inline script at parse time before CSP is evaluated on the injected DOM. If the artifact is served from the same origin as the application (not a sandboxed subdomain), this is a stored XSS allowing session hijacking and credential theft. The simple regex scan for process.env / require / eval is trivially bypassed with string splitting or Unicode escapes.

Required Fix
