After chunking and vectorizing a document, the knowledge worker calls: await spaceDO.query('INSERT INTO knowledge_docs ... VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,NOW())', [...]); This has three violations: (1) $1-style placeholders are PostgreSQL, not SQLite; (2) NOW() is PostgreSQL; (3) the spaceDO.query() call assumes a database-like interface on the SpaceDO stub, but SpaceDO exposes HTTP endpoints via fetch(), not a .query() method. The knowledge_docs record is never written, so document lists are empty and deletion/re-indexing operations have no metadata to work with. Every document ingested into the knowledge base is vectorized but has no accompanying metadata record.

Required Fix

Replace with an HTTP call to SpaceDO's knowledge management endpoint: const result = await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/knowledge/record', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ docId, spaceId, projectId, name, r2Path, chunkCount }) })); SpaceDO's /knowledge/record handler internally executes: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `INSERT INTO knowledge_docs (id, space_id, project_id, name, r2_path, chunk_count, created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,unixepoch('now')*1000)`, docId, spaceId, projectId, name, r2Path, chunkCount );

G-K28 HIGH §82 — Space Templates

space_templates Schema Contains Supabase RLS Policies, auth.users FK, and TIMESTAMPTZ — Crashes SpaceDO Initialization

The Gap

The space_templates and space_template_installs tables are declared with TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id), ON DELETE CASCADE with FK to auth.users, followed by ALTER TABLE space_templates ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and two CREATE POLICY statements using auth.uid(). SpaceDO's initSchema() calls this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(entireSchemaString). SQLite does not support TIMESTAMPTZ, auth.users FK references, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or CREATE POLICY. The entire schema initialization fails with a SQLite syntax error, crashing the DO and making every space that includes template functionality permanently uninitialized.

Required Fix

Remove all RLS policies, auth.users references, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and CREATE POLICY statements from the SpaceDO SQLite schema. Replace TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() with INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000). Replace UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) with TEXT NOT NULL. Enforce access control at the TypeScript method level in SpaceDO instead of database-level RLS: getTemplate(templateId: string, requestingSpaceId: string) { // Authorization check at the TypeScript level: if (!this.isAuthorized(requestingSpaceId)) throw new Error('Unauthorized'); return this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT * FROM space_templates WHERE id = ?', templateId); }

G-K29 HIGH §35 SandboxDO / §85 AssistantSandboxDO

node:path Module Used for Path Traversal Validation in SandboxDO — Not Available in CF Workers Runtime

The Gap

The path traversal prevention in SandboxDO and AssistantSandboxDO uses: import { resolve, normalize } from 'path'; The CF Workers runtime does not include the Node.js path module. The import throws ReferenceError: path is not defined at DO initialization, making the entire validateContainerPath() function non-functional. Without this validation, path traversal attacks (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) in container exec() calls are not blocked. Note: This issue was also identified in G-J04 from §25. This entry confirms the same vulnerability from a direct read of §35 and §85.

Required Fix

Replace import { resolve, normalize } from 'path' with a pure-JS WHATWG URL implementation: function validateContainerPath(agentPath: string): string { // Resolve against a fake base to handle relative paths and traversal const resolved = new URL(agentPath, 'file:///workspace/').pathname; if (!resolved.startsWith('/workspace/')) { throw new Error('Path traversal detected: ' + agentPath); } return resolved; } This uses the WHATWG URL API which is available in all CF Workers environments. No import needed.

G-K30 HIGH §45 — Platform Skills

Platform Skill SHA-256 Signing Uses Node.js crypto.createHash() — Not Available in CF Workers Runtime

The Gap

scripts/sign-platform-skills.ts uses: import { createHash } from 'crypto'; createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex'); This is the Node.js crypto module, not available in the CF Workers runtime. While the signing script runs in Node.js CI, the signature verification code runs inside Workers at skill load time. If the verification code also uses createHash, it will throw ReferenceError in the Worker. Any developer who ports the signing script to run in a Worker context hits the same error. Additionally, the verification code must use Web Crypto API for correctness in the CF Workers environment.

Required Fix

For verification code running in Workers, use the Web Crypto API: async function sha256Hex(content: string): Promise<string> { const hashBuffer = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(content)); return Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuffer)) .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')) .join(''); } The signing script (scripts/sign-platform-skills.ts) can remain Node.js as it runs in CI. Document this split clearly in the spec: "signing: Node.js CI only; verification: Web Crypto API in Workers."

G-K31 HIGH §82 — FinetuneJobDO

FinetuneJobDO Calls Together AI Directly, Bypassing SSRF Prevention Layer — And this.rootSpaceId Is Never Initialized

The Gap

FinetuneJobDO.alarm() calls: fetch('https://api.together.xyz/v1/fine-tunes/${jobId}') directly, bypassing the api-caller CF Worker which enforces SSRF prevention, URL allowlisting, and credential injection. The spec's security architecture (CVE-2026-26322) declares all outbound HTTP from agents must go through the SSRF-filtered api-caller. A compromised FinetuneJobDO (via a malformed jobId containing path traversal characters) could probe internal infrastructure. Additionally, this.rootSpaceId is never initialized in the shown FinetuneJobDO implementation, so any call to getProductDO(this.rootSpaceId, this.env) throws TypeError immediately.

Required Fix

Add https://api.together.xyz to an explicit allowlist checked at the DO level. Validate jobId against /^ft-[a-z0-9-]+$/ before interpolating into the URL. Initialize this.rootSpaceId from persistent storage: constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) { super(ctx, env); this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { this.rootSpaceId = await ctx.storage.get<string>('rootSpaceId') ?? ''; }); } On first POST /init: await ctx.storage.put('rootSpaceId', params.rootSpaceId); this.rootSpaceId = params.rootSpaceId;

G-K32 HIGH §82 — WorkflowRegistryDO

WorkflowRegistryDO.sweepSchedules() References this.spaceId Which Is Never Initialized — Every Scheduled Workflow Dispatch Creates a Workflow with spaceId=undefined

The Gap

sweepSchedules() calls: env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW.create({ id: '...', params: { spaceId: this.spaceId, workflowPath: wf.r2_path } }); WorkflowRegistryDO is instantiated with idFromName('wfreg:${spaceId}:global'), but this.spaceId is an instance property that is never set in the shown constructor or fetch() handler. It will be undefined at runtime. Every workflow cron dispatch creates a workflow instance with spaceId: undefined, causing the workflow's security check (spaceId validation: /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(spaceId)) to immediately throw, aborting all scheduled workflows on the platform.

Required Fix

Parse spaceId from the DO's own name string in the constructor: constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) { this.ctx = ctx; this.env = env; // Extract spaceId from the DO's own ID name: 'wfreg:{spaceId}:global' const nameParts = ctx.id.name?.split(':') ?? []; this.spaceId = nameParts[1] ?? ''; } Alternatively, persist spaceId on first /init call: await ctx.storage.put('spaceId', spaceId) and retrieve via ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { this.spaceId = await ctx.storage.get('spaceId') ?? ''; }).

G-K33 HIGH §05 AssistantDO — Sub-Agent Spawning

checkSubAgentStatus() Constructs AgentDO ID with Two Components — Misses projectId, Polls Wrong DO Instance

The Gap

checkSubAgentStatus() constructs the AgentDO ID as: env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName('${this.spaceId}:${threadId}') // two components But the AgentDO naming spec explicitly states the ID is: idFromName('${spaceId}:${projectId}:${threadId}') // three components The two-component ID resolves to a different DO instance than the one actually running the sub-agent. The GET http://agent/status call hits the wrong DO, which has no knowledge of the run and returns an empty/error response. Sub-agent completion is never detected, sub-agent results are never incorporated into the assistant's context, and sub_agents table rows remain status='running' forever, exhausting concurrency slots.

Required Fix

Store projectId alongside threadId in the sub_agents table when the sub-agent is spawned: INSERT INTO sub_agents (thread_id, project_id, parent_thread_id, status, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'running', unixepoch('now')*1000); In checkSubAgentStatus(), read back the stored projectId and use all three components: const sub = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'SELECT thread_id, project_id FROM sub_agents WHERE thread_id = ?', threadId )[0]; const agentDO = env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.get( env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName('${this.spaceId}:${sub.project_id}:${sub.thread_id}') );

G-K34 HIGH §05 AssistantDO — Slack Integration

AssistantDO Uses this.ctx.waitUntil() — waitUntil() Is on ExecutionContext, Not DurableObjectState — Slack Webhook Handler Crashes

The Gap

The Slack webhook handler calls: this.ctx.waitUntil(asyncDODispatch()); In a Durable Object, this.ctx is DurableObjectState, which does NOT have a waitUntil() method. waitUntil() is a method on ExecutionContext (the third argument ctx in Worker fetch handlers). Calling this.ctx.waitUntil() throws TypeError: this.ctx.waitUntil is not a function, meaning the Slack webhook handler crashes before ACKing Slack's 3-second requirement. Slack retries the webhook up to 3 times, and the DO processes duplicate messages — causing duplicate agent runs for every Slack message.

Required Fix

DurableObjectState does not expose waitUntil(). Restructure the Slack handler to respond immediately and then process asynchronously using DO's natural single-threaded model: async handleSlack(request: Request): Promise<Response> { const payload = await request.json(); // Persist the Slack event to SQLite for async processing this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'INSERT INTO slack_event_queue (event_id, payload, created_at) VALUES (?,?,unixepoch('now')*1000)', payload.event_id, JSON.stringify(payload) ); // Schedule immediate alarm to process it this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 100); return new Response('ok', { status: 200 }); // ACK Slack immediately }

G-K35 HIGH §72 — Mini-AGI Federated Query Loop

Mini-AGI executeFederatedQueryLoop() Synthesizes Answer Before Writing Audit Log — DO Eviction Between Steps Permanently Loses Mandatory Audit Trail

The Gap

executeFederatedQueryLoop() executes sequentially: (1) build secure query plan, (2) run Vectorize queries, (3) call Claude Opus synthesis (~800–1200ms), (4) call miniAgiDO.logQuery() for the mandatory audit log. Total wall-clock time: 2–5 seconds. If the DO is evicted between step 3 (answer synthesized) and step 4 (audit logged), the answer has already been sent to the user but the audit log is never written. For regulated industries (HR data, financial data), this missing audit trail is a compliance violation. The in-memory memoryContexts array containing sensitive HR/financial data is also silently lost with no recovery path.

Required Fix

Reverse the order to write-before-synthesize for audit integrity: // Step 1: Write preliminary audit entry BEFORE synthesis await miniAgiDO.logQuery({ queryId, status: 'in_progress', query: userQuery, timestamp: Date.now() }); // Step 2: Synthesize answer const answer = await claudeClient.messages.create({ ... }); // Step 3: Update audit entry with completed result await miniAgiDO.updateQueryLog({ queryId, status: 'complete', answer: answer.content }); This ensures the audit trail exists even if the DO is evicted mid-synthesis. The sweeper cleans up status='in_progress' entries older than 5 minutes.

G-K36 HIGH §43 — naelao-sweeper

Sweeper Enumerates Active Assistants via KV list() with No Pagination — All Spaces Beyond 1,000 Silently Skipped

The Gap

The sweeper's sweepAssistantHeartbeats task queries the active assistant list with: const { keys } = await env.PRODUCT_DB_REGISTRY.list({ prefix: 'assistant:' }); KV list() returns a maximum of 1,000 keys per call. Without cursor-based pagination, any platform with more than 1,000 active spaces silently skips their assistants during heartbeat sweeps. Skipped assistants miss their scheduled cron jobs, sub-agent status checks, and memory consolidation. The keys.truncated boolean flag from the KV response is not checked, so there is no indication that keys were missed.

Required Fix

Implement cursor pagination to process all spaces: let cursor: string | undefined; do { const result = await env.PRODUCT_DB_REGISTRY.list({ prefix: 'assistant:', limit: 1000, cursor }); for (const key of result.keys) { await processAssistantHeartbeat(key.name); } cursor = result.cursor; } while (!result.list_complete); Apply the same cursor pagination fix to all other KV list() calls in the sweeper (project heartbeats, space cleanup, etc.).

G-K37 HIGH §77 — Naelao Apps / §62 SpaceTypeRegistryDO

AppRegistryDO and SpaceTypeRegistryDO Are Global Singleton DOs — Single-Threaded Bottleneck Under Concurrent Platform Load

The Gap

AppRegistryDO uses idFromName('global-app-registry') and SpaceTypeRegistryDO uses idFromName('global-space-type-registry') — single DO instances serving all app installs and space type queries for the entire platform globally. Durable Objects are single-threaded. Every app install from any user anywhere in the world must be processed sequentially by this one DO. Under load (e.g., a popular app launch, a viral space type), all install requests queue up behind this single-threaded bottleneck, causing P99 latencies measured in seconds and timeout failures for concurrent installs. At 100+ concurrent installs/second, requests queue up faster than the DO can process them.

Required Fix

Shard the registry by a consistent hash of app_id or space_type_id. Use multiple AppRegistryDO instances: const shardId = parseInt(appId.slice(-2), 16) % 16; // 16 shards const registryDO = env.APP_REGISTRY_DO.get( env.APP_REGISTRY_DO.idFromName('app-registry-shard-' + shardId) ); Use KV to cache read-heavy operations (per-app install counts, manifests) with a 5-minute TTL. The DO only handles write operations (installs, publishes). Reads that don't require strong consistency should bypass the DO and read from KV cache directly.

G-K38 MEDIUM §22 — Artifacts Dynamic Worker Loader

wrapArtifactCode() Template Literal Injection — ${...} Expressions in User Code Are Expanded, Leaking Worker Environment Variables

The Gap

The HTML artifact wrapper uses: const html = \`${code.replace(/\`/g, '\`')}\`; The code replaces backticks but does NOT escape ${...} template literal expressions. An HTML artifact containing ${env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} or ${globalThis} will interpolate those values into the served HTML when the wrapper string is evaluated. The 27-pattern scanner blocks process.env. but not template literal interpolation of runtime globals. A malicious artifact author can craft content like ${''.constructor.constructor('return env')()} to exfiltrate Worker environment variables into the served HTML. Note: G-J10 identified the backtick interpolation XSS vector. This entry documents the additional ${...} expression expansion vector that remains even after backtick escaping.

Required Fix

Use JSON serialization instead of template literal embedding to safely include user code: // Before (vulnerable): const html = \`${code.replace(/\`/g, '\`')}\`; // After (safe): const html = JSON.stringify(code); // produces a quoted string literal with all special chars escaped Alternatively, store the artifact code in R2 and serve it via a separate GET /artifact/{id}/content endpoint with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none' headers. This separates the serving boundary from the wrapper execution context entirely.

G-K39 MEDIUM §24 naelao-workflows / AgentDO

NaelaoAgentDO ID Constructed from Three Unsanitized Components — Colon Collisions Between spaceId:projectId:threadId Can Point to Wrong DO

The Gap

NaelaoAgentDO is named idFromName('${spaceId}:${projectId}:${threadId}') with no separator escaping. If spaceId, projectId, or threadId ever contain colons (e.g., from legacy migration data or a validation gap), two different (spaceId, projectId, threadId) triples can produce the same concatenated string: spaceId='a:b', projectId='c', threadId='d' → 'a:b:c:d' spaceId='a', projectId='b:c', threadId='d' → 'a:b:c:d' Both point to the same DO, causing two different agent sessions to share the same SQLite WAL, message history, and execution state. While UUID format is validated for spaceId, it is not explicitly enforced for projectId and threadId in the shown validation code.

Required Fix

Validate all three components against UUID format (/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/) before constructing the DO ID: function makeAgentDOId(env: Env, spaceId: string, projectId: string, threadId: string): DurableObjectId { if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(spaceId)) throw new Error('Invalid spaceId'); if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(projectId)) throw new Error('Invalid projectId'); if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/.test(threadId)) throw new Error('Invalid threadId'); return env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(spaceId + ':' + projectId + ':' + threadId); } Document this constraint explicitly in the AgentDO naming spec section.

G-K40 MEDIUM §43 — naelao-sweeper DLQ

Sweeper Reads DLQ via CF REST API with Account-Level Token — Security Anti-Pattern; DLQ Should Use Consumer Binding

The Gap

The sweeper's sweepDeadLetterQueue task calls: fetch('https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${env.NAELAO_ACCOUNT_ID}/queues/naelao-dlq/messages', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + env.CF_API_TOKEN } }); This requires an account-level CF API token stored in Worker secrets. An account-level token grants full access to ALL CF resources in the account. Exposure of this secret (via a logging mistake, error message, or spec leak) allows complete account takeover. Additionally, this is not the intended pattern for DLQ consumption — CF Queues provides consumer bindings for exactly this purpose.

Required Fix

Declare naelao-dlq as a second Queue consumer binding in wrangler.jsonc for the sweeper Worker: [[queues.consumers]] queue = "naelao-dlq" binding = "NAELAO_DLQ" max_retries = 0 # DLQ — no further retries DLQ messages are automatically delivered to the consumer via the queue() handler. This eliminates the need for CF_API_TOKEN entirely. Remove CF_API_TOKEN from Worker secrets. Declare naelao-dlq as the dead_letter_queue for NAELAO_AGENT_QUEUE in its producer configuration.

G-K41 MEDIUM §82 — WorkflowRegistryDO

WorkflowRegistryDO sweepSchedules() Has No Idempotency Guard — Concurrent Sweeper Invocations Trigger Duplicate Workflow Runs

The Gap

sweepSchedules() queries workflows with next_run <= now, creates workflow instances, then updates next_run. If two sweeper cron invocations overlap (CF Cron is at-least-once), both reads may return the same set of due workflows before either updates next_run. Both instances then call env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW.create() for the same workflow, creating duplicate runs. CF Cron Triggers can fire multiple times within a given window if previous invocations haven't completed, making this race practically guaranteed on any busy platform.

Required Fix

Use SQLite atomic compare-and-swap in sweepSchedules(): // Atomic: only update if next_run hasn't changed since we read it const result = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'UPDATE workflows SET next_run = ?, last_run = ? WHERE id = ? AND next_run = ?', nextRunTime, Date.now(), workflowId, readNextRun ); // Only create workflow instance if we won the CAS if (result.rowsWritten > 0) { await env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW.create({ id: workflowRunId, params: { spaceId: this.spaceId, workflowPath: wf.r2_path } }); } This ensures at most one workflow instance per schedule cycle regardless of concurrent invocations.

G-K42 MEDIUM §79 — naelao-notifications VAPI

VAPI Voice Call Configuration Hardcodes Deprecated claude-3-haiku-20240307 Model ID — Voice Alerts Will Fail or Route to Stale Model

The Gap

The VAPI phone call configuration hardcodes "model": "claude-3-haiku-20240307" (an April 2024 model). The current model lineup uses claude-haiku-4-5 (consistent with the rest of the spec). The old model ID will either be rejected by Anthropic's API (returning a model-not-found error), causing all critical voice alert calls to silently fail, or it will route to a deprecated model that may be phased out without notice. During a critical production incident, failed voice alerts can delay emergency response.

Required Fix

Replace "model": "claude-3-haiku-20240307" with "model": "claude-haiku-4-5" in the VAPI assistant configuration. Consider reading the model name from an environment variable: assistantConfig.model.model = env.VAPI_MODEL ?? 'claude-haiku-4-5'; This allows model updates without a code deployment. Audit all hardcoded model IDs in the spec for the same staleness issue and replace them with environment variable references where appropriate.

G-K43 MEDIUM §84 — SpaceDO

SpaceDO.spaceId and rootSpaceId Are In-Memory Instance Properties Never Persisted — Lost on Every DO Restart

The Gap

this.spaceId and this.rootSpaceId are used throughout SpaceDO methods (auth check, sub-space hierarchy queries, credential lookups) but are never persisted or re-initialized from storage in the shown code. After any DO eviction/restart, both properties are undefined, causing every method that references them to throw or return incorrect results. The auth cache's recursive CTE query WHERE id = $1 would use undefined as the spaceId, returning empty results and denying access to all space members. This bug silently breaks the entire SpaceDO on every cold start.

Required Fix

In the SpaceDO constructor, initialize from persistent storage: constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) { this.ctx = ctx; this.env = env; this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { const stored = await ctx.storage.get<string>('spaceId'); if (stored) this.spaceId = stored; }); } On first POST /init: await ctx.storage.put('spaceId', spaceId); this.spaceId = spaceId; As a resilient fallback, extract spaceId from the DO's own name string: const match = ctx.id.name?.match(/^space:([0-9a-f-]+)/); if (match) this.spaceId = match[1];

G-K44 MEDIUM §43 — naelao-sweeper

Sweeper Abandoned Agent Run Detection Uses NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' PostgreSQL Syntax — Query Throws on Every Sweeper Tick

The Gap

The sweeper queries for abandoned runs with: WHERE status = 'running' AND updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' This is PostgreSQL syntax. SpaceDO SQLite uses datetime('now', '-10 minutes') or (unixepoch('now') - 600) * 1000 for millisecond timestamps. The query throws a SQLite syntax error on every sweeper tick. Abandoned agent runs are never cleaned up: their concurrency slots remain held in ConcurrencyDO, eventually exhausting the per-user concurrency limit and blocking all new agent runs for the affected space.

Required Fix

Replace PostgreSQL INTERVAL syntax with SQLite equivalents based on the timestamp column type: For INTEGER millisecond timestamps (recommended): WHERE status = 'running' AND updated_at < (unixepoch('now') - 600) * 1000 For TEXT ISO timestamps: WHERE status = 'running' AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-10 minutes') Apply the same fix to all other INTERVAL-based queries in the sweeper, including the stale project detection and memory consolidation sweep queries.

G-K45 MEDIUM §56 — Bootstrap Autopilot Activation

Bootstrap Autopilot Activation Has No Atomic Check-and-Transition — Concurrent Checkers Can Trigger Duplicate Activations

The Gap

The autopilot activation flow checks five independent criteria (R2 file count, annotation quality score, FinetuneJobDO status, admin approval flag, eval pass rate) and transitions the space to autopilot mode. These checks are not atomic — two concurrent processes (the daily QA standup fiber and the fine-tune completion handler) can both check all five criteria, both find them met, and both trigger the activation sequence. This may result in duplicate activate_autopilot workflow instances, duplicate notifications to the space admin, and duplicate billing state transitions that double-charge the space for activation.

Required Fix

Add a single-writer atomicity guard using SpaceDO SQLite: const result = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `UPDATE spaces SET status = 'autopilot', activated_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'bootstrap'`, Date.now(), this.spaceId ); if (result.rowsWritten === 0) { return; // Another process already activated, or not in bootstrap state — skip } // Only one process reaches here — proceed with activation steps await triggerActivationWorkflow(); await sendActivationNotification();

G-K46 MEDIUM §78 — naelao-admin / §09 wrangler.jsonc

naelao-dlq Dead Letter Queue Binding Not Declared in wrangler.jsonc — Failed Messages Are Discarded, Not Routed to DLQ

The Gap

The sweeper's dead letter queue processing calls the CF REST API with queues/naelao-dlq/messages. The wrangler.jsonc bindings section shows Queue bindings for NAELAO_AGENT_QUEUE, NAELAO_ANALYTICS_QUEUE, and NAELAO_NOTIFICATIONS_QUEUE but does not declare naelao-dlq as a dead letter queue or as a consumer binding. Without dead_letter_queue: 'naelao-dlq' configured on the source queue's settings, failed messages are discarded after max_retries exhaustion. The entire DLQ infrastructure (sweeper sweep, admin retry endpoint) operates on a queue that never receives any messages.

Required Fix

In wrangler.jsonc, add the DLQ declaration to the NAELAO_AGENT_QUEUE configuration: [[queues.producers]] binding = "NAELAO_AGENT_QUEUE" queue = "naelao-agent-queue" dead_letter_queue = "naelao-dlq" // ADD THIS Create the naelao-dlq queue resource in the CF dashboard or via Terraform. Declare a consumer binding for the sweeper Worker: [[queues.consumers]] queue = "naelao-dlq" binding = "NAELAO_DLQ" max_retries = 0

G-K47 MEDIUM §63 — naelao-portal-router / §09 wrangler.jsonc

Portal Router References Undeclared env.PORTAL_ROUTES KV Binding — Deploy-Time Binding Error on All Portal Routing Calls

The Gap

The portal Worker routing logic references env.PORTAL_ROUTES as a separate KV binding in some code paths. The wrangler.jsonc only declares three KV namespaces (NAELAO_CONFIG_KV, NAELAO_CIRCUIT_KV, NAELAO_ARTIFACT_KV). PORTAL_ROUTES is not declared. Workers deployed without a declared binding throw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined when accessing env.PORTAL_ROUTES, causing all portal routing to fail with 500 errors. The spec appears to have been partially refactored to use NAELAO_CONFIG_KV for slug lookups but left residual PORTAL_ROUTES references in other code paths.

Required Fix

Audit all env.PORTAL_ROUTES references in the portal router and replace them with env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV. Use a consistent key prefix for portal slug entries: portal-slug:${slug} → spaceId. Remove PORTAL_ROUTES from any wrangler configurations where it may appear. Add a wrangler.jsonc validation step to CI that ensures all env.* references in Worker source files have corresponding binding declarations.

G-K48 MEDIUM §81 — naelao-categorizer

Categorizer Cron Has No Idempotency — CF At-Least-Once Cron Fires Cause Double-Categorization and Doubled LLM Costs

The Gap

The categorizer's scheduled() handler queries up to 50 stale projects and immediately calls LLM for each. If CF Cron fires the handler twice within the same minute (at-least-once delivery), all 50 projects are double-categorized: two LLM calls per project, two UPDATE projects SET tags = ... calls (second overwrites first with potentially different LLM output), and doubled LLM costs. The stale-project query filters on last_categorized_at < NOW() - 24 hours, but both invocations run before any last_categorized_at update, so both see the same 50 projects.

Required Fix

Use a SpaceDO SQLite advisory lock at the start of scheduled(): try { this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `INSERT INTO categorizer_locks (id, locked_at) VALUES ('singleton', unixepoch('now')*1000)` ); } catch { return; // Lock exists — another instance is running, skip this invocation } try { await runCategorizationBatch(); } finally { this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`DELETE FROM categorizer_locks WHERE id = 'singleton'`); } The sweeper cleans up stale locks (handles crashes): DELETE FROM categorizer_locks WHERE locked_at < unixepoch('now')*1000 - 300000.

G-K49 MEDIUM §81 — naelao-feedback Daily Standup

Daily Standup Clears Feedback Log After LLM Analysis — Feedback Written During 2-Second LLM Call Window Is Permanently Lost

The Gap

The daily standup fiber reads feedback-log.jsonl from R2, analyzes it with Claude (~2 seconds), writes improvement-addendum.md, then clears the log with env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(logKey, ''). Any feedback event written to the log after the get() read but before the final put('') clear is permanently lost (overwritten with empty string). The window spans two LLM calls (~2 seconds each), making this race practically certain to occur in active production spaces with regular feedback activity.

Required Fix

Use a timestamp-based snapshot approach instead of in-place clear: // Rename current log to a dated snapshot before processing const snapshotKey = logKey.replace('.jsonl', '-' + Date.now() + '.jsonl'); const existing = await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.get(logKey); if (existing) { const content = await existing.text(); await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(snapshotKey, content); await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.delete(logKey); // New feedback writes to fresh logKey } // Process the snapshot file — new feedback goes to the fresh logKey await analyzeAndWriteAddendum(snapshotKey); // Sweeper archives or deletes old snapshot files after 30 days

G-K50 MEDIUM §22 — Artifacts wrapArtifactCode() React

React Artifact Wrapper Imports from react-dom/server — Unavailable in Tier 2 Worker Isolate Without npm Resolution

The Gap

The React artifact wrapper generates code that starts with: import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server'; CF Workers do not have React in their default runtime; react-dom/server must be bundled or resolved at deploy time. The Dynamic Worker Loader uses Tier 2 (V8 isolate, no npm resolution) for artifacts. Without Tier 3 (NPM) resolution, the import statement fails with a module-not-found error when the artifact Worker is executed, making all React artifacts non-functional. Note: G-J06 identified that the React type generates renderToString(<App />) with JSX. This gap confirms the additional problem: even without JSX, the react-dom/server import itself fails in Tier 2.

Required Fix

Route React artifacts through the Tier 3 (NPM) execution tier in the execution ladder. Update TOOL_TIERS['render_artifact'] to 'npm' instead of 'isolate' for React-type artifacts. Alternatively, add React and React-DOM to the DW Loader's pre-bundled module list (bundled at deploy time, not resolved at runtime). Document clearly in the spec that React artifacts require Tier 3 dispatch and cannot run in the default Tier 2 isolate environment.

G-K51 LOW §30 — ConcurrencyDO

ConcurrencyDO Tier Limits Are Hardcoded Constants — Cannot Update Without Worker Redeployment; Subscription Upgrades Not Wired to ConcurrencyDO

The Gap

const TIER_LIMITS = { free: 1, maker: 3, pro: 10, team: 25, enterprise: 100 } is a module-level constant in ConcurrencyDO. Changing a tier limit requires redeploying all Workers. Additionally, the billing_tier is read from the DO's local config table (initialized to 'free') and is never updated when a space upgrades their subscription. A space that upgrades from Free to Pro continues to be limited to 1 concurrent run until the DO is explicitly updated. The spec shows no endpoint or mechanism for the billing Worker to notify ConcurrencyDO of tier changes after subscription upgrades.

Required Fix

Store tier limits in KV (NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get('tier-limits')) with a 1-hour in-memory cache in the DO: const tierConfig = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get('tier-limits', { type: 'json' }) ?? { free: 1, maker: 3, pro: 10, team: 25, enterprise: 100 }; const limit = tierConfig[currentTier]; Add a POST /update-tier endpoint to ConcurrencyDO called by the billing Worker on subscription changes: app.post('/update-tier', async (c) => { const { spaceId, newTier } = await c.req.json(); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('UPDATE config SET value = ? WHERE key = ?', newTier, 'billing_tier'); return c.json({ success: true }); });

Appendix K complete. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) + G (26) + H (15) + I (34) + J (20) + K (51) = 395 documented technical gaps with required fixes.

Appendix L — Additional Technical Gap Audit (Fourth Pass)

Fourth-pass gap analysis targeting previously unread spec sections: §security (credential allowlist, skill signing), §container-system (SandboxDO fields), §schema (global SpaceDO schema), §file-manager-skill (append locking), §agentdo-api (human-in-the-loop), §mcp-hub (tool resolution), §naelao-triggers (webhook verification), §space-type-versioning (canary function scope), §naelao-apps-registry (AppRegistryDO), §registry-finetune-dos (FinetuneJobDO alarm), §execution-ladder-spec (Browser Worker, Tier 1 locking), §agent-env-declaration (Enterprise tier config), §operator-shell-slots (postMessage security). This pass identified 23 new gaps: 13 CRITICAL, 9 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM.

G-L01 CRITICAL §security — naelao-credentials

SSRF Allowlist Check Uses endsWith() — evilgithub.com Passes as github.com

The Gap

The credential injection layer validates outbound URLs against an allowlist using: parsedUrl.hostname.endsWith(d) // where d = 'github.com', 'api.openai.com', etc. This check incorrectly matches any hostname ending in a whitelisted string. An attacker-controlled host such as evilgithub.com passes for d='github.com', and evilapi.openai.com passes for d='openai.com'. Any agent or tool call with a crafted URL can route requests — including requests that carry injected API credentials — to an attacker-controlled server, exfiltrating every secret injected into the request.

Required Fix

Replace endsWith(d) with a proper domain-boundary check: function matchesDomain(hostname: string, allowed: string): boolean { return hostname === allowed || hostname.endsWith('.' + allowed); } This requires either an exact match (github.com) or a dot-separated subdomain (api.github.com), rejecting evilgithub.com. Apply the same fix to every allowlist check in the naelao-credentials credential injection path and the api-caller SSRF filter. Add a unit test suite specifically for the allowlist matching logic.

G-L02 CRITICAL §container-system — SandboxDO

sandboxRef Cached In-Memory Is Null After DO Hibernation — All Container exec() Calls Return 503

The Gap

private sandboxRef: SandboxStub | null = null is a class field populated once and cached. The DO uses WebSocket hibernation, which destroys the entire class instance between messages. After any hibernation cycle, ensureRunning() reads container_status = 'running' from SQLite and returns 'already_running' without re-calling getSandbox(). As a result, this.sandboxRef remains null for the remainder of the session and every subsequent exec() call throws a null-dereference TypeError, returning 503. Note: The same in-memory stub pattern was documented for §25 SandboxDO (G-J03) and §85 AssistantSandboxDO (G-K05). This instance is in the separate §container-system section.

Required Fix

Remove the cached sandboxRef field entirely. At the start of every request handler, call getSandbox() fresh: async exec(params: ExecParams): Promise<ExecResult> { const sandboxRef = await this.env.CONTAINERS.getSandbox(this.sandboxId); // cheap, idempotent if (!sandboxRef) throw new ContainerNotRunningError(); return await sandboxRef.exec(params); } getSandbox() is a cheap stub lookup, not a container creation. Never cache DO stubs or Worker Service Binding stubs across potential hibernation boundaries.

G-L03 CRITICAL §container-system — SandboxDO

lastCommandAt Resets to 0 After Hibernation — Container Stopped Immediately on Every Alarm Tick

The Gap

private lastCommandAt = 0 is an in-memory field updated on each exec() call. After any DO hibernation this field resets to 0. The alarm handler evaluates Date.now() - this.lastCommandAt >= IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS; with lastCommandAt = 0, this difference equals the Unix epoch age and is always enormous, so every alarm fires an immediate container termination even if the user issued a command 30 seconds before hibernation.

Required Fix

Persist lastCommandAt to DO SQLite on every exec() call: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO container_state (key, value) VALUES ('last_command_at', ?)`, Date.now().toString() ); In alarm(), read it back before evaluating idle timeout: const rows = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT value FROM container_state WHERE key = ?', 'last_command_at')]; const lastCommandAt = rows[0] ? parseInt(rows[0].value) : Date.now(); if (Date.now() - lastCommandAt >= this.idleTimeoutMs) { await this.stopContainer(); }

G-L04 CRITICAL §container-system — LocalTunnelDO

LocalTunnelDO.grants Array Is In-Memory and Never Persisted — All Permissions Lost on Hibernation, Permanent 403

The Gap

grants: LocalPermissionGrant[] = [] is a plain class field populated by grantPermission() but never written to SQLite. After any hibernation cycle the array is empty, and checkPermission() always returns false, causing every subsequent tool call to return 403. The spec provides no mechanism for the client to automatically re-grant permissions after a hibernation — the agent loop silently fails on all local PC tool calls until the entire session is manually restarted.

Required Fix

Persist grants to a local_tunnel_grants SQLite table on every grantPermission() call: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO local_tunnel_grants (tool_name, path_prefix, granted_at) VALUES (?,?,unixepoch('now')*1000)`, grant.toolName, grant.pathPrefix ); In checkPermission(), query SQLite directly: const rows = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `SELECT 1 FROM local_tunnel_grants WHERE tool_name = ? AND ? LIKE path_prefix || '%'`, toolName, requestedPath )]; return rows.length > 0;

G-L05 HIGH §container-system — LocalTunnelDO

pendingCalls Map and WebSocket Ref Destroyed on Hibernation — In-Flight RPC Responses Silently Dropped

The Gap

pendingCalls: Map<string, {resolve, reject, timer}> and the localAgentWs WebSocket reference are both in-memory fields. The DO uses WebSocket hibernation which destroys both on every hibernation event. When the local PC sends a response to an in-flight RPC call, webSocketMessage() calls this.pendingCalls.get(callId) and finds nothing, silently dropping the response. The original awaiting Promise in the agent loop hangs until a 30-second timeout — and that setTimeout callback is also destroyed on hibernation, so it never fires either. Note: G-K04 documented the pendingCalls Map issue in §40 LocalTunnelDO. This extends the finding to include the WebSocket reference loss, which means the DO also cannot re-issue the in-flight call after wake.

Required Fix

Replace the in-memory pendingCalls Map with a persistent SQLite table (as described in G-K04). Additionally, persist the WebSocket session identity to SQLite on webSocketOpen. In webSocketMessage, reconstruct response routing from SQLite state rather than in-memory Maps. For timeouts, use ctx.storage.setAlarm() rather than setTimeout() — alarms survive hibernation and fire reliably after wake.

G-L06 HIGH §security — Platform Skills

Skill Signature Verification Reads from KV — 60-Second Eventual Consistency Allows Revoked Skills to Execute

The Gap

Platform skill signatures are written to NAELAO_CONFIG_KV on publish and read from KV on every skill invocation for HMAC verification. KV has up to 60-second eventual consistency lag between global PoPs. A skill whose signing key is revoked (due to a discovered vulnerability in the skill code) continues to pass signature verification for up to 60 seconds after revocation. During a security incident requiring immediate skill disablement, this 60-second window is unacceptable for a platform where skills execute arbitrary code in sandboxed containers.

Required Fix

Store the authoritative skill signature and revocation state in a SkillRegistryDO (strongly consistent). On skill invocation, verify against the DO: const sigResult = await skillRegistryDO.fetch(new Request('http://skill/verify', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ skillId, signature }) })); KV may be used as a read-through cache with a short TTL (5 seconds max) and a mandatory DO fallback on miss or cache expiry. This bounds the revocation propagation lag to 5 seconds instead of 60.

G-L07 CRITICAL §schema — Global SpaceDO Schema

Global Schema Uses gen_random_uuid() as Column Default — no such function Error Crashes Schema Init for Every Space

The Gap

Multiple core tables in the global SpaceDO schema declare: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() This is a PostgreSQL function. SQLite has no gen_random_uuid() built-in. When SpaceDO's initSchema() runs this CREATE TABLE statement, SQLite throws: 'no such function: gen_random_uuid'. Schema initialization fails entirely, preventing the DO from functioning. This affects every space on the platform — the global schema must be fixed before any space can be created or used.

Required Fix

Replace all DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() with DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))) for inline UUID generation in SQLite: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(16)))) Alternatively, generate UUIDs explicitly in application code using crypto.randomUUID() and insert them explicitly rather than relying on a column default. Apply this fix to ALL tables in the global schema that use gen_random_uuid() as a default value.

G-L08 CRITICAL §schema — Global SpaceDO Schema

Global Schema Declares TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() — Every INSERT Using Default Stores NULL, Breaking All Time-Based Logic

The Gap

Columns throughout the global SpaceDO schema are declared: created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() SQLite treats TIMESTAMPTZ as NUMERIC affinity but has no NOW() function. Every INSERT that relies on the DEFAULT clause will either throw ('no such function: NOW') or store NULL. With NULL in created_at and updated_at, all heartbeat logic, TTL cleanup, abandoned-run detection, and time-based queries across the platform produce incorrect results or errors.

Required Fix

Replace all TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() with INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch('now') * 1000) for millisecond-precision epoch timestamps. Update all timestamp comparisons to use epoch arithmetic: WHERE created_at > (unixepoch('now') - 3600) * 1000 Apply consistently to all timestamp columns in the global schema and any section-specific schema definitions.

G-L09 HIGH §schema — Global SpaceDO Schema

JSONB Column Type Declared in SQLite Schema — Missing NOT NULL Constraints and Broken Type Contract

The Gap

Multiple columns are declared with PostgreSQL's JSONB type: settings JSONB DEFAULT '{}' metrics JSONB skills JSONB DEFAULT '[]' SQLite ignores unknown type names and treats them with NUMERIC affinity, so no JSON binary encoding occurs. The absence of NOT NULL on metrics means any INSERT omitting that column stores NULL, breaking any code that calls JSON_extract() or parses the column value. ORM tools and query builders that inspect declared column types will also reject or mishandle the schema.

Required Fix

Declare all JSON columns as TEXT with explicit NOT NULL and a valid default: settings TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' metrics TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' skills TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' Optionally add a CHECK constraint: settings TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' CHECK(json_valid(settings)) Apply to all JSONB columns throughout the global schema and any section-specific schema definitions.

G-L10 CRITICAL §schema — Global SpaceDO Schema

Foreign Keys Reference auth.users(id) — Supabase-Internal Table Does Not Exist in CF DO SQLite

The Gap

Multiple tables in the global SpaceDO schema include: user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE owner_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) The auth schema and auth.users table are Supabase-internal. They do not exist in CF Durable Object SQLite. SQLite may silently accept these FK declarations but the referenced table is absent, making FK enforcement impossible. Schema migration tooling that validates FK targets will also fail, blocking any automated schema management.

Required Fix

Remove all REFERENCES auth.users(id) foreign key declarations. User identity validation must happen at the application code level — verify JWTs and check the authenticated userId in TypeScript before executing any SQL that modifies user-owned data. If a local user record is needed, define a space_members table explicitly in the SpaceDO schema and reference that instead of auth.users.

G-L11 CRITICAL §schema — Global SpaceDO Schema

ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY Statements in Global Schema — Syntax Error Crashes All Space Init

The Gap

The global SpaceDO schema includes multiple statements like: ALTER TABLE spaces ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY "Users can only see their own spaces" ON spaces FOR SELECT ...; ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY "Project access" ON projects FOR ALL ...; SQLite has no ROW LEVEL SECURITY feature. These statements raise a syntax error when initSchema() executes the schema string, aborting initialization entirely. No space can be created or used until fixed. This is a platform-wide initialization failure. Note: G-K28 documented RLS policies in the space_templates schema. This gap covers the same issue in the global core schema tables (spaces, projects, and more).

Required Fix

Remove ALL ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY statements from every SQLite schema definition. Multi-tenant row isolation must be enforced at the TypeScript layer by always parameterising queries with the verified spaceId: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT * FROM projects WHERE space_id = ? AND id = ?', this.spaceId, projectId) Never rely on database-level RLS for multi-tenancy in CF DO SQLite.

G-L12 CRITICAL §agentdo-api — Human-in-the-Loop

Human Approval Awaiting In-Memory Promise Lost on DO Hibernation — Agent Loop Permanently Stuck

The Gap

The AgentDO human-in-the-loop flow stores approval callbacks in an in-memory Map: private pendingApprovals = new Map<string, { resolve: (v: boolean) => void, reject: (e: Error) => void }>(); When the agent pauses for human approval, it awaits a Promise whose resolver lives in this Map. CF DOs hibernate after a short period of inactivity — especially likely during human review which can take minutes or hours. After hibernation the Map is empty. The subsequent POST /approval/:id/decide call finds no entry and the resolve callback is gone forever. The original await never resumes; the agent is permanently stuck consuming a concurrency slot with no way to recover.

Required Fix

Replace in-memory approval tracking with persistent SQLite state: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_approvals ( approval_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now')*1000) ); On /approval/:id/decide: UPDATE status in SQLite then call ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 100) to wake the DO. In the agent loop's next iteration (triggered by the alarm), query pending_approvals for decided approvals and resume. This makes approval state durable across any number of hibernation cycles.

G-L13 CRITICAL §naelao-triggers — Webhook Ingress

Webhook Signature Verification Returns true Unconditionally for All Non-GitHub Providers — Complete Auth Bypass

The Gap

The webhook ingress handler calls verifySignature(provider, headers, body). The implementation only performs HMAC validation when provider === 'github'. For Stripe, Linear, custom webhooks, and all other providers, the function returns true unconditionally: if (provider === 'github') { /* HMAC check */ return valid; } return true; // every other provider accepted without verification Any attacker who discovers a webhook URL can POST arbitrary payloads that trigger agent workflows for Stripe charge events, Linear issue updates, or custom triggers — completely bypassing authentication. This enables arbitrary agent execution on behalf of any space that has registered non-GitHub webhooks.

Required Fix

Default to false (reject) and implement per-provider HMAC verification for each supported provider: switch (provider) { case 'github': return verifyGithubSignature(headers, body, secret); case 'stripe': return verifyStripeSignature(headers, body, secret); // 'Stripe-Signature' header case 'linear': return verifyLinearSignature(headers, body, secret); default: return false; // Reject unknown providers } For custom providers, require an explicit HMAC token in the registered webhook configuration. Store per-provider webhook secrets in naelao-credentials (encrypted), looked up by (spaceId, webhookId) before verification.

G-L14 CRITICAL §space-type-versioning — Canary Rollouts

processCanaryRollouts Is a Module-Level Function That References this.ctx — TypeError on Every Invocation

The Gap

processCanaryRollouts is declared as: async function processCanaryRollouts(env: Env) { const staleVersions = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT ...')]; // ... } This is a standalone module-level function, not a class method. In CF Workers (strict mode), this inside a regular function is undefined. Calling processCanaryRollouts(env) immediately throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ctx'). Even if the alarm/cron wiring were fixed (G-K26), the function itself crashes on invocation and the canary advancement logic never executes.

Required Fix

Convert processCanaryRollouts into a method of the DO class that manages canary rollouts: class SpaceTypeRegistryDO { async processCanaryRollouts(): Promise<void> { const staleVersions = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT ...')]; // advancement logic } async alarm(): Promise<void> { await this.processCanaryRollouts(); } } Alternatively, pass ctx as an explicit parameter: async function processCanaryRollouts(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env).

G-L15 CRITICAL §naelao-apps-registry — AppRegistryDO

AppRegistryDO.handleInstall Uses db.query() with $N PostgreSQL Placeholders — All App Installs Fail

The Gap

AppRegistryDO.handleInstall executes: await db.query( 'INSERT INTO app_installations (id, space_id, app_id, installed_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)', [installId, spaceId, appId, new Date().toISOString()] ); Both db.query() and $1/$2 positional parameters are PostgreSQL syntax. CF DO SQLite requires this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...params) with ? placeholders. This INSERT fails with a SQLite syntax error on every app install attempt. No app installations are ever recorded. The app ecosystem — installs, listing installed apps, and uninstalls — is entirely non-functional. The same $N pattern recurs in handleList and handleUninstall.

Required Fix

Replace all db.query(sql, [...params]) with this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql_with_?, ...params): this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'INSERT INTO app_installations (id, space_id, app_id, installed_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?)', installId, spaceId, appId, Date.now() ); Replace new Date().toISOString() with Date.now() (integer epoch ms) for timestamp consistency with the rest of the schema. Apply to all db.query() calls in handleList (SELECT) and handleUninstall (DELETE) as well.

G-L16 CRITICAL §registry-finetune-dos — FinetuneJobDO

FinetuneJobDO.alarm() Uses db.query() with $N Placeholders and NOW() — All Fine-Tune Jobs Permanently Stuck in 'running'

The Gap

The FinetuneJobDO alarm handler polls Together AI for completion then updates the job record: await db.query( 'UPDATE fine_tune_jobs SET status = $1, result_model = $2, completed_at = NOW() WHERE job_id = $3', [status, resultModel, jobId] ); db.query(), $N placeholders, and NOW() are all PostgreSQL syntax. CF DO SQLite requires this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() with ? and datetime('now'). This UPDATE throws on every alarm invocation. All fine-tune jobs are permanently stuck with status = 'running', users never see their trained models, and the alarm continues re-firing indefinitely. Note: G-K31 documented FinetuneJobDO's SSRF bypass. This gap covers the separate db.query syntax error in the alarm's status update path.

Required Fix

Replace with DO SQLite syntax: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `UPDATE fine_tune_jobs SET status = ?, result_model = ?, completed_at = unixepoch('now')*1000 WHERE job_id = ?`, status, resultModel, jobId ); Also audit WorkflowRegistryDO.handleRegister and handleList which use the same db.query() pattern. Apply the same fix throughout all DO methods in the registry-finetune-dos section.

G-L17 HIGH §file-manager-skill — append_to_file

append_to_file Skips the Advisory File Lock — Concurrent Appends Silently Corrupt File Contents

The Gap

The file manager skill's write_file handler correctly acquires an advisory lock via projectDO.fetch('/acquire-lock') before modifying R2 content. However, append_to_file does NOT acquire the lock: it directly reads the R2 object, concatenates the new content, and writes it back without any lock or ETag check. Two concurrent appends to the same file will both read the same original content and each write back only their own addition — one of the two appended entries is silently discarded.

Required Fix

Apply the same advisory lock pattern used by write_file: const lock = await projectDO.fetch(new Request('http://project/acquire-lock', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ path: params.path, sessionId }) })); try { const existing = await env.R2.get(r2Key); const newContent = (existing ? await existing.text() : '') + params.content; await env.R2.put(r2Key, newContent); } finally { await projectDO.fetch(new Request('http://project/release-lock', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ path: params.path, sessionId }) })); }

G-L18 HIGH §execution-ladder-spec — Browser Worker

Buffer.from(screenshot).toString('base64') Uses Node.js Buffer — Not Available in CF Workers

The Gap

The Browser Worker (Tier 4/5) returns screenshots by calling: const base64 = Buffer.from(screenshot).toString('base64'); Buffer is a Node.js global. In CF Workers, Buffer is not available in the standard runtime. Even with the nodejs_compat compatibility flag, Buffer in the Workers environment is an incomplete polyfill that does not support all .from() overloads reliably. If screenshot is a Uint8Array from Puppeteer's page.screenshot(), this call throws ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined and the screenshot action returns an error instead of an image.

Required Fix

Use the Web platform API instead: function uint8ArrayToBase64(bytes: Uint8Array): string { let binary = ''; for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) { binary += String.fromCharCode(bytes[i]); } return btoa(binary); } const base64 = uint8ArrayToBase64(new Uint8Array(screenshot)); For large screenshots (>1 MB), process in 8192-byte chunks to avoid stack overflow from String.fromCharCode spread: chunk the Uint8Array and concatenate the results before calling btoa().

G-L19 HIGH §mcp-hub — Tool Resolution

resolveToolRoute() Hardcodes agentId='unknown' in KV Cache Lookup — All Agent-Specific Tools Never Found

The Gap

The MCP hub caches tool schemas in KV under the key tool-schemas:${spaceId}:${agentId}. However, resolveToolRoute() performs the lookup with: const cached = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get('tool-schemas:${spaceId}:unknown'); The agentId is hardcoded as the literal string 'unknown'. Tools registered for a specific agent (e.g., tool-schemas:abc-123:agent-456) are never found because the lookup uses tool-schemas:abc-123:unknown. The resolution falls through to the "tool not found" error path for every tool call, making the entire MCP tool routing system non-functional for any tool registered against a specific agent ID.

Required Fix

Pass the authenticated agentId from the validated JWT into resolveToolRoute(): async resolveToolRoute(spaceId: string, agentId: string, toolName: string) { const cacheKey = `tool-schemas:${spaceId}:${agentId}`; const cached = await env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get(cacheKey, { type: 'json' }); // ... } Ensure the agentId used at write time (tool registration) matches the agentId used at read time (tool resolution). For space-wide tools accessible to all agents, use a consistent space-scoped key like tool-schemas:${spaceId}:global at both read and write.

G-L20 HIGH §agent-env-declaration — Enterprise Containers

idleTimeoutMs = -1 for Enterprise Tier Stored In-Memory — Resets to 1 Hour After Hibernation, Enterprise Containers Shut Down

The Gap

The DO constructor reads the space tier and sets: if (tier === 'enterprise') this.idleTimeoutMs = -1; // Never time out this.idleTimeoutMs is a plain instance field that resets to the class default (60 * 60 * 1000 = 1 hour) on any DO hibernation. After hibernation, the alarm handler uses the reset value rather than -1. Enterprise containers that should never idle-out are terminated after 1 hour of post-hibernation activity, violating the Enterprise tier entitlement. This is invisible to users — containers disappear silently.

Required Fix

Store the tier (or derived idleTimeoutMs) in DO SQLite and rehydrate on every wake: ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { const rows = [...ctx.storage.sql.exec('SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = ?', 'billing_tier')]; const tier = rows[0]?.value ?? 'free'; this.idleTimeoutMs = tier === 'enterprise' ? -1 : 60 * 60 * 1000; }); On first POST /init: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO config (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)', 'billing_tier', tier).

G-L21 HIGH §execution-ladder-spec — Tier 1 Workspace

Tier 1 write_file Bypasses Advisory Lock — Parallel Tier 1 Writes Race and Corrupt Files

The Gap

The Tier 1 workspace tool handler (executeWorkspaceTool in the Tier 1 isolate path) calls: await env.R2.put(key, content); directly, without acquiring the advisory lock from the projectDO lock table. The lock is only acquired via the Tier 3+ MCP hub code path. Two concurrent Tier 1 write_file calls to the same path — common when an agent issues multiple file writes in a parallel tool call batch — will race, with the second write silently overwriting the first with no error reported to either caller.

Required Fix

Extract lock acquisition into a shared writeFileSafe() helper used by ALL file write paths regardless of execution tier: async function writeFileSafe(env: Env, projectDO: DurableObjectStub, r2Key: string, content: string) { await projectDO.fetch(new Request('http://project/acquire-lock', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ path: r2Key }) })); try { await env.R2.put(r2Key, content); } finally { await projectDO.fetch(new Request('http://project/release-lock', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ path: r2Key }) })); } } Alternatively, consolidate all write paths through the MCP hub layer to ensure locking is always applied.

G-L22 HIGH §operator-shell-slots — Shell postMessage

WRITE_LEARNING postMessage Handler Accepts Arbitrary Key/Value from Any Iframe — Storage Flooding and Instruction Injection

The Gap

The operator shell processes postMessage events from embedded App iframes: if (msg.type === 'WRITE_LEARNING') { await uiInstructionsDO.writeLearning(msg.key, msg.value); } There is no validation of msg.key against an allowlist, no maximum length on msg.value, no rate limiting, and event.origin is not verified. A malicious or compromised App iframe can: (1) flood the DO with arbitrary key/value pairs causing unbounded storage growth and cost; (2) overwrite system-level shell instruction keys that control agent behavior; (3) inject malicious content into the operator's UI learning state. Any document in the operator's browser (not just registered Apps) can send this message.

Required Fix

Add three layers of defense: window.addEventListener('message', (event) => { // 1. Verify origin if (event.origin !== registeredAppOrigin) return; const msg = event.data; if (msg.type !== 'WRITE_LEARNING') return; // 2. Validate key against allowlist const ALLOWED_KEYS = ['theme-pref', 'layout-pref', 'shortcut-pref']; if (!ALLOWED_KEYS.includes(msg.key)) return; // 3. Enforce value length if (typeof msg.value !== 'string' || msg.value.length > 512) return; await uiInstructionsDO.writeLearning(msg.key, msg.value); }); Add KV-based rate limiting: max 10 WRITE_LEARNING writes per App per minute.

G-L23 MEDIUM §operator-shell-slots — Shell Personalization

Per-User Personalization Injected in Iframe src URL Hash — Leaks Email and Plan Tier to Browser History

The Gap

The operator shell injects per-user personalization (theme, locale, userId, email, planTier) into the embedded App iframe's src URL as a hash fragment: iframeEl.src = appUrl + '#' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ theme, locale, userId, email, planTier })); URL hashes appear in browser history (visible to any browser extension with tabs permission), can be captured by browser sync services, and may be reflected server-side if the App does server-side rendering of the hash. Sensitive user attributes (email address, plan tier, userId) are unnecessarily exposed in a URL that is visible outside the JavaScript execution context.

Required Fix

Remove personalization from the URL entirely. Load the iframe with a neutral URL and send personalization after load via postMessage with a verified target origin: iframeEl.src = appUrl; // No hash fragment iframeEl.addEventListener('load', () => { iframeEl.contentWindow?.postMessage( { type: 'INIT_PERSONALIZATION', theme, locale, userId, planTier }, new URL(appUrl).origin // verified target origin ); }); This keeps all personalization data within the JavaScript execution boundary and out of URLs.

Appendix L complete. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) + G (26) + H (15) + I (34) + J (20) + K (51) + L (23) = 418 documented technical gaps with required fixes.

Appendix M — Final Technical Gap Audit (Fifth Pass)

Fifth and final pass covering all remaining spec sections: §28 naelao-threads (WebSocket upgrade detection, SSE waitUntil, undefined db), §30 pricing/billing (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, PostgreSQL syntax), §naelao-os createSpace (use-before-declaration), §space-type-registry-appendix (missing settled column, undefined db in settleEarnings), §naelao-spaces-deep (duplicate const declarations causing SyntaxError, COUNT::int cast, NOW()+INTERVAL invite logic), §workflow-examples (SSRF on sourceUrl, GET with body, external fetch), §remoteloop + §remoteloop-appendix (dynamic binding undefined, TTL insufficient), §appendix-custom-dos (CartDO token loss, provisioner errors swallowed, admin db artifacts), §agentpress (truncateMiddle reverse order, StreamingXMLParser hibernation, Orchestrator timeout), §56 analytics (ClickHouse SQL dialect errors, index2 never populated), §observability (silent writeDataPoint failures), §space-type-sites (external fetch), §file-manager-skill-spec (path-stripping offset). This pass identified 31 new gaps: 10 CRITICAL, 12 HIGH, 7 MEDIUM, 2 LOW.

G-M01 CRITICAL §28 — naelao-threads

WebSocket Upgrade Detection Reads URL Query Param Instead of Upgrade Header — All WebSocket Clients Silently Downgraded to SSE

The Gap

openStreamConnection() decides whether to open a WebSocket vs SSE stream with: url.searchParams.get('upgrade') === 'websocket' The WebSocket protocol upgrade is signaled by the Upgrade: websocket HTTP header, not a query-string parameter. This condition is always false — no client sends an ?upgrade= param by default. All WebSocket connection requests are silently downgraded to SSE with no error, and the WebSocket code path is dead code that can never be reached.

Required Fix

Replace the URL-param check with the correct header check: request.headers.get('Upgrade')?.toLowerCase() === 'websocket' Then return the WebSocket upgrade response: const [client, server] = Object.values(new WebSocketPair()); server.accept(); return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client }); The SSE path remains the fallback for any non-upgrade request.

G-M02 CRITICAL §28 — naelao-threads

SSE Background Writer Started with void async IIFE and No waitUntil — Stream Killed After First Chunk

The Gap

createSSEStream() spawns the streaming delivery loop as: void (async () => { for await (const chunk of stream) { writer.write(...); } })() In CF Workers, the runtime terminates the isolate as soon as the Response is returned; any in-flight promise not registered with ctx.waitUntil() is torn down. The SSE stream is cut short mid-delivery — typically after the first chunk — with no error surfaced to the client. The user sees a partial agent response that silently stops.

Required Fix

Pass the async IIFE promise to ctx.waitUntil() on the ExecutionContext: const streamPromise = (async () => { for await (const chunk of stream) { writer.write(...); } writer.close(); })(); ctx.waitUntil(streamPromise); The ExecutionContext (third argument to the Worker fetch handler) must be threaded down from the top-level handler to createSSEStream(). Do NOT call waitUntil on DurableObjectState — that method does not exist on this.ctx in a DO.

G-M03 CRITICAL §28 — naelao-threads

createThread() and getMessages() Reference Undefined db Variable — ReferenceError on Every Call

The Gap

createThread() calls await db.from('projects').select(...) and await db.from('threads').insert(...). getMessages() calls await db.from('messages').select(...). The variable db is never declared in the naelao-threads Worker — it is a Supabase client artifact left over from the PostgreSQL migration. The spaceDO Service Binding is correctly obtained just lines earlier but then ignored. Every call to createThread() or getMessages() throws ReferenceError: db is not defined, making thread creation and message retrieval completely non-functional.

Required Fix

Remove all db.* calls. Use the already-obtained spaceDO Service Binding for all reads and writes: const result = await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('https://do/threads', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ sql: 'INSERT INTO threads (id, space_id, title, created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?)', params: [id, spaceId, title, Date.now()] }) })); Replace all $N placeholders with ? and ensure every route handler uses spaceDO.fetch() not db.*.

G-M04 CRITICAL §30 — Pricing / handleTokenUsage

handleTokenUsage() Uses BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK Manual Transactions — No-Op or Parse Error in DO SQLite

The Gap

The billing handler calls await db.query('BEGIN'), await db.query('COMMIT'), and in the catch block await db.query('ROLLBACK'). DO SQLite (this.ctx.storage.sql.exec()) does not support explicit transaction control statements — each exec() call is automatically atomic and single-threaded within the DO. Sending 'BEGIN' as a standalone SQL statement is either a no-op or causes a parse error; the catch block's ROLLBACK then triggers a second error, leaving the handler in an unrecoverable state with partial billing data written.

Required Fix

Remove all BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK calls. To achieve multi-statement atomicity, combine all related DML statements into a single this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() call as a semicolon-separated string. The DO's single-threaded model guarantees that no other request can interleave with a single exec() call. Replace all $1/$N placeholders with ? and replace NOW() with Date.now() passed as a parameter.

G-M05 CRITICAL §30 — Pricing / handleTokenUsage

handleTokenUsage() Uses NOW(), DATE_TRUNC(), and $N PostgreSQL Syntax — All Billing Queries Fail

The Gap

The billing queries in handleTokenUsage() use NOW(), DATE_TRUNC('month', NOW()), and $1/$2/$N positional placeholders. None of these are valid SQLite constructs. NOW() is undefined, DATE_TRUNC does not exist, and $N causes a parse error. The billing system fails to record any token usage, silently allowing unlimited consumption and producing no revenue data. This affects the pricing section's billing logic, which is distinct from the naelao-billing Worker covered in G-K02.

Required Fix

Replace NOW() with a JavaScript Date value passed as a ? parameter: const now = new Date().toISOString(). Replace DATE_TRUNC('month', NOW()) with strftime('%Y-%m', 'now') for monthly bucketing in SQLite. Replace all $N placeholders with ?. Example: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( `INSERT INTO token_usage (space_id, model, tokens, month, created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,strftime('%Y-%m','now'),?)`, spaceId, model, tokens, now );

G-M06 CRITICAL §naelao-os — createSpace()

createSpace() Calls spaceDO.query() Before spaceDO Is Declared — ReferenceError: Cannot Access spaceDO Before Initialization

The Gap

In createSpace(), the line await spaceDO.query('INSERT INTO spaces ... VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5)', [...]) appears before the const spaceDO = ... declaration. JavaScript const does not hoist; accessing a const before its declaration throws ReferenceError: Cannot access 'spaceDO' before initialization. Additionally, spaceDO.query() is not a valid Service Binding method — Service Bindings only expose fetch(). Every space creation call throws immediately and no space is ever created.

Required Fix

Move the const spaceDO declaration to before its first use. Replace spaceDO.query() with spaceDO.fetch(): const spaceDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName('space:' + spaceId)); await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('https://do/init', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, name, ownerId, spaceType, planTier }) })); Replace all $N PostgreSQL placeholders with ? in any SQL executed within the SpaceDO's init handler.

G-M07 CRITICAL §space-type-registry-appendix — SpaceTypeRegistryDO

settleEarnings() Queries Non-Existent settled Column — SQLite: no such column Crashes Every Earnings Settlement

The Gap

settleEarnings() runs: SELECT ... FROM registry_earnings WHERE settled = 0 UPDATE registry_earnings SET settled = 1 WHERE id = ? The registry_earnings table DDL defines only id, app_id, author_id, amount, and created_at — there is no settled column. Both the SELECT and UPDATE throw SQLite: no such column: settled. No earnings are ever settled, no Stripe payouts are ever triggered, and app developers are never paid — silently and permanently.

Required Fix

Add settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 to the registry_earnings DDL: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS registry_earnings ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, app_id TEXT NOT NULL, author_id TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL, settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, settled_at INTEGER, created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now')*1000) ); Apply as a migration for existing DO instances. Alternatively, use a separate registry_earnings_settled table for an append-only ledger pattern.

G-M08 CRITICAL §space-type-registry-appendix — SpaceTypeRegistryDO

settleEarnings() References Undefined db Variable and Uses $N Placeholders — Every Settlement Throws ReferenceError

The Gap

settleEarnings() calls db.query('SELECT stripe_connect_account_id ... WHERE author_id = $1', [row.author_id]). The db variable is the undefined Supabase client artifact that recurs throughout the spec. The $1 PostgreSQL placeholder syntax is also wrong for SQLite. This function throws ReferenceError: db is not defined on every invocation, making it impossible to look up Stripe connect accounts or complete any earnings settlement cycle. App developers can never receive payments.

Required Fix

Replace the db.query() call with this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() using ? placeholders: const rows = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( 'SELECT stripe_connect_account_id FROM author_profiles WHERE author_id = ?', row.author_id )]; if (!rows[0]?.stripe_connect_account_id) throw new Error('No Stripe account for author: ' + row.author_id); Remove all db.* references from SpaceTypeRegistryDO. Use this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() for every SQL operation.

G-M09 CRITICAL §naelao-spaces-deep — Space Routes

Duplicate const spaceDO Declarations in Route Handler Scope — SyntaxError Prevents Worker from Deploying

The Gap

Multiple route handlers in naelao-spaces declare const spaceDO = ... twice within the same function scope. JavaScript's const does not allow redeclaration in the same block scope — this is a SyntaxError thrown at parse time, before any request is handled. The entire naelao-spaces Worker fails to deploy and returns 500 for every request. This is a compile-time error: the Worker is dead on deployment and cannot serve any traffic.

Required Fix

Remove the duplicate declarations. Declare spaceDO once at the top of each route handler (or inside a block scope using curly braces) and reuse the single reference throughout. If the same binding is needed in multiple branches, extract it to a shared helper function: function getSpaceDO(env: Env, spaceId: string): DurableObjectStub { return env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName('space:' + spaceId)); }

G-M10 CRITICAL §workflow-examples — DataPipelineWorkflow

DataPipelineWorkflow Step 'extract' Fetches Arbitrary User-Supplied sourceUrl Without Validation — SSRF

The Gap

DataPipelineWorkflow.run() step 'extract' executes: await fetch(pipelineConfig.sourceUrl) pipelineConfig comes directly from user-supplied workflow input with no URL validation. An attacker can set sourceUrl to http://169.254.169.254/ (EC2 IMDS), http://localhost:8080/, or any Cloudflare-internal address to probe internal services or exfiltrate cloud metadata. CF Workers can reach internal network addresses not publicly accessible, making this a concrete SSRF attack vector.

Required Fix

Validate pipelineConfig.sourceUrl against a domain allowlist before fetching: const parsed = new URL(pipelineConfig.sourceUrl); // throws on invalid URL if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') throw new Error('Only HTTPS sources allowed'); const ALLOWED_DOMAINS = env.ALLOWED_SOURCE_DOMAINS?.split(',') ?? []; if (!ALLOWED_DOMAINS.some(d => parsed.hostname === d || parsed.hostname.endsWith('.' + d))) { throw new Error('Source domain not in allowlist: ' + parsed.hostname); } Store approved source configurations in DO storage rather than accepting raw URLs from user input.

G-M11 HIGH §56 — Analytics Engine Queries

Analytics Engine Queries Use PostgreSQL Syntax — All Health, Error-Rate, and Latency Dashboards Return Errors

The Gap

Multiple named query constants throughout the analytics section use PostgreSQL-specific syntax: NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour' (no equivalent in CF AE SQL) DATE_TRUNC('minute', timestamp) (use toStartOfMinute() in ClickHouse) PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) (use quantile(0.95)(value)) CF Analytics Engine uses ClickHouse-style SQL, not PostgreSQL. Every one of these queries throws a SQL parse error at runtime, silently returning no data. The platform health monitor, error rate dashboard, LLM latency percentiles, and security timeline all show zero or error states permanently.

Required Fix

Replace PostgreSQL constructs with ClickHouse equivalents: • NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour' → toDateTime(now() - 3600) • DATE_TRUNC('minute', timestamp) → toStartOfMinute(timestamp) • PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) → quantile(0.95)(value) • INTERVAL '30 days' → now() - (30 * 86400) Consult the CF Analytics Engine SQL reference (ClickHouse subset) for the complete function catalog. Add a CI check that lints AE SQL strings for prohibited PostgreSQL-only functions.

G-M12 HIGH §56 — Analytics Engine Queries

SECURITY_EVENT_TIMELINE Filters on index2 — index2 Is Never Populated, Security Dashboard Always Empty

The Gap

The SECURITY_EVENT_TIMELINE Analytics Engine query includes: WHERE index2 LIKE 'security_%' CF Analytics Engine only stores indexes[0] as the indexed field (documented in G-J18). indexes[1] and beyond are silently dropped. As a result, index2 is always NULL across all records. This query permanently returns an empty result set regardless of how many security events are recorded. The security event timeline dashboard is structurally broken and cannot display any data.

Required Fix

Store the security event discriminator in indexes[0] using a composite key: indexes: ['security_' + event.subtype + ':' + event.spaceId] Alternatively, store it in blob1 and update the query: WHERE blob1 LIKE 'security_%' Update all queries that reference index2 to reference the correct storage field. Apply the same audit to any other query that references index2 through indexN.

G-M13 HIGH §workflow-examples — DailyReportWorkflow

DailyReportWorkflow Uses Public HTTPS fetch() for All Internal API Calls — Violates Service Binding Architecture

The Gap

DailyReportWorkflow.run() calls: await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/analytics/...') await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/ai/analyze') await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/...') for all internal operations. This routes traffic out of Cloudflare's network and back in via public DNS, adding 50–200ms per call and consuming egress bandwidth. CF architecture requires all internal Worker-to-Worker calls to use Service Bindings. For a workflow that may issue 10–20 internal calls per run, this adds 1–4 seconds of unnecessary latency per execution.

Required Fix

Inject the target Worker bindings into WorkflowEntrypoint via this.env: const analyticsResult = await this.env.ANALYTICS_WORKER.fetch(new Request('/query', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(params) })); const aiResult = await this.env.AI_WORKER.fetch(new Request('/analyze', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(content) })); Register all required Service Bindings (ANALYTICS_WORKER, AI_WORKER, WORKSPACE_WORKER) in the Workflow Worker's wrangler.jsonc. Remove all fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/...') calls from Workflow implementations.

G-M14 HIGH §workflow-examples — DataPipelineWorkflow

DataPipelineWorkflow Step 'transform' Sends GET Request with a Body — Body Silently Stripped

The Gap

DataPipelineWorkflow.run() step 'transform' calls: await fetch('https://app.naelao.dev/api/workspace/read', { method: 'GET', body: JSON.stringify({...}) }) The HTTP specification prohibits GET requests from having a body. Most HTTP clients and proxies silently strip GET bodies. CF Workers' fetch() implementation will either drop the body or throw a TypeError. The workspace read endpoint never receives the payload, causing the step to return an empty or error response and silently corrupting the pipeline output data.

Required Fix

Change the method to POST and ensure the target endpoint accepts a JSON body: await this.env.WORKSPACE_WORKER.fetch(new Request('/workspace/read', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ spaceId, projectId, paths }) })) Alternatively, encode short read parameters as URL query params on a GET request: GET /workspace/read?spaceId=...&projectId=.... Convert to Service Binding (see G-M13).

G-M15 HIGH §remoteloop — RemoteLoop Dispatch
