`runCutoverChecks` runs `SELECT ... FROM pg_tables WHERE rowsecurity=false`, references `auth.users`, and verifies RLS state. These are Postgres/Supabase catalogs and concepts; the target architecture is per-product DO SQLite with no `pg_tables`, no RLS, and no `auth.users`. The 'SpaceDO per-product isolation verified' check always errors or returns meaningless results, so the cutover gate provides false assurance.

Required Fix

Replace catalog-based checks with SpaceDO health-check method calls (per-DO row counts, schema-version reads). Drop the RLS/`pg_tables` verification entirely — isolation in this architecture is the DO boundary, not row-level security. The cutover gate must test what actually exists in production.

G-O27 CRITICAL §84 SpaceDO — fetch() / authCheck

SpaceDO.fetch(req) Body References Undefined `request` — ReferenceError on Hottest Path

The Gap

`async fetch(req: Request)` declares the parameter as `req`, but the body does `const url = new URL(request.url)` referencing `request`, which is not in scope. Because `authCheck` runs on almost every platform request, this throws `ReferenceError: request is not defined` at the entry of the single hottest code path on the platform — effectively a total outage the moment the DO is exercised.

Required Fix

Rename to `const url = new URL(req.url)` (or rename the parameter to `request`) and audit the entire DO for `req`/`request` inconsistency. Add a smoke test that issues one real request through SpaceDO.fetch — a typo this load-bearing must be caught by the most basic test.

G-O28 HIGH §77 AppRegistryDO — handleInstall

App Install Count Incremented Non-Atomically — Inflates on Duplicate/Failed Installs

The Gap

`handleInstall` inserts into `installs` and runs `UPDATE apps SET install_count = install_count + 1`, then separately writes the space-side record. The count increment is not conditioned on a genuinely new install: a re-install or a downstream failure path can still increment the counter, and the second (cross-store) write has no compensation, so the registry can show 'installed' while the SpaceDO has no record. Install counts drift upward and the two stores diverge.

Required Fix

Use `INSERT OR IGNORE` into `installs` and increment `install_count` only when `changes() === 1` (a real new row). Move the space-side install record into the same SpaceDO via a typed RPC within one serialized method, with rollback if it fails, so the count, the install row, and the space record commit together or not at all.

G-O29 HIGH §90 WorkflowRegistryDO — parseCronToNextTimestamp

Cron Parser Skips Day-of-Month and Mishandles Ranges/Steps — Wrong/Duplicate Schedules

The Gap

`const [min, hour, , month, dow] = cron.split(' ')` deliberately discards the 3rd field (day-of-month), so `0 9 1 * *` (09:00 on the 1st) fires every day. It also supports only `*` or a single integer per field — `*/5`, `1-5`, and `1,15` are not handled, so `'*/5 * * * *'` does `parseInt('*/5') → NaN`, never matches, and falls back to a 24h default. Month matching compares `getUTCMonth()+1` against a possibly-NaN value.

Required Fix

Use a real cron parser that supports all five fields plus lists, ranges, and steps, and honors day-of-month. At minimum, parse the day-of-month field and treat any unparseable field as a hard error rather than silently degrading to daily/24h. Add tests for `*/5`, day-of-month, and weekday expressions.

G-O30 HIGH §76 SpaceTypeRegistryDO — /migrate

Major Migration Runs ALTER TABLE + R2 Move Non-Transactionally and Returns success Unconditionally

The Gap

The migration Worker fires `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` then an R2 `/move` as two independent `fetch` calls and returns `{success:true}` regardless of either outcome — neither response's `ok` is checked. If the R2 move fails after the ALTER succeeds, the schema is half-migrated with no compensation; re-running double-applies. No `fromVersion` guard is persisted, so a retried opt-in re-runs the ALTER.

Required Fix

Check each response's `ok` and fail loudly on partial completion. Make the column add idempotent (it uses `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, but the R2 move is not idempotent — guard it). Record completion in a `schema_migrations` table keyed by `(spaceId, toVersion)` and refuse to re-run a completed migration. Surface partial failure instead of returning unconditional success.

G-O31 MEDIUM §80 naelao-eval — evaluateOutput

Two evaluateOutput Definitions With Incompatible Signatures — Extended Scorers Get Wrong Arguments

The Gap

The section defines `evaluateOutput(actual, expected, type, env)` and later, under 'Extended Scorer Types', redefines `evaluateOutput(actual, testCase, env, spaceId)` with an incompatible parameter list. The caller in `runEvaluationSuite` uses the 4-arg `(actualOutput, testCase.expected, scorerType, env)` form, so the extended scorers (`file-exists`, `json-field`, `numeric-within`) that need `testCase` and `spaceId` receive `scorerType` and `env` in the wrong slots and silently misbehave. The llm-judge scorer also does an unguarded `JSON.parse(judgement.content[0].text)`.

Required Fix

Consolidate to a single `evaluateOutput` signature and update the call site to pass `testCase` and `spaceId` so extended scorers get their required arguments. Wrap the judge parse in try/catch returning `{passed:false}` on malformed output.

G-O32 MEDIUM §81 naelao-categorizer — analyzeFailure

feedback-log.jsonl Appended via R2 Read-Modify-Write — Concurrent Feedback Lost, Truncate Races Writers

The Gap

`analyzeFailure` appends to `feedback-log.jsonl` by `get` then `put(existing + entry)` — a read-modify-write on R2 with no concurrency control. R2 has no append, so concurrent negative-feedback events lose entries (last write wins). The daily review then `put(logKey, '')` to clear the log, racing with in-flight appends and silently dropping feedback that arrived during the review.

Required Fix

Write each feedback entry as its own R2 object (`feedback/{ts}-{uuid}.json`) and `list()` them at review time, or route appends through a per-agent DO that serializes writes. Never truncate a shared mutable object that concurrent writers are appending to — archive-then-delete the individual objects instead.

G-O33 MEDIUM §80 naelao-eval — temporary AgentDOs

Eval Creates AgentDOs by Random idFromName and Never Destroys Them — Unenumerable Orphans

The Gap

Each test case creates `env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName('${spaceId}:eval-project:${testThreadId}')` with a fresh UUID and runs it, but nothing calls `/destroy` afterward. The claim that 'naelao-sweeper deletes these temporary DO instances' is unworkable: DOs addressed by random `idFromName` leave no enumerable index, so a sweeper has no way to find them. Their SQLite storage persists and bills indefinitely.

Required Fix

Record each eval DO ID in a list/table and explicitly POST `/destroy` (which deletes the DO's storage) after the run, or reuse a single eval DO with table-per-case isolation. A sweeper cannot enumerate DOs it has no record of — cleanup must be driven by an index the eval runner maintains.

G-O34 MEDIUM §A6 external-portals — portal router cache

Portal Router Caches Before Checking Method — Non-GET Responses Cached and Cross-Served

The Gap

The portal router consults `caches.default.match` before any method check and populates the cache for any response whose `Cache-Control` includes `max-age`, keyed on `route.spaceId + pathname` with the query string dropped. A cacheable response to one user's POST or authenticated request can be served to another user, and distinct query strings collide on one cache entry. There is also no WebSocket-upgrade bypass.

Required Fix

Only consult and populate the cache for GET requests, include the full URL (query string) in the cache key, and add `Vary`/auth awareness so authenticated responses are never shared. Detect `Upgrade: websocket` and bypass cache/dispatch for live connections.

G-O35 MEDIUM §A6 external-portals — attachCustomDomain

attachCustomDomain Spreads a Host String as if It Were a PortalRoute — Empty Route Written

The Gap

`provisionExternalPortal` writes `portal:space:${spaceId}` = a bare `platformHost` string. `attachCustomDomain` then reads that key with `get(..., 'json')`, casts the result to `PortalRoute`, and spreads `{...existingRoute}` — but the key holds a plain string, not JSON, so the parse yields null and the spread produces a route missing `spaceId`, `enabled`, and `scopedToken`. The router then 404s the custom domain or serves a route with no space context.

Required Fix

Read the actual route object from `portal:host:${platformHost}` (which stores the JSON `PortalRoute`), spread that, and write it under the custom hostname. Keep `portal:space:` as a pointer-only key and never spread it as a route object.

G-O36 MEDIUM §87 naelao-billing — /community/split

Community Revenue Split Mixes Dollars and Cents — Ledger Amounts Corrupted

The Gap

In `/community/split`, `amount` is treated as dollars for `creatorCents = Math.floor(amount * 0.80 * 100)`, but the ledger insert stores `gross_amount_usd = amount/100` and `platform_amount_usd = (amount - creatorCents)/100` — mixing dollars (`amount`) with cents (`creatorCents`). Gross is recorded 100× too small, and the platform amount subtracts cents from dollars, yielding a large negative number. The revenue ledger is systematically corrupt.

Required Fix

Pick one unit and use it consistently. If `amount` is USD: `creatorUsd = amount*0.8`, `platformUsd = amount*0.2`, store those directly, and convert to cents only for the Stripe transfer field (`Math.round(amount*0.8*100)`). Add an invariant test that gross == creator + platform.

G-O37 MEDIUM §88 naelao-spaces — quota enforcement

Sub-Space / Member Quota Is Check-Then-Insert in the Worker — Race Exceeds Plan Limits

The Gap

`/spaces` and `/members/invite` read `SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE parent_space_id=?` (or a member count), compare to the plan quota, then later `INSERT`. Between the count and the insert, concurrent requests both pass the check and both insert, exceeding `maxSubSpaces`/`maxMembers`. The §88 narrative claims the DO 'prevents concurrent provisioning from racing past the limit', but the shown code does the count in the Worker against the DB, not atomically in a DO.

Required Fix

Enforce the limit inside SpaceDO with `blockConcurrencyWhile` so the count and insert run in one serialized method, or use a conditional `INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)...) < limit` backed by a unique/trigger guard. A Worker-side count-then-insert cannot be made race-safe across concurrent requests.

G-O38 MEDIUM §75 remoteloop — dispatchRemoteLoop

dispatchRemoteLoop Reads ctx.manifest That Was Never Assigned — TypeError on Delegation

The Gap

`dispatchTurn` resolves `const manifest = await ctx.spaceTypeRegistry.getManifest(ctx.spaceTypeId)` into a local variable and passes `manifest.customLoopWorker` onward, but inside `dispatchRemoteLoop` the token issuance reads `ctx.manifest.agentEnvironment.agentPermissions` and the request body reads `ctx.toolManifest` — neither of which was ever assigned on `ctx`. `ctx.manifest` is undefined, so reading `.agentEnvironment` throws.

Required Fix

Pass the resolved `manifest` into `dispatchRemoteLoop` as an argument (or assign `ctx.manifest = manifest` before delegating) and read permissions/tools from that object. Ensure `ctx.toolManifest` is populated before the remote loop is dispatched.

G-O39 MEDIUM §A7 operator-shell — postMessage origins

Shell and Panel postMessage Origin Constants Disagree — Cross-Frame Messages Silently Dropped

The Gap

The app panel pins `shellOrigin = 'https://app.naelao.dev'` and only accepts messages whose `e.origin` matches it, while the shell listener accepts only `event.origin === 'https://ui.naelao.app'`, and the prose says panels run on `ui.naelao.app`. The two sides whitelist different origins, so at least one direction of CONTEXT/THEME messaging is silently dropped — panels never receive context, or the shell ignores panel events, with no error surfaced.

Required Fix

Define exactly one shell-origin constant and one panel-origin constant, shared by both sides, and verify the shell actually sends from the origin the panel whitelists (and vice versa). Reconcile `app.naelao.dev` vs `ui.naelao.app` everywhere so the allowlists are provably symmetric.

G-O40 MEDIUM §80 naelao-eval — /eval/run CI gate

/eval/run Returns Immediately via waitUntil But CI Expects a Synchronous Score

The Gap

`app.post('/eval/run')` fires `c.executionCtx.waitUntil(runEvaluationSuite(...))` and returns `{status:'started'}` with no `score`, ignoring the request's `waitForCompletion:true` and `timeoutSeconds` flags. The GitHub Actions gate does `SCORE=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.score')` and compares `null < 70` — so the score is always null and the deploy gate either always blocks or errors on `bc`.

Required Fix

Honor `waitForCompletion`: when set, `await runEvaluationSuite()` (within Worker time limits) and return the final `score`; otherwise expose an `/eval/status` endpoint for CI to poll until the run completes. Do not advertise a flag the handler silently drops — the deploy gate depends on a real score.

G-O41 LOW §83 WorkflowRegistryDO — sweepSchedules SQL

WHERE status = "active" Uses Double Quotes — Identifier, Not String Literal, in SQLite

The Gap

The §83 `sweepSchedules` query is `SELECT * FROM workflows WHERE status = "active" AND schedule IS NOT NULL AND next_run <= ?`. In SQLite, double quotes denote an identifier (a column name), not a string literal. `"active"` is interpreted as a column reference and only resolves to the string by SQLite's legacy fallback quirk — fragile, and it breaks outright under strict/`PRAGMA` modes. The §90 complete version correctly uses single quotes.

Required Fix

Use single quotes for the string literal: `WHERE status = 'active'`. Standardize on single-quoted string literals throughout all DO SQL, and enable strict-quoting in tests so the identifier-vs-literal confusion is caught rather than silently tolerated.

Appendix O complete — seventh pass, full three-band spec re-audit. Combined gap audit total: A (125) + B (30) + C (22) + D (22) + E (24) + F (26) + G (26) + H (15) + I (34) + J (20) + K (51) + L (23) + M (31) + N (24) + O (41) = 514 documented technical gaps with required fixes.

Appendix P

Eighth-Pass Technical Gap Analysis

35 new critical and high-severity gaps discovered in the eighth full-spectrum audit pass: hibernation state loss across AssistantDO, SandboxDO and ConcurrencyDO; non-atomic cross-DO payment flows; PostgreSQL DDL and DML syntax throughout DO SQLite tables; security vulnerabilities in APNs JWT generation, BYOK key exposure, webhook signature bypass, and Analytics Engine SQL injection; Hono framework spread export destroying the fetch handler; and Cloudflare platform API correctness issues in Vectorize filters, CF Workflows stubs, and token-usage billing.

G-P01 CRITICAL §launchpad — NaelaoAgentDO.requestApproval() / handleApprovalDecision()

pendingApprovals Map Lost on DO Hibernation — Agent Hangs Forever

The Gap

this.pendingApprovals = new Map() stores {resolve, reject} Promise callbacks for human-approval pauses. When the DO hibernates between the approval request and the owner's response, all class fields are wiped. On wake, this.pendingApprovals.get(approvalId) returns undefined, the resolver is gone, and the agent run hangs permanently waiting for a callback that can never fire — no timeout, no error, just silence.

Required Fix

Persist approval records to DO SQLite with a status column (pending/approved/rejected). On wake, query for status='pending' rows and implement polling via a DO alarm rather than an in-memory Promise resolver. The alarm fires every N seconds, checks the SQLite record, and proceeds if the admin has updated it. Remove all in-memory Map usage for cross-request state.

G-P02 CRITICAL §schema — SpaceDO.initSchema() — §22 canonical DDL block

SpaceDO Canonical §22 Schema Uses PostgreSQL — Incompatible with DO SQLite

The Gap

The §22 canonical schema block uses gen_random_uuid(), auth.users foreign keys, JSONB, TIMESTAMPTZ, DEFAULT NOW(), ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY, and ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT — none of which exist in SQLite. Executing this DDL via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() throws a parse error immediately, preventing any SpaceDO from initialising its schema on first wake.

Required Fix

Rewrite the entire canonical DDL to valid SQLite: replace gen_random_uuid() with crypto.randomUUID() in application code passed as a ? parameter, replace TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() with INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch()*1000), replace JSONB with TEXT (store as JSON.stringify), delete all ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY statements, and remove all auth.users references. Tenant isolation is enforced via space_id column checks in application logic, not DB-level RLS.

G-P03 CRITICAL §naelao-os — createSpace() in workers/spaces/index.ts

createSpace() Calls spaceDO.query() Before Declaration — ReferenceError + PostgreSQL $N Placeholders

The Gap

spaceDO.query('INSERT INTO spaces ... VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)', [...]) is called several lines before the spaceDO variable is instantiated, producing a ReferenceError at runtime. The $1/$2/$N PostgreSQL positional placeholders are also invalid in DO SQLite which requires ? for all bound parameters. Additionally spaceDO.query() is a non-existent method — DO SQLite uses this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...params).

Required Fix

Move the spaceDO instantiation before any call to it. Replace all $N placeholders with ? and use this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...params) spread syntax throughout. Run a global search for db.query and spaceDO.query across all Workers to find other instances of the same leftover Supabase API pattern.

G-P04 CRITICAL §assistants — handleSlackWebhook() in naelao-router / naelao-assistant

handleSlackWebhook Double-Reads Consumed Request Body — Signature Always Fails

The Gap

await request.json() consumes the body stream as parsed JSON. The subsequent verifySlackSignature(..., await request.text(), ...) call re-reads the already-consumed body, returning an empty string. Slack HMAC-SHA256 verification is computed over the raw request body bytes; using an empty string produces a signature that never matches, causing every legitimate Slack event to be rejected as 401 Unauthorized.

Required Fix

Read the body exactly once as text: const rawBody = await request.text(). Verify the Slack signature against rawBody, then parse the event with JSON.parse(rawBody) for application use. Never call both .json() and .text() on the same request — the first call to consume the body makes the stream unreadable for all subsequent reads.

G-P05 CRITICAL §assistants — AssistantDO constructor and all public methods

AssistantDO this.spaceId and this.userId Not Persisted — Undefined After Hibernation, Cross-Tenant R2 Paths

The Gap

Every AssistantDO method references this.spaceId and this.userId (e.g., R2 path spaces/${this.spaceId}/..., DO ID lookups). The constructor and initSchema() never INSERT or SELECT these values from SQLite. After DO hibernation and wake, both fields are undefined, causing every method to construct the path spaces/undefined/... — reading from and writing to the wrong R2 prefix and potentially blending data across tenants silently.

Required Fix

Persist spaceId and userId to a config table in initSchema() immediately after first construction. Add an ensureLoaded() guard called at the top of every public method that reads them back from SQLite if not already set: if (!this.spaceId) { const row = this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = ?", 'spaceId').one(); this.spaceId = row?.value as string; }. Add a similar guard for userId.

G-P06 CRITICAL §walletdo-deep — x402Payment() in workers/billing/x402.ts

x402Payment Non-Atomic Two-DO Debit-Then-Credit — Money Lost If Credit Call Fails

The Gap

Step 1 debits companyWalletDO and Step 2 separately credits workerDefDO via two independent DO fetch() calls with no transaction wrapping or compensation record. If Step 2 fails (network error, DO crash, 5xx), the company is debited but the creator is never credited. The platform fee (Step 3) is also sent to a Queue independently. There is no idempotency key, no retry log, and no rollback path.

Required Fix

Implement two-phase commit: (1) write an x402_transfer record with status='pending' to a TransferLedgerDO before debiting, (2) debit with an idempotency key referencing the transfer ID, (3) credit with the same key, (4) mark status='settled' after both succeed. A sweeper alarm retries any status='pending' records older than N minutes. The idempotency key on both DOs prevents double-debit or double-credit on retry.

G-P07 CRITICAL §concurrency-do — ConcurrencyDO.checkAndReserve()

ConcurrencyDO setAlarm Replaced on Every Reservation — Zombie Slots Never Cleaned

The Gap

checkAndReserve() calls this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + HEARTBEAT_WINDOW) on every invocation. CF Durable Objects support only one alarm at a time; each setAlarm() call replaces the previous one. Under concurrent reservations, the cleanup alarm is continuously pushed forward. Expired reservations are never collected because the alarm never fires, and the concurrency ceiling is permanently consumed by zombie slots.

Required Fix

Implement an alarm multiplexer: store the current earliest-deadline timestamp in SQLite. Only call setAlarm() if the newly computed deadline is earlier than the currently stored one. The alarm handler should re-schedule itself if unexpired slots still exist after cleanup, using the earliest remaining expiry as the next alarm target.

G-P08 CRITICAL §analytics — AnalyticsWorker queue handler

Analytics Queue msg.ack() Called Before writeDataPoints — Events Permanently Lost on Error

The Gap

The queue message handler calls msg.ack() before the await writeDataPoints(...) call completes. CF Queues provide at-least-once delivery only when ack() is deferred until after successful processing. Acknowledging first means any exception or transient failure in writeDataPoints() permanently silently drops the analytics event — no retry, no dead-letter, no error log. All billing, usage metering, and observability data in transit is at risk.

Required Fix

Move msg.ack() to after await writeDataPoints(...) succeeds. Wrap the write in try/catch; on failure, do not call ack() — the queue will redeliver automatically. Add a retry counter in the message metadata to apply exponential back-off and route persistently failing events to the dead-letter queue after max_retries is exceeded.

G-P09 CRITICAL §naelao-threads-impl — POST /threads/:id/messages handler in workers/threads/index.ts

billingTier Never Passed to ConcurrencyDO — Paid Spaces Throttled to Free-Tier Limits

The Gap

The threads handler calls concurrencyDO.checkAndReserve() with only { spaceId, agentId } in the request body — it never reads or forwards billingTier from the space record. ConcurrencyDO applies different concurrency slot limits per billing tier; with the tier always absent, it defaults to the 'free' limit for every space regardless of subscription. Enterprise workspaces with 10-agent concurrency entitlements are incorrectly limited to 1-2 free-tier slots.

Required Fix

Before calling checkAndReserve(), fetch the space record from SpaceDO to extract billingTier, then include it in the request body: { spaceId, agentId, billingTier }. In ConcurrencyDO, treat a missing or unrecognised tier as an error that returns 400 rather than silently defaulting to 'free'. Add a unit test asserting that maker/business/enterprise spaces receive their correct slot allocations.

G-P10 CRITICAL §naelao-admin / §naelao-admin-full — handleAdminAuditLog in naelao-admin worker

Admin Audit Analytics Engine Query Built via String Interpolation — SQL Injection

The Gap

The audit log query builds a CF Analytics Engine SQL string via template literals: WHERE index1 = '${spaceId}' and ${eventType ? `AND blob1 = '${eventType}'` : ''}. Both spaceId and eventType are taken directly from c.req.param() / c.req.query() without sanitisation. An attacker with admin credentials can exfiltrate arbitrary Analytics Engine data by injecting SQL fragments. The LIMIT ${parseInt(limit)} coercion provides no protection against the string-based filter fields.

Required Fix

Parameterise all dynamic values using the CF Analytics Engine SQL binding syntax (? positional params). Replace template-literal construction with a static query string and pass [spaceId, eventType, parsedLimit] as the params array to env.ANALYTICS.query(). Validate eventType against an allowlist of known event-type strings before including it in any query context.

G-P11 CRITICAL §naelao-notifications-full — generateAPNsJWT in naelao-notifications worker

APNs JWT Signed with DER-Encoded ECDSA Signature — iOS Push Always Rejected

The Gap

crypto.subtle.sign({ name: 'ECDSA', hash: 'SHA-256' }, signingKey, data) returns a DER-encoded ECDSA signature on all Web Crypto implementations. APNs requires raw P1363 format (two 32-byte big-endian integers R||S concatenated, 64 bytes total). The code immediately base64url-encodes the DER blob without conversion, producing a JWT signature that APNs always rejects with HTTP 403. Every iOS push notification silently fails.

Required Fix

After obtaining the DER-encoded rawSig, parse the ASN.1 DER structure: locate the two INTEGER TLV fields in the SEQUENCE, extract the R and S integers, left-pad each to exactly 32 bytes, concatenate them into a 64-byte buffer, and base64url-encode the result. Implement a derToP1363(buf, coordSize) helper and add a test asserting the output is exactly 64 bytes when coordSize=32.

G-P12 CRITICAL §naelao-notifications-full — sendPush in naelao-notifications worker

sendPush References spaceDO Variable Never Defined in Scope — ReferenceError on Every Call

The Gap

sendPush calls spaceDO.getActiveDeviceTokens(payload.userId) but spaceDO is not declared or passed anywhere in the function signature or its enclosing scope. This is a ReferenceError that crashes the function on every invocation, making all push notification delivery completely non-functional at runtime. No test catches this without an end-to-end push path exercise.

Required Fix

Add env: Env to the sendPush signature and construct the SpaceDO stub inside the function: const id = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.idFromName(payload.spaceId); const spaceDO = env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(id);. Then call spaceDO.fetch(new Request('https://internal/devices/active', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ userId: payload.userId }) })) using the standard Service Binding .fetch() pattern.

G-P13 CRITICAL §naelao-billing-full / §naelao-together-ai-full — Worker default export in naelao-billing and naelao-together-ai

export default { ...app, scheduled } Spread Destroys Hono Fetch Handler

The Gap

Spreading a Hono app instance with { ...app, scheduled } copies only enumerable own properties of the app object. The fetch method is defined on Hono's prototype chain and is therefore not an enumerable own property — it is not copied by the spread. The resulting export object has a scheduled property but no callable fetch handler, causing all HTTP requests to these workers to receive an unhandled-fetch error. The scheduled handler also breaks because the spread loses the correct this binding for app.fetch.

Required Fix

Export an explicit object literal: export default { fetch: app.fetch.bind(app), scheduled: async (event, env, ctx) => { ctx.waitUntil(runDailyMaintenance(env)); } }. This preserves the Hono fetch handler with the correct binding and adds the scheduled handler independently. Never spread a class or framework instance — prototype methods are invisible to the spread operator.

G-P14 CRITICAL §space-templates — space_templates DDL in SpaceDO / template-installer worker

space_templates DDL Uses PostgreSQL RLS, TIMESTAMPTZ, auth.users — SQLite Incompatible

The Gap

The space_templates schema DDL includes author_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), ALTER TABLE space_templates ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and CREATE POLICY ... USING (status = 'approved'). None of these are valid SQLite syntax. Executing this DDL via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() throws a parse error on first contact, making the entire Space Templates system inoperable from cold start.

Required Fix

Rewrite the DDL for SQLite: use TEXT for all UUID and timestamp columns, replace TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() with INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch()*1000), remove all REFERENCES auth.users(id) constraints, and delete the ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and CREATE POLICY statements entirely. Enforce access control in application logic by filtering on space_id and checking membership. Apply the same audit to installTemplate and every related stored function.

G-P15 CRITICAL §naelao-billing-full — GET /byok/:spaceId/anthropic in naelao-billing worker

BYOK Endpoint Returns Decrypted API Key in Plaintext JSON Response — Secret Exposed

The Gap

The BYOK retrieval route decrypts the stored AES-GCM ciphertext and returns c.json({ hasByok: true, apiKey }) where apiKey is the fully decrypted secret. Any intermediary that can read the response body — CDN edge logs, Cloudflare dashboard request logging, client-side JavaScript — now has the plaintext key. The decrypted value is included unconditionally regardless of call context.

Required Fix

Return only { hasByok: true } from the GET endpoint and never include the decrypted key in any response body. If the key must be used downstream, implement a proxy pattern where the billing worker makes the LLM call on behalf of the space using the key server-side and returns only the result. If the user must see the key (e.g., for rotation UI), mask it to sk-ant-...XXXX and gate the unmasked display behind a separate admin-scoped endpoint with full audit logging.

G-P16 CRITICAL §naelao-apps-registry — handleInstall in AppRegistryDO

AppRegistryDO.handleInstall Uses PostgreSQL db.query + $N Params — App Installation Broken

The Gap

handleInstall executes await db.query('INSERT INTO space_app_installs ... VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)', [spaceId, appId, ...]) using PostgreSQL positional parameter syntax. Durable Objects use SQLite via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...params) which requires ? placeholders. The db variable is undefined in the DO runtime (no Postgres client exists), causing a ReferenceError that crashes every app install attempt.

Required Fix

Replace db.query(sql, paramsArray) with this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...paramsArray) and change all $1/$2/$3/$4 placeholders to ?. Ensure the space_app_installs table DDL is created in blockConcurrencyWhile() during AppRegistryDO's first init via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ...').

G-P17 CRITICAL §space-templates — installTemplate in template-installer worker / SpaceDO

installTemplate Uses gen_random_uuid() + $N Params + NOW() — SQLite Incompatible

The Gap

installTemplate executes await db.query('INSERT INTO agent_definitions (id, ...) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, ...)', [...]) and await db.query('INSERT INTO space_template_installs ... VALUES ($1, $2, NOW())', [...]). gen_random_uuid() and NOW() are PostgreSQL functions with no SQLite equivalents. The $N positional syntax is also incompatible. All three constructs throw errors when executed via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(), making template installation completely broken.

Required Fix

Generate UUIDs in application code using crypto.randomUUID() and pass as a ? parameter. Replace NOW() with unixepoch()*1000 or pass Date.now() as a bind parameter. Rewrite all queries to use ? placeholders: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('INSERT INTO agent_definitions (id, space_id, name, ...) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ...)', uuid, spaceId, agent.name, ...). Run a global search for gen_random_uuid() and NOW() across all DDL and DML in the spec.

G-P18 CRITICAL §naelao-triggers — verifySignature in naelao-triggers worker

Non-GitHub Webhook Providers Return true from verifySignature — Auth Bypass

The Gap

verifySignature implements real HMAC-SHA256 verification only for the 'github' provider. All other providers — Stripe, Linear, Jira, and any future webhook sources — fall through to return true unconditionally. Any unauthenticated HTTP POST to a non-GitHub trigger endpoint is accepted as a valid signed webhook. An attacker can trigger arbitrary automation workflows by posting crafted payloads to any Stripe or Linear trigger URL without knowing the webhook secret.

Required Fix

Implement provider-specific HMAC verification for each supported provider before any fallback. For Stripe, verify using the Stripe-Signature header with 5-minute timestamp-tolerance validation. For Linear and Jira, verify their respective HMAC-SHA256 header signatures using the stored webhook secret. Add an explicit throw new Error(`Unsupported provider: ${provider}`) as the final fallback to prevent silent acceptance of unknown providers.

G-P19 CRITICAL §naelao-spaces-full — POST /spaces/:spaceId/archive handler in naelao-spaces worker

Duplicate const spaceDO in Archive Handler — SyntaxError Prevents Worker from Loading

The Gap

Within the same async route handler function, spaceDO is declared twice with const: first as const spaceDO = getProductDO(rootSpaceId, c.env) and then again as const spaceDO = c.env.NAELAO_SPACE_DO.get(...). In strict-mode JavaScript (all CF Workers run in strict mode) redeclaring a const in the same lexical scope throws a SyntaxError at parse time. The entire naelao-spaces worker fails to load and all space management routes return 500 errors.

Required Fix

Rename the second declaration to a distinct identifier (e.g., const spaceDOStub = ...) or consolidate both into a single declaration if they refer to the same object. Audit all other route handlers in naelao-spaces/index.ts for duplicate variable declarations — a single redeclared const in any handler prevents the entire worker module from loading.

G-P20 CRITICAL §space-type-versioning — processCanaryRollouts in SpaceTypeRegistryDO / canary cron

processCanaryRollouts Standalone Function Accesses this.ctx — TypeError on Every Invocation

The Gap

processCanaryRollouts is declared as async function processCanaryRollouts(env: Env) — a standalone function, not a class method — but its body calls this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(...) and this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`UPDATE versions ...`). In strict-mode JS, this inside a regular function call is undefined, so this.ctx throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ctx'). The canary rollout engine is entirely broken; no rollout percentage ever advances.

Required Fix

Either convert processCanaryRollouts to a method on the DO class (async processCanaryRollouts() using this.env and this.ctx stored at construction), or refactor it to accept the DO's sql storage context as an explicit parameter: async function processCanaryRollouts(sql: SqlStorage, env: Env) and replace all this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() calls with sql.exec(). If called from a cron handler, pass the DO stub explicitly.

G-P21 CRITICAL §naelao-billing-deep — POST /token-usage handler in naelao-billing worker

naelao-billing Token-Usage Handler Uses PostgreSQL BEGIN/COMMIT + db.query — Billing Writes Never Execute

The Gap

The token-usage handler issues await db.query('BEGIN'), multiple db.query(INSERT/UPDATE ...) calls, and await db.query('COMMIT') / await db.query('ROLLBACK'). This is PostgreSQL transaction syntax via a db client that does not exist in a Cloudflare Worker. Workers have no persistent database connection and no db global. The entire billing-write path throws a ReferenceError on db, meaning token usage is never recorded and credit deduction never occurs — allowing unbounded free usage.

Required Fix

Move all billing state into a BillingDO where SQLite transactions are available. Inside the DO, use this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('BEGIN') / COMMIT for atomicity, or wrap all writes in a single this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile() block which provides DO-level serialisation. Replace all $1/$2 placeholders with ? and all db.query(sql, arr) calls with this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...arr).

G-P22 HIGH §ai-gateway — getAvailableModels() in workers/agents/models.ts

getAvailableModels() References Undeclared spaceDO and Uses Non-Existent .rows on SQLite Result

The Gap

const fineTunedModels = await spaceDO.query(...) uses spaceDO which is never declared in that function's scope, producing a ReferenceError. Additionally, DO SQLite .exec() returns an object exposing .toArray() and .one() — not a .rows property — so result.rows.map(...) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map') at runtime. Both errors combine to make fine-tuned model listing completely broken.

Required Fix

Pass a spaceDO: DurableObjectStub parameter into getAvailableModels() or instantiate it from env inside the function. Replace all .rows with .toArray() on DO SQLite exec results. Apply a project-wide search for .rows on sql.exec() results to find and fix all other occurrences of this pattern.

G-P23 HIGH §assistants — AssistantDO.handleChannelMessage()

handleChannelMessage Session Scoped to Channel Type Only — Cross-User Conversation Bleed

The Gap

SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE channel = ? finds a session by channel type alone (e.g., 'slack'). All users who message via Slack share the same session row, causing every user's messages to be concatenated into one conversation context. User B's question is answered in the context of User A's entire session history — a privacy violation and a source of incorrect LLM responses for every user after the first.

Required Fix

Scope the session query by both channel and user: SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE channel = ? AND user_id = ?. Extract user_id from the incoming message payload (Slack provides event.user; other providers have equivalent user identifiers). Ensure the sessions table has a UNIQUE constraint on (channel, user_id) and an index on (channel, user_id) for efficient lookup.

G-P24 HIGH §ai-gateway — createTogetherAIClient() in shared/ai-client.ts

createTogetherAIClient() Instantiates Anthropic SDK Against OpenAI-Compatible Together AI — 422 on All Calls

The Gap

new Anthropic({ baseURL: 'https://app.naelao.dev/api/together-ai/v1', ... }) sends requests in Anthropic wire format (top-level system, max_tokens, Anthropic-specific headers). Together AI's API is OpenAI-compatible, not Anthropic-compatible. Every Together AI model call — fine-tune polling, AutoResearch, vision tasks — receives 422 Unprocessable Entity due to the format mismatch.

Required Fix

Use the OpenAI SDK to call Together AI: new OpenAI({ baseURL: 'https://api.together.xyz/v1', apiKey: env.TOGETHER_AI_API_KEY }). All Together AI endpoints expect { model, messages, max_tokens, temperature } in OpenAI format, not Anthropic format. Alternatively, call fetch() directly with OpenAI-format JSON bodies and a Bearer token. Update the shared factory to switch SDK based on provider.

G-P25 HIGH §skills — loadSkillsFromR2() in shared/skill-loader.ts; list_files in file-manager handler

loadSkillsFromR2() and list_files Both Truncate at 1000 R2 Objects — Skills and Files Silently Lost

The Gap

Both implementations call bucket.list({ prefix, delimiter: '/' }) without checking listing.truncated or following the cursor. R2 list() returns at most 1000 objects per call. Spaces with more than 1000 installed skills or workspace files silently lose all objects beyond the first 1000 with no error, no log, and no indication to the caller that the result is incomplete.

Required Fix

Wrap every r2.list() call in a cursor loop: let listing = null; const results = []; do { listing = await bucket.list({ prefix, cursor: listing?.cursor, limit: 1000 }); results.push(...listing.objects); } while (listing.truncated); Apply the same pattern to VerticalFinetuneWorkflow, archiveSpace, and every other R2 list() call in the codebase.

G-P26 HIGH §workers-sp — WalletDO.deductCredits() / recordCreatorEarning()

WalletDO Creator Earning Fired as Bare void in DO Handler — Silently Lost on Response Return

The Gap

void this.recordCreatorEarning(params.amount * 0.15) inside a DO fetch() handler fires an unregistered Promise. When the DO returns its Response the runtime can cancel the in-flight Promise. DOs do not have ExecutionContext.waitUntil(). Creator earnings that represent 15% of every paid agent run are silently lost on any DO eviction or Worker recycle.

Required Fix

Write the creator earning record synchronously to DO SQLite inside deductCredits() before returning the Response: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec('INSERT INTO pending_earnings (id, amount, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', ...). A separate alarm-based sweeper then processes pending_earnings in bulk and credits the creator wallet. The initial record must be durable before the DO response returns.

G-P27 HIGH §workflows — WorkflowRegistryDO in workers/workflows/index.ts

WorkflowRegistryDO Calls Non-Existent instance.id() on CF Workflows Stub — Workflow Creation Throws

The Gap

After const instance = await env.NAELAO_WORKFLOW.create({ id: workflowId, ... }), the code calls await instance.id() to register the workflow. The CF Workflows WorkflowInstance stub does not expose an .id() method. This throws TypeError: instance.id is not a function at runtime on every workflow creation, making the entire Workflows feature non-functional.

Required Fix

Use workflowId directly — it is the value already passed to .create(). The CF Workflows API exposes .status(), .pause(), .resume(), and .abort() on the instance stub, not .id(). Immediately register the workflow ID in WorkflowRegistryDO using the workflowId local variable: await registryDO.fetch(new Request('http://registry/register', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ workflowId }) })).

G-P28 HIGH §naelao-threads-impl — GET /threads Hono handler in workers/threads/index.ts

GET /threads Uses PostgreSQL $N Placeholders + Dead db.query Reference — ReferenceError on Every List Request

The Gap

The GET /threads implementation builds a SQL string with $1, $${params.length+1} (PostgreSQL positional syntax) and calls await db.query(query, params) where db is the removed Supabase client. The comment // SpaceDO replaces Hyperdrive appears but db.query() is used anyway. At runtime db is undefined and db.query() throws ReferenceError immediately, making thread listing completely non-functional.

Required Fix

Replace all db.query(sql, params) calls with the SpaceDO Service Binding pattern: await spaceDO.fetch(new Request('http://space/query', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ sql, params }) })). Replace all $N placeholders with ? for SQLite compatibility. Run a project-wide search for db.query to find all other leftover Supabase call sites.

G-P29 HIGH §naelao-threads-impl — createSSEStream() in workers/threads/index.ts

createSSEStream Bare void IIFE Killed When Response Returns — Zero SSE Tokens Delivered

The Gap

The SSE stream driver uses void (async () => { ... })() — a bare unregistered Promise. When createSSEStream() returns its Response, the Workers runtime recycles the execution context and cancels the in-flight async IIFE before any tokens are forwarded to the client. The text/event-stream response closes immediately with no events, making the SSE fallback permanently broken for all clients.

Required Fix

Use ctx.waitUntil(streamDriverPromise) on the ExecutionContext to keep the Worker alive until the stream completes. Thread the ExecutionContext down to wherever the SSE Response is constructed and ensure the entire async streaming loop is registered with waitUntil before the Response is returned.

G-P30 HIGH §execution-ladder — SandboxDO.alarm() in durable-objects/sandbox-do.ts

SandboxDO Alarm Reads this.lastActiveAt Class Field — Always 0 After Hibernation, Stops Every Container

The Gap

private lastActiveAt: number = 0 is a class field that resets to 0 after every DO hibernation. The alarm() handler checks Date.now() - this.lastActiveAt >= IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS. Since this.lastActiveAt is always 0 on wake, Date.now() - 0 always exceeds 10 minutes, and the container is stopped on every alarm regardless of actual recent activity — destroying any long-running container session.

Required Fix

Persist lastActiveAt to DO SQLite on every activity event: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("UPDATE container_state SET value = ? WHERE key = 'last_active'", Date.now()). In alarm(), read it back before computing the idle delta: const lastActive = parseInt(this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("SELECT value FROM container_state WHERE key = 'last_active'").one()?.value ?? '0'). Default to Date.now() (not 0) when the key is absent to avoid false-positive idle detection.

G-P31 HIGH §sandbox-do — SandboxDO in durable-objects/sandbox-do.ts

SandboxDO sandboxRef In-Memory Field Nulled on Hibernation — Container Orphaned, All Exec Calls Fail

The Gap

private sandboxRef = null is a class-level field never persisted to SQLite. When the DO hibernates between exec() calls, sandboxRef is wiped. On wake, ensureRunning() has no mechanism to re-attach to an already-running external container — it only starts new ones. The previously active container is silently orphaned, and subsequent exec() calls start a duplicate container or fail, leaking container resources.

Required Fix

Persist the container's unique identifier string to SQLite (INSERT OR REPLACE INTO container_state (key, value) VALUES ('sandbox_id', containerId)) whenever a container is started. In ensureRunning(), first query SQLite for an existing sandbox_id and attempt re-attachment before launching a new container. Gate the entire ensureRunning() body inside this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile() to prevent concurrent duplicate starts.

G-P32 HIGH §naelao-credentials — getCredentialForUrl() in workers/credentials/index.ts

getCredentialForUrl endsWith Domain Check — Subdomain Bypass Forwards Credentials to Attacker

The Gap

The domain validation uses domains.some(d => parsedUrl.hostname.endsWith(d)). A hostname like evilnaelao.com satisfies endsWith('naelao.com'), bypassing the allowlist entirely. The credential routing forwards matching credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens) to any domain sharing the suffix with an allowed domain, enabling SSRF and credential theft by an attacker who registers a suffix-matching domain.

Required Fix

Replace the endsWith check with the correct prefix-anchored subdomain test: hostname === d || hostname.endsWith('.' + d). This ensures the match is against the domain itself or a proper subdomain, not an arbitrary suffix. Apply the same fix to every domain validation in the credentials worker and add a unit test asserting that evilnaelao.com does not match naelao.com.

G-P33 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — knowledge/index.ts GET /knowledge/search

Vectorize Filter Uses Flat Object — Cross-Space Knowledge Returned, Tenant Data Leak

The Gap

The vector search query passes filter: { spaceId } — a flat key-value object. Cloudflare Vectorize requires filter expressions using explicit operator syntax: { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } }. A flat object is not a valid filter expression and is either silently ignored or returns an API error. In the ignore case, the search returns results across all spaces rather than scoping to the requesting space, exposing cross-tenant knowledge base content.

Required Fix

Change the filter to { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } } (and similarly for all other filter fields such as agentId, projectId, domainId). Verify that all filtered fields are declared as metadata indexes at Vectorize index creation time — undeclared fields silently produce unfiltered results. Add an integration test asserting that results returned by any search belong only to the authenticated space.

G-P34 HIGH §stored-functions — deduct_space_credits stored function

deduct_space_credits Uses SELECT FOR UPDATE Row Lock — Invalid Syntax in SQLite, Billing Deduction Broken

The Gap

The deduct_space_credits function uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock the credits row before the deduction. FOR UPDATE is a PostgreSQL row-level locking clause that does not exist in SQLite. Executing this statement via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() throws a syntax error, causing every credit deduction to fail. Because this function gates all paid AI operations, the entire billing enforcement layer is inoperable.

Required Fix

Remove FOR UPDATE entirely. In Durable Objects, concurrency is serialised by the single-threaded execution model — row locks are unnecessary. Wrap the read-modify-write in this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile() if atomicity across awaited calls is needed within the same handler. Use a single atomic SQL UPDATE: UPDATE space_credits SET balance = balance - ? WHERE space_id = ? AND balance >= ? RETURNING balance to perform the deduction atomically without a separate lock.

G-P35 HIGH §naelao-notifications-full — initiateVoiceCall / VAPI webhook handler in naelao-notifications

VAPI Voice Escalation Has No Approval-Outcome Webhook Handler — Call Result Never Processed

The Gap

initiateVoiceCall posts a call to VAPI and stores callId in KV, but there is no registered POST /vapi/webhook route to receive the VAPI call.ended or call.transcript callback. Without this handler the platform never learns whether the human approved or rejected the escalation, so all downstream logic gated on the call outcome (resuming paused workflows, logging approval decisions) never executes. KV entries for pending calls also accumulate indefinitely with no TTL.

Required Fix

Register a POST /vapi/webhook route that verifies the VAPI HMAC signature, reads callId from the payload, fetches the KV record, determines the outcome from call.status or the call transcript, and either resumes the paused workflow via WorkflowRegistryDO or logs a rejection. Set a TTL of <= 24 hours on all KV entries written by initiateVoiceCall to prevent unbounded accumulation.

Appendix Q

Ninth-Pass: CF Think / Workspace / OpenClaw / Hermes Gap Analysis

30 new gaps focusing on missing @cloudflare/think base class integration, @cloudflare/workspace virtual filesystem, CF Agents lifecycle hooks, extended thinking persistence, OpenClaw-pattern tool policy enforcement, Hermes-style skill learning, sub-agent streaming, and prompt cache optimisation for the Space Assistant architecture.

G-Q01 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO

AssistantDO Does Not Extend @cloudflare/think Think Class — Hand-Rolled Loop Misses Stream Resumption and Lifecycle Hooks

The Gap

AssistantDO is a raw DurableObject with a hand-rolled agentic loop. The CF Agents SDK ships @cloudflare/think — class Think<Env,State,Props> extends Agent — which provides: full agentic loop with configurable maxSteps, automatic message persistence in DO SQLite, stream resumption when a WebSocket client reconnects mid-tool-call, lifecycle hooks (beforeTurn, beforeStep, beforeToolCall, afterToolCall, onStepFinish, onChatEnd, onChatError), and a built-in this.workspace virtual filesystem. When a WebSocket client disconnects and reconnects during a long-running tool call, the spec starts a fresh completion — the in-flight tool result is lost, the conversation diverges from the persisted message list, and the client sees duplicate assistant messages.

Required Fix

Refactor AssistantDO to extend Think<Env, AssistantState, AssistantProps> from @cloudflare/think. Remove the hand-rolled while(continueLoop) loop — the SDK replaces it. Implement abstract getModel(): LanguageModel and the lifecycle hooks. Message persistence, tool execution routing, and stream resumption come from the base class at no cost. Existing DO SQLite schema for messages/sessions can co-exist via this.ctx.storage.sql alongside the Think SDK tables.

G-Q02 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.runAgentLoop()

Extended Thinking Signature Never Captured — Multi-Turn Chain-of-Thought Broken at Turn 2

The Gap

Anthropic extended thinking requires persisting each thinking block's `signature` field across turns. The signature lives at reasoning-end.providerMetadata.anthropic.signature. When the agent continues in the next turn it must re-include the accumulated thinking blocks with their signatures — the API returns a 400 error otherwise. The spec stores assistant messages but never extracts or persists this signature. Result: every turn starts fresh reasoning from scratch; multi-turn chain-of-thought is impossible; enabling extended thinking causes a 400 on turn 2.

Required Fix

After each AI call extract thinking block signatures: const thinkingBlocks = response.steps.flatMap(s => s.experimental_providerMetadata?.anthropic?.thinking ?? []). Persist thinkingBlocks as a JSON column on the assistant message row in DO SQLite. On the next turn, prepend persisted thinking blocks (with signatures) to the messages array before calling streamText. The CF Think SDK handles this automatically when you extend Think.

G-Q03 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO tool execution

No beforeToolCall() Hook — Malicious Skill Tool Invocations Cannot Be Intercepted or Blocked

The Gap

The spec's loop executes every tool call the LLM produces with no interception layer. The Think SDK's beforeToolCall(toolName, args) fires between "LLM decides to call tool X" and "tool X executes", enabling allow/modify/block/substitute. Without this hook, a tier-3 agent-created skill that passes the 27-pattern scanner at install time but contains a prompt-injection payload can instruct the LLM to call write() with path ../../spaces/otherSpaceId/config.json — and the agent will execute it. There is no runtime policy enforcement layer between LLM decision and side-effect.

Required Fix

Implement beforeToolCall(toolName, args): ToolCallDecision on AssistantDO. Check: (1) toolName is in agent's allowedTools set, (2) for filesystem tools, path is within spaces/{spaceId}/workspace/ (path traversal guard), (3) for exec tools on tier-3 skills, sandbox_only flag is enforced by requiring SandboxDO routing. Block the call and return a structured error to the LLM when any check fails. If using Think SDK, register this as the beforeToolCall lifecycle hook.

G-Q04 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.spawnSubAgent()

Sub-Agents Dispatched via Raw HTTP fetch() — No Abort Propagation, No Typed Streaming RPC, Orphaned Agents

The Gap

The spec dispatches sub-agents by calling fetch() on NaelaoAgentDO's HTTP endpoint and polling for results. The CF Think SDK provides subAgent(id, props) for typed streaming RPC, abortSubAgent(id) to propagate cancellation, and deleteSubAgent(id) for cleanup. With raw HTTP fetch: (1) if the parent agent is aborted (credits exhausted, user cancels), the sub-agent continues running and consuming credits indefinitely — no abort signal reaches it; (2) the parent must wait for the full HTTP response before seeing any result — no incremental streaming; (3) dead sub-agents from crashed parents are never cleaned up.

Required Fix

Use this.subAgent() from the Think SDK for sub-agent spawning to get typed streaming RPC, automatic abort propagation, and resource tracking. If retaining custom HTTP dispatch, at minimum: (1) persist the sub-agent DO id in the parent's sub_agents SQLite table, (2) pass an AbortController signal with timeout to fetch(), (3) have a cleanup alarm terminate sub-agents whose parent_id has no recent heartbeat. Never hold a live HTTP connection to a sub-agent for operations that may take minutes.

G-Q05 CRITICAL §16 — skills — SkillLoader / AssistantDO

Skill Executor Component Missing — SKILL.md Instructions Injected as Markdown with No Runtime Enforcement

The Gap

Skills inject SKILL.md instructions into the system prompt as XML and rely entirely on the LLM to interpret the markdown and generate correct tool calls. There is no executor that: (a) validates the LLM's tool call matches the skill's declared scripts array and resource_type, (b) routes execution to the correct tier (bash/python/cf-worker/cf-dynamic-worker), (c) enforces required_bins/required_env constraints before attempting execution. An agent invoking a Python-typed script will use the bash tool and try python3 — failing silently in a tier that lacks Python, or succeeding unsandboxed where it should not.

Required Fix

Implement a SkillExecutor that intercepts execute_script(skillName, scriptName, args) tool calls: (1) look up the skill in the loaded registry, (2) verify scripts[scriptName].type matches the target tier, (3) check required_bins are available (cached at skill-load time), (4) route to the correct executor: bash→WorkspaceDO.runBash(), python→SandboxDO.runPython(), cf-worker→deployDynamicWorker(). Return structured {stdout, stderr, exitCode}. Reject cross-tier escalation attempts (workspace-typed script calling browser APIs).

G-Q06 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — runFiber() / AssistantDO

Fiber Result Delivery Mechanism Undefined — runFiber() Returns Workflow ID with No Callback Path

The Gap

runFiber(task) starts a CF Workflow asynchronously and returns the workflow ID immediately. The spec never defines how the eventual result is delivered back to the AssistantDO. There is no polling endpoint, no callback webhook the workflow calls on completion, no Queue message, and no DO alarm triggered on fiber completion. The fiber pattern creates fire-and-forget workflows whose results are permanently lost — the agent never learns the outcome of async tasks it dispatches.

Required Fix

Implement fiber result delivery via CF Queues: (1) the Workflow's final step sends a Queue message to naelao-fiber-results with {fiberJobId, result, status}, (2) AssistantDO has a Queue consumer that matches fiberJobId to a pending fiber in the sub_agents SQLite table, (3) on match, deliver the result to the agent's conversation as a tool-result message, resuming the paused generation. Track fiber state in sub_agents: (pending|running|complete|failed) with result_json column.

G-Q07 CRITICAL §27 — execution-ladder — SpaceR2 / Tier 1 workspace tools

Workspace R2 Writes Are Non-Transactional — Concurrent Batch File Operations Can Partially Succeed

The Gap

The spec's Tier 1 tools (write_file, copy_file, move_file, delete_file) call R2 directly via SpaceR2. R2 has no native transaction support: if an agent issues write A, write B, write C and B fails, write A is committed and C never runs — the workspace is left in a partially written, internally inconsistent state. The @cloudflare/shell virtual filesystem provides transactional batch writes with auto-rollback on failure. The spec provides no equivalent atomicity for multi-file agent operations such as refactors or schema migrations.

Required Fix

Replace direct R2 multi-write sequences with @cloudflare/shell batch transactions: import { Shell } from "@cloudflare/shell"; const shell = new Shell({ sql: this.ctx.storage.sql, r2: env.WORKSPACE_BUCKET }). Wrap multi-file operations in shell.batch([...writes]) for atomicity. If using the Think SDK, this.workspace already uses this abstraction. Document which operations require batch transactions (multi-file refactors, schema migrations) vs. single-file ops that can call R2 directly.

G-Q08 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO architecture

AssistantDO Conflates MCP Server and AIChatAgent — Violates CF Think SDK Protocol Separation

The Gap

AssistantDO handles both AI chat completion (agentic loop, streaming responses) and MCP tool exposure (providing tools to other agents via MCP protocol) in a single class. The CF Agents SDK distinguishes Think/AIChatAgent (consumes tools, manages conversation) from McpAgent (exposes resources/tools over MCP to other agents). Mixing both means: the WebSocket handler must serve two different protocol handshakes, tools exposed via MCP cannot be independently versioned, and the MCP server cannot be composed with different chat agents.

Required Fix

Separate into AssistantDO (extends Think for chat) and AssistantMcpDO (extends McpAgent for tool exposure): class AssistantMcpDO extends McpAgent { server = new McpServer({name: "naelao-assistant", version: "1.0.0"}); init() { this.server.tool("searchMemory", ..., this.searchMemory.bind(this)); } }. AssistantDO connects to AssistantMcpDO as an MCP client, consuming its tools alongside other platform tools. This allows AssistantMcpDO to serve NaelaoAgentDO sub-agents without going through the chat loop.

G-Q09 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — Memory OS / AssistantDO

Agent Cannot Self-Manage Its Own Memory — No memory Tool Exposed to LLM (Hermes Pattern Missing)

The Gap

The spec's Memory OS stores facts in DO SQLite but memory management is only callable server-side (triggered by the extraction pipeline). The LLM has no tool to add, replace, or remove its own memory entries — it can only read them via system prompt injection. Hermes agents self-manage memory via a memory({action, key, value}) tool. Without this, the agent cannot correct a stale belief it discovers is wrong, add a new learning from a solved task, or remove a conflicting fact — all memory updates require explicit server-side code paths that may never fire.

Required Fix

Expose a memory tool to the agent: registerTool("memory", { description: "Add, replace, or remove entries in your persistent memory", parameters: { action: z.enum(["add","replace","remove"]), key: z.string(), value: z.string().optional() }, execute: async ({action, key, value}) => { if (action !== "remove") await this.upsertMemory(key, value, {confidence: 1.0, source: "agent-self"}); else await this.deleteMemory(key); return `Memory ${action} complete`; } }). Cap total memory entries per agent at 500; require removing an entry before adding when at capacity.

G-Q10 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.loadConfig()

Runtime Agent Config Stored in KV — Up to 60-Second Stale Config After Tool Revocation or Model Change

The Gap

The spec stores AssistantDO runtime configuration (model name, persona, allowed tools, billing tier) in Cloudflare KV, read at turn start. KV has eventual consistency with up to ~60 seconds of propagation lag. A space admin revoking a dangerous tool permission after a security incident will not take effect for up to a minute — the agent continues using the old tool allowlist. The CF Think SDK's configure<T>(config)/getConfig<T>() stores typed config in DO SQLite with immediate consistency within the DO.

Required Fix

Migrate agent runtime config from KV to DO SQLite using Think SDK's configure/getConfig: async updateConfig(newConfig) { await this.configure(newConfig); } and async getAgentConfig() { return this.getConfig<AgentConfig>() ?? defaultConfig; }. For cross-space config broadcast (platform-wide model change), send a CF Queue message to all AssistantDOs; the Queue consumer calls this.configure() on receipt — immediate within the DO. Retain KV only for the DO namespace registry lookup (routing spaceId to stub) where eventual consistency is acceptable.

G-Q11 CRITICAL §16 — skills — SkillSystem / AssistantDO

Hermes-Style Skill Learning Absent — Agent Never Crystallizes Solved Workflows into Reusable Skills

The Gap

Hermes agents automatically convert successfully solved multi-step workflows into reusable tier-3 skills: after task completion the agent generates a SKILL.md capturing the approach, tool sequence, and gotchas. The spec defines tier-3 as "agent-created" but never specifies when or how the agent creates skills. The agent repeats the same planning steps for identical tasks, never builds institutional knowledge, and the tier-3 skill directory remains empty unless a human explicitly creates skills. This negates the core self-improvement capability cited as the Hermes inspiration.

Required Fix

After each successfully completed multi-turn task (outcome=success, turn_count>3), trigger skill crystallization: (1) call the LLM with the task transcript and a classifier prompt ("Is this workflow generalizable?"), (2) if yes, generate a SKILL.md and save to spaces/{spaceId}/agents/{agentId}/skills/{id}/ in R2, (3) run the 27-pattern security scanner on the generated skill before activating, (4) reload skills on the next turn. Track crystallizations in a skill_crystallizations SQLite table. Cap auto-skills at 50 per agent to prevent unbounded growth.

G-Q12 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.beforeTurn()

No beforeTurn() Hook — Per-Turn Model/System-Prompt Override Impossible for Multi-Model Routing

The Gap

AssistantDO uses a single fixed model for all turns. For a production assistant, different turns need different models: simple queries → haiku (cheap, fast), code generation → sonnet, complex multi-step planning → opus with extended thinking. The CF Think SDK's beforeTurn(config): TurnConfig fires before each turn and can return overrides for model, system prompt, messages, tools, activeTools, toolChoice, maxSteps, and providerOptions. Without it, all turns run the same model regardless of task complexity, wasting cost on simple turns and underserving complex ones.

Required Fix

Implement beforeTurn(config: TurnConfig): TurnConfig on AssistantDO (or override in the Think subclass). Classify the incoming message with a lightweight heuristic (no LLM call needed): if simple → return {...config, model: haiku}; if code → return {...config, model: sonnet, maxSteps: 10}; if deep → return {...config, model: opus, providerOptions: {anthropic: {thinking: {type: "enabled", budgetTokens: 8000}}}}. This enables cost optimization without changing the user-facing API.

G-Q13 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.runAgentLoop()

No maxSteps Guard in Agentic Loop — Runaway Agent Exhausts Credits and CPU Without Bound

The Gap

The spec's while(continueLoop) agentic loop has no hard ceiling on tool-call iterations. A malicious prompt-injection payload or a skill in an infinite retry loop can trigger hundreds of sequential tool calls. Each call consumes tokens billed against space credits, occupies DO CPU, and triggers downstream side effects (R2 writes, sub-agent spawns, Queue messages). Credit exhaustion is a lagging signal — thousands of dollars of compute can be consumed before it fires.

Required Fix

Add maxSteps to the loop: const MAX_STEPS = config.maxSteps ?? 25; let steps = 0; while (continueLoop && steps < MAX_STEPS) { steps++; ... }. When MAX_STEPS is hit, append a system message: "Maximum tool call depth reached. Summarize progress and ask the user for guidance." and break. Expose maxSteps as a per-turn configurable via beforeTurn(). Also track accumulated tokens per turn and break on budget exhaustion. Emit both conditions to Analytics Engine.

G-Q14 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO observability

Agent Decisions Invisible to Tail Workers — CF Agents Observability Channels Not Wired

The Gap

The CF Agents SDK emits structured events for every agent decision point via observability channels (import { subscribe } from "agents/observability"): agentTool (tool invocations), agentSchedule (cron/alarm executions), agentState (state mutations), agentRpc (inter-agent calls), agentMcp (MCP connections). These auto-forward to Tail Workers with zero overhead when no subscriber is present. The spec's AssistantDO emits no structured telemetry for these events — only high-level Analytics Engine writes for billing. Debugging a misbehaving agent requires reading raw SQLite message history.

Required Fix

Wire observability channels in AssistantDO's lifecycle hooks: subscribe("agentTool", (event) => { env.ANALYTICS.writeDataPoint({ blobs: [event.payload.toolName, event.payload.status, spaceId], doubles: [event.payload.durationMs], indexes: [agentId] }); }). Add a naelao-agent-tail Tail Worker that receives these events and routes them to: (1) Analytics Engine for dashboards, (2) a DEBUG queue for forensic replay, (3) real-time alerts when tool error rates spike. Zero hot-path latency cost.

G-Q15 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO WebSocket handler

WebSocket Reconnect Creates Fresh Completion — In-Flight Tool Results Lost During Long-Running Tools

The Gap

When a WebSocket client disconnects and reconnects mid-turn (network hiccup, mobile app backgrounded), the spec creates a new completion context. If the agent was 10 steps into a 20-step tool chain, the reconnect causes: in-progress tool calls are duplicated (file writes and API calls run twice), and the client receives duplicate or inconsistent assistant messages. The CF Think SDK's AIChatAgent handles this with stream resumption: the in-flight stream is stored in DO state and replayed to the reconnecting client.

Required Fix

Buffer streamed chunks in DO SQLite: (1) on turn start, write stream_state={status:"streaming", turn_id, started_at} to storage, (2) buffer chunks in stream_buffer(chunk_index, content, turn_id), (3) on WebSocket reconnect, detect stream_state.status==="streaming" and replay buffered chunks to the new connection while continuing the live stream, (4) on turn completion delete stream_buffer rows for the turn_id. If adopting Think SDK, AIChatAgent provides this automatically.

G-Q16 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO scheduling

Global 5-Minute Cron Fires All Assistants Simultaneously — Thundering Herd on KV Registry

The Gap

A single CF Cron Trigger (*/5 * * * *) wakes all AssistantDOs simultaneously. For N active assistants this creates N concurrent DO activations with correlated KV reads at the same second. At 10,000 active assistants, the correlated spike causes KV read latency spikes affecting all heartbeats simultaneously. The CF Agents SDK provides this.schedule(cronExpression, taskName) within each DO, enabling independent per-DO heartbeats staggered by creation time.

Required Fix

Replace the global cron with per-DO scheduling: in AssistantDO.initialize(), call this.schedule("*/5 * * * *", "heartbeat") if not already scheduled. Each DO manages its own independent alarm, naturally staggered. The global cron trigger is only needed for the platform-level sweeper (stalled-DO detection, billing reconciliation). Migrate the heartbeat logic from the Worker's scheduled() export into a named task: async heartbeat() { await this.processScheduledJobs(); await this.checkSubAgents(); await this.processChannelMessages(); }.

G-Q17 HIGH §27 — execution-ladder — SpaceR2 workspace

No Versioned Workspace Storage — File Overwrites Are Permanent with No Diff or Rollback

The Gap

The spec's R2 workspace stores files with no version history. When an agent calls write_file(path, content), the previous content is permanently overwritten with no recovery path. For a coding assistant rewriting source files: a bad rewrite is irreversible, there's no way to diff before-vs-after, and the agent cannot undo its own changes if a test fails. Cloudflare's ArtifactFS (cloudflare/artifact-fs) provides git-based versioned storage for agent workspaces with commit history, branch-based experimentation, and rollback.

Required Fix

Integrate ArtifactFS as the backing store for Tier 1 workspace operations. For write_file: instead of r2.put(path, content), call artifactFS.write(path, content, {message: "agent: updated " + path}). Expose undo_last_write(path) calling artifactFS.revert(path, "HEAD~1") and diff_file(path) returning unified diff. If full ArtifactFS is too heavyweight, implement a lightweight versioning layer: before overwriting, copy current content to spaces/{spaceId}/workspace/.history/{path}/{timestamp} and keep the 10 most recent versions per file.

G-Q18 HIGH §27 — execution-ladder — Tier 1 workspace tools

Structured edit() Tool Missing from Tier 1 — LLM Reads Entire File and Writes Entire File Back

The Gap

The spec's Tier 1 tools include read_file and write_file but no structured patch/edit tool. For large files (>1000 lines), the LLM must read all N lines (O(N) context tokens), compute the diff mentally, then produce the entire modified file in write_file (O(N) output tokens). This wastes tokens quadratically with file size. The @cloudflare/workspace provides edit(path, edits[]) where edits is an array of {lineStart, lineEnd, newContent} patches applied atomically server-side.

Required Fix

Add edit_file(path, edits[]) to Tier 1: type Edit = {startLine: number; endLine: number; newContent: string}. Sort edits by startLine descending (bottom-to-top to preserve line numbers), apply each patch to R2 content, return {linesChanged, hunks, newLineCount}. Also add replace_in_file(path, pattern, replacement, flags) for regex replacements, and grep_workspace(pattern, glob) for project-wide search. These reduce token cost for large file edits from O(N) to O(edit_size).

G-Q19 HIGH §27 — execution-ladder — SandboxDO / Tier 5

Tier 5 Sandbox Is Custom Implementation — Misses CF Sandboxes GA Product (Ephemeral Micro-VMs with FUSE Workspace)

The Gap

The spec's Tier 5 SandboxDO implements custom resource management on top of a Dynamic Worker, which shares the same V8 isolate pool — not a separate VM. Cloudflare Sandboxes (GA 2026) provide ephemeral micro-VMs with: full POSIX filesystem, FUSE-mounted R2 workspace (writes auto-persist without explicit upload), configurable network isolation, pre-installed language runtimes (Python 3.11, Node.js 20, Ruby), and exec() API returning {stdout, stderr, exitCode}. The custom SandboxDO has weaker process isolation and requires explicit R2.put() for every file write.

Required Fix

Bind CF Sandboxes in wrangler.toml: [[sandboxes]] binding = "SANDBOX". Refactor SandboxDO to manage a CF Sandbox lifecycle: const sb = await env.SANDBOX.create({ network: "restricted", mounts: [{r2: env.WORKSPACE_BUCKET, path: "/workspace", prefix: `spaces/${spaceId}/workspace/`}] }). Persist sandbox ID in DO SQLite via this.configure({sandboxId: sb.id}). For exec: const result = await sb.exec({cmd: [...], timeoutMs: 30_000}). Set a DO alarm to call sb.terminate() after idle timeout. FUSE mount eliminates explicit file-upload bookkeeping.

G-Q20 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.runStep()

No beforeStep() Hook — Per-Step Tool Narrowing and Token Budget Injection Impossible

The Gap

The spec's agentic loop runs all steps identically with the same tool set and model parameters. The CF Think SDK's beforeStep(stepIndex, context) hook fires before each streamText call in the loop and can modify active tools, model override, and providerOptions for that step. This enables: narrowing available tools as the task progresses (disable write tools in the verification step), upgrading to a more capable model for the final synthesis step, and injecting remaining token budget into the step's system prompt to prevent overruns.

Required Fix

Implement beforeStep(stepIndex, context): StepOverride on AssistantDO. Track task phase in DO state (planning/implementing/verifying). For each phase narrow tools: planning→all tools; implementation→execution tools only (disable create_plan); verification→read/test tools only (disable write tools). Inject budget: const remaining = tokenBudget - context.usedTokens; if (remaining < 1000) add a system message warning. This prevents the agent from calling write tools when it should only be reading, reducing accidental overwrites in verification steps.

G-Q21 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.getModel()

AI Model Hardcoded at Module Level — No Per-Agent or Per-Space Model Override, No Billing-Tier Enforcement

The Gap

The spec initializes the AI model as a constant (anthropic("claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022")) at module or constructor level. The Think SDK requires implementing abstract getModel(): LanguageModel called once per turn. Without it: space admins cannot configure different models for different spaces (code-focused vs. customer-support space have different optimal models), and the platform cannot enforce billing-tier allowlists (free tier → haiku only, pro → sonnet, enterprise → opus).

Required Fix

Implement getModel(): LanguageModel on AssistantDO: const config = await this.getAgentConfig(); const modelId = config.modelOverride ?? BILLING_TIER_DEFAULT[this.billingTier]; const allowed = BILLING_TIER_MODELS[this.billingTier]; if (allowed !== "*" && !allowed.includes(modelId)) throw new Error(`Model ${modelId} not allowed on ${this.billingTier} tier`); return createAnthropic({apiKey: await this.getAnthropicKey()})(modelId). Store modelOverride in DO SQLite via configure<T>() for immediate consistency.

G-Q22 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.spawnSubAgent()

Sub-Agent Results Block Parent — No Incremental Streaming of Sub-Agent Progress

The Gap

The spec's sub-agent dispatch via fetch() requires the parent to hold a live HTTP connection until the sub-agent's complete HTTP response arrives. For a sub-agent doing a 10-step research task (minutes of execution), the parent is blocked the entire time. The Think SDK's WebSocket-based this.subAgent() streams results incrementally: the parent receives partial text, tool call events, and step completions in real-time. Without streaming, the parent cannot relay sub-agent progress to the user or detect and abort a stalled sub-agent early.

Required Fix

Upgrade sub-agent communication to WebSocket: (1) parent opens a WebSocket to the sub-agent DO endpoint, (2) sub-agent sends events: {type:"text",delta:"..."}, {type:"tool_call",name:"..",args:{}}, {type:"done",result:{}}, (3) parent forwards text deltas to the end-user's WebSocket in real-time. For abort, parent sends WS close(1000,"parent_abort") which the sub-agent's close handler uses to abort its own agentic loop. If adopting Think SDK, this.subAgent() provides this natively.

G-Q23 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — Memory OS / AssistantDO.buildSystemPrompt()

Memory OS Grows Without Bound — No Pruning Causes System Prompt Bloat and Context Window Exhaustion

The Gap

The spec injects all facts from the memory SQLite table into the system prompt each turn. With no upper bound and no pruning (decay_rate is defined but never applied per G-N40), a long-running assistant accumulates thousands of entries. The total character count can exceed 50,000 tokens, causing API errors when the full context exceeds the model's context window and burying critical instructions in noise. Hermes solves this with a bounded snapshot (fixed max entries, agent self-manages via the memory tool from G-Q09).

Required Fix

Enforce a memory budget at prompt construction: const MAX_MEMORY_TOKENS = 4096; const MAX_ENTRIES = 200. At buildSystemPrompt(): (1) query memory ORDER BY (confidence * exp(-decay_rate * age_days)) DESC LIMIT 200, (2) estimate token count of the rendered XML, (3) if over budget, drop lowest-scored entries until under limit. Run a weekly DO alarm trim: DELETE FROM memory WHERE (confidence * exp(-decay_rate * (julianday("now") - julianday(created_at)))) < 0.1. This keeps prompt size bounded while preserving the most relevant recent facts.

G-Q24 HIGH §16 — skills — SkillLoader / MCP integration

No MCP Tool Auto-Discovery — All Skills Hand-Registered, Cannot Leverage External MCP Catalogs

The Gap

The spec's skill system reads SKILL.md files from R2 and injects their descriptions into the system prompt. Adding a new integration (e.g., Jira search) requires writing a SKILL.md, an execution script, and uploading both to R2. OpenClaw and Hermes agents instead discover tools dynamically via MCP: connect to a Composio MCP server, call tools/list, and automatically gain access to hundreds of pre-built integrations (GitHub, Jira, Slack, Notion) without writing skill files. The spec's AssistantDO has no MCP client for dynamic tool discovery.

Required Fix
