Add MCP client support to AssistantDO: store MCP server URLs in the agent's DO SQLite config (per-space MCP catalog configuration). In beforeTurn(), connect to configured MCP servers via the Think SDK's built-in McpClient (Agent base class supports McpClient), call tools/list, and merge discovered tools into the turn's tools object alongside static skill tools. Cache discovered tools in DO SQLite with a 5-minute TTL to avoid per-turn latency. This allows spaces to add MCP server URLs and instantly gain new capabilities without deploying skill files.

G-Q25 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO turn lifecycle

No onChatEnd() or onChatError() Hooks — No Guaranteed Post-Turn Cleanup or Error Reporting

The Gap

The spec's agentic loop has no defined post-turn lifecycle boundary. When a turn completes or errors, no cleanup callback fires. This means: (1) temporary file write locks acquired during tool execution may not be released if the turn errors mid-flight, (2) sub-agents spawned during the turn that are no longer needed are not cleaned up, (3) billing events (deduct tokens used this turn) are best-effort inline rather than guaranteed post-turn, (4) metrics (turn duration, tool count, token usage) are not reliably emitted on error paths.

Required Fix

Implement onChatEnd(turn) and onChatError(error, turn) as explicit lifecycle boundaries. Use try/finally wrapping the agentic loop: finally { await this.releaseLocks(turn.locksAcquired); await this.cleanupOrphanSubAgents(turn.subAgentIds, turn.completedIds); await this.billTurn(turn.tokensUsed); await this.emitTurnMetrics(turn); }. On error: await this.abortSubAgents(turn.subAgentIds ?? []); await this.emitErrorMetric(error, turn). This guarantees cleanup even on WebSocket disconnects or DO evictions.

G-Q26 HIGH §16 — skills — SkillLoader

Skill Version Pinning Absent — Skill Updated in R2 Mid-Task Causes Tool Signature Mismatch

The Gap

Skills are loaded at the start of an agent session (or DO wake) by reading SKILL.md from R2. The spec provides no version pinning: if a space admin updates a tier-2 skill's SKILL.md (renaming a parameter or removing a tool) while an agent is mid-task using that skill, the agent's in-memory registry references the old interface but the executor may use the new one on next access. There's no ETag or version field checked at load time and no mechanism to detect a skill changed mid-session.

Required Fix

Add version pinning to the skill loading flow: each SKILL.md must declare version: semver in YAML frontmatter. At session start, record the loaded ETag/version for each skill in DO SQLite (skill_versions: skill_id, version, etag, loaded_at). Before each tool call that invokes a skill, check if the current R2 ETag matches the loaded one. On mismatch: abort the task with "skill updated mid-task, restart required". Tier-1 platform skills must follow semver breaking-change policy (no tool renames in patch releases). Tier-2/3 skills are immutable during a session — version locked at load time for the DO instance's lifetime.

G-Q27 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO tool execution

No afterToolCall() Hook — Tool Results Not Sanitized or Audited Before Being Sent Back to LLM

The Gap

After a tool executes, the spec forwards the raw tool output directly to the next streamText call with no interception point. This means: (1) a read_file result beginning with "Ignore all previous instructions..." is fed verbatim to the LLM (prompt injection via file content), (2) a list_directory on a 10,000-file directory returns a result that blows the context window, (3) tool results are never logged for audit/forensic purposes. The CF Think SDK's afterToolCall(toolName, args, result) fires after tool execution and before the result is appended to messages.

Required Fix

Implement afterToolCall(toolName, args, result): ProcessedResult: (1) prompt injection sanitization: if INJECTION_PATTERNS.some(p => p.test(result.content)) return {content: "[Result sanitized: potential prompt injection]"}; (2) size truncation: if result.content.length > 50_000 return {content: result.content.slice(0, 50_000) + "\n[...truncated]"}; (3) audit logging: INSERT INTO tool_audit_log(turn_id, tool_name, args_hash, result_size, executed_at). If using Think SDK, register as the afterToolCall hook.

G-Q28 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.initialize()

AssistantDO Schema Initialization Missing blockConcurrencyWhile() — First-Wake Race Corrupts Tables

The Gap

AssistantDO.initialize() creates SQLite tables (sessions, messages, memory, channels, sub_agents, etc.) via this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(). If two concurrent requests reach the DO on its first wake (a user message and the heartbeat cron firing simultaneously), both callers enter initialize() in parallel. Without blockConcurrencyWhile(), both execute the initialization sequence concurrently: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prevents duplicate tables, but subsequent INSERTs or ALTER TABLEs in the init sequence can run twice — causing duplicate seed rows, double column additions (SQLite errors on duplicate column names), and inconsistent initial state.

Required Fix

Wrap AssistantDO initialization in blockConcurrencyWhile() to serialize first-wake setup: await this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { const initialized = await this.ctx.storage.get("schema_initialized"); if (initialized) return; this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(CREATE_TABLES_DDL); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(SEED_DATA_SQL); await this.ctx.storage.put("schema_initialized", true); }). Note: blockConcurrencyWhile() is on this.ctx (DurableObjectState) not this.ctx.waitUntil (which is on ExecutionContext). All request handlers that depend on the schema must call a guarded ensureInitialized() before proceeding.

G-Q29 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.heartbeat()

Heartbeat Handler Calls runFiber() as Bare void — Fire-and-Forget Jobs Killed When Alarm Returns

The Gap

The spec's heartbeat handler calls void runFiber(job) for each scheduled job that is due. In a Durable Object alarm handler, the DO request lifecycle ends when the alarm handler's Promise resolves — any background promises not awaited are killed by the runtime. DurableObjectState does NOT have a waitUntil() method (only ExecutionContext does). So void runFiber() inside the alarm handler creates CF Workflow instances (incurring cost) but the DO may be evicted before the Workflow fully starts, leaving orphaned workflow instances in limbo.

Required Fix

For DO alarm handlers, all async work must be awaited or delegated. Fire workflows from the alarm via CF Queues: (1) in the alarm handler, enqueue all pending jobs to naelao-fiber-queue (Queue writes are guaranteed even if the DO is subsequently evicted), (2) a separate Worker consumes the Queue and calls workflow.create() using ctx.waitUntil() to keep execution alive. Queue delivery is guaranteed independent of DO lifecycle — this ensures all jobs are dispatched even if the alarm handler returns quickly. Never use bare void promise() inside a DO alarm handler for operations that must complete.

G-Q30 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.buildSystemPrompt()

System Prompt Fully Rebuilt Every Turn — No CF AI Gateway Prompt Cache Anchor for Memory OS Injection

The Gap

AssistantDO rebuilds the entire system prompt every turn: base persona, skill XML, channel configs, memory facts, cron schedules — all reconstructed from SQLite. Anthropic's prompt caching requires the system prompt to start with a static cacheable prefix. Because the Memory OS injection (potentially thousands of tokens) is included in the single system prompt string, the cache sees a MISS on every turn where any memory fact changed. At 4,000 tokens of memory per turn billed at full input price, a busy assistant accumulates 10x cost vs. a cached equivalent.

Required Fix

Split the system prompt into a static cached prefix and a dynamic suffix. Pass them as separate array entries in the system messages parameter: messages: [{role:"system", content: STATIC_PREFIX, experimental_providerMetadata: {anthropic: {cacheControl: {type: "ephemeral"}}}}, {role:"system", content: dynamicMemorySuffix}]. The static prefix contains: base persona, platform rules, skill instructions (rarely change), channel configs (change infrequently). The dynamic suffix contains: current memory facts, today's date, current task context. This makes 80-90% of the system prompt cacheable, reducing input token cost by 50-80% for long-running agents.

Appendix R

Tenth-Pass Full-Spectrum Technical Gap Analysis

35 new gaps covering: eval() prohibition breaking artifacts, float money storage, shell injection via LLM tool names, space isolation timing, DO non-storage I/O interleaving, GDPR ghost-vector deletion, space cleanup cascade, CF Workflows 1000-step limit, embedding model versioning, streaming billing on disconnect, slug race conditions, skill scanner obfuscation bypass, Hono body double-read, Workflow replay side effects, and CF platform limit gaps.

G-R01 CRITICAL §artifact / dynamic-workers — Artifact execution engine

Dynamic TypeScript eval() Prohibited in CF Workers — Artifacts Feature Is Non-Functional

The Gap

The spec describes an Artifacts system where agents write TypeScript to R2 and execute it at runtime. CF Workers' V8 isolate explicitly prohibits runtime code generation from strings: eval(), new Function(string), and dynamic import() of data-URI strings all throw "Code generation from strings disallowed" at runtime, regardless of Content Security Policy headers. Any implementation that loads TypeScript source from R2 and attempts to execute it via eval() or new Function() will fail 100% of the time. The entire artifact execution feature as described is non-functional on the CF Workers runtime.

Required Fix

Use CF Workers for Platforms (Dispatch Namespace) to execute agent-written code. Workers for Platforms allows deploying arbitrary user-written Workers into a namespace at runtime via the API and invoking them via a dispatch Worker: const ns = env.DISPATCH_NAMESPACE; const worker = ns.get(workerId); return worker.fetch(request). Alternatively, restrict agent-generated logic to a JSON-based DSL (step definitions, conditional branches, tool call sequences) interpreted by a fixed platform Worker with no dynamic code execution. Never pass agent-generated strings to eval() or new Function().

G-R02 CRITICAL §naelao-billing / §schema — SpaceDO / BillingDO

Money Stored as REAL (Float) in SQLite — Rounding Errors Compound Over Millions of Transactions

The Gap

SpaceDO's SQLite schema declares balance_usd REAL, amount_usd REAL, and credits_limit REAL. JavaScript and SQLite IEEE 754 doubles cannot represent all decimal fractions exactly: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004. Billing calculations like (inputTokens / 1_000_000) * 3.00 propagate rounding error into every stored balance. Over millions of agent runs, rounding errors accumulate into unaccounted revenue in the tens-of-thousands-of-dollars range. Additionally, the code path that calculates remaining credits uses Infinity cast to number when credits_limit is null — Infinity - positive_number = Infinity, making every comparison against a budget nonsensical.

Required Fix

Store all monetary values as INTEGER in micro-cents (1 USD = 100,000,000 micro-cents) or as TEXT in exact decimal format: ALTER TABLE spaces CHANGE balance_usd balance_microcents INTEGER DEFAULT 0. Perform all arithmetic in integer micro-cents: const costMicrocents = Math.round((inputTokens * MODEL_PRICE_PER_TOKEN_MICROCENTS)); then use SQLite integer arithmetic. Never store financial values as REAL/float. Replace the Infinity fallback with a large sentinel integer (e.g., 9_007_199_254_740_991 for "unlimited") and document what the sentinel means.

G-R03 CRITICAL §27 — execution-ladder / §sandbox-do — SandboxDO.exec()

Shell Injection via LLM-Supplied Tool Name — Unsanitized Command Passed Directly to exec()

The Gap

The spec's SandboxDO routes tool calls by using the LLM-produced toolName directly as part of the shell command dispatched to the execution environment. There is no whitelist check between "LLM selects a tool name" and "that name becomes a shell argument." A prompt-injection attack can cause the LLM to produce toolName values like "ls; rm -rf /workspace" or tool argument strings that embed shell metacharacters. Even if the sandbox is isolated, the agent can destroy its own workspace, exfiltrate file contents via DNS channels, or exhaust disk quota — all through tool name / argument injection.

Required Fix

Whitelist every tool name against a hardcoded registry before dispatch: const ALLOWED_TOOLS = new Set(["read_file","write_file","list_directory","bash","python"]); if (!ALLOWED_TOOLS.has(toolName)) throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${toolName}`). For bash/python execution, pass code as a stdin pipe rather than shell argument: exec({cmd: ["python3"], stdin: codeFromLLM}) so that the code string is never interpolated into a shell command. For file path arguments, normalize with path.posix.normalize() and assert the result starts with /workspace/ before use. Treat all LLM-generated strings as untrusted user input.

G-R04 CRITICAL §naelao-agent-do / §naelao-threads-impl — NaelaoAgentDO.run()

Space Isolation Check Fires After Database Writes — Attacker Records Session Before Receiving 403

The Gap

NaelaoAgentDO.run() validates that the incoming request's spaceId matches this.spaceId only after creating a session row and inserting the user message into DO SQLite. An attacker who sends a cross-space request will have their message persisted, a session ID allocated, and token usage tentatively recorded — all before the 403 is returned. This means cross-space messages appear in audit logs as legitimate sessions, token allocations are charged to the wrong space's quota, and session IDs from other spaces are disclosed in error response bodies.

Required Fix

Move the space isolation check to the very first line of NaelaoAgentDO.run() before any database operations: if (this.spaceId !== spaceId) return new Response("Forbidden", {status: 403}). Also remove spaceId from the error response body (do not disclose what spaceId the DO was actually configured for). Additionally, add space_id to the sessions table WHERE clause on every query: SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ? AND space_id = ? — preventing a session from one space being used in another even if the check is bypassed.

G-R05 CRITICAL §naelao-agent-do — AssistantDO / NaelaoAgentDO

Non-Storage I/O (fetch, R2 writes) Inside DO Allows Request Interleaving — State Corruption

The Gap

CF Durable Objects' input gate only protects storage operations (this.ctx.storage.*). Calls to fetch(), env.R2.put(), env.QUEUE.send(), and similar non-storage I/O do NOT block incoming requests during their execution. If AssistantDO issues a fetch() to an external LLM API (which may take 5-30 seconds), concurrent WebSocket messages or heartbeat requests can arrive and interleave — reading stale in-memory state (this.activeRuns, this.lastHeartbeat, etc.) while the first request awaits the network call. This causes: lost increments to in-memory counters, race conditions in the agentic loop state machine, and double-processing of scheduled jobs.

Required Fix

Two mitigations: (1) For mutable in-memory state accessed around await boundaries, use blockConcurrencyWhile() to serialize: await this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { const state = readInMemoryState(); await fetch(externalAPI); writeInMemoryState(newState); }). This blocks all other requests until the critical section completes. (2) Eliminate reliance on mutable in-memory class fields for any state that must survive concurrent access — store it in DO SQLite (which IS protected by the input gate) and reload it around each await boundary. Document which class fields are safe to read across await (read-only, initialized once) vs. unsafe (mutated during request handling).

G-R06 CRITICAL §naelao-knowledge — Knowledge deletion handler

Vectorize.deleteByIds() Never Called on Document Deletion — Ghost Vectors Accumulate, GDPR Violation

The Gap

When a knowledge document is deleted via the DELETE /knowledge/documents/:id endpoint, the handler removes rows from the DO SQLite knowledge_chunks table but never calls env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(chunkVectorIds). The deleted document's embedding vectors remain indexed in Vectorize indefinitely. This causes: (1) semantic search returns results from documents the user has explicitly deleted — a correctness failure and a GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure) violation, (2) the Vectorize index grows without bound and costs accumulate for vectors that serve no purpose, (3) a content moderation scenario where a user deletes harmful content but it continues surfacing in search.

Required Fix

Before executing the DELETE SQL, query all vector IDs for the document: const chunks = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("SELECT vector_id FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE document_id = ?", docId)]; const vectorIds = chunks.map(r => r.vector_id).filter(Boolean). Then atomically delete from both: await Promise.all([this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("DELETE FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE document_id = ?", docId), env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(vectorIds)]). Add a nightly reconciliation CF Workflow that queries all vector IDs in Vectorize metadata and cross-references with knowledge_chunks to find and delete orphans from any missed deletions.

G-R07 CRITICAL §naelao-spaces-full — Space deletion endpoint

Space Deletion Leaves R2, Vectorize, and KV Orphans — No Cascade Cleanup, Unbounded Storage Cost

The Gap

The space deletion endpoint removes the SpaceDO and its SQLite records but does not clean up: R2 objects under spaces/{spaceId}/ (workspace files, skill archives, session exports), Vectorize vectors with metadata.space_id = spaceId, KV entries prefixed with space:{spaceId}:*, or nested sub-space DOs. For a space with 10,000 workspace files and a rich knowledge base, this leaves gigabytes of R2 storage billing indefinitely post-deletion. R2 charges $0.015/GB/month — 100 deleted spaces each with 5 GB of orphaned files = $7,500/month in phantom charges. GDPR Article 17 requires data erasure.

Required Fix

Implement deletion as a CF Workflow to handle the multi-step, long-running cleanup: step 1: list and delete R2 objects with cursor pagination (do { page = await env.R2.list({prefix: `spaces/${spaceId}/`, cursor}); await Promise.all(page.objects.map(o => env.R2.delete(o.key))); cursor = page.cursor; } while (page.truncated)), step 2: env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByMetadata({filter: {space_id: {$eq: spaceId}}}), step 3: scan and delete KV entries (list with prefix), step 4: mark SpaceDO as deleted (not hard-delete immediately — wait for Workflow completion). Add a space_deletion_status SQLite table tracking workflow progress.

G-R08 CRITICAL §workflows — CF Workflows / runFiber()

CF Workflows 1,000 Step Hard Limit — Long-Running Agent Tasks Silently Terminate Mid-Run

The Gap

CF Workflows enforces a hard limit of 1,000 steps per workflow instance. A research agent running an autonomous task loop with 10 tool calls per iteration × 150 iterations = 1,500 steps will be silently terminated at step 1,000 with no error propagated to the user and no continuation. The spec describes fibers running until task completion with no mention of the step limit, no checkpoint strategy, and no continuation workflow pattern. Agents that hit this limit appear to hang — the fiber status goes to "failed" but the user was never told the task was truncated.

Required Fix

Implement checkpoint-and-continue for long-running fibers. Track step_count within the workflow. At step 800 (80% of limit): step.do("checkpoint", async () => { const state = gatherCurrentState(); await env.R2.put(`fibers/${fiberId}/checkpoint.json`, JSON.stringify(state)); return {checkpointed: true, state} }). Then await step.sleep(100) and spawn a continuation workflow: const next = await env.FIBER_WORKFLOW.create({params: {fiberId, resumeFromCheckpoint: true}}). The continuation workflow loads the checkpoint and continues. This creates a transparent chain of workflow instances from the user's perspective while staying within the 1,000 step limit per instance.

G-R09 CRITICAL §naelao-knowledge — knowledge_chunks schema

Embedding Model Version Not Tracked — Model Upgrade Silently Invalidates All Existing Vectors

The Gap

The knowledge_chunks table stores chunk text and vector_id but no embedding_model field. Vectorize vectors embed documents in a specific model's vector space (e.g., @cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5 produces 768-dimensional vectors). When the platform upgrades the embedding model (to a different dimension count or different model family), new query embeddings live in a different vector space from existing indexed vectors. Cosine similarity between a new query vector and an old indexed vector becomes essentially random noise. The knowledge search feature silently degrades to returning random results with no error.

Required Fix

Add embedding_model TEXT NOT NULL to the knowledge_chunks DDL and to the Vectorize vector metadata: await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.insert([{id: chunkId, values: embedding, metadata: {space_id, doc_id, model: EMBEDDING_MODEL}}]). On knowledge search, verify the query uses the same model as indexed chunks: const models = [...new Set(chunks.map(c => c.embedding_model))]; if (models.some(m => m !== CURRENT_MODEL)) throw new Error("Knowledge index needs re-embedding; model has changed"). Implement a re-embedding Workflow triggered on model upgrades: iterate all chunks, re-embed with new model, deleteByIds old, insert new vectors with updated model metadata.

G-R10 CRITICAL §naelao-threads-impl / §ai-gateway — createSSEStream / token billing

Token Billing Skipped When Streaming Client Disconnects — Free Inference via Intentional Disconnect

The Gap

The spec records token usage only when the streaming response reaches its final SSE chunk ([DONE] marker). If a client intentionally disconnects after receiving the first streamed token, the LLM continues generating to completion (the server side does not know the client disconnected until it tries to write to the closed socket) but the final billing event is never written. An attacker can receive the first sentence of a response, disconnect, and pay zero tokens. With a 100K-token context window, a single "free" run costs $0.30-$3.00 in unrecorded inference cost.

Required Fix

Pre-deduct an estimated credit before streaming starts, then reconcile after the stream ends regardless of client connection state. Pattern: (1) const estimatedCost = estimateTokens(messages) * COST_PER_TOKEN; await deductCredits(spaceId, estimatedCost, {provisional: true}), (2) start streaming via ctx.waitUntil() so the stream continues even if the Response has been sent, (3) after stream completion (or AbortError from disconnected client), record actual token counts and refund the difference: await reconcileCredits(spaceId, estimatedCost, actualCost). The key is using ctx.waitUntil() to keep the token recording alive after the Response returns, and using a provisional charge that prevents double-spending.

G-R11 CRITICAL §naelao-agent-do — NaelaoAgentDO session queries

Session Queries Lack space_id Predicate — Cross-Space Session Hijacking

The Gap

Multiple DO SQLite queries in NaelaoAgentDO look up sessions by thread_id alone: SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?. The returned session is used to authorize subsequent operations (appending messages, running tools, accessing memory). An attacker who discovers a valid thread_id from one space can send a request to a different space's AgentDO and receive that thread's session, gaining access to another space's conversation history, tool execution context, and memory. The DO sharding means space B's AgentDO holds thread data for space B — but if a session lookup doesn't validate space_id, a crafted request can land on the correct DO with a foreign thread_id.

Required Fix

Add space_id to every session lookup and all child table queries: SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ? AND space_id = ?. The space_id should be stored in the sessions row at insert time (INSERT INTO sessions (thread_id, space_id, ...) VALUES (?, ?, ...)) and validated on every subsequent access. Additionally, add a foreign-key-like application-level assertion: after loading the session, assert session.space_id === this.spaceId before proceeding with any operation. This is defense-in-depth in addition to the early-check fix from G-R04.

G-R12 CRITICAL §naelao-spaces-full / §naelao-admin — Product conversation access flag

Conversation Log Access Flag Settable Without Admin Approval — GDPR Data Processing Bypass

The Gap

The spec's product PATCH endpoint allows builders to set conversationLogAccess: true on their product, enabling them to read user conversation histories. The endpoint does not verify that conversationAccessApprovedBy is populated with a valid Naelao admin ID. Any builder can enable this flag immediately via API, reading user private conversations without the human review process that data protection laws (GDPR Article 6, CCPA) require before enabling conversation data processing. This is a consent and authorization bypass, not a theoretical privacy risk.

Required Fix

In the product PATCH handler, if the request includes conversationLogAccess: true: (1) verify the requesting user is a Naelao platform admin (check against a naelao_admins KV list or a platform-admin JWT claim), (2) if not admin, return 403 "Conversation log access requires Naelao admin approval"; (3) if admin, set both conversationLogAccess = true AND conversationAccessApprovedBy = adminId AND conversationAccessApprovedAt = now(). Only the naelao-admin Worker should be able to set this flag. Regular builders should submit a request that creates a pending approval record, not directly toggle the flag. Audit all toggles to Analytics Engine.

G-R13 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — buildMemoryContext()

Memory Context Silently Capped at 20 Items — Oldest Memories Discarded Without Archival

The Gap

The spec's buildMemoryContext() implementation calls memory.slice(0, 20) to limit the context injection to 20 memory items. This is a silent, hard cap with no configuration, no notification to the agent that memories were truncated, and no archival of the discarded entries. An agent that has learned 50 important facts about a user's project will have 30 of them silently dropped from its context on every turn. The agent will then make decisions contradicting knowledge it demonstrably learned, with no indication of why.

Required Fix

Replace the hard slice with a token-budget-aware selection: (1) order memories by relevance score: confidence * exp(-decay_rate * age_days), (2) select memories greedily until token budget is exhausted (MAX_MEMORY_TOKENS = 4096), (3) append a count of omitted memories at the end of the memory block: "[...38 additional memories not shown due to context budget]". Archive memories that fall below relevance threshold rather than discarding: INSERT INTO archived_memory SELECT * FROM memory WHERE score < 0.1. Expose an un-archive command so the agent can request archived memory on demand via the memory tool.

G-R14 HIGH §16 — skills — SkillLoader.scanSkillContent()

27-Pattern Skill Scanner Bypassed by Obfuscation — AST Analysis Required for Untrusted Skills

The Gap

The skill scanner checks SKILL.md scripts against 27 regex patterns (process.env., require(, eval(, etc.) to detect dangerous code. This regex approach is trivially bypassed: process["en"+"v"], globalThis["proc"+"ess"].env, atob("cHJvY2Vzcy5lbnY="), Array.prototype.constructor.constructor("return process")(), and dozens of other obfuscation patterns pass all 27 checks. Tier-3 agent-created skills can use any of these to exfiltrate environment secrets, call external APIs, or escape the sandbox. The scanner provides a false sense of security that may cause operators to disable sandboxing for "verified" skills.

Required Fix

Replace regex scanning with AST-based static analysis for tier-2 and tier-3 skills: parse the script using a JavaScript/TypeScript parser (e.g., @typescript-eslint/parser available as a CF Worker bundle) and walk the AST to detect: MemberExpression on process/globalThis/eval, CallExpression for eval/Function/require/import(), string concatenation into member access (dynamic property access with computed keys). For tier-3 (agent-created) skills, mandatory SandboxDO execution regardless of scan result — treat as always-untrusted. For tier-1 platform skills, keep the regex scanner as a fast pre-check but require SHA-256 signature verification as the primary trust anchor.

G-R15 HIGH §naelao-credentials / §naelao-triggers — Webhook credential storage

Webhook Secrets Have No Rotation Mechanism — Compromised Secret Permanently Valid

The Gap

Webhook signing secrets stored in naelao-credentials have no expiry, no rotation API, and no revocation mechanism. If a webhook secret is exposed (logged in a request body, leaked in a browser network tab, found in a git history), an attacker can forge signed webhook events indefinitely. There is no 90-day automatic rotation, no "rotate now" endpoint for space admins, and no grace period for dual-valid secrets during rotation. This applies to all external webhook sources: Stripe, Slack, GitHub, Linear, and custom providers.

Required Fix

Add webhook_secret_rotated_at TIMESTAMP and webhook_secret_previous TEXT columns to the credentials schema. Implement rotation: (1) generate new secret, (2) store new secret as active, (3) store old secret in webhook_secret_previous with a 7-day grace period, (4) during verification accept either current or previous secret (if previous still within grace), (5) after 7 days, null out previous. Trigger automatic rotation at 90 days via a DO alarm in CredentialsDO. Add a POST /credentials/:id/rotate endpoint for manual rotation. Emit a rotation event to Analytics Engine and notify space admins via email when rotation occurs.

G-R16 HIGH §space-type-versioning / §naelao-spaces-full — SpaceTypeRegistryDO.loadManifest()

Space Type Manifest Loaded Without Signature — Missing signature Field Silently Ignored

The Gap

The spec describes SpaceTypeRegistryDO loading space type manifests that include configuration for allowed skills, billing caps, and execution permissions. The loading code calls verify(manifest.signature) but does not check whether the signature field is present before calling verify(). If a compromised SpaceTypeRegistryDO or a man-in-the-middle serves a manifest without a signature field, verify(undefined) returns true (or throws an uncaught TypeError that is silently swallowed) and the unsigned manifest is applied. An attacker controlling a single SpaceTypeRegistry can push malicious configuration to all spaces of that type.

Required Fix

Add an explicit presence check before signature verification: if (!manifest.signature || typeof manifest.signature !== "string") { throw new Error("Manifest rejected: signature field missing or invalid"); }. Verify signature before accessing ANY other field of the manifest — a rejection must happen before the manifest content is read. Pin the verification public key in the Worker code (not in wrangler vars or KV) so it cannot be overwritten. Add a manifest version field and reject versions older than the minimum acceptable (prevents rollback attacks). Log all manifest loads with their signature hashes to Analytics Engine.

G-R17 HIGH §naelao-spaces-full — Provisioner slug allocation

Portal Slug KV Lock Uses 30-Second TTL — Concurrent Provisioning Race Allocates Duplicate Slugs

The Gap

Slug allocation during space provisioning uses a KV lock: env.PORTAL_ROUTES.put("slug-lock:" + slug, spaceId, {expirationTtl: 30}). KV writes have eventual consistency — two concurrent provisioning requests can both read "slug available" and both successfully write the lock before either sees the other's write. Result: two spaces share the same portal slug. The portal routing lookup returns the first matching space, making the second space's portal permanently unreachable. Since KV doesn't support compare-and-swap, the entire approach is broken under concurrent load.

Required Fix

Move slug allocation to a SlugRegistryDO with DO SQLite (strong consistency): CREATE TABLE slugs (slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY, space_id TEXT NOT NULL, reserved_at INTEGER NOT NULL). Allocation becomes: INSERT OR FAIL INTO slugs VALUES (?, ?, unixepoch("now")*1000). SQLite PRIMARY KEY enforces uniqueness; DO single-threaded execution prevents races. If INSERT fails (UNIQUE constraint), the slug is taken. The DO stub is keyed by a constant ID (e.g., "slug-registry-singleton") to ensure all slug allocations go through the same DO instance. Retain KV for slug→spaceId lookup cache (fast, eventual consistency is fine for reads — a slug owner never changes after allocation).

G-R18 HIGH §naelao-spaces-full — Product creation handler

Product Slug Has No UNIQUE Constraint or Atomic Reservation — Concurrent Creates Produce Duplicates

The Gap

Product slug generation derives a slug from the product name (e.g., "My Product" → "my-product") in application code and inserts it into SpaceDO SQLite without a UNIQUE constraint on the slug column or an atomic reservation step. Two concurrent POST /products requests with the same product name will both compute "my-product", both check for availability (both see it as available), and both attempt INSERT — whichever finishes last wins but the first has already returned a 201 with the slug to the client. The client now has a slug that leads to the wrong product.

Required Fix

Add CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_slug ON products(slug) to the SpaceDO DDL (or UNIQUE in the column definition). This makes the second concurrent INSERT fail with a SQLite UNIQUE constraint error (error message contains "UNIQUE constraint failed"). Catch this specific error in the handler and return 409 Conflict with a message "Slug already in use — try a different product name". If the business requirement is to guarantee uniqueness with a suffix: attempt INSERT, on UNIQUE failure append -2, -3, etc. until success (all within the same DO request, leveraging DO single-threaded writes for atomicity).

G-R19 HIGH §naelao-spaces-full — SSO/OIDC config storage

OIDC Client Secret Tied to CF-Managed Master Key — Secret Rotation Impossible After Key Rotation

The Gap

SSO configuration stores the OIDC client_secret encrypted with a platform master key (stored in CF Secrets Store). If Cloudflare rotates the Secrets Store master key (for compliance, incident response, or routine key hygiene), the encrypted client_secret becomes unreadable — the Space's OIDC login stops working with no warning. There is no re-encryption workflow, no backup of the plaintext secret, and no mechanism for the space admin to detect the failure until users start getting authentication errors.

Required Fix

Implement application-level key versioning independent of the CF Secrets Store master key: (1) generate a data encryption key (DEK) per space: const dek = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)), (2) store the DEK encrypted with the platform master key in SpaceDO SQLite: dek_encrypted BLOB, dek_version INTEGER, (3) encrypt all secrets with the DEK (AES-256-GCM), (4) to rotate: decrypt DEK with old master key, re-encrypt with new master key, update dek_encrypted — client_secret itself doesn't need to change. Add a CredentialHealthDO alarm that tests OIDC config decryptability weekly and alerts admins if decryption fails before users experience login failures.

G-R20 HIGH §naelao-spaces-full — Space type/scenario management

Sub-Space scenario_type Mutable After Creation — Space Type Contract Violated by PATCH

The Gap

The spec establishes immutable scenario types (agency_shell, workspace, marketplace, etc.) that govern permission models, billing, and capability sets. However, the space PATCH endpoint allows updating scenario_type without verifying immutability. A builder who starts with a "workspace" space and later changes it to "agency_shell" bypasses the approval flow required for agency-shell spaces, gains access to sub-space management APIs they should not have, and potentially violates billing tier contracts tied to space type. There is no CHECK constraint or application guard preventing this.

Required Fix

Make scenario_type immutable after creation. In the space PATCH handler: if (body.scenario_type && body.scenario_type !== existingSpace.scenario_type) { return new Response("scenario_type is immutable after space creation", {status: 400}); }. Add a SQLite trigger as belt-and-suspenders: CREATE TRIGGER prevent_scenario_change BEFORE UPDATE ON spaces WHEN NEW.scenario_type != OLD.scenario_type BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, "scenario_type is immutable"); END. For legitimate type migrations (rare), provide a separate admin-only migration endpoint with audit logging and require explicit confirmation from a Naelao admin.

G-R21 HIGH §naelao-threads-impl / §naelao-agent-do — Message listing queries

Message Listing Queries Missing ORDER BY — Tool Results Arrive Out of Sequence in Agent Context

The Gap

Multiple message listing queries in the spec use SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ? or SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ? LIMIT ? OFFSET ? without any ORDER BY clause. SQLite's row return order without ORDER BY is undefined — it may return rows in insertion order, in rowid order, or in any order depending on internal page layout, DELETE history, and update operations. In an agent context where message ordering is semantically critical (tool result must follow the tool call that preceded it), arbitrary ordering means the LLM receives a corrupted context: tool results appear before tool calls, user messages appear after assistant responses. The agent produces non-sequitur replies.

Required Fix

Add ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC to every message listing query. For cursor-based pagination (WHERE id > ? LIMIT ?), the ORDER BY is especially critical: ORDER BY id ASC ensures the cursor correctly picks up from the last-seen message. Add a composite covering index: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_thread_time ON messages(thread_id, created_at ASC, id ASC). This index satisfies both the WHERE predicate and the ORDER BY in a single B-tree traversal with no sort step. Also apply this fix to all context reconstruction queries in AssistantDO and NaelaoAgentDO where thread messages are loaded for LLM context.

G-R22 HIGH §naelao-threads-impl — POST /threads/:id/messages handler

No Message Content Size Limit — Unbounded User Input Causes DO OOM on Context Reconstruction

The Gap

The POST /messages endpoint calls await c.req.json() with no size limit enforcement before inserting message content into DO SQLite. A user can POST a message with a 10 MB content string. When NaelaoAgentDO reconstructs the full thread context (SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ?), it loads all messages into memory simultaneously. Three 5 MB messages = 15 MB of in-memory string data before even considering token serialization. CF Workers have a 128 MB memory limit — large threads with oversized messages trigger OOM crashes mid-agent-run, losing the in-progress response and leaving the thread in an inconsistent state.

Required Fix

Enforce a message size limit at the POST /messages handler: const MAX_CONTENT_BYTES = 131_072; // 128 KB. const body = await c.req.json(); if (new TextEncoder().encode(body.content).byteLength > MAX_CONTENT_BYTES) { return c.json({error: "Message content exceeds 128 KB limit"}, 413); }. For legitimate large content (pasted code files, document text), implement a split-and-reference pattern: content larger than 128 KB is uploaded to R2 (POST /workspace/upload), receives a reference URL, and the message body contains the reference: {type: "r2_reference", url: "...", preview: "first 200 chars..."}. The agent loads large references on demand rather than in bulk context reconstruction.

G-R23 HIGH §naelao-sweeper — Sweeper cron handler

Sweeper Fan-Out to All Active Spaces Exceeds CF Workers 1,000 Subrequest Limit

The Gap

The spec's naelao-sweeper runs as a CF Cron Trigger and fans out to all active spaces by making one subrequest (fetch to a Worker or DO) per space. CF Workers have a hard limit of 1,000 external subrequests per invocation (paid plan, configurable to 10 million with higher plan). For a deployment with 2,000+ active spaces, the sweeper silently stops dispatching after the first 1,000 — the remaining spaces miss their WAL cleanup, scheduled job dispatch, billing reconciliation, and sub-agent monitoring. This failure is silent: the sweeper returns 200 OK but has done nothing for half the fleet.

Required Fix

Replace fan-out with a Queue-based dispatch pattern: instead of the sweeper making one subrequest per space, it enqueues one message per space to naelao-sweeper-queue: await env.SWEEPER_QUEUE.sendBatch(spaces.map(s => ({body: {spaceId: s.id, tasks: ["heartbeat","cleanup","billing"]}}))); CF Queues support batch sends of up to 100 messages per call and have no fan-out limits. A separate Queue consumer Worker processes each space independently. This also adds retry logic (at-least-once delivery) for spaces where the Worker temporarily fails, and allows the consumer to scale horizontally with multiple consumer Workers.

G-R24 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — GET /knowledge/search handler

Vectorize topK Hardcoded at 20 — Relevant Documents Beyond Rank 20 Never Surface

The Gap

The knowledge search handler calls env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query(embedding, {topK: 20, filter: ...}). For a space with a large knowledge base (5,000+ indexed chunks), the 20th-most-similar chunk has a cosine similarity score well below the top-5 results. The actual answer to a user's question may be the 35th-most-similar chunk — below the cutoff. The agent appears to have amnesia on topics that are definitively indexed. This becomes worse as the knowledge base grows and the score distribution spreads. Additionally, the spec applies no score threshold — results with similarity 0.3 (essentially random) are returned alongside results with 0.95.

Required Fix

Make topK configurable per space with a sensible default: const topK = spaceConfig.knowledgeTopK ?? 50. Add a minimum score threshold: filter out results below 0.5 cosine similarity. Implement a two-stage retrieval: (1) fetch topK=100 candidates from Vectorize (fast ANN search), (2) apply cross-encoder re-ranking using a small re-ranker model (env.AI.run("@cf/cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2", {query, passages: candidates.map(c => c.metadata.text)})) to select the top 5-10 truly relevant results. The re-ranker step adds ~50ms latency but dramatically improves precision, especially for paraphrased queries.

G-R25 HIGH §naelao-credentials — OAuth token refresh handler

OAuth Token Refresh Retains All Historical Token Values — Breach Exposes Full Token History

The Gap

The OAuth credential refresh handler writes the new access_token and refresh_token values to DO SQLite alongside the previous values (in a credentials_history table or via INSERT rather than UPDATE). If the credentials store is breached via any other vulnerability, an attacker gains not just the current token but every historical token for every OAuth integration ever refreshed. Many OAuth providers do not immediately revoke previously issued access tokens — historical tokens may still be valid. The credentials table should never store more than the current token pair.

Required Fix

Use atomic UPDATE (not INSERT) for token refresh: this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("UPDATE oauth_credentials SET access_token = ?, refresh_token = ?, expires_at = ?, updated_at = unixepoch('now')*1000 WHERE credential_id = ? AND space_id = ?", encryptedAccess, encryptedRefresh, expiresAt, credentialId, spaceId). Never store old token values — not in a history table, not in a backup column. For audit purposes, log only the credential_id, refresh timestamp, and a non-sensitive token fingerprint (first 6 chars of SHA-256 hash) to Analytics Engine. If a refresh fails, keep the old token active until the new one is confirmed valid.

G-R26 HIGH §naelao-agent-do — wrangler.toml / NaelaoAgentDO

NaelaoAgentDO Missing Unbound CPU Limit Declaration — Agent Times Out Under Default 30-Second CPU Budget

The Gap

CF Workers default CPU time budget is 30 seconds for paid plans (10ms for free). NaelaoAgentDO's per-turn processing includes: loading all thread messages from SQLite, building the system prompt with memory injection and skill XML, serializing tool schemas, calling the LLM (network I/O, doesn't count against CPU), parsing streamed XML/JSON responses, and executing multiple tool calls. The CPU-bound phases (prompt construction, JSON parsing, tool result processing) across a 20-step agentic loop can easily consume 30+ seconds of CPU time, causing the Worker to be killed mid-run. The spec does not declare a Unbound CPU limit.

Required Fix

Add an explicit CPU limit declaration in wrangler.toml for all agent-related Workers and Durable Objects: [limits] cpu_ms = 300000. This enables the 5-minute CPU budget available on paid plans. For prompt construction (the most CPU-intensive non-network operation), profile and optimize: pre-compute the static system prompt prefix once per DO wake (cache in a class field) rather than rebuilding it from scratch on every turn. For the message context, use SQLite's built-in JSON functions to serialize directly in SQL rather than loading all rows into JavaScript objects. Add CI linting to assert that all Workers handling agent loops declare cpu_ms >= 30000.

G-R27 HIGH §naelao-threads-impl / §naelao-agent-do — Hono middleware chain

Auth Middleware Calls c.req.json() — Route Handler Gets Empty Body on Second Parse Attempt

The Gap

The spec's auth middleware parses the request body to extract parameters: const body = await c.req.json(). HTTP request bodies are single-read streams in the CF Workers runtime — once consumed, the stream is exhausted. Any downstream route handler that also calls await c.req.json() (the most common pattern) reads an exhausted stream and gets either an empty object or a "Body already consumed" error. This silently breaks all POST endpoints that have this middleware in their chain: login, message send, tool execution, webhook handling — all receive empty payloads.

Required Fix

In middleware that needs to read the body, parse once and attach to context: const body = await c.req.json(); c.set("parsedBody", body). Downstream handlers retrieve via c.get("parsedBody") instead of re-calling c.req.json(). Alternatively, use c.req.clone().json() in middleware to read from a cloned request, leaving the original stream unconsumed — but verify this creates a full copy and not a shared underlying stream. A simpler fix: move auth parameter extraction from the body to Authorization headers or query params (which are not consumed on read), reserving body parsing exclusively for route handlers.

G-R28 HIGH §ai-gateway / §together-ai — createTogetherAIClient() / model routing

Together AI Model Translation Has No Fallback Validation — Unknown Model Returns Opaque 400 Error

The Gap

The model translation function translateModelName() maps Naelao-internal model names to Together AI API names via a modelMap lookup. If the requested model name is not in modelMap (misspelling, new model added to Together's catalog but not to modelMap, or a space passing an arbitrary model name), the function returns the unmapped name directly to the Together AI API. Together AI rejects unknown model names with a 400 error whose message ("model not found") provides no indication of which model was requested, why it failed, or what valid alternatives exist. The agent run fails with an opaque error.

Required Fix

Add validation before the API call: const translatedModel = modelMap[requestedModel]; if (!translatedModel) { return new Response(JSON.stringify({error: `Model "${requestedModel}" is not supported. Available models: ${Object.keys(modelMap).join(", ")}`}), {status: 400, headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"}}); }. Also validate that the space's billing tier allows the requested model (cheaper models only for free tier). Maintain the modelMap in a DO SQLite table or KV (rather than hardcoded) so new Together AI models can be added without code deploys. Log all model translation failures to Analytics Engine to detect when clients are requesting unsupported models.

G-R29 HIGH §ai-gateway — AI Gateway DLP configuration

AI Gateway DLP Response Scanning Silently Disables Streaming — Agent Gets Buffered Response

The Gap

Cloudflare AI Gateway's DLP (Data Loss Prevention) response scanning buffers the entire LLM response before forwarding to the client when response scanning is enabled. This silently overrides the streaming flag: a request sent with stream: true gets a buffered response with DLP enabled, eliminating the time-to-first-token benefit of streaming. For a 2,000-token response at 30 tokens/second, streaming delivers first token in ~100ms; buffering delivers nothing for ~67 seconds. The spec enables DLP on the AI Gateway binding but expects streaming latency — these two are mutually exclusive when DLP scans responses.

Required Fix

If low latency is required: enable DLP on REQUEST only (scan the system prompt and user message for PII before sending to LLM), not on the response. This catches PII leakage in inputs without buffering the output: aiGatewayConfig = {dlp: {request: true, response: false}}. If response scanning is a hard requirement: disable streaming for that gateway binding and compensate with a streaming simulation — poll for completion and send the full response when ready. Document this constraint prominently: "AI Gateway DLP response scanning is incompatible with streaming responses. Choose one." Add a CI check that rejects any config with both dlp.response: true and stream: true.

G-R30 HIGH §workflows — CF Workflows step execution

Code Outside step.do() Re-Executes on Workflow Replay — Side Effects Duplicated on Retry

The Gap

CF Workflows caches the result of each step.do() call and skips re-execution on replay. However, code outside step.do() blocks (variable initialization, logging, analytics writes, webhook calls, Queue messages) re-executes every time the workflow replays or retries a failed step. The spec's workflow implementations write analytics events and send Queue messages at the top level of the run() method (outside step.do() blocks). On a replay from step 3 (after step 2 failed), steps 0 and 1 are skipped (cached) but the top-level code runs again — logging the same events twice, sending duplicate Queue messages, and calling external webhooks a second time.

Required Fix

Wrap ALL side effects inside step.do() blocks. No code with external effects should appear at the top level of workflow run(): ❌ await env.QUEUE.send({...}); at top level. ✅ await step.do("notify-queue", async () => { await env.QUEUE.send({...}); }). step.do() result caching ensures Queue sends happen exactly once even on replay. For logging, use the step's output as the log payload: const logResult = await step.do("log-start", async () => ({timestamp: Date.now(), runId})); — the log event is captured in the step cache and not re-emitted on replay. Apply this pattern to all workflow definitions in the spec.

G-R31 HIGH §execution-ladder / §naelao-spaces-full — R2 multipart upload

R2 Multipart Upload UploadId Not Persisted Across DO Wakes — Large File Uploads Always Fail

The Gap

R2 multipart uploads require persisting the uploadId and each completed part's ETag across multiple Worker invocations. The spec's file upload handler initiates multipart upload (gets uploadId), uploads parts across multiple HTTP requests, and completes. Between upload part requests, the DO may be evicted (inactivity timeout 70-140s). The uploadId and parts array are stored in a class field (this.pendingUploads = new Map()) which is lost on DO hibernation. The next upload-part request finds no pending upload and returns 404, corrupting the multipart upload. R2 charges for incomplete multipart uploads (storage cost) that can never be completed.

Required Fix

Persist multipart upload state to DO SQLite: CREATE TABLE r2_multipart_uploads (upload_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, r2_key TEXT NOT NULL, parts_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT "[]", initiated_at INTEGER, status TEXT DEFAULT "pending"). On each upload-part completion, UPDATE r2_multipart_uploads SET parts_json = json_insert(parts_json, "$[#]", json_object("PartNumber", partNum, "ETag", etag)) WHERE upload_id = ?. On complete-upload: read all parts from SQLite, call r2.completeMultipartUpload(key, uploadId, parts), then DELETE the row. Add a DO alarm to call r2.abortMultipartUpload() for uploads older than 24 hours — R2 charges for incomplete multiparts until explicitly aborted.

G-R32 HIGH §operator-shell / §naelao-spaces-full — App iframe message handlers

postMessage Origin Not Validated in App Iframes — Forged Token Injection from Third-Party Pages

The Gap

App iframes in the Naelao operator shell receive TOKEN_REFRESH and CONTEXT messages via window.postMessage without validating event.origin. Any third-party page that embeds the Naelao app iframe (or opens it in a popup) can send arbitrary messages and have them processed as legitimate platform messages. A malicious page can send TOKEN_REFRESH with a forged JWT containing elevated role claims, or a CONTEXT message with a spoofed spaceId, tricking the iframe into operating in a different space's context. This is a standard postMessage spoofing attack.

Required Fix

Add event.origin validation to all postMessage handlers: window.addEventListener("message", (event) => { const ALLOWED_ORIGINS = ["https://app.naelao.dev", "https://app.naelao.com"]; if (!ALLOWED_ORIGINS.includes(event.origin)) { console.warn("Rejected message from untrusted origin:", event.origin); return; } processMessage(event.data); }). Also set Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'self' https://app.naelao.dev on all pages that should only be embeddable within Naelao (prevents third-party embedding). For TOKEN_REFRESH messages, validate the token's signature independently rather than trusting the message content — treat postMessage payloads as untrusted user input.

G-R33 HIGH §space-type-versioning / §dynamic-workers — Workflow / Dynamic Worker path validation

Workflow R2 Path Validation Uses startsWith — Crafted spaceId Bypasses Isolation

The Gap

Dynamic Worker and Workflow loading validates paths with: if (!workflowPath.startsWith(`spaces/${spaceId}/`)) throw Forbidden. A space with ID "abc-123" crafts path "spaces/abc-123" (no trailing slash); startsWith("spaces/abc-123/") fails for legitimate paths but a space with ID "abc-123-evil" has all its paths pass the check because startsWith("spaces/abc-123") is true for "spaces/abc-123-evil/workflows/backdoor.ts". Similarly, R2 list operations with prefix "spaces/abc-123" will match objects from space "spaces/abc-123-evil" in a flat namespace. Path construction must use exact structural matching.

Required Fix

Use path segments with explicit trailing slashes and structural extraction: const expectedPrefix = `spaces/${spaceId}/`; if (!workflowPath.startsWith(expectedPrefix)) throw new Response("Forbidden", {status:403}). For extracting paths, use URL path parsing: const segments = workflowPath.split("/"); if (segments[0] !== "spaces" || segments[1] !== spaceId) throw Forbidden — this ensures segment[1] is exactly spaceId, not a spaceId prefix. For R2 list operations, always append "/" to the prefix: env.R2.list({prefix: `spaces/${spaceId}/`}) ensuring the prefix terminates at a path separator. Audit all R2 prefix usages in the codebase for this pattern.

G-R34 HIGH §naelao-spaces-full — Space member role management

Member Role Downgrade Does Not Invalidate Active Sessions — Privilege Window Until Session Expiry

The Gap

When a space member's role is downgraded (e.g., from admin to viewer) or when a member is removed, the handler updates the space_members SQLite row but does not invalidate active WebSocket sessions or cached JWT tokens that still carry the old role claim. If the member has an active browser session with a JWT that expires in 24 hours, they retain admin privileges for the full 24 hours after being downgraded. During a security incident (compromised employee account), revoking access takes effect only after the attacker's session expires naturally. This is unacceptable for a platform handling user data and AI agent execution.

Required Fix

On role change or member removal: (1) query all active sessions for the member in that space: SELECT session_id FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ? AND space_id = ? AND expires_at > unixepoch("now")*1000; (2) for each session, close the associated WebSocket: const ws = this.ctx.getWebSockets().find(w => w.serializeAttachment()?.sessionId === sessionId); ws?.close(1008, "Role changed — please re-authenticate"); (3) add the session_id to a revoked_sessions KV set with TTL matching the token expiry; (4) in all auth middleware, check revoked_sessions before accepting a token. Also implement short-lived JWTs (15-minute expiry) with refresh tokens for lower blast radius.

G-R35 HIGH §ai-gateway / §naelao-knowledge — Workers AI / embedding calls

Workers AI Context Window Claimed in Docs Differs From Actual — Silent 400 on Oversized Prompts

The Gap

The spec references Workers AI model capabilities from Cloudflare documentation, which may overstate context windows. As of 2026, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it's actual context window is 128K (131,072) tokens, not the 256K documented in some sources. An agent constructing a prompt with full conversation history, memory injection, skill XML, and a large document chunk can easily exceed the actual limit. Workers AI returns a 400 error with a generic message; the agent has no fallback — it crashes the turn rather than truncating the context and retrying. This is a silent failure mode for users with long conversation histories.

Required Fix

Before every LLM call, count tokens and enforce a hard budget: const promptTokens = countTokens(messages, systemPrompt, tools); const MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW = MODEL_LIMITS[modelId] ?? 128_000; const MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS = Math.floor(MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW * 0.75); // reserve 25% for output. if (promptTokens > MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS) { messages = truncateMessages(messages, MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS - systemPromptTokens - toolTokens); }. Truncation strategy: keep system prompt and last N user/assistant turns intact, drop the oldest turns first. Maintain MODEL_LIMITS as a verified-from-source table in the codebase, not from documentation. Add a quarterly CI test that queries the actual Workers AI API with a boundary-condition prompt to catch limit changes.

Appendix S

Eleventh-Pass: Use the Platform — CF Native vs. Spec Custom Implementations

35 architectural gaps where the spec hand-rolls what Cloudflare already provides natively: withVoice mixin replacing VAPI, this.schedule() replacing cron-jobs.json sweeper, this.subAgent() replacing HTTP fetch dispatch, needsApproval: true replacing in-memory Promise resolvers, routeAgentRequest() replacing manual DO routing, useAgent/useAgentChat/useVoiceAgent replacing missing client SDK, this.setState() replacing ad-hoc SQL, this.sql template literal, Workers AI STT/TTS replacing external speech APIs, CF Realtime SFU for browser audio, and multi-agent team composition via facet hierarchies.

G-S01 CRITICAL §naelao-notifications-full / §05 — initiateVoiceCall() / AssistantDO

Voice Built on Third-Party VAPI Instead of CF withVoice Mixin + Workers AI Native STT/TTS

The Gap

The spec integrates VAPI (third-party) for voice agent calls: POST to api.vapi.ai with an external model, an 11labs voice provider, and a phone_number_id. This creates: (1) per-minute billing from VAPI on top of CF costs, (2) a complex webhook lifecycle that the spec never fully implements (no POST /webhooks/vapi handler), (3) dependency on VAPI availability for a critical escalation path, (4) no transcript access within the agent DO. CF provides a complete native voice agent stack: the withVoice mixin from @cloudflare/voice, native STT via @cf/deepgram/flux (built-in end-of-turn detection, 16kHz mono), native TTS via @cf/deepgram/aura-1 (context-aware pacing), and Twilio telephony via @cloudflare/voice-twilio — all processed in-process in the DO with zero external API cost.

Required Fix

Replace VAPI with the CF native voice pipeline: import { withVoice } from "@cloudflare/voice"; import { WorkersAIFluxSTT } from "@cloudflare/voice/stt"; import { WorkersAITTS } from "@cloudflare/voice/tts". class AssistantVoiceDO extends withVoice(Agent) { transcriber = new WorkersAIFluxSTT(this.env.AI, { eotThreshold: 0.75 }); tts = new WorkersAITTS(this.env.AI, { model: "@cf/deepgram/aura-1", speaker: "asteria" }); async onTurn(transcript, ctx) { const reply = await runAgentTurn(transcript, ctx); this.saveMessage("user", transcript); this.saveMessage("assistant", reply); return reply; } }. For telephony, use @cloudflare/voice-twilio adapter which routes Twilio Media Streams directly to the VoiceDO WebSocket — eliminating VAPI entirely.

G-S02 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants / §launchpad — AssistantDO.requestApproval()

pendingApprovals In-Memory Map Lost on DO Hibernation — CF needsApproval Tool Flag Is the Native Solution

The Gap

The spec implements human-in-the-loop approval by storing Promise resolvers in an in-memory Map: pendingApprovals.set(approvalId, resolve). When the DO hibernates (inactivity eviction after 70-140s), the Map is destroyed — all pending approvals are permanently lost. The waiting fiber hangs until the DO alarm fires and auto-rejects. This also has a race condition: the alarm and the approval decision handler can both fire near-simultaneously, calling the same resolver twice and executing the approved action twice (double email, double charge). CF's @cloudflare/ai-chat provides needsApproval: true on any tool definition — the framework pauses execution, sends the approval request to the client over WebSocket, and resumes when the client calls addToolApprovalResponse({id, approved}) — no in-memory Map, no lost promises, no race condition.

Required Fix

Replace the custom approval mechanism with the CF SDK pattern. In tool definitions: tools: { sendEmail: tool({ description: "Send email to user", inputSchema: z.object({to: z.string(), body: z.string()}), needsApproval: true, execute: async ({to, body}) => sendEmail(to, body) })}. The SDK persists the paused turn in DO SQLite automatically — hibernation does not lose the state. On the client, use the useAgentChat() hook which exposes addToolApprovalResponse: const {messages, addToolApprovalResponse} = useAgentChat({agent: "AssistantDO"}); and render approval UI when messages contain a tool-approval part. If retaining a custom flow (e.g., for mobile push approvals), store approval state in DO SQLite (not in-memory): INSERT INTO pending_approvals (approval_id, fiber_id, tool_name, args_json, expires_at) and use a DO alarm (not a Map Promise) to timeout.

G-S03 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — cron-jobs.json / AssistantDO heartbeat

Scheduled Tasks Use cron-jobs.json in R2 + Global Sweeper — CF this.schedule() Is the Native Solution

The Gap

The spec stores per-assistant scheduled tasks in cron-jobs.json in R2, read by a global sweeper cron every 5 minutes. Problems: (1) R2 read on every heartbeat tick for every active assistant, (2) the sweeper cron fires all assistants simultaneously (thundering herd), (3) no built-in retry for failed scheduled tasks, (4) cron expression parsing must be hand-implemented in the DO, (5) concurrent sweeper invocations can run the same task twice (no dedup). CF's Agent base class provides this.schedule(when, callback, payload, retryOptions) and this.scheduleEvery(intervalSeconds, callback, payload) — stored in a SQL-backed cf_agents_schedules table inside the DO itself, with built-in retry (maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs), cron expression support, and deduplication by schedule ID.

Required Fix

Replace cron-jobs.json with CF Agent scheduling. In AssistantDO: async addScheduledJob(job: CronJob) { const schedId = await this.schedule(job.schedule, "runScheduledJob", {jobId: job.id, task: job.task}); await this.sql`INSERT INTO job_schedules (job_id, sched_id, ...) VALUES (${job.id}, ${schedId.id}, ...)`; }. async runScheduledJob(payload: {jobId: string, task: string}) { await this.executeTask(payload.task); }. The SDK fires the callback in the DO at the correct time with per-call retry. To list active schedules: this.getSchedules(). To cancel: this.cancelSchedule(schedId). This replaces the entire cron-jobs.json / sweeper / R2-read architecture with in-DO SQL-backed scheduling.

G-S04 CRITICAL §naelao-sweeper / §05 — sweepSchedules() / heartbeat cron

Concurrent Sweeper Invocations Create Duplicate Cron Job Runs — No Atomic Dedup Guard

The Gap

The sweeper cron reads all due cron jobs (nextRun <= now), dispatches them, then updates nextRun. With at-least-once cron delivery, two sweeper invocations can overlap: both read the same set of due jobs before either writes the updated nextRun, both dispatch the same jobs as separate workflow instances. The user receives two emails, two charges are processed, two sub-agents are spawned — for every job that was due during the overlap window. The spec has no atomic compare-and-swap to prevent this: the UPDATE sets nextRun unconditionally, not conditionally on the old value.

Required Fix

Use an atomic compare-and-swap UPDATE as the dispatch gate: UPDATE cron_jobs SET next_run = computeNext(schedule), dispatched_at = unixepoch("now")*1000 WHERE job_id = ? AND next_run = ? AND (dispatched_at IS NULL OR dispatched_at < next_run). The WHERE next_run = ? clause ensures only the invocation that read that specific nextRun value can update it — the second concurrent invocation reads a different value (already updated by the first) and gets rowsAffected = 0, skipping dispatch. Only proceed to workflow.create() if rowsAffected = 1. This pattern is the SQLite equivalent of compare-and-swap and works correctly given DO single-threaded execution. Also, if using CF Agent scheduling (G-S03), this dedup is built into the SDK.

G-S05 CRITICAL §naelao-agent-do / §05 — NaelaoAgentDO / AssistantDO state

Agent State Managed via Ad-Hoc SQL Queries — CF this.setState() Provides Typed Persistent State

The Gap

NaelaoAgentDO and AssistantDO manage all persistent state through raw this.ctx.storage.sql.exec() calls, manually building INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT queries for every state field. CF's Agent base class provides this.setState(state: State) which: (1) persists state to a cf_agents_state SQLite table automatically, (2) broadcasts the state update to all connected WebSocket clients via the SDK's state sync protocol, (3) exposes this.state getter for reading current state, (4) fires this.onStateChanged(newState, oldState) hook for side effects. The current spec's pattern requires separate code for persistence, serialization, and broadcasting — three concerns the SDK collapses into one call.

Required Fix

Define a typed state interface and use setState: interface AgentState { currentTask: string|null; pendingApprovals: string[]; lastHeartbeat: number; activeSubAgents: string[]; }. In AssistantDO: await this.setState({...this.state, currentTask: taskId, lastHeartbeat: Date.now()}). Read state: const task = this.state.currentTask. Implement the hook: onStateChanged(state: AgentState, oldState: AgentState) { if (state.currentTask !== oldState.currentTask) { env.ANALYTICS.writeDataPoint({blobs: [state.currentTask ?? "idle"], indexes: [this.spaceId]}); } }. On client, useAgent<AgentState>({agent: "AssistantDO", name: spaceId}) provides a live-updating state object — no polling needed.

G-S06 CRITICAL §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO.spawnSubAgent()

Sub-Agents Dispatched via Raw HTTP fetch() — CF this.subAgent(ChildClass, name) Is the Native Solution

The Gap

The spec dispatches sub-agents by constructing HTTP requests to NaelaoAgentDO endpoints via service binding fetch(). CF's Agent base class provides this.subAgent(ChildAgentClass, instanceName) which: (1) resolves the child DO by class name + instance name (URL routing: /agents/{child-kebab}/{name}), (2) returns a typed stub with direct method RPC — no HTTP serialization, (3) supports nested addressing (grandchild via this.subAgent(GrandchildClass, name) on the child stub), (4) provides this.parentAgent(ParentClass) from the child to call back to the parent, (5) exposes this.parentPath (array of ancestors root-first). The spec's HTTP approach requires manual URL construction, response parsing, and provides no typed interface.

Required Fix

Replace HTTP sub-agent dispatch with CF SDK facets: async spawnResearcher(task: string) { const researcher = await this.subAgent(ResearcherDO, `researcher-${task.slice(0,20)}`); const result = await researcher.research(task); return result; }. Define ResearcherDO as a standard Agent subclass with typed RPC methods. The child can notify the parent: class ResearcherDO extends Agent { async research(task: string) { const parent = await this.parentAgent(AssistantDO); await parent.onSubAgentProgress({task, status: "started"}); const result = await doResearch(task); await parent.onSubAgentComplete({task, result}); return result; } }. Sub-agent URLs are auto-registered at /agents/assistant-do/{name}/sub/researcher-do/{name} — no wrangler.toml changes needed for routing.

G-S07 CRITICAL §05 / §operator-shell — Frontend client

No Client SDK Documented — CF Provides useAgent(), useAgentChat(), useVoiceAgent() React Hooks

The Gap

The spec describes the Naelao operator shell frontend but provides no client SDK documentation. Builders integrating the Space Assistant must write raw WebSocket or SSE code to connect to AgentDOs, parse tool call events, handle reconnections, and render approval prompts. The CF Agents SDK ships a complete React client: useAgent<State>({agent, name}) provides bidirectional state sync and typed RPC; useAgentChat({agent}) provides a full chat interface with streaming tokens, tool call visualization, and approval handling; useVoiceAgent({agent}) provides a complete voice UI with transcript, audio level, mute, and status. None of these are documented or integrated in the spec.

Required Fix

Define the client SDK layer. Install: npm install agents @cloudflare/voice. In the operator shell React app: const {state, call} = useAgent<AgentState>({agent: "AssistantDO", name: spaceId}); const {messages, input, handleInputChange, handleSubmit, addToolApprovalResponse} = useAgentChat({agent: "AssistantDO", name: spaceId, onToolCall: (tc) => handleClientTool(tc)}). Render approval prompts: messages.filter(m => m.parts?.some(p => p.type === "tool-approval")).map(m => <ApprovalCard onApprove={() => addToolApprovalResponse({id: m.id, approved: true})} />). Add to wrangler.toml: [assets] directory = "./dist" to serve the React app from the same Worker. Document this in the spec as the canonical integration pattern for space builders embedding the assistant.

G-S08 CRITICAL §naelao-router — Worker routing / DO resolution

Manual idFromName() Routing — CF routeAgentRequest(request, env) Handles Agent URL Dispatch Natively

The Gap

The spec's naelao-router Worker resolves agent DOs by calling env.NAELAO_AGENT_DO.idFromName(compositeKey) and constructing custom stub lookups for each DO class. The CF Agents SDK provides routeAgentRequest(request, env) which: (1) parses the URL path /agents/{class-kebab-name}/{instance-name}, (2) resolves the corresponding DO binding by class name → kebab conversion, (3) forwards the request to the correct DO instance, (4) handles sub-agent URL routing (/agents/{parent}/{name}/sub/{child}/{name}) automatically. The spec's manual routing requires maintaining a routing table, handling kebab-to-class mapping, and creating separate stubs for each DO type.

Required Fix

Replace the custom routing logic in naelao-router with routeAgentRequest: import { routeAgentRequest } from "agents"; export default { async fetch(request, env, ctx) { const agentResponse = await routeAgentRequest(request, env); if (agentResponse) return agentResponse; return handleNonAgentRequest(request, env, ctx); } }. In wrangler.toml, register all agent DOs: [[durable_objects.bindings]] name = "AssistantDO" class_name = "AssistantDO". The SDK maps the URL /agents/assistant-do/{id} to env.AssistantDO automatically. Agent class names are converted to kebab-case (AssistantDO → assistant-do) for URL segments. This eliminates the entire custom routing layer including the DO registry KV lookup.

G-S09 CRITICAL §naelao-notifications-full — Twilio / VAPI telephony

Twilio Media Streams Integration Hand-Rolled — @cloudflare/voice-twilio Provides It Natively

The Gap

The spec implements phone call integration via VAPI which internally manages the Twilio connection. If the spec ever integrates Twilio directly (for cost reduction or VAPI replacement), it would need to implement: Twilio Media Streams WebSocket protocol, audio format conversion (mulaw 8kHz ↔ 16kHz PCM), stream SID tracking, and call control REST calls. CF provides @cloudflare/voice-twilio adapter that handles all of this: it connects a Twilio Media Stream WebSocket to a VoiceDO WebSocket, converts audio formats, and routes control messages. The integration is: configure Twilio webhook URL to point at the Worker, adapter handles the rest.

Required Fix

Replace VAPI with direct Twilio + @cloudflare/voice-twilio: import { TwilioAdapter } from "@cloudflare/voice-twilio". In naelao-router, add a Twilio webhook handler: app.post("/webhooks/twilio/voice", async (c) => { const twiml = new VoiceResponse(); twiml.connect().stream({url: `wss://${c.req.header("host")}/agents/assistant-voice-do/${spaceId}`}); return c.text(twiml.toString(), 200, {"Content-Type": "text/xml"}); }). The Twilio Media Stream then connects to AssistantVoiceDO's WebSocket endpoint where the TwilioAdapter translates between Twilio's mulaw protocol and CF's PCM voice pipeline. In AssistantVoiceDO: const adapter = new TwilioAdapter(); this.onMessage = adapter.onMessage.bind(adapter). Cost: eliminates VAPI subscription entirely. Latency: one fewer hop (Twilio → CF directly vs. Twilio → VAPI → CF).

G-S10 CRITICAL §naelao-notifications-full — Voice call lifecycle

Voice Call Transcript Not Persisted via saveMessage() — Conversation History Broken After Voice Turns

The Gap

The spec's voice call implementation (via VAPI) fires initiateVoiceCall() and returns immediately. The voice turn transcript (what the user said, what the agent replied) is never stored in the agent's conversation history. After a voice interaction, the text conversation has a gap — the next text message has no context of what was discussed in the voice call. The agent may contradict itself, repeat questions it just asked verbally, or fail to act on commitments made during the voice turn. The CF withVoice mixin provides saveMessage(role, text) specifically to store voice turns in the conversation history shared with the text chat pipeline.

Required Fix

After every voice turn, call saveMessage() to persist to shared history: async onTurn(transcript, ctx) { const reply = await this.runAgentTurn(transcript); this.saveMessage("user", transcript); this.saveMessage("assistant", reply); return reply; }. Additionally, on call end: async onCallEnd(connection) { const summary = await summarizeCall(this.getConversationHistory()); await this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("INSERT INTO voice_calls (space_id, user_id, summary, transcript_json, ended_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,unixepoch('now')*1000)", this.spaceId, userId, summary, JSON.stringify(this.getConversationHistory())); }. This ensures the text conversation seamlessly continues after a voice interaction, and the full call transcript is available for audit and billing reconciliation.

G-S11 HIGH §05 — space-assistants — AssistantDO keep-alive

DO Keep-Alive Relies on 5-Minute Global Cron — CF this.keepAlive() Is the Native Solution

The Gap

The spec keeps AssistantDOs alive through the global 5-minute sweeper cron trigger that sends a heartbeat fetch to each active DO. This requires: the sweeper Worker, KV registry of active DOs, and a global cron schedule. CF's Agent class provides this.keepAlive() which: returns a dispose function, sends internal heartbeats at configurable intervals (default 30s), and this.keepAliveWhile(fn) which keeps the DO alive for the duration of an async operation. These are in-process — no Worker overhead, no KV lookup, no cron coordination.

Required Fix

Replace the external heartbeat with in-DO keepAlive: async onStart() { const dispose = await this.keepAlive(); this.ctx.waitUntil(Promise.resolve()); }. For long-running agent tasks: const result = await this.keepAliveWhile(async () => { return await runLongAgentTask(); }). Configure keepAlive interval: static options = { keepAliveIntervalMs: 60_000 }. The sweeper cron is only needed for platform-level maintenance (billing reconciliation, orphaned DO cleanup) — not for individual DO keep-alive. This eliminates the thundering-herd issue from G-Q16 where all DOs wake simultaneously.

G-S12 HIGH §naelao-notifications-full / §ai-gateway — VAPI / Workers AI audio

VAPI External Speech Models Used Instead of CF Workers AI Native STT/TTS

The Gap

The VAPI integration sends audio to external speech providers (11labs for TTS, VAPI's own STT). CF Workers AI provides free (included in platform cost) speech models: @cf/deepgram/flux for STT (continuous streaming, built-in end-of-turn detection with eotThreshold, end-of-utterance events, keyword boosting via keyterms[]), and @cf/deepgram/aura-1 for TTS (context-aware pacing, multiple speakers). Using external providers adds per-minute billing from a third party, increases latency (round-trip to external API), and introduces a dependency on provider availability.

Required Fix

Use Workers AI speech models via the withVoice mixin: transcriber = new WorkersAIFluxSTT(this.env.AI, { eotThreshold: 0.75, eagerEotThreshold: 0.55, eotTimeoutMs: 3000, keyterms: ["Naelao", spaceKeywords] }); tts = new WorkersAITTS(this.env.AI, { model: "@cf/deepgram/aura-1", speaker: "asteria" }). For multi-lingual spaces, choose model: "@cf/myshell/melotts". For alternative TTS: "@cf/xai/grok-tts". Configure eotThreshold between 0.5 (sensitive, picks up short pauses) and 0.9 (conservative, waits for definitive end of speech). The keyterms option boosts domain-specific vocabulary recognition for terms like "refund", "escalate", or custom product names.

G-S13 HIGH §naelao-notifications-full / §execution-ladder — CF Realtime SFU

CF Realtime SFU Not Used for Browser-to-Agent Real-Time Audio — Could Eliminate Telephony Dependency

The Gap

The spec's voice calls require a phone number (VAPI phone_number_id) — users must receive a phone call to interact with the voice agent. For browser-based users, CF Realtime provides a WebRTC SFU running at CF edge (330+ PoPs, anycast) that routes browser audio directly to a VoiceDO WebSocket. The SFU WebSocket adapter (auto-reconnect as of May 2026) connects the browser's microphone stream to the VoiceDO's PCM input, eliminating the phone call requirement entirely for desktop/mobile web users.

Required Fix
