Serialize turns with an explicit per-thread lock/queue: ```typescript private turnQueue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve(); async handleMessage(msg: UserMessage) { // Each turn runs strictly after the previous one finishes const run = this.turnQueue.then(() => this.runTurn(msg)); this.turnQueue = run.catch(() => {}); // keep the chain alive on error return run; } ``` Alternatively reject a new message with `409 turn_in_progress` while a turn is active, and let the client decide to queue or cancel.

G-W30 HIGH §Orchestration — Reliability — AssistantDO / orphaned sub-agents

Sub-agents have no parent-liveness link — if the parent dies, results are never delivered and work runs to waste

The Gap

A spawned sub-agent runs in its own DO and reports back by writing to the parent's status table, which the parent polls on heartbeat. If the parent is deleted or permanently fails, the sub-agent keeps executing (consuming credits), finishes, writes a result no one reads, and is never cleaned up. There is no parent-liveness heartbeat, no result delivery via a durable channel, and no orphan timeout.

Required Fix

Give sub-agents a durable result sink and an orphan timeout: ```typescript // Sub-agent delivers results to a queue keyed by parent, not by polling the parent DO await env.SUBAGENT_RESULTS_QUEUE.send({ parentRef, handoffId, subAgentId, result, completedAt: Date.now(), }); // A consumer routes the result to the parent if alive, or to a dead-letter store if not. // Sub-agent self-terminates if the parent is unreachable for N checks: if (await parentUnreachable(parentRef, { checks: 3 })) { await this.saveResult(result); // persist for later retrieval await this.terminate("orphaned"); // stop consuming credits } ```

G-W31 MEDIUM §Orchestration — Broadcast — NaelaoAgentDO / broadcast error isolation

broadcast loop has no per-socket error isolation — one closed socket aborts delivery to the rest

The Gap

The broadcast pattern `getWebSockets().forEach(ws => ws.send(...))` calls `send()` on each socket with no try/catch. A socket that closed between enumeration and send throws on `send()`, and because the throw is uncaught inside the synchronous `forEach`, delivery to all sockets later in the array is aborted. Clients enumerated after the dead one miss the message entirely.

Required Fix

Isolate each send and prune dead sockets: ```typescript broadcast(data: string) { for (const ws of this.ctx.getWebSockets()) { try { ws.send(data); } catch { // Socket is dead/closing — prune it, keep delivering to the rest try { ws.close(1011, "send failed"); } catch {} } } } ``` If using the SDK's native `this.broadcast()`, this isolation is handled — another reason to prefer it (see Appendix S).

G-W32 HIGH §Orchestration — Lifecycle — NaelaoAgentDO / onConnect ordering

onConnect can fire before schema/state is initialized — handlers read undefined state

The Gap

There is no guaranteed ordering that the DO's SQLite schema and initial state are fully loaded before `onConnect()` runs for an incoming WebSocket. If `onConnect()` (or the first message handler) reads `this.state.sessionId` or queries a table, it can hit undefined state or a not-yet-created table on a cold DO, causing intermittent errors that only appear under cold-start + immediate-connect timing.

Required Fix

Gate all entry points behind an init promise via blockConcurrencyWhile: ```typescript constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) { super(ctx, env); ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => { await this.initSchema(); // CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + migrations await this.loadState(); // hydrate this.state from SQLite this.ready = true; }); } async onConnect(ws: WebSocket) { // blockConcurrencyWhile guarantees init finished before any handler runs, // but assert defensively for clarity: if (!this.ready) throw new Error("not initialized"); // ... safe to read state } ```

G-W33 CRITICAL §Deployment — Migrations — platform / DO schema migration system

No versioned migration system — schema changes cannot be applied to a live fleet of thousands of DOs

The Gap

DO schema is created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in the constructor. This is idempotent but not versionable: there is no `PRAGMA user_version` tracking, no migration runner, and no path to apply `ALTER TABLE`/backfill changes to DOs that already exist. When a new column or table is needed, existing DOs never receive it (queries return NULL or error), and there is no way to coordinate or observe migration progress across the fleet.

Required Fix

Add a versioned migration runner keyed on PRAGMA user_version, run on every wake: ```typescript private migrations: ((sql: SqlStorage) => void)[] = [ (sql) => sql.exec("CREATE TABLE messages (...)"), // v1 (sql) => sql.exec("ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN workspace_id TEXT"), // v2 (sql) => { /* backfill */ }, // v3 ]; private migrate() { const cur = Number([...this.ctx.storage.sql.exec("PRAGMA user_version")][0].user_version); for (let v = cur; v < this.migrations.length; v++) { this.migrations[v](this.ctx.storage.sql); this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(`PRAGMA user_version = ${v + 1}`); } } // Call inside blockConcurrencyWhile in the constructor so it runs once per wake. ```

G-W34 CRITICAL §Deployment — Migrations — platform / hibernated DO schema drift

Hibernated DOs wake with stale schema after a schema-changing deploy — drift between dormant and active instances

The Gap

A new deploy ships schema changes, but a DO that has been hibernated for days does not run any code (and thus no migration) until its next wake. Between deploy and wake, the fleet is split: recently-active DOs may have run the new init path while dormant ones still have the old schema. Without a migration runner (G-W33) that reconciles on wake, a dormant DO can wake and run queries against a schema that does not match the deployed code, corrupting state or failing silently. This interaction is not covered by the chaos test suite.

Required Fix

Ensure the migration runner (G-W33) runs unconditionally on every wake, and make all queries schema-version-tolerant: ```typescript // In constructor, before serving any request: this.ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(async () => this.migrate()); ``` Add tests that explicitly exercise the dormant→deploy→wake path: ```typescript it("dormant DO migrates on wake after schema-change deploy", async () => { const id = newDOWithSchemaV1(); deploySchemaV2(); // bump migration list const woken = await wake(id); // must run v1->v2 migration on wake expect(await woken.userVersion()).toBe(2); }); ```

G-W35 HIGH §Deployment — Atomicity — platform / version skew

Deploying 22 Workers is non-atomic — a skew window breaks Service Binding contracts between callers and callees

The Gap

The platform is ~22 Workers deployed via `wrangler deploy`. Deploys are per-Worker and not atomic across the fleet, so during a rollout there is a window where some Workers run the new version and others the old. If a new caller expects a v2 Service Binding contract (new field, renamed route) while the callee is still v1 (or vice versa), inter-Worker calls fail or behave incorrectly for the duration of the skew. No compatibility strategy is documented.

Required Fix

Make Service Binding contracts backward/forward compatible and deploy callees first: ``` // 1. Expand-then-contract: add new fields/routes as ADDITIVE first (callee tolerates // both old and new request shapes), deploy callees, then deploy callers, then // remove the old shape in a later release. // 2. Version the internal contract explicitly: ``` ```typescript await env.NAELAO_BILLING.fetch(new Request("http://billing/v2/usage", { headers: { "x-contract-version": "2" }, /* ... */ })); // Callee handles both /v1/ and /v2/ during the transition. ``` Deploy in dependency order (leaf services first) and never remove a contract in the same release that introduces its replacement.

G-W36 HIGH §Deployment — Rollback — platform / schema rollback

No rollback strategy for schema-changing deploys — DO SQLite changes are not backward-compatible

The Gap

There is no documented rollback procedure. Rolling back Worker code is straightforward, but if a deploy applied a DO SQLite migration (dropped a column, changed a constraint, backfilled data), rolling the code back to the previous version leaves it running against a schema it does not understand. Destructive migrations (DROP, type changes) are irreversible, so a bad deploy that includes one cannot be safely undone.

Required Fix

Make migrations rollback-safe by policy and keep code compatible across one version: ``` // Migration rules: // - Only ADDITIVE migrations in a normal deploy (add column/table/index). // - Never DROP or rename in the same release that stops using the old shape. // - Destructive cleanup happens N releases later, after rollback window closes. // - New code must read BOTH old and new schema for one release (tolerant reads). ``` For data backfills, write to new columns while still maintaining old ones until the rollback window passes; only then switch reads and, later, drop the old columns.

G-W37 MEDIUM §Deployment — Config — wrangler / DO migration tag

wrangler.jsonc has no migration tags — renaming or deleting a DO class will fail or break instances

The Gap

Cloudflare requires a `migrations` block with a tag (and `renamed_classes`/`deleted_classes` directives) in wrangler config whenever a Durable Object class is renamed or removed. None of the ~14 DO bindings declare migration tags. A future refactor that renames `NaelaoAgentDO` will either be rejected by wrangler or, worse, strand all existing instances of the old class with no way to address them.

Required Fix

Declare DO migrations with tags from the start: ```jsonc { "durable_objects": { "bindings": [ /* ... */ ] }, "migrations": [ { "tag": "v1", "new_classes": ["NaelaoAgentDO", "AssistantDO", "WalletDO", "SpaceDO"] }, // Future rename: { "tag": "v2", "renamed_classes": [{ "from": "NaelaoAgentDO", "to": "AgentDO" }] } // Future delete (only after instances drained): // { "tag": "v3", "deleted_classes": ["LegacyDO"] } ] } ``` Never rename/delete a DO class without a corresponding migration tag.

G-W38 MEDIUM §Testing — Isolation — test harness / Service Binding isolation

Per-test DO isolation via random IDs does not isolate Service Bindings — tests cross-contaminate via inter-Worker calls

The Gap

Tests isolate DO instances by using fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` IDs per test, but Service Bindings between test Workers are not isolated: a test exercising naelao-router that triggers a Service Binding call into naelao-spaces hits the shared test instance of that Worker, whose DO namespace and any module-scope state are common across tests. Tests marked `concurrent` can therefore pollute each other through the binding layer even though their DO IDs differ.

Required Fix

Isolate cross-Worker state per test and avoid module-scope mutable state: ```typescript // Namespace all DO IDs created via Service Bindings with a per-test prefix const testPrefix = `test-${crypto.randomUUID()}`; // Pass it through so downstream Workers derive DO names within the test namespace // e.g. idFromName(`${testPrefix}:space:${id}`) // Run cross-binding integration tests serially, not concurrently: describe.sequential("router -> spaces integration", () => { /* ... */ }); ``` Forbid module-scope mutable state in Workers; keep all state in DO storage keyed by the test-prefixed names.

G-W39 MEDIUM §Deployment — CI/CD — pipeline / CI and secret handling

No CI/CD pipeline, deploy ordering, or secret-handling documented for the 22-Worker fleet

The Gap

There is no `.github/workflows` or equivalent CI/CD definition. The spec does not specify how the 22 Workers are linted, tested, and deployed; in what order (which matters for version skew, G-W35); whether deploys are automated or manual; or how deployment secrets (`NAELAO_JWT_SECRET`, the CF API token, signing keys) are stored and injected. This leaves deployment ad hoc and secret handling undefined — a significant operational and security gap.

Required Fix

Define a CI/CD pipeline with ordered deploys and secret hygiene: ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml (sketch) jobs: test: { steps: [ checkout, "npm ci", "npm run test" ] } # vitest-pool-workers deploy: needs: test steps: # Deploy in dependency order: leaf services first, edge router last - run: wrangler deploy --config workers/naelao-credentials/wrangler.jsonc - run: wrangler deploy --config workers/naelao-billing/wrangler.jsonc # ... then dependent services ... - run: wrangler deploy --config workers/naelao-router/wrangler.jsonc env: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }} # GitHub Secrets, never in repo ``` Use `wrangler secret put` for runtime secrets; never bake them into wrangler.jsonc or env vars in the repo.

G-W40 MEDIUM §Deployment — Config — wrangler / compatibility_date consistency

compatibility_date not validated for consistency across dev/test/prod environments

The Gap

The vitest config and the root wrangler.jsonc both pin `compatibility_date` to the same value, but there is no check that every per-Worker and per-environment wrangler config (especially production) sets a consistent, intentional date. A missing or mismatched `compatibility_date` across environments changes runtime semantics (which APIs and behaviors are active), so a Worker can behave differently in prod than in test for reasons unrelated to code — a class of bug that is very hard to diagnose.

Required Fix

Centralize and assert the compatibility date: ```typescript // scripts/check-compat-date.ts — run in CI before deploy import { readFileSync, globSync } from "node:fs"; const EXPECTED = "2026-05-01"; for (const cfg of globSync("workers/**/wrangler.jsonc")) { const d = JSON.parse(stripJsonc(readFileSync(cfg, "utf8"))).compatibility_date; if (d !== EXPECTED) throw new Error(`${cfg}: compatibility_date ${d} != ${EXPECTED}`); } ``` When bumping the date, bump it everywhere in one change and re-run the full test suite against the new date.

Appendix X — Sixteenth Pass

Rate Limiting & Abuse · RAG Pipeline · WebSocket Protocol · Observability · Skills Security · Multi-Tenancy Isolation

G-X01 CRITICAL §Agent Runtime — Tool Execution — AgentDO / tool dispatch

Per-Tool-Call Rate Limit Missing — Unbounded Recursive Tool Loops Drain Credits

The Gap

The spec defines agent tiers and allowed tools but places no ceiling on how many times an agent may call a single tool within one run. A misbehaving agent can issue web_search 10,000 times recursively before the run is manually cancelled, consuming the entire space credit balance in minutes. The MAX_ITERATIONS guard exists for agentic reasoning loops but is never applied to individual tool invocation counts.

Required Fix

Add maxToolCallsPerTool (default 100) and maxToolCallsPerRun (default 500) counters to AgentDO per-run state, enforced in the tool dispatch layer before each invocation. Return a structured error and mark the run failed-rate-exceeded when exceeded. Log the event to Analytics Engine for billing reconciliation and admin alerting.

G-X02 CRITICAL §Queue Consumers — naelao-notifications — CF Queues / maxConcurrency

Queue Consumer Unbounded Parallelism — Burst Traffic Causes Thundering Herd on Downstream APIs

The Gap

CF Queues dispatches all messages in a batch to the consumer Worker in parallel when maxConcurrency is unset. A space completing a large batch job can enqueue 10,000 notification events simultaneously, triggering 10,000 concurrent downstream API calls (APNs, FCM, Slack) and immediately rate-limiting those services. The cascade affects all spaces sharing the consumer Worker, not just the offending space.

Required Fix

Set maxConcurrency: 50 and maxBatchSize: 100 on every queue consumer binding in wrangler.jsonc. Implement a per-space semaphore inside the consumer: allow at most 10 concurrent deliveries per spaceId. Log consumer queue depth to Analytics Engine every minute as a capacity-alerting metric.

G-X03 HIGH §AI Gateway — Model Invocation — callAIGateway / retry logic

AI Gateway 429 Response Not Caught at Worker Level — No Per-Space Exponential Backoff

The Gap

When a space exhausts its AI Gateway token-per-minute quota the gateway returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. The agent Workers do not inspect this header; they either surface the error immediately to the user or retry in a tight synchronous loop, burning the remaining quota and locking the space out for the entire minute. No backoff is stored across requests.

Required Fix

Wrap all callAIGateway() calls in a retry helper that detects status 429, reads the Retry-After header (default 60 s), and stores a per-space backoff timestamp in KV (TTL = backoff seconds). Reject subsequent calls for that space until the backoff expires. Surface a structured error to clients: { type: "quota_exceeded", retry_after_ms }.

G-X04 CRITICAL §Billing — Credit Enforcement — SpaceDO / billing queue

No Pre-Run Credit Reservation — Asynchronous Billing Enables Unbounded Overspend

The Gap

Credit checks occur after each LLM call via the billing event queue, which is processed asynchronously. Between the first LLM call and the billing event being consumed by naelao-billing, dozens more LLM calls can be issued. Under high concurrency a space with zero remaining credits can accumulate a large negative balance before the first billing event closes the account, incurring real API cost with no immediate enforcement.

Required Fix

Pre-reserve credits synchronously at run start: deduct a worst-case reservation (e.g., 10,000 tokens x tier rate) from the SpaceDO SQLite credit ledger before the first LLM call. Refund the unused portion at run end. Reject run start with a user-facing quota error if available_credits < minimum_reservation.

G-X05 MEDIUM §Personalisation — Apps Economy — KV TTL / cache expiry

Personalisation Cache TTL Has No Jitter — Simultaneous Expiry Causes Hourly Rate-Limit Spike

The Gap

UI personalisation profiles are cached with a fixed 3600-second TTL set at first authentication. All users who authenticated around the same time expire their caches simultaneously, issuing hundreds of synchronous LLM personalisation calls to the AI Gateway at the same clock second. This spikes per-space token consumption and triggers quota limits, degrading experience for all concurrent users.

Required Fix

Apply jitter at cache-write time: ttl = 3600 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 600). Store next_regen_at = Date.now() + ttl * 1000 in the cached KV value. Derive TTL from last cache write rather than user login time, so rolling updates spread expirations uniformly across a 10-minute window.

G-X06 HIGH §Billing — naelao-billing queue consumer — Analytics Engine / SpaceDO ledger

Billing Events Lost on Analytics Engine Unavailability — No Durable Fallback Ledger

The Gap

The billing pipeline writes credit deduction events to Analytics Engine via the naelao-billing queue consumer. If Analytics Engine is unavailable the consumer nacks the message; after maxRetries is exhausted the message is dead-lettered. The credit ledger in SpaceDO SQLite is never updated, leaving the space with phantom credits — balances that were spent but never deducted.

Required Fix

Make SpaceDO SQLite the authoritative billing ledger: subtract credits synchronously from SQLite at the moment of LLM call, before enqueuing to Analytics Engine. AE receives analytics-only copies; AE loss is cosmetic. Reconcile monthly by querying AE against SpaceDO and alerting on divergence above a threshold.

G-X07 HIGH §Knowledge — naelao-knowledge — chunker / embedding pipeline

Chunker Uses Word Count Not BPE Token Count — Chunks Overflow Embedding Model Context Window

The Gap

The chunker splits documents at 512 "tokens" measured as whitespace-separated words. One word averages 1.3–1.8 BPE subword tokens for the @cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5 model, whose maximum context is 512 subword tokens. A 512-word chunk routinely exceeds 700 subword tokens, causing the embedding call to silently truncate the tail of each chunk and losing the last ~30% of information before indexing.

Required Fix

Replace word-count splitting with a BPE tokenizer matching the embedding model (e.g., gpt-tokenizer, ~20 kB WASM). Target 400 subword tokens per chunk with 50-token overlap. Validate chunk.tokenCount <= 512 before calling ai.run(); log a warning and split further if exceeded. This applies to all content types including code and non-Latin documents.

G-X08 HIGH §Knowledge — Vectorize — embedding model metadata

No Embedding Model Version Tracked in Vectorize — Upgrade Causes Silent Vector Space Drift

The Gap

Vectors are upserted to Vectorize with no embedding_model metadata field. When the platform upgrades from bge-base-en-v1.5 to a newer model, new document embeddings occupy a different vector space than existing ones. Cosine similarity between old and new vectors is meaningless noise; semantic search quality degrades silently across all spaces that contain pre-upgrade knowledge documents.

Required Fix

Add embedding_model TEXT NOT NULL to the knowledge_chunks SQLite table and to every Vectorize vector's metadata. On model upgrade, run a background migration job that re-embeds all chunks with the new model, upserts to Vectorize, and deletes old vectors. Gate query paths to compare only vectors whose model version matches the query embedding's model.

G-X09 CRITICAL §Knowledge — Vectorize — document update / vector cleanup

Stale Vectors Accumulate on Document Updates — Old Chunk Versions Permanently Indexed

The Gap

When a knowledge document is edited, new chunks are upserted by ID but if the new version produces fewer chunks than the old version, surplus old-version vector IDs are never deleted. After ten edits, up to ten versions of the same document are simultaneously indexed, causing semantic search to return duplicates, outdated content, and potentially confidential draft material that has since been revised or deleted.

Required Fix

Maintain a vector_ids JSON column in knowledge_chunks SQLite. On each document update, read the old vector IDs, call vectorize.deleteByIds(oldIds) before upserting new chunks, then write the new IDs back in the same SQLite transaction so a partial failure does not orphan vectors. Schedule a nightly reconciliation job to detect and remove any orphaned vectors.

G-X10 HIGH §Knowledge — RAG Pipeline — retrieval quality / re-ranking

No Relevance Score Threshold or Re-ranking — Low-Quality Chunks Injected into Prompt

The Gap

The RAG pipeline queries Vectorize for top-K results and injects all K into the system prompt regardless of similarity scores. A weak semantic match at 0.55 is injected alongside a strong match at 0.95, diluting answer quality with irrelevant context. For large knowledge bases the true answer may rank beyond the hardcoded retrieval window, making it invisible to the agent.

Required Fix

Set a minimum relevance threshold (default 0.72, configurable per space). After Vectorize returns topK=20 candidates, filter out scores below the threshold. Optionally pass the shortlist to a cross-encoder re-ranker for final scoring before injection. Log retrieved chunk IDs, scores, and the injected count in run telemetry to enable quality debugging.

G-X11 MEDIUM §Knowledge — ContextManager — system prompt / context assembly

Knowledge Block Has No Token Budget — Context Overflow Crashes Turn With Unspecified Error

The Gap

The ContextManager inserts retrieved knowledge chunks into the system prompt with no declared token budget. If five chunks total 12,000 tokens and the model's context window is 32,000 tokens, the combined system prompt plus conversation history overflows and the model API returns a context-length error that surfaces as an opaque run failure with no user-visible explanation about what happened.

Required Fix

Define max_knowledge_tokens (default 4,000, configurable in space settings) for the knowledge block. ContextManager sorts chunks by relevance DESC, appends chunks until the budget is exhausted, then stops. Log { chunks_available, chunks_injected, tokens_used } per turn and surface a user-visible notice when knowledge was truncated due to context limits.

G-X12 CRITICAL §Knowledge — GDPR / Vectorize — right-to-erasure / deleteByIds

Deleted Knowledge Documents Leave Vectors in Vectorize — GDPR Article 17 Violation

The Gap

The knowledge deletion endpoint removes rows from SpaceDO SQLite and the R2 object but never calls vectorize.deleteByIds(). Deleted documents' chunk vectors remain indexed and searchable indefinitely. Semantic queries against the space may return content from legally erased records, violating GDPR Article 17 right to erasure and exposing the platform to regulatory liability.

Required Fix

On knowledge document deletion, retrieve all vector IDs from the knowledge_chunks.vector_ids column and call await env.VECTORIZE.deleteByIds(vectorIds) before returning 200. Confirm deletion in the response. Add a nightly reconciliation job that cross-checks Vectorize metadata against SpaceDO knowledge_chunks and deletes any orphaned vectors with no matching document record.

G-X13 MEDIUM §Knowledge — Vectorize — topK / retrieval configuration

topK Hardcoded at 5 — Builders Cannot Tune Retrieval Depth for Larger Knowledge Bases

The Gap

The knowledge search endpoint reads topK from the query string but falls back to 5 with no upper-bound cap or builder-level configuration. Vectorize supports up to 100 results. Builders debugging why their agent misses known information have no way to increase retrieval depth without modifying platform code, and the default of 5 frequently misses relevant chunks in knowledge bases larger than 500 documents.

Required Fix

Add knowledge.retrieval_top_k (range 5–50, default 10) to space configuration in SpaceDO. Expose it in the builder dashboard. The knowledge search endpoint reads this config and clamps topK: Math.min(requested, space.retrieval_top_k). Document the trade-off in the builder docs: higher topK increases retrieved tokens and context cost per turn.

G-X14 HIGH §WebSocket — AgentDO streaming — token broadcast / message envelope

Token Stream Has No Sequence Numbers — Clients Cannot Detect Dropped or Duplicate Messages

The Gap

Token streaming broadcasts { type: "token", delta, runId } with no sequence counter. If a client loses connectivity for 200 ms and reconnects, it receives a replay from the token_buffer but has no way to determine whether replayed messages overlap with ones already received. Duplicate tokens silently render twice in the UI; dropped tokens create invisible gaps in the streamed response with no way for the client to detect them.

Required Fix

Maintain a per-run seqId counter (auto-incrementing integer) in AgentDO state. Include seqId in every outbound message: { type: "token", delta, runId, seqId }. On reconnect the client sends its lastSeqId; the server replays only messages with seqId > lastSeqId. The client detects gaps when incoming seqId !== lastSeqId + 1 and requests explicit re-sync from the server.

G-X15 HIGH §WebSocket — AgentDO broadcast — ws.send / backpressure

Broadcast Blocks on Slow Socket — One Lagging Client Stalls Token Delivery for All Others

The Gap

The token broadcast loop calls ws.send() synchronously for each connected WebSocket via getWebSockets(). If one client is on a throttled connection, its TCP send buffer fills and ws.send() blocks the Durable Object thread. While the LLM continues generating tokens, other clients stop receiving updates until the slow client drains or disconnects, potentially timing out the entire agent run.

Required Fix

Wrap each ws.send() in a non-blocking check: if the socket's bufferedAmount exceeds 65,536 bytes, skip that socket for the current batch and log a slow-client event. After three consecutive skips, close the socket with code 4002 and notify it to reconnect. Store unsent messages in a per-socket ring buffer (max 200 messages) so they are available on immediate reconnect.

G-X16 HIGH §WebSocket — DO eviction recovery — reconnect / subrequest limits

Reconnect Storm After DO Eviction — Simultaneous Reconnects Exhaust CF Subrequest Limit

The Gap

When a Durable Object is evicted from memory, all connected WebSockets receive close events simultaneously and all clients attempt reconnection within the same millisecond. A space with 200 connected clients triggers 200 simultaneous DO hydration requests, each performing SQLite reads and potentially KV reads, exceeding Cloudflare's subrequest limits and returning 429 errors for the majority of clients.

Required Fix

Clients must reconnect with full jitter: delay = Math.random() * 10000 ms. The server sets a retry hint in the WebSocket close reason: { code: 4003, retryAfterMs: Math.floor(Math.random() * 10000) }. Cap concurrent DO instantiations per space to 5 using a KV-based semaphore so the hydration load is throttled even if all clients ignore the retry hint.

G-X17 MEDIUM §WebSocket — Auth / DO hibernation — JWT / session token refresh

JWT Expires During Hibernated Long-Lived WebSocket — No Re-Auth Path for Service Bindings

The Gap

The WebSocket upgrade validates a JWT from the query string but the token is not stored in DO state. If the DO hibernates and wakes hours later (while CF Hibernation holds the WebSocket open), outgoing calls to other Workers via Service Bindings require a valid access token; the DO has no valid token to present. Authenticated context is stale; downstream Workers reject the calls silently.

Required Fix

Store the decoded JWT payload and its exp in SpaceDO SQLite on WebSocket accept. Define a { type: "auth_refresh", jwt: newToken } client-to-server message type that clients send proactively 30 s before token expiry. The DO validates the new token, updates stored claims in SQLite, and uses the refreshed token for all subsequent Service Binding calls.

G-X18 MEDIUM §WebSocket — Network reliability — ping/pong / keepalive

No Ping/Pong Keepalive — Network Proxies Drop Idle WebSocket Connections After 60 s

The Gap

The spec does not implement WebSocket ping frames. HTTP proxies, CDNs, and mobile network gateways commonly close idle TCP connections after 60–90 seconds of inactivity. During a long agent tool execution where no tokens are streamed for 2+ minutes, intermediary proxies silently close the socket. The client is unaware until it next tries to send and discovers the connection is dead, having missed the entire tool result.

Required Fix

Send a WebSocket ping frame every 20 seconds from the DO: ctx.getWebSockets().forEach(ws => ws.ping()). Track last-pong timestamp per socket in DO memory. If a socket has not ponged within 30 seconds of the last ping, close it with code 4004 (keepalive timeout), log to Analytics Engine, and let clients auto-reconnect.

G-X19 MEDIUM §WebSocket — Message framing — onMessage / frame type guard

Binary WebSocket Frame Silently Coerced to String — Causes Spurious Client Disconnects

The Gap

The onMessage handler casts the incoming frame as string: const data = message as string; JSON.parse(data). If a client sends a binary frame (opcode 0x82), ArrayBuffer coercion produces "[object ArrayBuffer]", which throws a JSON parse error. The catch block sends a JSON error response, but some clients interpret a server-sent message during a binary send as a framing error and close the connection, causing spurious disconnects.

Required Fix

Add an explicit type guard before parsing: if (message instanceof ArrayBuffer || message instanceof Uint8Array) { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "error", code: "BINARY_NOT_SUPPORTED" })); return; }. Place this check before the try/catch to prevent ArrayBuffer coercion. Document in the client SDK that only UTF-8 text frames are accepted.

G-X20 LOW §WebSocket — Protocol versioning — Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header

No WebSocket Subprotocol Negotiation — Clients Cannot Detect Incompatible Message Types

The Gap

The WebSocket upgrade does not negotiate a subprotocol via the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header. When new message types are added to the wire protocol, existing clients receive unknown types they cannot handle gracefully. There is no versioned handshake; both new and old clients connect on the same endpoint with no compatibility signal, making it impossible to introduce breaking protocol changes safely.

Required Fix

Define named subprotocols: naelao.agent.v1 (current), naelao.agent.v2 (next). Clients include supported versions in the Upgrade request. The server selects the highest mutually supported version and responds with it in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header. The server sends only message types defined in the negotiated version. Increment version on any new message type.

G-X21 HIGH §Observability — Distributed Tracing — Service Bindings / X-Trace-Id

No Trace ID Propagated Across 22 Workers — Cross-Service Errors Cannot Be Correlated

The Gap

A single user request routes through multiple Workers (naelao-api → naelao-agents → naelao-ai → naelao-knowledge). No trace ID is generated at the edge and propagated via headers (X-Trace-Id or W3C traceparent). When an error occurs in a downstream Worker there is no way to link it to the originating request; debugging requires guessing by timestamp across Worker logs in different Cloudflare accounts.

Required Fix

Generate a UUID trace ID at the CF edge entry point and propagate it in every Service Binding call via X-Naelao-Trace-Id. Each Worker logs { trace_id, span_id, service, duration_ms, status } to Analytics Engine. Provide an admin trace viewer: SELECT * FROM events WHERE trace_id = ? ORDER BY timestamp to reconstruct the full execution path of any request.

G-X22 MEDIUM §Observability — Logging — console.log / log schema

No Standard Structured Log Schema — Worker Logs Are Ad-Hoc Text Prefixes Unqueryable at Scale

The Gap

Worker logging uses ad-hoc console.log calls with text prefixes: [NAELAO], [SWEEPER], [model-fallback]. These are queryable only via substring matching in Cloudflare Workers Logs. There is no consistent JSON structure with fields like service, level, trace_id, and timestamp, making cross-Worker log aggregation and automated alerting practically impossible without expensive text parsing pipelines.

Required Fix

Define a log utility: log({ level, service, trace_id, event, ...context }) emitting structured JSON to stdout. All Workers import this utility instead of calling console.log directly. Require fields: level (debug|info|warn|error), service, trace_id. Provide a dashboard template for log exploration via Cloudflare Workers Analytics or an external SIEM.

G-X23 MEDIUM §Observability — Dead-Letter Queue — sweeper / DLQ retry trace

DLQ Retry Requeue Loses Original Failure Context — No Parent-Message Correlation

The Gap

The sweeper fetches failed messages from the dead-letter queue and requeues them via CF Queues REST API. The requeued message receives a new message ID with no reference to its original ID, failure reason, or attempt count. When the retry also fails, the second DLQ entry has no parent-message link. Operations cannot distinguish retries from new failures, making root-cause analysis for recurring failures impossible.

Required Fix

Enrich messages with retry metadata before requeue: { original_message_id, attempt_count, first_failure_at, last_failure_reason, dlq_ingress_at }. Log each requeue to Analytics Engine. Expose GET /admin/dlq/history?original_message_id=X returning the full retry chain. Alert when attempt_count >= 3 for the same original message.

G-X24 MEDIUM §Observability — Cron Monitoring — sweeper / cron_jobs table

Cron Job Skip Accumulation Has No SLO Threshold or Alert — Silent Starvation of Background Jobs

The Gap

When a cron job's previous run is still active, the sweeper logs a skip and returns. No counter tracks consecutive skips. A cron job that consistently exceeds its interval (e.g., a billing reconciliation that runs 70 minutes on a 60-minute schedule) is skipped indefinitely with no alert, silently accumulating billing drift, missed cleanups, or stale state with no operational visibility.

Required Fix

Add consecutive_skips INT and last_successful_run_at TIMESTAMP columns to the cron_jobs SQLite table. Increment on each skip; reset to 0 on successful completion. Write an Analytics Engine alert event when consecutive_skips >= 3. Expose GET /admin/crons returning { jobId, lastRun, consecutiveSkips, status } for each registered job.

G-X25 HIGH §Observability — Skill Integrity — SkillRegistryDO / SHA256 verification

Skill SKILL.md Hash Verified Only at Load Time — Post-Load Tampering in R2 Goes Undetected

The Gap

The skills loader computes a SHA256 hash of SKILL.md at startup and caches it. If the R2 object is subsequently overwritten via a compromised API token or insider threat, the cached skill continues executing with its original definition and the tampered version is never detected until the DO restarts or the cache expires. A tampered skill could silently exfiltrate conversation data or issue unauthorized tool calls.

Required Fix

Re-verify the SKILL.md SHA256 hash on each execution, not only at load. If the hash does not match the value stored in SkillRegistryDO, immediately suspend the skill, log { type: "skill_tamper_detected", skill_id, expected_hash, actual_hash } to an immutable append-only audit table, and alert the space admin. Limit hash verification cache to 5 minutes maximum.

G-X26 MEDIUM §Observability — Analytics Engine Schema — blob field positions / versioning

Analytics Engine Blob Positions Not Versioned — Inserting a Field Silently Corrupts All Queries

The Gap

Analytics Engine events use positional arrays: blobs[0] = eventType, blobs[1] = userId, blobs[2] = agentId, etc. If a new field is inserted in the middle, all downstream queries and dashboards relying on positional indexes silently read the wrong data. There is no schema registry, migration plan, or query compatibility layer for evolving Analytics Engine event schemas across the 22 Workers.

Required Fix

Treat Analytics Engine blob arrays as strictly append-only: never insert a field in the middle, only append at the end. Maintain an analytics-schema.ts manifest committed to the repo documenting the exact field positions. Include schema_version (blobs[19]) in every event. On any breaking change bump the version and provide a query adapter that re-maps old field positions.

G-X27 HIGH §Skills — Marketplace Security — npm integrity / SkillRegistryDO

Community Skills Reference npm Packages Without Version Pin — Supply Chain Attack Vector

The Gap

Community skills reference npm packages without pinning to an exact version or cryptographic hash. A compromised npm account can publish a malicious patch version (e.g., 1.2.4 over 1.2.3) that is automatically pulled on next cache miss by any space using that skill. The SkillRegistryDO's SHA256 covers only the cached SKILL.md, not the npm package artifact itself, so the attack is undetected.

Required Fix

Require exact version strings (1.2.3, not ^1.2 or latest) in community skill manifests. Store the npm package's integrity hash from package-lock.json in SkillRegistryDO at install time. Verify the hash on each fetch. Introduce a community skill review queue: flag new versions as pending-review until a platform reviewer approves before the new version goes live to spaces.

G-X28 HIGH §Skills — MCP Integration — naelao-mcp-hub / CF Worker CPU limit

MCP Tool Calls via naelao-mcp-hub Hit 30 s Worker CPU Limit — Long Tools Return Truncated Results

The Gap

naelao-mcp-hub proxies MCP tool calls over HTTP. CF Workers have a 30-second wall-clock CPU limit. Long-running MCP tools (web scrapers, LLM-backed tools, file converters) that take 45+ seconds cause the hub Worker to time out, returning a partial or empty response. The agent receives a truncated tool result and may hallucinate, retry in a loop, or report a false completion.

Required Fix

Introduce an async MCP tool pattern: if the tool declares estimated_duration > 10 s in its schema, the hub returns { callId, status: "pending" } immediately and streams results to an R2 staging path. The agent polls GET /mcp/calls/{callId}/result with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, max 30 s). Tools must declare estimated_duration or default to the async path for safety.

G-X29 HIGH §Skills — Loading — Promise.all / tier merge order

Skill Loader Tier Merge Uses Promise.all — Non-Deterministic Resolution Breaks Precedence

The Gap

The skill loader fetches platform, space, and agent skills in parallel via Promise.all and merges them. When multiple tiers define a skill with the same name, the merge result depends on Promise resolution order, which varies based on R2 list latency. The intended precedence (agent > space > platform) is maintained only if promises resolve in the correct order, which is not guaranteed under load.

Required Fix

Await all tier fetches in parallel for speed but merge deterministically by iterating tiers in explicit precedence order: const merged = { ...platform, ...space, ...agent }. Write a unit test that shuffles resolution order and asserts the merged result is identical regardless of timing. Log the precedence decision for each overridden skill name to the run's audit trace.

G-X30 HIGH §Skills — Runtime Contract — SKILL.md / execution reliability

Skills Are Markdown Documents With No Formal Execution Contract — Reliability Depends on LLM Interpretation

The Gap

Platform and community skills are SKILL.md markdown files describing what the skill does and what tools to call. There is no executable schema: no typed input/output contract, no parameter validation, no deterministic dispatch. The LLM reads the markdown and generates tool calls that may or may not match the skill's intent, depending on prompt formatting, context length, and model temperature. Skill reliability cannot be unit-tested without a live LLM call.

Required Fix

Define skills as typed Worker endpoints with a manifest: { name, version, tools: [{ name, inputSchema: ZodSchema, handler: (input) => Promise<output> }] }. Register dispatch namespace entries that execute deterministically. Keep SKILL.md as human-readable documentation only; the authoritative contract is the TypeScript handler. This enables unit testing of skill behavior without any LLM call.

G-X31 MEDIUM §Skills — Audit Trail — skill override logging / SkillRegistryDO

Agent-Tier Skill Overrides Have No Audit Trail — Malicious Shadowing Is Invisible to Admins

The Gap

Agent-tier skills silently shadow same-named space-tier skills with no log entry at load time. A compromised agent definition or an accidental builder override can replace a security-critical space skill with a modified version. Space admins have no way to discover which agents have overridden which skills, when those overrides were introduced, or whether the shadowed skill was security-relevant.

Required Fix

Log every skill override at load time: { type: "skill_override", agent_id, skill_name, overriding_tier: "agent", shadowed_tier: "space", timestamp } to Analytics Engine. Expose GET /admin/spaces/{spaceId}/skill-overrides returning active overrides with agent ID and effective-since date. Alert admins when a security-tagged skill is overridden by any agent.

G-X32 MEDIUM §Skills — MCP Tool Caching — naelao-mcp-hub / KV schema TTL

MCP Tool Schemas Cached 1 Hour in KV — App Updates Invisible to Running Agents

The Gap

naelao-mcp-hub caches MCP tool schemas (name, description, inputSchema) in KV with a 1-hour TTL. When an MCP app developer updates a tool's parameter schema (e.g., renames a required field), running agents use the stale schema for up to one hour, generating tool calls that the app rejects with a validation error. There is no cache invalidation mechanism or developer-facing flush endpoint.

Required Fix

Add schema_version to MCP app manifests. On app update, increment schema_version to trigger automatic KV cache invalidation (key includes version hash). Expose POST /admin/apps/{appId}/invalidate-schemas for manual clearing. Return schema_version and cached_at in tool list responses so agents and builders can verify schema freshness.

G-X33 HIGH §Skills — Marketplace — community skill fetch() / domain allowlist

Community Skill External Fetch URLs Unchecked at Runtime — Skills Can Exfiltrate Conversation Data

The Gap

Platform validation checks for external URLs in skill metadata at submission time but does not prevent the LLM from following skill instructions to call arbitrary URLs at runtime. A malicious skill can direct the LLM to POST { user_message, conversation_history } to an attacker-controlled endpoint. The skill sandbox has no network egress restriction to enforce the declared allowed_domains list at execution time.

Required Fix

Maintain a per-skill allowed_domains allowlist in the skill manifest. Wrap all fetch() calls inside skill execution with a domain-check interceptor that rejects requests to undeclared domains. At submission require explicit declaration of all external domains. Platform reviewers approve the allowlist for community skills. Write tests that assert fetch() to an undeclared domain throws before the request is sent.

G-X34 MEDIUM §Multi-tenancy — DO Identity — idFromName / spaceId format

DO Name Contains Raw spaceId — Colon in spaceId Enables Cross-Space Namespace Collision

The Gap

Durable Objects are named with patterns like ${spaceId}:${agentId}:${threadId}. If spaceId is generated from user-provided input without strict UUID enforcement, an attacker can supply a spaceId containing a colon (e.g., victim-space-id:agent-x) to collide with another space's DO namespace, potentially routing requests to the wrong DO and exposing its SQLite state to an unauthorized caller.

Required Fix

Validate and enforce that spaceId is a v4 UUID at all API entry points using a strict regex. Never embed raw spaceId in DO name strings without sanitization; strip all colon characters as a defense-in-depth measure. Add an integration test asserting that two crafted space IDs designed to collide produce distinct DO identifiers when used as name components.

G-X35 HIGH §Multi-tenancy — Auth / RBAC — JWT / role revocation

Admin Role Cached in Session JWT — Downgraded Admin Retains Privileges for Full Token Lifetime

The Gap

Space admin privileges are embedded in the JWT at authentication time. When a space admin is removed or downgraded to viewer, the change is written to SpaceDO SQLite but the existing JWT remains valid and unchecked against the updated role for its full TTL. The former admin retains the ability to call admin-gated API endpoints for up to one hour after demotion, enabling destructive actions on the space they no longer control.

Required Fix

On role change, write a revocation record to KV: key = revoked-session:{userId}:{spaceId}, value = { newRole, revokedAt }, TTL = tokenMaxLifetime. Auth middleware checks this KV key on every request to admin-gated endpoints. Additionally, broadcast { type: "role.changed", newRole } via WebSocket to close the former admin's active connections and force immediate re-authentication.

G-X36 MEDIUM §Multi-tenancy — KV Isolation — shared KV namespace / prefix enforcement

KV Namespaces Shared Across All Spaces — Prefix-Only Isolation Breakable by Application Bug

The Gap

All spaces share NAELAO_CONFIG_KV, NAELAO_ARTIFACT_KV, and NAELAO_CIRCUIT_KV namespaces, isolated only by key prefixes (spaces:{spaceId}:...). A Worker bug constructing KV keys without the spaceId prefix can read or overwrite another space's configuration. There is no KV-level ACL or prefix enforcement; isolation is entirely dependent on every Worker correctly applying the prefix in every code path.

Required Fix

Create a namespaced KV helper: const kv = scopedKV(env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV, spaceId) that auto-prefixes all keys and prevents raw namespace access. Add an ESLint rule prohibiting direct env.NAELAO_CONFIG_KV.get/put calls outside the scoped helper. For enterprise spaces, provision dedicated KV namespaces to achieve hardware-level isolation independent of application correctness.

G-X37 HIGH §Multi-tenancy — Audit Integrity — Analytics Engine / HMAC signing

Audit Log Has No Integrity Guarantee — Compromised Worker Can Insert False Audit Entries

The Gap

Audit events are written to Analytics Engine, which is append-only at the infrastructure level. However, the application layer performs no signing or integrity verification of audit entries. A compromised Worker with Analytics Engine write access can insert falsified audit records. Future read-modify-write paths added for GDPR redaction could silently alter historical entries with no tamper detection.

Required Fix

Sign each audit event batch with HMAC-SHA256 using a dedicated audit signing key separate from NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN. Store the batch signature in a reserved blob field. Provide a verification endpoint: GET /admin/audit/verify?from=&to= that recomputes signatures and reports mismatches. Treat any verification failure as a security incident requiring immediate investigation.

G-X38 MEDIUM §Multi-tenancy — Cross-Space Grants — grant validation / TOCTOU

Cross-Space Grant Validated at Auth Time Not Data-Access Time — TOCTOU Window Allows Post-Revocation Access

The Gap

When Space A grants Space B's user read access to a shared resource, the grant is validated at WebSocket authentication and its result cached for the session duration. Between authentication and the actual data fetch, the grant may expire or be explicitly revoked. The TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) window permits data access to proceed after the grant becomes invalid, violating the access control contract.

Required Fix

Re-validate grants at data-access time, not only at authentication time. On every cross-space read operation, call await grantDO.checkGrant(spaceA, spaceB, userId) synchronously before returning data. Cache positive results for at most 60 seconds with the grant's expires_at as the hard upper bound. Log every grant check with its outcome for audit and anomaly detection.

G-X39 HIGH §Multi-tenancy — R2 Storage — SpaceR2 / path traversal

R2 Path Traversal via Crafted File Key — SpaceR2 Prefix Enforcement Bypassable by .. Sequences

The Gap

SpaceR2 prepends spaces/{spaceId}/ to all keys. If a file key supplied by the user or agent contains path traversal sequences (../../other-space-id/secret.txt), the concatenated key resolves to a different space's prefix. R2 treats the key as a literal string and does not normalize separators or reject traversal sequences, so a crafted key can read or overwrite another space's files.

Required Fix

Validate file keys before prefix concatenation: reject any key containing .., //, or beginning with /. Implement assertSafeKey(key) called in every SpaceR2 method and throw a 400 error on violation. Add integration tests asserting keys with traversal sequences are rejected. Normalize the final composed R2 path and assert it begins with the expected spaces/{spaceId}/ prefix after normalization.

G-X40 MEDIUM §Multi-tenancy — GDPR / Analytics Engine — right-to-erasure / crypto-shredding

Analytics Engine Has No Per-Space Erasure Path — GDPR Article 17 Compliance Gap for Event Stores

The Gap

GDPR Article 17 right-to-erasure requires deleting all personal data on request. Analytics Engine is ClickHouse-backed and does not support row-level deletion. The spec acknowledges this limitation for naelao-analytics but does not define a compliant alternative. Events containing PII (user IDs, message excerpts in blobs) remain in Analytics Engine indefinitely after a space deletion or user erasure request.

Required Fix

Write only pseudonymous identifiers to Analytics Engine: hash user IDs via HMAC-SHA256 with a per-space erasure key stored in SpaceDO SQLite. On erasure request, delete the erasure key — all prior AE entries become permanently unresolvable (crypto-shredding). Document this approach in the privacy policy and DPA. Test that post-erasure AE queries for the hashed ID return zero matching events.

Appendix Y — Seventeenth Pass

The Configurable Product Platform · Capability Kernel & Manifests · No-Code Configurator & Constraint Engine · Tenancy / Product-Admin / Billing Strategy · Account-Scale Concurrency · Storage Topology Beyond 10GB · Dynamic Orchestration

G-Y01 CRITICAL §07 Naelao OS — Space Type model — CapabilityRegistry / manifest engine

No Formal Capability Kernel — Space Types Risk Forking Into Separate Codebases

The Gap

The spec loads a NaelaoSpaceTypeManifest per type from R2, which is the right instinct, but there is no formal shared capability kernel that all Space Types compose from. Without it, Workers, MiniAGI, Verticals, Launchpad and future types drift toward bespoke code paths, and the stated goal — a company space that combines Workers agents + space assistants + Naelao agents by configuration — becomes a custom build each time instead of a manifest selection.

Required Fix

Define a versioned CapabilityRegistry: every building block (naelao-agents, space-assistants, channels, tools, mcp, memory, rag, voice, project-think, workflows, wallet, sub-spaces, bootstrap, billing, tenancy) is a self-contained module with a typed config schema. A Space Type is purely a manifest that enables and parametrizes capabilities. The hypothetical "one giant Space Type" is simply a manifest with every capability enabled; a MiniAGI type is the same kernel with a narrower selection. No capability is ever reimplemented per type.

G-Y02 HIGH §07 Naelao OS — Space Type model — manifest inheritance

No Base/Standard Space Type or Manifest Inheritance — Every Manifest Re-declares Everything

The Gap

There is no "Standard" base Space Type, and manifests cannot inherit from one another. Verticals, Launchpad and enterprise manifests must each restate common defaults, so a change to shared behaviour requires editing every manifest. This duplicates configuration and makes the platform brittle as the number of Space Types grows.

Required Fix

Introduce manifest inheritance: a base "standard" manifest declares platform defaults; specialized types declare extends: "standard" and override only deltas. Resolve manifests at create time by deep-merging the inheritance chain. This makes a new Space Type a small overlay rather than a full re-declaration, and lets platform-wide defaults propagate to all derived types.

G-Y03 HIGH §07 Naelao OS — capability versioning — semver / compatibility

Capability Modules Have No Versioning — Upgrading a Block Silently Breaks Live Products

The Gap

Capabilities have no version identity. When the memory, RAG or channels module changes behaviour, every product that composed the old behaviour can break with no compatibility signal. A product manifest references capabilities by name only, so an upgrade is an uncontrolled, fleet-wide change.

Required Fix

Assign semver to every capability module. Product manifests pin the capability major version they were configured against (e.g., rag@2). The platform runs old and new majors side by side during an expand-then-contract migration window and provides a per-product migration path. Breaking changes require a major bump and an explicit, audited product re-configuration before the old major is retired.

G-Y04 MEDIUM §07 Naelao OS — manifest validation — Zod schema / CI guard

Manifest Schema Not Statically Validated — Malformed Manifests Can Reach Production

The Gap

Manifests are JSON loaded from R2 with no enforced schema. A malformed or internally inconsistent manifest (unknown capability, missing required parameter, invalid enum) is only discovered at runtime when a space fails to initialize, potentially after creation has been billed.

Required Fix

Define the manifest as a Zod schema and validate it in CI before any manifest is published to naelao-assets R2, and again at runtime before a space is created. Reject unknown capability keys, missing required parameters, and type mismatches with a precise error. Treat the manifest schema as the single source of truth for what is configurable.

G-Y05 HIGH §MP Community — Templates vs Space Types — template overlay / merge precedence

Blueprint vs Preset Boundary Unclear — Template/Space-Type Merge Order Undefined

The Gap

You distinguished Space Types (blueprints) from Templates (presets a user selects/configures), but the data model conflates them and never defines how a template combines with its Space Type. If both set the same capability parameter, the resulting value is undefined, so two users selecting the same template can get different products depending on load order.

Required Fix

Model a Template as a partial manifest overlay scoped to exactly one Space Type. Define a deterministic merge: Space Type base manifest → Template overlay → product-admin configuration → user selection, with later layers overriding earlier ones field-by-field. Persist the fully-resolved manifest snapshot on the space so the product is reproducible regardless of load timing.

G-Y06 MEDIUM §07 Naelao OS — config drift — space_manifest snapshot / reconcile

No Per-Space Manifest Snapshot — Reconfiguring a Type Drifts Existing Spaces

The Gap

A space is created from a manifest but the spec does not snapshot which manifest version produced it. When the Space Type manifest is later edited, existing spaces silently diverge from both the old and new definitions, and there is no reconcile path to bring a live space to a new configuration.

Required Fix

Persist a versioned space_manifest snapshot (the fully-resolved manifest) on each space at creation. Configuration changes produce a new snapshot version and a reconcile plan describing what is added, removed, or migrated. Apply reconciliation explicitly (with the diff/impact preview from G-Y09), never implicitly, so a space never silently drifts.

G-Y07 CRITICAL §Builder Console — Configuration — Configurator service

No No-Code Configurator Specified — Configuration Implies Code, Violating the Security Goal

The Gap

The platform requires that builders configure products by selecting features, never by writing code, explicitly for security. Yet there is no Configurator service that turns selections into a validated manifest; the spec exposes low-level tables and Worker endpoints instead. Without a constrained configurator, builders are pushed toward code or raw API calls, reintroducing the security risk the design exists to avoid.

Required Fix

Specify a Configurator service whose only output is a schema-validated manifest JSON. It never accepts or executes user code; every option maps to a pre-built capability parameter. All product behaviour is therefore the composition of audited platform code, and the attack surface is the (validated) manifest, not arbitrary user logic.

G-Y08 HIGH §Builder Console — AI Configurator — NL-to-manifest agent

AI Product-Builder Agent Unspecified — NL-to-Manifest Could Emit Invalid or Unsafe Config

The Gap

The vision includes an AI agent a builder describes their product to in natural language, which then configures it. This is unspecified. A naive implementation could emit a manifest that is invalid, violates compatibility constraints, or enables capabilities the builder is not entitled to.

Required Fix

Constrain the AI configurator to emit only manifest JSON conforming to the Zod schema, then pass it through the constraint engine (G-Y11) and entitlement checks before anything is applied. Present the resolved configuration to the builder as a human-readable summary plus diff for explicit confirmation. The agent proposes; the validated pipeline and the human dispose.

G-Y09 MEDIUM §Builder Console — Config changes — dry-run diff / impact analysis

No Preview/Impact Analysis for Config Changes — Disabling a Capability Can Silently Delete Data

The Gap

Reconfiguring a live product (e.g., turning off a capability, switching tenancy) can be destructive — disabling RAG may orphan vectors, disabling sub-spaces may strand data. The spec has no dry-run or impact analysis before a change is applied, so a builder cannot see consequences in advance.

Required Fix

Every configuration change runs a dry-run that computes a structured diff and an impact report: which data stores are affected, what will be deleted, archived, or migrated, and the estimated cost/credit effect. Destructive changes require explicit confirmation and create a reversible migration job. Surface this preview in both the manual configurator and the AI configurator path.

G-Y10 MEDIUM §Builder Console — Config governance — config_versions / rollback

No Configuration Versioning or Rollback — A Bad Config Cannot Be Reverted

The Gap

Product configuration is mutable with no version history. If a builder or product-admin makes a change that degrades the product, there is no audit trail of who changed what, and no way to roll back to a known-good configuration.

Required Fix

Store every applied configuration as an immutable row in a config_versions table with actor, timestamp, and the resolved manifest snapshot. Provide one-click rollback that re-applies a prior snapshot through the same reconcile/impact pipeline. Expose the configuration history in the admin console for audit and incident response.

G-Y11 CRITICAL §Configurator — Compatibility — constraint DSL / solver

No Formal Configuration Constraint Graph — Incompatible Options Can Be Selected Together

The Gap

You require that some configurations cannot coexist, some require others, and some are unsuitable for certain Space Types, with the UI blocking invalid options based on prior selections. The spec only has ad-hoc gates (minimumTier, allowedChildTypes). There is no constraint graph, so nothing prevents a manifest that enables mutually exclusive or unsupported capability combinations.

Required Fix

Define a declarative constraint DSL on capabilities: requires, conflictsWith, requiredBy, suitableFor: [spaceType], and parameter-level rules. A solver evaluates the partial selection live and returns which options are forced, forbidden, or still free, so the configurator UI can grey out invalid choices as the user selects. Encode domain rules (e.g., MiniAGI requires the orchestration capability; bootstrapping requires the vertical capability) as data in the registry, never hardcoded in the UI.

G-Y12 HIGH §Configurator — Compatibility — server-side validateManifest()

Constraint Enforcement Only in UI — API Callers Can Bypass Compatibility Rules

The Gap

If compatibility is enforced only by greying out options in the configurator UI, any caller hitting the manifest API directly can submit an invalid combination, exactly as paid-feature gating is currently UI-only (Gap D-12). The constraint graph must be authoritative on the server.

Required Fix

Run the same constraint solver server-side in validateManifest() on every create and reconfigure request, rejecting non-compliant manifests with the specific violated rule. The UI greying is a convenience layer; the server check is the security boundary. Reuse one constraint definition for both so they cannot diverge.

G-Y13 HIGH §Configurator — Domain rules — capability rule encoding

Domain Compatibility Rules Not Encoded — Adding a Space Type Requires Editing Core Logic

The Gap

Rules like "MiniAGI is standalone but composes into a company type", "bootstrapping needs a vertical", or "agency_shell is a narrow exception" live as scattered conditionals rather than declarative capability metadata. Adding a new Space Type or capability therefore means editing core code and risking regressions in unrelated types.

Required Fix

Move all domain compatibility rules into the capability and Space Type registry as declarative metadata consumed by the solver. Adding a capability or Space Type becomes a data change plus tests, not a code change to the engine. This keeps the "configure, don't code" promise true for the platform team as well as builders.

G-Y14 MEDIUM §Configurator — Transitions — transition validation

No Validation of Configuration Transitions — Upgrades/Downgrades Can Strand State

The Gap

Even if start and end configurations are individually valid, the transition between them may be unsafe (downgrading tenancy from SaaS to single-user when many end-users exist, or disabling a capability with live dependents). The spec validates states, not transitions.

Required Fix

Extend the constraint engine with transition rules that evaluate the delta against current runtime state (user counts, data presence, active runs). Block or require a migration plan for unsafe transitions, and surface the reason. Pair this with the impact preview (G-Y09) so transitions are never applied blindly.

G-Y15 CRITICAL §Tenancy — Product model — tenancy enum / DO topology

Tenancy Model Not a First-Class Configurable Dimension — SaaS vs Team vs Single-User Undefined

The Gap

A builder must be able to choose whether a product is single-user, a team product, or a multi-tenant SaaS (Claude/ChatGPT-style) where end-users join. The spec has a three-tier platform model and a per-space billing_mode (independent/parent) but no explicit product-level tenancy selector mapping to a data topology and isolation strategy. The same primitives cannot correctly serve a single-user app and a public multi-tenant SaaS without an explicit tenancy contract.

Required Fix

Make tenancy a required manifest dimension: tenancy: "single" | "team" | "saas". Each value maps to a defined DO topology, user/identity model, data-isolation strategy, and default billing model. Single = one space, one owner; team = one space, shared members; saas = product root plus per-end-user isolation. The constraint engine then enables only the configurations valid for the chosen tenancy.

G-Y16 HIGH §Tenancy — SaaS isolation — per-user child DO / facet

Multi-Tenant SaaS Has No Per-End-User Isolation — Shared SpaceDO Risks Data Mixing

The Gap

For a SaaS product where many strangers join one product, the "one SpaceDO per product with a space_id column" model puts all end-users in one shared database. This is acceptable for a team but weak for an open SaaS: a single missing filter leaks one user's data to another, and a single 10GB DO cannot hold a large public user base.

Required Fix

For tenancy: "saas", provision a per-end-user child Durable Object (facet) under the product root, each with its own SQLite and 10GB budget; the root DO holds only the user registry, auth, and billing. Per-user DOs make isolation structural (separate databases) rather than dependent on a correct WHERE clause, and the storage ceiling scales with users instead of being capped per product.

G-Y17 HIGH §Tenancy — Shared assistant — shared DO namespace / ACL

Shared-Assistant Mode Has No Per-User Partition — Admin Sharing Mixes User Data

The Gap

You want an admin option to let multiple users share one assistant while keeping their data unmixed. The spec models one AssistantDO per (space, user) and has no shared-assistant mode, so naively sharing one DO would commingle every user's memory and history.

Required Fix

Add a sharedAssistant configuration where a single AssistantDO serves multiple users but partitions all state by user namespace with per-user ACLs, so shared instructions/knowledge are common while conversations, memory, and outputs remain isolated. The constraint engine offers this only when the admin explicitly enables sharing, and the impact preview explains the isolation guarantees.

G-Y18 MEDIUM §Tenancy — Assistant entitlement — assistantsPerUser config

Assistant-Per-User Count Hardcoded — Admin Cannot Configure It Within Plan Limits

The Gap

The rule "one assistant per user per space unless the admin changes it to X" is a stated requirement, but the spec hardcodes a cap (up to 5). Product admins cannot raise or lower the count, and it is not bounded by the billing plan.

Required Fix

Expose assistantsPerUser as a product-admin-configurable entitlement, defaulting to 1, with an upper bound derived from the product's plan. AssistantDO acquisition checks the live entitlement. Changing the value flows through the configurator and is recorded in the config version history.

G-Y19 HIGH §Tenancy — White-label — brandConfig / delegated admin

No White-Label / Delegated User Management — A Company Cannot Own Its Own Product

The Gap

A company should be able to run its own branded product on Naelao, managing its own users, without the SaaS owner (or the original builder) managing those users. The spec has no white-label brand configuration and no delegated user-management model scoped to a product, so end-user administration cannot be cleanly handed to the product owner.

Required Fix

Add a brandConfig capability (logo, palette, domain, copy) and a delegated administration model where product-admins manage only their product's users, plans, and admin-configurable features. The platform owner and builder retain platform-level control but do not appear in or manage the white-labelled product's user base. Scope every admin endpoint to the actor's product boundary.

G-Y20 HIGH §Roles — product-admin — permission matrix

Product-Admin Permissions Undefined Beyond "Full Visibility"

The Gap

The schema defines a product-admin role (product_users.role) distinct from the platform owner and the builder, but its permissions are only described as "full visibility across sub-spaces." It is unclear whether a product-admin can manage users, set seats, adjust credits, configure features, export data, or suspend accounts.

Required Fix

Define an explicit product-admin permission matrix: manage end-users, set/seat allocation, adjust per-user credits within the product budget, toggle only the manifest options flagged admin-configurable, export product data, and suspend users. Every permission is bounded by what the builder's manifest exposes, so a product-admin can never exceed the product's configured surface.

G-Y21 MEDIUM §Roles — privilege bounds — capability allowlist per role

Product-Admin Could Reach Platform-Security Config — No Privilege Ceiling Defined

The Gap

Without an explicit ceiling, a product-admin configuring "things" might reach security-sensitive settings (encryption, internal tokens, tenancy topology) that must remain platform-controlled. Configuration freedom must stop at the security boundary.

Required Fix

Tag each manifest option with the minimum role allowed to change it (platform-owner, builder, product-admin). The configurator and server validation expose to a product-admin only the subset flagged product-admin-configurable. Security-critical options (encryption, internal auth, tenancy topology, capability versions) are never product-admin-editable.

G-Y22 MEDIUM §Roles — hierarchy — canonical actor model

Four Actor Layers Not Canonically Modeled — Role Confusion Across Endpoints

The Gap

There are at least four distinct actors — platform owner, builder, product-admin, end-user — but the spec defines them piecemeal across sections, risking inconsistent scope checks where, for example, an end-user action is mistakenly authorized at builder scope.

Required Fix

Establish a canonical role hierarchy with explicit scopes (platform > builder > product > end-user) and a single authorization helper that every endpoint calls with the required scope. Document the matrix once and reference it everywhere. Add tests asserting that each actor is rejected at every endpoint above its scope.

G-Y23 HIGH §Billing — Strategy config — BillingStrategy manifest section

Per-Product Billing Strategy Not Configurable — Only Fixed Platform Tiers Exist

The Gap

Builders need to choose their product's billing strategy — flat subscription, usage-based credits, per-seat, or a team plan inside a SaaS. The spec offers only fixed platform tiers (free–enterprise) and a credit model, with no per-product strategy configuration, so a builder cannot price their product the way their market expects.

Required Fix

Add a BillingStrategy object to the product manifest: model (flat | usage | per-seat | hybrid), price points, included quotas, and overage behaviour. The platform enforces wholesale cost to the builder; the builder configures retail pricing on top. Selectable strategies are filtered by the constraint engine against the chosen tenancy.

G-Y24 HIGH §Billing — Wholesale/retail — two-sided ledger

Wholesale vs Retail Billing Flow Undocumented — Builder Margin and Reconciliation Unclear

The Gap

A builder pays Naelao (wholesale) while their end-users pay the builder (retail), but the spec does not document this two-sided flow. There is no clear separation between builder-facing wholesale credits and end-user-facing retail credits, nor a reconciliation between them.

Required Fix

Model two ledgers: a wholesale ledger (builder ↔ Naelao, actual infra/model cost) and a retail ledger (end-user ↔ builder, configured pricing/markup). Every chargeable event posts to both with the same trace ID. Provide the builder a reconciliation view (retail revenue, wholesale cost, margin) and alerts on negative-margin configurations.

G-Y25 MEDIUM §Billing — Tenancy coupling — constraint rules

Billing Strategy and Tenancy Not Constrained Together — Invalid Combinations Possible

The Gap

Some billing strategies only make sense for certain tenancies — per-seat suits teams, per-user usage suits SaaS, flat suits single-user. Nothing prevents an incoherent pairing such as per-seat pricing on a single-user product.

Required Fix

Encode billing-strategy/tenancy compatibility in the constraint engine so the configurator only offers coherent combinations and the server rejects the rest. Document the valid matrix. This keeps pricing configuration self-consistent without manual review.

G-Y26 MEDIUM §Billing — Mid-run exhaustion — pre-reservation in SaaS

Credit Exhaustion Mid-Run Undefined in Multi-Tenant Context — Whose Balance, What Degradation

The Gap

The existing mid-run credit-exhaustion gap (D-13) is sharper under SaaS tenancy: when an end-user runs out mid-run, it is unclear whose balance is checked (end-user retail vs builder wholesale) and whether the run aborts, degrades, or completes.

Required Fix

Pre-reserve credits at run start against the correct ledger for the tenancy (end-user retail balance for SaaS, space budget for team/single), reusing the reservation mechanism in G-X04. On exhaustion, fail gracefully with a typed quota error and a partial-result checkpoint rather than crashing. Refund the unused reservation at run end.

G-Y27 CRITICAL §Scale — Account governance — global AdmissionController

No Account-Level Admission Control — One Tenant Can Exhaust the Whole CF Account

The Gap

All products run inside one Cloudflare account with account-wide ceilings (concurrent Container instances, subrequests, DO counts). The spec governs per-(space,user) concurrency via ConcurrencyDO but has no account-level admission controller, so a single busy tenant can consume the global Container/sandbox budget and starve every other product on the platform.

Required Fix

Add a global AdmissionController Durable Object that tracks account-wide resource usage (active sandboxes, concurrent runs) and enforces both per-tenant fair-share and an account safety ceiling. Requests beyond fair-share queue; requests beyond the account ceiling shed gracefully with backpressure. This protects platform-wide availability independent of per-tenant limits.

G-Y28 HIGH §Scale — Entitlements — live plan → ConcurrencyDO

Concurrency Limits Hardcoded and Not Wired to Live Billing

The Gap

ConcurrencyDO tier limits are compile-time constants and are not updated when a subscription changes (Gaps K-51, G-DUR-04). A user who upgrades does not get more concurrency until redeploy, and a downgrade is not enforced, so entitlements and billing diverge.

Required Fix

Introduce an entitlements service that resolves a plan into concrete limits (concurrent runs, sandboxes, agents-per-user, DO-hours). ConcurrencyDO reads entitlements live and is invalidated on subscription-change webhooks. Limits become data, not constants, and track billing in real time.

G-Y29 HIGH §Scale — Sandbox quotas — maxConcurrentSandboxes per plan

Sandbox Concurrency Count Not Plan-Gated — Only Per-Sandbox Size Is Defined

The Gap

The spec proposes per-sandbox resource sizes by tier (OPE-11) but not a limit on the number of concurrent sandboxes a space/user may hold. A lower-paying tenant could hold many sandboxes simultaneously, consuming account capacity disproportionately to their plan.

Required Fix

Define maxConcurrentSandboxes (and maxConcurrentBrowsers) per plan in the entitlements service, enforced at SandboxDO acquisition: requests beyond the limit queue or are rejected with a typed error. Combine with the account-level ceiling (G-Y27) so both per-tenant and global limits hold.

G-Y30 MEDIUM §Scale — Admission UX — fair queue / waitlist

No Admission Queue — Concurrency-Limited Requests Hard-Fail Instead of Waiting

The Gap

When a concurrency limit is hit, requests fail immediately. For interactive products this is a poor experience; a brief wait is often preferable to an error, and there is no fairness between competing users of the same space.

Required Fix

Add a fair admission queue per (space, user) with bounded wait and position feedback for interactive runs, falling back to a typed error on timeout. Use FIFO with per-user fairness to prevent one user monopolizing a shared space's slots. Background runs may queue longer than interactive ones.

G-Y31 CRITICAL §Storage — DO limit — sharded DO topology

10GB-Per-DO Limit vs One-SpaceDO-Per-Product — Busy SaaS Products Will Hit the Ceiling

The Gap

Durable Object SQLite is capped at 10GB per object, yet the data plane is "one SpaceDO per product" with all sub-spaces and end-users sharing that database. A successful multi-tenant SaaS product will exceed 10GB, and the R2 archival pattern (G-DUR-01 / HybridQueryDO) only offloads cold messages — it does not raise the ceiling for live relational data.

Required Fix

Adopt a sharded DO topology: the product root SpaceDO becomes a coordinator/registry (users, routing, billing), while live data is partitioned into child DOs (per sub-space for team/single, per end-user for SaaS), each with its own 10GB budget. HybridQueryDO federates reads across shards plus R2 archive. Total capacity then scales with shards instead of being capped per product.

G-Y32 HIGH §Storage — Topology config — storageTopology dimension

Storage Topology Not Tied to Tenancy/Plan — No Selectable Data-Plane Strategy

The Gap

The correct storage layout depends on tenancy and scale: a single-user app is fine on one DO + R2, while a SaaS needs per-tenant sharding. The spec offers only one fixed layout, so the platform cannot serve both efficiently.

Required Fix

Make storageTopology a manifest dimension (single-do | sharded-do | container-db | per-tenant-d1), defaulted automatically from the chosen tenancy and plan but overridable for large products. The constraint engine validates the choice against tenancy. This lets a hobby product stay cheap on one DO while a SaaS scales horizontally.

G-Y33 HIGH §Storage — Filesystem DB — Container SQLite on R2

No Filesystem-Backed Database Option for Heavy Data Planes

The Gap

You asked whether a Cloudflare filesystem can back a database for workloads larger than a DO. The spec has no such option, so analytics-heavy or very large per-product datasets have nowhere to live beyond the 10GB DO ceiling and R2 blobs.

Required Fix
