Manual dashboard creation leads to environment drift, un-versioned resource config, and inability to stand up a fresh environment (disaster recovery, new region, ephemeral test env) deterministically.

Required Fix

Provision all infrastructure as code: (1) Declare every CF resource (KV, R2, Queues + DLQs, Vectorize, Analytics Engine, DO migrations, cron triggers, Pages projects) in versioned config — wrangler resource declarations + Terraform (the cloudflare provider) for account-level resources. (2) A single provision-resources script stands up a complete environment from scratch, used for staging, production, DR, and ephemeral CI environments. (3) Resource IDs flow into worker bindings via the IaC outputs (no hand-copied IDs). (4) Drift detection (G-AE35) covers resources too. (5) This makes a new-region or DR bring-up a one-command, deterministic operation.

G-AE40 HIGH §deploy — cross-worker version skew

No Cross-Worker Version Compatibility Handling — Deploy Skew Breaks Service-Binding Contracts Mid-Rollout

The Gap

During a gradual rollout, worker A v2 (new request shape) may call worker B still on v1 (old handler), or vice versa. The spec has no contract-versioning between workers, so any change to a Service Binding's request/response shape risks breaking calls during the rollout window when versions are mixed. This is the internal analog of public API versioning (G-AD37) and is unaddressed.

Required Fix

Make inter-worker contracts version-tolerant: (1) Treat Service Binding request/response shapes as versioned contracts; changes must be backward-compatible within a major version (additive only) — enforced by a contract diff in CI. (2) For unavoidable breaking changes, deploy in two phases: first deploy the callee to accept both old and new shapes, then deploy the caller to use the new shape, then remove old-shape support. (3) Include a contract version field in inter-worker calls so the callee can branch if needed. (4) The deploy orchestrator (G-AE34) sequences callee-before-caller for contract changes. (5) Integration tests run against mixed-version combinations.

G-AE41 MEDIUM §ops — cron registry

No Cron/Scheduled-Task Registry or Observability — Scheduled Jobs Fail Silently

The Gap

The platform runs scheduled work (sweeper every 5 min, categorizer hourly, billing/canary/archive jobs, DO alarms). There is no central registry of scheduled tasks, no record of last-run/next-run/duration/outcome, and no alerting when a scheduled job stops running or starts failing. A silently-dead sweeper (e.g., DLQ reprocessing) degrades the platform invisibly.

Required Fix

Add scheduled-task observability: (1) A registry of all cron jobs and recurring DO alarms with their schedule and purpose. (2) Each run records job_runs(job, started_at, finished_at, status, items_processed, error) to Analytics Engine / a job-runs store. (3) A watchdog alerts if a job has not run within its expected interval (missed execution) or if its failure rate or duration exceeds thresholds. (4) An ops dashboard shows each job's health, last run, and recent outcomes. (5) Jobs are idempotent and overlap-guarded (per G-AA42) so a slow run does not double-execute. This makes the entire background-work layer observable.

G-AE42 MEDIUM §ops — fair job scheduling

Background Job Queues Have No Fair Scheduling — One Heavy Tenant Starves All Others' Jobs

The Gap

Shared queues (analytics, knowledge indexing, notifications, agent runs) process work FIFO. A single tenant that floods a queue (bulk-ingesting 100K documents, a runaway agent) monopolizes the consumer and starves every other tenant's jobs, which back up behind the heavy tenant with no fairness guarantee. This is the queue analog of the admission-control gap (G-AC44) for async work.

Required Fix

Implement fair scheduling for background work: (1) Partition queue consumption by tenant using per-tenant concurrency caps (a semaphore per space) so no tenant occupies more than its share of consumer capacity. (2) Use weighted fair queuing: round-robin across tenants with pending work rather than strict FIFO, optionally weighted by plan tier. (3) For very large jobs (bulk ingestion), chunk and interleave so they yield between chunks (cooperative scheduling). (4) Per-tenant rate caps on enqueue for abusive patterns. (5) Surface per-tenant queue depth and wait time; alert when fairness SLOs are breached.

G-AE43 MEDIUM §ops — resource quota dashboard

No Per-Space Resource Quota Visibility or Enforcement Across All Stores

The Gap

A space consumes multiple metered resources: DO SQLite storage (10GB), KV entries, R2 storage, Vectorize vectors (G-AB49), Analytics Engine events, container minutes, concurrent agents. The spec enforces some limits in isolation but there is no unified per-space quota model, no dashboard showing consumption vs limit per resource, and no consistent enforcement, so a space can silently exhaust a resource and hit confusing failures.

Required Fix

Unify resource quotas: (1) Define per-plan quotas for every metered resource in one place (the plan manifest). (2) Track consumption per space per resource (storage bytes, vector count, KV keys, container minutes, concurrent agents, monthly events). (3) A QuotaService checks/enforces consistently across stores before allowing growth, returning a uniform 402/429 with the specific resource and upgrade path. (4) A builder-facing usage dashboard shows each resource: used / limit, with 80%/95% warnings (per G-AB42). (5) Ops dashboard shows top consumers per resource for capacity planning. (6) Quotas tie into the infrastructure cost model (G-AC20).

G-AE44 MEDIUM §data — large export streaming

Large Data Exports Buffer in Worker Memory — Exports for Big Spaces Hit the 128MB Memory Limit and Fail

The Gap

Data exports (GDPR portability G-AB32, space config bundles, analytics dumps) appear to assemble the full payload in memory before returning. For a large space (millions of messages, large knowledge bases), this exceeds the Worker 128MB memory limit and the export fails or times out — precisely for the customers (big spaces) where export matters most.

Required Fix

Stream large exports instead of buffering: (1) Run exports as a CF Workflow that writes incrementally to an R2 object (multipart), paging through source data in bounded chunks (e.g., 10K rows at a time) so memory stays flat regardless of total size. (2) The export produces a downloadable R2 artifact (signed URL, expiring) rather than an inline response. (3) Report progress (rows exported / total) for long exports. (4) Use streaming serialization (JSONL/NDJSON) so each chunk is appended without holding the whole document. (5) Apply the same pattern to large imports (G-AB30) and analytics dumps. (6) Rate-limit concurrent large exports per account.

G-AE45 HIGH §entitlements — plan enforcement consistency

Plan Entitlements Are Not Enforced Consistently — Capabilities Gated in the UI But Reachable via the API

The Gap

Plan-gated features (capabilities, limits, white-label, SSO, advanced models) are described, but the spec does not define a single authoritative entitlement-enforcement layer. If gating happens only in the UI or per-handler ad hoc, a user can bypass it by calling the API directly, or different workers disagree on what a plan allows, leading to revenue leakage and inconsistent behavior.

Required Fix

Centralize entitlement enforcement: (1) Define entitlements declaratively per plan (capabilities allowed, resource limits, feature flags). (2) A single EntitlementService (backed by the space's plan in the strongly-consistent store) answers can(space, entitlement) and is called by every worker at the point of action — never only in the UI. (3) The UI uses the same entitlement data to hide/disable gated features, but the backend is the source of truth. (4) Entitlement checks are cached briefly with revocation on plan change. (5) Log entitlement denials for upsell analytics. (6) Changing a plan instantly and consistently changes effective entitlements everywhere.

G-AE46 MEDIUM §ops — recovery runbook matrix

No Per-Store Backup/Restore Runbook With RTO/RPO Targets — Recovery Is Improvised During an Incident

The Gap

The platform spans many data stores (DO SQLite, Turso, R2, Vectorize, KV, Analytics Engine, external provider state). The spec lacks a recovery runbook mapping each store to its backup mechanism, recovery procedure, RTO (recovery time objective), and RPO (recovery point objective). In a real data-loss incident, the team would improvise per store, with no rehearsed procedure or known recovery guarantees.

Required Fix

Produce a recovery matrix + runbook: for each data store, document the backup mechanism (WAL streaming G-AB31, Turso PITR G-AC26, R2 versioning, KV re-derivation, Analytics retention), the restore procedure (step-by-step), the RTO and RPO targets, and the owner. (2) Define dependency order for a full-platform restore (which stores first). (3) Rehearse quarterly: restore each store into a staging environment from real backups and verify integrity (ties to G-AE39 IaC for spinning up the target). (4) Keep the runbook in the repo and link it from the incident process. (5) Track actual vs target RTO/RPO from drills and close gaps.

G-AE47 MEDIUM §ops — synthetic journey monitoring

No End-to-End Synthetic Journey Monitoring — Outages Are Detected by Users, Not the Platform

The Gap

Component health checks (G-AB13) confirm individual workers are up, but nothing continuously exercises the full critical user journey (sign in → create/open space → send a message → receive a streamed agent reply → see it billed). A broken integration between healthy components (e.g., the agent worker is up but billing rejects all turns) is invisible to component checks and only surfaces via user complaints.

Required Fix

Add synthetic journey monitoring: (1) A scheduled synthetic test (Checkly or a dedicated monitor worker) runs the full critical journey end-to-end every few minutes from multiple regions against production (using a dedicated synthetic test account). (2) It asserts each step succeeds within latency budgets (auth, space load, message send, first token, completion, billing recorded). (3) Failures page on-call (G-AA43) with the failing step and trace_id. (4) Track journey success rate and step latencies as top-line SLO dashboards. (5) Additional synthetics for other key journeys (marketplace install, channel message round-trip, voice call). This catches integration outages before users do.

G-AE48 MEDIUM §testing — integration test harness

No Integration Test Harness for the Full Service-Binding Mesh — Only Unit Tests or Prod

The Gap

Tests run per-worker in isolation (vitest-pool-workers) or against production. There is no harness that stands up the full mesh of workers + their bindings + DOs + local resource emulations so that multi-worker flows (a request traversing router → auth → agents → billing → DOs) can be tested together before deploy. Cross-worker regressions are only caught in production.

Required Fix

Build an integration test harness: (1) A local/CI environment that runs all workers together with Service Bindings wired (wrangler multi-worker dev / Miniflare) plus local emulations of KV, R2, Queues, and DOs. (2) Seed deterministic fixtures (a test space, users, plans). (3) Integration test suites exercise full flows across worker boundaries and assert end-to-end outcomes (message → streamed reply → credits debited → analytics event written). (4) Run in CI on every PR before deploy. (5) Include contract tests that verify each worker honors its Service Binding contract (pairs with G-AE40). (6) A start-dev script reproduces the same mesh locally for developers.

G-AE49 HIGH §data — tenant isolation verification

No Automated Tenant-Isolation Verification — Cross-Tenant Leakage Regressions Can Ship Undetected

The Gap

Tenant isolation (one space never reads another's data) is enforced by spaceId scoping on every query, Vectorize filters, R2 prefixes, and DO addressing. The spec relies on developers getting this right everywhere, with no automated test that systematically attempts cross-tenant access and asserts it fails. A single missing filter (the kind already found in earlier gaps) silently leaks one tenant's data to another.

Required Fix

Add continuous tenant-isolation verification: (1) An automated test suite that, for every data-access endpoint and store, creates two tenants, writes data as tenant A, and asserts tenant B cannot read/list/search/address it (SQLite rows, Vectorize vectors, R2 objects, KV keys, DO state). (2) Run a "fuzzing" pass that mutates spaceId/credentials and confirms denials. (3) Static analysis/lint that flags any DO SQLite query or Vectorize query lacking a spaceId predicate. (4) Run in CI on every PR and as a periodic production canary against synthetic tenants. (5) Treat any leakage as a release-blocking severity. This makes isolation a verified invariant, not a hope.

G-AE50 MEDIUM §ops — config & feature-flag store

No Unified Configuration / Feature-Flag Store With Safe, Consistent Propagation

The Gap

Operational config and feature flags are scattered (KV with 60s eventual consistency, per-worker constants, env vars). There is no unified, strongly-consistent, audited flag system for: gradual feature rollout, per-plan/per-space overrides, kill switches, and operational tuning (timeouts, limits). KV's eventual consistency (per G-AC11) makes it unsafe for anything security- or correctness-sensitive.

Required Fix

Adopt a unified flag/config layer: (1) Use a managed feature-flag service (LaunchDarkly/Statsig per G-AA11) or a strongly-consistent ConfigDO for flags that must be consistent (kill switches, security toggles). (2) Support targeting: global, per-plan, per-space, and percentage rollouts (consistent hashing). (3) Changes are audited (who/when/old→new) and instantly + consistently propagated (no 60s window for critical flags). (4) Workers read flags via a thin SDK with a short in-memory cache + change subscription. (5) Provide an ops UI to view/flip flags and see current targeting. (6) Document which flags are safe in eventually-consistent KV vs which require the consistent store.

Appendix AF — Full System File-Tree Map

Complete functional monorepo · every worker, durable object, package, frontend, container, infra & test — nothing left out

A buildable monorepo layout for the entire platform: pnpm workspaces + Turborepo. Every Cloudflare Worker is a self-contained package (own wrangler.toml, src/, migrations/, test/); Durable Objects live in the owning worker's src/do/; shared logic lives in packages/*; infra/ provisions all Cloudflare resources as code. Gap references (e.g. G-AC11) point to the appendix entry whose fix that file implements.

├── LICENSE

├── pnpm-workspace.yaml               # packages/*, workers/*, apps/*
├── turbo.json                        # build/test/deploy task graph (dependency-ordered, G-AE34)
├── tsconfig.base.json                # shared strict TS config
├── .editorconfig

Appendix AG — Additional Technical Gaps (50 items)

Execution ladder · agent memory · analytics API · Space Type lifecycle · accessibility · i18n · observability · billing completeness · content safety · custom domains · message ordering · fine-tuning pipeline · test infrastructure

G-AG01 HIGH §40 Execution Ladder — Tier Upgrade Mid-Task

No Runtime Tier Escalation Path for In-Flight Agent Tasks

The Gap

Tools are assigned static tiers via TOOL_TIERS at manifest load time. Once an agent task begins executing in, say, the "isolate" tier and then discovers it needs npm packages, there is no documented re-dispatch mechanism to the "npm" tier. The orchestrator errors out with a capability mismatch rather than transparently escalating. This prevents agents from dynamically adapting their execution environment as task complexity unfolds.

Required Fix

Add a TierEscalationError type that agents can throw to signal they need a higher tier. The orchestrator catches it, persists task state (serialise current tool arguments and partial results to SpaceDO SQLite), enqueues a new task stub at the required tier, and resumes from the persisted checkpoint. Surface the tier upgrade as a billed event so WalletDO can charge the delta cost. Document the escalation contract in ToolManifest as an optional "minTier" / "maxTier" range instead of a fixed tier assignment.

G-AG02 MEDIUM §40 Execution Ladder — Tier Cost Model

Zero Per-Tier Infrastructure Cost Rate-Card — Agents Cannot Make Cost-Aware Tier Decisions

The Gap

The execution ladder documents boot latencies (workspace 0ms, isolate 200ms, npm 500ms, browser 800ms, sandbox 2-3s) but provides no cost attribution per tier. The billing handler tracks per-LLM-token costs but never records infra costs: isolate ~$0.0001/req vs. container ~$0.015/hr are orders of magnitude apart. Agents have no cost signal to decide whether to attempt a task in a cheaper tier first. Builders receive monthly bills with no breakdown by execution tier, making cost optimisation impossible.

Required Fix

Define a cost rate-card per tier (aligned to Cloudflare published pricing) and publish it in the platform manifest. Record tier+duration as a billed line item in WalletDO alongside LLM tokens. Expose a cost-estimate API that the orchestrator calls before dispatching so agents can choose a cheaper tier when capabilities overlap. Add per-tier cost columns to the builder analytics dashboard.

G-AG03 HIGH §40 Execution Ladder / Browser Tier — Puppeteer Session Management

Browser Tier Sessions Are Stateless Per-Request — Multi-Step Workflows Relaunch Chrome for Every Tool Call

The Gap

The browser tier re-launches a full Puppeteer/Chrome instance for every individual tool call. A multi-step workflow (navigate → fill form → click submit → verify result) is forced to relaunch Chrome between steps, losing cookies, local storage, and in-flight navigation state. Cold-start overhead (~800ms) is paid repeatedly. Pages that require JavaScript-rendered content must re-render from scratch. This makes interactive browser automation tasks impractically slow and unreliable.

Required Fix

Introduce a BrowserSessionDO (one per space, or one per active agent task) that holds a long-lived Puppeteer browser reference. Tools within the same task share the session context. Expose session.id in the tool manifest so the agent can pass it across calls. Implement session eviction after a configurable idle TTL (default 5 minutes). Store screenshots and HAR traces to R2 with AES-256 encryption. Add anti-bot headers (randomised User-Agent, stealth mode, viewport randomisation) as a capability flag.

G-AG04 MEDIUM §40 Execution Ladder / Browser Tier — Anti-Bot Detection

Browser Tier Has Zero Guidance for Handling reCAPTCHA, Cloudflare Bot Management, or CAPTCHA Bypass

The Gap

The spec provides no strategy for pages that deploy bot-detection (reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, Akamai Bot Manager). An agent dispatched to interact with such a page silently fails or receives a CAPTCHA challenge it cannot solve. There is no integration with CAPTCHA-solving services, no detection of CAPTCHA presence in the DOM, and no graceful degradation path that surfaces the block to the user.

Required Fix

Add a CaptchaDetectedError with a structured payload (captcha_type, page_url, screenshot URL in R2). Integrate an optional CAPTCHA-solving provider (2Captcha, Anti-Captcha) as a plan-gated capability. Surface the block to the end-user via a WebSocket event so they can solve it manually and resume the agent task. For Cloudflare Turnstile pages, note that CF Browser Rendering should be allowed through automatically; document the CF Browser Rendering allow-listing approach for first-party CF-protected targets.

G-AG05 MEDIUM §40 Execution Ladder / Sandbox Tier — CF Container Eviction Policy

Cloudflare Container Eviction Timeline Beyond "10-Minute Sleep" Is Undocumented — Stale Refs Accumulate

The Gap

The spec documents that containers sleep after 10 minutes of idle but does not specify when Cloudflare actually evicts (terminates) a sleeping container. SandboxDO caches containerRef in-memory; after CF eviction the ref is a dead stub. The existing stale-ref bug (G-Q14) documents the detection gap, but without knowing the eviction TTL the retry back-off window cannot be correctly sized. Downstream: billing for the idle period is ambiguous and warm-pool sizing cannot be computed.

Required Fix

Instrument a canary container that emits a heartbeat every 30 seconds and measures when CF stops delivering it. Document the measured eviction TTL in the runbook. Set containerRef TTL in SandboxDO to 80% of the measured eviction window. Add a health-check probe (exec a no-op command) before every substantive exec() to eagerly detect dead refs and trigger fresh container allocation. Expose eviction event metrics to the platform ops dashboard via Analytics Engine.

G-AG06 HIGH §17 Memory Architecture — Memory Consolidation Scheduler

Episodic-to-Semantic Memory Promotion Has No Trigger, No Timeline, and No Scheduled Job

The Gap

The spec defines four memory layers (episodic, semantic, procedural, working) and describes consolidation as a background sweep. However, the consolidation job is never scheduled: there is no CF Cron trigger, no Workflow step, and no event that fires the episodic→semantic promotion. Episodic memories accumulate indefinitely with no compression. The sweeper that should drive this also has a pagination bug (G-K43) that silently skips spaces beyond 1,000. Without consolidation, long-lived agents degrade in quality as their context fills with raw episodes rather than distilled facts.

Required Fix

Define the consolidation policy in the space manifest: a configurable "consolidate_after" threshold (default: 50 episodic entries or 7 days, whichever first). Implement MemoryConsolidationWorkflow as a CF Workflow with steps: (1) load episodic batch, (2) LLM-summarise into semantic facts, (3) upsert to Vectorize with spaceId+userId filters, (4) mark episodes as consolidated. Schedule via CF Cron (nightly). Fix sweeper cursor pagination (G-K43) as a prerequisite.

G-AG07 HIGH §17 Memory Architecture — Cross-Session Context Reconstruction

Resuming a Conversation Days Later Replays Raw Message History — No Episodic Replay or Summary Injection

The Gap

When an end-user resumes a conversation after a gap, the agent reconstructs context by fetching raw message history from SpaceThreadsDO and replaying it into the LLM context window. There is no semantic summary injection, no episodic replay strategy, and no distinction between recent (high-weight) and distant (low-weight) messages. For long conversations this exceeds the context window and the middle is silently truncated (G-R23 related), causing the agent to "forget" earlier commitments and facts.

Required Fix

Implement a session-resume hydration pipeline: (1) query the consolidated semantic memories for this (spaceId, userId) pair from Vectorize, (2) prepend a system block "Key facts about this user: ..." with the top-K semantic facts, (3) include only the last N raw messages (configurable, default 20) for recency context, (4) if the full history fits in the context window include it verbatim. Emit a resumption event to Analytics Engine so session-quality metrics can be tracked.

G-AG08 MEDIUM §16 Context Manager — Context Truncation Feedback

Agent Is Never Informed When Its Context Has Been Silently Truncated — Continuity Breaks Invisibly

The Gap

ContextManager.truncateMiddle() removes messages from position 2 onward when the 85% token threshold is crossed (hard-coded to 2,633 tokens). The truncation happens silently: the agent receives a reduced context with no indication that messages were dropped. This leads to the agent referring to information it "remembers" from the dropped messages, producing hallucinations or contradictions that are invisible to the end-user and undetectable in telemetry.

Required Fix

Before performing truncation, emit a structured truncation_event to the agent's working memory: { "type": "context_truncated", "dropped_count": N, "oldest_kept_ts": T }. Inject a synthetic system message ("Note: earlier messages were summarised for context length") at the truncation boundary. Expose a truncation metric to the builder analytics dashboard. Long-term: replace truncateMiddle with LLM-based progressive summarisation of the oldest messages before they are dropped.

G-AG09 HIGH §17 Memory Architecture — Memory GDPR Data Portability

No Export Pathway for Agent Memory — GDPR Article 20 Data Portability Right Unimplemented

The Gap

GDPR Article 20 grants users the right to receive their personal data in a structured, machine-readable format. Agent memory (episodic events, semantic facts, procedural skills, working-memory snapshots) is stored across SpaceDO SQLite, Vectorize, and R2 but there is no export endpoint that collects and packages this data. The GDPR erasure saga (G-AD13) addresses deletion but not portability. Users cannot download their memory, preventing them from migrating to another provider or auditing what was learned.

Required Fix

Implement GET /users/{userId}/memory/export that triggers a MemoryExportWorkflow: (1) query all episodic/semantic/procedural rows from SpaceDO SQLite filtered by userId, (2) query Vectorize for all vectors with metadata.userId, (3) list R2 artifacts tagged with userId, (4) stream all collected data as a NDJSON archive to a signed R2 URL with 24h TTL. Email the download link to the user. Honour the 30-day GDPR response deadline by queuing the request as a CF Workflow with a deadline alarm.

G-AG10 CRITICAL §Analytics Engine — Builder Analytics Query API

No REST Endpoint or Query Builder UI for Builders to Query Their Analytics Engine Data

The Gap

The spec declares GET /builder/products/{productId}/analytics and GET /builder/products/{productId}/analytics/revenue but provides no implementation. There is no REST endpoint that accepts a query, validates it against the builder's spaceId scope, executes it against Analytics Engine, and returns results. Without this API, builders cannot build custom dashboards, cannot run ad-hoc analyses, and cannot access the event data they generate. The spec's builder dashboard is inoperable.

Required Fix

Implement naelao-analytics-api Worker with: POST /query (body: { sql, spaceId }) → validates SQL does not contain cross-space reads (must include WHERE index1 = 'spaceId' predicate), executes against CF Analytics Engine SQL API, returns rows as JSON. Enforce per-query row limits (10K) and execution timeouts (30s). Add a query builder UI in the builder dashboard (drag-and-drop chart builder on top of Recharts). Publish the Analytics Engine SQL dialect reference (ClickHouse subset) in the developer docs.

G-AG11 MEDIUM §Analytics Engine — Analytics Data Export

No CSV or Parquet Export for Builder Analytics — Builders Cannot Perform Offline Analysis

The Gap

Builders who want to perform offline analysis (Excel, Jupyter, data warehouse ETL) have no way to export their Analytics Engine data. The spec mentions "CSV export for product team" only in the context of internal agent analysis, not as a builder-facing feature. Analytics Engine's immutable append-only store makes ad-hoc downloads non-trivial, but there is no export-to-R2 pipeline or streaming download endpoint.

Required Fix

Implement POST /builder/products/{productId}/analytics/export with body { format: "csv" | "parquet" | "ndjson", dateRange, eventTypes }. The Worker runs the Analytics Engine query, streams results through a CF Stream Transform Worker that serialises rows, writes the file to a builder-scoped R2 path with a signed 1h URL, and emails the link. For large exports (>100K rows) use a CF Workflow with step checkpoints to avoid the 30s Worker timeout. Document size limits in the API reference.

G-AG12 MEDIUM §Analytics Engine — Analytics Write Throughput Limits

No Backpressure or Throttling When Analytics Engine Write Quota Is Exceeded

The Gap

CF Analytics Engine allows up to 100,000 writes per second per account. At platform scale (millions of builder products × millions of end-users), this per-account ceiling can be breached by a single viral product. When exceeded, writes are silently dropped with no error returned to the writing Worker. The spec never references this limit, never instruments it, and has no fallback (e.g. Queue-based buffering) when the quota is approached.

Required Fix

Instrument a per-account analytics write rate counter using a RateCounterDO (100ms sliding window). When the rate exceeds 80% of the quota, start buffering writes to a CF Queue (naelao-analytics-buffer) and drain the queue at the safe rate. Emit a platform_quota_warning event to the ops Slack channel via PagerDuty webhook. For enterprise builders with high-volume products, document the option to use a dedicated CF account with its own Analytics Engine quota.

G-AG13 HIGH §Space Type System — Space Type Schema Migration

No Automated Migration Path When a Space Type's Schema Changes for Existing Spaces

The Gap

The spec documents a 90-day deprecation grace period and acknowledges that existing Spaces "remain functional until they migrate," but provides zero migration tooling. When a Space Type's capability schema evolves (new required field, renamed key, changed default), all existing Spaces using that type become schema-diverged. There is no migration runner, no diff tool, no admin endpoint to apply the schema change to existing Spaces, and no builder-facing migration wizard.

Required Fix

Implement a SpaceTypeMigrationWorkflow: given (old_version, new_version, spaceId), (1) diff the manifests to produce a change-set (added, removed, renamed, changed-default fields), (2) apply additive changes immediately (new optional fields get defaults), (3) for breaking changes generate a migration plan JSON, present it to the builder for approval, (4) on approval execute the migration with full rollback on failure. Emit migration_applied events to Analytics Engine. Surface pending migrations as a dashboard notification.

G-AG14 LOW §Space Type System — Space Type Forking

Builders Cannot Fork or Derive Custom Space Type Variants — One-Size-Fits-All Blueprint Constraint

The Gap

Space Types are exclusively authored by Naelao. Builders who need a hybrid (e.g., an e-commerce Space Type with an added healthcare compliance module) cannot fork the base type and add capability overrides. They are forced to choose the closest existing type and work around its limitations. This creates a bottleneck where every new builder need requires a Naelao platform engineering cycle.

Required Fix

Introduce a Space Type Extension manifest: builders (on enterprise plan) can declare "extends": "naelao/ecommerce@2", plus a "capabilities_override" object that adds or disables specific capabilities. Extensions are validated against the parent type's extension policy (which capabilities are extensible vs. locked). Extensions go through a 48h platform review (same as Apps). Publish an Extension SDK with type-safe schemas generated from the parent Space Type manifest.

G-AG15 MEDIUM §Template System — Template Version Pinning

No Specification on Whether Template Updates Auto-Apply to Existing Spaces or Stay Pinned at Selection Time

The Gap

The spec pre-loads Space Templates but is silent on versioning semantics: if a template author publishes v2 of a template (new capability config, changed defaults), do all Spaces that used v1 automatically update? Or are they pinned to v1? Auto-update could break existing Spaces; staying pinned means security fixes are not applied. Neither policy is documented, and there is no template version field in the schema.

Required Fix

Add a template_version field to the space manifest and a pinning policy enum: "auto" (always follow latest), "semver" (auto-apply patch/minor, not major), "pinned" (never update without explicit builder action). Default to "semver". When a template publishes a new version, run compatibility checks against all pinned Spaces and surface incompatibilities as dashboard alerts. Publish a template changelog API. Allow builders to preview the diff before approving an upgrade.

G-AG16 HIGH §UI Accessibility — WCAG Focus Management and Keyboard Navigation

Agent Chat UI and Builder Canvas Have No Keyboard Navigation, Focus Traps, or ARIA Labels

The Gap

The builder canvas and agent chat UI are entirely mouse-driven. There are no keyboard navigation affordances (Tab order, focus rings, Enter/Escape for modal dismissal), no ARIA landmark regions (role="main", role="complementary"), no aria-label attributes on icon buttons, and no focus trap implementation for modals and drawers. This makes the platform inaccessible to keyboard-only users and screen-reader users, violating WCAG 2.1 AA (Success Criteria 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 4.1.2) and potentially ADA/EAA requirements.

Required Fix

Audit all interactive elements against WCAG 2.1 AA using the axe-core automated scanner in CI (add @axe-core/playwright to the E2E suite). Fix: add logical Tab order (tabindex="0" on all interactive elements), implement a FocusTrap component for modals, add aria-label to all icon-only buttons, declare landmark roles, add visible focus rings (outline: 2px solid var(--accent)). For the builder canvas, implement keyboard-driven node selection (arrow keys) and action triggers (Enter to activate, Escape to cancel).

G-AG17 HIGH §UI Accessibility — Screen Reader Streaming LLM Response Announcements

Streaming Agent Responses Have No aria-live Regions — Screen Readers Cannot Announce Incremental Output

The Gap

The agent chat UI streams LLM response tokens via WebSocket and appends them to the DOM one chunk at a time. There are no aria-live regions declared on the response container, so screen readers are unaware of the incrementally appearing text. The user experiences silence until the full response is complete, at which point nothing may be announced if the reader focus has moved away. This affects all agent interactions for visually impaired users.

Required Fix

Wrap the streaming response container in <div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="false" aria-relevant="additions">. Buffer incoming tokens (emit aria-live updates in 500ms batches rather than per-token to avoid overwhelming screen readers). On response completion, set aria-live="off" to prevent duplicate reads. Add a "skip to response" keyboard shortcut (Alt+R). For code blocks inside responses, announce "code block follows" before the block and "end code block" after. Test with VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Windows) in the E2E suite.

G-AG18 MEDIUM §i18n / Localisation — RTL Language Support

CSS Layout Is Entirely LTR-Hardcoded — Arabic, Hebrew, and Farsi Users See Broken Mirrored UI

The Gap

All CSS in the builder and generated product UIs uses hardcoded directional properties: margin-left, padding-right, text-align: left, float: left, border-left. None of these use CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end) or respect the document dir attribute. Arabic, Hebrew, and Farsi speakers (collectively >500M) see a layout that is neither mirrored correctly nor reflowed for RTL reading order.

Required Fix

Adopt CSS logical properties throughout the design system: replace margin-left/right with margin-inline-start/end, padding-left/right with padding-inline-start/end, border-left with border-inline-start, and text-align: left with text-align: start. Set dir="auto" on <html> and let the browser mirror the layout. Add a language detector (franc-min) that sets dir="rtl" when the detected language is Arabic, Hebrew, or Farsi. Run a visual regression suite in RTL mode using Playwright with Arabic locale.

G-AG19 MEDIUM §i18n / Localisation — Translation Key System

No Translation Infrastructure — Builder-Defined Content Strings Are Hardcoded and Cannot Be Localised

The Gap

The platform has no i18n framework. UI strings are hardcoded literals in TSX/HTML; builder-configured content (agent instructions, Space descriptions, email templates) is stored as a single locale-unaware string. Builders whose end-users speak multiple languages have no way to provide translated variants of their product UI or agent responses. The spec mentions agent responses "in the user's preferred language" as a pillar but provides zero implementation.

Required Fix

Integrate i18next (or equivalent) for the builder dashboard and generated product UIs. Extract all UI strings to locale/*.json files. For builder content strings, add a translations: Record<locale, string> field to the manifest schema. When the agent generates a response, check the end-user's Accept-Language header and the user's language preference (stored in SpaceDO users table) and select the appropriate locale. For languages not explicitly translated, fall back to the builder's default locale with an auto-translate disclaimer.

G-AG20 LOW §i18n / Localisation — Locale-Aware Date and Number Formatting

All Date, Time, Currency, and Number Values Are Hardcoded to US Locale — Incorrect in 190+ Countries

The Gap

The platform formats dates as MM/DD/YYYY, numbers with commas as thousands separators and dots as decimal separators, and currency values prefixed with "$" throughout the builder dashboard, invoices, and agent responses. European users (period as thousands, comma as decimal), ISO date users (YYYY-MM-DD), and non-dollar-currency builders see incorrectly formatted values. Browser APIs Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat are never used.

Required Fix

Replace all date/number formatting calls with Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat using the user's resolved locale (from Accept-Language or user preference). Add a currencyCode field to the builder product manifest (default: "USD"). Format monetary values with Intl.NumberFormat({ style: "currency", currency: currencyCode }). For agent-generated text containing numbers, pass the user locale to the LLM via a system instruction ("Format all numbers and dates using {locale} conventions"). Store locale preference in the users table.

G-AG21 CRITICAL §Observability — W3C Trace Context Propagation

No Distributed Tracing Across 22 Workers and Durable Objects — Requests Are Invisible Beyond One Hop

The Gap

The platform routes requests through up to 22 Workers (portal-router → gateway → auth → space → agent → tool → billing → queue → …). No traceparent header (W3C Trace Context) is generated, propagated, or consumed anywhere. Each Worker logs in isolation with its own request ID. When a request fails deep in the chain (e.g., a tool call in a sandbox Worker), there is no way to reconstruct the full causal chain. Debugging production incidents requires manually correlating logs across 22 isolated log streams.

Required Fix

Implement a TraceContext middleware that (1) generates a W3C traceparent at the portal-router entry point, (2) extracts it from incoming headers at every Worker and passes it to all downstream fetch() and Service Binding calls, (3) includes traceId in every Analytics Engine write and every DO SQLite log row. Integrate with Axiom or Baselime for cross-Worker trace assembly. Expose a GET /traces/{traceId} endpoint in the developer dashboard for builder-visible request traces.

G-AG22 HIGH §Platform Operations — On-Call Alert Routing

No PagerDuty or Opsgenie Integration — Critical Production Alerts Only Go to Slack Without Escalation

The Gap

The spec documents alerting via Analytics Engine → Slack webhook for critical thresholds (DO SQLite >9GB, error rate >1%). However, Slack is not an on-call escalation system: alerts can be missed overnight, there is no acknowledgment tracking, no escalation to secondary on-call if primary does not respond, and no incident timeline. For a platform with SLA commitments (99.9% uptime implied by enterprise pricing), this on-call gap means incidents go unresolved for hours.

Required Fix

Integrate PagerDuty (or Opsgenie) via their Events API v2. Define severity tiers: P1 (data loss, auth down, >5% error rate) → immediate page; P2 (quota >80%, DO near-full) → 15-min acknowledgment SLA; P3 (slow queries, partial feature degradation) → next business day. Implement auto-resolution when the alert condition clears. Document the on-call rotation schedule and runbook links in each alert. Add a status page (Statuspage.io or equivalent) that auto-updates from PagerDuty incident state.

G-AG23 HIGH §Platform Operations — Scheduled Job Monitoring

No Registry or Dead-Man-Switch Alerting for Sweeper, Billing, and Categorizer Cron Jobs

The Gap

The platform runs multiple critical cron jobs (memory sweeper, billing cycle reset, subscription categorizer, vector indexer). None have a dead-man's-switch pattern: if the job silently fails to run (CF Cron scheduling glitch, Worker deployment failure), there is no alert. Memory consolidation, billing resets, and vector re-indexing would silently stop without any operator notification. The spec never mentions a job registry or heartbeat pattern.

Required Fix

Implement a JobRegistryDO that maintains a map of { jobName: { expectedInterval, lastRunAt, lastStatus } }. Each cron job writes a heartbeat on completion. A separate Watcher cron (runs every 5 min) checks: for each registered job, if (now - lastRunAt) > 2 × expectedInterval, fire a P2 PagerDuty alert. Expose GET /ops/jobs/status in the internal ops dashboard. Add per-job success/failure counters to Analytics Engine for trend analysis. Document each job's expected runtime, SLA, and manual re-trigger procedure in the runbook.

G-AG24 CRITICAL §Billing / Wallet — Double-Entry Ledger

WalletDO Uses a Single Running Balance — No Double-Entry Journal, No Audit Trail for Financial Disputes

The Gap

WalletDO tracks finances as a single balance column plus a spent_this_month counter. There is no double-entry ledger (every debit has a corresponding credit; every credit has a corresponding debit). This means: (1) there is no immutable audit trail of every financial event — balance mutations are direct UPDATE statements with no history, (2) in the event of a billing dispute there is no transaction-level evidence, (3) accounting reconciliation against Stripe charges is impossible, (4) partial failures leave the balance in an unknown state with no journal to replay.

Required Fix

Replace the balance mutation model with a double-entry ledger table: CREATE TABLE ledger (id TEXT, ts INTEGER, type TEXT, debit_account TEXT, credit_account TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, description TEXT, idempotency_key TEXT UNIQUE, metadata TEXT). Derive balance via SELECT SUM(amount) WHERE account = 'wallet'. Define account types: CASH (wallet balance), REVENUE (earned), DEFERRED (prepaid), REFUND (reversal). Expose GET /billing/ledger as a paginated audit log for builders. Run a nightly reconciliation job comparing ledger totals against Stripe charges.

G-AG25 HIGH §Billing / Wallet — Partial Refund and Reversal Entry Types

No REVERSAL Ledger Entry Type or Refund Workflow — Credits Cannot Be Partially Refunded

The Gap

WalletDO has checkAndDeduct() and addCredits() but no reversal primitive. When a charge must be reversed (failed tool call, disputed AI response, partial service outage SLA credit), there is no way to create a compensating entry. Calling addCredits() with a positive amount is semantically ambiguous (new purchase vs. refund). This makes financial statements incorrect and prevents automated SLA credit issuance.

Required Fix

Add a reverseCharge(originalEntryId, amount, reason) method to WalletDO that: (1) looks up the original ledger entry by ID, (2) validates amount ≤ original, (3) inserts a REVERSAL entry with debit_account=REVENUE, credit_account=CASH, (4) updates the balance atomically within DO serialisation, (5) emits a reversal_event to Analytics Engine. Implement a RefundWorkflow for Stripe-linked charges: create Stripe refund → on success call reverseCharge → on failure log to DLQ. Expose POST /billing/refund to builder support tooling.

G-AG26 HIGH §Billing / Wallet — Billing Cycle Reset Atomicity

Monthly spent_this_month Reset Is a Non-Atomic Direct Mutation — Partial Failure Leaves Balance Corrupted

The Gap

The billing cycle rollover resets spent_this_month to 0 after 30 days via a direct UPDATE statement in a CF Workflow step. If the Workflow fails after the reset but before issuing the new period's credit grant (or before updating the cycle_start timestamp), the user will have their spend counter zeroed but not receive their credits, or their credits applied but the cycle start not updated, causing double-resets on the next run. There is no idempotency key on the reset operation.

Required Fix

Model the billing cycle reset as a single atomic WalletDO operation: resetCycle(idempotency_key, new_credits). Inside the DO: check if idempotency_key already exists in the ledger (skip if so), then in a single JS transaction: insert CYCLE_RESET ledger entry, insert CREDIT_GRANT entry, update cycle_start. The Workflow step calls this single method. On retry, the idempotency check prevents double-reset. Store cycle_start as a ledger-derivable value (first entry timestamp of the current period) rather than a mutable column.

G-AG27 MEDIUM §Billing / Wallet — Invoice PDF Generation

No Invoice Template, PDF Generation, or R2 Storage Path — Builders Cannot Provide Receipts to End-Users

The Gap

The billing system tracks charges but never generates a PDF invoice. B2B builders whose enterprise customers require invoices for accounts payable cannot satisfy this requirement. There is no invoice template, no PDF rendering pipeline (Puppeteer/PDF, or a service like Gotenberg), no R2 storage path for generated PDFs, and no email delivery of monthly statements. Tax line items are explicitly listed as unresolved.

Required Fix

Implement InvoiceGenerationWorkflow triggered on billing cycle close: (1) query ledger for the period, (2) calculate tax using Stripe Tax API (or Anrok for usage-based), (3) render an HTML invoice template using the platform's branded HTML/CSS, (4) convert to PDF via CF Browser Rendering (headless print), (5) store at r2://naelao-invoices/{builderId}/{year}-{month}.pdf, (6) generate a 7-day signed URL, (7) email the link to the builder's billing email. Expose GET /billing/invoices as a paginated list of signed PDF links.

G-AG28 MEDIUM §Billing / Subscription — Proration for Mid-Cycle Plan Changes

No Proration Logic for Plan Upgrades or Downgrades Mid-Billing-Cycle

The Gap

When a builder upgrades from Pro to Enterprise mid-month, the system creates a new subscription record but does not calculate or apply a prorated credit for the unused portion of the old plan, nor a prorated charge for the partial period of the new plan. Builders are effectively charged double for the overlap period, or the new plan's features are activated without payment for the partial period. Stripe's proration API is never referenced.

Required Fix

Use Stripe's built-in proration (proration_behavior: "create_prorations") when updating the Stripe subscription item. On receipt of the Stripe invoice.created webhook (which Stripe generates with proration line items), record the proration amounts in the WalletDO ledger as PRORATION_CREDIT or PRORATION_CHARGE entries. Surface the proration breakdown in the builder's invoice for that period. For credit-based plans, calculate the prorated credit grant as (days_remaining / total_days_in_cycle) × monthly_credits and apply atomically via addCredits().

G-AG29 MEDIUM §Billing / Accounting — Revenue Recognition for Prepaid Credits

No Deferred vs. Earned Revenue Distinction — Prepaid Credit Purchases Incorrectly Recognised as Immediate Revenue

The Gap

When a builder purchases a $500 credit pack, the entire $500 is implicitly treated as immediate revenue. Under ASC 606 / IFRS 15, prepaid credits are a liability (deferred revenue) until the credits are consumed. The platform has no deferred revenue balance tracking, no earned-upon-consumption mechanism, and no deferred revenue schedule. For SaaS companies that sell credit packs this is a material accounting error that will fail any financial audit.

Required Fix

Add DEFERRED_REVENUE and EARNED_REVENUE account types to the double-entry ledger. On credit purchase: debit CASH, credit DEFERRED_REVENUE (full amount). On each credit spend (checkAndDeduct call): debit DEFERRED_REVENUE, credit EARNED_REVENUE (proportional to credits spent). Expose a deferred_revenue_balance computed property via GET /billing/metrics. Run a nightly reconciliation that asserts DEFERRED_REVENUE balance ≥ 0 and equals outstanding unspent credits × price_per_credit. Include deferred/earned breakdown in the monthly financial export.

G-AG30 HIGH §Content Safety — Builder Asset Content Moderation

No Virus Scanning or Content Moderation for Builder-Uploaded Images, PDFs, and Binaries

The Gap

Builders upload arbitrary files (images, PDFs, videos, code archives) that are stored in R2 and potentially served to end-users. There is no virus/malware scanning pipeline, no NSFW image detection, no document malware analysis (malicious PDF JavaScript, macro-embedded Office files), and no content policy enforcement. A malicious builder (or a compromised builder account) could distribute malware to millions of end-users through the platform's R2-backed CDN.

Required Fix

Implement an AssetModerationWorkflow triggered on every R2 PUT via Queue: (1) download the asset to a CF Container sandbox, (2) run ClamAV (open source) for virus scanning, (3) for images run the CF Workers AI nsfw-image-detection model, (4) for PDFs strip active content (JavaScript, embedded macros) using pdf-lib, (5) set an r2_object_metadata "moderation_status": "safe" | "quarantined" | "pending". Quarantined assets return 451 Unavailable for Legal Reasons. Alert the builder and the Naelao trust & safety team on quarantine. Never serve assets with pending or quarantined status.

G-AG31 HIGH §Content Safety — LLM Jailbreak and System Prompt Injection Policy

No Content Policy Layer Beyond Base LLM Safety — Adversarial Prompts Can Override Agent Behaviour

The Gap

The agent's system prompt is set by the builder and injects into the LLM context. An end-user can craft adversarial messages ("Ignore previous instructions and instead ...") that override builder-defined behaviour. There is no secondary safety classifier that detects jailbreak attempts, no output filter for policy violations, and no rate-limiting specifically targeting adversarial users. The existing prompt injection defence (G-S17) covers memory writes but not direct chat messages.

Required Fix

Implement a TwoLayerSafetyFilter: (1) before injecting user message into context, classify it with a lightweight safety model (CF Workers AI or Perspective API) for jailbreak intent (output: safe | warn | block), (2) block messages scored as jailbreak and return a structured refusal with a reference ID the user can share with support, (3) after the LLM response, run an output classifier for policy violations (hate speech, explicit content, PII leakage), (4) record all jailbreak attempts in Analytics Engine for the trust & safety dashboard. Builders can configure the strictness level in the manifest.

G-AG32 HIGH §Agent Orchestration — Sub-Agent Spawn Resource Limits

No Per-Agent CPU, Memory, or Execution-Time Quotas — Malicious Builders Can Trigger Infinite Spawn Loops

The Gap

Sub-agent spawning is depth-limited to max_sub_agent_depth = 5 but has no horizontal width limit: a single agent can spawn 100 parallel sub-agents at depth 1. Each sub-agent can spawn 100 more at depth 2, giving 10,000 concurrent agents. There is no per-space concurrent agent limit, no total CPU quota per agent run, and no wall-clock timeout beyond the per-step LLM timeout. A single builder product can consume the entire platform's Durable Object compute budget.

Required Fix

Add three resource parameters to AgentManifest: maxConcurrentSubAgents (default: 10, max by plan: free=3, pro=25, enterprise=100), maxAgentWallClock (default: 5 min, max: 30 min), maxAgentLLMTokens (per-run budget). Enforce these in the orchestrator by maintaining an AgentBudgetDO per (spaceId, runId) that tracks active sub-agent count. When limit is reached, new spawn requests return AgentQuotaExceededError which the parent agent must handle. Emit quota_exceeded events to Analytics Engine and alert the trust & safety team on repeated violations.

G-AG33 CRITICAL §Security — Container Sandbox Credential Exposure via Environment Variables

Secrets Passed to Sandboxes as Environment Variables Are Readable by Any Code Running in the Container

The Gap

The SandboxDO passes NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN, API keys, and other secrets to container instances via environment variables at container start time. Any code executing inside the sandbox (including agent-executed shell commands, npm scripts, or code injected via prompt injection) can read all secrets via `process.env`, `printenv`, or `cat /proc/self/environ`. A prompt-injected command "echo $NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN" exfiltrates the platform's master auth token, giving the attacker full platform API access.

Required Fix

Never pass secrets as environment variables to containers. Instead: (1) generate a short-lived (15 min TTL) sandbox-scoped JWT signed with a per-sandbox private key at container boot, (2) the JWT encodes only the capabilities the sandbox needs (e.g., read-only access to a specific R2 path), (3) the container fetches the actual secret from a secrets sidecar endpoint (localhost:2525/secrets/{name}) that verifies the JWT before returning the value, (4) the sidecar applies request-rate limiting per secret name. For NAELAO_INTERNAL_TOKEN, replace the static shared secret with per-caller service JWTs (G-A28).

G-AG34 MEDIUM §Trust & Safety — Builder Free-Tier Abuse and Credit Grant Fraud

No Detection for Repeated Free-Tier Signups, Trial Resets, or Credit Grant Exploitation

The Gap

The platform offers a free tier with initial credit grants. There is no velocity check on account creation: a malicious user can create hundreds of accounts with disposable email addresses (Mailinator, 10-minute mail) and repeatedly claim free credits. The rate limiter covers LLM API calls but not account creation or credit grant flows. At scale, this abuse pattern can cost the platform significant GPU/API spend without revenue.

Required Fix

Implement a FraudSignalDO that aggregates signup velocity signals: IP address (max 3 accounts per /24 subnet per 24h), email domain (block disposable email domains via a maintained blocklist), payment fingerprint (for pro trial: Stripe Radar score). Add a credit_grant_log table in the platform Turso DB recording (userId, ip_hash, email_domain, grant_amount, ts). Run a fraud classifier on new signups: high-risk accounts are queued for manual review before credits are granted. For enterprise trials, require a corporate email domain and a Stripe card on file.

G-AG35 CRITICAL §Custom Domains — DNS Domain Ownership Verification

No DNS Ownership Challenge Before Domain Activation — Builders Can Claim Any Domain Including Competitor Sites

The Gap

The portal-router allows a builder to activate any custom domain by adding it to the naelao-domains KV namespace. There is no DNS TXT record challenge, no CNAME verification, and no ownership proof required. A malicious builder can claim competitor.com, a brand domain, or a government TLD. Requests to that domain will be routed to the attacker's Space. Combined with a phishing page, this is a trivial credential-harvesting attack vector.

Required Fix

Before activating any custom domain: (1) generate a unique verification token (UUID v4), (2) instruct the builder to add a DNS TXT record _naelao-verify.{domain} = {token}, (3) poll the Cloudflare Custom Hostnames API every 15 seconds for 5 minutes to check TXT resolution, (4) on verification success activate the domain in KV and issue the SSL certificate via Cloudflare API, (5) schedule a weekly re-verification job — revoke if TXT record disappears. Add a domain blocklist for known brand names, government TLDs, and previously-abused domains.

G-AG36 HIGH §Custom Domains — SSL Certificate Provisioning Race Condition

Custom Domains Serve Without Valid TLS Certificate During DNS Propagation — Browser Security Errors

The Gap

When a builder activates a custom domain, DNS propagation can take up to 5 minutes. During this window, the portal-router routes HTTPS requests to the space but the Cloudflare-managed certificate for the custom domain has not yet been issued. Browsers display ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. The spec has no "certificate pending" state, no fallback to the platform wildcard cert, and no user notification when the cert is issued.

Required Fix

Model the domain lifecycle as a state machine: PENDING_VERIFICATION → VERIFIED → CERT_PROVISIONING → ACTIVE → SUSPENDED. In the CERT_PROVISIONING state, serve requests from the custom domain over the platform's wildcard cert with a banner "SSL certificate provisioning — fully active in ~5 minutes." Poll the Cloudflare Custom Hostnames API for ssl.status == "active" at 15-second intervals (CF Workflow with step.sleep). On activation, WebSocket-push a domain_activated event to the builder's dashboard. Add the domain_lifecycle state to the custom domains KV entry.

G-AG37 MEDIUM §Custom Domains — Domain Conflict Resolution

No Conflict Detection or Resolution for Two Builders Claiming the Same Custom Domain

The Gap

The domain activation flow does a KV.put() on the custom domain key without checking if another builder already owns it. A domain claimed by Builder A can be silently overwritten by Builder B. The first builder's users are then redirected to the second builder's space with no warning. This is a denial-of-service vector against legitimate builders who have paid for custom domain routing.

Required Fix

Add an atomic claim-check to the domain activation flow using KV.put with expiration metadata that includes the owning builderId and claimedAt timestamp. Before activating: check if domain is already claimed by a different builder; if so, return 409 Conflict with a reference to the claim timestamp. Add a dispute resolution endpoint (POST /ops/domains/{domain}/dispute) for platform admins to transfer or revoke a domain claim. Require re-verification after any ownership transfer. Notify both builders via email on conflict detection.

G-AG38 MEDIUM §Custom Domains — Domain Health Monitoring

No Periodic DNS Health Checks — Stale or Broken Custom Domain Routing Goes Undetected

The Gap

After initial activation, custom domains are never re-checked. If a builder's DNS configuration drifts (nameserver change, deleted CNAME, expired domain), the portal-router will continue routing to their space but incoming requests will fail SSL verification or never reach CF. The builder and their end-users experience silent failures with no alerting and no automated remediation.

Required Fix

Add a DomainHealthMonitorWorkflow that runs nightly: for each active custom domain, (1) issue a DNS resolution check via Cloudflare's DNS-over-HTTPS API (1.1.1.1), (2) verify the CNAME still points to the platform endpoint, (3) check SSL certificate expiry (warn at 30 days, alert at 7 days), (4) on health check failure for 3 consecutive runs, set domain status to DEGRADED and email the builder. On 7 consecutive failures, set to SUSPENDED and stop routing. Log all health check results to Analytics Engine for trend analysis.

G-AG39 LOW §Custom Domains — Domain Reservation Cleanup on Account Deletion

Custom Domain Reservation Is Never Released When a Builder Account Is Deleted

The Gap

When a builder deletes their account, the account deletion workflow removes their SpaceDO and billing records but does not release their custom domain reservations from the portal-router KV namespace. These orphaned domain entries permanently block future builders from registering the same domains, and since the KV entry has no expiry, they accumulate indefinitely. A builder could also maliciously squat on a domain by creating and deleting accounts repeatedly.

Required Fix

Add a domain cleanup step to the AccountDeletionWorkflow: (1) list all custom domains owned by the builder from the domains KV namespace, (2) for each domain set a 90-day grace period entry (status: PENDING_RELEASE with expiry timestamp), (3) send the builder a "domain release in 90 days" notification, (4) after 90 days delete the KV entry. If another builder claims the domain during the grace period, send an email to the original owner. For immediate release, provide a POST /domains/{domain}/release endpoint.

G-AG40 HIGH §Message Ordering — Global Causal Message Ordering Guarantee

No Causal Ordering Guarantee Across Queue → DO → WebSocket Pipeline — Retried Messages Can Arrive Out of Sequence

The Gap

CF Queues provide at-least-once delivery with no FIFO guarantee. A message retried after a transient failure can arrive after a later message that already processed successfully. The agent pipeline (user message → Queue → ConversationDO → SpaceDO → WebSocket stream) has no sequence number, no causal ordering check, and no idempotency gate. End-users can see responses delivered out of order, or the same response delivered twice.

Required Fix

Add a sequence_number field (monotonically increasing, scoped to spaceId+threadId) to all Queue messages. The ConversationDO maintains a next_expected_seq counter; messages arriving out of order are buffered in a priority queue and held until their predecessor arrives (or a 30s gap timeout triggers a recovery path). Idempotency keys on all Queue producers prevent duplicate processing. Consider using CF Queues with FIFO configuration (when available) for conversation message queues. WebSocket stream chunks carry seq numbers for client-side ordering.

G-AG41 HIGH §Message Ordering — Platform-Wide Idempotency Framework

No Idempotency Keys Enforced Across Workers and DOs — At-Least-Once Queue Delivery Causes Duplicate Side Effects

The Gap

CF Queues guarantee at-least-once delivery. The platform has identified at least 4 known duplicate side-effect bugs (notification double-send, idempotency KV lock without TTL, append_to_file race, ingestion re-upload dedup missing) but there is no platform-wide idempotency framework. Each Worker handles (or fails to handle) duplicates in ad-hoc ways. Adding new queue consumers requires each developer to re-invent idempotency from scratch.

Required Fix

Implement an IdempotencyDO that provides: checkAndSet(key, TTL) → returns "first_call" | "duplicate". All Queue message handlers call this before processing. The idempotency key is the Queue message ID (which CF guarantees is stable across retries). TTL should be 2× the Queue's max retry window (24 hours). Use an IdempotencyMiddleware wrapper that automatically gates all Queue consumer handle() methods. Document the idempotency contract in the developer guide: "all Queue consumers must be idempotent; use IdempotencyMiddleware."

G-AG42 MEDIUM §WebSocket Streaming — Stream Chunk Sequence Numbers

Streaming LLM Response Chunks Have No Sequence Numbers — Out-of-Order Delivery Corrupts Displayed Text

The Gap

The agent WebSocket stream sends LLM response tokens as raw text chunks with no sequence number. TCP retransmission normally preserves order, but WebSocket reconnects (which the spec handles via G-X16) can cause chunk redelivery from the server's buffer. Without sequence numbers, the client cannot detect or reorder duplicates, and text can appear scrambled after a reconnect. The hibernation reconnect logic does not specify chunk deduplication semantics.

Required Fix

Add a { seq: number, chunk: string, done: boolean } envelope to all WebSocket stream messages. The client maintains a next_expected_seq counter; received chunks with seq < next_expected_seq are silently discarded (duplicates). Chunks with seq > next_expected_seq are buffered and rendered in order. The server buffers the last 100 chunks per stream in DO storage so that a reconnecting client can request "replay from seq N" via a reconnect message. Test this with Playwright WebSocket interception that randomly drops and duplicates chunks.

G-AG43 HIGH §CF Queues / DLQ — DLQ Visibility for Builders

Dead-Letter Queue Messages Are Auto-Discarded After 4 Days — Builders Never Notified of Permanent Processing Failures

The Gap

CF Queues retain DLQ messages for only 4 days. The spec declares a naelao-dlq queue binding but never implements a DLQ consumer. Messages that permanently fail (malformed payload, bug in consumer) are silently discarded. Builders whose events (e.g., webhook delivery, document ingestion) are DLQ'd have no visibility into what failed, why, or that it happened at all. The 4-day auto-discard means the window to diagnose and recover is very narrow.

Required Fix

Implement a DLQConsumer Worker that is bound to naelao-dlq: on receipt, (1) write the failed message to the builder's event_failures table in SpaceDO SQLite (message body, error reason, original queue, failed_at, retry_count), (2) surface the failure in the builder dashboard under "Event Failures" with a one-click retry button, (3) for P1 failure types (billing, auth) trigger a PagerDuty alert. Add a DLQ health metric to the ops dashboard showing DLQ message rate by queue and failure reason. Implement a manual retry endpoint: POST /ops/dlq/{messageId}/retry.

G-AG44 MEDIUM §CF Queues — Queue Message Schema Version Migration

No Version Tags or Compatibility Layer on Queue Messages — Consumer Schema Changes Break In-Flight Messages

The Gap

Queue message payloads have no schema version field. When a consumer is updated (new field added, field renamed, type changed), in-flight messages written by the old producer will be consumed by the new consumer and parsed with the old schema. This causes silent data loss (missing fields default to undefined) or crashes (schema validation errors). There is no consumer migration strategy or backward compatibility policy.

Required Fix

Add a "v" (version) field to all Queue message schemas, starting at 1. Consumers handle messages by version: a switch(msg.v) block with a case for each known version. When adding a field, bump the version; the new consumer handles both v_old (with default for the new field) and v_new. Provide a message version registry in the developer docs listing all active message types and their versions. For breaking changes (field removal, type change), deploy a bridge consumer that reads old messages and re-publishes them in the new format before the old consumer is retired.

G-AG45 HIGH §Fine-Tuning Pipeline — Training Data Quality Gates

No Deduplication, PII Scrubbing, or Format Validation Before Fine-Tune Data Upload to Together AI

The Gap

Training data submitted by builders is uploaded directly to Together AI without any preprocessing. There is no JSONL format validation (missing prompt/completion fields cause Together AI job failures that are hard to diagnose), no deduplication (duplicate examples degrade model quality and waste GPU compute), and no PII scrubbing (names, emails, SSNs in training data violate GDPR if the data is used to train models that could regurgitate it). Together AI has no BAA, so HIPAA builders cannot lawfully upload PHI.

Required Fix

Implement a TrainingDataQualityWorker triggered before upload: (1) parse and validate JSONL (each line must have {prompt: string, completion: string}), (2) deduplicate using MinHash LSH (threshold 0.9 Jaccard similarity), (3) run PII detection (Microsoft Presidio or a CF Workers AI model) and either reject or anonymise detected PII, (4) for HIPAA spaces, block upload entirely and return error("PHI in training data: use a HIPAA-compliant provider"). Store the quality report (row count, dedup_removed, pii_detected) in the fine-tune job record.

G-AG46 HIGH §Fine-Tuning Pipeline — Fine-Tune Job Checkpoint Recovery and 1000-Step Ceiling

Long Fine-Tune Jobs Loop Toward the CF Workflow 1000-Step Limit with No Recovery Path

The Gap

The fine-tune polling loop uses step.sleep("30 minutes") on each iteration. A Together AI job taking 24 hours requires 48 polling steps just for status checks, plus setup, eval, and notification steps. Large training runs (7B+ parameter models) can exceed 24 hours, pushing the Workflow past the 1000-step hard limit, which terminates the Workflow. The running fine-tune job has no mechanism to recover the Workflow or clean up the dangling Together AI job.

Required Fix

Switch the polling loop to a CF Workflow scheduled callback pattern: after each step.sleep, use a step.do("check_status_" + iteration) that is uniquely named to avoid step name collision. Add a max_poll_iterations guard (default: 200) that, when reached, creates a continuation Workflow (same runId but a new Workflow instance) and terminates the current one cleanly. The continuation inherits the Together AI job ID from the SpaceDO fine_tune_jobs table. Add a checkpoint_at field to the job record updated on each successful poll.

G-AG47 MEDIUM §Fine-Tuning Pipeline — Fine-Tuned Model A/B Traffic Routing

No Traffic-Splitting Mechanism Between Fine-Tuned Model and Base Model for Evaluation

The Gap

After a fine-tune job completes and the model is registered, all traffic for that space is immediately switched to the fine-tuned model. There is no gradual rollout, no A/B traffic split, and no automatic rollback if the fine-tuned model performs worse than the base model on key metrics. Builders have no way to validate that the fine-tuned model is actually better before committing 100% of traffic to it.

Required Fix

Add a model_rollout_config to the fine_tune_jobs record: { strategy: "immediate" | "canary" | "ab_test", canary_percent: 10, base_model_id, fine_tuned_model_id, promotion_criteria: { min_evals_passed: 5, min_user_rating: 4.2 } }. In the LLM routing layer (naelao-model-router), for each request hash (userId, spaceId) to a bucket 0-99 and route to the fine-tuned model if bucket < canary_percent. Record base vs. fine-tuned model for each response in Analytics Engine. Run a nightly promotion check: if criteria are met for 7 days, auto-promote to 100%.

G-AG48 HIGH §Fine-Tuning Pipeline — Fine-Tuned Model Versioning and Rollback

Approved Fine-Tuned Models Are Registered Once with No Version History or Rollback Capability

The Gap

When a builder trains a new model version (v2), it replaces v1 in the model registry. The v1 adapter weights and evaluation results are not retained. If v2 degrades quality (a common occurrence when training data drifts), there is no rollback path. The builder must re-submit a new training job from scratch, waiting hours for the job to complete while users experience the degraded model.

Required Fix

Implement versioned model registration: each fine-tune job produces a unique model_version_id. Store all versions in a model_versions table: (space_id, version_id, together_ai_model_id, created_at, eval_scores, r2_path_of_adapter_weights, status: active|archived|deprecated). Provide POST /spaces/{id}/models/{versionId}/rollback that atomically switches the active version pointer. Retain at least 3 prior versions (configurable). For the adapter weights themselves, copy from Together AI's storage to R2 (naelao-model-artifacts/{spaceId}/{versionId}/) immediately after training completes to prevent Together AI retention policy from deleting them.

G-AG49 HIGH §Fine-Tuning Pipeline — Fine-Tune Cost Attribution and Billing

Together AI Fine-Tune Jobs Called Directly, Bypassing the Billing Proxy — Costs Completely Untracked

The Gap

Agent tool calls route through naelao-llm-proxy which enforces wallet reservations and bills LLM costs per token. However, fine-tuning job submissions call Together AI directly using env.TOGETHER_AI_API_KEY, bypassing the proxy. Together AI charges for GPU training compute (e.g., $0.10/min for A100) but these costs are never recorded in WalletDO, never shown on the builder's invoice, and never attributed to the correct space. The platform absorbs all fine-tuning costs without builder recovery.

Required Fix

Route fine-tune job submissions through the billing proxy. Before submitting to Together AI: (1) estimate the training cost (dataset_tokens × estimated_training_flops × cost_per_TFLOP), (2) pre-authorise the estimated amount in WalletDO as a PENDING_FINE_TUNE_CHARGE, (3) submit to Together AI via the proxy which forwards the request and captures the job_id, (4) on job completion, query Together AI for actual GPU minutes used, (5) finalise the charge (FINE_TUNE_COMPUTE line item) and release the pre-auth hold. Surface fine-tuning costs as a separate line item in the builder invoice.

G-AG50 HIGH §Testing Infrastructure — Durable Object SQLite Unit Test Mock

No Test Double for ctx.storage.sql.exec() — DO Unit Tests Require Live Miniflare or Cannot Run

The Gap

Durable Object business logic uses this.ctx.storage.sql.exec(sql, ...params) for all database operations. The test suite has DO unit tests (suites 02-04) but never specifies the test double for this API. Without a mock, every DO unit test requires a live Miniflare environment (slow, ~5s cold start), making the unit test suite impractically slow for TDD workflows. Teams resort to skipping DO tests or testing only through integration tests, losing fast-feedback cycle.

Required Fix

Implement a SqliteStorageMock class that replicates the ctx.storage.sql.exec() API using better-sqlite3 (synchronous, in-process, identical SQL dialect): class SqliteStorageMock { exec(sql, ...params) { return this.db.prepare(sql).all(...params); } }. Provide a createTestDO<T>(DoClass, env, storageState?) factory that injects SqliteStorageMock as ctx.storage. Ship the mock as @naelao/testing package. Also provide mocks for: ctx.waitUntil() (queues promises), ctx.acceptWebSocket() (records WS interactions), and ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile() (executes the callback immediately). Add examples for all DO classes in the test suite.

Appendix AH — Additional Technical Gaps (50 items)

Tool registry · MCP resilience · voice/WebRTC · enterprise compliance · multi-tenancy isolation · webhooks · SDK · RAG quality · LLM streaming · CI/CD · GDPR · SOC 2 · prompt injection

G-AH01 HIGH §MCP Hub / Tool Registry — Tool Schema Versioning and Deprecation

No Versioned Tool Registry — Breaking Schema Changes Silently Break All Deployed Agents Calling Old Signatures

The Gap

Tools are registered in the MCP hub with a single current schema. When a tool author adds a required parameter or renames a field, all existing agents that call the old signature receive a validation error at runtime with no migration path. There is no tool version field (e.g. tool@2.0), no deprecation grace period, no backward-compatibility shim, and no way for a builder to pin an agent to a specific tool version. A single platform team update can break thousands of builder agents simultaneously.

Required Fix

Add a semver version field to every tool manifest. Store all versions in the tool registry (tool_versions table in RegistryDO). When resolving a tool call, match by (name, version_range) — agents specify a minimum version, the hub selects the newest compatible version. On publishing a breaking change (major version bump): run a compatibility scanner that identifies all agents using the old version, send builder notifications, and enforce a 30-day deprecation window before removing the old version. Expose GET /tools/{name}/versions for discovery.

G-AH02 HIGH §MCP Hub — MCP Server Circuit Breaking

No Circuit Breaker or Fast-Fail for Flaky MCP Servers — One Unavailable Server Stalls All Dependent Agents

The Gap

When a third-party MCP server is unavailable, slow, or returning errors, the MCP hub waits for the full connection timeout before failing a tool call. Agents block waiting for the response; the LLM context window is held open; and the DO concurrency slot is consumed. There is no circuit breaker that tracks error rates per MCP server and fast-fails when a server is known-bad. One degraded third-party MCP server can cascade into an agent execution outage affecting every builder product that installed that app.

Required Fix

Implement a CircuitBreakerDO per MCP server endpoint. States: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (fast-fail), HALF-OPEN (probe). Thresholds: open after 5 consecutive errors in 60s; probe after 30s in OPEN; close after 2 successful probes. On OPEN: immediately return MCP_UNAVAILABLE error to the agent (do not wait for timeout). Emit circuit_state_change events to the builder's event failure log and the platform ops dashboard. Expose current circuit state via GET /apps/{appId}/health. Allow builders to configure per-app timeout and circuit thresholds in the app manifest.

G-AH03 MEDIUM §Tool Invocation Layer — Tool Output Caching vs Side-Effect Safety

No Caching Policy Distinguishes Read-Only Tools from Side-Effectful Tools — Duplicate Actions or Stale Reads

The Gap

The tool invocation layer has no output caching. Pure read-only tools (web_search, get_weather, read_file) called with identical parameters multiple times in one agent run re-execute the full call each time, wasting latency and quota. Conversely, if caching were naively added, side-effectful tools (send_email, charge_card, create_calendar_event) would be incorrectly served stale cached results, suppressing duplicate side effects that should have fired. Neither problem is addressed.

Required Fix

Add a "cacheable": true | false field to every tool manifest (side-effectful tools must declare cacheable: false). For cacheable tools, implement a ToolResultCache using SpaceDO SQLite: key = SHA-256(tool_name + sorted_params), TTL configurable per tool (default 5 minutes). Cache hits skip the MCP call and return the cached value immediately. For non-cacheable tools, add an idempotency_key parameter that callers supply; the MCP hub records calls and deduplicates by idempotency_key within a 24h window. Document the policy in the tool authoring guide.

G-AH04 MEDIUM §Agent Orchestration — Per-Agent Concurrent Tool Call Limit

Unbounded Parallel Tool Execution Per Agent — One Agent Can Launch Hundreds of Concurrent MCP Calls

The Gap

The agent can issue parallel tool calls (Claude supports multi-tool_use blocks). There is no cap on how many tools can run simultaneously within a single agent step. A single agent step requesting 50 parallel web searches exhausts the platform's outbound HTTP connection quota, creates 50 concurrent DO sleeps waiting for results, and can trigger rate limits on downstream APIs. There is no per-agent concurrency limit, no per-step budget, and no prioritisation of critical tools over background tools.

Required Fix

Add maxConcurrentToolCalls (default: 5, plan max: free=2, pro=10, enterprise=25) to the agent manifest. In the orchestrator, implement a semaphore (ToolConcurrencySemaphore) scoped to (spaceId, agentRunId) that blocks tool dispatches beyond the limit. Queue excess tool calls and dispatch as slots free. Emit tool_concurrency_throttled events to Analytics Engine. For the LLM response parsing step that extracts parallel tool calls, group them into batches of maxConcurrentToolCalls and execute batches sequentially, passing results from each batch back to the LLM for intermediate reasoning.

G-AH05 HIGH §Tool Access Control — Tool Allowlist and Blocklist Per Space

No Per-Space Tool Allowlist — Any Agent Can Call Any Installed Tool Including Payment and Credential Tools

The Gap
